profileDesc.creation:
Initially created: 2025-12-17T20:55:42.576+09:00 by chris Translate the following text from Classical Chinese into English.
Requirements: 1. The text contains page numbers in square brackets, such as [01], [02], etc. - These must be passed through unchanged. - Each page number must appear in exactly the same position in the translation as in the source. - The number of page markers in the output must match the input exactly.
2. Personal names, place names, titles, and other proper nouns should be rendered in Hànyǔ Pīnyīn with tone marks.
3. Do NOT transcribe the full Classical Chinese text into Pinyin.
4. Do NOT include explanatory notes, annotations, or commentary — output only the English translation.
5. The target language is English.

p.seg: Běnjì yī Tàizǔ yī
Tàizǔ Kāitiān Xíngdào Zhàojì Lìjí Dàshèng Zhìshén Rénwén Yìwǔ Jùndé Chénggōng Gāohuángdì,
taboo name Yuánzhāng,
courtesy name Guóruì,
surname Zhū shì.
His ancestors lived in Pèi,
then moved to Jùróng,
and again moved to Sìzhōu.
His father, Shìzhēn,
first moved to Zhōnglí in Háozhōu.
He had four sons,
Tàizǔ being the youngest.
His mother was née Chén.
While pregnant,
she dreamed that a deity bestowed a pill,
which glowed in her palm.
She swallowed it and awoke,
her mouth still fragrant.
When he was born,
a red light filled the room.
From then on,
light frequently appeared at night.
Neighbors, seeing it,
mistook it for fire
and often rushed to help,
but found nothing upon arrival.
As he grew,
his appearance was heroic and outstanding,
with a remarkable bone protuberance on his head.
His will and ambition were vast,
and no one could fathom them.
In Zhìzhèng four years
there was drought and locusts,
and a great famine and epidemic.
Tàizǔ was seventeen at the time;
his parents and elder brother successively died,
and he was too poor to bury them.
A villager, Liú Jìzǔ, gave him land,
and he was thus able to bury them.
This is the Fèngyáng mausoleum.
Tàizǔ, an orphan with no one to rely on,
entered the Huángjué Temple to become a monk.
A month later,
he traveled to Héféi to beg for food.
He fell ill on the way,
and two purple-robed men accompanied him,
caring for him very attentively.
When he recovered,
they disappeared.
He traveled through Guāng, Gù, Rǔ, and Yǐng prefectures for three years,
then returned to the temple.
At this time,
the Yuán government was in disarray,
and bandits rose everywhere.
Liú Fútōng, supporting Hán Shāntóng, claimed to be a descendant of the Sòng dynasty and rose in Yǐng;
Xú Shòuhuī usurped the imperial title and rose in Qí;
Lǐ Èr, Péng Dà, and Zhào Jūnyòng rose in Xú.
Each host numbered tens of thousands,
all appointing generals and commanders,
killing officials,
and encroaching upon prefectures and counties.
Fāng Guózhēn had already risen earlier along the coast.
Other bandits commanded troops and occupied territories,
plundering extensively.
The world was in great chaos.
In the spring, second month, of the twelfth year
Guō Zǐxìng of Dìngyuǎn, with his associates Sūn Déyá and others, raised an army in Háozhōu.
The Yuán general Chèlíbùhuā was intimidated and dared not attack,
but daily captured good people to claim rewards.
Tàizǔ was twenty-five at the time.
He intended to avoid the war,
and consulted the gods with divination.
Both going and staying were inauspicious.
He then said:
"Could it be that I am destined to undertake a great enterprise?"
The divination was auspicious, and he was greatly pleased.
So, on the first day of the intercalary third month, Jiǎxū [April 15, 1352], he entered Háo and met Zǐxìng.
Zǐxìng was impressed by his appearance,
and kept him as a personal guard.
He won every battle.
Zǐxìng then gave him his adopted daughter, Miss Mǎ, in marriage,
who became Empress Gāo.
Zǐxìng and Déyá had disagreements,
and Tàizǔ repeatedly mediated and protected him.
In the autumn, ninth month [October 1352],
Yuán forces recaptured Xúzhōu.
Lǐ Èr fled and died,
Péng Dà and Zhào Jūnyòng fled to Háo,
and Déyá and others took them in.
Zǐxìng treated Péng Dà courteously but slighted Zhào Jūnyòng,
which caused Jūnyòng to resent him.
Déyá then plotted with him.
When Zǐxìng went out,
they seized and shackled him at Sūn's residence,
intending to kill him.
Tàizǔ was then in Huáiběi.
Hearing of the danger, he rushed back,
and pleaded with Péng Dà.
Péng Dà was furious,
called his soldiers, and set out.
Tàizǔ also donned armor and carried a shield,
broke into the house to free Zǐxìng,
smashed his shackles,
and had someone carry him back.
Thus, Zǐxìng was saved.
That winter
the Yuán general Jiǎ Lǔ besieged Háo.
Tàizǔ and Zǐxìng strenuously resisted him.
In the spring of the thirteenth year
Jiǎ Lǔ died,
and the siege was lifted.
Tàizǔ gathered seven hundred soldiers from the local area.
Zǐxìng was pleased
and appointed him as a zhènfǔ (pacification commissioner).
At this time, the troops of Péng and Zhào were unruly and abusive.
Zǐxìng was weak,
and Tàizǔ judged that he was not worth working with.
So he attached his troops to other generals,
and went alone with Xú Dá, Tāng Hé, Fèi Jù, and others to campaign south in Dìngyuǎn.
He planned to persuade three thousand militiamen from the Lǘpái Stockade to surrender,
and they went east together.
That night, they ambushed the Yuán general Zhāng Zhīyuàn at Héngjiàn Mountain,
and captured twenty thousand of his soldiers.
On the way, he met Lǐ Shàncháng of Dìngyuǎn.
He conversed with him and was greatly pleased,
so they together attacked Chúzhōu,
and captured it.
That year
Zhāng Shìchéng occupied Gāoyóu
and declared himself King Chéng.
In the winter, tenth month, of the fourteenth year [November 1354],
Yuán Chancellor Tuòtuò greatly defeated Shìchéng at Gāoyóu,
and detached troops to besiege Liùhé.
Tàizǔ said:
"If Liùhé falls,
Chú will also not be spared."
He and Gěng Zàichéng garrisoned Wǎliánglěi,
and went to relieve it.
They fought fiercely,
and protected the old and weak returning to Chú.
Soon after, large Yuán forces arrived
and attacked Chú.
Tàizǔ set ambushes and defeated them.
However, judging that the Yuán forces were strong and would return,
he returned the horses he had captured,
and sent elders with cattle and wine to thank the Yuán general, saying:
"We are defending the city against other bandits;
why should you abandon the great bandit and kill good people?"
The Yuán forces withdrew,
and the city was thus preserved.
After Tuòtuò defeated Shìchéng,
his military prestige greatly rose.
But he was soon slandered and suffered calumny,
and abruptly disbanded his troops.
The chaos in Jiāng and Huái intensified even more.
In the spring, first month of the fifteenth year,
Gūo Zǐxīng, using Tàizǔ's plan,
sent Zhāng Tiānyòu and others to capture Hézhōu.
He then issued a dispatch appointing Tàizǔ to command his army.
Tàizǔ, fearing that the various generals would not submit to each other,
kept the dispatch secret,
and scheduled a meeting in the main hall for the next day.
At that time, the right side of the seating was considered more honorable.
The generals entered first,
and all took seats on the right.
Tàizǔ deliberately arrived late and sat on the left.
When it came to handling affairs,
he made decisions swiftly and decisively,
leaving the assembled generals wide-eyed and speechless.
Only then did they gradually submit.
He proposed dividing the work of building a brick city wall,
setting a three-day deadline.
Tàizǔ completed his section on time,
while all the other generals were late.
Thereupon, he finally produced the dispatch,
and sitting facing south, said:
"By order, I am to command all your armies.
Now that you have all been late in building the brick wall,
what is to be done about military law?"
All the generals were greatly alarmed and apologized.
He then searched the army for women who had been plundered and released them to return home,
which greatly pleased the people.
The Yuán army of one hundred thousand attacked Hézhōu.
They resisted for three months,
and food was almost exhausted,
while Prince Tūjiān, Deputy Military Commissioner Bànzhùmǎ, and Civilian Militia Marshal Chén Yěxiān were separately stationed at Xīntáng, Gāowàng, and Jīlóng Shān to cut off the supply route.
Tàizǔ led his forces to defeat them,
and all the Yuán soldiers fled across the river.
In the third month,
Gūo Zǐxīng died.
At that time, Líu Fútōng welcomed and enthroned Hán Shāntóng's son, Lín’ér, in Bózhōu,
establishing the state of Sòng,
and instituting the era name Lóngfèng.
He issued a dispatch appointing Gūo Zǐxīng's son Tiānxù as Grand Marshal,
and Zhāng Tiānyòu and Tàizǔ as Left and Right Deputy Marshals.
Tàizǔ declared with emotion:
"How can a true man be subject to others?"
So he refused to accept the appointment.
However, considering that Lín’ér's power was strong and could be relied upon,
he used his era name to issue orders to the army.
In the summer, fourth month,
Cháng Yùchūn came and submitted.
In the fifth month,
Tàizǔ planned to cross the river,
but had no boats.
Just then, the Cháohú chiefs Líao Yǒng’ān and Yú Tōnghǎi came to join him with a thousand boats of naval forces.
Tàizǔ was greatly pleased,
and went to rally their troops.
But the Yuán Vice Censor Mánzǐ Hǎiyá blocked various passes such as Tóngchéngzhá and Mǎchánghé,
preventing the Cháohú fleet from moving out.
Suddenly, there was a heavy rain.
Tàizǔ happily exclaimed:
"Heaven helps me!"
So, taking advantage of the rising water, he sailed his boats back through a small creek,
and then attacked Hǎiyá at Yùxīkǒu,
utterly defeating him.
Thus, he decided on a plan to cross the river.
The generals asked to proceed directly to Jíqìng.
Tàizǔ said:
"To take Jíqìng, one must start from Cǎishí.
Cǎishí is a critical strategic point,
and its defenses are certainly strong.
Níuzhǔ faces the great river,
making it difficult for them to prepare defenses,
so it can surely be conquered."
On the Yǐmǎo day of the sixth month,
taking advantage of the wind, they hoisted sails
and arrived directly at Níuzhǔ.
Cháng Yùchūn was the first to land,
and captured it.
The Cǎishí forces also collapsed.
All the strongholds along the river submitted.
The generals, due to the famine in Hézhōu,
contended for provisions and planned to return.
Tàizǔ said to Xú Dá:
"Fortunately, we succeeded in crossing the river.
If we abandon it and return,
Jiāngdōng will not be ours."
He then cut all the boat cables,
and let them drift downstream in the swift current,
telling the generals:
"Tàipíng is very close;
we should take it together, gentlemen."
So they pressed on to victory and captured Tàipíng,
seizing the chiliarch Nàhāchū.
The intendant Jìn Yì jumped into the water and died.
Tàizǔ said:
"He is a righteous warrior,"
and buried him with honors.
He posted a proclamation prohibiting looting.
When a soldier violated the order,
he was beheaded as a warning to all,
and the army became solemn and orderly.
He changed the designation of lù (circuit) to fǔ (prefecture).
He established the Tàipíng Xīngguó Yì Yuánshuàifǔ (Prefectural Commandery of Tàipíng Xīngguó),
personally assuming the duties of marshal,
and summoned Táo Ān to serve in the staff headquarters,
appointing Lǐ Xí as prefect.
At that time, Tàipíng was surrounded by Yuán forces on all sides.
Right Chancellor Ālúhuī, Vice Censor Mánzǐ Hǎiyá, and others deployed a strong army to block Gūshúkǒu,
while Chén Yěxiān, the naval commander of Kāng Máocái, with tens of thousands of troops, attacked the city.
Tàizǔ sent Xú Dá, Dèng Yù, and Tāng Hé to meet them in battle,
while another general secretly went around to their rear,
attacking them from both sides.
They captured Yěxiān and accepted the surrender of his troops,
and Ālúhuī and others withdrew.
In the autumn, ninth month,
Gūo Tiānxù and Zhāng Tiānyòu attacked Jíqìng.
Yěxiān rebelled,
and both were killed in battle.
Thereupon, all of Zǐxīng's generals returned to Tàizǔ.
Yěxiān was soon killed by the civilian militia.
His nephew Zhào Xiān gathered his forces,
stationing them at Fāngshān,
and collaborating with Hǎiyá to keep watch over Tàipíng.
In the winter, twelfth month, on the Rénzǐ day,
Nàhāchū was released and returned north.
In the spring, second month of the sixteenth year, on the Bǐngzǐ day,
Hǎiyá was soundly defeated at Cǎishí.
In the third month, on the Guǐwèi day,
Jíqìng was attacked,
and Zhào Xiān was captured,
with his thirty-six thousand troops surrendering.
All of them were suspicious and fearful for their safety.
Tàizǔ selected five hundred brave and strong men to serve as his personal guards,
who disarmed and slept soundly until dawn,
and only then did the hearts of the troops become settled.
On the Gēngyín day,
the Yuán forces were again defeated at Jiǎngshān.
Yuán Imperial Censor Dàfū Fúshòu fought bravely and died in battle.
Mánzǐ Hǎiyá fled and returned to Zhāng Shìchéng,
and Kāng Máocái surrendered.
Tàizǔ entered the city,
and summoned all officials, elders, and fathers to instruct them, saying:
"The Yuán administration was corrupt and disturbing,
and conflicts arose everywhere.
I came to eliminate the chaos for the people;
let each of you dwell peacefully as before.
I will respectfully employ worthy scholars.
Inconvenient old policies will be abolished.
Officials must not be greedy or tyrannical and harm my people."
The people were then overjoyed beyond expectation.
He changed Jíqìng Lù to Yìngtiān Fǔ,
and recruited more than ten people including Xià Yù, Sūn Yán, and Yáng Xiàn.
He buried Imperial Censor Dàfū Fúshòu to commend his loyalty.
At this time,
the Yuán general Dìngdìng held Zhènjiāng,
Biébùhuá and Yáng Zhòngyīng were stationed at Níngguó,
the Qīngyī army of Zhāng Míngjiàn occupied Yángzhōu,
Bāsī’ěrbùhuā was stationed at Huīzhōu,
Shímò Yísūn guarded Chǔzhōu,
his brother Hòusūn guarded Wùzhōu,
Sòng Báiyánbùhuā guarded Qúzhōu,
and Chízhōu was already occupied by Xú Shòuhuī's general.
Zhāng Shìchéng had seized Píngjiāng from Huáidōng,
and then plundered Zhèxī.
After Tàizǔ secured Jíqìng,
he feared that Shìchéng and Shòuhuī were strong,
and that the various commanderies of Jiāngzuǒ and Zhèyòu would be annexed by them.
Therefore, he sent Xú Dá to attack Zhènjiāng,
and captured it.
Dìngdìng died in battle.
In the summer, sixth month,
Dèng Yù conquered Guǎngdé.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the Jǐmǎo day,
the generals enthroned Tàizǔ as Wú Guógōng.
He established the Jiāngnán Xíng Zhōngshūshěng (Branch Secretariat of Jiāngnán),
personally overseeing its affairs,
and appointed officials.
He sent a letter to Zhāng Shìchéng,
but Shìchéng did not reply,
and instead led his troops to attack Zhènjiāng.
Xú Dá defeated him,
and then advanced to besiege Chángzhōu,
but could not take it.
In the ninth month, on the Wùyín day,
he went to Zhènjiāng,
and visited the Temple of Confucius.
He sent scholars to instruct the elders and fathers,
encouraging agriculture and sericulture,
then soon returned to Yìngtiān.
In the spring, second month of the seventeenth year,
Gěng Bǐngwén conquered Chángxīng.
In the third month,
Xú Dá conquered Chángzhōu.
In the summer, fourth month, on the Dīngmǎo day,
he personally led an attack on Níngguó,
and captured it,
with Biébùhuá surrendering.
In the fifth month,
Shàngyuán, Níngguó, and Jùróng presented auspicious wheat.
In the sixth month,
Zhào Jìzǔ conquered Jiāngyīn.
In the autumn, seventh month,
Xú Dá (徐達) captured Chángshú (常熟).
Hú Dàhǎi (胡大海) captured Huīzhōu (徽州),
and Bāsī'ěrbùhuā (八思爾不花) fled.
In the winter, tenth month,
Cháng Yùchūn (常遇春) captured Chízhōu (池州).
Miáo Dàhēng (繆大亨) captured Yángzhōu (揚州),
and Zhāng Míngjiàn (張明鑑) surrendered.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jǐchǒu (己丑),
prisoners were released.
In this year,
Xú Shòuhuī’s (徐壽輝) general Míng Yùzhēn (明玉珍) occupied Chóngqìng Lù (重慶路).
In the eighteenth year, spring, second month, on the day Yǐhài (乙亥),
Kāng Màocái (康茂才) was made Superintendent of Military Colonies.
In the third month, on the day Jǐyǒu (己酉),
prisoners were reviewed.
Dèng Yù (鄧愈) captured Jiàndé Lù (建德路).
In the summer, fourth month,
Xú Shòuhuī’s (徐壽輝) general Chén Yǒuliàng (陳友諒) sent Zhào Pǔshèng (趙普勝) to seize Chízhōu (池州).
In this month,
Yǒuliàng (友諒) occupied Lóngxīng Lù (龍興路).
In the fifth month,
Liú Fútōng (劉福通) breached Biànliáng (汴梁),
and welcomed Hán Lín'ér (韓林兒) to make it his capital.
Initially,
Fútōng (福通) sent generals in various directions,
who conquered Shāndōng (山東),
raided Qín (秦) and Jìn (晉),
and plundered Yōu (幽) and Jì (薊).
The Central Plains were in great chaos,
which allowed Tàizǔ (太祖) to gradually pacify the regions south of the Yangtze River.
Wherever he went, he did not kill indiscriminately,
and he recruited talented individuals,
thus gaining the people's allegiance day by day.
In the winter, twelfth month,
Hú Dàhǎi (胡大海) attacked Wùzhōu (婺州).
As it did not fall for a long time,
Tàizǔ (太祖) personally led troops to attack it.
Shímò Yísūn (石抹宜孫) sent a general with chariots from Sōngxī (松溪) to reinforce.
Tàizǔ (太祖) said:
"The road is narrow,
chariot warfare will only lead to defeat."
He ordered Hú Déjì (胡德濟) to engage them in battle at Méihuā Mén (梅花門),
where they were utterly defeated.
Wùzhōu (婺州) surrendered,
and Hòusūn (厚孫) was captured.
The day before,
the people in the city saw a five-colored cloud like a carriage canopy west of the city,
considering it an omen.
It was only then that they knew it was where Tàizǔ (太祖) had stationed his troops.
Upon entering the city,
he distributed grain to aid the poor citizens,
and renamed the prefecture Níngchéng Fǔ (寧城府).
He appointed Fàn Zǔgàn (范祖幹), Yè Yí (葉儀), Xǔ Yuán (許元), and ten other individuals,
to take turns lecturing on classics and history.
On the day Wùzǐ (戊子),
an envoy was sent to summon and admonish Fāng Guózhēn (方國珍).
In the nineteenth year, spring, first month, on the day Yǐsì (乙巳),
Tàizǔ (太祖) planned to capture the remaining prefectures in Zhèdōng (浙東).
He admonished his generals, saying:
"Capture cities with military might,
but pacify chaos with benevolence.
When I entered Jíqìng (集慶),
I did not harm a single person or thing,
which is why it was settled in one fell swoop.
Every time I hear that my generals capture a city without indiscriminate killing,
I am overjoyed.
An army on the march is like fire;
if not restrained, it will spread to consume the plains.
For a general to wield not killing as military might,
not only benefits the state,
but also truly blesses his descendants."
On the day Gēngshēn (庚申),
Hú Dàhǎi (胡大海) captured Zhūjì (諸暨).
In this month,
Wáng Zōngxiǎn (王宗顯), the Zhīfǔ (知府) of Níngyuè (寧越), was ordered to establish a prefectural school.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎwǔ (甲午),
a general amnesty was granted for crimes of grand treason and below.
On the day Dīngsì (丁巳),
Fāng Guózhēn (方國珍) offered Wēn (溫), Tái (台), and Qìngyuán (慶元),
and sent his son Guān (關) as a hostage,
but it was not accepted.
In the summer, fourth month,
Yú Tōnghǎi (俞通海) and others recaptured Chízhōu (池州).
At this time, Gěng Bǐngwén (耿炳文) defended Chángxīng (長興),
Wú Liáng (吳良) defended Jiāngyīn (江陰),
and Tāng Hé (湯和) defended Chángzhōu (常州);
all repeatedly defeated Shìchéng’s (士誠) forces.
For this reason, Tàizǔ (太祖) remained in Níngyuè (寧越) for a long time,
campaigning in Zhèdōng (浙東).
In the sixth month, on the day Rénxū (壬戌),
he returned to Yìngtiān (應天).
In the autumn, eighth month,
Yuán (元) Cháhàn Tiēmù'ér (察罕帖木兒) recaptured Biànliáng (汴梁).
Fútōng (福通) withdrew with Lín'ér (林兒) to secure Ānfēng (安豐).
In the ninth month,
Cháng Yùchūn (常遇春) captured Qúzhōu (衢州),
and captured Sòng Bóyánbùhuā (宋伯顏不花).
In the winter, tenth month,
Xià Yù (夏煜) was sent to confer Fāng Guózhēn (方國珍) with the title Xíngshěng Píngzhāng (行省平章),
but Guózhēn (國珍) declined due to illness.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rén Yín (壬寅),
Hú Dàhǎi (胡大海) captured Chǔzhōu (處州),
and Shímò Yísūn (石抹宜孫) fled.
At this time, the Yuán (元) defending forces were few and weak,
and hearing of the chaos in the Central Plains,
people's hearts were scattered.
Thus, all the prefectures in Jiāngzuǒ (江左) and Zhèyòu (浙右) surrendered as soon as troops arrived,
and thus bordered Yǒuliàng (友諒) to the west.
In the twentieth year, spring, second month,
Yuán (元) Fújiàn Xíngshěng Cānzhèng (福建行省參政) Yuán Tiānlù (袁天祿) surrendered Fúníng (福寧).
In the third month, on the day Wùzǐ (戊子),
Liú Jī (劉基), Sòng Lián (宋濂), Zhāng Yì (章溢), and Yè Chēn (葉琛) were summoned.
In the summer, fifth month,
Xú Dá (徐達) and Cháng Yùchūn (常遇春) defeated Chén Yǒuliàng (陳友諒) at Chízhōu (池州).
In the intercalary month, on the day Bǐngchén (丙辰),
Yǒuliàng (友諒) seized Tàipíng (太平).
The defending general Zhū Wénxùn (朱文遜),
Court Administrator Huā Yún (花雲) and Wáng Dǐng (王鼎),
and Zhīfǔ (知府) Xǔ Yuàn (許瑗) died there.
Soon after,
Yǒuliàng (友諒) assassinated his lord Xú Shòuhuī (徐壽輝),
declared himself Emperor,
named his state Hàn (漢),
and took control of all of Jiāngxī (江西) and Húguǎng (湖廣).
He allied with Shìchéng (士誠) to jointly attack Yìngtiān (應天),
causing great alarm in Yìngtiān (應天).
The generals discussed first recapturing Tàipíng (太平) to tie him down.
Tàizǔ (太祖) said:
"No.
He is upstream,
and his fleet is ten times ours;
it will be difficult to recapture it quickly."
Someone suggested he personally lead the charge to engage them.
Tàizǔ (太祖) said:
"No.
If he uses a detachment to tie us down,
and his main army heads to Jīnlíng (金陵),
they can arrive in half a day by river.
Our infantry and cavalry will be hard-pressed to return quickly,
and fighting after a hundred-li march
is forbidden in military strategy;
it is not a good plan."
He then swiftly ordered Hú Dàhǎi (胡大海) to attack Xìnzhōu (信州) to distract him from behind,
and instructed Kāng Màocái (康茂才) to deceive Yǒuliàng (友諒) with a letter,
urging him to come quickly.
Yǒuliàng (友諒) indeed led his troops eastward.
Thereupon, Cháng Yùchūn (常遇春) ambushed at Shíhuī Shān (石灰山),
Xú Dá (徐達) arrayed his troops outside the South Gate,
Yáng Jǐng (楊璟) garrisoned Dàshèng Gǎng (大勝港),
Zhāng Déshèng (張德勝) and others led the fleet out of Lóngjiāng Guān (龍江關),
and Tàizǔ (太祖) personally supervised the army at Lúlóng Shān (盧龍山).
On the day Yǐchǒu (乙丑),
Yǒuliàng (友諒) arrived at Lóngwān (龍灣).
The troops wanted to fight,
but Tàizǔ (太祖) said:
"It will rain soon;
quickly eat,
and attack them during the rain."
In a short while,
it indeed rained heavily.
The soldiers fought with enthusiasm.
When the rain stopped, they engaged in battle,
attacking from both land and water,
and utterly defeated them.
Yǒuliàng (友諒) escaped on a separate boat.
Tàipíng (太平) was then recaptured,
Ānqìng (安慶) was taken,
and Dàhǎi (大海) also captured Xìnzhōu (信州).
Earlier,
when Tàizǔ (太祖) ordered Màocái (茂才) to deceive Yǒuliàng (友諒),
Lǐ Shàncháng (李善長) expressed doubt.
Tàizǔ (太祖) said:
"If the two bandits unite,
we will be attacked from both front and rear.
Only by making him come quickly and defeating him first,
will Shìchéng (士誠) lose heart."
Afterwards, Shìchéng’s (士誠) troops indeed did not come out.
On the day Dīngmǎo (丁卯),
the Rúxué Tíju Sī (儒學提舉司) was established,
with Sòng Lián (宋濂) as its Tíju (提舉).
His son Biāo (標) was sent to study the classics.
In the sixth month,
Gěng Zàichéng (耿再成) defeated Shímò Yísūn (石抹宜孫) at Qìngyuán (慶元).
Yísūn (宜孫) died in battle,
and an envoy was sent to offer sacrifices to him.
In the autumn, ninth month,
Xú Shòuhuī’s (徐壽輝) former general Ōu Pǔxiáng (歐普祥) surrendered Yuánzhōu (袁州).
In the winter, twelfth month,
Xià Yù (夏煜) was again sent with a letter to admonish Guózhēn (國珍).
In the spring, second month, *jiǎshēn* day of the twenty-first year (1361),
a salt and tea tax was established.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Báoyuán Bureau was set up.
In the third month, *dīngchǒu* day,
the Pīmì Yuàn was reformed into the Dàdūdū Fǔ.
Yuán general Xuē Xiǎn surrendered Sīzhōu.
On the *wùyín* day,
Guózhēn sent an envoy to express gratitude,
offering a saddle adorned with gold and jade.
It was refused, with the statement:
"Currently, we have matters in the four directions;
what we need are talented individuals,
and what we use are grain and silk.
Precious trinkets are not what I desire."
In the autumn, seventh month,
Yǒuliàng's general Zhāng Dìngbiān captured Ānqìng.
In the eighth month,
an envoy was sent to the Yuán Píngzhāng Cháhǎn Tiēmù'ér.
At that time, Cháhǎn had pacified Shāndōng,
forced Tián Fēng to surrender,
and his military reputation greatly flourished.
Therefore, Tàizǔ sought to establish good relations with him.
It happened that Cháhǎn was then attacking Yìdū and had not yet captured it,
so Tàizǔ personally led a naval force to campaign against Chén Yǒuliàng.
On the *wùxū* day,
Ānqìng was captured,
and Yǒuliàng's generals Dīng Pǔláng and Fù Yǒudé welcomed the surrender.
On the *rényín* day,
he reached Húkǒu,
pursued and defeated Yǒuliàng at Jiāngzhōu,
and captured its city.
Yǒuliàng fled to Wǔchāng.
He then dispatched forces to conquer Nánkāng, Jiànchāng, Ráo, Qí, Huáng, and Guǎngjì, all of which fell.
In the winter, eleventh month, *jǐwèi* day,
Fǔzhōu was captured.
In the spring, first month of the twenty-second year (1362),
Yǒuliàng's Jiāngxī Xíngshěng Chéngxiàng Hú Tíngruì surrendered Lóngxīng.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
he went to Lóngxīng,
which was renamed Hóngdū Fǔ.
He paid respects at the Confucian Temple.
He issued a proclamation to the elders,
abolishing Chén's harsh policies,
ending various military levies,
and providing relief to the poor and helpless.
The people were greatly pleased.
Yuán, Ruì, Línjiāng, and Jí'ān successively fell.
In the second month,
he returned to Yìngtiān.
Dèng Yù was left to guard Hóngdū.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the surrendered man Jiǎng Yīng killed Hú Dàhǎi, the defending general of Jīnhuá,
and Lángzhōng Wáng Kǎi died with him.
Yīng rebelled and defected to Zhāng Shìchéng.
Lǐ Yòuzhī, a surrendered man from Chǔzhōu, heard of the change,
and also killed Gěng Zàichéng, the Pàn of the Xíng Pīmì Yuàn, in rebellion.
Dūshì Sūn Yán, Zhīfǔ Wáng Dàotóng, and Yuánshuài Zhū Wéngāng died with him.
In the third month, *guǐhài* day,
the surrendered men Zhù Zōng and Kāng Tài rebelled,
capturing Hóngdū.
Dèng Yù fled to Yìngtiān,
and Zhīfǔ Yè Chēn and Dūshì Wàn Sīchéng died with him.
In this month,
Míng Yùzhēn proclaimed himself emperor in Chóngqìng,
naming his state Xià.
In the summer, fourth month, *jǐmǎo* day,
Shào Róng recaptured Chǔzhōu.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Xú Dá recaptured Hóngdū.
In the fifth month, *bǐngwǔ* day,
Zhū Wénzhèng, Zhào Déshèng, and Dèng Yù garrisoned Hóngdū.
In the sixth month, *wùyín* day,
Cháhǎn sent a letter in response,
detaining our envoy and not sending him back.
Cháhǎn was subsequently killed by Tián Fēng.
In the autumn, seventh month, *bǐngchén* day,
Píngzhāng Shào Róng and Cānzhèng Zhào Jìzǔ conspired in rebellion,
and were executed.
In the winter, twelfth month,
the Yuán sent Shàngshū Zhāng Chǎng by sea to Qìngyuán,
offering Tàizǔ the title of Jiāngxī Xíngshěng Píngzhāng Zhèngshì,
which he did not accept.
Cháhǎn's son Kuòkuò Tiēmù'ér sent a letter returning the envoy.
In the spring, first month, *bǐngyín* day of the twenty-third year (1363),
Wāng Hé was sent to respond to him.
In the second month, *rénshēn* day,
soldiers were ordered to cultivate fields and store grain.
In this month,
Yǒuliàng's general Zhāng Dìngbiān captured Ráozhōu.
Shìchéng's general Lǚ Zhēn defeated Ānfēng,
killing Liú Fútōng.
In the third month, *xīnchǒu* day,
Tàizǔ personally led troops to relieve Ānfēng.
Zhēn was defeated and fled.
Hán Lín'ér was brought back to Chúzhōu,
and then Tàizǔ returned to Yìngtiān.
In the summer, fourth month, *rénxū* day,
Yǒuliàng mustered a large army and besieged Hóngdū.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Xiè Zàixīng, the defending general of Zhūquán, rebelled
and defected to Shìchéng.
In the fifth month,
the Lǐxián Guǎn was built.
Yǒuliàng divided his forces and captured Jí'ān,
where Cānzhèng Liú Qí
and Zhīfǔ Zhū Shúhuá died.
He captured Línjiāng,
where Tóngzhī Zhào Tiānlín died.
He captured Wúwéi Zhōu,
where Zhīzhōu Dǒng Zēng died.
In the autumn, seventh month, *guǐyǒu* day,
Tàizǔ personally led troops to relieve Hóngdū.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
he reached Húkǒu.
He first laid ambushes at Jīngjiāng Kǒu and Nánhúzī,
blocking Yǒuliàng's return route,
and ordered the Xìnzhōu troops to guard Wǔyáng Dù.
When Yǒuliàng heard that Tàizǔ had arrived,
he lifted the siege
and engaged in battle at Póyáng Hú.
Yǒuliàng's army numbered 600,000,
linking giant ships into a formation,
with towers and turrets over ten *zhàng* high,
stretching for dozens of *lǐ*.
Banners, flags, spears, and shields
made them look like a mountain from afar.
On the *dīnghài* day,
they met at Kāngláng Shān.
Tàizǔ divided his army into eleven divisions to resist them.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
they joined battle.
Xú Dá attacked their vanguard,
and Yú Tōnghǎi used fire cannons to burn dozens of their ships,
with roughly equal casualties on both sides.
Yǒuliàng's fierce general Zhāng Dìngbiān directly attacked Tàizǔ's ship.
The ship was stuck in the sand
and could not retreat,
being in extreme danger.
Cháng Yùchūn shot and wounded Dìngbiān from the side.
Tōnghǎi then came to reinforce,
and as the ship swiftly moved forward, water surged,
allowing Tàizǔ's ship to escape.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Yǒuliàng brought out all his giant ships to battle.
The generals' ships were small,
making an uphill assault disadvantageous,
and they showed fear.
Tàizǔ personally waved them forward.
When they did not advance,
he beheaded over ten who retreated,
and everyone then fought desperately.
At dusk,
a strong wind arose from the northeast.
He then ordered brave suicide squads to operate seven ships,
filled with gunpowder and reeds,
and set fire to Yǒuliàng's ships.
The wind was fierce and the fire intense,
smoke and flames filled the sky,
and the lake water turned entirely red.
Yǒuliàng's army fell into great disarray.
The generals beat drums and shouted, pressing the attack,
beheading over two thousand and
countless others who were burned or drowned.
Yǒuliàng's morale was broken.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
they battled again,
and Yǒuliàng was again greatly defeated.
Thereupon, he gathered his ships and defended himself,
not daring to fight again.
On the *rénchén* day,
Tàizǔ moved his forces to block Zuǒlí,
and Yǒuliàng also retreated to defend Zhǔjī.
After a three-day standoff,
both of his Left and Right Jīnwú Generals surrendered.
Yǒuliàng's situation became increasingly dire,
and he was extremely enraged,
killing all the captured generals and soldiers.
Tàizǔ, however, returned all the captives,
treated the wounded with good medicine,
and offered sacrifices to the relatives of his generals who had died in battle.
In the eighth month, *rénxū* day,
Yǒuliàng ran out of food and
rushed towards Nánhúzī,
where he was blocked by the Nánhú army.
He then broke through to Húkǒu.
Tàizǔ intercepted him,
fighting downstream
to Jīngjiāng.
The Jīngjiāng army again intercepted and attacked him,
and Yǒuliàng was killed by a stray arrow.
Zhāng Dìngbiān fled to Wǔchāng with Yǒuliàng's son, Lǐ.
In the ninth month,
he returned to Yìngtiān
to reward those with meritorious service.
Earlier,
Tàizǔ had gone to rescue Ānfēng,
but Liú Jī's remonstrance was not heeded.
Now, he said to Jī:
"I should not have undertaken the expedition to Ānfēng.
Had Yǒu Liàng seized the opportunity to strike directly at Yìngtiān,
the great endeavor would have been lost.
Instead, he halted his troops at Nánchāng;
what else could be expected but his downfall?
With Yǒu Liàng vanquished,
securing the realm will not be difficult."
On the day of Rénwǔ,
he personally led an expedition against Chén Lǐ.
In this month,
Zhāng Shìchéng declared himself King of Wú.
In winter, on the Rén Yín day of the tenth month,
he besieged Wǔchāng
and divided his forces to subdue various routes in Húběi,
all of which surrendered.
On the Bǐng Shēn day of the twelfth month,
he returned to Yìngtiān,
leaving Cháng Yùchūn to oversee the various armies.
In the twenty-fourth year, on the Bǐng Yín day, the first day of the first month of spring,
Lǐ Shàncháng and others led the officials to urge him to ascend the throne,
but he refused.
After persistent pleas,
he then assumed the title of King of Wú.
He established a bureaucracy.
He appointed Shàncháng as Right Prime Minister,
Xú Dá as Left Prime Minister,
and Cháng Yùchūn and Yú Tōnghǎi as Administrators of Governmental Affairs.
He instructed them, saying:
"At the beginning of establishing a nation,
the fundamental principles must first be rectified.
The Yuán dynasty was dark and weak,
its authority and power devolved downwards,
gradually leading to chaos.
Now, we should learn from this."
He established his son Biāo as the Crown Prince.
On the Yǐ Wèi day of the second month,
he again personally led an expedition against Wǔchāng.
Chén Lǐ surrendered,
and Hán, Miǎn, Jīng, and Yuè all submitted.
On the Yǐ Chǒu day of the third month,
he returned to Yìngtiān.
On the Dīng Mǎo day,
he established the Office of the Diarist.
On the Gēng Wǔ day,
he abolished the various Wing Commanderies,
and established seventeen Commands of the Imperial Guards.
He ordered the Central Secretariat to recruit civil and military talents.
In summer, the fourth month,
he built shrines
to sacrifice to Dīng Pǔláng and others who died in service at Kāngláng Shān,
and to Zhào Déshèng and others at Nánchāng.
In autumn, on the Dīng Chǒu day of the seventh month,
Xú Dá captured Lúzhōu.
On the Wù Yín day,
Cháng Yùchūn campaigned in Jiāngxī.
On the Wù Xū day of the eighth month,
Jí'ān was recovered,
and then Gànzhōu was besieged.
Dá campaigned through the various routes of Jīng and Xiāng.
On the Jiǎ Shēn day of the ninth month,
Jiānglíng was captured,
and Yílíng, Tán, and Guī all surrendered.
In winter, on the Gēng Yín day of the twelfth month,
Dá captured Chénzhōu,
and dispatched a separate general to take Héngzhōu.
In the twenty-fifth year, on the Jǐ Sì day of the first month of spring,
Xú Dá captured Bǎoqìng,
and Húxiāng was pacified.
Cháng Yùchūn captured Gànzhōu,
and Xióng Tiānruì surrendered.
He then advanced to Nán'ān,
recruiting and pacifying various routes in Lǐngnán,
and captured Sháozhōu and Nánxióng.
On the Jiǎ Shēn day,
he went to Nánchāng,
arrested Grand Commander Zhū Wénzhèng and returned,
enumerated his crimes,
and placed him under house arrest in Tóngchéng.
On the Jǐ Chǒu day of the second month,
Chén Yǒudìng, Administrator of Governmental Affairs for Fújiàn Province, invaded Chǔzhōu.
Staff Officer Hú Shēn defeated him,
and then captured Pǔchéng.
On the Bǐng Wǔ day,
Shìchéng's general Lǐ Bóshēng attacked the new city of Zhūquán.
Lǐ Wénzhōng thoroughly defeated him.
In summer, on the Gēng Yín day of the fourth month,
Cháng Yùchūn campaigned through the various routes of Xiāng and Hàn.
On the Yǐ Hài day of the fifth month,
he captured Ānlù.
On the Jǐ Mǎo day,
he captured Xiāngyáng.
On the Rén Zǐ day of the sixth month,
Zhū Liàngzǔ and Hú Shēn attacked Jiànníng.
They fought beneath the city walls;
Shēn was captured
and died.
In autumn, the seventh month,
he ordered that soldiers who had crossed the river and suffered wounds or debilitating illnesses be cared for,
and their wives and children supported if they died.
On the Bǐng Chén day of the ninth month,
he established the National Academy.
In winter, on the Wù Xū day of the tenth month,
he issued an order to attack Zhāng Shìchéng.
At this time,
Shìchéng's territory
extended south to Shàoxīng,
and north it included Tōng, Tài, Gāoyóu, Huái'ān, Háo, and Sì,
and further north to Jìníng.
He then ordered Xú Dá, Cháng Yùchūn, and others to first plan the capture of Huáidōng.
In the intercalary month,
they besieged Táizhōu
and captured it.
In the eleventh month,
Zhāng Shìchéng raided Yíxīng.
Xú Dá defeated him,
and then returned from Yíxīng to attack Gāoyóu.
In the twenty-sixth year, on the Guǐ Wèi day of the first month of spring,
Shìchéng spied on Jiāngyīn.
Tàizǔ personally led troops to relieve it;
Shìchéng fled,
and Kāng Màocái pursued and defeated him at Fúzǐ Mén.
Tàizǔ returned to Yìngtiān.
In the second month,
Míng Yùzhēn died,
and his son Shēng declared himself ruler.
On the Bǐng Shēn day of the third month,
he ordered the Central Secretariat to rigorously select officials.
Xú Dá captured Gāoyóu.
In summer, on the Yǐ Mǎo day of the fourth month,
he launched a surprise attack and defeated Shìchéng's general Xú Yì's navy at Huái'ān.
Yì fled,
and Méi Sīzǔ surrendered the city.
Háo, Xú, and Sù prefectures subsequently surrendered,
and Huáidōng was pacified.
On the Jiǎ Zǐ day,
he went to Háozhōu to visit his ancestors' tombs,
established twenty families to guard the tombs,
and bestowed grain and silk upon old acquaintances Wāng Wén and Liú Yīng.
He hosted a banquet and invited the elders to drink with great joy,
saying:
"I have been away from my hometown for more than ten years,
enduring hardships and hundreds of battles,
before I could return to visit my ancestral tombs
and reunite with the elders and young men.
Now, I regret that I cannot stay long to enjoy this joyful gathering.
Elders, please instruct your sons and brothers to be filial, fraternal, and diligent in farming.
Do not travel far to trade.
The prefectures and counties along the Huái River still suffer from banditry and plunder.
Elders, please take good care of yourselves."
He ordered the relevant authorities to abolish their taxes and levies,
and they all bowed their heads in thanks.
On the Xīn Wèi day,
Xú Dá captured Ānfēng,
and divided his troops to defeat Kuòkuò at Xúzhōu.
In summer, on the Rén Wǔ day of the fifth month,
he arrived from Háo.
On the Gēng Yín day,
he sought out lost writings.
In autumn, on the Gēng Xū day of the eighth month,
he began rebuilding the city of Yìngtiān
and constructing a new palace on the southern side of Zhōng Shān.
On the Xīn Hài day,
he appointed Xú Dá as Commander-in-Chief,
and Cháng Yùchūn as Vice Commander-in-Chief,
to lead an army of 200,000 to attack Zhāng Shìchéng.
He made an oath to the army at the Jǐmén Gate, saying:
"On the day the city falls,
do not kill or plunder,
do not destroy houses,
and do not disturb graves.
Shìchéng's mother is buried outside Píngjiāng city;
do not invade or destroy her tomb."
Afterwards, he summoned and asked Dá and Yùchūn what should be attacked first in the military campaign.
Yùchūn wanted to strike directly at Píngjiāng.
Tàizǔ said:
"Zhāng Tiānqí of Húzhōu and Pān Yuánmíng of Hángzhōu are Shìchéng's arms and fingers.
If Píngjiāng is hard-pressed,
these two will exert all their strength to rush to its aid,
making victory difficult to achieve.
It would be better to first attack Húzhōu,
making them exhaust themselves in constant relief efforts.
Once his wings are broken,
Píngjiāng will be isolated,
and can be swiftly taken."
On the Jiǎ Xū day,
he defeated Zhāng Tiānqí at Húzhōu.
Shìchéng personally led troops to relieve it,
but was again defeated at Zàolín.
On the Yǐ Wèi day of the ninth month,
Lǐ Wénzhōng attacked Hángzhōu.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Cháng Yùchūn defeated Shìchéng's troops at Wūzhèn.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Zhāng Tiānqí surrendered.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Lǐ Wénzhōng captured Yúháng,
Pān Yuánmíng surrendered,
and the surrounding commanderies all fell.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Píngjiāng was besieged.
In the twelfth month,
Hán Lín'ér died.
The next year was designated the first year of Wú.
Temples, altars, and palaces were built,
and sacrifices were offered to mountains and rivers.
The officials presented palace blueprints,
but he ordered the removal of overly ornate and extravagant designs.
This year,
Kuòkuò Tièmù'ér of the Yuán quarreled with Lǐ Sīqí and Zhāng Liángbì,
attacking each other repeatedly,
and imperial orders were not enforced,
further distressing the people of the Central Plains.
In the twenty-seventh year, spring, first month, on the day Wùxū,
an edict was issued to the Central Secretariat, saying:
"The southeast has long suffered from war,
and the people's lives are in decline.
I deeply pity them.
Moreover, the commanderies of Tàipíng and Yìngtiān
were the lands I opened up after crossing the river,
and they have long endured the burden of tribute and labor.
Now, with every household empty,
officials are urgently collecting taxes,
further afflicting my people.
How can this be endured?
Therefore, grant Tàipíng a two-year exemption from land tax,
and Yìngtiān, Zhènjiāng, Níngguó, and Guǎngdé each a one-year exemption."
In the second month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Fù Yǒudé defeated Lǐ Èr, a general of Kuòkuò, at Xúzhōu,
and captured him.
In the third month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
civil and military examinations for selecting officials were first established.
In the summer, fourth month,
Fāng Guózhēn secretly sent people to communicate with Kuòkuò and Chén Yǒudìng,
and a letter was dispatched to reprimand him.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐhài,
the Hànlín Academy was first established.
This month,
due to drought, meals were reduced to a vegetarian diet,
and Xú, Sù, Háo, Sì, Shòu, Pī, Dōnghǎi, Āndōng, Xiāngyáng, Ānlù, and newly annexed territories were granted a three-year exemption from land tax.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùchén,
there was heavy rain.
The assembled officials requested the restoration of normal meals.
Tàizǔ said:
"Although it has rained,
much of the grain has already been damaged.
Therefore, grant the people a one-year exemption from land tax for this year."
On the day Guǐyǒu,
an order was issued to discontinue female entertainers during court greetings.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
officials of prefectures, departments, and counties were given travel expenses upon assuming office,
and brocade and silk were bestowed upon their parents, wives, and eldest sons, with varying amounts,
which was established as a regulation.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
thunder struck the beast-head decoration on the palace gate,
and a general pardon was issued for criminals.
On the day Gēngyín,
envoys were dispatched to demand grain tribute from Fāng Guózhēn.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
the Circular Mound Altar, the Square Mound Altar, and the Altars of Land and Grain were completed.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed.
Zhū Liàngzǔ led an army to attack Guózhēn.
On the day Wùyín,
an imperial edict stated:
"The policies of the former kings stipulated that
punishment should not extend to wives and children.
From now on, except for high treason and outrageous acts,
the practice of collective punishment shall be abolished."
On the day Xīnsì,
Xú Dá captured Píngjiāng,
seized Shìchéng,
and the Wú territory was pacified.
On the day Wùxū,
envoys were dispatched to send a letter to the Yuán ruler,
returning their imperial clan member, Prince Shénbǎo, and others to the north.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the merits of pacifying Wú were assessed.
Lǐ Shàncháng was enfeoffed as Xuānguó Gōng,
Xú Dá as Xìnguó Gōng,
Cháng Yùchūn as Èguó Gōng,
and generals and soldiers were rewarded with varying amounts.
Zhū Liàngzǔ captured Táizhōu.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the new palace was completed.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Wu Lín and Wèi Guān, recorders of court activities, were sent with gifts to seek talented individuals from all directions.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
it was ordered that in official ceremonies, the left side should be honored.
Lǐ Shàncháng was redesignated as Left Grand Councilor,
and Xú Dá as Right Grand Councilor.
On the day Xīnhài,
sacrifices were offered to the Yuán minister Yú Quē in Ānqìng,
and to Lǐ Fǔ in Jiāngzhōu.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Censorate was established.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Tāng Hé was made General-in-Chief for the Suppression of the South,
with Wú Zhēn as his deputy,
to attack Guózhēn.
On the day Jiǎyín,
laws and statutes were codified.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the ceremonial music for suburban sacrifices and the Imperial Ancestral Temple was standardized.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the generals were summoned to discuss the northern expedition.
Tàizǔ said:
"In Shāndōng, Wáng Xuān is wavering;
in Hénán, Kuòkuò is arrogant;
in Guān and Lǒng, Lǐ Sīqí and Zhāng Sīdào are ambitious and suspicious.
The Yuán dynasty is about to perish,
and the Central Plains are in great misery.
Now we are about to launch a northern expedition
to save the people from dire suffering.
How shall we achieve victory?"
Yùchūn replied:
"With our army, seasoned by a hundred battles,
to face their troops, long accustomed to ease,
we shall strike directly at the Yuán capital,
like splitting bamboo."
Tàizǔ said:
"The Yuán established their state a hundred years ago;
their defenses must be strong.
If we march deep with an isolated army,
and provisions cannot keep up,
and relief forces gather from all sides,
it will be a perilous path.
I wish to first take Shāndōng,
removing their shield;
then move our troops to the two Hés (Hénán and Héběi),
breaking their fences;
capture and hold Tóngguān,
blocking their gateway.
The strategic advantage of the realm will then be in our grasp.
Then, when we advance our troops,
the Yuán capital, isolated and without reinforcements,
will fall without a fight.
We can then advance westward,
and Yúnzhōng, Jiǔyuán, Guān, and Lǒng can be swept away."
All the generals said,
"Excellent."
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Xú Dá was made General-in-Chief for Conquering the North,
and Cháng Yùchūn his deputy general,
leading an army of two hundred and fifty thousand,
to proceed from the Huái River into the Yellow River,
and conquer the Central Plains to the north.
Hú Tíngruì was made General-in-Chief for the Suppression of the South,
with Hé Wénhuī as his deputy general,
to conquer Fújiàn.
Yáng Jǐng, administrator of the Húguǎng Provincial Secretariat, Zhōu Déxīng, Left Assistant Administrator, and Zhāng Bīn, Policy Councilor, were to conquer Guǎngxī.
On the day Jǐsì,
Zhū Liàngzǔ captured Wēnzhōu.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
Tāng Hé captured Qìngyuán,
and Fāng Guózhēn fled into the sea.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Xú Dá captured Yízhōu,
and beheaded Wáng Xuān.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Liáo Yǒngzhōng was made Deputy General-in-Chief for the Suppression of the South,
to join Hé (Tāng Hé) by sea in attacking Guózhēn.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Dàtǒng Calendar was promulgated.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Xú Dá captured Yìdū.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
the laws and statutes were promulgated.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Fāng Guózhēn surrendered,
and eastern Zhè was pacified.
Zhāng Xīngzǔ captured Dōngpíng,
and the prefectures and counties east of Yǎn (Yǎnzhōu) surrendered one after another.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Xú Dá captured Jǐnán.
Hú Tíngruì captured Shàowǔ.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Lǐ Shàncháng led the assembled officials in urging him to ascend the throne.
After three petitions,
he finally agreed.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
he made a solemn declaration to Shangdì.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Tāng Hé and Liáo Yǒngzhōng captured Fúzhōu by sea.
Collation Notes
Basic Annals II: Tàizǔ II
In the spring, first month, *yǐhài* day, of the first year of Hóngwǔ
, offerings were made to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburbs
, and the Emperor ascended the throne.
The dynastic title for all under Heaven was declared as Míng,
and the era name was established as Hóngwǔ.
The great-great-grandfather was posthumously honored as Xuán Huángdì,
with the temple name Dézǔ;
the great-grandfather as Huángdì,
with the temple name Yìzǔ;
the grandfather as Yù Huángdì,
with the temple name Xīzǔ;
the father as Chún Huángdì,
with the temple name Rénzǔ;
all grandmothers and mothers were honored as Empresses.
Consort Mǎ Shì was elevated to Empress,
and the heir apparent, Biāo, was made Crown Prince.
Lǐ Shàncháng and Xú Dá were appointed Left and Right Chéngxiàng (Chancellors),
and various meritorious ministers were promoted in rank, with differences.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the edict of accession was promulgated throughout the realm.
Imperial uncles and those below them were all posthumously enfeoffed as Kings.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Lǐ Shàncháng, Xú Dá, and others concurrently held posts in the Eastern Palace (Crown Prince's establishment).
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
envoys were dispatched to verify the land taxes in Zhèxī.
On the *rénchén* day,
Hú Tíngruì captured Jiànníng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Dèng Yù was appointed Grand General for Pacification and Garrisoning,
and campaigned through the prefectures and commanderies north of Nányáng.
Tāng Hé captured Yánpíng
and apprehended Chén Yǒudìng, the Yuán Píngzhāng (Chancellor),
thus Fújiàn was pacified.
That month,
officials from prefectures, subprefectures, and counties throughout the realm came to court.
An imperial edict stated:
"The realm has just been settled;
the people's resources are exhausted.
It is crucial to allow them to recuperate and rest.
Only those who are incorruptible can restrain themselves and benefit others.
Strive for this."
On the *rénrín* day of the second month,
the rites for the suburban sacrifices, state altars, and ancestral temples were established,
to be personally performed annually as a permanent custom.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Tāng Hé was appointed to oversee maritime transport.
Liáo Yǒngzhōng was made Grand General for Southern Pacification,
with Zhū Liàngzǔ as his deputy,
to take Guǎngdōng via the sea route.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
a grand sacrificial offering (tàiláo) was made to the Former Master Kǒngzǐ at the National Academy.
On the *wùshēn* day,
sacrifices were made to the Gods of Earth and Grain.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
an edict decreed that attire should follow the Táng dynasty system.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Cháng Yùchūn captured Dōngchāng,
and Shāndōng was pacified.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Yáng Jǐng captured Bǎoqìng.
On the *xīnwèi* day of the third month,
an edict instructed the Confucian scholars to compile "Admonitions for Women,"
cautioning empresses and consorts not to interfere in government.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Zhōu Déxīng captured Quánzhōu.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Dèng Yù captured Nányáng.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Xú Dá marched to Biànliáng,
and Zuǒ Jūnbì surrendered.
In the summer, on the *xīnchǒu* day of the fourth month,
Qízhōu offered bamboo mats,
which were rejected,
and an order was issued that all regions should not offer frivolous tributes.
Liáo Yǒngzhōng's army reached Guǎngzhōu,
and Hé Zhēn, the Yuán defending official, surrendered,
thus Guǎngdōng was pacified.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
a joint sacrifice (xiáxiǎng) was made at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Xú Dá and Cháng Yùchūn decisively defeated the Yuán army north of the Luò River,
then besieged Hénán.
Liáng Wáng Ālǔwēn surrendered,
and Hénán was pacified.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Yáng Jǐng captured Yǒngzhōu.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor visited Biànliáng.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Féng Shèng captured Tóngguān,
and Lǐ Sīqí and Zhāng Sīdào fled.
On the *jǐmǎo* day of the fifth month,
Liáo Yǒngzhōng captured Wúzhōu,
and all prefectures of Xún, Guì, Róng, and Yùlín surrendered.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Biànliáng Circuit was renamed Kāifēng Prefecture.
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the sixth month,
Xú Dá came to court at the temporary imperial residence (xíngzài).
On the *jiǎchén* day,
all circuits of Hǎinán and Hǎiběi surrendered.
On the *rénxū* day,
Yáng Jǐng and Zhū Liàngzǔ captured Jìngjiāng.
In the autumn, on the *wùzǐ* day of the seventh month,
Liáo Yǒngzhōng captured Xiàngzhōu,
and Guǎngxī was pacified.
On the *gēngyín* day,
relief was distributed to the impoverished people of the Central Plains.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
about to return to Yìngtiān,
the Emperor instructed Dá and others, saying:
"The people of the Central Plains
have long suffered under various warlords,
wandering far and wide.
Therefore, I ordered generals to campaign north
to rescue the people from dire straits.
Though the Yuán ancestors' merits and virtues benefited the people,
their descendants neglected the people's suffering;
Heaven abhorred and abandoned them.
If the ruler is guilty,
what crime have the people committed?
During previous dynastic changes,
wanton slaughter was committed,
defying Heaven and oppressing the people.
I truly cannot bear this.
When my generals capture a city,
they must not wantonly burn, loot, or kill.
The Yuán imperial clan and relatives
must all be protected.
This will hopefully respond to the will of Heaven above,
and soothe the hopes of the people below,
thereby fulfilling my intention of punishing the wicked and bringing peace to the people.
Those who disobey this command will be punished without mercy."
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Féng Shèng was ordered to remain and guard Kāifēng.
In the intercalary month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
the Emperor returned from Kāifēng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Xú Dá assembled the generals and troops at Línqīng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Cháng Yùchūn captured Dézhōu.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Tōngzhōu was captured,
and the Yuán emperor fled to Shàngdū.
That month,
wise and talented individuals from throughout the realm were recruited as governors and magistrates.
Land taxes were remitted for the disaster-stricken areas of Wújiāng, Guǎngdé, Tàipíng, Níngguó, Chú, and Hé.
In the eighth month, on the Jǐsì day,
Yìngtiān was established as Nánjīng,
and Kāifēng as Běijīng.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
Xú Dá entered the Yuán capital,
sealed the government treasuries and archives,
guarded the palace gates,
forbade soldiers from plunder and violence,
and dispatched generals to patrol the passes of Gǔběikǒu.
On the Rénshēn day,
due to a fire in the capital [Jīngshī]
and floods and droughts across the land,
an imperial edict ordered the Zhōngshūshěng to convene and discuss matters beneficial to the people.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
the official system of the Six Ministries was established.
Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Liú Jī retired from office.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
an amnesty was granted for crimes punishable by death and lesser offenses.
The families of officers and soldiers who participated in campaigns were to be compensated.
Fugitives were allowed to surrender themselves.
No arbitrary killings were permitted in newly conquered prefectures and counties.
For those whose route for paying taxes was long,
officials were to arrange transportation.
Disasters and famines were to be reported truthfully.
Taxes in Zhènjiāng were remitted.
People who had fled from chaos and now wished to resume their livelihoods
were allowed to cultivate barren land
and were exempted from taxes for three years.
The Yǎnshèng Gōng's succession and appointment as Zhīxiàn of Qūfù
were to follow the precedents of previous dynasties.
Officials were to invite worthy scholars with proper礼,
and schools were not to engage in superficial formalities.
Punishments were to be fair,
and prisoners were not to be executed out of season.
Taxes on books and farming tools were abolished,
and private debts were exempted from collection.
Mongols and Semu people with talent
were permitted to be promoted and employed.
Widows, widowers, orphans, the solitary, and the disabled
were to be cared for and provided for.
For people aged seventy and above,
one son was exempted from corvée.
Other matters of benefit or harm requiring reform not included in the edict
were to be reported by officials.
On the Rénwǔ day,
the emperor visited Běijīng.
Dàdū Lù was renamed Běipíng Fǔ.
Former officials of the Yuán dynasty were summoned.
On the Guǐwèi day,
an imperial edict ordered Xú Dá and Cháng Yùchūn to take Shānxī.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
the Yuán palace women were released.
In the ninth month, on the Guǐhài day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The governance of All-under-Heaven [Tiānxià]
is to be jointly managed by the worthy of All-under-Heaven.
Currently, many worthy scholars are hidden in mountains and caves.
Is it that officials have failed in their encouragement,
or that the court has been remiss in its respectful treatment,
or is it that I am ignorant and unworthy of attracting the virtuous,
or are those in office obstructing them from reaching me?
Otherwise,
how could worthy scholars and high officials,
who studied in their youth and acted bravely in their prime,
be content to pass their lives in obscurity?
Now that All-under-Heaven is settling,
I wish to discuss governance with all scholars.
If there are those who can assist me in benefiting the people,
officials are to send them respectfully."
On the Yǐchǒu day,
Cháng Yùchūn captured Bǎodìng,
and then Zhēndìng.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the Gēngwǔ day,
Féng Shèng and Tāng Hé captured Huáiqìng;
Zé and Lù successively fell.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
the emperor returned from Běijīng.
On the Wùyín day,
with the pacification of the Yuán capital,
an imperial edict was issued to All-under-Heaven.
In the eleventh month, on the Jǐhài day,
envoys were dispatched across All-under-Heaven
to seek out talented individuals.
On the Gēngzǐ day,
the worship of the Lord on High [Shàngdì] at the Round Altar [Huánqiū] began.
On the Guǐhài day,
an imperial edict ordered Liú Jī to return.
In the twelfth month, on the Dīngmǎo day,
Xú Dá conquered Tàiyuán,
Kuòkuò Tiēmùér fled to Gānsù,
and Shānxī was pacified.
On the Jǐsì day,
the Drum of Complaint [Dēngwéngǔ] was established.
On the Rénchén day,
a letter was sent to Yù Míngshēng.
In the second year, spring, in the first month, on the Yǐsì day,
a temple for meritorious officials was established on Jīlóng Shān.
On the Dīngwèi day,
sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple [Tàimiào].
On the Gēngxū day,
an imperial edict stated:
"I, a commoner from Huáinán,
due to the chaos in All-under-Heaven,
led troops across the river,
to protect the people and strive for good governance.
Now, fifteen years have passed.
With Heaven's favor and protection,
all has been pacified.
Thus, I ordered my generals to march north.
The people of Qí and Lǔ supplied provisions to the army,
not fearing a thousand li.
I am concerned about their toil,
and have already remitted the land rent for the first year.
The people affected by drought have not yet recovered,
so an additional year's remission is granted.
Recently,
the grand army pacified Yāndū [Běijīng],
and conquered Jìn and Jì.
The people were afflicted by war and fire,
and burdened by levies.
Therefore, this year's land rent in Běipíng, Yānnán, Hédōng, and Shānxī is also remitted.
The various prefectures of Hénán have submitted,
and I have long wished to benefit them.
However, as the northwest was not yet pacified,
and the army passed through their territory,
there was no time for this.
Now that Jìn and Jì are pacified,
reaching Tóngguān in the west,
bordered by the Yellow River [Dàhé] in the north,
and extending south to Táng, Dèng, Guāng, and Xī,
this year's grain taxes are all abolished."
Another edict stated:
"Yìngtiān, Tàipíng, Zhènjiāng, Xuānchéng, and Guǎngdé have provided vast amounts of supplies.
Last year's tax remission,
due to drought, did not fully benefit the lower strata.
Therefore, this year's taxes for these prefectures and Wúwéi Zhōu are again remitted."
On the Gēngshēn day,
Cháng Yùchūn captured Dàtóng.
In this month,
Japanese pirates raided coastal prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
In the second month, on the Bǐngyín day (the first day of the month),
an imperial edict ordered the compilation of the Yuán Shǐ.
On the Rénwǔ day,
the emperor personally tilled the sacrificial field [Jìtián].
In the third month, on the Gēngzǐ day,
Xú Dá arrived at Fèngyuán,
and Zhāng Sīdào fled.
Famine relief was provided in Shǎnxī,
with three shi of rice per household.
On the Bǐngwǔ day,
Cháng Yùchūn arrived at Fèngxiáng,
and Lǐ Sīqí fled to Líntáo.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the Bǐngyín day,
Yùchūn's army returned peacefully.
On the Jǐsì day,
the various princes received instruction from Professor Kǒng Kèrén.
The children of meritorious officials were ordered to attend school.
On the Yǐhài day,
the Zǔxùn Lù was compiled,
and the system of enfeoffing [fēngjiàn] princes was established.
Xú Dá captured Gǒngchāng.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
tax grain was bestowed upon the newly submitted prefectures and counties of Qín and Lǒng.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
Féng Shèng arrived at Líntáo,
and Lǐ Sīqí surrendered.
On the Yǐyǒu day,
Xú Dá surprised and defeated Yuán Yù Wáng in Xī'ān.
In the fifth month, on the Jiǎwǔ day (the first day of the month),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the Dīngyǒu day,
Xú Dá captured Píngliáng and Yán'ān.
Zhāng Liángchén surrendered with Qìngyáng,
but soon rebelled.
On the Guǐmǎo day,
the worship of Earth at the Square Altar [Fāngqiū] began.
In the sixth month, on the Jǐmǎo day,
Cháng Yùchūn captured Kāipíng,
and the Yuán emperor fled north.
On the Rénwǔ day,
Chén Rìkuí was enfeoffed as the King of Ānnán.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day bǐngchén,
an edict was issued for Confucian scholars to take turns on duty at Wǔmén Gate,
to lecture on the classics and history for military officials.
On the day guǐhài,
Zhōu Déxīng was made General Who Conquers the South,
to suppress Tán Hòu.
Hòu escaped.
On the day xīnsì,
a letter was sent to Yuán's heir.
In the eleventh month, on the day rénchén,
the northern expeditionary army returned.
On the day jiǎwǔ,
a ceremony announcing military success was held at the suburban altars and ancestral temples.
On the day bǐngshēn,
great enfeoffments were granted to meritorious officials.
Lǐ Shàncháng was promoted to Hánguó Gōng,
Xú Dá to Wèiguó Gōng,
Lǐ Wénzhōng was enfeoffed as Cáoguó Gōng,
Féng Shèng as Sòngguó Gōng,
Dèng Yù as Wèiguó Gōng,
Cháng Yùchūn's son Mào as Zhèngguó Gōng,
and twenty-eight others, including Tāng Hé, were granted marquisates.
On the day jǐhài,
an altar was set up and a personal sacrifice was offered to the generals and soldiers who died in battle.
On the day gēngxū,
a ceremony was performed at the Yuánqiú Altar.
On the day xīnhài,
an edict was issued for the Hùbù to establish household registers and household certificates,
and to report annually on increases and decreases in population,
making it a permanent regulation.
On the day yǐmǎo,
Wāng Guǎngyáng, Right Assistant of the Zhōngshū, was enfeoffed as Zhōngqín Bó,
and Liú Jī, Censor-in-Chief, as Chéngyì Bó.
In the twelfth month, on the day guǐhài,
another letter was sent to Yuán's heir,
and also an admonition to the various tribes of Hélín.
On the day jiǎzǐ,
the Fèngxiān Diàn was constructed.
On the day gēngwǔ,
envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifices at the imperial tombs of past dynasties,
and also to carry out repairs.
On the day jǐmǎo,
land was bestowed upon meritorious officials.
On the day rénwǔ,
as from the first month until this month,
sunspots had repeatedly appeared at noon,
an edict was issued for court officials to speak on gains and losses.
In this year,
Zhànchéng, Zhǎowā,
and Xīyáng paid tribute.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day bǐngxū,
Lǐ Shàncháng was dismissed,
and Wāng Guǎngyáng became Right Chancellor.
On the day dīnghài,
Tāng Hé, Marquis of Zhōngshān, was made General Who Conquers the West;
Zhōu Déxīng, Marquis of Jiāngxià, and Liáo Yǒngzhōng, Marquis of Déqìng, served as his deputies,
leading a naval force via Qútáng.
Fù Yǒudé, Marquis of Yǐngchuān, was made Vanguard General Who Conquers the Captives;
Gù Shí, Marquis of Jìníng, served as his deputy,
leading infantry and cavalry via Qín and Lǒng to attack Shǔ.
Xú Dá, Duke of Wèi, trained troops in Běipíng.
On the day wùzǐ,
Dèng Yù, Duke of Wèi, supervised the provisioning of supplies for the Shǔ expeditionary army.
On the day gēngyín,
suburban altars and ancestral temples were constructed in Zhōngdū.
On the day dīngwèi,
an edict ordered the establishment of the imperial examination system for three consecutive years,
and thereafter once every three years.
On the day wùshēn,
land taxes were remitted in Shānxī due to drought.
In the second month, on the day jiǎxū,
the emperor made an inspection tour to Zhōngdū.
On the day rénwǔ,
the emperor returned from Zhōngdū.
Liú Yì, a Yuán píngzhāng, surrendered from Liáodōng.
In this month,
land taxes were remitted in Tàipíng, Zhènjiāng, and Níngguó.
In the third month, on the first day yǐyǒu,
the imperial examination for scholars throughout the realm was held for the first time;
Wú Bózōng and others were granted the title of jìnshì with varying ranks.
On the day yǐsì,
seventeen thousand households from Shānhòu were relocated to garrison Běipíng.
On the day dīngwèi,
Liú Jī, Count of Chéngyì, retired from office.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day bǐngxū,
Fù Yǒudé captured Jiēzhōu;
Wén, Lóng, and Mián prefectures successively fell.
In the fifth month,
autumn grain taxes were remitted in Jiāngxī and Zhèjiāng.
In the sixth month, on the day rénwǔ,
Fù Yǒudé captured Hànzhōu.
On the day xīnmǎo,
Liáo Yǒngzhōng captured Kuízhōu.
On the day wùxū,
Dīng Shìzhēn, a general under Míng Shēng, attacked Wénzhōu;
the defending general Zhū Xiǎnzhōng died.
On the day guǐmǎo,
Tāng Hé arrived at Chóngqìng,
and Míng Shēng surrendered.
On the day wùshēn,
Japanese pirates raided Jiāozhōu.
In this month,
thirty-five thousand households from Shānhòu were relocated to the interior,
and another thirty-two thousand households of refugees from the desert were relocated to cultivate land in Běipíng.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day xīnhài,
Xú Dá trained troops in Shānxī.
On the day xīnyǒu,
Fù Yǒudé took Chéngdū;
Sìchuān was pacified.
On the day yǐchǒu,
Míng Shēng arrived in Jīngshī,
and was enfeoffed as Guīyì Hóu.
In the eighth month, on the day jiǎwǔ,
land taxes were remitted in Zhōngdū, Huái, Yáng, and Tàizhōu, Chúzhōu, Wúwéi.
On the day jǐyǒu,
famine relief was provided in Shǎnxī.
In this month,
sea pirates caused disturbances in Gāozhōu;
the Assistant Prefect Wáng Míngshàn died.
In the ninth month, on the first day gēngxū,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day bǐngshēn,
the Shǔ expeditionary army returned.
In the eleventh month, on the day bǐngchén,
a ceremony was performed at the Yuánqiú Altar.
On the day gēngshēn,
an order was issued that officials who committed embezzlement should not be pardoned.
In this month,
land taxes were remitted in disaster-stricken areas of Shǎnxī and Hénán.
In the twelfth month,
Xú Dá returned.
In this year,
Ānnán, Bóní, Gāolí, Sānfóqí, Xiāmluó, Rìběn, and Zhēnlà paid tribute.
In the fifth year, spring, first month, on the day guǐchǒu,
Wáng Yī, a Dàizhì, was sent as envoy to Yúnnán,
with an edict to admonish Bá Zālawa'ěrmì, the Yuán Prince of Liáng.
Yī arrived,
but refused to submit and died.
On the day yǐchǒu,
Chén Lǐ and Míng Shēng were relocated to Gāolí.
On the day jiǎxū,
Xú Dá, Duke of Wèi, was made Commander-in-Chief Who Conquers the Captives,
departing from Yànmén,
and heading towards Hélín.
Lǐ Wénzhōng, Duke of Cáo, was made Left Deputy General,
departing from Yìngchāng.
Féng Shèng, Duke of Sòng, was made General Who Conquers the West,
to take Gānsù,
and suppress Kuòkuò Tièmù'ěr.
Wú Zhēn, Marquis of Jìnghǎi, supervised sea transport,
supplying Liáodōng.
Dèng Yù, Duke of Wèi, was made General Who Conquers the South;
Zhōu Déxīng, Marquis of Jiāngxià, and Wú Liáng, Marquis of Jiāngyīn, served as his deputies,
dividing their forces to suppress the cave barbarians in Húnán and Guǎngxī.
In the second month, on the day bǐngxū,
Chén Shúmíng of Ānnán assassinated his lord Rì Jiān and usurped the throne;
he sent envoys to pay tribute,
but was rejected.
In the third month, on the day dīngmǎo,
Lán Yù, Grand Supervisor of the Dudū, defeated Kuòkuò at Tǔlá Hé.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
relief was provided to the starving in Jǐnán and Láizhōu.
On the day Wùxū,
the Village Drinking Ritual was first implemented.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Dèng Yù pacified the various aboriginal tribes of Sǎnmáo.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Xú Dá and the Yuán forces fought north of the ridge,
and were defeated.
In this month,
an imperial edict stated:
"The realm is largely settled,
and rites, customs, and practices must not be left unrectified.
All those who became slaves during the chaos shall be restored to commoner status.
For those suffering from cold and hunger, wealthy families in their villages shall lend to them;
orphans, widows, the solitary, and the disabled shall be cared for by the officials,
so that none are left without support.
In the villages, seniority shall be determined by age;
upon meeting, people shall bow and pay respects,
without violating decorum.
Marriages shall not be determined by wealth.
Funerals shall be conducted according to the family's means,
without being misled by yin and yang superstitions
that lead to coffins being left exposed.
Displaced people who resume their occupations shall cultivate land according to their labor capacity,
without being limited by their old fields.
Buddhist monks and Daoist priests who mix men and women during fasting rituals,
and indulge in excessive eating and drinking,
shall be severely punished by the authorities.
Wealthy families in Mǐn and Yuè shall not castrate their sons to serve as eunuchs;
violators shall be punished."
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
regulations for eunuchs were established.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the system for palace officials and female offices was established.
On the day Wùyín,
Féng Shèng conquered Gānsù,
and pursued and defeated the Yuán forces in Guāzhōu and Shāzhōu.
On the day Guǐsì,
the responsibilities of the Six Ministries and the year-end performance review method were established.
On the day Rényín,
Wú Liáng pacified the aboriginal tribes of Jìngzhōu.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Lǐ Wénzhōng defeated the Yuán forces at the Ālǔhún River,
and the Xuānníng Hóu, Cáo Liángchén, died in battle.
On the day Yǐsì,
an iron plaque was erected to admonish meritorious officials.
In this month,
relief was provided to the starving in Shāndōng,
and land taxes were remitted for affected prefectures and counties.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Tāng Hé and the Yuán forces fought at Duàntóu Shān,
and were defeated.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Wú Liáng pacified the various aboriginal tribes of Wǔkāi and Gǔzhōu.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Yuán forces attacked Yúnnèi,
and the Assistant Prefect, Huáng Lǐ, died.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Zhōu Déxīng pacified the various aboriginal tribes of Lánfèng and Āntián.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Féng Shèng's army returned.
In this month,
land taxes were remitted for Yìngtiān, Tàipíng, Zhènjiāng, Níngguó, and Guǎngdé.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
rituals were performed at the Yuánqiū.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the southern expeditionary army returned.
On the day Rénshēn,
Náhāchū invaded Liáodōng.
In this month,
Xú Dá and Lǐ Wénzhōng were recalled.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
an imperial edict tasked officials with promoting agriculture, sericulture, and schools.
On the day Xīnsì,
officials were ordered to report all matters to the Crown Prince.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Dèng Yù was made General Who Conquers the West,
and dispatched to conquer Tǔfān.
On the day Rényín,
a letter was sent to the Yuán successor ruler.
In this year,
Suǒlǐ, Zhànchéng, Gāolí, Líuqiú, and Wūsī Zàng offered tribute.
The Gāolí tribute envoys arrived again,
and were instructed to offer tribute once every three years thereafter.
In the sixth year, spring, first month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Wāng Guǎngyáng was demoted to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guǎngdōng.
In the second month, on the day Yǐwèi,
an edict temporarily suspended the imperial examinations,
and instead called for the recommendation of worthy talents.
On the day Rényín,
Censorates and Surveillance Commissioners were ordered to inspect officials.
In the third month, on the first day, Guǐmǎo,
there was a solar eclipse.
The Zhāojiàn Lù was issued,
to instruct and admonish the various princes.
On the day Wùshēn,
a grand review of troops was held.
On the day Rényǐ,
Xú Dá was made Grand General Who Conquers the Captives,
with Lǐ Wénzhōng, Féng Shèng, Dèng Yù, and Tāng Hé as his deputies,
to guard the borders of Shānxī and Běipíng.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Commander Yú Xiǎn was made Commander-in-Chief,
to guard against the Japanese pirates.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
officials were ordered to submit maps of mountains, rivers, and strategic locations.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Xūyí presented auspicious wheat,
which was offered at the imperial ancestral temple.
On the day Rénchén,
Köke Temür sent troops to attack Yànmén,
and Commander Wú Jūn repelled them.
In this month,
land taxes for affected areas in Běipíng, Héjiān, Hénán, Kāifēng, Yán'ān, and Fénzhōu were remitted.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Rényín,
the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to calculate the extent of drought and flood damage in various provinces since crossing the Yangtze River,
and provide generous relief.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Hú Wéiyōng was made Right Chancellor.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐhài,
an edict ordered sacrifices to the Three Sovereigns and successive emperors.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Xīnsì,
Xú Dá and Féng Shèng were recalled.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Köke Temür attacked Dàtóng,
and Xú Dá dispatched generals to defeat him,
with Dá remaining to guard the area.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Minister of War Liú Rén was sent to Zhenzheng to investigate the famine.
On the day Bǐngyín,
it was the winter solstice,
but the Emperor was unwell,
so the suburban sacrifice was re-divined.
In the intercalary month, on the day Yǐhài,
two hundred nine descendants of deceased meritorious officials who had not yet inherited titles were registered.
On the day Rénwǔ,
rituals were performed at the Yuánqiū.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Great Míng Code was promulgated.
In this year,
Xiāmluó, Gāolí, Zhànchéng, Zhēnlà, and Sānfóqí offered tribute.
Chén Shúmíng of Ānnán was appointed to provisionally administer state affairs.
In the seventh year, spring, first month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Assistant Commanders-in-Chief Wáng Jiǎn and Wáng Chéng,
and Provincial Administrator Lǐ Bóshēng,
were stationed to reclaim land for cultivation in Hénán, Shāndōng, and Běipíng.
The Jìnghǎi Hóu, Wú Zhēn, was made Commander-in-Chief,
with Commander-in-Chief Yú Xiǎn as his deputy,
to patrol the seas and capture Japanese pirates.
In the second month, on the first day, Dīngyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Confucius' temple in Qūfù was repaired,
and schools for the Kǒng, Yán, and Mèng clans were established.
In this month,
Píngyáng, Tàiyuán, Fénzhōu, Lìchéng, and Jíxiàn suffered from drought and locusts,
and all their rent and taxes were remitted.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Commander Lán Yù defeated the Yuán forces at Báijiǔquán,
and then captured Xīnghé.
On the day Rényín,
Golden Guard Commander Lù Líng attacked the aboriginal tribes of Yǒng and Dào prefectures,
and pacified them.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
land taxes for forty-two affected prefectures, sub-prefectures, and counties, including Zhēndìng, were remitted.
On the day Xīnsì,
relief was provided to three hundred thousand starving households in Sūzhōu.
On the day Guǐsì,
the extremely heavy land taxes in Sū, Sōng, Jiā, and Hú were halved.
In the sixth month,
Píngliáng, Yán'ān, Jìngníng, and Fūzhōu in Shǎnxī suffered from hail,
while Shānxī, Shāndōng, Běipíng, and Hénán suffered from locusts,
and all their land taxes were remitted.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Lǐ Wénzhōng defeated the Yuán forces at Dàníng and Gāozhōu.
On the day Rénshēn,
Japanese pirates attacked Dēng and Lái.
In the eighth month, on the first day, Jiǎwǔ,
sacrifices were offered at the Temple of Successive Emperors.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
an imperial edict stated that if soldiers died in battle,
and their parents, wives, and children could not support themselves,
the government would provide for them.
If commoners fled due to war or died as strangers,
leaving behind elderly and young dependents,
they would all be provided with funds and sent back home.
If officials died far from home,
and their wives and children could not return,
the authorities would provide boats, carts, and funds for their return.
On the day Gēngshēn,
relief was provided to the starving in Héjiān, Guǎngpíng, Shùndé, and Zhēndìng,
and their rent and taxes were remitted.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the Chónglǐ Hóu Màidílǐbālā was sent back,
with a letter to the Yuán successor ruler.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the day Rénxū,
Náhāchū invaded Liáoyáng.
The chiliarch Wú Shòu repelled him.
On the day Xīnwèi,
rites were performed at the Yuánqiū (Altar of Heaven).
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùxū,
Dèng Yù and Tāng Hé were summoned back.
In this year,
Ānán Gōngdéguó, Xiāmluó, Liúqiú, Sānfóqí, Wūsīzàng, Sālǐ, and Wèiwú'ér offered tribute.
In the eighth year, spring, the first month, on the day Xīnwèi,
one hundred and eight more meritorious officials were enshrined in the Jīlóngshān Temple.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
officials were ordered to investigate the poor and destitute
and provide them with housing, clothing, and food.
On the day Xīnsì,
Dèng Yù, Tāng Hé, and thirteen others were stationed to guard Běipíng, Shǎnxī, and Hénán.
On the day Dīnghài,
an imperial edict ordered the establishment of community schools throughout the realm.
In this month,
the river breached at Kāifēng,
and common laborers were dispatched to plug it.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
pardons were granted for miscellaneous capital offenses and lesser crimes, as well as for officials who committed private offenses.
They were exiled to Fèngyáng to perform labor and cultivate land as atonement.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the ceremonial plowing of the Jìtián was performed.
Xú Dá, Lǐ Wénzhōng, and Féng Shèng were summoned back,
while Fù Yǒudé and others remained to garrison Běipíng.
In the third month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the paper currency system was established.
On the day Xīnsì,
the minting of coins by the Bǎoyuán Bureau was suspended.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the emperor visited Zhōngdū.
On the day Dīngsì,
he returned from Zhōngdū.
Land taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken fields in Zhāngdé, Dàmíng, Líntáo, Píngliáng, and Hézhōu.
Construction in Zhōngdū was halted.
Liú Jī, the retired Earl of Chéngyì, passed away.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐsì,
Zhū Liàngzǔ, the Marquis of Yǒngjiā, together with Fù Yǒudé, garrisoned Běipíng.
In the sixth month, on the day Rényín,
Hú Rúpíng, an Assistant Commissioner, pacified the indigenous people of Guìzhōu.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Jǐwèi,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Tàimiào (Imperial Ancestral Temple) was renovated.
On the day Rénxū,
Fù Yǒudé and Zhū Liàngzǔ were summoned back,
while Lǐ Wénzhōng and Gù Shí garrisoned Shānxī and Běipíng.
On the day Wùchén,
an imperial edict decreed that officials could return home for parental mourning without waiting for approval.
There was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
land taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken fields in Yìngtiān, Tàipíng, Níngguó, Zhènjiāng, as well as the prefectures of Qí and Huáng.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Yuán Kuòkuò Tièmù'ér passed away.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Dīnghài,
an imperial edict ordered the recommendation of wealthy citizens known for their upright conduct and understanding of current affairs.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Crown Prince and various princes were ordered to practice military drills in Zhōngdū.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
rites were performed at the Yuánqiū.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day Jiǎyín,
envoys were dispatched to relieve the flood-stricken areas of Sūzhōu, Húzhōu, Jiāxīng, Sōngjiāng, Chángzhōu, Tàipíng, Níngguó, and Hángzhōu.
In this month,
Náhāchū invaded Liáodōng,
and Commissioners Mǎ Yún and Yè Wàng decisively defeated him.
In this year,
Sālǐ, Gāolí, Zhānchéng, Xiāmluó, Rìběn, Zhǎowā, and Sānfóqí offered tribute.
In the ninth year, spring, the first month,
Tāng Hé, Marquis of Zhōngshān,
Fù Yǒudé, Marquis of Yǐngchuān,
Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Lán Yù and Wáng Bì,
and Right Vice Grand Councilor Dīng Yù
garrisoned the frontier in Yán'ān.
In the third month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
