an imperial edict stated:
"In recent years, the western expedition to Dūnhuáng
and the northern campaign into the desert
have relied on Shān (Shānxī) and Shǎn (Shǎnxī) for military provisions and weaponry.
Furthermore, the construction of palaces for the two princely establishments of Qín and Jìn
has severely burdened our people.
Since the pacification,
the common folk have not had respite.
The capital was recently established,
and civil engineering projects have been numerous.
The imperial domain has been excessively fatigued by labor,
and external prefectures are exhausted by transportation.
Now, with a surplus in reserves,
the annual land taxes for the five prefectures of Huái, Yáng, Ān, Huī, and Chí,
as well as Shānxī, Shǎnxī, Hénán, Fújiàn, Jiāngxī, Zhèjiāng, Běipíng, and Húguǎng for this year,
are all remitted."
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Gēngxū,
after the capital had no rain since the eighth month of last year,
it began to rain on this day.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
the rain which started on Gēngxū
ceased on this day.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng (Branch Secretariat) was reformed into the Chéngxuān Bùzhèng Shǐsī (Provincial Administration Commission).
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Lǐ Wénzhōng returned.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Guǐchǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
In this month,
land taxes were remitted for flood-stricken areas in Sū, Sōng, Jiā, and Hú,
and relief was provided for drought in Yǒngpíng.
Yuán general Bóyán Tièmù'ér invaded Yán'ān,
and Fù Yǒudé defeated and accepted his surrender.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
officials were dispatched to inspect the imperial tombs of past dynasties,
forbidding grazing,
and establishing tomb-guarding households.
The shrines for loyal ministers and martyrs
were to be maintained by officials in a timely manner.
Students from the Guózǐjiān (Imperial Academy) were sent to repair the shrines of the Five Sacred Mountains and Four Sacred Rivers.
The Xīfān Dài'ér zhī Bā raided Hǎndōng,
and Níng Zhèng, Commissioner of Hézhōu, repelled him.
In the intercalary ninth month, on the day Gēngyín,
an imperial edict was issued seeking frank opinions due to calamitous omens.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Tàimiào was completed,
and from then on, the combined sacrificial rites were performed there.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the princes of Qín, Jìn, Yān, Wú, Chǔ, and Qí were ordered to train troops in Fèngyáng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Réngwǔ,
rites were performed at the Yuánqiū.
On the day Wùzǐ,
landless commoners from Shānxī and Zhēndìng were resettled in Fèngyáng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
relief was provided for flood-stricken areas in Jīněi, Zhèjiāng, and Húběi.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Mù Yīng was dispatched by post-horse to Shǎnxī to inquire about the people's hardships.
In this year,
Lǎnbāng, Liúqiú, Ānnán, Rìběn, Wūsīzàng, and Gāolí offered tribute.
In the tenth year, spring, the first month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
troops from the Yǔlín and other guards were added to the escorts of the three princely establishments of Qín, Jìn, and Yān.
In this spring,
relief was provided for flood-stricken areas in Sū, Sōng, Jiā, and Hú.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Dèng Yù was made General who Pacifies the West,
and Mù Yīng his deputy general.
They led troops to suppress the Tǔfān,
and thoroughly defeated them.
In this month,
relief was provided for flood-stricken areas in Tàipíng, Níngguó, and the counties of Yíxīng and Qiántáng.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Lǐ Shàncháng, Duke of Hánguó, and Lǐ Wénzhōng, Duke of Cáoguó, jointly headed the Zhōngshū Shěng (Secretariat), Dà Dūdū Fǔ (Chief Military Commission), and Yùshǐ Tái (Censorate)
to deliberate on important military and state affairs.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
relief was provided for flood-stricken Húguǎng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Zhào Qián, a Secretary of the Board of Revenue, was executed for his slow response in providing relief to Jīng and Qí.
He was put to death.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngsì,
an imperial edict ordered that memorials from officials and commoners
be sealed and presented directly to the emperor.
On the day Bǐngyín,
it was ordered that political matters be presented to the Crown Prince for decision and then reported.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the Tōngzhèng Sī (Office of Transmission) was established.
In this month,
censors were first dispatched to tour and inspect prefectures and counties.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Dàsì Diàn (Great Sacrificial Hall) was rebuilt in the southern suburbs.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
sons of military officials were selected to study at the Guózǐjiān.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
relief was provided for flood-stricken Shàoxīng, Jīnhuá, and Qúzhōu.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Hú Wéiyōng was made Left Grand Councilor,
and Wāng Guǎngyáng Right Grand Councilor.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Mù Yīng was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xīpíng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
public fields were bestowed upon all officials.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Dèng Yù, Duke of Wèiguó, passed away.
On the day Dīnghài,
combined sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were performed at Fèntiān Diàn.
In this month,
land taxes were remitted for Hénán, Shǎnxī, Guǎngdōng, and Húguǎng.
The indigenous people of Wēimào rebelled,
and Censor-in-Chief Dīng Yù was made General who Pacifies the Qiāng,
and suppressed them.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Yǐsì,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Dīngwèi,
more than five hundred descendants of deceased meritorious officials were recorded
and granted offices of varying ranks.
In this year,
Zhānchéng, Sānfóqí, Xiāmluó, Zhǎowā, and Zhēnlà offered tribute.
Gāolí envoys came five times,
but were rejected
because the heir to the throne had not yet been established.
In the eleventh year, spring, the first month, on the *Jiǎxū* day,
Imperial Prince Chūn was enfeoffed as the Prince of Shǔ.
Bó was enfeoffed as the Prince of Xiāng.
Guì was enfeoffed as the Prince of Yù.
Yǎng was enfeoffed as the Prince of Hàn.
Zhí was enfeoffed as the Prince of Wèi.
Wú Wáng Shū was re-enfeoffed as the Prince of Zhōu.
On the *Jǐmǎo* day,
Tāng Hé was promoted to Xìnguó Gōng.
In this month,
provincial administration commissioners (*Bùzhèngshǐ*) and prefects (*Zhīfǔ*) from across the realm were summoned to court.
In the second month,
Commander Hú Yuān pacified the Mán people of Máozhōu.
In the third month, on the *Rénwǔ* day,
it was ordered that reports to the throne should no longer involve the Central Secretariat (*Zhōngshū Shěng*).
In this month,
the officials who came to court were ranked into three classes.
Summer, fourth month,
Yuán successor Aiyoushili Dalá passed away.
His son Tuōgǔsī Tièmù'ér succeeded him.
Fifth month, on the *Dīngyǒu* day,
inquiries were made regarding the flood victims in Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu.
Each household was granted one *shí* of rice,
and over 650,000 arrears of taxes were remitted.
Sixth month, on the *Rénzǐ* day,
envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifices to the late Yuán successor.
On the *Jǐsì* day,
the Mán people of Wǔkāi rebelled,
killing Guò Xīng, the commander of Jìngzhōu.
Yáng Zhòngmíng, the commander of Chénzhōu, was appointed commander-in-chief (*Zǒngbīng Guān*)
to suppress them.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *Dīngchǒu* day,
relief was provided for the famine in Píngyáng.
In this month,
the sea overflowed in Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Yángzhōu, and Táizhōu,
and officials were sent to provide relief and care.
Eighth month,
autumn grain taxes were remitted for the prefectures and sub-prefectures of Yìngtiān, Tàipíng, Zhènjiāng, Níngguó, and Guǎngdé.
Ninth month, on the *Bǐngshēn* day,
Liú Jìzǔ was posthumously enfeoffed as Yìhuì Hóu.
Winter, tenth month, on the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
the Great Sacrifice Hall was completed.
Eleventh month, on the *Gēngwǔ* day,
General for Campaigning in the West (*Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn*), Xīpíng Hóu Mù Yīng, led Grand Mentors (*Dūdū*) Lán Yù and Wáng Bì to suppress the Western Fan.
In this month,
Wǔkāi Mán was pacified.
In this year,
Xiāmluó, Zhēpó, Gāolí, Liúqiú, Zhānchéng, Sānfóqí, Běigān, Wūsīzàng, Pénghéng, and Bǎihuā offered tribute.
In the twelfth year, spring, the first month, on the *Jǐmǎo* day,
the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb commenced.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
the eighteen tribes of Fān in Táozhōu rebelled,
and Mù Yīng was ordered to redeploy his troops to suppress them.
On the *Bǐngshēn* day,
Dīng Yù pacified the Mán people of Sōngzhōu.
Second month, on the *Wùxū* day,
Lǐ Wénzhōng supervised military affairs in Hézhōu, Mínzhōu, Línxiāo, and Gǒngchāng.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
an edict stated:
"This spring, snow and rain have lasted for a *xún* (ten days),
and many common people throughout the realm are suffering from hunger and cold.
Therefore, the authorities are ordered to provide them with paper currency."
On the *Bǐngyín* day,
Xìnguó Gōng Tāng Hé led various marquises to train troops in Línqīng.
Summer, fifth month, on the *Kuǐwèi* day,
land taxes in Běipíng were remitted.
Sixth month, on the *Dīngmǎo* day,
Grand Mentor Mǎ Yún campaigned in Dàníng.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *Bǐngchén* day,
Dīng Yù returned with his army to suppress the rebels in Méixiàn,
and pacified them.
On the *Jǐwèi* day,
Lǐ Wénzhōng returned to take charge of the Grand Commandery (*Dà Dūdū Fǔ*).
Eighth month, on the *Xīnsì* day,
an edict ordered that all retired officials should have their households restored,
and be exempt from all duties for life.
Ninth month, on the *Jǐhài* day,
Mù Yīng dealt a great defeat to the Western Fan,
capturing three of their chiefs and deputy envoys.
Winter, eleventh month, on the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
Mù Yīng returned with his army.
Qíu Chéng, Lán Yù, and twelve others were enfeoffed as marquises.
On the *Gēngshēn* day,
Dàníng was pacified.
Twelfth month,
Wāng Guǎngyáng was demoted to Guǎngnán,
and granted death.
Scholars of extensive learning and mature age from across the realm were summoned to the capital.
In this year,
Zhānchéng, Zhǎwā, Xiāmluó, Rìběn, Ānnán, and Gāolí offered tribute.
Gāolí offered 100 *jīn* of gold and 10,000 *liǎng* of silver,
but as it did not conform to the agreement,
it was rejected.
In the thirteenth year, spring, the first month, on the *Wùxū* day,
Left Chancellor Hú Wéiyǒng plotted rebellion,
and he and his partisans, including Censor-in-Chief (*Yùshǐ Dàfū*) Chén Níng and Vice Censor-in-Chief (*Zhōngchéng*) Tú Jié, were executed.
On the *Guǐmǎo* day,
a great sacrifice was made to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
The Central Secretariat (*Zhōngshū Shěng*) was abolished,
the offices of Chancellor and others were eliminated,
the ranks of the Six Ministries were revised,
and the Grand Commandery (*Dà Dūdū Fǔ*) was reformed into the Central, Left, Right, Front, and Rear Five Military Commander's Offices (*Wǔ Jūn Dūdū Fǔ*).
Second month, on the *Rénxū* day, the first day of the month,
an edict called for intelligent and upright, filial and fraternal, diligent in agriculture, virtuous and upright, literary and scholarly individuals.
Tally certificates (*Dānfú*) were issued,
to verify the numbers of gold and grain throughout the realm.
On the *Wùchén* day,
civil and military officials aged sixty and above were permitted to retire,
and were given imperial edicts of commendation.
Third month, on the *Rénchén* day,
the heavy taxes in Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu were reduced by two-tenths.
On the *Rényín* day,
Yān Wáng Dì went to his domain in Běipíng.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
Mù Yīng attacked Yuán general Tuōhuǒchì in Yìjí Nǎi,
captured him,
and completely received the surrender of his troops.
Summer, fourth month, on the *Jǐchǒu* day,
all officials were ordered to recommend those they knew to be capable.
Fifth month, on the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
lightning struck the Jǐnshēn Diàn.
On the *Yǐwèi* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *Bǐngshēn* day,
those involved in military farm settlements (*túntián shūzuò*) in the capital and Línháo were released.
On the *Jǐhài* day,
land taxes throughout the realm were remitted.
Officials dismissed for errors or mistakes were reinstated.
On the *Rényín* day,
Grand Mentor Pú Yīng advanced his troops to Chìjīnzàn,
captured the former Yuán Bīn Wáng Yìliánzhēn and his subordinates, and returned.
In this month,
the Censorate (*Yùshǐ Tái*) was abolished.
Soldiers who had participated in campaigns and were old or sick were allowed to have their sons replace them;
those who were old and had no sons, and widows,
were provided for by the authorities and sent back home.
Sixth month, on the *Bǐngyín* day,
lightning struck Fèngtiān Mén,
and the emperor retired to the main hall to reflect on his faults.
On the *Dīngmǎo* day,
labor for princely estates was abolished.
On the *Dīngchǒu* day,
the office of the remonstrance bureau (*Jiànyuàn Guān*) was established.
Autumn, eighth month,
teachers and students of schools throughout the realm
were granted daily allowances of grain and food.
Ninth month, on the *Xīnmǎo* day,
Jǐngchuān Hóu Cáo Zhèn, Yíngyáng Hóu Yáng Jǐng,
and Yǒngchéng Hóu Xuē Xiǎn established military farm settlements in Běipíng.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
on the Tiānshòu Festival,
the emperor first received congratulations from his officials,
and granted a banquet in the Jǐnshēn Diàn.
This became a regular practice thereafter.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
the four辅 (*Fǔ*, assistants) were established,
and announced at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
Confucian scholars Wáng Běn, Dù Yòu, Gōng Xué, Dù Xué, Zhào Mínwàng, and Wú Yuán were appointed as spring and summer officials.
In this month,
an edict ordered that two-thirds of the Shǎnxī guard troops engage in military farm settlements.
Academician-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy (*Hànlín Xuéshì Chéngzhǐ*) Sòng Lián was settled in Máozhōu,
where he died on the way.
Winter, eleventh month, on the *Yǐwèi* day,
Xú Dá returned.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
Yuán ministers Wánzhěbùhuā and Nǎ'érbùhuā encroached upon Yǒngpíng.
Commander Liú Guǎng was killed in battle.
Commander of a Thousand Households (*Qiānhù*) Wáng Lù defeated them,
and captured Wánzhěbùhuā.
Twelfth month,
over 860 scholars recommended by prefectures, sub-prefectures, and counties across the realm arrived,
and were granted various official positions.
Nánxióng Hóu Zhào Yōng garrisoned Guǎngdōng,
and suppressed the Yángchūn Mán.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Rìběn, Ānnán, Zhānchéng, Zhēnlà, and Zhǎwā offered tribute.
The tribute from Rìběn was rejected due to the absence of a proper memorial (*biǎo*).
In the fourteenth year, spring, the first month, on the *Wùzǐ* day,
Xú Dá was appointed Great General for Suppressing the Barbarians (*Zhēnglǔ Dà Jiāngjūn*).
Tāng Hé and Fù Yǒudé were appointed Left and Right Deputy Generals,
leading the army to suppress Nǎ'érbùhuā.
Newly appointed officials were ordered to recommend those they knew to be capable.
On the *Yǐwèi* day,
a great sacrifice was made to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
the annual production of weapons throughout the realm was abolished.
On the *Guǐchǒu* day,
sons of dukes and marquises were ordered to enter the Imperial Academy (*Guóxué*).
On the *Bǐngchén* day,
an edict called for recluses.
Second month, on the *Gēngchén* day,
official lands throughout the realm were audited.
Third month, on the *Bǐngxū* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *Xīnchǒu* day,
the Five Classics and Four Books were distributed to schools in the north.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Xú Dà led his generals out of the frontier pass.
They reached the Northern Yellow River,
defeated the Yuán soldiers,
and returned with the four tribes of Quánníng.
In the fifth month,
the Wǔxī Mán rebelled.
Jiāngxià Hóu Zhōu Déxīng suppressed them.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
an edict was issued to seek officials who were learned in the classics and of mature virtue;
the relevant authorities were to send them to the capital.
On the day Gēngchén,
the river burst its banks at Yuánwǔ, Xiángfú, and Zhōngmóu.
On the day Xīnsì,
Xú Dà returned.
In the ninth month, on the first day Rénwǔ,
Fù Yǒudé was made General Who Quells the South (Zhēngnán Jiāngjūn),
while Lán Yù and Mù Yīng were made Left and Right Deputy Generals, respectively.
They were to lead an army to conquer Yúnnán.
Xú Dà was stationed at Běipíng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Zhōu Déxīng moved his army to suppress the Shīzhōu Mán,
and pacified them.
In the winter, tenth month, on the first day Rénzǐ,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Ministry of Justice (fǎsī) was ordered to review prisoners,
and to hold a joint meeting with officials from the Hànlín Yuàn (Hanlin Academy) and Chūnfāng (Spring Hall) to discuss and reach a fair decision, which was then to be reported.
On the day Jiǎyín,
land rents in Yìngtiān, Tàipíng, Guǎngdé, Zhènjiāng, and Níngguó were remitted.
On the day Guǐhài,
imperial censors were dispatched to review prisoners.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Yán'ān Hóu Táng Shèngzōng led an army to suppress mountain bandits in eastern Zhèjiāng,
and pacified them.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Jí'ān Hóu Lù Zhònghēng was stationed at Chéngdū.
On the day Gēngxū,
Zhào Yōng attacked sea bandits in Guǎngzhōu,
and utterly defeated them.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngsì,
officials from the Hànlín Yuàn and Chūnfāng were ordered to examine and scrutinize memorials and reports from various ministries.
On the day Wùchén,
Fù Yǒudé decisively defeated Yuán soldiers at Báishí Jiāng,
and subsequently captured Qǔjìng.
On the day Rénshēn,
Yuán Liángwáng Bǎzālàwá'ěrmì fled to Pǔníng and committed suicide.
In this year,
Xiānluó (Siam), Ānnán, Zhǎowā (Java), Gǎn Gān, and Wūsīzàng paid tribute.
As Ānnán's Kòu Sīmíng
did not submit, the tribute was not accepted.
Jiaokanji
Běnjì No. 3, Tàizǔ No. 3
In the fifteenth year, spring, first month, on the day Xīnsì,
the emperor hosted a banquet for his officials in the Jǐnshēn Diàn,
and for the first time, used the Nine-Movement Music.
Jǐngchuān Hóu Cáo Zhèn and Dìngyuǎn Hóu Wáng Bì took Wēichǔ Lù.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Yuán Qǔjìng Xuānwèi Sī (Pacification Commissioner's Office of Qǔjìng) and the roads of Zhōngqìng, Chéngjiāng, and Wǔdìng all surrendered,
and Yúnnán was pacified.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the number of prisoners facing capital punishment was reduced.
On the day Yǐwèi,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Gēngxū,
all officials presenting themselves at court were ordered to recommend one person they knew to be worthy.
In the second month, on the day Rénzǐ,
the river burst its banks in Hénán,
and Fùmǎ Dūwèi Lǐ Qí was ordered to provide relief.
On the day Jiǎyín,
with Yúnnán pacified,
an edict was issued to the whole realm.
In the intercalary month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Lán Yù and Mù Yīng captured Dàlǐ,
and divided their forces to attack Hèqìng, Lìjiāng, and Jīnchǐ,
all of which were taken.
In the third month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
the river burst its banks at Cháoyì.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the family members of Yuán Liángwáng Bǎzālàwá'ěrmì and Wēishùn Prince Bó Bó were relocated to Dānmóluó.
On the day Bǐngxū,
an edict was issued for the universal worship of Kǒngzǐ (Confucius) throughout the realm.
On the day Rénchén,
taxes on grain in Jīnnèi, Zhèjiāng, Jiāngxī, Hénán, and Shāndōng were remitted.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
the Imperial Academy (Tàixué) was completed,
and a ceremony was held to honor the Former Master Kǒngzǐ.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Wáng Yǔndào, an official from Guǎngpíng Fǔ, requested to open an iron smelter in Cízhōu.
The Emperor said:
"I have heard that a king ensures no worthy person is overlooked in the realm,
but I have not heard that he ensures no profit is overlooked.
Currently, military equipment is not lacking,
and the people's livelihoods are settled.
This would not benefit the state,
and would furthermore greatly disturb the people."
He was flogged
and exiled to Lǐngnán.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
envoys (xíngrén) were dispatched to seek out learned and virtuous scholars.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
the river burst its banks at Xíngzé and Yángwǔ.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Four Auxiliary Officials were abolished.
On the day Yǐhài,
Fù Yǒudé and Mù Yīng attacked the Wūsā Mán,
and utterly defeated them.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the imperial examination system was reinstituted for selecting scholars,
to be held every three years,
and this became the established rule.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Empress passed away.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Yán'ān Hóu Táng Shèngzōng and Chángxīng Hóu Gěng Bǐngwén established military colonies in Shǎnxī.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the scholar Zēng Tài was promoted to Minister of Revenue (Hùbù Shàngshū).
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the recruited scholars were ordered to be tested and assigned to the six ministries for trial appointments.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Ministry of Personnel (Lìbù) presented more than 3,700 learned and virtuous scholars, including Zhèng Tāo, for audience.
They were ordered to recommend others they knew,
and envoys were again dispatched to recruit them.
Zhèng Tāo and others were granted banknotes,
and subsequently, each was appointed to various official positions such as Provincial Administration Commissioner (Bùzhèng Shǐ) and Administration Vice Commissioner (Cānzhèng).
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Empress Xiàocí was buried at Xiàolíng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Censorate (Dùchá Yuàn) was established.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Xú Dà returned.
In this month,
the bandits in Guǎngdōng were pacified,
and Zhào Yōng was ordered to return with his army.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Grand Academicians of the Halls and Pavilions (Diàngé Dàxuéshì) were appointed,
with Shào Zhì, Wú Bózōng, Sòng Nà, and Wú Chén filling these posts.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
relief was provided to soldiers in Běipíng whose military colonies had suffered from disaster.
On the day Jǐhài,
Yǒngchéng Hóu Xuē Xiǎn managed military affairs in Shānxī.
In this year,
Zhǎowā, Liúqiú, Wūsīzàng, and Zhànchéng paid tribute.
In the sixteenth year, spring, first month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Xú Dà was stationed at Běipíng.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
it was first ordered that schools throughout the realm should annually recommend scholars to the capital.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎchén,
the Southern Expeditionary Army was recalled,
and Mù Yīng was left to guard Yúnnán.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the corvée labor and taxes of the people of Fèngyáng and Línhuái counties were remitted,
and they were exempt for all generations.
In the summer, fifth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
land rents in the various prefectures of Jīnnèi were remitted.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
land rents for households raising horses in the twelve prefectures and counties of Jīnnèi were remitted for one year,
and for Chúzhōu for two years.
In the autumn, seventh month,
imperial censors were dispatched to review prisoners.
In the eighth month, on the first day Rénshēn,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Shēnguó Gōng Dèng Zhèn was appointed General Who Quells the South,
to suppress the Longquán mountain bandits,
and he pacified them.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Xú Dà and others were recalled.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Kāi Jì, Minister of Justice (Xíngbù Shàngshū), was executed for his crimes.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Zhànchéng, Xīfān, Dǎjiànlú, Xiānluó, and Xūwéndádà paid tribute.
In the seventeenth year, spring, first month, on the day Dīngwèi,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Wùshēn,
Xú Dà was stationed at Běipíng.
On the day Rénxū,
Tāng Hé inspected the coastal cities to defend against Wō (Japanese pirates).
In the third month, on the first day Wùxū,
the regulations for the imperial examinations for selecting scholars were promulgated.
Cáoguó Gōng Lǐ Wénzhōng died.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
the merits for pacifying Yúnnán were assessed,
and Fù Yǒudé was promoted to Yǐngguó Gōng,
while Chén Huán and four other marquises were granted rewards,
and generals and soldiers received great bounties.
On the day Gēngyín,
the remains of those who died in battle were collected.
The dormitories of the Guózǐ Xué (Imperial Academy) were expanded.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Sòng Shèng, Commander of Liángzhōu, attacked Xīfān at Yìjí Nǎi,
and defeated them.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Wùxū,
eunuchs were prohibited from interfering in external affairs.
An imperial edict was issued to all departments, forbidding communication with eunuchs regarding official documents.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
an imperial decree was issued that officials who brought their parents to live with them
should be provided with boats and carriages by the government.
On the day Dīngsì,
half of the year's land tax in the imperial domain was remitted.
On the day Gēngshēn,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day Rénxū,
a person from Xūyí presented a "heavenly book" (tiānshū),
and was executed.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
the Yellow River breached its banks at Kāifēng.
On the day Rénshēn,
it breached at Máoxiàn,
and officials were dispatched to repair the breach.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
arrears of taxes in Hénán and other provinces were remitted.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Hénán and Běipíng experienced severe floods,
and Fùmǎ Dūwèi Lǐ Qí and others were sent to provide relief.
In the intercalary month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
an imperial decree was issued that for all criminals in the realm,
the Xíngbù and the Dūcháyuàn should deliberate in detail,
and the Dàlǐsì should review and re-examine before submitting for final decision.
In this month,
Xú Dá was recalled.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
arrears of taxes in Yúnnán were remitted.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Xiāmluó, Ānnán, and Zhànchéng paid tribute.
In the eighteenth year, in the first month of spring, on the day Xīnwèi,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the southern suburbs.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
officials who came for audience were graded into five ranks based on their performance,
with differing promotions and demotions.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎchén,
due to prolonged overcast weather, rain, thunder, and hail,
an imperial edict commanded officials and common people to speak frankly about gains and losses.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Wèiguógōng Xú Dá passed away.
In the third month, on the day Rénxū,
Dīng Xiǎn and others were granted the Jinshì Jídì and Chūshēn degrees, with differing ranks.
An imperial decree was issued that for officials, both central and local, whose parents died at their post,
the relevant authorities should provide boats and carriages to transport their remains home,
and this was established as a standing rule.
On the day Yǐhài,
this year's land tax in the imperial domain was remitted.
It was ordered that all prefectures and counties in the realm should bury exposed bones.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
for the first time, Jinshì were selected as Shùjíshì for the Hànlín Yuàn, Chéngchì Jiān, and the six divisions (Liù Kē).
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Hùbù Shìláng Guō Huán was executed for embezzling government grain.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Lìbù Shàngshū Yú Xī was executed for a crime.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the barbarians of Sīzhōu rebelled.
Tāng Hé was appointed Zhēnglǔ Jiāngjūn,
and Zhōu Déxīng as Fùjiāngjūn,
leading an army to suppress them with Chǔwáng Zhēn.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùshēn,
it was decreed that external officials should have an audience once every three years,
and this was established as a standing rule.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Jiǎxū,
Wáng Yáo was enfeoffed as King of Gāolí.
On the day Gēngchén,
the barbarians of Wǔkāi rebelled.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Féng Shèng, Fù Yǒudé, and Lán Yù garrisoned the borders at Běipíng.
In this month,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Hénán.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day Jǐchǒu,
the Dà Gào was promulgated throughout the realm.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Féng Shèng was recalled.
On the day Jiǎchén,
an imperial edict stated:
"Mèngzǐ transmitted the Way,
and contributed to education and morality.
Many years have passed,
and his descendants are few and humble.
Recently, some have been subjected to forced labor due to crimes;
how can this accord with the respect due to a former sage?
Therefore, make earnest inquiries and investigations,
and all descendants of sages and worthies who have been subjected to forced labor
shall be exempted."
In this month,
Chǔwáng Zhēn and Xìnguógōng Tāng Hé suppressed the Wǔkāi barbarians.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐhài,
land taxes in Hénán, Shāndōng, and Běipíng were remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
an imperial decree ordered officials to recommend filial and incorrupt (xiàolián) individuals.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Sīlúnfā, the Xuānwèishǐ of Lùchuān Píngmiǎn, rebelled.
Dūdū Féng Chéng suffered a defeat,
and Qiānhù Wáng Shēng died.
In this year,
Gāolí, Liúqiú, Ānnán, and Xiāmluó paid tribute.
In the nineteenth year, in the first month of spring, on the day Xīnyǒu,
relief was provided for the flood disasters in Dàmíng and Jiāngpǔ.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the southern suburbs.
In this month,
the army suppressing the barbarians returned.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
the ceremonial plowing (jítán) was performed.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
relief was provided for famine in Hénán.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day Jiǎchén,
an imperial decree ordered the redemption of children sold by famine victims in Hénán.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
an imperial decree ordered officials to visit and inquire after the elderly.
Poor people aged 80 and above
were to be given five dòu of rice,
three dòu of wine,
and five jīn of meat monthly;
those aged 90 and above
were to be given an additional bolt of silk
and one jīn of floss annually;
those with property were to have their rice stipend stopped.
Wealthy commoners in Yìngtiān and Fèngyáng aged 80 and above were granted the title of Shèshì,
and those 90 and above, Xiāngshì;
wealthy commoners throughout the realm aged 80 and above were granted Lǐshì,
and those 90 and above, Shèshì.
All of them were to be treated with equal respect as county officials,
and their households exempted from labor.
The widowed, lonely, orphaned, and childless who could not support themselves
were to be given six shí of rice annually.
Soldiers wounded in battle were to have their registration exempted,
and granted three years of tax exemption.
If generals or officers died in battle,
their sons were to inherit their rank with an additional step.
Scholars in reclusion
were to be invited with proper rites.
On the day Dīngwèi,
relief was provided for famine in Qīngzhōu and Zhèngzhōu.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Guǐwèi,
an imperial decree ordered the recommendation of scholars who were learned in classics, virtuous in conduct, and proficient in current affairs.
Those aged 60 and above
were to be appointed to the Hànlín Yuàn for consultation;
those below 60
were to be employed in the six ministries (Liù Bù) or the two provincial administrative commissions (Bù-Àn Èr Sī).
In the eighth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
the Crown Prince was ordered to renovate the ancestral tomb at Sìzhōu Xūyí,
and bury the emperors and empresses from Dézǔ downwards in their ceremonial robes (miǎnfú).
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
military agricultural colonies (túntián) were established in Yúnnán.
In the tenth month of winter,
it was ordered that imperial army officers and soldiers whose children had died young or whose parents were elderly should all be given full salaries,
and this was established as a standing rule.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Guǐwèi,
there was a solar eclipse.
In this month,
Sòngguógōng Féng Shèng was ordered to divide his troops to guard the borders.
People from Běipíng, Shāndōng, Shānxī, and Hénán were conscripted to transport grain to Dàníng.
In this year,
Gāolí, Liúqiú, Xiāmluó, Zhànchéng, and Ānnán paid tribute.
In the twentieth year, in the first month of spring, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Féng Shèng was appointed Zhēnglǔ Dàjiāngjūn,
with Fù Yǒudé and Lán Yù as his deputies,
leading an army to campaign against Nàháchū.
The torture instruments of the Jǐnyīwèi were burned,
and prisoners were transferred to the Xíngbù.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the southern suburbs.
After the ceremony was completed,
the weather was clear and bright.
Attendant ministers came forward and said:
"This is due to Your Majesty's sincerity in revering Heaven."
The Emperor said:
"What is called revering Heaven
is not merely being solemn and courteous;
it must have substance.
Heaven entrusts the duty of nurturing the people to the ruler;
if a ruler wishes to serve Heaven,
he must first care for the people.
Caring for the people
is the substance of serving Heaven.
Just as the state appoints someone to the position of a governor or magistrate,
if they cannot bring prosperity to the people,
then they have abandoned the ruler's command;
what greater disrespect is there than this?"
He further said:
"For one who is a ruler,
to father Heaven, mother Earth, and child the people,
these are all duties that must be fulfilled.
Sacrificing to Heaven and Earth
is not to pray for blessings for oneself,
but truly for all the common people under Heaven."
In the second month, on the day Rénwǔ,
a military review was conducted.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the ceremonial plowing (jítán) was performed.
In the third month, on the day Xīnhài,
Féng Shèng led his army out of Sōngtíng Guān,
and fortified Dàníng, Kuānhé, Huìzhōu, and Fùyù.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *wùzǐ*,
Zhōu Déxīng (周德xīng), Marquis of Jiāngxià, built coastal cities in Fújiàn,
and trained troops to defend against *wō* (倭) pirates.
In the sixth month, on the day *gēngzǐ*,
Chén Yōng (陳yōng), Marquis of Línjiāng, lost his way during a punitive expedition,
and died in battle.
On the day *guǐmǎo*,
Féng Shèng's (馮shèng) army crossed Jīnshān (金山).
On the day *dīngwèi*,
Nàhāchū (納哈chū) surrendered.
In the intercalary month, on the day *gēngshēn*,
the army returned to Jīnshān,
and Dū Dū Pú Yīng (濮yīng), while defending the rear, encountered an ambush
and died.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day *guǐyǒu*,
Féng Shèng's general's seal was recalled,
and he was summoned back.
Lán Yù (藍yù) took charge of military affairs.
Cáo Zhèn (曹zhèn), Marquis of Jǐngchuān, established military colonies in Pǐndiàn (品甸), Yúnnán.
In the ninth month, on the day *wùyín*,
Nàhāchū was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hǎixī.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
the Dàníng Dū Zhǐhuīshǐ Sī (大níng Dū Zhǐhuīshǐ Sī) was established.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
Cháng Mào (常mào), Duke of Zhèngguó, was settled in Lóngzhōu.
On the day *dīngwèi*,
Lán Yù was appointed Grand General for Punishing the Barbarians,
with Táng Shèngzōng (唐shèngzōng), Marquis of Yán'ān, and Guō Yīng (郭yīng), Marquis of Wǔdìng, as his deputies,
to campaign north into the desert.
In this month,
Xīníng (西níng) city was built.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *wùshēn*,
Zhū Shòu (朱shòu) was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhúlú,
and Zhāng Hè (張hè) as Marquis of Hánghǎi.
In this month,
Féng Shèng was dismissed and returned to Fèngyáng,
attending court as requested.
In the eleventh month, on the day *rényǔ*,
Chén Huán (陳huán), Marquis of Pǔdìng, and Yè Shēng (葉shēng), Marquis of Jìngníng, established military colonies in the garrisons of Dìngbiān, Yáo'ān, and Bìjié.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
Tāng Hé (湯hé) returned,
having built fifty-nine cities including Nínghǎi and Línshān.
In the twelfth month,
relief was distributed for the famine in Dēng and Lái.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Ānnán, Gāolí, Zhànchéng, Zhēnlà, Wūgān, and Wūsīzàng sent tribute.
In the twenty-first year, spring, first month, on the day *xīnsì*,
the Lùchuān (麓chuān) barbarian Sīlúnfā (思倫fā) invaded Mǎlóng Tāolángdiàn (馬lóng Tāolángdiàn),
and Dū Dū Níng Zhèng (寧zhèng) defeated him.
On the day *xīnmǎo*,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the southern altar.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
relief was distributed for the famine in Qīngzhōu,
and officials who concealed the disaster and failed to report it were arrested and tried.
In the third month, on the day *yǐhài*,
Rèn Hēngtài (任hēngtài) and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree and official positions with various ranks.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
relief was distributed for the famine in Dōngchāng.
On the day *jiǎchén*,
Mù Yīng (沐yīng) campaigned against Sīlúnfā and defeated him.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *bǐngchén*,
Lán Yù raided and defeated the Yuan successor monarch at Bǔyú'ér Hǎi (捕yú'ér Hǎi),
capturing his second son, Dìbǎonú (地保nú), along with princesses, lords, dukes, and tens of thousands of others, and returned.
In the fifth month, on the first day *jiǎxū*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the sixth month, on the day *jiǎchén*,
Tāng Hé (湯hé), Duke of Xìnguó, returned to Fèngyáng.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
Fù Yǒudé (傅yǒudé) was appointed General for Punishing the South,
with Mù Yīng and Chén Huán as his Left and Right Deputy Generals,
to lead the army against the rebellious barbarians of Dōngchuān.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *wùyín*,
Dìbǎonú was settled in Liúqiú.
In the eighth month, on the day *guǐchǒu*,
unemployed people from Zé and Lù were resettled to reclaim fields in Hénán and Hénán,
and were given paper currency to prepare farming tools,
with taxes remitted for three years.
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
Lán Yù's army returned,
and the officers and soldiers of the northern expedition were greatly rewarded.
On the day *wùchén*,
Sūn Kè (孫kè) was enfeoffed as Marquis of Quánníng.
In this month,
the emperor personally issued eight edicts to admonish military officials.
In the ninth month, on the day *bǐngxū*,
the nine princes of Qín, Jìn, Yān, Zhōu, Chǔ, Qí, Xiāng, Lǔ, and Tán came to court.
On the day *guǐsì*,
the Yuèzhōu (越zhōu) barbarian Āzī (阿zī) rebelled,
and Mù Yīng joined Fù Yǒudé to campaign against him.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *dīngwèi*,
the Dōngchuān barbarians were pacified.
In the twelfth month, on the day *rénxū*,
Lán Yù was promoted to Duke of Liángguó.
In this year,
Gāolí, Zhànchéng, Liúqiú, Xiāmluó, Zhēnlà, Sāmǎ'érhǎn, and Ānnán sent tribute.
An edict commanded Ānnán to come to court once every three years,
and to offer no more elephants or rhinoceroses.
Lí Jìlí (黎jìlí) of Ānnán assassinated his lord Wěi.
In the twenty-second year, spring, first month, on the day *bǐngxū*,
the Dà Zōngzhèng Yuàn was renamed Zōngrén Fǔ,
with Qín Wáng Shǎng (秦wáng Shǎng) as Zōngrén Lìng,
Jìn Wáng Gāng (晉wáng Gāng) and Yān Wáng Dì (燕wáng Dì) as Left and Right Zōngzhèng,
and Zhōu Wáng Sù (周wáng Sù) and Chǔ Wáng Zhēn (楚wáng Zhēn) as Left and Right Zōngrén.
On the day *dīnghài*,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the southern altar.
On the day *yǐwèi*,
Fù Yǒudé defeated Āzī at Pǔ'ān.
In the second month, on the day *jǐwèi*,
Lán Yù trained troops in Sìchuān.
On the day *rénxū*,
military officials were prohibited from interfering in civilian affairs.
On the day *guǐhài*,
Xià Dézhōng (夏dézhōng), a *qiānhù* of Húguǎng, incited the Jiǔxī (九xī) barbarians to rebel,
and Yè Shēng, Marquis of Jìngníng, campaigned against and pacified them,
and Dézhōng was executed.
In this month,
Āzī surrendered.
In the third month, on the day *gēngwǔ*,
Fù Yǒudé led various generals to establish garrisons in Sìchuān and Húguǎng,
to defend against the southwestern barbarians.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *jǐhài*,
people from the southern side of the Yangtze were resettled to fields north of the Huái River,
and were given paper currency to prepare farming tools,
with taxes remitted for three years.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
Xú Yǔngōng (徐yǔngōng), Duke of Wèiguó, Cháng Shēng (常shēng), Duke of Kāiguó, and others trained troops in Húguǎng.
On the day *jiǎyín*,
the surrendered Yuan princes were resettled to Dānlúo.
In this month,
imperial censors were dispatched to investigate officials in Shāndōng who concealed disasters and failed to report them.
In the fifth month, on the day *xīnmǎo*,
the three garrisons of Tàiníng, Wūyán, and Fúyú were established in Wùliánghā.
In the autumn, seventh month,
Fù Yǒudé and others returned.
In the eighth month, on the day *yǐmǎo*,
an edict commanded all under heaven to recommend elderly people of virtue who understood current affairs.
In this month,
the *Dà Míng Lǜ* (大míng Lǜ) was revised and codified.
In the ninth month, on the first day *bǐngyín*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the winter, eleventh month, on the day *bǐngyín*,
Jīn Zhèn (金zhèn), Marquis of Xuāndé, and others trained troops in Húguǎng.
On the day *jǐmǎo*,
Sīlúnfā sent tribute and apologized,
and Lùchuān was pacified.
In the twelfth month, on the day *jiǎchén*,
Zhōu Wáng Sù (周wáng Sù) was found guilty,
and was relocated to Yúnnán,
but was soon dismissed from there and resettled,
remaining in the capital.
Wáng Bì (王bì), Marquis of Dìngyuǎn, and others trained troops in Shānxī, Hénán, and Shǎnxī.
In this year,
Gāolí, Ānnán, Zhànchéng, Xiāmluó, and Zhēnlà sent tribute.
Yuán Yěsùdié'ér (元yěsùdié'ér) assassinated his lord Tuōgǔsītiēmù'ér (脫gǔsītiēmù'ér) and enthroned Kūntiēmù'ér (坤tiēmù'ér).
Gāolí deposed its lord *,
and then deposed its lord Chāng.
Lí Jìlí (黎jìlí) of Ānnán again assassinated his lord Rìkūn.
In the twenty-third year, spring, first month, on the day *dīngmǎo*,
Jìn Wáng Gāng (晉wáng Gāng) and Yān Wáng Dì (燕wáng Dì) led armies to campaign against Yuan Prime Minister Yǎozhù (咬zhù) and Grand Commandant Nǎ'érbùhuā (乃'érbùhuā),
and Fù Yǒudé, Duke of Yǐngguó and former General for Punishing the Barbarians, and others all submitted to their command.
On the day *jǐmǎo*,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the southern altar.
On the day *gēngchén*,
the Guìzhōu barbarians rebelled,
and Táng Shèngzōng, Marquis of Yán'ān, campaigned against and pacified them.
On the day *yǐyǒu*,
Qí Wáng Bó (齊wáng Bó) led an army to join Yān Wáng Dì in the northern expedition.
Bandits in Gànzhōu caused unrest,
and Hú Hǎi (胡hǎi), Marquis of Dōngchuān, was appointed Commander-in-Chief,
with Chén Huán, Marquis of Pǔdìng, and Yè Shēng, Marquis of Jìngníng, as Deputy Generals,
to campaign against and pacify them.
Táng Shèngzōng supervised the establishment of military colonies in the various garrisons of Guìzhōu.
In the second month, on the day *wùshēn*,
Lán Yù campaigned against and pacified the rebellious barbarians of Xīfān.
On the day *bǐngchén*,
the imperial fields were plowed.
On the day *guǐhài*,
the Yellow River breached its banks at Guīdé,
and various military and civilian forces were dispatched to block it.
In the third month, on the day *guǐsì*,
Yān Wáng Dì's army arrived at Yídu,
and Yǎozhù and others surrendered.
In the summer, fourth month,
Jí'ān Hóu Lù Zhònghēng and others were imprisoned for being part of Hú Wéiyōng's faction.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Tán Wáng Zǐ died by self-immolation.
In the intercalary month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Lán Yù pacified the rebellious Man people of Shī'nán and Zhōngjiàn.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the various Gōng and Hóu were sent back to their hometowns,
and were granted gold and silk fabrics according to their ranks.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Grand Tutor Hánguó Gōng Lǐ Shàncháng was granted death,
and Lù Zhònghēng and others were all executed.
The "Zhāoshì Jiāndǎng Lù" (Record Exposing Traitorous Faction) was compiled,
and proclaimed throughout the realm.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Lán Yù sent Fèngxiáng Hóu Zhāng Lóng to pacify the Man people of Dūyún and Sànmáo.
On the day Gēngyín,
elderly people with talent, virtue, and knowledge of classical precedents were granted official positions.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Rénchén,
the Yellow River burst its banks at Kāifēng,
and relief was provided.
On the day Guǐsì,
Chóngmíng and Hǎimén experienced strong winds and rain, and the sea overflowed;
officials were sent to provide relief,
and 250,000 commoners were conscripted to build dikes.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénshēn,
an edict prohibited recruiting petty officials and soldiers for elections.
Lán Yù returned.
This month,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Hénán, Běipíng, and Shāndōng.
In the ninth month, on the first day Gēngyín,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
relief was provided for famine in Húguǎng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
land rents were exempted for disaster-stricken areas in Shāndōng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐhài,
prisoners sentenced to death or lesser penalties were ordered to transport grain to the northern frontier to redeem themselves.
On the day Rénshēn,
the annual weaving of patterned brocade throughout the realm was abolished.
This year,
Mòlà, Hāměilǐ, Gāolí, Zhànchéng, Zhēnlà, Liúqiú, and Xiāmluó presented tribute.
In the 24th year, spring, first month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were performed in the southern suburbs.
On the day Wùshēn,
Yǐngguó Gōng Fù Yǒudé was appointed General Who Conquers Barbarians,
with Dìngyuǎn Hóu Wáng Bì and Wǔdìng Hóu Guō Yīng as his deputies,
to guard the Běipíng frontier.
On the day Dīngsì,
land rents in Shāndōng were exempted.
In the second month, on the day Rénshēn,
the sacrificial field was plowed.
In the third month, on the first day Wùzǐ,
there was a solar eclipse.
Wèiguó Gōng Xú Huīzǔ, Cáoguó Gōng Lǐ Jǐnglóng, Liángguó Gōng Lán Yù and others guarded the frontier in Shǎnxī.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Jìngníng Hóu Yè Shēng trained troops in Gānsù.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Xǔ Guān and other Jinshì graduates were granted ranks according to their achievements.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Imperial Prince Gù was enfeoffed as Qìng Wáng,
Quán as Níng Wáng,
Pián as Mín Wáng,
Huì as Gǔ Wáng,
Sōng as Hán Wáng,
Mó as Shěn Wáng,
Yíng as Ān Wáng,
Jīng as Táng Wáng,
Dòng as Yǐng Wáng,
Yì as Yī Wáng.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Yān Wáng Dì led Fù Yǒudé and other generals to sortie beyond the Great Wall,
defeated the enemy, and returned.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùxū,
the six princes, Hàn, Wèi, Gǔ, Qìng, Níng, and Mín, trained troops at Línqīng.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
an edict ordered court officials to consult the ritual systems of past dynasties
and revise the regulations for attire, residences, and utensils.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
due to prolonged drought, prisoners were reviewed.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
wealthy commoners were relocated to populate the capital.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
half of the land rents for official fields in the capital region were exempted.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Qín Wáng Shǎng, having committed an offense,
was summoned back to the capital.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Crown Prince toured and inspected Shǎnxī.
On the day Yǐhài,
Dūdū Qiānshì Liú Zhēn and Sòng Chéng attacked Hāměilǐ,
and defeated them.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
envoys were sent to instruct the Western Regions.
This month,
Japanese pirates raided Léizhōu;
Bǎihù Lǐ Yù and Zhènfǔ Táo Dǐng died in battle.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Dīngsì,
land rents for flood-stricken areas in Běipíng and Héjiān were exempted.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Man people of Wǔkāi rebelled;
Dūdū Qiānshì Máo Dǐng attacked and pacified them.
On the day Gēngxū,
the Crown Prince returned to the capital,
and Jìn Wáng Gāng came to court.
On the day Xīnhài,
relief was provided for flood disaster in Hénán.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Zhōu Wáng Sù was restored to his state.
On the day Xīnsì,
Āzī rebelled again;
Dūdū Qiānshì Hé Fú attacked and forced him to surrender.
This year,
the Yellow Registers of land and labor taxes for all prefectures and counties were completed,
totaling 10,684,435 households,
and 56,774,561 adult males.
Liúqiú, Xiāmluó, Biéshībālǐ, and Sāmǎ'érhǎn presented tribute.
As Zhànchéng had a matter of usurpation and rebellion,
their tribute was rejected.
In the 25th year, spring, first month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Zhōu Wáng Sù came to court.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Yellow River burst its banks at Yángwǔ;
troops and commoners were dispatched to block it,
and land rents in flood-stricken areas were exempted.
On the day Yǐwèi,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were performed in the southern suburbs.
Hé Fú attacked and pacified the Man people of Dūyún and Bìjié.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
death row prisoners were ordered to transport grain to the frontier.
On the day Rényín,
Jìn Wáng Gāng, Yān Wáng Dì, Chǔ Wáng Zhēn, and Xiāng Wáng Bó came to court.
In the second month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Cáoguó Gōng Lǐ Jǐnglóng and others were recalled to the capital.
Jìngníng Hóu Yè Shēng and others trained troops in Hénán, and at Lín, Gǒng, Gān, Liáng, and Yánqìng.
Dūdū Máo Dǐng and others pacified the Wǔkāi Man people.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the sacrificial field was plowed.
On the day Gēngchén,
an edict ordered seven-tenths of the military garrisons throughout the realm to engage in agricultural屯田.
In the third month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Féng Shèng and fourteen others were assigned to manage military affairs in the garrisons of Shǎnxī, Shānxī, and Hénán.
On the day Gēngyín,
Yù Wáng Guì was re-enfeoffed as Dài Wáng,
Hàn Wáng Yǎng as Sù Wáng,
and Wèi Wáng Zhí as Liáo Wáng.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Rényǐ,
Liángguó Gōng Lán Yù campaigned against Hǎndōng.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Jiànchāng Wèi Commander Yuèlǔ Tièmù'ér rebelled;
Commander Lǔ Yì defeated him.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Crown Prince Biāo passed away.
On the day Wùyín,
Dūdū Niè Wěi, Xú Sīmǎ, and Qú Néng attacked Yuèlǔ Tièmù'ér,
and upon Lán Yù's return,
they were all to be under his command.
In the fifth month, on the day Xīnsì,
Lán Yù arrived at Hǎndōng;
the invaders fled,
and he then proceeded to Jiànchāng.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
relief was provided for flood disaster in Chénzhōu and Yuánwǔ.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Xīpíng Hóu Mù Yīng died in Yúnnán.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Gēngchén,
Qín Wáng Shǎng was restored to his state.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Commander Qú Néng defeated Yuèlǔ Tièmù'ér at Shuāngláng Zhài.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Jiāngxià Hóu Zhōu Déxīng was executed for an offense.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Féng Shèng and Fù Yǒudé led Kāiguó Gōng Cháng Shēng and others to distribute themselves in Shānxī,
register commoners as soldiers,
and establish agricultural屯田 garrisons at Dàtóng and Dōngshèng,
founding sixteen garrisons (wèi).
On the day Jiǎxū,
the annual stipends were issued to the Gōng and Hóu,
and the previously granted lands were returned to the state.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Jìngníng Hóu Yè Shēng was executed for being part of Hú Wéiyōng's faction.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Imperial Grandson Yǔnwén was established as the Imperial Grand-heir.
Lǐ Chéngguì of Gāolí imprisoned his lord Yáo and enthroned himself;
he sent a memorial from his people to request a mandate,
and an edict granted it,
changing the name of his country to Cháoxiǎn.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Mù Chūn was installed as Marquis of Xīpíng,
and garrisoned Yúnnán.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Lán Yù captured Yuèlǔ Tièmù'ér
and executed him.
Lán Yù was recalled.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Duke of Sòng Fény Sg, Duke of Yǐng Fù Yǒudé, and others were concurrently appointed tutors and guardians to the Heir Apparent.
In the intercalary month, on the *wùxū* day,
Féng Shèng was appointed Commander-in-Chief,
with Fù Yǒudé as his deputy.
They trained troops in Shānxī and Hénán,
and concurrently supervised military colonies.
In this year,
Zhōngshān and Shānnán of Liúqiú,
Gāolí,
and Hāměilǐ offered tribute.
In the twenty-sixth year, in spring, in the first month, on the *wùshēn* day,
elderly commoners from all under Heaven were exempted from coming to court.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were offered in the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
Jìn Wáng Gāng led troops from Shānxī and Hénán out of the frontier.
Féng Shèng, Fù Yǒudé, Cháng Shēng, Wáng Bì, and others were recalled.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Shǔ Wáng Chūn came to court.
Duke of Liáng Lán Yù was accused of conspiracy to rebel,

and together with Marquis of Hèqìng Zhāng Yì, Marquis of Pǔdìng Chén Huán, Marquis of Jǐngchuān Cáo Zhèn, Marquis of Zhúlú Zhū Shòu, Earl of Dōngguǎn Hé Róng, Minister of Personnel Zhān Huī, and others, were all executed.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Record of Rebellious Ministers was promulgated throughout the empire.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the sacrificial field was plowed.
In the third month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Dài Wáng Guì led his guard troops out of the frontier,
subject to the command of Jìn Wáng.
Marquis of Chángxīng Gěng Bǐngwén trained troops in Shǎnxī.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Féng Shèng and Fù Yǒudé prepared defenses along the borders of Shānxī and Běipíng.
Their subordinate guard officers were all subject to the command of Jìn Wáng and Yān Wáng.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
an edict stated that important military matters of the two princes should first be reported.
On the *rénxū* day,
Marquis of Huìníng Zhāng Wēn was executed as part of Lán Yù's faction.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Xiàogǎn suffered famine.
Envoys were dispatched by post-horse to open granaries and lend grain.
An edict stated that from now on, in case of famine,
loans should be made first, and then reported,
to be established as a regulation.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Zhōu Wáng Sù came to court.
On the *gēngyín* day,
there was a drought.
An edict ordered all officials to speak frankly about successes and failures,
and to review prisoners.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
because Ānnán arbitrarily deposed and installed rulers,
its tribute was cut off.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the first day, *jiǎchén*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *wùshēn* day,
scholars such as Zhāng Zōngjùn were selected to serve in the Wénhuà Hall with officials from the Zhānshì Fǔ,
attending to the Imperial Grandson.
In the eighth month,
the five princes Qín, Jìn, Yān, Zhōu, and Qí came to court.
In the ninth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
the five princes Dài, Sù, Liáo, Qìng, and Níng came to court.
A general amnesty was granted to the remaining factions of Hú Wéiyōng and Lán Yù.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
sixty-four students from the Guózǐjiān were promoted to officials such as Provincial Administration Commissioner.
In the twelfth month,
the Yǒngjiàn Lù was promulgated to the various princes.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Zhǎowā, and Xiāmluó offered tribute.
In the twenty-seventh year, in spring, in the first month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were offered in the southern suburbs.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Lǐ Jǐnglóng was appointed General Pacifying Qiāng,
garrisoning Gānsù.
Granaries throughout the empire were opened to lend grain to the poor.
In the third month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Zhāng Xìn and others were granted metropolitan graduate degrees and positions of varying ranks.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Duke of Wèi Xú Huīzǔ and Marquis of Ānlù Wú Jié prepared defenses against Japanese pirates in Zhèjiāng.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the people were instructed to plant mulberry, jujube, and kapok trees.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
as the four quarters were largely pacified,
weapons and armor were stored away,
indicating they would not be used again.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Wú Jié and Marquis of Yǒngdìng Zhāng Quán led retired military officials
to prepare defenses against Japanese pirates in Guǎngdōng.
On the *yǐhài* day,
students from the Guózǐjiān were dispatched throughout the empire
to supervise officials and commoners in repairing water conservancy projects.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the armies of Jiē and Wén rebelled.
Grand General Níng Zhèng was appointed General Pacifying Qiāng to suppress them.
In the ninth month,
Xú Huīzǔ assumed command of all border armies in Shǎnxī.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
Duke of Yǐng Fù Yǒudé was executed for a transgression.
Āzī rebelled again.
Marquis of Xīpíng Mù Chūn defeated him.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Marquis of Dìngyuǎn Wáng Bì was executed for a transgression.
In this year,
Wūsīzàng, Liúqiú, Miǎn, Duógān, Zhǎowā, Sàmǎ'érhǎn, and Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
Ānnán offered tribute,
but it was rejected.
In the twenty-eighth year, in spring, in the first month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Jiē and Wén bandits were pacified.
Níng Zhèng led his troops with Qín Wáng Shǎng to campaign against the rebellious barbarians in Táozhōu.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were offered in the southern suburbs.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Marquis of Xīpíng Mù Chūn captured and beheaded Āzī.
Yuèzhōu was pacified.
In this month,
Zhōu Wáng Sù and Jìn Wáng Gāng led the various guard armies of Hénán and Shānxī out of the frontier,
building cities and establishing military colonies.
Yān Wáng Dì led Commander-in-Chief Zhōu Xìng out of the Liáodōng frontier.
In the second month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Duke of Sòng Féng Shèng was executed for a transgression.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to organize the populace into *lǐ* (villages) of one hundred households each.
In matters of marriage, death, illness, and hardship,
the wealthy within the *lǐ* were to provide financial assistance,
and the poor were to provide labor.
During spring plowing and autumn harvest,
they were to work together,
to teach the people harmony.
In summer, in the sixth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
an edict ordered all indigenous chieftains to establish Confucian schools.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Zhōu Xìng and others pursued the enemy from Kāiyuán to the city of Pǔdámí,
but returned without catching them.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor held court at the Fèngtiān Gate
and addressed his officials, saying:
"I have been raising troops for over forty years,
and have clearly seen sincerity and deceit.
I have punished evil and stubborn individuals,
sometimes applying punishments outside the law,
which was not the usual norm.
My successors shall only follow the statutes and the Great Proclamation;
they are not permitted to use tattooing, foot amputation, nose removal, or castration as punishments.
Any official who dares to request such shall be subject to severe penalties."
He also said:
"I abolished the position of Chancellor
and established the offices, ministries, and Censorate to manage various government affairs,
with authority centralized at the imperial court.
Successor rulers are not permitted to re-establish the Chancellor.
Any official who dares to request this shall be subject to severe penalties.
Imperial relatives shall be pardoned only for plotting rebellion.
For other crimes,
the imperial clan shall deliberate and submit their decision for imperial sanction.
Judicial offices are only permitted to report cases,
not to arrest arbitrarily.
These are inscribed in the statutes
to be observed forever."
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Grand General Yáng Wén was appointed General Conquering the South,
with Commander Hán Guān and Assistant Grand General Sòng Shèng as his deputies,
to suppress the indigenous official Zhào Zōngshòu of Lóngzhōu.
On the *wùchén* day,
Duke of Xìnguó Tāng Hé died.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Zhào Zōngshòu confessed his guilt and came to court.
Yáng Wén moved his troops to suppress the rebellious barbarians of Fèngyì and Nándān.
In the ninth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
autumn grain taxes were remitted in Jī nèi and Shāndōng.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the chapters of the Huáng Míng Zǔ Xùn (Ancestral Injunctions of the August Míng) were promulgated domestically and abroad,
stating, "Those in later generations who speak of changing the ancestral system
shall be regarded as treacherous ministers."
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the Fèngyì and Nándān barbarians were completely pacified.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénchén* day,
an edict declared that mulberry and jujube trees in Hénán and Shāndōng, and newly cultivated land after the twenty-seventh year,
should be exempted from taxation.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Xiāmluó offered tribute.
In the twenty-ninth year, in spring, in the first month, on the *rénshēn* day,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were offered in the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
Former General Conquering the Captives Hú Miǎn suppressed the Chēn and Guì barbarians,
pacifying them.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Yān Wáng Dì led his army to patrol Dàníng.
Zhōu Shìzǐ Yǒu Dùn led his army to patrol the passes of Běipíng.
In the third month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Chǔ Wáng Zhēn and Xiāng Wáng Bǎi came to court.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Yān Wáng defeated the enemy at Chèchè'ér Shān,
and then pursued and defeated them again at Wūliánghā Tū Chéng before returning.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
the land taxes for the five prefectures of Yìngtiān and Tàipíng were remitted.
In the ninth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
over two thousand five hundred retired military officials were summoned to court,
and greatly rewarded.
Each was promoted one rank.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Ānnán, Cháoxiǎn, and Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the thirtieth year, spring, the first month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
Gěng Bǐngwén was made General Who Pacifies the West (Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn),
with Guō Yīng as his deputy,
to patrol the northwestern border.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Branch Taipusi (Xíng Tàipú Sì) offices were established in Shānxī, Běipíng, Shǎnxī, Gānsù, and Liáodōng,
to manage horse administration.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Left Chief Commander (Zuǒ Dūdu) Yáng Wén established military colonies in Liáodōng.
In this month,
bandits rose in Miǎn Xiàn,
and an imperial edict commanded Gěng Bǐngwén to suppress them.
In the second month, on the *gēngyín* day,
the barbarians of Shuǐxī rebelled.
Assistant Chief Commander (Dūdu Qiānshì) Gù Chéng was made General Who Pacifies the South (Zhēngnán Jiāngjūn),
and suppressed them.
In the third month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Chén Mǒu and others were granted the titles of *jìnshì jíyǐ* and *chūshēn*, with different grades.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the barbarians of Gǔzhōu rebelled.
Wú Dé, commander of a thousand households (Qiānhù) in Lónglǐ, and Jǐng Fú, a garrison commander (Zhènfǔ), died in battle.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Chief Commander (Dū Zhǐhuī) Qí Ràng was made General Who Pacifies the Qiāng (Píngqiāng Jiāngjūn),
to suppress them.
On the *rényín* day,
the Shuǐxī barbarians were pacified.
In the fifth month, on the first day, *rénzǐ*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Zhū Zhēn, Prince of Chǔ, and Zhū Bǎi, Prince of Xiāng, led armies to suppress the Gǔzhōu barbarians.
In the sixth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
the *gòngshì* who passed the Ministry of Rites re-examination, Hán Kèzhōng and others, were granted the titles of *jìnshì jíyǐ* and *chūshēn*, with different grades.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Ōuyáng Lún, commander of the imperial son-in-law (Fùmǎ Dūwèi), was granted death for his crimes.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
the Hé River burst its banks at Kāifēng.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Lǐ Jǐnglóng was made Grand General Who Conquers the Barbarians (Zhēnglǔ Dàjiāngjūn),
training troops in Hénán.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
the bandits of Hàn and Miǎn were pacified.
On the *wùchén* day,
Dāo Gànmèng, a native chieftain (tǔqiú) of Lùchuān Píngmiǎn, expelled his Pacification Commissioner (Xuānwèishǐ) Sī Lúnfā and rebelled.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Chief Commander (Dūdu) Yáng Wén was made General Who Conquers the Barbarians (Zhēnglǔ Jiāngjūn),
replacing Qí Ràng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
sea transport to Liáodōng was suspended.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Gěng Bǐngwén trained troops in Shǎnxī.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the reconstruction of the temple for the Former Sages at the Guózǐjiān (National Academy) was completed.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Mù Chūn was made Vanguard General Who Conquers the Barbarians (Zhēnglǔ Qiánjiāngjūn),
with Chief Commander (Dūdu) Hé Fú and others as his deputies,
to suppress Dāo Gànmèng.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Zhānchéng, Cháoxiǎn, Xiāmluó, Wūsīzàng, and Níbālā presented tribute.
In the thirty-first year, spring, the first month, on the *rénxū* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
envoys were dispatched to Shāndōng and Hénán to inspect farming.
In the second month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Japanese pirates raided Nínghǎi.
Commander (Zhǐhuī) Táo Duó defeated them.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Gǔzhōu barbarians were pacified,
and Yáng Wén was summoned back.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Assistant Chief Commander (Dūdu Qiānshì) Xú Kǎi suppressed the Mǒxiē barbarians.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
court officials requested to suppress Cháoxiǎn due to repeated provocations,
but it was not permitted.
In the fifth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Mù Chūn attacked Dāo Gànmèng,
and severely defeated him.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the emperor fell ill.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Chief Commander (Dūdu) Yáng Wén followed Zhū Dì, Prince of Yān,
and Marquis of Wǔdìng (Wǔdìng Hóu) Guō Yīng followed Zhū Zhí, Prince of Liáo,
to defend Kāipíng,
all under the command of the Prince of Yān.
In the intercalary month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
the emperor's illness worsened significantly.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
he passed away in the Western Palace,
aged seventy-one.
His last edict stated:
"I received the mandate of Heaven for thirty-one years,
with worries and dangers accumulating in my heart,
working diligently day and night without slack,
striving for the benefit of the people.
Alas, I rose from humble origins,
without the extensive knowledge of the ancients.
My love for good and hatred for evil
falls far short.
Now that I have attained the natural principle of all things,
what sorrow or lamentation is there?
The Imperial Grandson Zhū Yǔnwén is benevolent, enlightened, filial, and friendly;
the hearts of all under Heaven turn to him.
He should ascend the great throne.
Internal and external civil and military officials should unite their hearts to assist him in governing,
to bring peace to my people.
For funeral sacrifices and objects,
do not use gold or jade.
The mountains and rivers of the Xiàolíng Mausoleum should remain as they are,
without alteration.
All officials and people under Heaven
should mourn for three days,
then all should remove their mourning attire,
without hindering marriages.
The princes should remain in their respective states,
and not come to the capital.
For anything not covered by this decree,
act according to the spirit of this decree."
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
he was buried in the Xiàolíng Mausoleum.
His posthumous title was Gāo Huángdì,
and his temple name was Tàizǔ.
In the first year of Yǒnglè,
his full posthumous title was "Shèngshén Wǔwǔ Qīnmíng Qǐyùn Jùndé Chénggōng Tǒngtiān Dàxiào Gāo Huángdì".
In the seventeenth year of Jiājìng,
the title was further augmented to "Kāitiān Xíngdào Zhàojì Lìjí Dàshèng Zhìshén Rénwén Yìwǔ Jùndé Chénggōng Gāo Huángdì".
The Emperor was endowed by Heaven with wisdom and courage,
unifying the land.
His military strategies and civil administration
surpassed those of the lords of Hàn, Táng, and Sòng.
At the very beginning of his founding,
he was able to deeply consider and observe changes,
and systematically plan,
having a clear calculation for success.
He once discussed the strategy for conquering the realm with his officials,
saying:
"I encountered a time of chaos and disarray.
When I first rose from my hometown,
my original intention was merely to preserve myself.
But since crossing the Jiāng River,
observing the actions of the various warlords,
they only brought harm to the common people,
and Zhāng Shìchéng and Chén Yǒuliàng were especially great scourges.
Shìchéng relied on his wealth,
Yǒuliàng relied on his strength,
while I alone had nothing to rely on.
I merely did not delight in killing,
spread trustworthiness and righteousness,
practiced frugality,
and worked with you, my ministers, with one heart to succeed.
Initially, when confronting the two rebels,
Shìchéng was particularly close,
and some suggested we should attack him first.
I believed that Yǒuliàng was arrogant,
and Shìchéng was narrow-minded.
The arrogant tend to stir up trouble,
and the narrow-minded have no long-term vision.
Therefore, I first attacked Yǒuliàng.
During the Battle of Póyáng,
Shìchéng ultimately could not advance a single step beyond Gūsū to assist him.
If we had attacked Shìchéng first,
Zhéxī would have fortified itself and held firm,
and Yǒuliàng would certainly have come with his entire army,
and we would have been attacked from front and rear.
Once the two rebels were eliminated,
to pacify the Central Plains in the north,
the reason we first took Shāndōng, then Héluò,
and stopped our troops at Tóngguān without rushing to take Qín and Lǒng,
was because Kuòkuò Tièmùér, Lǐ Sīqí, and Zhāng Sīdào were all veterans of many battles,
and would not easily surrender.
If pressed, they would concentrate their forces in one area,
and it would not be easy to pacify them quickly.
Therefore, unexpectedly,
we turned our banners north.
Once Yāndū was captured,
then we campaigned west.
With their hopes dashed and power exhausted, Zhāng and Lǐ
were conquered without a fight.
However, Kuòkuò still resisted fiercely without yielding.
If we had not yet captured Yāndū,
and had rashly engaged them,
victory and defeat would have been uncertain."
The Emperor's heroic talent and grand strategy,
in assessing the enemy and securing victory,
were consistently like this.
Thus, he was able to quell chaos and rebellion,
and possess the realm.
As the saying goes,
"The way of Heaven favors those who rise later,"
how could this be accidental?
A eulogy states: Tài zǔ, with his intelligent and divinely martial natural endowments,
embraced the aspiration to save the world and pacify the people.
Seizing the opportune moment and responding to the call of destiny,
heroes followed him,
suppressing chaos and crushing the strong.
In fifteen years, he established his imperial enterprise.
Rising from commoner status,
he swiftly pacified the realm,
a feat unprecedented since the Western Hàn dynasty.
He rectified the laxity and decay of the Yuán government,
governing with a stern hand.
Yet, he was able to礼致 (treat with respect and summon) elderly scholars,
examine and establish rites and music,
clarify the meanings of the Classics,
and uphold orthodox learning.
He showed grace to the fallen dynasty,
cleansed the officialdom,
repaired human relationships,
promoted moral education,
and rectified the status of the imperial harem.
Internal governance was purified,
eunuchs were forbidden from interfering in politics,
and the officials of the Five Bureaus and Six Ministries mutually restrained each other.
He established military garrisons for farming,
ensuring ample soldiers and provisions.
Through military means, he settled calamities and chaos;
through civil means, he brought about great peace.
Tài zǔ truly embodied both.
Furthermore, he admired integrity and principle,
allowing Cài Zǐyīng to return north.
In his later years, his concern for the people grew even more pressing.
He once, in a single year, opened tens of thousands of irrigation canals and dikes to benefit agriculture and prevent drought and flood.
Because of this, his descendants held the throne for over two hundred years.
Scholars valued integrity,
and common households were prosperous.
Even today, his descendants still enjoy his favor,
like the Dōnglóu and Báimǎ families,
who generation after generation maintain their ancestral sacrifices.
This is not without reason!
Collation Notes
Annals, Chapter Four: Gōngmǐn Dì
Gōngmǐn Huì Huángdì, personal name Yǔnwén,
was the grandson of Tài zǔ
and the second son of Yìwén Tàizǐ.
His mother was Consort Lǚ.
The Emperor was born intelligent and fond of learning,
and of utmost filial piety.
At fourteen,
he attended to Yìwén Tàizǐ during his illness,
not leaving his side day or night.
Two years later,
the Crown Prince died,
and he wasted away from grief during mourning.
Tài zǔ caressed him and said,
"You are truly purely filial,
but do you not think of me?"
In the ninth month of the twenty-fifth year of Hóngwǔ,
he was established as the Imperial Grandson.
In the twenty-ninth year,
the rituals for the various princes to see the Crown Prince were re-established.
After the formal audience, they performed family rites in the inner hall,
as all the princes were senior relatives.
Initially,
Tài zǔ ordered the Crown Prince to review and decide on memorials.
The Crown Prince, being benevolent and kind,
often reduced sentences in criminal cases.
At this time, this duty was entrusted to the Imperial Grandson,
who also assisted with leniency.
He once petitioned Tài zǔ,
to widely study the Classics on rites,
and consult the penal laws of successive dynasties,
and revised seventy-three excessively harsh articles in the Hóngwǔ Code.
Everyone in the realm praised his virtue.
In the intercalary fifth month of the thirty-first year,
Tài zǔ passed away.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
he ascended the imperial throne.
A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and the following year was designated the first year of Jiànwén.
On that same day,
Gāo Huángdì was buried at Xiàolíng.
An edict commanded a three-year mourning period.
The assembled officials requested to shorten it from years to months.
The Emperor said,
"I am not emulating the ancients by remaining in silent mourning.
In court, I wear mourning attire (má miǎncháng);
when retired, I wear the deepest mourning (qīcuī) and carry a staff and wear a head-cord (zhàngdié);
for food, I partake of thick gruel;
the suburban and ancestral temple sacrifices are performed according to normal rites."
Thereupon, he ordered the establishment of the rituals and their presentation.
On the Bǐngshēn day,
an edict ordered civil officials of the fifth rank and above, as well as prefectural and county officials, to each recommend those they knew,
with punishment for those who recommended unsuitable individuals.
In the sixth month,
prefectures and counties were merged,
and redundant officials were eliminated.
Qí Tài, Assistant Minister of War, was made Minister of War.
Huáng Zǐchéng, Compiler of the Hànlín Academy, was made Grand Master of Ceremonies,
both participating in military and state affairs.
In the autumn, seventh month,
Fāng Xiáorú, Professor of Hànzhōng Prefecture, was summoned to be a Lecturer in the Hànlín Academy.
An edict proclaimed lenient governance,
pardoning criminals and remitting overdue taxes.
In the eighth month,
Zhōu Wáng Shū was found guilty,
deposed as a commoner,
and exiled to Yúnnán.
An edict exempted one person
from military service for all families in the garrisons of Xīngzhōu, Yíngzhōu, and Kāipíng
who had their entire family enrolled in the military.
For soldiers in garrisons throughout the empire who were sole surviving males,
they were released to become commoners.
In the ninth month,
Mù Chūn, Marquis of Xīpíng and Commander-in-Chief of Yúnnán, died in the field.
Hé Fú, Left Assistant General, took over command of his troops.
In the winter, eleventh month,
Zhāng Bǐng, Assistant Minister of Works, was made Administration Commissioner of Běipíng.
Xiè Guì and Zhāng Xìn were put in charge of the Běipíng Regional Military Commission,
to investigate clandestine affairs in Yān.
An edict sought candid advice
and recommended talented and virtuous recluses from the mountains and forests.
On the Guǐmǎo day of the twelfth month,
Hé Fú defeated and beheaded Dāogānmèng,
and Lùchuān was pacified.
In this month,
half of the land tax for the following year was remitted throughout the empire.
Branded soldiers and prisoners were released to return to their hometowns.
In this year,
Xiānluó and Zhànchéng sent tribute.
In the spring, first month, Guǐyǒu day of Jiànwén's first year,
the court audience was held,
without music.
On the Gēngchén day,
a great sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the southern suburb,
with Tài zǔ honored as co-sacrificed.
The Veritable Records of Tài zǔ were compiled.
In the second month,
the deceased imperial father was posthumously honored as Xiàokāng Huángdì,
with the temple name Xīngzōng;
his mother, Lady Cháng, was honored as Xiàokāng Huánghòu.
His birth mother, Consort Lǚ, was honored as Huáng Tàihòu.
Consort Mǎ was enfeoffed as Empress.
His younger brother Yǔntēng was enfeoffed as Wú Wáng,
Yǔnjiān as Héng Wáng,
and Yǔnxī as Xú Wáng.
His eldest son Wénkuí was established as Crown Prince.
An edict was proclaimed throughout the empire,
calling for hidden talents.
Elderly commoners were bestowed with rice, meat, floss, and silk;
widowers, widows, orphans, childless, disabled, and infirm were officially cared for.
Agriculture was promoted,
schools were established,
officials were evaluated,
disaster-stricken poor people were relieved,
filial and chaste individuals were commended,
unburied bones were interred,
and barren land taxes were remitted.
Military households in garrisons that had no heirs were exempted from further levies.
An edict forbade the various princes from controlling civil and military officials and scholars,
and reformed the internal and external official systems of all ranks.
In the third month,
a ceremony was held for the first teacher, Kǒngzǐ.
Unnecessary duties in all government departments were abolished throughout the empire.
Grandees-General Sòng Zhōng, Xú Kǎi, and Gěng Huán led troops to garrison Kāipíng, Línqīng, and Shānhǎiguān.
Troops from the Běipíng and Yǒngqīng garrisons were deployed to Zhāngdé and Shùndé.
Assistant Ministers Bào Zhāo, Xià Yuánjí, and twenty-four others were appointed as Investigation Commissioners,
to tour the empire.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
there was an earthquake in the capital,
and candid advice was sought.
In the summer, fourth month,
Xiāng Wáng Bó immolated himself.
Qí Wáng Fú and Dài Wáng Guì were found guilty,
and deposed as commoners.
Yān Wáng's heir-apparent Gāo Chì and his younger brothers Gāo Xù and Gāo Suì were sent back to Běipíng.
In the sixth month,
Mín Wáng Pián was found guilty,
deposed as a commoner,
and exiled to Zhāngzhōu.
On the Jǐyǒu day,
Ní Liàng, a hundred-household commander of the Yānshān Guard, initiated a rebellion.
Yān banner officials such as Yú Liàng were executed.
An edict reprimanded Yān Wáng Dì
and arrested officials of the princely establishment.
Zhāng Xìn, Běipíng Regional Commander, defected to Yān.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day of Guǐyǒu,
Zhū Dì, the Prince of Yān, raised troops in rebellion,
killing the Administration Commissioner Zhāng Bǐng and the Regional Military Commissioner Xiè Guì.
The Chief Clerk Gě Chéng, Commander Lú Zhèn, and Professor Yú Fēngchén died.
Policy Counselor Guō Zī, Vice Commissioner Mò Lín, Reviewer Lǚ Zhèn, and others surrendered to Yān.
Commander Mǎ Xuān fled to Jìzhōu,
and Yú Tián fled to Jūyōng.
Sòng Zhōng hastened to Běipíng,
but upon hearing of the uprising, retreated to secure Huáilái.
