Tōngzhōu, Zūnhuà, and Mìyún successively surrendered to Yān.
On the day of Bǐngzǐ,
the Yān army captured Jìzhōu,
and Mǎ Xuān died in battle.
On the day of Jǐmǎo,
the Yān army captured Jūyōng Pass.
On the day of Jiǎshēn,
Huáilái was captured.
Sòng Zhōng and Yú Tián were captured and died.
Regional Military Commissioners Péng Jù and Sūn Tài died fighting bravely.
Commander Guō Liàng of Yǒngpíng and others rebelled and surrendered to Yān.
On the day of Rénchén,
Zhū Huì, the Prince of Gǔ, fled from Xuānfǔ to the capital, Jīngshī.
The Marquis of Chángxīng, Gěng Bǐngwén, was appointed Commander-in-Chief for Quelling the Barbarians,
and the Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Lǐ Jiān and Regional Military Commissioner Níng Zhōng were appointed Left and Right Deputy Commanders-in-Chief, respectively,
to lead the army to suppress Yān.
Sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Altars of Land and Grain.
The Prince of Yān was removed from the imperial clan registry.
An imperial edict stated:
"The nation is not blessed.
My close relatives have repeatedly plotted usurpation.
Last year,
Zhū Sù, the commoner Prince of Zhōu, unlawfully rebelled,
and the charges implicated the three princes of Yān, Qí, and Xiāng.
Because of our kinship,
We only punished Sù's crimes.
This year, Zhū Fú, the Prince of Qí, plotted rebellion,
also conspiring with Dì and Bǎi.
Bǎi confessed his guilt and immolated himself,
and Fú has been deposed as a commoner.
As Dì is the closest of our relatives,
We were reluctant to thoroughly investigate his involvement.
But now he has raised an army and stirred up rebellion,
threatening the imperial ancestral altars.
He has sinned against Heaven and Earth and the ancestors;
justice does not permit leniency.
Therefore, We have mobilized a large army
to inflict punishment upon him.
You, Our officials, common people, and soldiers, both within and outside the capital,
should each uphold loyalty and righteousness,
be of one heart with the state,
sweep away this rebellious atmosphere,
and forever secure an era of perfect peace."
Soon after, the Marquis of Ānlù, Wú Jié;
the Marquis of Jiāngyīn, Wú Gāo;
Regional Military Commissioner Gěng Huán;
and Regional Military Commissioners Shèng Yōng, Pān Zhōng, Yáng Sōng, Gù Chéng, Xú Kǎi, Lǐ Yǒu, Chén Huī, and Píng Ān
were ordered to advance simultaneously along separate routes.
A Bureau of Administration for Pacifying Yān was established in Zhēndìng,
with Minister Bào Zhāo overseeing its affairs.
In the eighth month, on the day of Jǐyǒu,
Gěng Bǐngwén's army reached Zhēndìng.
Xú Kǎi was stationed in Héjiān,
and Pān Zhōng and Yáng Sōng were stationed in Màozhōu.
On the day of Rénzǐ,
the Yān army captured Xióngxiàn.
Pān Zhōng and Yáng Sōng fought at Yuèyàngqiáo,
and were captured.
Màozhōu fell.
On the day of Rénxū,
Gěng Bǐngwén and the Yān army fought north of the Hūtuó River,
suffering a defeat.
Lǐ Jiān, Níng Zhōng, and Gù Chéng were captured.
Bǐngwén retreated to secure Zhēndìng.
The Yān army attacked it but could not overcome it,
and then withdrew.
Zhū Zhí, the Prince of Liáo, and Zhū Quán, the Prince of Níng, were summoned back to the capital.
Quán did not arrive,
so an edict stripped him of his guards.
On the day of Dīngmǎo,
Lǐ Jǐnglóng, Duke of Cáo, was appointed Commander-in-Chief for Quelling the Barbarians,
replacing Gěng Bǐngwén.
In the ninth month, on the day of Wùchén,
Wú Gāo, Gěng Huán, and Yáng Wén led troops from Liáodōng
to besiege Yǒngpíng.
On the day of Wùyín,
Jǐnglóng's army reached Héjiān.
The Yān army reinforced Yǒngpíng,
and Wú Gāo retreated to secure Shānhǎiguān.
In the tenth month of winter,
the Yān army attacked Dàníng via a shortcut through Liújiākǒu, capturing it.
Its defending commander, Zhū Jiàn, died.
Grand General Liú Zhēn and Regional Military Commissioner Chén Hēng reinforced Dàníng.
Hēng rebelled and surrendered to Yān.
The Yān forces returned to Běipíng with Zhū Quán, the Prince of Níng, and the troops of the Wányán Three Guards.
On the day of Xīnhài,
Lǐ Jǐnglóng besieged Běipíng,
and the Yān army returned to relieve it.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Xīnwèi,
Lǐ Jǐnglóng and the Yān army fought at Zhèngcūnbà,
suffering a defeat.
He fled to Dézhōu,
and all his armies collapsed.
Zhū Dì, the Prince of Yān, again submitted a letter to the court.
The Emperor dismissed Qí Tài and Huáng Zǐchéng from office,
but kept them in the capital.
In the first month of spring of the second year, on the first day of Bǐngyín,
an edict was issued for officials coming to court from throughout the empire not to offer congratulations.
On the day of Dīngmǎo,
sacrifices were offered to the Former Master Kǒngzǐ.
In the second month,
the Yān army captured Wèizhōu
and advanced to attack Dàtóng.
Lǐ Jǐnglóng came from Dézhōu to reinforce it,
and the Yān army returned to Běipíng.
Luò Qiān, the Prefect of Bǎodìng, rebelled and surrendered to Yān.
On the day of Jiǎzǐ,
the Censorate was reinstated as the Imperial Censorate.
Land taxes in Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng were equalized.
An edict stated:
"The state has righteous levies,
but the taxes in Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng are uniquely heavy,
and all the official lands in Sūzhōu and Sōngjiāng are treated as private tax lands.
While this was done to punish for a time,
it cannot be a fixed rule.
Now, all are granted reductions and exemptions,
with no more than one dou per mu.
People from Sūzhōu and Sōngjiāng can still hold official positions in the Ministry of Revenue."
In the third month, on the first day of Bǐngyín,
there was a solar eclipse.
Hú Guǎng and others were granted the degrees of Jìnshì and Xuèshēn with varying ranks.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day of Jǐwèi,
Lǐ Jǐnglóng and the Yān army fought at Báigōu River,
and he defeated them.
The next day, they fought again,
and he suffered a defeat.
Regional Military Commissioner Qú Néng, the Marquis of Yuèsuì Yú Yuān, Commander Téng Jù, and others all died in battle.
Jǐnglóng fled to Dézhōu.
In the fifth month, on the day of Xīnwèi,
he fled to Jǐnán.
The Yān army captured Dézhōu,
and then attacked Jǐnán.
On the day of Gēngchén,
Jǐnglóng suffered a defeat beneath the city walls
and fled south.
Policy Counselor Tiě Xuàn and Regional Military Commissioner Shèng Yōng exerted all their strength to resist them.
In the sixth month, on the day of Jǐyǒu,
Assistant Minister of the Imperial Seal Lǐ Déchéng was sent to admonish Yān to cease hostilities.
In the eighth month of autumn, on the day of Guǐsì,
the Chéngtiānmén gate caught fire,
and an edict sought frank advice.
On the day of Wùshēn,
Shèng Yōng and Tiě Xuàn defeated the Yān army,
the siege of Jǐnán was lifted,
and Dézhōu was recovered.
In the ninth month,
an edict ordered the recording of descendants of meritorious officials who were disgraced or deposed during the Hóngwǔ era.
On the day of Xīnwèi,
Shèng Yōng was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lìchéng.
Tiě Xuàn was promoted to Administration Commissioner of Shāndōng,
participating in military affairs,
and soon advanced to Minister of War.
Yōng was appointed General for Pacifying Yān,
with Regional Military Commissioners Chén Huī and Píng Ān as his deputies.
Yōng was stationed in Dézhōu,
Píng Ān and Wú Jié were stationed in Dìngzhōu,
and Xú Kǎi was stationed in Cāngzhōu.
In the tenth month of winter,
Lǐ Jǐnglóng was recalled,
pardoned, and not executed.
On the day of Gēngshēn,
the Yān army attacked Cāngzhōu,
and Xú Kǎi was captured.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Jiǎwǔ,
the Yān army encroached upon Jìníng
and approached Dōngchāng.
On the day of Yǐmǎo,
Shèng Yōng defeated them,
beheading their general Zhāng Yù.
On the day of Bǐngchén,
they fought again,
and he defeated them once more.
The Yān army fled to Guǎntáo.
Yōng's army's morale greatly surged.
He dispatched urgent orders to all stationed armies to unite and attack Yān,
cutting off their retreat.
In the spring of the third year, on the *xīnyǒu* day of the first month, the first day of the lunar month,
the "Coagulated Mandate Divine Treasure" (*Níngmìng Shénbǎo*) was completed.
It was announced to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple.
The Emperor received congratulations and tributes at Fèngtiān Diàn.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Wú Jié and Píng Ān ambushed the Yān forces at Shēnzhōu,
but were unsuccessful.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburban altar.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
a sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào,
announcing the victory at Dōngchāng.
Qí Tài and Huáng Zǐchéng's official positions were restored.
In the third month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Shèng Yōng defeated the Yān forces at Jiāhé,
beheading their general Tán Yuān.
A second battle was unfavorable,
and commander Zhūang Dé, Chǔ Zhì, and others fought to their deaths.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
they fought again,
and were routed.
Yōng fled to Dézhōu.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Grand Commandant Hé Fú reinforced Dézhōu.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Qí Tài and Huáng Zǐchéng were demoted,
and a decree was issued to Yān to cease hostilities.
In the intercalary month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Wú Jié and Píng Ān engaged the Yān forces at Gǎochéng,
suffered a rout,
and returned to defend Zhēndìng.
The Yān forces plundered Zhēndìng, Shùndé, Guǎngpíng, and Dàmíng.
Dì submitted a memorial requesting the recall of the various generals and a cessation of hostilities.
He sent the Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, Xuē Yán, to report on this.
In this month,
the rituals were completed,
and promulgated throughout the empire.
In the summer of the fifth month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
Shèng Yōng attempted to block the Yān supply route with his troops,
but failed.
Dì again sent an envoy with a memorial,
but the envoy was imprisoned.
In the sixth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
the Yān general Lǐ Yuǎn raided Pèixiàn,
burning the grain ships.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Grand Commandant Yuán Yǔ ambushed them,
but was routed.
In the autumn of the seventh month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Yān forces plundered Zhāngdé.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Píng Ān attacked Běipíng from Zhēndìng.
On the *rényín* day,
the Grand Commandant of Dàtóng, Fáng Zhāo, led his troops from Zǐjīng Guān towards Bǎodìng,
stationing them at Xīshuǐzhài in Yìzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Píng Ān fought the Yān general Liú Jiāng at Běipíng,
suffered a rout,
and returned to defend Zhēndìng.
In the winter of the tenth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
the generals at Zhēndìng sent troops to reinforce Fáng Zhāo,
and fought the Prince of Yān at Qíméi Shān,
suffering a rout.
In the eleventh month, on the *rénchén* day,
the Regional Commander of Liáodōng, Yáng Wén, attacked Yǒngpíng,
and fought Liú Jiāng at Chānglí,
suffering a rout.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Píng Ān defeated the Yān general Lǐ Bīn at Yángcūn.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
the Yān forces burned the military supplies at Zhēndìng.
An imperial edict ordered that eunuchs dispatched on missions who abused officials and common people
should be arrested and punished by the local authorities.
In this month,
the Consort-General Méi Yīn garrisoned Huái'ān.
The Veritable Records of Tàizǔ were completed.
In the spring of the fourth year, in the first month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
the former Prince of Zhōu, Zhū Sù, was recalled from Ménghuà
to reside in the capital.
The Yān forces successively captured Dōng'ē, Dōngpíng, Wénshàng, Yǎnzhōu, and Jìyáng.
The Chief Clerk of Dōngpíng, Zhèng Huá,
and the Instructor of Jìyáng, Wáng Xǐng, both died there.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Duke of Wèi, Xú Huīzǔ, led his army to reinforce Shāndōng.
The Yān forces captured Pèixiàn.
The county magistrate, Yán Bówěi, the chief clerk, Táng Zǐqīng, and the jail warden, Huáng Qiān, died there.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
they approached Xúzhōu.
In the second month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
Grand Commandants Hé Fú, Chén Huī, and Píng Ān's armies were at Jìníng,
and Shèng Yōng's army was on the Huái River.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the ranks and meritorious titles for officials were revised.
In the third month,
the Yān forces attacked Sùzhōu.
Píng Ān pursued them to Féihé,
beheaded their general Wáng Zhēn,
but encountered an ambush and was routed.
Sùzhōu fell.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Hé Fú and Píng Ān defeated the Yān forces at Xiǎohé,
beheading their general Chén Wén.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Xú Huīzǔ and others defeated the Yān forces at Qíméi Shān,
beheading their general Lǐ Bīn.
The Yān forces were afraid
and planned to return north.
Meanwhile, the Emperor heard a false rumor,
believing the Yān forces had already gone north,
and recalled Huīzǔ.
Hé Fú's army was also isolated.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the various generals and the Yān forces fought a major battle at Língbì,
and were routed.
Chén Huī, Píng Ān, Minister of Rites Chén Xìngshàn, and Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Péng Yǔmíng were all captured.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Yáng Wén led Liáodōng troops to Jìnán,
but they disintegrated at Zhígū.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Shèng Yōng's army disintegrated on the Huái River.
The Yān forces crossed the Huái River
and advanced towards Yángzhōu.
Commander Wáng Lǐ and others rebelled and surrendered to Yān.
Censor Wáng Bīn and Commander Chóng Gāng died there.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Yān forces reached Liùhé.
The various armies met them in battle
and were routed.
On the *rényín* day,
an imperial edict was issued to the whole empire to send loyal armies to defend the throne.
Censor-in-chief Liàn Zǐníng, Vice Minister Huáng Guān, and compiler Wáng Shúyīng were dispatched to raise troops from different routes.
Qí Tài and Huáng Zǐchéng were recalled.
The Prefect of Sūzhōu, Yáo Shàn, the Prefect of Níngbō, Wáng Jìn, the Prefect of Huīzhōu, Chén Yánhuí, and the Magistrate of Lèpíng, Zhāng Yánfāng, each raised troops to defend the capital.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Princess Qìngchéng was sent to the Yān army
to negotiate ceding territory and cessation of hostilities.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Shèng Yōng led a naval force and defeated the Yān forces at Púzǐkǒu.
A subsequent battle was unfavorable.
Assistant Grand Commandant Chén Xuān, with his naval force, rebelled and joined Yān.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Yān forces crossed the Jiāng River.
Shèng Yōng fought at Gāozī Gǎng
and was routed.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Zhènjiāng garrison commander Tóng Jùn rebelled and surrendered to Yān.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Yān forces reached Lóngtán.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the various princes were ordered to guard the capital city.
Lǐ Jǐnglóng, along with Minister of War Rú Cháng and Grand Commandant Wáng Zuǒ, were sent to the Yān army
to reiterate the previous agreement.
On the *rénxū* day,
Prince Gǔ, Zhū Huì, and Prince Ān, Zhū Yíng, were again sent.
Neither was listened to.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
envoys were sent out with sealed letters
to urge the loyalist armies to come.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Yān forces attacked Jīnchuánmén.
Left Grand Commandant Xú Zēngshòu plotted an internal betrayal
and was executed.
Prince Gǔ, Zhū Huì, and Lǐ Jǐnglóng rebelled,
admitting the Yān forces,
and the capital city fell.
A fire broke out in the palace,
and the Emperor's fate was unknown.
The Prince of Yān sent eunuchs to retrieve the Emperor and Empress's bodies from the fire,
and they were buried eight days later on the *rénshēn* day.
Some say the Emperor escaped through a secret tunnel.
In the fifth year of Zhèngtǒng,
a monk came from Yúnnán to Guǎngxī,
falsely claiming to be Emperor Jiànwén.
The Prefect of Sī'ēn, Cén Yīng, reported it to the court.
Upon interrogation,
he was found to be Yáng Xíngxiáng from Jūnzhōu,
already over ninety years old.
He was imprisoned
and died four months later.
Twelve conspiring monks
were all exiled to Liáodōng.
Afterwards, in the regions of Diān, Qián, Bā, and Shǔ,
there were circulating stories of the Emperor's travels during his time as a monk.
During the Zhèngdé, Wànlì, and Chóngzhēn reigns,
various officials requested the re-burial of the Emperor and Empress
and the addition of a temple name and posthumous title.
All were referred to the ministries for deliberation,
but never carried out.
In the first year of Dàqīng Qiánlóng,
an imperial edict ordered court officials to convene and deliberate,
and he was posthumously honored as Gōngmǐn Huì Huángdì.
An appreciation states: Emperor Huì’s natural disposition was benevolent and magnanimous.
At the beginning of his reign,
he cultivated virtuous individuals and loved learning,
summoning and employing Fāng Xiàorú and others.
Regarding institutions and regulations,
he was keen to restore ancient practices.
Once, due to illness, he was late for court.
Yǐn Chānglóng submitted a remonstrance,
and he immediately took deep personal blame,
broadcasting the memorial to both court and country.
He also exempted single men from military service
and reduced the heavy taxes in Sūzhōu and Sōngjiāng,
all of which were great benefits to the people.
However, after the revolution,
the reign era was again called Hóngwǔ.
Thereafter, his descendants, ministers, and commoners considered recording this to be a sensitive matter,
and doubts circulated among the populace,
leading to unavoidable errors and falsehoods.
Furthermore, after the current sagely dynasty,
it was settled through discussion,
honoring his name as Yī Huì,
and thus his imperial virtue was glorified.
How admirable!
Collation Notes
Basic Annals V: Chéngzǔ I

Emperor Chéngzǔ Qǐtiān Hóngdào Gāomíng Zhàoyùn Shèngwǔ Shéngōng Chúnrén Zhìxiào Wén (Chéngzǔ, who opened the heavens, broadly cultivated the Dao, was enlightened and wise, initiated fortune, was sagely and martial, divine and meritorious, perfectly benevolent and utterly filial, and was a cultivated emperor), personal name Dì,
was the fourth son of Tàizǔ.
His mother was Empress Xiàocí Gāo.
In the third year of Hóngwǔ (1370),
he was enfeoffed as the Prince of Yān.
In the thirteenth year (1380),
he went to his fiefdom in Běipíng.
The Prince was remarkably imposing in appearance
and had a handsome beard.
He was intelligent, brave, possessed great strategic vision,
and was capable of sincerely trusting and employing others.
In the twenty-third year (1390),
he joined the Prince of Jìn in campaigning against Nǎi’érbùhuā.
The Prince of Jìn was timid and dared not advance,
but the Prince (of Yān) doubled his march to Yídu Mountain,
captured the entire enemy force, and returned.
Tàizǔ was greatly pleased.
Thereafter, he repeatedly led various generals on campaigns,
and the emperor also ordered the Prince to command the soldiers and cavalry along the border.
The Prince’s prestige and reputation greatly increased.
In the intercalary fifth month of the thirty-first year of Hóngwǔ (1398),
Tàizǔ passed away.
The Imperial Grandson ascended the throne,
and the imperial will decreed that all princes should remain in their respective states
and not come to the capital.
The Prince (of Yān) set out from Běipíng to attend the mourning rites,
but upon hearing the edict, he stopped.
At that time, many princes, being senior in rank and commanding large armies,
acted unlawfully.
The Emperor, adopting the advice of Qí Tài and Huáng Zǐchéng,
intended to gradually eliminate them due to various incidents.
Fearing the strong Prince of Yān,
he had not yet acted,
but first deposed Prince Zhōu Sù,
hoping to implicate Yān.
Consequently, accusations and denunciations arose everywhere;
Xiāng, Dài, Qí, and Mǐn were all deposed for crimes.
The Prince (of Yān) felt endangered within
and feigned madness and illness.
Qí Tài and Huáng Zǐchéng secretly urged the Emperor to eliminate the Prince,
but the Emperor was undecided.
In the sixth month of summer, the first year of Jiànwén (1399),
Ní Liàng, a centurion from Yānshān, reported a rebellion.
The officers and guards, including Yú Liàng and Zhōu Duó, were arrested and executed.
An imperial edict was issued to reprimand the Prince (of Yān),
and palace eunuchs were dispatched to arrest the Prince’s staff.
The Prince then claimed his illness had worsened.
The Regional Military Commissioner Xiè Guì and the Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhāng Bǐng guarded the Prince’s palace with troops.
The Prince secretly conspired with the monk Dàoyǎn,
ordering Commanders Zhāng Yù and Zhū Néng to secretly bring 800 brave warriors into the palace for defense.
On the Guǐyǒu day of the seventh month of autumn (August 6, 1399),
he hid strong men at the Duānlǐ Gate,
tricked Xiè Guì and Zhāng Bǐng into entering,
killed them,
and then seized the nine gates.
He submitted a memorial to the Son of Heaven, accusing Qí Tài and Huáng Zǐchéng of being treacherous ministers,
and also cited the Ancestral Injunctions:
“If there are no upright ministers at court,
and there are treacherous evildoers within,
then the imperial princes shall train their troops and await orders.
The Son of Heaven shall secretly issue edicts to the princes to lead their garrison troops to suppress them.”
After the memorial was dispatched,
he raised an army.
He appointed his own officials
and named his campaign “Jìngnán” (Pacify the Disorder).
He captured Jūyōng Pass,
defeated Huáilái,
captured Sòng Zhōng,
took Mìyún,
conquered Zūnhuà,
and accepted the surrender of Yǒngpíng.
Within twenty days, his forces grew to tens of thousands.
In the eighth month (August 7 – September 4, 1399),
the Son of Heaven appointed Gěng Bǐngwén as Grand General
to lead an army to suppress him.
On the Jǐyǒu day (August 12, 1399),
the army reached Zhēndìng,
with its vanguard arriving at Xióng County.
On the Rénzǐ day (August 15, 1399),
the Prince crossed the Báigōu River by night,
besieged Xióng,
captured the city,
and massacred its inhabitants.
On the Jiǎyín day (August 17, 1399),
Regional Commanders Pān Zhōng and Yáng Sōng came from Màozhōu to reinforce,
but were ambushed and captured.
The Prince then occupied Màozhōu
and returned to station at Báigōu.
The Grand General’s officer Zhāng Bǎo surrendered
and reported that the Grand General’s army numbered 300,000,
with 130,000 arriving first,
half encamped south of the Huòtuó River,
and half encamped north of the river.
The Prince feared that if he fought the northern army,
the southern army would also attack him.
So he released Zhāng Bǎo,
ordering him to spread rumors that the Prince was leading his army and about to arrive,
to lure their entire army to cross the river northward.
On the Rénxū day (August 25, 1399),
the Prince arrived at Zhēndìng
and, together with Zhāng Yù, Tán Yuān, and others, launched a pincer attack on Gěng Bǐngwén’s army,
greatly defeating them.
They captured his deputy generals Lǐ Jiān and Níng Zhōng, as well as the Military Commissioner Gù Chéng, and others,
beheading 30,000.
He advanced to besiege Zhēndìng,
but failed to take it in two days,
so he withdrew.
The Son of Heaven, hearing of Gěng Bǐngwén’s defeat,
dispatched Duke of Cáo Lǐ Jǐnglóng to replace him in commanding the army.
On the Wùchén day of the ninth month (September 11, 1399),
Marquis of Jiāngyīn Wú Gāo besieged Yǒngpíng with Liáodōng troops.
On the Wùyín day (September 21, 1399),
Lǐ Jǐnglóng combined his forces, numbering 500,000,
and advanced to encamp at Héjiān.
The Prince said to his generals:
“Lǐ Jǐnglóng appears stern but is inwardly timid.
Hearing of my presence, he will surely not dare to advance rashly.
It is better to go to Yǒngpíng’s aid to draw out his forces.
Wú Gāo is timid and not fit for battle;
he will certainly flee upon my arrival.
Then we will return to attack Lǐ Jǐnglóng.
With a strong city ahead
and a large army behind,
we will surely capture him.”
On the Bǐngxū day (September 29, 1399),
the Yān army went to reinforce Yǒngpíng.
On the Rénchén day (October 5, 1399),
Wú Gāo, hearing of the Prince’s arrival,
indeed fled.
The Prince pursued and defeated him.
He then headed north to Dàníng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Rén-yín,
he entered their city by stratagem.
He stayed for seven days,
then, holding Níng Wáng Quán (寧王權) captive,
he led the troops of Dàníng (大寧) and the soldiers of the Wùyán Sān Wèi (𩽆顏三衞) southward.
On the day Yǐ-mǎo,
he arrived at Huìzhōu (會州).
He then established five armies: Zhāng Yù (張玉) commanded the Central Army,
with Zhèng Hēng (鄭亨) and Hé Shòu (何壽) as his deputies;
Zhū Néng (朱能) commanded the Left Army,
with Zhū Róng (朱榮) and Lǐ Jùn (李濬) as his deputies;
Lǐ Bīn (李彬) commanded the Right Army,
with Xú Lǐ (徐理) and Mèng Shàn (孟善) as his deputies;
Xú Zhōng (徐忠) commanded the Vanguard Army,
with Chén Wén (陳文) and Wú Dá (吳達) as his deputies;
Fáng Kuān (房寬) commanded the Rear Army,
with Hé Yǔnzhōng (和允中) and Máozhěng (毛整) as his deputies.
On the day Dīng-sì,
he entered Sōngtíngguān (松亭關).
Jǐnglóng (景隆), hearing that the King was campaigning in Dàníng (大寧),
indeed led his army to besiege Běipíng (北平),
building ramparts at the nine gates.
The heir apparent held firm, refusing to engage in battle.
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēng-wǔ,
the King encamped at Gūshān (孤山).
His scouts returned and reported that the Báihé (白河) river was frozen and impassable.
The King prayed to the spirits,
and upon reaching it, the ice had merged,
allowing him to cross with his army.
Jǐnglóng (景隆) sent Dudū Chén Huī (都督陳暉) to scout the enemy,
who went to the left of the road,
and came out behind the King's army.
The King divided his forces to counterattack him.
Huī’s (暉) troops scrambled to cross the river,
when the ice suddenly broke apart,
and countless drowned.
On the day Xīn-wèi,
they battled Jǐnglóng (景隆) at Zhèngcūnbà (鄭村壩).
The King, with his elite cavalry, first broke through seven of their camps.
The other generals followed,
and Jǐnglóng (景隆) was greatly defeated,
fleeing back.
On the day Yǐ-hài,
he again submitted a memorial pleading his case.
In the twelfth month,
Jǐnglóng (景隆) mobilized troops at Dézhōu (德州),
planning a major offensive in the spring of next year.
The King then plotted to invade Dàtóng (大同),
saying:
"If we attack Dàtóng (大同),
they will surely rush to its rescue.
Dàtóng (大同) is bitterly cold,
and the Southern army is weak and fragile.
Moreover, they will be exhausted without even fighting."
On the day Gēng-shēn,
Guǎngchāng (廣昌) surrendered.
In the second year, spring, first month, on the day Bǐng-yín,
Wèizhōu (蔚州) was captured.
In the second month, on the day Guǐ-chǒu,
they reached Dàtóng (大同).
Jǐnglóng (景隆) indeed came to relieve it via Zǐjīngguān (紫荊關).
The King had already rotated his army to Jūyōng (居庸).
Many of Jǐnglóng’s (景隆) soldiers died from freezing and starvation,
and they returned without encountering the enemy.
In the summer, fourth month,
Jǐnglóng (景隆) advanced his army to Héjiān (河間),
and was scheduled to meet Guō Yīng (郭英), Wú Jié (吳傑), and Píng Ān (平安) at Báigōuhé (白溝河).
On the day Yǐ-mǎo,
the King encamped at Sūjiāqiáo (蘇家橋).
On the day Jǐ-wèi,
he encountered Píng Ān’s (平安) troops by the river.
The King went ahead with a hundred cavalry,
feigning retreat
to lure Ān’s (安) formation into motion.
He then attacked them,
and Ān (安) was defeated and fled.
He then approached Jǐnglóng’s (景隆) army,
but the battle went unfavorably.
At dusk, he withdrew his forces.
The King, with three cavalrymen, covered the rear,
but got lost in the night.
He dismounted and lay on the ground to observe the river flow,
thus distinguishing east from west,
and crossed the river to leave.
On the day Gēng-shēn,
they fought again.
Jǐnglóng (景隆) deployed a battle line several tens of li long,
and broke the Yān (燕) rear army.
The King personally led elite cavalry to strike horizontally,
killing Qú Néng (瞿能) and his son.
He ordered Qiū Fú (丘福) to charge the central core,
but he could not break through.
The King swept through their left,
and Jǐnglóng’s (景隆) soldiers then circled out behind the King.
A great battle ensued for a long time,
with arrows raining down.
The King changed horses three times.
When his arrows were exhausted, he brandished his sword.
When his sword broke, he fled up an embankment,
feigning to wave his whip as if summoning reinforcements.
Jǐnglóng (景隆) suspected an ambush and
dared not advance.
Gāo Xù (高煦) arrived with aid,
and the situation was resolved.
At this time, the Southern army gathered more,
and all of the Yān (燕) generals and soldiers paled.
The King fiercely declared:
"If I do not advance,
the enemy will not retreat.
There must be a fight!"
He then again led his strong troops to burst out behind them,
attacking from both sides.
Just then, a whirlwind arose,
snapping Jǐnglóng’s (景隆) banner.
The King took advantage of the wind, set fire, and attacked fiercely,
beheading several tens of thousands,
and over a hundred thousand drowned.
Guō Yīng (郭英) broke and fled west,
while Jǐnglóng (景隆) broke and fled south,
losing all the imperial seals, documents, axes, and battle-axes bestowed upon him,
and escaping to Dézhōu (德州).
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐ-yǒu,
the King entered Dézhōu (德é州).
Jǐnglóng (景隆) fled to Jǐnán (濟南).
On the day Gēng-chén,
they attacked Jǐnán (濟南) and
defeated Jǐnglóng’s (景隆) army outside the city.
Tiě Xiàn (鐵鉉) and Shèng Yōng (盛庸) held firm,
and it could not be taken.
In autumn, eighth month, on the day Wù-shēn,
the siege was lifted, and they returned to Běipíng (北平).
In the ninth month,
Shèng Yōng (盛庸) replaced Lǐ Jǐnglóng (李景隆) as commander.
He recaptured Dézhōu (德州)
and, with Wú Jié (吳傑), Píng Ān (平安), and Xú Kǎi (徐凱), formed a pincer movement
to besiege Běipíng (北平).
At this time, Xú Kǎi (徐凱) was just fortifying Cāngzhōu (滄州).
The King feigned sending troops to attack Liáodōng (遼東).
Upon reaching Tōngzhōu (通州),
he followed the river south,
crossed Zhígū (直沽),
marching day and night.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Wù-wǔ,
he ambushed and captured Xú Kǎi (徐凱),
captured his city,
and buried three thousand surrendered soldiers alive that night.
He then crossed the river and passed Dézhōu (德州).
Shèng Yōng (盛庸) sent troops to attack,
but he defeated them.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rén-shēn,
they reached Línqīng (臨清).
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīng-yǒu,
they ambushed and defeated Shèng Yōng’s (盛庸) general Sūn Lín (孫霖) at Huákǒu (滑口).
On the day Yǐ-mǎo,
they battled Yōng (庸) at Dōngchāng (東昌).
Yōng (庸) used firearms and powerful crossbows to annihilate the King's soldiers.
Just then, Píng Ān’s (平安) army arrived,
surrounding them in several layers.
The King was greatly defeated,
breaking through the encirclement to escape,
losing several tens of thousands of men.
Zhāng Yù (張玉) died in battle.
In the third year, in spring, the first month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Wú Jié and Píng Ān were defeated at Wēixiàn,
and again defeated at Shēnzhōu.
Then, the army returned to Běipíng.
In the second month, on the *yǐsì* day,
the army was again led southward.
In the third month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Shèng Yōng was encountered at Jiāhé.
Tán Yuān died in battle.
Zhū Néng and Zhāng Wǔ fought desperately,
and Yōng's army retreated slightly.
As dusk fell,
each army gathered its troops and entered camp.
The Prince, with more than ten horsemen, pressed close to Yōng's camp and camped in the open.
At dawn, he got up and looked,
only to find himself surrounded.
He then calmly led his horse,
sounded his horn, passed through the camp, and left.
The generals, remembering the Emperor's decree
not to let him bear the name of having killed his uncle,
looked at each other in shock and bewilderment,
not daring to fire a single arrow.
On that day, battle resumed.
From *chén* (7-9 AM) to *wèi* (1-3 PM),
the two armies gained and lost ground against each other.
A northeast wind suddenly rose,
dust obscured the sky,
and the Yān troops shouted loudly,
taking advantage of the wind to attack.
Yōng suffered a great defeat
and fled to Dézhōu.
Wú Jié and Píng Ān led their armies from Zhēndìng to meet Yōng,
but before they had gone eighty *lǐ*,
they heard of the defeat and turned back.
The Prince used a stratagem to lure them,
and Jié and Ān led troops to raid the Prince.
In the intercalary month, on the *wùxū* day,
they met at Gǎochéng.
On the *jǐhài* day,
they fought.
A great wind uprooted trees,
and Jié and Ān were defeated and fled.
The pursuit reached the walls of Zhēndìng.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
upon reaching Dàmíng,
the Prince heard that Qí Tài and Huáng Zǐchéng had been dismissed.
He submitted a memorial requesting the recall of Wú Jié, Píng Ān, and Shèng Yōng's troops.
The Emperor sent Dàlǐ Shàopíng Xuē Yán to reply,
instructing the Prince to lay down his arms.
The Prince did not obey the decree.
In the summer, the fifth month,
Jié, Ān, and Yōng divided their forces to cut off Yān's supply routes.
The Prince sent Commander Wǔ Shèng to submit a memorial,
questioning the reason for this.
The Emperor was angry
and imprisoned Shèng.
The Prince then sent Lǐ Yuǎn to raid Péixiàn,
burning tens of thousands of grain boats.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Zhāngdé was plundered.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Línxiàn surrendered.
Píng Ān took advantage of the weakness to attack Běipíng.
The Prince sent Liú Jiāng to meet him in battle,
and Ān was defeated and fled.
Fáng Zhāo was stationed at Xīshuǐzhài in Yìzhōu,
and attacked Bǎodìng.
The Prince led troops to besiege him.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
Commandant Huā Yīng came to aid Zhāo,
but was defeated at the foot of Éméishān,
with ten thousand heads severed.
Zhāo abandoned his camp and fled.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the army returned to Běipíng.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐsì* day,
the Prince personally composed a text to offer sacrifices to the officers and soldiers who died in battle, both North and South.
At this time,
the Prince had been in rebellion for three years.
He personally fought on the battlefield,
braving arrows and stones,
leading his soldiers by example.
He often pursued the defeated enemy when victorious,
but also frequently faced danger.
The cities and towns he captured,
once his troops left, quickly reverted to being held by the imperial court,
and he merely held Běipíng, Bǎodìng, and Yǒngpíng prefectures.
Shortly thereafter,
dismissed eunuchs came to defect,
fully explaining that the capital was empty and could be taken.
The Prince then said with emotion,
"We have been using troops for many years,
when will this end?
We must make a final decision by the river,
and not look back again."
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the army set out again.
In the fourth year, in spring, the first month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
the army crossed the river from Guǎntáo.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Xúzhōu was subdued.
In the third month, on the *rénchén* day,
Píng Ān, with forty thousand cavalry, pursued the Prince's army.
The Prince set an ambush at Féihé
and thoroughly defeated him.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Tán Qīng was sent to cut off Xúzhōu's supply route.
On his return to Dàdiàn,
he was surrounded by Tiě Xuàn's army.
The Prince led troops to rush to his aid,
and Qīng broke out of the encirclement.
They combined forces and defeated Tiě Xuàn.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the Prince camped by a small river
and built a bridge to cross.
Píng Ān rushed to contest the bridge,
and Chén Wén died in battle.
Píng Ān's army was south of the bridge,
and the Prince's army was north of the bridge,
in a stalemate for several days.
Píng Ān shifted his position and fought,
meeting the Prince at Běibǎn.
The Prince was almost struck by Ān's spear.
The foreign cavalryman Wáng Qí leaped into the formation,
pulled the Prince away, and escaped.
The Prince said,
"The Southern army is hungry.
If supplies arrive in another day or two,
they cannot be easily broken right away."
So he ordered more than a thousand men to guard the bridge,
and at midnight, crossed the river to the south,
circumventing to the rear of Ān's army.
By dawn,
Ān finally realized it,
just as Xú Huīzǔ arrived to join him.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
a great battle was fought at the foot of Qíméishān.
At this time, Yān had successively lost its great generals,
and the Huái region was oppressively hot and humid.
The generals requested a rest for the army east of Xiǎohé,
to await the wheat harvest and observe the situation.
The Prince said,
"Now the enemy has been holding out for a long time, hungry and exhausted.
If we cut off their supply routes,
we can corner them.
Why cross north and demoralize the officers and soldiers?"
He then ordered, "Those who wish to cross the river, go left."
All the generals competed to go left.
The Prince angrily said,
"Go wherever you wish!"
Thereafter, no one dared to speak again.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Hé Fú and others camped at Língbì.
Yān cut off their supply routes.
Píng Ān detached sixty thousand troops to protect them.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Prince led his elite forces to strike horizontally,
cutting their army in two.
Hé Fú came to reinforce with an empty camp,
the Prince's army retreated slightly,
Gāo Xù's ambush troops rose,
and Fú was defeated and fled.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Prince advanced and pressed their encampment,
breaking it.
Píng Ān, Chén Huī, and thirty-seven others were captured alive.
Hé Fú escaped.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Sīzhōu was taken.
The Prince visited the ancestral tombs
and bestowed oxen and wine upon the elders.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Shèng Yōng blocked the southern bank of the Huái River.
Zhū Néng and Qiū Fú secretly crossed and attacked, driving him away.
Then Xūyí was captured.
On the *Guǐ-sì* day,
the King gathered his generals to discuss the direction of attack.
Some suggested taking Fèngyáng,
while others advocated first taking Huái'ān.
The King said:
"Fèngyáng's towers and battlements are intact,
and Huái'ān has many grain stores.
Attacking them would not be easy to succeed.
It would be better to press on with our victory and head directly for Yángzhōu,
pointing at Yízhēn.
Then Huái and Fèng will be shaken by themselves.
If we display our military might on the Jiāng river,
the capital will be isolated and precarious,
and internal changes are bound to occur."
All the generals said, "Good!"
On the *Jǐ-hài* day,
Yángzhōu was taken,
and the army was stationed north of the river.
The Son of Heaven sent the Princess Qìngchéng to the army
and offered to cede territory for peace,
but she was not heard.
On the *Guǐ-chǒu* day of the sixth month,
Chén Xuān, the Assistant Commandant-in-Chief of River Defense, rebelled with his fleet
and submitted to the King.
On the *Jiǎ-yín* day,
sacrifices were offered to the Great Jiāng river.
On the *Yǐ-mǎo* day,
they crossed from Guāzhōu.
Shèng Yōng met them in battle with his sea vessels
and was defeated.
On the *Wù-wǔ* day,
Zhènjiāng fell.
On the *Gēng-shēn* day,
they reached Lóngtán.
On the *Xīn-yǒu* day,
the Son of Heaven again sent high officials to negotiate territorial cession,
and several princes arrived later,
but none were heeded.
On the *Yǐ-chǒu* day,
they reached Jīnchuānmén.
Gǔ Wáng Huì and Lǐ Jǐnglóng opened the gates and admitted the King,
and the capital thus fell.
On this day,
the King ordered his generals to guard the city and the Imperial City,
returned to station at Lóngjiāng,
and issued orders to pacify the military and the people.
A massive search was conducted for Qí Tài, Huáng Zǐchéng, Fāng Xiàorú, and over fifty others,
whose names were posted as "treacherous ministers."
On the *Bǐng-yín* day,
the princes and officials submitted a memorial urging the King to ascend the throne.
On the *Jǐ-sì* day,
the King paid homage at Xiàolíng.
The officials prepared the imperial carriage,
presented the imperial seal,
and cheered "Long Live!"
The King ascended the imperial carriage
and proceeded to Fèngtian Diàn to assume the imperial throne.
The titles of Zhōu Wáng Sù and Qí Wáng Fú were restored.
On the *Rén-shēn* day,
Emperor Jiànwén was buried.
On the *Dīng-chǒu* day,
Qí Tài, Huáng Zǐchéng, and Fāng Xiàorú were executed,
and their clans were exterminated.
Many others died for being implicated as "treacherous party members."
On the *Wù-yín* day,
the spirit tablet of Xīngzōng Xiàokāng Huángdì was moved to the imperial tomb garden,
still referred to as Yìwén Tàizǐ.
On the first day of the seventh month, *Rén-wǔ*, in autumn,
grand sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb,
with Tàizǔ enshrined as co-sacrificed.
An edict stated:
"This year shall be recorded as the 35th year of Hóngwǔ.
Next year shall be the 1st year of Yǒnglè.
All changes to established laws made during the Jiànwén reign
shall be restored to the old system.
For prefectures and counties in Shāndōng, Běipíng, and Hénán that suffered from warfare,
corvée labor is remitted for three years.
For those not affected by warfare, as well as Fèngyáng, Huái'ān, Xú, Chú, and Yáng three prefectures, rent is exempted for one year.
For the rest of the prefectures and counties nationwide, half of this year's land tax is remitted."
On the *Guǐ-wèi* day,
Chén Yīng, former Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Běipíng, was summoned to be Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
All officials who had been dismissed or degraded during the Jiànwén reign were reinstated.
On the *Jiǎ-shēn* day,
the official system was restored.
On the *Guǐ-sì* day,
Wú Wáng Yǔntēng was re-enfeoffed as Guǎngzé Wáng,
Héng Wáng Yǔnjiān as Huái'ēn Wáng,
Xú Wáng Yǔn... as Fūhuì Wáng,
to reside with their mother, Consort Lǚ, in the Yìwén Tàizǐ's tomb garden.
On the *Guǐ-mǎo* day,
Wú Gāo, Marquis of Jiāngyīn, supervised military preparations in Hénán and Shǎnxī,
and pacified the military and the people.
On the *Jiǎ-chén* day,
Ministers Yán Zhènzhí and Wáng Dùn,
Prefect Xuē Zhèngyán, and others inspected Shānxī, Shāndōng, Hénán, and Shǎnxī.
On the *Rén-zǐ* day of the eighth month,
Expositor Xiè Jìn and Compiler Huáng Huái entered the Wényuān Gé for duty.
Soon after, Expositor Hú Guǎng,
Reviser Yáng Róng,
Compiler Yáng Shìqí,
Reviewer Jīn Yòuzī, and Hú Yǎn were ordered to enter for duty,
and all were involved in state affairs.
Minister of War Tiě Xuàn was brought in,
but he did not yield,
so he was killed.
Liú Zhēn, Left Army Commandant-in-Chief, was stationed in Liáodōng.
On the *Dīng-sì* day,
Censors were dispatched to investigate advantages and disadvantages across the realm.
On the *Wù-wǔ* day,
Commandant-in-Chief Hé Fú was made General Who Conquers Barbarians,
stationed in Níngxià,
and exercised command over the Shǎnxī Provincial Military Commission.
Han Guān, Assistant Commandant-in-Chief, trained troops in Jiāngxī,
and exercised command over Guǎngdōng and Fújiàn.
On the *Jiǎ-zǐ* day,
Mù Shèng, Marquis of Xīpíng, was stationed in Yúnnán.
On the *Jiǎ-shēn* day of the ninth month,
the merits of the Jìngnàn Campaign were assessed.
Qiū Fú was enfeoffed as Qí Guó Gōng,
Zhū Néng as Chéng Guó Gōng.
Thirteen others, including Zhāng Wǔ, were enfeoffed as Marquises,
and eleven, including Xú Xiáng, as Earls.
For merits in reporting and submission,
Prince Consort-in-Chief Wáng Níng was enfeoffed as a Marquis,
and Rú Cháng, Chén Xuān, and Assistant Commandant-in-Chief Wáng Zuǒ were all made Earls.
On the *Jiǎ-wǔ* day,
regulations for reducing the salaries of meritorious officials guilty of capital crimes were established.
On the *Yǐ-wèi* day,
landless people from Shānxī were resettled in Běipíng,
given paper currency,
and exempted from taxes for five years.
Hán Guān was made General Who Conquers the South,
stationed in Guǎngxī.
On the *Dīng-sì* day of the tenth month in winter,
Zhū Níng and 218 other officials from Běipíng prefectures and counties who had abandoned their posts to avoid the Jìngnàn army were ordered to offer grain to avoid death,
and were exiled to Xīngzhōu.
On the *Jǐ-wèi* day,
the Veritable Records of Tàizǔ were compiled.
On the *Bǐng-yín* day,
Gù Chéng, Marquis of Zhènyuǎn, was stationed in Guìzhōu.
On the *Rén-shēn* day,
Gǔ Wáng Huì was re-enfeoffed in Chángshā.
On the *Jiǎ-xū* day,
an edict ordered the return of kidnapped commoners' daughters to their homes by accompanying generals and soldiers.
On the *Rén-chén* day of the eleventh month,
Consort Xú was established as Empress.
Guǎngzé Wáng Yǔntēng and Huái'ēn Wáng Yǔnjiān were demoted to commoners.
On the *Guǐ-chǒu* day of the twelfth month,
next year's summer taxes for prefectures and counties affected by warfare were remitted.
Collation Notes
Annals Volume 6, Chéngzǔ 2
On the first day of the first month, *Jǐ-mǎo*, of the 1st year of Yǒnglè in spring,
the Emperor held court in Fèngtian Diàn to receive congratulations and hosted a banquet for officials and envoys from tributary states.
On the *Yǐ-yǒu* day,
sacrifices were offered at Tàimiào.
On the *Xīn-mǎo* day,
grand sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
The former enfeoffments of Zhōu Wáng Sù, Qí Wáng Fú, Dài Wáng Guì, and Mín Wáng Pián were restored.
Běipíng was renamed Běijīng.
On the *Guǐ-sì* day,
Mèng Shàn, Marquis of Bǎodìng, was stationed in Liáodōng.
On the *Dīng-yǒu* day,
Sòng Chéng was made General Who Pacifies the Qiāng,
stationed in Gānsù.
On the *Gēng-xū* day of the second month,
the Běijīng Auxiliary Command-in-Chief, Provincial Administrations, and Guózǐjiān were established;
Běipíng was renamed Shùntiān Fǔ.
On the *Yǐ-mǎo* day,
Censors were dispatched to inspect various parts of the realm,
establishing this as a regular system.
On the *Jǐ-wèi* day,
Níng Wáng Quán was re-enfeoffed in Nánchāng.
A letter was sent to Khagan Guǐlìchì,
permitting him to send envoys to establish friendly relations.
On the *Guǐ-hài* day,
the ceremonial plowing of the *jìtián* was performed.
On the *Yǐ-chǒu* day,
an envoy was sent to Wūsīzàng to summon the Guru Hālìmá.
On the *Jǐ-sì* day,
relief was provided to the starving in the six prefectures of Běijīng.
On the *Xīn-wèi* day,
the Ministry of Justice was ordered to present criminal cases every five days.
On the *Rén-shēn* day,
unburied bones on battlefields were interred.
On the *Jiǎ-xū* day,
Gāoyáng Wáng Gāoxù was assigned to guard the border at Kāipíng.
On the *Gēng-chén* day of the third month,
Wú Gāo, Marquis of Jiāngyīn, was stationed in Dàtóng.
On the *Rén-wǔ* day,
the Běipíng Provincial Military Commission was renamed Dàníng Military Commission,
and relocated to Bǎodìng.
The Dàníng territory was first granted to the Wūliánghā.
On the *Wù-zǐ* day,
Chén Xuān, Earl of Píngjiāng, and Assistant Commandant-in-Chief Xuān Xìn were appointed Commander-in-Chief,
to supervise sea transport
for provisioning Liáodōng and Běijīng,
which became a regular annual practice.
On the *Jiǎ-wǔ* day,
relief was provided to the starving in Zhílì, Běijīng, Shāndōng, and Hénán.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *dīngwèi* day, the first day of the month,
Hú Kuì (胡●) of Ānnán (安南) requested to inherit the 陳 (Chén) clan's title and enfeoffment.
An envoy was dispatched to investigate the facts and report back.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Hùbù Shàngshū (戶部尚書) Xià Yuánjí (夏原吉) governed the flood control in Sūzhōu (蘇), Sōngjiāng (松), Jiāxīng (嘉), and Húzhōu (湖).
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Mín Wáng (岷王) Zhū Biǎn (朱楩) was found guilty,
and his officials and retainers were demoted.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Xiāngchéng Bó (襄城伯) Lǐ Jùn (李濬) was appointed to govern Jiāngxī (江西).
In the fifth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
the tax on uncultivated wasteland throughout the empire was abolished.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
those sentenced to death or lesser crimes were pardoned,
with each punishment reduced by one degree.
On the *gēngyín* day,
locusts in Shāndōng (山東) were captured.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
there were locusts in Hénán (河南),
and the summer tax for this year was remitted.
In this month,
the merits of the Jìngnán (靖難) campaign were re-evaluated,
and Fùmǎ Dūwèi (駙馬都尉) Yuán Róng (袁容) and two others were enfeoffed as hóu (侯),
while Chén Hēng's (陳亨) son Mào (懋) and five others were enfeoffed as bó (伯).
In the sixth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Dài Wáng (代王) Zhū Guì (朱桂) was found guilty,
and his guard detachment was abolished.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Gěishìzhōng (給事中) and Yùshǐ (御史) were dispatched throughout the empire
to pacify the military and civilian populace,
and corrupt and greedy officials were arrested and prosecuted.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the posthumous titles of Gāo Huángdì (高皇帝) and Gāo Huánghòu (高皇后) were revised.
On the *wùchén* day,
Wǔ'ān Hóu (武安侯) Zhèng Hēng (鄭亨) was appointed to govern Xuānfǔ (宣府).
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *gēngyín* day,
another letter was sent to Guǐlìchì (鬼力赤).
In the eighth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
those sentenced to exile or lesser crimes were sent to cultivate land in Běijīng (北京).
On the *jiǎxū* day,
wealthy residents from ten prefectures, including Sūzhōu (蘇州) in Zhílì (直隸), and nine provinces, including Zhèjiāng (浙江), were relocated to populate Běijīng (北京).
In the ninth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
the Báoyuán Jú (寶源局) was ordered to cast agricultural implements
to be distributed to the impoverished populace of Shāndōng (山東) affected by war.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the first dispatch of the eunuch Mǎ Bīn (馬彬) as envoy to various states of Jawā (爪哇) occurred.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Lìchéng Hóu (歷城侯) Shèng Yōng (盛庸)'s title was revoked,
and he subsequently committed suicide.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Mín Wáng (岷王) Zhū Biǎn (朱楩) was found guilty,
and his guard detachment was abolished.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the *yǐhài* day, the first day of the month,
the calendar was promulgated to Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮) and other states,
and established as a regulation.
On the *rénchén* day,
the dispatch of civilian laborers for river dredging was suspended.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an earthquake occurred in Běijīng (北京).
On the *yǐwèi* day,
officials from the Six Offices (六科) were ordered to report on affairs.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Hán Guān (韓觀) suppressed the mountain bandits in Liǔzhōu (柳州),
and pacified the area.
In the intercalary month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Hú Kuì (胡●) was enfeoffed as King of Ānnán (安南) State.
In this year,
eunuchs were first ordered to serve as regional commanders and supervisors of the Imperial Garrisons (京營軍).
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮) made six tribute missions,
and from this year on, regular annual tribute and congratulatory missions became customary.
The Central, Northern, and Southern Mountains of Liúqiú (琉球),
Xiānluó (暹羅),
Zhànchéng (占城),
the Western King of Jawā (爪哇),
Rìběn (日本),
Lànī (剌泥),
and Ānnán (安南) made tribute missions.
Second year, spring, the first month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Heir Apparent Gāo Chì (高熾) and Gāoyáng Wáng (高陽王) Gāo Xù (高煦) were summoned back to the capital.
In the third month, on the *yǐsì* day,
Zēng Qǐ (曾棨) and other *jìnshì* (進士) were awarded degrees and official ranks with distinctions.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
*jìnshì* were first selected to serve as *shùjíshì* (庶吉士) in the Hànlín Yuàn (翰林院).
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Lìbù (吏部) requested punishment for *qiānhù* (千戶) who recommended scholars in violation of regulations.
The Emperor said:
"Did Mǎ Zhōu (馬周) not advance through Cháng Hé (常何)?
If they are truly talented,
bestow them official posts;
otherwise, dismiss them."
On the *wùchén* day,
Fūhuì Wáng (敷惠王) Yǔn Yǎn (允●) was re-enfeoffed as Ōuníng Wáng (甌寧王),
to attend to the sacrifices for Yìwén Tàizǐ (懿文太子).
Summer, the fourth month, on the *xīnwèi* day, the first day of the month,
officials for the Eastern Palace were established.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the monk Dàoyǎn (道衍) was appointed Tàizǐ Shàoshī (太子少師),
his original surname Yáo (姚) was restored,
and he was bestowed the name Guǎngxiào (廣孝).
On the *jiǎxū* day,
his son Gāo Chì (高熾) was established as Crown Prince,
Gāo Xù (高煦) was enfeoffed as Hàn Wáng (漢王),
and Gāo Suì (高燧) as Zhào Wáng (趙王).
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Wāng Yìngzǔ (汪應祖) was enfeoffed as King of the Southern Mountain of Liúqiú (琉球) State.
In the fifth month, on the *rén'yín* day,
Fēngchéng Hóu (豐城侯) Lǐ Bīn (李彬) was appointed to govern Guǎngdōng (廣東),
and Qīngyuǎn Bó (清遠伯) Wáng Yǒu (王友) was appointed Commander-in-Chief (總兵官),
leading the naval fleet on sea patrols.
In the sixth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
superfluous officials were dismissed.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
relief was provided for famine in Sōngjiāng (松江), Jiāxīng (嘉興), Sūzhōu (蘇州), and Húzhōu (湖州).
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Ānkè Tiěmù'ěr (安克帖木兒) of Hāmì (哈密) was enfeoffed as Zhōngshùn Wáng (忠順王).
Autumn, the seventh month, on the *rénxū* day,
a commoner from Póyáng (鄱陽) presented a book slandering ancient sages,
was flogged,
and his book was destroyed.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
flood relief was provided in Jiāngxī (江西) and Húguǎng (湖廣).
In the eighth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
Tiānpíng (天平), younger brother of the late King of Ānnán (安南) State, Chén Rìkuí (陳日煃), came to defect.
In the ninth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Zhōu Wáng (周王) Zhū Sù (朱橚) came to court,
presenting a *zōuyú* (騶虞).
All officials requested to offer congratulations.
The Emperor said:
"Auspicious omens arrive in accordance with virtue.
If the *zōuyú* is indeed an auspicious sign,
I, the Emperor, should all the more cultivate virtue and reflect."
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
ten thousand households of commoners from Shānxī (山西) were relocated to populate Běijīng (北京).
It was ordered that from now on, Censors (御史) on巡行 (xúnháng) tours investigating officials were not to gather hearsay,
but to report both the virtuous and the corrupt with concrete evidence.
Winter, the tenth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Yellow River overflowed at Kāifēng (開封).
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Yellow River became clear at Púchéng (蒲城) and Héjīn (河津).
In this month,
the property of Chángxīng Hóu (長興侯) Gěng Bǐngwén (耿炳文) was confiscated,
and Bǐngwén (炳文) committed suicide.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
the Emperor personally reviewed prisoners at Fèngtīan Mén (奉天門).
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
earthquakes occurred in the capital, Jǐnán (濟南), and Kāifēng (開封),
and an edict was issued for all officials to cultivate virtue and reflect.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
land taxes were remitted for the flood-affected areas of Sūzhōu (蘇), Sōngjiāng (松), Jiāxīng (嘉), Húzhōu (湖), and Hángzhōu (杭).
In the twelfth month, on the *rénchén* day,
the Yellow River became clear at Tóngzhōu (同州) and Hánchéng (韓城).
In this month,
Lǐ Jǐnglóng (李景隆) was imprisoned.
In this year,
Zhànchéng (占城),
Bíeshībālǐ (別失八里),
the Northern and Southern Mountains of Liúqiú (琉球),
Jawā (爪哇),
and Zhēnlà (真臘) made tribute missions.
Xiānluó (暹羅),
Rìběn (日本),
and the Central Mountain of Liúqiú (琉球) made tribute missions twice.
Third year, spring, the first month, on the *gēngxū* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
an envoy was dispatched to admonish Ānnán (安南).
On the *gēngshēn* day,
land taxes for Shùntiān (順天), Yǒngpíng (永平), and Báodìng (保定) were again remitted for two years.
In the second month, on the *jǐsì* day,
Lào Qiān (雒僉), an official of the Lìbù (吏部), was executed for remarks that involved resentment and slander.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Zhào Wáng (趙王) Gāo Suì (高燧) was stationed in Běijīng (北京).
In the third month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
land taxes for flood-affected areas in Húguǎng (湖廣) were remitted.
Summer, the sixth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the eunuch Zhèng Hé (鄭和) led a naval fleet on a mission to various states in the Western Oceans.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the eunuch Shān Shòu (山壽) and others led troops out of Yúnzhōu (雲州) to scout the enemy.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Xià Yuánjí (夏原吉) and others provided famine relief in Sūzhōu (蘇), Sōngjiāng (松), Jiāxīng (嘉), and Húzhōu (湖).
Salt taxes (食鹽鈔) for peasant households throughout the empire were remitted.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Hú Kuì (胡●) apologized
and requested to welcome Chén Tiānpíng (陳天平) back to his country.
Autumn, the ninth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
land taxes were remitted for the flood-affected areas of Sūzhōu (蘇), Sōngjiāng (松), Jiāxīng (嘉), and Húzhōu (湖),
totaling three million three hundred and thirty-eight thousand *shí* (石) of grain.
On the *dīngsì* day,
ten thousand households of commoners from Shānxī (山西) were relocated to populate Běijīng (北京).
In the winter, tenth month,
bandits murdered Fùmǎ Dūwèi Méi Yīn.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Qí Wáng Fú was guilty of an offense,
and was sent three imperial letters of admonition.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Ancestral Instructions were promulgated to all the princes.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùchén,
Mù Shèng campaigned against the Bābǎi,
who submitted.
On the day Gēngchén,
Dūdū Qiānshì Huáng Zhōng and Lǚ Yì led troops to install Chén Tiānpíng in Ānnán.
This year,
Sūméndálà, Mǎlájiā, Gǔlǐ, and Bóní came to offer tribute,
and their chiefs were enfeoffed as kings.
Rìběn offered tribute of horses,
and also presented captured Wōkòu who had been plaguing the borders.
The eastern and western parts of Zhǎowā,
Zhànchéng,
Diélǐ,
Rìluó Xiàzhì,
Hémāolǐ,
and Huǒzhōu Huíhuí presented tribute.
Xiāmluó,
Liúqiú Shānnán, and Shānběi presented tribute for a second time,
while Liúqiú Zhōngshān presented tribute for a third time.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day Dīngwèi,
a great sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburban altar.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the emperor presided over the noon court for the first time,
allowing officials to present their memorials and discuss matters at their leisure.
In the third month, on the first day Xīnmǎo,
a ceremony was held for the former teacher Kǒngzǐ.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
horse markets were established in Liáodōng's Kāiyuán and Guǎngníng.
On the day Yǐsì,
Lín Huán and others were granted the titles of Jìnshì Jíyǐ and Chūshēn with varying ranks.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Hú Kuáng ambushed and killed Chén Tiānpíng at Qínzhàn.
The former Dàlǐ Qīng Xuē Yán died with him,
and Huáng Zhōng and others led their troops back.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
envoys were dispatched to purchase lost books.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
relief was provided for the famine in Chángzhōu, Lúzhōu, and Ānqìng.
On the day Gēngxū,
Qí Wáng Fú was guilty of an offense,
his officials and guards were stripped,
and he was kept in the capital.
In the sixth month, on the first day Jǐwèi,
there was supposed to be a solar eclipse,
but it was not seen due to dark clouds.
The ritual officials requested to present a congratulatory memorial,
but it was denied.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Nányáng presented auspicious wheat,
and an imperial edict to the Ministry of Rites stated:
"Although various prefectures and counties have repeatedly reported auspicious signs,
this alone is a sign of a bountiful year."
It was ordered to be offered in the ancestral temple.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Zhū Néng was made Zhēngyí Jiāngjūn,
with Mù Shèng and Zhāng Fǔ as his deputies,
to lead troops in separate routes to campaign against Ānnán.
Bīngbù Shàngshū Liú Jùn participated in military affairs,
while Xíngbù Shàngshū Huáng Fú and Dàlǐ Qīng Chén Qià supervised provisions.
The imperial edict stated:
"All people of Ānnán are Our children.
Only Lí Jìlí and his son, the chief culprits, must be executed.
Others who were coerced should be released.
Once the culprits are apprehended,
a worthy descendant of the Chén clan shall be enthroned.
Do not foster chaos,
do not trifle with bandits,
do not destroy homes or graves,
do not harm crops,
do not seize property or abduct women and children,
and do not kill those who surrender.
If any of these are violated,
even merits shall not be excused."
On the day Yǐsì,
the prohibition against slander was reiterated.
In the intercalary month, on the day Réxū,
an imperial edict announced that construction of the Běijīng palace would begin in the fifth month of the following year,
and ministers were dispatched to Sichuan, Húguǎng, Jiāngxī, Zhèjiāng, and Shānxī to procure timber.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
an imperial edict to the Tōngzhèng Sī stated:
“All who submit memorials concerning the people's affairs,
no matter how small, must be reported.”
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Qí Wáng Fú was deposed as a commoner.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùchén,
relief was provided for over 120,000 households of refugees in Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Chángzhōu, Hángzhōu, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu to resume their occupations.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Chéngguó Gōng Zhū Néng died in the army,
and Zhāng Fǔ took command of his troops.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Àiliú Guān was captured.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Mù Shèng led his troops to rendezvous at Báihè.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐsì,
sweet dew descended on the pines and cypresses of Xiàolíng,
and sweet spring water emerged from Shénlè Guàn.
They were presented to the Tàimiào,
and bestowed upon all officials.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
a general amnesty was granted to all except those sentenced to death.
Zhāng Fǔ greatly defeated the Ānnán army at Jiālín Jiāng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Duōbāng Chéng was captured.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
their Eastern Capital was captured.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
their Western Capital was captured,
and the rebels fled into the sea.
On the day Xīnhài,
the residence of Ōuníng Wáng Yǔnqú caught fire,
and the king died.
This year,
Xiāmluó,
Zhànchéng,
Yútián,
Bóní,
Rìběn,
Liúqiú Zhōngshān and Shānnán,
and Póluó presented tribute.
Eastern and Western Zhǎowā,
and Zhēnlà presented tribute for a second time.
Biéshībālǐ presented tribute for a third time.
Liúqiú offered eunuchs,
who were returned.
Huíhuí Jiéyáqǔ presented a jade bowl,
which was rejected.
In the fifth year, spring, first month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
a great sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburban altar.
On the day Jǐsì,
Zhāng Fǔ greatly defeated the Ānnán army at Mùwán Jiāng.
In the second month, on the day Gēngyín,
Hànlín Xuéshì Xiè Jìn was sent out as Cānyì of Guǎngxī.
In the third month, on the day Dīngsì,
Shàngshī Hālìmá was enfeoffed as Dàbǎo Fǎwáng.
On the day Xīnsì,
Zhāng Fǔ greatly defeated the Ānnán army at Fùliáng Jiāng.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
relief was provided for the famine in Shùntiān, Héjiān, and Bǎodìng.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Zhāng Fǔ captured Lí Jìlí and Lí Cāng and brought them to the capital,
and Ānnán was pacified.
Hénán suffered from famine,
and officials who concealed the disaster were arrested and punished.
An imperial edict to the Dūcháyùan stated:
“All who fail to report disaster and suffering truthfully shall be punished.”
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
due to the pacification of Ānnán,
an imperial edict was issued to the empire.
Jiāozhǐ Bùzhèng Sī was established.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Dīng Yù, a commoner from Shānyáng, reported his fellow villager for slander,
and was promoted to Xíngkē Jǐshìzhōng.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
an imperial edict ordered that all those who had committed crimes and been removed from office after the sixth month of Yǒnglè second year
be entirely pardoned.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Zhāng Fǔ moved his army to join Hán Guān in campaigning against the rebellious Man of Xún and Liǔ.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Zhāng Fǔ was ordered to seek out talented individuals in Jiāozhǐ,
and send them to the capital with due ceremony.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
the Empress passed away.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the river overflowed in Hénán.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Zuǒ Dūdū Hé Fú garrisoned Gānsù.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
prisoners were reviewed,
and those guilty of miscellaneous capital crimes had their sentences reduced to exile,
while those sentenced to exile or lighter punishments were released.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Zhèng Hé returned.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the emperor presided at Fèngtiānmén,
received the Ānnán captives,
and greatly rewarded the generals and soldiers.
In the winter, tenth month,
the Man of Xún and Liǔ were pacified.
This year,
Liúqiú Zhōngshān and Shānnán,
Póluó,
Rìběn,
Biéshībālǐ,
Ālǔ,
Sāmǎ'érhǎn,
Sūméndálà,
Mǎlájiā,
and Xiǎogélán presented tribute.
In the sixth year, in spring, the first month, on the *dīngsì* day,
Prince Mín, Zhū Biǎn, again committed an offense,
and his officials and subordinates were dismissed.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the southern suburb.
In the second month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
all outstanding taxes from Běijīng prior to the fifth year of Yǒnglè were remitted,
and all kinds of miscellaneous levies were exempted for three years.
In the third month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Earl Níngyáng, Chén Mào, was appointed to garrison Níngxià.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
outstanding taxes from Hénán, Shāndōng, and Shānxī prior to the fifth year of Yǒnglè were remitted.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
the provincial examination was first mandated for Yúnnán.
In the fifth month, on the night of the *rénxū* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
an imperial edict ordered the suspension of non-urgent tasks and procurement for all ministries in Běijīng,
to relieve the people's distress;
migrants who returned were exempted from labor service for three years.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Zhāng Fǔ and Mù Shèng returned.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
the achievements in pacifying Jiāozhǐ were assessed,
and Zhāng Fǔ was promoted and enfeoffed as Duke Yīngguó,
Mù Shèng as Duke Qiánguó,
Wáng Yǒu as Marquis Qīngyuǎn,
and Commander-in-chief Zhìshì Liǔ Shēng was enfeoffed as Earl Ānyuǎn;
other titles and rewards varied.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Jiāozhǐ Jiǎndìng rebelled,
and Mù Shèng was made General Zhēngyí
to suppress him,
with Liú Jùn still participating in military affairs.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Ministry of Justice was ordered to clear delayed lawsuits.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Zhèng Hé was again dispatched on an envoy mission to the Western Oceans.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the *dīngsì* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
Mù Shèng and Jiǎndìng engaged in battle at the Shēngjué River,
and Mù Shèng suffered a defeat.
Liú Jùn, Commander-in-chief Zhìshì Lǚ Yì, and Vice-Administrator Liú Yù died in the battle.
This month,
Liǔ Shēng, Chén Xuān, Lǐ Bīn, and others led a naval force to patrol the coast and capture Japanese pirates.
This year,
Guǐlìchì was assassinated by his subordinates,
who then enthroned Běnyáshīlǐ as Khan.
The King of the country of Bóní came to court.
Wǎlà,
Zhānchéng,
Yútián,
Xiāmluó,
Sāmǎ'érhǎn,
Bǎnggélà,
Féngjiāshīlán,
Rìběn,
Zhǎowā,
and Ryūkyū's Zhōngshān and Shānnán sent tribute.
In the seventh year, in spring, the first month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
officials were granted a ten-day holiday for the Yuánxiāo Festival,
which was made a standing regulation.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the southern suburb.
In the second month, on the *yǐhài* day,
envoys were sent to the prefectures and counties through which the Emperor would tour, to inquire after the elderly;
those eighty and above were granted wine and meat,
and those ninety and above received additional silk.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
ninety-two retired prefects, including Liú Yáncái, were summoned to be assigned to prefectures, subprefectures, and counties.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the northern tour was announced to Heaven, the ancestral temples, and the altars of land and grain.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor departed from the capital,
and the Crown Prince supervised the state.
Zhāng Fǔ and Wáng Yǒu led an army to suppress Jiǎndìng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Emperor visited the imperial mausoleum in Fèngyáng.
In the third month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
the Emperor arrived at Dōngpíng Prefecture
and offered a distant sacrifice to Mount Tài.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Emperor arrived at Jǐng Prefecture
and offered a distant sacrifice to Mount Héng.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Píng Ān committed suicide.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor arrived at Běijīng.
On the *guǐhài* day,
a grand reward was bestowed upon officials, soldiers, and common people.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an imperial edict pardoned all officers and soldiers who had fought during the uprising and people in Běijīng who had rendered meritorious service, who were guilty of various capital crimes;
those who had been exiled were restored to their posts,
and soldiers and common people returned to their native registers and military units.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Liǔ Shēng defeated Japanese pirates in the sea off Qīng Prefecture,
and an imperial edict ordered the army to return.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
the Crown Prince performed the sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
sea bandits attacked Qīn Prefecture,
and Vice Commander-in-chief Lǐ Guī dispatched a general to defeat them.
In the intercalary month, on the *wùshēn* day,
it was ordered that all administrative matters decided by the Crown Prince
should be reported monthly by the Six Offices of Scrutiny.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the judicial authorities in the traveling court were instructed
that serious crimes must be reported five times for review.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the imperial mausoleum was constructed in Chāngpíng,
and the mountain was named Tiānshòu.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Mǎhāmù of Wǎlà was enfeoffed as Prince Shùnníng,
Tàipíng as Prince Xiányì,
and Bātúbóluó as Prince Ānlè.
In the sixth month, on the *rénchén* day,
the chief officials of the prefectures and counties visited during the northern tour were inspected;
Shǐ Chéngzǔ, the magistrate of Wénshàng County, was promoted as having the best administration,
while Zhāng Téng, the assistant prefect of Yì Prefecture, was imprisoned.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Supervisor Guō Jì, sent as an envoy to Běnyáshīlǐ,
was killed by him.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Censor Hóng Bǐng and three others were dismissed,
and an imperial edict stated that henceforth censors should not be appointed from clerical staff.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Duke Qíguó Qiū Fú was made General Zhēnglǔ Dàjiāngjūn,
with Marquis Wǔchéng Wáng Cōng and Marquis Tóng'ān Huǒ Zhēn as his deputies,
and Marquis Jìng'ān Wáng Zhōng and Marquis Ānpíng Lǐ Yuǎn as the left and right assistant generals,
to suppress Běnyáshīlǐ.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
Qiū Fú suffered a defeat at the Lúqú River,
and Fú, Cōng, Zhēn, Zhōng, and Yuǎn all died in battle.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Zhāng Fǔ defeated the rebels at Xiánzǐ Pass.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Zhāng Fǔ defeated the rebels at Tàipíng Hǎikǒu.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Lǐ Yuǎn, who died in the northern campaign, was posthumously granted the title of Duke Jǔguó, and Wáng Cōng that of Duke Zhāngguó,
and the Emperor then firmly decided to personally lead the campaign.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Marquis Wǔ'ān Zhèng Hēng led an army to patrol the border.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Marquis Chéng'ān Guō Liàng prepared defenses at Kāipíng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Qiū Fú's enfeoffment and titles were revoked,
and his family was exiled to Hǎinán.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùyín* day,
Zhāng Fǔ captured Jiǎndìng at Měiliáng,
sent him to the capital,
and executed him.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
the villagers from Jìníng to Liángxiāng, who had frequently transported goods for years, were granted one year's exemption from land rent.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Zhāng Fǔ was recalled.
This year,
Mǎlǐjiā,
Hāliè,
Sāmǎ'érhǎn,
Huǒzhōu,
Gǔlǐ,
Zhānchéng,
Sūméndálà,
and Ryūkyū's Zhōngshān and Shānnán sent tribute.
Xiāmluó and Bǎnggélà sent tribute twice.
In the eighth year, in spring, the first month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Marquis Níngyáng Chén Mào was summoned to accompany the expedition to Mòběi.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Crown Prince performed the sacrifice to Heaven and Earth in the southern suburb.
On the *guǐsì* day,
land taxes for the previous year in Yángzhōu, Huái'ān, Fèngyáng, and Chénzhōu, which had suffered from floods, were remitted,
and children sold by soldiers and common people were redeemed.
In the second month, on the *xīnc丑* day,
an imperial edict for the northern expedition was issued to the empire,
and Minister of the Ministry of Revenue Xià Yuánjí was ordered to assist the Imperial Grandson Zhān Jī in guarding Běijīng.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Crown Prince reviewed prisoners
and requested the remission of all capital crimes below a certain level,
which was granted.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Emperor departed from Běijīng.
On the *guǐhài* day,
envoys were sent to offer sacrifices to the famous mountains and great rivers along the route.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
a grand military review was held.
In the third month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Marquis Qīngyuǎn Wáng Yǒu was appointed supervisor of the central army,
with Earl Ānyuǎn Liǔ Shēng as his deputy;
Marquis Níngyuǎn Hé Fú and Marquis Wǔ'ān Zhèng Hēng supervised the left and right vanguards;
Marquis Níngyáng Chén Mào and Earl Guǎng'ēn Liú Cái supervised the left and right flanks;
and Commander-in-chief Liú Jiāng supervised the forward vanguard.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the army arrived at Míngluán Outpost.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the oath to the army was administered.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor arrived at Wēilǔ Zhèn.
The water carried in saddlebags was distributed to the imperial guards.
After seeing that all the soldiers had eaten,
he began his own meal.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Lúqú Hé (River) was renamed Yǐnmǎ (River).
On the day Jiǎxū,
upon hearing that Běnyǎshīlǐ had fled west,
the army crossed Yǐnmǎ Hé to pursue him.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
they caught up with him at Wònán Hé
and inflicted a great defeat.
Běnyǎshīlǐ escaped with seven horsemen.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the army returned to Yǐnmǎ Hé.
An imperial edict ordered the army to move to campaign against Ālǔtái.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Huíhuí Hālà Mǎyá murdered Commander Liú Bǐngqiān,
occupied Sùzhōu Wèi, and rebelled.
Commander of a Thousand Zhū Dí and others suppressed the rebellion.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Ālǔtái feigned surrender.
The Emperor ordered his generals to prepare their formations,
and indeed, Ālǔtái came to attack with his entire force.
The Emperor personally led elite cavalry to meet and engage,
defeating him decisively,
and pursuing the routed enemy for over a hundred *lǐ*.
On the day Dīngwèi,
he was defeated again.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the army returned to the capital.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor arrived at Kāipíng.
While on campaign,
the Emperor, mindful of the hardships of the soldiers,
often ate vegetarian meals.
On this day, after a banquet and rewards,
he resumed regular meals.
Sīníng Hóu Sòng Hǔ was stationed in Gānsù.
On the day Xīnsì,
famine relief was provided to Ānqìng, Huīzhōu, Fèngyáng, and Zhènjiāng.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor arrived in Běijīng
and received congratulations in the Fèngtiān Diàn.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
rewards were dispensed according to merit.
In the eighth month, on the day Rényín,
Liǔ Shēng was promoted to Ānyuǎn Hóu.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Hé Fú committed suicide.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Yellow River overflowed at Kāifēng.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor visited Tiānshòu Shān.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor departed from Běijīng.
That month,
Japanese pirates raided Fúzhōu.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎxū,
the Emperor arrived in Jīngshī.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐsì,
Ālǔtái sent envoys to present horses as tribute.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Chén Jìkuò begged to surrender,
and was appointed You Bùzhèngshǐ of Jiāozhǐ,
but Chén Jìkuò did not accept the appointment.
That year,
Shīniēgān raided the eastern bank of the Yellow River,
and Níngxià Dūzhīhuī Wáng Chù was defeated and killed.
Bóní, Lǚsòng, Féngjiāshīlán, Sūméndálà, Bǎnggélà sent tribute.
Zhànchéng sent elephants as tribute.
Liúqiú Shānnán, Zhǎowā, Xiānluó sent horses as tribute.
Liúqiú Zhōngshān sent tribute three times.
In the ninth year, spring, first month, on the day Jiǎxū,
great sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Liǔ Shēng was stationed in Níngxià.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Zhāng Fǔ was appointed Zēnglǔ Fùjiàngjūn
to join Mù Shèng in suppressing Jiāozhǐ.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Fēngchéng Hóu Lǐ Bīn and Píngjiāng Bó Chén Xuān led troops from Zhèjiāng and Fújiàn to capture sea pirates.
In the second month, on the day Xīnhài,
Chén Yīng was found guilty,
imprisoned, and died.
On the day Bǐngchén,
an edict pardoned Jiāozhǐ.
On the day Dīngsì,
Japanese pirates captured Chānghuà Qiānhùsuǒ.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Gōngbù Shàngshū Sòng Lǐ opened the Huìtōng Hé (Grand Canal).
In the third month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Xiāo Shízhōng and other *jìnshì* were granted degrees and official ranks.
On the day Rényǐn,
the old course of the Yellow River in Xiángfú Xiàn was dredged.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Liú Jiāng was stationed in Liáodōng.
In the summer, sixth month, on the day Yǐsì,
Zhèng Hé returned from the Western Ocean.
That month,
Jiě Jìn, You Cānyì of Jiāozhǐ, was imprisoned.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Zhāng Fǔ defeated the rebels at Yuècháng Jiāng.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùyín,
the Emperor instructed the judicial authorities
that all death sentences must be reviewed five times.
On the day Rényǐn,
an order was issued that屯田軍 (military colonists) whose official duties interfered with farming
would be exempt from grain taxes,
and this was established as a regulation.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
taxes and labor services for the banished military and civilians in Běijīng were relaxed.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Tùlì Tiēmù'ér of Hāmì was enfeoffed as Zhōngyì Wáng.
On the day Yǐsì,
the *Shílù* (Veritable Records) of Tàizǔ was re-edited.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùwǔ,
arrears of taxes in Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the day Guǐhài,
Zhāng Fǔ defeated the rebels at Shēngjué Jiāng.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Zhān Jī, the Emperor's eldest grandson, was established as Huáng Tàisūn (Imperial Grandson).
On the day Rényǐn,
Hán Guān was appointed Zhēngyí Fùjiàngjūn
and reassigned to garrison Jiāozhǐ.
Dūzhīhuī Gě Sēn was stationed in Guǎngxī.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
an imperial edict commanded judicial authorities not to delay in resolving and releasing prisoners.
That month,
envoys were dispatched to supervise the burial of exposed bones on battlefields.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénhái,
an imperial edict pardoned the offenses of the three guards—Fúyú, Wǎnyán, and Tàiníng—
and ordered them to present tribute.
In the intercalary month, on the day Dīngsì,
officials of the various ministries were ordered to present proposals on matters beneficial or detrimental to the military and civilians.
That year,
there were floods in Zhèjiāng, Húguǎng, Hénán, Shùntiān, and Yángzhōu.
There were epidemics in Hénán and Shǎnxī.
Envoys were dispatched to provide relief.
The King of Mǎlājiā came to court.
Zhǎowā, Bǎnggélà, Gǔlǐ, Kēzhī, Sūméndálà, Ālǔ, Pénghéng, Jílánfó, Nánwūlǐ, and Xiānluó presented tribute.
Ālǔtái presented horses as tribute,
and Biéshībālǐ offered a spotted leopard.
Liúqiú Zhōngshān presented tribute three times.
In the tenth year, spring, first month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
over fifteen hundred officials who had come to court for an audience were ordered to each present concerns regarding the suffering of the people.
Those who did not speak would be punished,
but those whose statements were inappropriate would not be questioned.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
great sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
famine relief was provided in Píngyáng.
Officials of the Bùzhèngshǐ and the prefectures and counties who failed to report the famine were arrested and punished.
In the second month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
arrears of taxes in Shānxī and Hénán were remitted.
On the day Gēngchén,
Liáo Wáng Zhí was found guilty
and his guard detachment was abolished.
In the third month, on the day Dīnghài,
Fēngchéng Hóu Lǐ Bīn suppressed the rebellious bandits Bā'ěrsī Wǎluódǎi in Gānsù.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Mǎ Duó and other *jìnshì* were granted degrees and official ranks.
On the day Jiǎchén,
