land tax for areas affected by flood in Běijīng was remitted.
In summer, sixth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
the Hùbù (Ministry of Revenue) was instructed
that any local officials in prefectures and counties or imperial envoys who witnessed the suffering of the people and failed to report it
would all be arrested and punished.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
eunuchs were forbidden from interfering in the affairs of the various ministries.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Zhāng Fǔ decisively defeated the Jiāozhǐ rebels at Shéntóu Hǎi.
On the day Jǐwèi,
an imperial edict commanded border generals to construct a stone wall from Cháng'ān Lǐng westward to Xǐmǎ Lín
and deep moats.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Wùchén,
the Emperor hunted at Wǔgāng, south of the city.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rényǐn,
Shìjiǎng Yáng Róng managed the affairs of Gānsù.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Zhèng Hé was again sent as envoy to the Western Ocean.
That year,
Bóní, Zhànchéng, Xiānluó, Mǎlājiā, Bǎnggélà, Sūméndálà, Nánbó Lì, and Qiúliú Shānnán presented tribute.
In the eleventh year, in spring, the first month, on the *Xīnsì* day,
there was a solar eclipse.
An edict was issued to suspend court audiences, congratulations, and banquets.
On the *Rénwǔ* day,
an imperial instruction was given to the Grand Coordinator (*Tōngzhèngshǐ*) and the investigating censor of the Ministry of Rites (*Lǐkē gěishìzhōng*),
that any official entering the capital for an audience who, having suffered from disaster or damage in their jurisdiction, failed to report it and it was subsequently reported by others,
should be punished.
On the *Xīnmǎo* day,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the Southern Altar (*Nánjiāo*).
On the *Xīnchǒu* day,
Lǐ Bīn, Marquis of Fēngchéng, was appointed to garrison Gānsù,
and Sòng Hǔ was recalled.
In the second month, on the *Xīnhài* day,
the Guìzhōu Provincial Administration Commission (*Bùzhèngsī*) was first established.
On the *Guǐhài* day,
an order was issued for households in Běijīng to raise and breed horses on a shared basis,
and this was made into a permanent regulation.
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
the emperor traveled to Běijīng,
with the Imperial Grandson (*Huángtàisūn*) accompanying him.

The Minister (*Shàngshū*) Jiǎn Yì, the Grand Academicians (*Xuégù*) Huáng Huái, the Instructor of the Heir Apparent (*Yùdé*) Yáng Shìqí, and the Imperial Remembrancer (*Xǐmǎ*) Yáng Pǔ assisted the Crown Prince (*Huángtàizǐ*) in supervising the state.
On the *Yǐchǒu* day,
the emperor departed from the capital.
Investigating censors (*Gěishìzhōng*) and censors (*Yùshǐ*) were ordered to inquire after and show concern for the elderly in every place they passed,
bestowing wine, meat, and silk upon them.
On the *Bǐngyín* day,
Empress Rénxiào was interred at Chánglíng.
On the *Xīnwèi* day,
the emperor stopped at Fèngyáng
and paid respects at the imperial mausoleum (*Huánglíng*).
In summer, the fourth month, on the *Jǐyǒu* day,
the emperor arrived at Běijīng.
In the fifth month, on the *Dīngwèi* day,
Cáoxiàn presented a *zōuyú* (a mythical auspicious beast).
The ritual officials requested to offer congratulations,
but this was not permitted.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *Wùyín* day,
Ālǔtái was enfeoffed as the Prince of Héníng.
In the eighth month, on the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
there was an earthquake in Běijīng.
On the *Yǐchǒu* day,
Gù Chéng, Marquis of Zhènyuǎn, was dispatched to suppress the rebellious Miao people of Sīzhōu and Jìngzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the *Rénwǔ* day,
an edict was issued stating that from now on, county and prefecture officials should inspect their jurisdictions every spring,
and immediately capture and exterminate locusts and grasshoppers that harm crops.
Those who failed to comply with the edict, along with the two provincial administration commissions (*Èrsī*), would be punished.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *Bǐngyín* day,
an imperial letter sealed with the imperial seal was issued, ordering the Crown Prince to review prisoners.
In the eleventh month, on the *Wùyín* day,
quilts made from wild silkworm cocoons were prepared,
and the Crown Prince was ordered to offer them to the Imperial Ancestral Temple (*Tàimiào*).
On the *Rénwǔ* day,
Mahàmù of the Oirats (*Wǎlà*) led his troops across the Yǐnmǎhé.
Ālǔtái reported the alarm,
and frontier generals were ordered to strengthen their defenses.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
Chén Mào, Marquis of Níngyáng,
along with Grand Censors-in-chief (*Dūdū*) Tán Qīng, Mǎ Jù, and Zhū Chóng, were sent to patrol the borders of Níngxià, Dàtóng, and Shānxī,
to inspect and train soldiers and horses.
Soon after, troops from Shǎnxī, Shānxī, and the five guards (*wǔwèi*) including Tóngguān were ordered to be stationed at Xuānfǔ.
Troops from the three Regional Military Commissions (*Sāndūzhǐhuīshǐsī*) of Zhōngdū, Liáodōng, and Hénán, and the four guards including Wǔpíng, were ordered to rendezvous at Běijīng.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
Sūn Yán, Earl of Yìngchéng, was dispatched to defend Kāipíng.
In the twelfth month, on the *Rénzǐ* day,
Zhāng Fǔ and Mù Shèng decisively defeated the Jiaozhi rebels at the Àizǐjiāng.
In this year,
Mahàmù assassinated his lord, Běnyǎshīlǐ,
and installed Dálǐbā as Khan (*Kèhán*).
Béishībālǐ, Mǎnlàjiā, Zhànchéng, and the Western King of Zhǎowā offered tribute.
Zhōngshān of Liúqiú offered tribute four times.
Shānnán of Liúqiú offered tribute twice.

Basic Annals VII: Chéngzǔ III
In the twelfth year, spring, the first month, on the *Gēngyín* day,
the Miao rebellion in Sīzhōu was pacified.
On the *Xīnchǒu* day,
150,000 commoners from Shāndōng, Shānxī, Hénán, and Fèngyáng, Huái'ān, Xú, and Pī were dispatched
to transport grain to Xuānfǔ.
In the second month, on the *Jǐyǒu* day,
a grand military review was held.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
the emperor personally led an expedition against the Oirats.
Liǔ Shēng, Marquis of Ānyuǎn, commanded the main camp (*Dàyíng*).
Zhèng Hēng, Marquis of Wǔ'ān, commanded the central army (*Zhōngjūn*).
Chén Mào, Marquis of Níngyáng, and Lǐ Bīn, Marquis of Fēngchéng, commanded the left and right vanguards (*Zuǒ Yòushào*).
Wáng Tōng, Marquis of Chéngshān, and Grand Censor-in-chief Tán Qīng commanded the left and right flanks (*Zuǒ Yòuyì*).
Grand Censors-in-chief Liú Jiāng and Zhū Róng served as the vanguard (*Qiánfēng*).
On the *Gēngshēn* day,
relief was provided to the famine-stricken areas of Fèngxiáng and Lǒngzhōu,
and senior officials who failed to report the famine were punished.
In the third month, on the *Guǐwèi* day,
Zhāng Fǔ captured Chén Jìkuò in Laos and presented him,
and Jiaozhi was pacified.
On the *Gēngyín* day,
the emperor departed from Běijīng,
with the Imperial Grandson accompanying him.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *Jiǎchén* day,
the emperor stopped at Xīnghé,
where a grand military review was held.
On the *Jǐyǒu* day,
military awards, punishments, and orders were promulgated.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
officials for transmitting orders and recording merits were established.
On the *Dīngmǎo* day,
the emperor stopped at Túnyúngǔ,
where Bólúobùhuā and others surrendered.
In the fifth month, on the *Dīngchǒu* day,
ministers (*Shàngshū*), officials of the Court of Imperial Entertainments (*Guānglùqīng*), and investigating censors (*Gěishìzhōng*) were appointed as battle supervisors (*Dūzhèn guān*),
to observe whether generals and soldiers performed their duties or not.
In the sixth month, on the *Jiǎchén* day,
Liú Jiāng encountered Oirat troops
and fought them at Kānghālǐhái,
defeating them.
On the *Wùshēn* day,
the emperor stopped at Hūlánkūshīwēn,
where Mahàmù led his forces to attack.
They were decisively defeated,
and pursued to the Tǔláhé,
where Mahàmù fled under the cover of night.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
the army returned to the capital,
and victory was declared to Ālǔtái.
On the *Wùwǔ* day,
the emperor stopped at Sānfēngshān,
and Ālǔtái sent envoys to pay respects at court.
On the *Jǐsì* day,
an edict announcing the defeat of the Oirats was issued to the entire realm.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *Wùzǐ* day,
the emperor stopped at Hóngqiáo.
An edict was issued that if the six armies (*Liùshī*) entering the pass trampled fields or seized people's livestock,
they would be tried by military law.
On the *Jǐhài* day,
the emperor stopped at Shāhé,
and the Crown Prince sent envoys to welcome the imperial carriage.
In the eighth month, on the *Xīnchǒu* day,
the emperor arrived at Běijīng
and received court felicitations at the Fèngtiāndiàn.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
rent for Běijīng prefectures and counties was remitted for two years.
On the *Wùwǔ* day,
generals and soldiers who participated in the expedition were rewarded.
In the ninth month, on the *Guōwèi* day,
Guō Liàng and Xú Hēng were appointed to defend Kāipíng.
On the *Bǐngxū* day,
the Miao rebellion in Jìngzhōu was pacified.
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
Fèi Huán was appointed to garrison Gānsù,
and Liú Jiāng was appointed to garrison Liáodōng.
In the intercalary month, on the *Jiǎchén* day,
due to the Crown Prince's tardiness in sending envoys to welcome the imperial carriage,
the Imperial Lecturers (*Shìdú*) Huáng Huái and
Yáng Shìqí, the Proofreader (*Zhèngzì*) Jīn Wèn, and the Imperial Remembrancers (*Xǐmǎ*) Yáng Pǔ and Ruì Shàn were summoned and imprisoned.
Shortly after, Yáng Shìqí was released and reinstated to his position.
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
Wú Gāo was recalled.
On the *Dīngmǎo* day,
Grand Censor-in-chief Zhū Róng was appointed to garrison Dàtóng.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the *Jiǎchén* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
Jìn Wáng Jìxī was demoted to commoner status.
On the *Gēngshēn* day,
land tax amounting to over 479,000 *shí* was remitted for the flood-stricken areas of Sū, Sōng, Háng, Jiā, and Hú.
In this year,
Shānádéxīnggē from the country of Níbālǐ came to court
and was enfeoffed as a king.
Pénghéng and Wūsīzàng offered tribute.
Zhēnlà presented gold-embroidered robes.
The King of Zhōngshān of Liúqiú offered tribute horses.
Bǎnggélà offered a qílín.
In the thirteenth year, spring, the first month, on the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
the passes north of Jūyōng were blocked.
On the *Dīngwèi* day,
Mahàmù offered an apology and requested to pay tribute,
which was granted.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
the Wǔméngate in Běijīng suffered a fire.
On the *Wùwǔ* day,
an imperial decree ordered all internal and external government offices to remit all outstanding arrears,
and all generals, soldiers, and officers who had committed crimes were pardoned.
In the second month, on the *Guǐyǒu* day,

Commander Liú Bīn and Investigating Censor Zhāng Pán, along with twelve others, were dispatched to inspect military drills and garrison administration in Shānxī, Shāndōng, Dàtóng, Shǎnxī, Gānsù, and Liáodōng,
and to report their findings.
On the *Jiǎxū* day,
the traveling Ministry of Rites (*Xíngzài Lǐbù*) was ordered to conduct the metropolitan examination for scholars (*Gòngshì*) from across the realm.
On the *Guǐwèi* day,
Zhāng Fǔ and others returned with their armies.
On the *Wùzǐ* day,
rewards were bestowed according to their varying achievements in the pacification of Jiaozhi.
scholars were tested in Běijīng,
In the third month, on the *Jǐhài* day,
and Chén Xún and others were awarded the ranks of *Jìnshì* or other varying statuses.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
the Man barbarians of Guǎngxī rebelled,
and Commander (*Zhǐhuī tóngzhī*) Gé Sēn was dispatched to suppress them, which he successfully did.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *wùchén*,
Zhāng Fǔ garrisoned Jiāozhǐ.
Fifth month, on the day *dīngyǒu* at the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day *yǐchǒu*,
the Qīngjiāng Pǔ was dredged,
connecting Běijīng to the grain transport system.
Sixth month,
relief was distributed for floods in Běijīng, Hénán, and Shāndōng.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *guǐmǎo*,
Zhèng Hé returned.
On the day *yǐsì*,
the Dūzhǎng Mán in Róngxiàn, Sìchuān, were pacified.
Eighth month, on the day *gēngchén*,
relief was distributed for famine in Shāndōng, Hénán, and Shùntiān Zhōuxiàn in Běijīng.
Ninth month, on the day *rénxū*,
there was an earthquake in Běijīng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *jiǎshēn*,
hunting took place in the near suburbs.
On the day *rénchén*,
the judicial officials reported on those who embezzled official grain.
The Emperor was enraged
and ordered their execution.
When the report was resubmitted,
the Emperor said:
"I was mistaken.
They shall still be judged according to the law.
From now on, all cases involving capital punishment must undergo five reviews.
This shall be made into a decree."
Twelfth month,
land taxes were remitted for flooded and drought-stricken fields in Shùntiān, Sūzhōu, Fèngyáng, Zhèjiāng, Húguǎng, Hénán, and Shāndōng Zhōuxiàn.
In this year,
Liúqiú Shānnán and Shānběi,
the Western King of Zhǎowā,
Zhànchéng,
Gǔlǐ,
Kēzhī,
Nánbólì,
Gānbālǐ,
Mǎlájiā,
Hūlúmósī,
Hāmì,
Hāliè,
Sāmǎ'érhǎn,
Huǒzhōu,
Tǔlúfān,
Sūméndádá,
Ǎndūhuái,
Shīlásī came to pay tribute.
Málín and other foreign states presented麒麟 (qílín), celestial horses, and divine deer.

Fourteenth year, spring, first month, on the day *jǐyǒu*,
Běijīng, Hénán, and Shāndōng suffered famine.
Arrears of rent from the twelfth year of Yǒnglè were remitted,
and over 1.37 million *shí* of grain were issued for relief.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
Dūdū Jīn Yù suppressed the mountain bandits in Guǎnglíngshān, Shānxī,
and pacified them.
Third month, on the day *guǐsì*,
Dūdū Liáng Fú garrisoned Húguǎng and Guìzhōu.
On the day *rényín*,
Ālǔtái defeated the Wǎlà and
came to present a victory report.
Summer, fourth month, on the day *rénshēn*,
Lǐbù Shàngshū Lǚ Zhèn requested to perform the Fēngshàn sacrifices.
The Emperor said:
"Although there is peace in the realm today,
many regions suffer from floods, droughts, and epidemics.
How dare I claim it is an era of Great Peace?
Moreover, the Six Classics contain no texts on Fēngshàn sacrifices.
This act does not follow ancient precedents
and is utterly meaningless."
He did not permit it.
On the day *yǐhài*,
Hú Guǎng was appointed Wényuāngé Dàxuéshì.
Sixth month, on the day *dīngmǎo*,
Dūdū Tóngzhī Cài Fú and others prepared defenses against *wōkòu* in Shāndōng.
Autumn, seventh month, on the day *dīngyǒu*,
envoys were dispatched to capture locusts in Běijīng, Hénán, and Shāndōng Zhōuxiàn.
On the day *rényín*,
the Yellow River breached its banks at Kāifēng.
On the day *yǐsì*,
Jǐnyīwèi Zhǐhuīshǐ Jì Gāng was executed for his crimes.
Eighth month, on the day *guǐyǒu* at dawn,
the Star of Longevity appeared.
The protocol officials requested to submit a memorial of congratulations,
but it was not allowed.
On the day *dīnghài*,
construction began on the Western Palace in Běijīng.
Ninth month, on the day *guǐmǎo*,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day *wùshēn*,
the Emperor departed Běijīng.
Winter, tenth month, on the day *dīngchǒu*,
he stopped at Fèngyáng and
offered sacrifices at the Imperial Tombs.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
he arrived from Běijīng
and visited Xiàolíng.
Eleventh month, on the day *rényín*,
an edict ordered civil and military officials to convene and deliberate on the construction of Běijīng.
On the day *bǐngwǔ*,
Zhāng Fǔ was recalled.
On the day *wùshēn*,
Hàn Wáng Gāo Xù committed a crime,
and two of his bodyguards were dismissed.
Displaced people from Shāndōng, Shānxī, and Húguǎng were resettled in Bǎo'ānzhōu,
and granted three years of tax exemption.
Twelfth month, on the day *dīngmǎo*,
Zhèng Hé was dispatched again to the Western Oceans.
In this year,
Zhànchéng, Gǔlǐ, Zhǎowā, Mǎlájiā, Sūméndádá, Nánwūlǐ, Bóní, Pénghēng, Xīlánshān, Liúshān, Nánbólì, Ādān, Málín, Hūlúmósī, and Kēzhī came to pay tribute.
Liúqiú Zhōngshān paid tribute a second time.
Fifteenth year, spring, first month, on the day *dīngyǒu*,
the great sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were performed at the Southern Suburbs.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
Píngjiāng Bó Chén Xuān supervised grain transport
and delivered timber to Běijīng.
Second month, on the day *guǐhài*,
Gǔ Wáng Huì committed a crime
and was demoted to a commoner.
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
Fēngchéng Hóu Lǐ Bīn garrisoned Jiāozhǐ.
On the day *rénshēn*,
Tàiníng Hóu Chén Guī supervised the construction of Běijīng;
Liǔ Shēng and Wáng Tōng assisted him.
Third month, on the day *dīnghài*,
the first scholars from Jiāozhǐ arrived in the capital to pay tribute.
On the day *bǐngshēn*,
prisoners guilty of miscellaneous offenses, including those sentenced to death,
were sent to work in Běijīng to atone for their crimes.
On the day *bǐngwǔ*,
Hàn Wáng Gāo Xù committed a crime
and was transferred to be enfeoffed in Lè'ānzhōu.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
the Emperor embarked on a northern tour,
departing from the capital,
with the Crown Prince supervising the state.
Summer, fourth month, on the day *jǐsì*,
he stopped at Zhūchéng.
A strict prohibition was issued against soldiers trampling commoners' crops;
those who caused damage would have their year's rent remitted.
If they had already defaulted on rent due to floods or droughts,
it would also be remitted.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
the Western Palace was completed.
Fifth month, on the day *bǐngxū*,
the Emperor arrived in Běijīng.
Sixth month, on the day *dīngyǒu*,
Lǐ Bīn attacked the Jiāozhǐ rebel Lí Hé
and beheaded him.
On the day *jǐhài*,
the palace eunuch Zhāng Qiān returned from his mission to the Western Oceans.
