Autumn, eighth month, on the day *jiǎwǔ*,
a person from Ōuníng presented a golden elixir.
The Emperor said:
"This is a charlatan.
Order him to consume it himself,
and destroy his formula books."
Ninth month, on the day *dīngmǎo*,
the Kǒngzǐ Temple in Qūfù was completed,
and the Emperor personally composed an inscription carved into stone.
Winter, tenth month,
Lǐ Bīn defeated the Jiāozhǐ rebel Yáng Jìnjiāng
and beheaded him.
Eleventh month, on the day *guǐyǒu*,
Lǐbù Shàngshū Zhào Hóng was appointed Bīngbù Shàngshū
to inspect the advantages and disadvantages of military and civilian garrisons north of the frontier.
In this year,
the Eastern and Western Rulers of Sūlù from the Western Oceans came to court.
Liúqiú Zhōngshān, Biéshībālǐ, Liúqiú Shānnán, Zhēnlà, Bóní, Zhànchéng, Xiāmluó, Hāliè, Sāmǎ'érhǎn came to pay tribute.
Sixteenth year, spring, first month, on the day *jiǎyín*,
Lí Lì of Jiāozhǐ rebelled,
and Dūdū Zhū Guǎng defeated him.
On the day *jiǎxū*,
*wōkòu* captured Sōngménwèi,
and Ànchásī Qiānshì Shí Lǔ was executed for his involvement.
Xīng'ān Bó Xú Hēng and Dūdū Xià Guì prepared defenses at Kāipíng.
Second month, on the day *xīnchǒu*,
bandits in the Sìmángxiàn of Jiāozhǐ killed Zhīxiàn Ōuyáng Zhì in rebellion;
Lǐ Bīn dispatched generals to attack and drive them off.
Third month, on the day *jiǎyín*,
Lǐ Qí and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree and official positions with varying ranks.
Dūdū Qiānshì Liú Jiàn prepared border defenses at Dàtóng.
Summer, fifth month, on the day *gēngxū*,
the revised *Tàizǔ Shílù* was completed.
On the day *dīngsì*,
Hú Guǎng passed away.
Autumn, seventh month, on the day *jǐsì*,
an imperial edict reprimanded the officials of Shǎnxī:
"It has been heard that harvests in your jurisdiction have repeatedly failed in recent years,
causing people to become displaced and starve.
Officials have sat by idly, showing no concern,
nor have they reported this.
Where lies the fault?
Quickly dispatch stored grain for relief."
Zànshàn Liáng Qián and Sījiàn Zhōu Miǎn were imprisoned and died
for shortcomings in assisting and guiding the Crown Prince.
In the twelfth month of winter, on the day *wùzǐ*,
an edict was issued to the Ministry of Justice:
“I have repeatedly instructed officials both inside and outside the capital to be honest and love the people,
yet incompetent officials continue to act with wanton disregard,
causing suffering to the common people.
Just as a good farmer must remove weeds,
because they harm the crops.
From now on,
those who commit bribery or embezzlement shall be punished according to the law.”
On the day *xīnchǒu*,
Wáng Tōng, Marquis of Chéngshān, hastened by post to relieve the famine in Shǎnxī.
That year,

Siam (Xiānluó), Chámpā (Zhànchéng), Java (Zhǎowā), Sumatra (Sūméndálà), Nepal (Níbālà), Malacca (Mǎnlàjiā), Nánbólì, Herat (Hāliè), Shahrukh (Shāhālǔ), Qǐnlǐdá, and Samarkand (Sāmǎérhǎn) presented tribute.
Ryukyu Chūzan (Liúqiú Zhōngshān) presented tribute twice.
In the spring of the seventeenth year, in the second month, on the day *yǐyǒu*,
Xú Hēng, Earl of Xīng'ān, was ordered to guard Xīnghé, Kāipíng, and Dàtóng.
In the fifth month of summer, on the day *bǐngwǔ*,
Grand Commissioner Fāng Zhèng defeated Límì at Kělánzhà.
In the sixth month, on the day *rénwǔ*,
the land tax for the previous year's flood-stricken fields in Shùntiān Prefecture was remitted.
On the day *wùzǐ*,
Liú Jiāng annihilated the Japanese pirates at Wànghǎiguō,
and he was enfeoffed as Earl of Guǎngníng.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day *gēngshēn*,
Zhèng Hé returned.
In the eighth month,
the eunuch Mǎ Qí incited Pān Liáo, the Prefect of Yì'ān in Jiāozhǐ, to rebel.
In the ninth month, on the day *bǐngchén*,
auspicious clouds were seen,
and the court ritual officials requested to present a congratulatory memorial,
but this was not permitted.
In the twelfth month of winter, on the day *gēngchén*,
an edict was issued to the Ministry of Justice, stating:
“Punishment
is something the sagely rulers treat with caution.
If even ordinary men and women do not die a proper death,
it is enough to damage the harmony of heaven and earth,
and invite disasters of flood and drought.
This is very much contrary to my intention of benevolence and compassion.
From now on,
all death sentences from various provincial offices
shall be sent to the capital for review and record,
and only after three appeals will the execution be carried out.”
On the day *yǐwèi*,
Liú Zhònglián, Vice Minister of Works, verified the household registration and land tax in Jiāozhǐ,
and investigated the advantages and disadvantages for the military and civilians.
That year,

Hāmì, Turpan (Tǔlǔfān), Shiraz (Shīlàsī), Isfahan (Yìsīfúhǎn), Chenla (Zhēnlà), Chámpā (Zhànchéng), Herat (Hāliè), Ālǔ, Nánbólì, Sumatra (Sūméndálà), Bādáihēi merchants, and Malacca (Mǎnlàjiā) presented tribute.
Ryukyu Chūzan (Liúqiú Zhōngshān) presented tribute four times.
In the spring of the eighteenth year, in the first month, on the day *guǐmǎo*,
Lǐ Bīn, together with Grand Commissioners Sūn Lín and Xú Yuán, defeated Límì at Léijiāng.
In the intercalary month, on the day *bǐngzǐ*,
Yáng Róng and Jīn Yòuzī, Academicians of the Hànlín Academy, were appointed Grand Secretaries of the Wényuāngé.
On the day *gēngchén*,
talented individuals were promoted;
thirteen commoners, including Mǎ Lín, were made Provincial Administration Commissioners, Administration Vice Commissioners, and Administration Counselors.
In the second month, on the day *jǐyǒu*,
the sorceress Táng Sài'ér of Pútái rebelled,
and Liǔ Shēng, Marquis of Ānyuǎn, led an army to suppress her.
In the third month, on the day *xīnsì*,
the rebels were defeated at Xièshízhàzhài;
Grand Commissioner Liú Zhōng died in battle,
and Sài'ér escaped.
On the day *jiǎshēn*,
Wèi Qīng, Assistant Military Commissioner of Shāndōng, defeated the rebels at Ānqīu,
and Commander Wáng Zhēn defeated the rebels at Zhūchéng,
presenting captives to the capital.
On the day *wùzǐ*,
Chǔ Yán and Zhāng Hǎi, Provincial Administration Commissioners of Shāndōng,
and Liú Běn, Surveillance Commissioner, were executed for complicity in releasing bandits.
On the day *wùxū*,
Liǔ Shēng was brought to justice for dilatory action,
but was later released.
In the fifth month of summer, on the day *rénwǔ*,
Zhū Róng, Left Grand Commissioner, garrisoned Liáodōng.
On the day *gēngyín*,
Hóu Bǎo and Féng Guì, Administration Vice Commissioners of Jiāozhǐ, defended against the rebels,
and died in battle.
In the sixth month, on the day *bǐngwǔ*,
there was an earthquake in Běijīng.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day *dīnghài*,
Xú Hēng was ordered to guard Kāipíng.
In the eighth month, on the first day *dīngyǒu*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the ninth month, on the day *jǐsì*,
the Crown Prince was summoned.
On the day *dīnghài*,
an edict declared that from next year, the capital (Jīngshī) would be renamed Nánjīng,
and Běijīng would be renamed Jīngshī.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day *gēngshēn*,
Lǐ Bīn dispatched Commander Fāng Zhèng to defeat Límì in Laos (Lǎowō).
In the eleventh month, on the day *wùchén*,
an edict was issued to the empire regarding the transfer of the capital to Běijīng.
That month,
famine relief was provided in Qīngzhōu and Láizhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the day *jǐwèi*,
the Crown Prince and the Imperial Grandson arrived in Běijīng.
On the day *guǐhài*,
the altars, temples, palaces, and halls in Běijīng were completed.
That year,
the Eastern Depot (Dōngchǎng) was first established,
and eunuchs were ordered to secretly investigate matters.
The King of Gǔmálàláng came to court.
Siam (Xiānluó), Chámpā (Zhànchéng), Java (Zhǎowā), Malacca (Mǎnlàjiā), Sumatra (Sūméndálà), and the Western King of Sulu (Sūlù) arrived.
In the spring of the nineteenth year, on the first day *jiǎzǐ* of the first month,
the spirit tablets of the Five Ancestors were enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
The Emperor presided over the court audience and congratulations in the Fèngtiān Hall,
and a grand banquet was held.
On the day *jiǎxū*,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the southern suburbs.
On the day *wùyín*,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the day *guǐsì*,
Zhèng Hé was again dispatched on an envoy mission to the Western Ocean.
In the second month, on the day *xīnchǒu*,
Hú Yuán, Assistant Grand Commissioner, led an army to patrol the sea and capture Japanese pirates.
In the third month, on the day *xīnsì*,
Zēng Hèlíng and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree and official appointments with varying ranks.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day *gēngzǐ*,
the three halls of Fèngtiān, Huágài, and Jǐnshēn suffered a disaster (fire),
and an edict commanded all officials to directly point out deficiencies.
On the day *yǐsì*,
an edict ordered the cessation of all matters inconvenient to the people and non-urgent tasks,
the remission of outstanding taxes from before the seventeenth year,
and the exemption of land taxes for fields affected by disaster last year.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
for the Wànshòujié (Emperor's birthday),
congratulations were halted due to the disaster in the three halls.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
Jiǎn Yì and twenty-six others were dispatched to tour the empire,
to comfort the military and civilians.
In the fifth month, on the day *yǐchǒu*,
Kē Xiān, Censor who submitted remonstrances, and Censors Hé Zhōng, Zhèng Wéihuán, Luó Tōng, and others were dismissed and appointed Prefects (Zhīzhōu).
On the day *gēngyín*,
Jiāozhǐ was ordered to establish military agricultural colonies.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day *jǐsì*,
the Emperor was about to embark on a northern expedition,
and an imperial order appointed Grand Commissioner Zhū Róng to lead the vanguard,
Liǔ Shēng, Marquis of Ānyuǎn, to lead the central army,
Chén Mào, Marquis of Níngyáng, to lead the elite cavalry of the imperial guard,
Xuē Bīn, Earl of Yǒngshùn, and Wú Kèzhōng, Earl of Gōngshùn, to lead the cavalry units,
Zhèng Hēng, Marquis of Wǔ'ān, and Xuē Lù, Marquis of Yángwǔ, to lead the left and right scouts,
and Zhāng Fǔ, Duke of Yīng, and Wáng Tōng, Marquis of Chéngshān, to lead the left and right wings.
In the eighth month, on the first day *xīnmǎo*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the day *xīnyǒu*,
eunuchs Yáng Shí, Censor Dài Chéng, and others were separately dispatched to verify the accounts of receipts and disbursements in the empire's treasuries.
On the day *bǐngzǐ*,
the military provisions for the northern expedition were deliberated, leading to the imprisonment of Xià Yuánjí, Minister of Revenue, and Wú Zhōng, Minister of Justice;
Fāng Bīn, Minister of War, committed suicide.
On the day *xīnsì*,
Lǐ Shímiǎn, Assistant Lecturer, was imprisoned.
On the day *jiǎshēn*,
able-bodied men from Zhílì, Shānxī, Hénán, Shāndōng, and the five prefectures of Nánjī Yìngtiān,
and the three prefectures of Chú, Hé, and Xú, were mobilized to transport grain,
with a deadline of the second month of next year to reach Xuānfǔ.
That year,
the Wise and Righteous King Tàipíng and the Happy and Peaceful King Bǎtú Bóluó of Oirat (Wǎlà) came to court.

Hormuz (Hūlúmósī), Aden (Ādān), Dhofar (Zǔfáer), Lāsà, Brava (Bùlàwā), Mogadishu (Mùgǔdōushù), Calicut (Gǔlǐ), Cochin (Kēzhī), Kayal (Jiāyìlè), Ceylon (Xīlánshān), Lùshān, Nánbólì, Sumatra (Sūméndálà), Ālǔ, Malacca (Mǎnlàjiā), Kambari (Gānbālǐ), Sulu (Sūlù), Bengal (Bǎnggélà), Brunei (Bóní), and the King of Gǔmálàláng presented tribute.
Siam (Xiānluó) presented tribute twice.
In the spring of the twentieth year, on the first day *jǐwèi* of the first month,
there was a solar eclipse;
court congratulations were suspended,
and an edict commanded all officials to reform and reflect.
On the day *xīnwèi*,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the southern suburbs.
On the day *rénshēn*,
Lǐ Bīn, Marquis of Fēngchéng, died in Jiāozhǐ.
In the second month, on the day *yǐsì*,
Zhāng Xìn, Marquis of Lóngpíng, and Lǐ Qìng, Minister of War, were separately ordered to supervise military provisions for the northern expedition,
mobilizing over 235,000 common laborers
to transport 370,000 *shi* of grain.
In the third month, on the day *bǐngyín*,
an edict ordered officials to first provide disaster relief before reporting.
On the day *yǐhài*,
Ālǔtái raided Xīnghé,
and Grand Commissioner Wáng Huàn died in battle.
On the day *dīngchǒu*,
the Emperor personally led an expedition against Ālǔtái,
and the Crown Prince supervised state affairs.
On the day *wùyín*,
the expedition departed from Jīngshī.
On the day *xīnsì*,
the expedition reached Jīmíngshān,
and Ālǔtái fled.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *Yǐmǎo*
, the army arrived at Yúnzhōu
and conducted a grand review.
In the fifth month, on the day *Yǐchǒu*
, there was a hunt at Piānlǐng.
On the day *Dīngmǎo*
, a grand review was held.
On the day *Xīnwèi*
, the army reached Xīliángtíng.
On the day *Rénshēn*
, a grand review was held.
On the day *Yǐyǒu*
, the army arrived at Kāipíng.
In the sixth month, on the day *Rénchén*
, the army was ordered to march out to Yìngchāng
, forming a square formation as they advanced.
On the day *Guǐsì*
, intelligence reported that Ālǔtái's troops were attacking Wànquán.
The generals requested to divide forces to counterattack,
but the Emperor said:
“It is a trick.
They fear our large army will assault their stronghold
, and wish to tie up our forces;
how would they dare attack the city?”
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*
, the army arrived at Yánghégǔ,
and the bandits attacking Wànquán indeed fled.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *Jǐwèi*
, Ālǔtái abandoned his baggage train by the Kuòluán Hǎi and fled north.
Troops were dispatched to burn it
and collect his livestock.
Thereupon, the army returned.
The Emperor said to his generals:
“Ālǔtái dares to defy us
, relying on the Wùliánghā as his wings.
We should return and eliminate them.”
He selected twenty thousand infantry and cavalry
, dividing them into five columns to advance simultaneously.
On the day *Gēngwǔ*
, they encountered the enemy at Qūliè'ér Hé.
The Emperor personally led the attack, defeating them
and pursuing them for thirty *lǐ*,
slaying dozens of chiefs.
On the day *Xīnwèi*
, they swept through Hexi
, capturing and slaying many.
On the day *Jiǎxū*
, the remaining factions of the Wùliánghā came to the army gate to surrender.
In this month
, the Crown Prince remitted a total of more than 610,000 *dàn* of grain and fodder for flood-stricken prefectures and counties in the Northern and Southern Zhílì, Shāndōng, and Hénán regions.
In the eighth month, on the day *Wùxū*
, all the generals who had divided their forces reported victory.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*
, an edict announcing the army's return was issued to all under heaven.
On the day *Rényín*
, Zhèng Hēng and Xuē Lù were ordered to guard Kāipíng.
Zhèng Hé returned.
In the ninth month, on the day *Rénxū*
, the Emperor arrived in the capital.
On the day *Guǐhài*
, Yáng Shìqí, Grand Academician of the Left Spring Palace, was imprisoned.
On the day *Bǐngyín*
, Jiǎn Yì, Minister of Personnel, and Lǚ Zhèn, Minister of Rites, were imprisoned;
they were both released shortly after.
On the day *Xīnwèi*
, merits from the expedition were recorded,
and Zhū Róngwǔ, Left Chief Military Commissioner, was enfeoffed as *Jìnbó*,
while Xuē Guì, Assistant Chief Military Commissioner, was enfeoffed as *Ānshùnbó*.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *Guǐsì*
, eighty eunuchs and court officials were dispatched to audit the accounts of grain intake and expenditure in granaries across the empire.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Xīnmǎo*
, Zhū Róng was stationed in Liáodōng.
In the intercalary month, on the day *Wùyín*
, the Qiánqīng Gōng caught fire.
In this year
, envoys from Xiāmluó, Sūméndálà, Ādān, and other countries brought tribute.
Zhànchéng, Liúqiú Zhōngshān, Búhuā'ér, Hāmì, Wǎlà, Tǔlúfān, and Zhǎowā offered tribute.
In the twenty-first year, spring, first month, on the day *Yǐwèi*
, a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day *Guǐmǎo*
, Chén Zhì, Earl of Róngchāng and Deputy General of Jiāozhǐ, pursued and defeated Lí Lì at Chēlai.
In the second month, on the day *Jǐsì*
, Lù Róng, Regional Military Commissioner, suppressed a rebellion by barbarians in Liǔzhōu
and pacified the region.
In the third month, on the day *Gēngzǐ*
, Imperial Censor Wáng Yù and others, in collectively deciding cases of severe prisoners,
mistakenly executed four innocent people
and were punished with public execution.
In the summer, fifth month, on the day *Guǐwèi*
, land taxes for last year's flood-stricken fields in Kāifēng, Nányáng, Wèihuī, Fèngyáng, and other prefectures were remitted.
On the day *Jǐchǒu*
, Mèng Xián, Commander of the Chángshān Guard, and others plotted rebellion
and were executed.
In the sixth month, on the first day, *Gēngxū*
, there was a solar eclipse.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *Wùxū*
, the Emperor again personally led an expedition against Ālǔtái.
Liǔ Shēng, Marquis of Ānyuǎn, and Chén Yīng, Earl of Suí'ān, led the central army.
Zhèng Hēng, Marquis of Wǔ'ān, and Mèng Yīng, Marquis of Bǎodìng, led the left vanguard.
Xuē Lù, Marquis of Yángwǔ, and Tán Zhōng, Earl of Xīnníng, led the right vanguard.
Zhāng Fǔ, Duke of Yīng, and Lǐ Ān, Earl of Ānpíng, led the left flank.
Wáng Tōng, Marquis of Chéngshān, and Xú Hēng, Earl of Xīng'ān, led the right flank.
Chén Mào, Marquis of Níngyáng, led the vanguard.
On the day *Gēngzǐ*
, Lǐ Shímiǎn was released
and his official position restored.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*
, the Crown Prince supervised the state.
On the day *Rényín*
, the army departed from the capital.
On the day *Wùshēn*
, the army arrived at Xuānfǔ.
An edict was issued to the commander of Jūyōng Guān to stop all offices from presenting gifts.
In the eighth month, on the day *Jǐyǒu*
, a grand review was held.
On the day *Gēngshēn*
, dangerous border passes such as Hēiyù and Cháng'ānlǐng were fortified.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*
, the Crown Prince remitted land taxes for flood-stricken prefectures and counties in the two capitals and Shāndōng.
In the ninth month, on the day *Wùzǐ*
, the army arrived at Xīyánghé.
On the day *Guǐsì*
, upon hearing that Ālǔtái had been defeated by Wǎlà
and his tribes scattered,
the army halted its advance.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *Jiǎyín*
, the army arrived at Shàngzhuāngbǎo.
Yěxiāntǔgān, the prince from north of the desert, led his subordinates to surrender
, and was enfeoffed as King of Zhōngyǒng
, and granted the name Jīn Zhōng.
On the day *Gēngwǔ*
, the army returned to the capital.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Jiǎshēn*
, the Emperor arrived in the capital.
In this year
, the King of Xīlánshān came to court,
and also sent envoys to offer tribute.
Zhànchéng, Gǔlǐ, Hūlǔmósī, Ādān, Zǔfá'ér, Lāsā, Bùláwā, Mùgǔdūshù, Kēzhī, Jiāyìlēi, Liúshān, Nánbólì, Sūméndálà, Ālǔ, Mǎlájiā, Shīlásī, Bànggélà, and Liúqiú Zhōngshān offered tribute.
In the twenty-second year, spring, first month, on the day *Jiǎshēn*
, Ālǔtái invaded Dàtóng and Kāipíng.
An edict was issued to officials to discuss a northern expedition,
and border generals were ordered to prepare troops and await orders.
On the day *Bǐngxū*
, troops were levied from the five military commands of Shānxī, Shāndōng, Hénán, Shǎnxī, and Liáodōng, as well as the guards of Xīníng, Gǒngchāng, Táo, and Mín
, to assemble in Běijīng and Xuānfǔ by the third month.
On the day *Wùzǐ*
, a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day *Guǐsì*
, Zhèng Hé again led an envoy to the Western Oceans.
In the third month, on the day *Wùyín*
, a grand review was held,
and the generals were instructed about the personal expedition.
Liǔ Shēng and Chén Yīng were ordered to lead the central army.
Zhāng Fǔ and Zhū Yǒng led the left flank.
Wáng Tōng and Xú Hēng led the right flank.
Zhèng Hēng and Mèng Yīng led the left vanguard.
Xuē Lù and Tán Zhōng led the right vanguard.
Chén Mào and Jīn Zhōng led the front vanguard.
On the day *Jǐmǎo*
, Xíng Kuān and others were granted the *Jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *Wùshēn*
, the Crown Prince supervised the state.
On the day *Jǐyǒu*
, the Emperor departed from the capital.
On the day *Gēngwǔ*
, the army arrived at Xíníng.
Intelligence reported that Ālǔtái had fled to the Dálánnàmù'ér Hé
, so the army pressed forward.
In the fifth month, on the day *Jǐmǎo*
, the army arrived at Kāipíng.
Envoys were sent to persuade Ālǔtái's tribes.
On the day *Yǐyǒu*
, remains found along the road were buried.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*
, a banquet was held for officials at Yìngchāng.
Eunuchs were ordered to sing five chapters of verses composed by Grand Emperor Tàizǔ.
The Emperor said:
“These were the previous emperor's admonitions to his descendants;
even in military campaigns, how could we forget them?”
On the day *Jǐhài*
, the army arrived at Wēiyuǎn Zhōu.
Another banquet was held for officials,
and the Emperor himself composed five chapters of verses,
ordering eunuchs to sing them.
The Crown Prince ordered the remission of land taxes for flood-stricken prefectures and counties in Guǎngpíng, Shùndé, Yángzhōu, Húguǎng, and Hénán.
In the sixth month, on the day *Gēngshēn*
, the vanguard reached the Dálánnàmù'ér Hé
, but found no enemy.
Zhāng Fǔ and others were ordered to search the valleys for three hundred *lǐ* but found nothing.
The army then stationed by the river.
On the day *Guǐhài*
, Chén Mào and others led their troops to Báimáng Shān,
but returned due to lack of provisions.
On the day *Jiǎzǐ*
, the army returned to the capital.
Zhèng Hēng and others were ordered to meet in Kāipíng with infantry coming from the west.
On the night of *Rénshēn*
, there was an earthquake in Nánjīng.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day of Gēngchén,
a stone inscription was carved on the cliff at Qīngshuǐyuán.
On the day of Wùzǐ,
Lǚ Zhèn was dispatched with a message for the Crown Prince about the returning army,
and an imperial edict was announced to the world.
On the day of Jǐchǒu,
the army halted at Cāngyáshù,
where the emperor became unwell.
On the day of Gēngyín,
they reached Yúmùchuān,
and his illness worsened significantly.
A deathbed edict bequeathed the throne to the Crown Prince,
and stipulated that the funeral rites should follow the regulations left by Emperor Gāo exactly.
On the day of Xīnmǎo,
he passed away at the age of sixty-five.
The Grand Eunuch Mǎ Yún secretly conspired with Grand Academicians Yáng Róng and Jīn Yòuzī,
as the six armies were out in the field,
to keep his death a secret and not announce the mourning.
They melted tin to make a shroud for the burial,
and carried the body in an imperial carriage.
Wherever they stopped, meals were offered morning and evening as usual.
On the day of Rénchén,
Yáng Róng, accompanied by Junior Supervisor Hǎi Shòu of the Imperial Horse Bureau, hurried to inform the Crown Prince.
On the day of Rényín,
the army reached Wǔpíngzhèn,
where Zhèng Hēng's infantry joined them.
In the eighth month, on the day of Jiǎchén,
Yáng Róng and others arrived at the capital,
and the Crown Prince immediately dispatched the Grandson to welcome the emperor's coffin at Kāipíng.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
when they reached Diāo'ègǔ,
the Imperial Grandson arrived at the army and announced the mourning.
On the day of Rénzǐ,
when they reached the outskirts,
the Crown Prince welcomed the coffin into the Rénzhì Diàn,
where further embalming and placement in the coffin were performed.
In the ninth month, on the day of Rénwǔ,
the posthumous title was bestowed as Tǐtiān Hóngdào Gāomíng Guǎngyùn Shèngwǔ Shéngōng Chúnrén Zhìxiào Wén Huángdì,
and the temple name was Tàizōng.
He was buried in Chánglíng.
In the ninth month of the seventeenth year of Jiājìng,
the posthumous title was changed to Qǐtiān Hóngdào Gāomíng Zhàoyùn Shèngwǔ Shéngōng Chúnrén Zhìxiào Wén Huángdì,
and the temple name was Chéngzǔ.
The encomium states: Emperor Wén trained in military affairs from a young age,
occupied the strategically important land of Yōuyàn,
and, taking advantage of Jiànwén's weakness,
marched directly inland,
thereby taking possession of all under heaven.
After his enthronement,
he personally practiced frugality;
when floods or droughts were reported in the morning, relief was provided by evening,
without any obstruction.
He was skilled at knowing and employing people,
and his insights were clear and penetrating.
His heroic military strategies
were comparable to those of Emperor Gāo.
His six armies sallied forth repeatedly,
clearing the dust in the deserts to the north.
By his later years,
his prestige and virtue extended far and wide,
and the four quarters submitted.
Nearly thirty nations received imperial decrees and paid tribute.
The vastness of his domain
far surpassed that of the Hàn and Táng dynasties.
His accomplishments and great deeds were truly splendid.
However, at the time of the usurpation,
he acted contrary to principle,
and this shameful flaw cannot be concealed.
Collation Notes
Annals VIII, Rénzōng
Emperor Rénzōng Jìngtiān Tǐdào Chúnchéng Zhìdé Hóngwén Qīnwǔ Zhāngshèng Dáxiào Zhāo,
whose personal name was Gāo Chì,
was Chéngzǔ's eldest son.
His mother, Empress Rénxiào Wén,
dreamed that someone wearing a crown and holding a ceremonial tablet came to pay respects;
she woke up and gave birth to the emperor.
As a child, he was dignified, steady, and calm,
and his words and actions followed proper norms.
When he was slightly older, he practiced archery,
hitting the target with every shot.
He loved learning,
and constantly discussed scholarship with Confucian officials.
In the twenty-eighth year of Hóngwǔ,
he was enfeoffed as the Heir Apparent of Yān.
He was once ordered to inspect the guards along with the heirs apparent of Qín, Jìn, and Zhōu;
he alone returned late.
When asked why,
he replied:
"It was very cold in the morning,
so I waited until after breakfast to inspect them,
which is why I was late."
He was also ordered to review memorials separately,
and he alone selected those concerning the welfare of the military and common people to report.
If there were errors in the text,
he would not report them.
Emperor Tàizǔ pointed this out to him, saying:
"Are you neglecting this, my son?"
He replied:
"I would not dare to neglect it,
but minor errors are not worth troubling the emperor's ears."
He was also once asked:
"During the floods and droughts in the time of Yáo and Tāng,
what did the common people rely on?"
He replied:
"They relied on the sagely ruler's policy of caring for the people."
Emperor Tàizǔ rejoiced, saying:
"My grandson has the sagacity of a ruler."
When Chéngzǔ raised his army,
the Heir Apparent defended Běipíng,
and skillfully soothed the soldiers and common people.
With ten thousand men, he resisted Lǐ Jǐnglóng's half-million strong army,
and the city was preserved thanks to him.
Before this,
the imperial princes Gāo Xù and Gāo Suì were both clever and favored by Chéngzǔ.
And Gāo Xù had rendered meritorious service in the army;
furthermore, eunuchs such as Huáng Yǎn and others sided with Gāo Suì,
secretly plotting to usurp the succession,
and slandered the Heir Apparent.
At that time, the court sent a letter to the Heir Apparent,
intended to create discord.
The Heir Apparent did not open the sealed letter,
but sent it swiftly to the emperor.
However, Huáng Yǎn had already secretly reported to Chéngzǔ, saying:
"The Heir Apparent is communicating with the court, and an envoy has arrived."
Soon after,
the envoy sent by the Heir Apparent also arrived.
Chéngzǔ opened and read the letter,
then sighed, saying:
"I almost killed my son."
When Chéngzǔ ascended the throne,
he renamed Běipíng as Běijīng,
and still ordered the Heir Apparent to guard it.
In the second month of the second year of Yǒnglè,
he was finally summoned to the capital
and established as the Crown Prince.
Chéngzǔ frequently went on northern expeditions,
ordering him to oversee the state,
and decide on all matters of government.
When there were floods, droughts, or famines in various regions,
he would immediately dispatch aid and relief,
and his reputation for benevolence became widely known.
However, Gāo Xù, Gāo Suì, and their faction constantly sought opportunities to slander and frame him.
Someone asked the Crown Prince:
"Do you know that there are slanderers?"
He replied:
"I do not know,
I only know to fulfill my duties as a son."
In the tenth year,
upon returning from a northern expedition,
because the Crown Prince's envoy was late,
and his memorial contained inappropriate language,
all his palace officials, such as Huáng Huái, were arrested and imprisoned.
In the fifteenth year,
Gāo Xù was exiled to Lè'ān due to his crimes.
The following year,
Huáng Yǎn and others again slandered the Crown Prince for presumptuously pardoning criminals,
and many palace officials were executed.
Assistant Minister Hú Yíng was ordered to investigate,
and secretly submitted a memorial detailing seven instances of the Crown Prince's sincerity, reverence, filial piety, and prudence.
Chéngzǔ's suspicions were then allayed.
Later, when Huáng Yǎn and others plotted to establish Gāo Suì,
the plot was discovered and they were executed.
Gāo Suì was spared due to the Crown Prince's efforts,
and from then on, the Crown Prince finally enjoyed peace.
In the seventh month of the twenty-second year,
Chéngzǔ passed away at Yúmù Chuān.
In the eighth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
the imperial edict arrived,
dispatching the Imperial Grandson to meet the funeral cortege at Kāipíng.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Xià Yuángé and others were released from prison.
On the day Dīngsì,
he ascended the imperial throne.
A general amnesty was granted to the empire,
and the following year was designated the first year of Hóngxī.
The voyages of the treasure ships to the Western Ocean, the horse markets in the west, and the procurement operations in Yúnnán and Jiāozhǐ were abolished.
On the day Wǔwǔ,
Xià Yuángé and Wú Zhōng were reinstated to their offices.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Wǔ'ān Hóu Zhèng Hēng was stationed at Dàtóng,
Bǎodìng Hóu Mèng Yīng at Jiāozhǐ,
Xiāngchéng Bó Lǐ Lóng at Shānhǎi,
and Wǔjìn Bó Zhū Róng at Liáodōng.
The offices of the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries were reinstituted,
to be concurrently held by dukes, marquises, earls, and ministers.
Yáng Róng was promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (Tàicháng Sì Qīng),
Jīn Yòuzī to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue (Hùbù Shìláng),
both retaining their concurrent posts as Grand Secretaries as before.
Yáng Shìqí was made Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites (Lǐbù Zuǒ Shìláng) and concurrently Grand Secretary of Huágài Diàn.
Huáng Huái was made Transmission Commissioner (Tōngzhèng Shǐ) and concurrently Grand Secretary of Wǔyīng Diàn.
All were put in charge of internal decrees.
Yáng Pǔ was made Hanlin Academician (Hànlín Xuéshì).
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Zhènyuǎn Hóu Gù Xīngzǔ was appointed Commander-in-Chief (Zǒngbīng Guān)
to suppress the rebellious barbarians in Guǎngxī.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
redundant officials were dismissed.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Hàn Wáng Gāo Xù was summoned to the capital.
On the day Wùchén,
officials and clerks who had been banished to military service were allowed to return to their hometowns.
On the day Jǐsì,
an imperial edict stipulated that civil officials aged seventy should retire.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Jiāozhǐ Metropolitan Commissioner Fāng Zhèng fought Lǐ Lì in Chálóng Zhōu,
suffering a defeat,
and Assistant Commissioner Wǔ Yún died fighting.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Minister Huáng Fú was recalled from Jiāozhǐ.
On the day Gēngchén,
the river overflowed at Kāifēng,
tax grain was remitted,
and Right Censor-in-Chief Wáng Zhāng was dispatched to offer relief.
On the day Réngwǔ,
an imperial order stated that from now on, materials used by government offices should be purchased at their place of origin at market price,
and those who burdened the people with levies would not be pardoned.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Minister of Rites Lǚ Zhèn requested permission to shed mourning attire,
but it was not granted.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the annual stipends of the various princes were increased.
On the day Bǐngxū,
censorate officials were designated for external postings,
and thirty-five Supervising Secretaries, including Xiāo Qí, were appointed as local officials.
On the day Dīnghài,
Lǐ Lì raided Qīnghuà,
and Assistant Metropolitan Commissioner Chén Zhōng died fighting.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Nanjing Garrison Commander (Nánjīng Shǒubèi) was first established,
with Xiāngchéng Bó Lǐ Lóng appointed to the post.
On the day Yǐwèi,
government horses kept by the people in the imperial domains were distributed among the various guards.
On the day Wùxū,
Minister of Personnel Jiǎn Yì, along with Yáng Shìqí, Yáng Róng, and Jīn Yòuzī, were each granted a silver seal,
inscribed
“To correct errors and rectify mistakes.”
They were instructed to work together to assist in affairs,
and if there were any shortcomings that ought to be reported,
they were to use the seal to seal their reports and submit them.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Rényín,
the private purchase of gold and silver by the public was abolished,
and the two capitals' Ministry of Revenue treasuries for circulation were dismantled.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
an imperial edict ordered all Regional Military Commissions and Guards throughout the empire to repair their city walls.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Transmission Commissioner requested that memorialized reports on rainfall from the four quarters be sent to the Supervising Secretaries for storage.
The emperor said:
“The imperial ancestors ordered memorials on rainfall from the empire
to know about droughts and floods,
so as to implement policies of compassion for the people.
If they accumulate at the Transmission Office,
they are already missed;
now you wish them to be stored.
This means those above will never know.
From now on, memorials, when received, shall be immediately reported.”
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Consort Zhāng was enfeoffed as empress.
On the day Réngzǐ,
his eldest son, Zhān Jī, was established as Crown Prince.
His sons were enfeoffed: Zhān Jùn as Zhèng Wáng,
Zhān Yōng as Yuè Wáng,
Zhān Shàn as Xiāng Wáng,
Zhān Gāng as Jīng Wáng,
Zhān Ào as Huái Wáng,
Zhān Kǎi as Téng Wáng,
Zhān as Liáng Wáng,
Zhān Yán as Wèi Wáng.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
an imperial edict ordered officials inside and outside the court to recommend talented individuals,
and strictly enforced the law of joint responsibility for recommenders.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Three Judicial Offices, together with the Grand Secretaries, ministries, bureaus, Transmission Office, and Six Offices of Scrutiny, were ordered to review prisoners at Chéngtiānmén,
which was enacted as a permanent regulation.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the monthly stipends for capital officials and soldiers were increased.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
twenty imperial students, including Xú Yǒngjìn, were promoted to Supervising Secretaries.
On the first day of the eleventh month, Réngshēn,
an imperial edict to the Ministry of Rites stated:
“The family members of Jiànwén's officials who are enslaved in the Music Bureau, Embroidered Uniform Guard, Washing Bureau, or are artisan trainees or slaves in meritorious officials' households,
shall all be pardoned and made commoners,
and their land returned.
Those banished for speaking out shall also be treated likewise.”
On the day Guǐyǒu,
an imperial edict to the relevant offices stated:
“Report any inconvenient government regulations.
Anyone who suffers disaster and does not immediately request relief
shall be punished.”
Ālǔtái came to offer horses as tribute.
On the day Jiǎxū,
an imperial edict ordered all ministers to report shortcomings in current governance.
On the day Yǐhài,
the罪 (crimes) of Wūliánghā were pardoned.
It was then ordered that military officers and soldiers from the guards near the capital should take turns coming to the capital for training.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Censors were dispatched to inspect the border garrisons.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Censors were dispatched to tour the empire,
to investigate officials.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Minister of Revenue Xià Yuángé was granted
a silver seal inscribed “To correct errors and rectify mistakes.”
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Ministry of Rites requested to receive congratulations on the Winter Solstice festival,
but it was not granted.
On the day Gēngyín,
an imperial order instructed all generals to strictly guard the borders.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the unauthorized requisition of military agriculturists by relevant offices was prohibited.
On the day Rénchén,
Grand Coordinator Fāng Zhèng, along with Róngchāng Bó Chén Zhì, were stationed in Jiāozhǐ.
In this month,
Jiǎn Yì, Yáng Shìqí, Xià Yuángé, Yáng Róng, and Jīn Yòuzī were instructed:
“Rulers of previous generations,
some, out of self-importance,
detested hearing forthright criticism,
and their subjects flattered and complied,
leading to their downfall.
We and you, ministers, should take this as a warning.”
He further instructed Shìqí:
“Recently, my ministers have shown much loyalty and affection;
when I had faults and was regretting them,
those who offered advice had already arrived,
which greatly pleased my heart.”
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
the collateral relatives of Jiànwén's officials who had been exiled to the borders with their entire families were pardoned,
one person was allowed to remain,
and the rest were all released and returned home.
On the day Xīnhài,
the names of the officials of the Three Judicial Offices throughout the empire were displayed on the west corridor of Féngtiānmén.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
tax grain for disaster-stricken areas was remitted.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Emperor Wén was buried at Chánglíng.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Zhènyuǎn Hóu Gù Xīngzǔ defeated the barbarians of Pínglè and Xúnzhōu.
In this year,
Yútián, Liúqiú, Zhànchéng, Hāmì, Gǔmálàláng, Mǎlǐjiā, Sūlù, and Wǎlá all sent tribute.
In the spring, the first month, on the *rénshēn* day, the first of the month, of the first year of Hóngxī,
the Emperor held court at Fèntiānmén,
without music.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an imperial edict commanded all officials, internal and external, to attend to their duties.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
The Hóngwéngé was established,
and erudite officials were ordered to serve there,
with Yáng Pǔ in charge of its affairs.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
as snow had not yet fallen for the season,
an imperial edict commanded officials to reflect on themselves.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the southern suburb,
with Tàizǔ and Tàizōng as co-sacrificers.
On the *rénchén* day,
court officials who had been granted leave to return to their hometowns were given varying amounts of paper money,
which was established as a regulation.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhōu Gàn, the Surveillance Commissioner Hú Gài, and the Vice Administrator Yè Chūn were sent to inspect the Southern Capital region and Zhèjiāng.
In the second month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
general's seals were distributed to border commanders.
On the *wùshēn* day,
sacrifice was offered to the altars of Soil and Grain.
Eunuch Zhèng Hé was ordered to guard Nánjīng.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the ceremonial field was plowed.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the spirit tablet of Tàizōng was enshrined in the Tàimiào.
This month,
Nánjīng experienced repeated earthquakes.
In the third month, on the *rénshēn* day,
the former Assistant of the Guānglù Department, Quán Jǐn, was promoted to Grand Secretary of Wénhuádiàn for his filial conduct.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Emperor sought honest advice.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Lóngpíng suffered a famine.
The Ministry of Revenue requested to lend government wheat.
The Emperor said:
"Just relieve them,
why lend?"
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Punishments are for prohibiting violence and stopping evil,
guiding the people to goodness,
not for aiming at executions.
Officials sometimes meticulously apply the law and fabricate evidence,
leading to wrongful convictions and excessive punishments.
I deeply lament this.
From now on, all crimes shall be judged strictly according to the law.
If I, due to excessive hatred of evil,
apply punishments outside the law,
the judicial authorities shall remonstrate.
If my assent is not granted after five remonstrances,
they shall remonstrate jointly with the Three Ducal Ministers and Grand Ministers,
and my assent must be granted before they stop.
No departments shall whip prisoners on the back or castrate anyone.
Those who castrate themselves shall be judged as unfilial.
Unless it is rebellion,
relatives shall not be implicated.
In ancient prosperous eras,
the words of the people were listened to,
to serve as a warning and admonition.
Now, treacherous individuals often pick up trivialities,
falsely accusing others of slander,
and harsh legal officials
fabricate cases into convictions.
If punishments are not appropriate,
the people will be at a loss.
Therefore, the prohibition against slander is abolished;
those who report it shall not be prosecuted at all."
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Marquis of Yángwǔ, Xuē Lù, was made Grand General of Zhènshuò,
leading troops to patrol the borders of Kāipíng and Dàtóng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Assistant Commander Lǐ Ān, Earl of Ānpíng, and Chén Zhì, Earl of Róngchāng, were jointly stationed in Jiāozhǐ.
On the *wùxū* day,
intending to return to the capital Nánjīng,
an imperial edict commanded all departments in Běijīng to be referred to as "Traveling Residence,"
and the Traveling Provincial Administration Commission and Traveling Chief Military Commission of Běijīng were restored.
This month,
Nánjīng experienced repeated earthquakes.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *rényín* day,
the Emperor heard that the people of Shāndōng, Huái, and Xú were short of food,
and that officials were pressing for summer taxes.
He then went to the Xījiǎomén and ordered Grand Secretary Yáng Shìqí to draft an edict,
remitting this year's summer tax and half of the autumn grain tax.
Shìqí said:
"Your Majesty's grace is paramount,
but it requires the prior knowledge of the Ministries of Revenue and Works."
The Emperor said:
"Saving the people from destitution should be like fighting a fire or rescuing from drowning;
there must be no delay.
Officials, concerned about insufficient national expenditure,
will inevitably hesitate and be indecisive."
He immediately ordered an internal official to prepare paper and brush,
and instructed Shìqí to write the edict on the gate tower.
After the Emperor read it,
he immediately affixed his seal and sent it out for implementation.
He looked at Shìqí and said:
"Now you can tell the ministerial officials."
The Traveling Censorate of Běijīng was established.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Crown Prince was ordered to visit Xiàolíng,
and then to remain and guard Nánjīng.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Emperor went to Tiānshòushān
to visit Chánglíng.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
he returned to the palace.
This month,
relief was provided for the famine in Hénán and Dàmíng.
Nánjīng experienced repeated earthquakes.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Imperial Lecturer Lǐ Shímǐan and the Imperial Expositor Luó Rǔjìng were transferred to Censor for speaking out,
and subsequently imprisoned.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor became unwell,
and envoys were dispatched to summon the Crown Prince from Nánjīng.
On the *xīnsì* day,
he was critically ill,
and a dying edict transferred the throne to the Crown Prince.
On this day,
he died at the Qīn'āndiàn,
at the age of forty-eight.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *jǐsì* day,
an honored posthumous title was conferred,
with the temple name Rénzōng,
and he was buried at Xiànlíng.
An encomium says: When the "Jìngnán" campaign began,
Rénzōng, as the heir apparent, remained and guarded [the capital],
preserving the city and aiding the army.
Thereafter, when Chéngzǔ ascended the throne,
he campaigned north annually,
and the Eastern Palace supervised the state,
with no affairs neglected in court.
However, he frequently encountered intrigues and malicious slanders,
and was often on the verge of peril and suspicion,
yet ultimately survived through sincerity and reverence.
Well did he declare to others,
"I only know how to fulfill the duties of a son,
I know nothing of slanderers,"
which can serve as a model for sons and ministers for all generations.
During his one year on the throne,
his appointments and administration
were too numerous to fully record.
If Heaven had granted him more years,
allowing for nurturing and recuperation,
the flourishing of his virtuous transformations
would surely have rivaled that of Wén and Jǐng!
Collation Notes
Basic Annals 9: Xuānzōng
Xuānzōng Xiàntiān Chóngdào Yīngmíng Shénshèng Qīnwén Zhāowǔ Kuānrén Chúnxiào Zhāng Huángdì,
whose personal name was Zhānjī,
was the eldest son of Rénzōng.
His mother was Empress Chéngxiào Zhāo.
The night before his birth,
Chéngzǔ dreamt that Tàizǔ gave him a large *guī* (jade tablet) and said:
"Pass this to your descendants,
and they shall prosper for eternity."
When he was a full month old,
Chéngzǔ saw him and said:
"This child overflows with heroic spirit,
it matches my dream."
As he grew older,
he was fond of books,
and his wisdom and insight were outstanding.
In the seventh year of Yǒnglè,
he accompanied the Emperor on a visit to Běijīng,
and was made to observe farming tools and the clothing and food of farming families,
and taught the principles of prioritizing fundamental tasks.
In the eighth year,
when Chéngzǔ campaigned in the desert,
he was ordered to remain and guard Běijīng.
In the eleventh month of the ninth year,
he was established as the Imperial Grandson,
and began to wear the cap of adulthood.
From then on,
he accompanied the Emperor on all tours and punitive expeditions.
The Emperor once ordered academicians Hú Guǎng and others to lecture the Imperial Grandson on classics and history even in the army.
He often said to Rénzōng:
"This will be the Emperor of Great Peace one day."
When Rénzōng ascended the throne,
he was established as the Imperial Crown Prince.
In the summer, fourth month,
as Nánjīng experienced frequent earthquakes,
an order was issued to go and reside there to guard it.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngchén,
Rénzōng became unwell,
and an imperial edict summoned (him) back.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
he returned to Liángxiāng,
received the will,
and entered the palace to announce the mourning.
On the day Gēngxū,
he ascended the imperial throne.
A general amnesty was granted to the empire,
and the following year was designated Xuāndé元年.
On the day Xīnhài,
an edict was issued to border generals to strictly prepare defenses.
On the day Jiǎyín,
eunuchs sent out for procurement were urged to return,
and the purchased goods were abolished.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Yǐhài,
the Empress was honored as Empress Dowager,
and Consort Hú Shì was made Empress.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Zhènyuǎn Hóu Gù Xīngzǔ attacked the Mán people of Dàténgxiá,
and pacified them.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Judicial Offices were ordered to be prudent in criminal cases.
In the intercalary month, on the day Wùshēn,
Ānshùn Bó Xuē Guì, Qīngpíng Bó Wú Chéng,
Dūdū Mǎ Yīng, and Dū Zhǐhuī Liáng Chéng led troops to patrol the border.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Yáng Pǔ entered the Wényuān Gé to serve.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùchén,
Dū Zhǐhuī Lǐ Yīng attacked the rebellious Fān of Āndìng Qūxiān,
and greatly defeated them.
Āndìng Wáng Sāng'ér Jiāshījiā then came to the court to apologize for his crimes.
On the day Rénshēn,
an imperial decree ordered all officials, both inside and outside the court, to recommend those who were incorruptible, just, and capable of governing the people.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Dàlǐ Qīng Hú Gài and Cānzhèng Yè Chūn toured and pacified Nánjī and Zhèjiāng.
The establishment of touring and pacifying officials began from this point.
In the ninth month, on the day Rényín,
Zhāo Huángdì was buried at Xiànlíng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Wùyín,
Nánjīng experienced an earthquake.
On the day Wùzǐ,
an imperial edict ordered all Gōng, Hóu, Bó, the Five Military Commissions, the Six Ministries, Grand Secretaries, and Supervising Secretaries to review and re-examine serious prisoners.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùxū,
Gù Xīngzǔ attacked and pacified the Mán people of Sī'ēn.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Xuē Lù was made Zhènshuò Dà Jiāngjūn to patrol the border.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Gù Xīngzǔ attacked and pacified the Mán people of Yíshān.
In this year,
the Huíhuí of Hāmì, Mǎlāsādīng, Zhànchéng, Zhōngshān of Liúqiú, Jiǎwā, Wūsīzàng, Wǎlà, and Bóní paid tribute.
In Xuāndé元年, spring, first month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
sacrifices were offered at the Tàimiào.
On the day Dīngwèi,
great sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburbs.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
an amnesty was granted to those with death sentences or lesser crimes, allowing them to redeem themselves by transporting grain to Xuānfǔ.
On the day Jǐwèi,
attendant minister Huáng Zōngzài and fifteen others were sent to rectify the military forces throughout the empire.
Later, envoys were repeatedly dispatched,
establishing this as a regulation.
In the second month, on the day Wùchén,
sacrifices were offered to the deities of soil and grain.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the ceremonial field was plowed.
On the day Bǐngxū,
homage was paid at Chánglíng and Xiànlíng.
On the day Dīnghài,
he returned to the palace.
In the third month, on the day Jǐhài,
Róngchāng Bó Chén Zhì and Dūdū Fāng Zhèng attacked Lí Lì,
suffering a defeat at Chálóngzhōu,
and the Zhīfǔ of Yì'ān, Qín Péng, died.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Xíngzài Lǐbù Shìláng Zhāng Yīng was concurrently appointed Huágài Diàn Dàxuéshì,
and served in the Wényuān Gé.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Chéngshān Hóu Wáng Tōng was appointed Zhēngyí Jiāngjūn and commander-in-chief,
to attack Lí Lì.
Shàngshū Chén Qià was appointed to advise on military affairs,
and Chén Zhì and Fāng Zhèng were stripped of their offices and ordered to redeem themselves through meritorious service.
In the fifth month, on the first day Jiǎwǔ,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
an imperial edict pardoned Jiāozhǐ,
allowing Lí Lì to reform himself.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
an imperial edict ordered prefectures and counties to bury unburied remains.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Xuē Lù was recalled.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Guǐsì,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the summer tax in Shāndōng was remitted.
On the day Jǐhài,
an edict was issued to the Six Offices of Scrutiny,
stating that any imperial decree conveyed by eunuchs
must be reported back before execution.
On the day Rénzǐ,
timber felling in Húguǎng was suspended.
In the eighth month, on the day Réngxū,
Hàn Wáng Gāo Xù rebelled.
On the day Bǐngyín,
military officials with crimes deserving capital punishment or lesser penalties were pardoned,
and their offices restored.
On the day Jǐsì,
the emperor personally led an expedition against Gāo Xù,
ordering Zhèng Wáng Zhānjùn and Xiāng Wáng Zhānshàng to remain and guard.
Yángwǔ Hóu Xuē Lù and Qīngpíng Bó Wú Chéng led the vanguard,
and great rewards were bestowed upon the officers and soldiers of the Five Armies.
On the day Xīnwèi,
they departed from the capital.
On the day Xīnsì,
they arrived at Lè'ān.
The Emperor twice sent letters urging surrender,
and also shot an imperial edict tied to an arrow into the city, explaining the consequences of prosperity and misfortune.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Gāo Xù surrendered.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Lè'ān was renamed Wǔdìngzhōu.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the army returned.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
he returned from Wǔdìngzhōu,
and Gāo Xù was imprisoned in the Western Palace.
On the day Wùxū,
the Judicial Offices interrogated Gāo Xù's co-conspirators.
Their confessions implicated Jìn Wáng and Zhào Wáng,
but an imperial decree ordered no further investigation.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Wùyín,
Lǐ Shímiǎn was released,
and reinstated as Shìdú.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Chéngshān Hóu Wáng Tōng attacked Lí Lì at Yìngpíng,
suffering a defeat,
and Shàngshū Chén Qià died.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the autumn grain tax in areas traversed by the Six Armies was remitted.
On the day Xīnwèi,
prisoners were reviewed,
and over three thousand people were pardoned.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Zhēngnán Jiāngjūn, commander-in-chief Qiánguó Gōng Mù Shèng, leading Xīng'ān Bó Xú Hēng and Xīnníng Bó Tán Zhōng,
and Zhēnglǔ Fù Jiāngjūn, Ānyuǎn Hóu Liǔ Shēng, leading Bǎodìng Bó Liáng Míng and Dūdū Cuī Jù,
marched from Yúnnán and Guǎngxī respectively to attack Lí Lì.
Bīngbù Shàngshū Lǐ Qìng advised on military affairs.
In this year,
Jiǎwā, Xiāmluó, Liúqiú, Sūméndálà, Mǎlájiā, Báigédá, Sāmǎ'érhǎn, Tǔlǔfān, Hāmì, and Wūsīzàng paid tribute.
In the second year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
great sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburbs.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the officials reported the annual number of prisoners.
The Emperor remarked that the common people lightly violated laws
due to the lack of effective moral education,
and ordered the strengthening of moral education.
In the second month, on the day Guǐhài,
Xíngzài Hùbù Shìláng Chén Shān was appointed Shàngshū of his department, concurrently Jǐnshēn Diàn Dàxuéshì,
and served in the Wényuān Gé.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Lí Lì attacked Jiāozhǐchéng,
and Wáng Tōng defeated him.
In the third month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Mǎ Yú and others were granted the Jinshi degree and various ranks.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
Lí Lì captured Chāngjiāng.
Dū Zhǐhuī Lǐ Rèn,
Zhǐhuī Gù Fú, Liú Shùn,
Zhīfǔ Liú Zǐfǔ,
and the eunuch Féng Zhì died.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Jìn Wáng Jìhuáng was found guilty,
and demoted to commoner.
On the day Jǐsì,
Wáng Tōng agreed to make peace with Lí Lì.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐsì,
Xuē Lù supervised the transport of provisions to Kāipíng.
On the day Jǐhài,
Rénzōng's spirit tablet was enshrined in the Tàimiào.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
prisoners were reviewed.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùyín,
prisoners were reviewed.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jǐhài,
Lí Lì captured Àiliú Pass.
The Marquis Zhènyuǎn, Gù Xīngzǔ, held back his troops and did not rescue them.
He was arrested and tried.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Dū Dū Tóngzhī Chén Huái was appointed as the commander-in-chief,
to lead an army to suppress the Mán of Sōngpān.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Xuē Lù defeated the enemy at Kāipíng.
In the eighth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Huáng Huái retired.
Taxes and grain duties were remitted for disaster-stricken prefectures and counties in the two capitals, Shānxī, and Hénán.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénchén,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Liǔ Shēng's army reached Dàomǎpō,
where they encountered an ambush and he died in battle.
On that same day,
the Earl Bǎodìng, Liáng Míng, died of illness.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Shàngshū Lǐ Qìng died of illness.
The army was routed;
Cānjìang Cuī Jù,
Lángzhōng Shǐ Ān,
Zhǔshì Chén Yōng and Lǐ Zōngfǎng died there.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Wùyín,
Wáng Tōng abandoned Jiāozhǐ
and made an alliance with Lí Lì.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Lí Lì was pardoned,
and Attendants Lǐ Qí and Luó Rǔjìng were sent to enthrone Chén Gǎo as the King of Ānnán.
All civil and military officials and soldiers were summoned back.
On the day Jǐhài,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire due to the birth of the imperial eldest son,
and one-third of next year's taxes and grain duties were remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
relief was provided for the famine in Shǎnxī,
and 150,000 bolts of silk and cloth were distributed.
In this year,
Zhǎowā, Zhànchéng, Xiāmluó, Liúqiú, Wǎlà, Hāmì, Yìlìbǎlǐ, and Sāmǎ'érhǎn paid tribute.
In the third year, spring, the first month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Chén Huái pacified the Mán of Sōngpān.
In the second month, on the day Wùwǔ,
the imperial eldest son, Qízhèn, was made Crown Prince.
In this month,
the book Dì Xùn was completed.
In the third month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Empress Hú Shì was deposed,
and Noble Consort Sūn Shì was made Empress.
On the day Rénchén,
prisoners were reviewed.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guǐhài,
an imperial edict stated that all memorials from officials and commoners
should be discussed by the Shàngshū, Dū Yùshǐ, and Jǐshìzhōng and then reported,
without concealment.
In the intercalary month, on the day Rénryín,
prisoners were reviewed.
Taxes and grain duties for drought-stricken Shānxī were remitted.
On the day Jiǎchén,
officials were ordered to provide relief.
On the day Gēngxū,
the crime of abandoning Jiāozhǐ was judged;
Wáng Tōng and others, along with Bùzhèngshǐ Yì Qiān, eunuchs Shān Shòu and Mǎ Qí, were imprisoned and sentenced to death,
and their properties confiscated.
The Marquis Zhènyuǎn, Gù Xīngzǔ, was also imprisoned.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Lǐ Qí and Luó Rǔjìng returned.
Lí Lì reported that Chén Gǎo had died,
and his descendants were extinct,
requesting to govern the country pending imperial command.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day Jǐsì,
Luó Rǔjìng and others were again sent to instruct Lí Lì to establish a descendant of the Chén clan.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the officials who died in service in Jiāozhǐ were posthumously honored.
On the day Rénshēn,
summer taxes for disaster-stricken Běijīng were remitted.
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
summer taxes for disaster-stricken Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Dū Yùshǐ Liú Guān inspected the riverways.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Wùchén,
prisoners were reviewed.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the Běijīng Xíngbù and Xíng Hòujūn Dūdū Fǔ were abolished.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor personally led a tour of the border.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnhài,
he reached Shímén Post Station.
The Wùliánghā raided Huìzhōu,
and the Emperor led 3,000 elite soldiers to attack them.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
he exited Xǐfēngkǒu,
and attacked the raiders at Kuānhé.
The Emperor personally shot at their vanguard,
killing three men.
The two wing armies advanced simultaneously,
and severely defeated them.
The raiders, seeing the yellow dragon banner,
dismounted and bowed in submission, requesting to surrender.
All were captured alive,
and their chieftain was beheaded.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the army returned.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
he arrived back from Xǐfēngkǒu.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Jǐnyī Zhǐhuī Zhōng Fǎbǎo requested to collect pearls in Dōngguǎn.
The Emperor said:
“This is to disturb the people for profit,”
and sent him to prison.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Guǎngxī Zǒngbīngguān Shān Yún attacked and captured the Mán of Xīnchéng.
In this year,
Zhànchéng, Xiāmluó, Zhǎowā, Liúqiú, Wǎlà, Hāmì, Ānnán, Qǔxiān, Tǔlǔfān, Yìlìbǎlǐ, and Sāmǎ'érhǎn paid tribute.
In the fourth year, spring, the first month,
there were earthquakes in the two capitals.
On the day Jǐwèi,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Nánjīng presented two Zōuyú.
The Ministry of Rites requested to offer congratulations,
but this was not permitted.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Lǐ Qí was again sent to instruct Lí Lì to find and establish a descendant of the Chén clan.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Xīnsì,
Shān Yún attacked and pacified the Mán of Liǔ and Xún.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Gōngbù Shàngshū Huáng Fú and the Earl Píngjiāng, Chén Xuān, managed the grain transport system.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
prisoners were reviewed.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the practice of civil officials committing embezzlement being allowed to atone by payment was abolished.
On the day Jǐhài,
raiders attacked Kāipíng,
and Zhènfǔ Zhāng Xìn and others died in battle.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Xuē Lù supervised the provisioning of Kāipíng.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor visited the Wényuāngé.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Yáng Pǔ was reinstated.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Gù Xīngzǔ was released from prison.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor visited the Wényuāngé.
On the day Guǐwèi,
due to the cold weather, the judicial authorities were ordered to review prisoners.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the "Yīlán Cāo" was composed and bestowed upon court officials,
instructing them on the way of recommending worthy individuals for the state.
On the day Gēngyín,
Zhāng Yīng and Chén Shān were dismissed.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
a military review was held in the nearby suburbs.
On the day Yǐwèi,
a hunt was held at Yùkǒu.
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Xuē Lù and the Marquis Gōngshùn, Wú Kèzhōng, led an army to patrol Xuānfǔ.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐhài,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day Rénchén,
the eunuchs' shipbuilding activities on the Sōnghuā Jiāng were stopped.
In this year,
Zhǎowā, Zhànchéng, Liúqiú, Bǎnggélà, Hāmì, Tǔlǔfān, Yìlìbǎlǐ, and Sāmǎ'érhǎn paid tribute.
In the fifth year, in spring, the first month, on the day *Guǐchǒu* (January 24, 1430),
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the day *Wùchén* (February 7),
Shàngshū Xià Yuánjí passed away.
In the second month, on the day *Rénchén* (February 21),
the logging work by the Ministry of Works was halted.
On the day *Guǐsì* (February 22),
an edict of leniency and relief was issued: reducing taxes on disaster-stricken areas,
easing the horse administration,
waiving outstanding arrears of salaries and fodder,
inviting displaced people to return and granting them a one-year exemption from taxes,
halting government requisitions,
reducing the old levies on official lands by three-tenths,
providing relief to artisans,
prohibiting warehouse officials from engaging in corrupt practices,
and instructing judicial authorities to exercise caution in criminal cases.
On the day *Yǐwèi* (March 6),
the Empress Dowager was escorted to visit the imperial mausoleum.
In the third month, on the day *Wùshēn* (March 27),
on the road, seeing farmers plowing,
he dismounted to inquire about agricultural matters,
took a plow and pushed it three times.
He looked at his attending officials and said:
"I, having pushed the plow three times, am already overcome with fatigue,
how much more so for our people who toil diligently all year round!"
He ordered cash to be bestowed upon the farmers along the route.
On the day *Jǐyǒu* (March 28),
he returned to the palace.
On the day *Xīnhài* (March 30),
Lǐ Qí returned.
Lê Lợi claimed that the Chén (陳) clan had no heir,
and submitted a memorial requesting enfeoffment.
On the day *Bǐngchén* (April 4),
the land rent for disaster-stricken fields in Shānxī from the previous year was waived.
On the day *Dīngsì* (April 5),
Lín Zhèn and others were granted the *Jìnshì Jídì* and *Chūshēn* degrees with varying ranks.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day *Wùyín* (April 16),
Xuē Lù commanded troops to build the fortresses of Chìchéng, Diāo'è, Yúnzhōu, Dúshí, and Tuánshān.
In the fifth month, on the day *Guǐmǎo* (May 1),
the official seals and edicts of corrupt officials were retroactively revoked,
and this was established as a regulation.
On the day *Bǐngchén* (May 14),
emergency granaries were repaired,
and government funds were released to purchase grain in preparation for famine.
On the day *Guǐhài* (May 31),
Lángzhōng Kuàng Zhōng, Yùshǐ Hé Wényuān, and nine others were promoted to Zhīfǔ,
and given imperial decrees to depart.
In the sixth month, on the day *Jǐmǎo* (June 16),
officials were dispatched to catch locusts in the imperial vicinity,
and the Ministry of Revenue was instructed:
"In previous years, the envoys dispatched to catch locusts harmed the people no less than the locusts themselves.
You should be aware of this abuse."
Thereupon, a poem about catching locusts was composed and shown to them.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day *Guǐhài* (July 20),
the performance of local officials was evaluated.
In the eighth month, on the day *Jǐsì* (August 15), the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Due to overcast and rainy weather, it was not visible.
The ceremonial officials requested to present congratulations,
but this was not permitted.
In the ninth month, on the day *Bǐngwǔ* (September 22),
Yùshǐ Yú Qiān, Zhǎngshǐ Zhōu Chén, and six others were promoted to Shìláng,
to serve as Grand Coordinators (*Xúnfǔ*) in the two capitals, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Hénán, Jiāngxī, Zhèjiāng, and Húguǎng.
On the day *Yǐmǎo* (October 11),
he inspected the nearby suburbs.
On the day *Jǐwèi* (October 15),
he returned to the palace.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day *Yǐhài* (October 31),
Ālǔtái raided Liáodōng.
Huángfǔ Bīn, Zhīhuī Tóngzhī of Liáohǎi Wèi, died bravely in battle.
On the day *Bǐngzǐ* (November 1),
he inspected the nearby suburbs.
On the day *Jǐmǎo* (November 4),
he hunted at Bèndào.
On the day *Bǐngxū* (November 17),
he arrived at Xǐmǎlín,
and thoroughly inspected the fortresses and military preparations.
On the day *Rénchén* (November 27),
he returned to the palace.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Guǐsì* (January 7, 1431),
the rebellion of the Qūxiān (曲先) barbarians was pacified.
In the intercalary month, on the day *Jǐwèi* (January 23),
an imperial edict was issued to various internal and external offices,
ordering punishment for those who had prolonged imprisonment of inmates.
In this year,
Zhànchéng, Liúqiú, Zhǎowā, Wǎlà, Hāmì, Hǎndōng, Tǔlúfān, Sāmǎ'érhǎn, and Yìlìbǎlǐ sent tribute.
In the sixth year, in spring, the first month, on the day *Dīngchǒu* (February 2, 1431),
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the day *Gēngchén* (February 5),
there was heavy rain with thunder and lightning.
In the second month, on the day *Dīngyǒu* (February 22),
Shìláng Luó Rǔjìng supervised military agricultural colonies (*túntián*) in Shǎnxī.
On the day *Jǐhài* (February 24),
Jīnlóngkǒu was dredged,
and the river was diverted to reach Xúzhōu to facilitate grain transport.
In the third month, on the day *Yǐhài* (March 22),
the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to evaluate external officials, starting with those in the Bùzhèng and Ànchá departments,
and this was established as a regulation.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day *Jǐyǒu* (April 15),
Shìláng Chái Chē managed military agricultural colonies in Shānxī.
In the sixth month, on the day *Jǐhài* (June 4),
an envoy was dispatched to issue an imperial edict to Lê Lợi, authorizing him to provisionally administer the affairs of Ānnán (安南) country.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day *Jǐsì* (July 14),
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day *Rénwǔ* (July 23),
trade was permitted for the three guards of Yìyán (宜顏).
In winter, the tenth month, on the day *Jiǎchén* (November 7),
Chén Huái pacified the Mán (蠻) people of Sōngpān.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Bǐngzǐ* (November 29),
officers and soldiers were for the first time ordered to transport civilian grain.
On the day *Yǐyǒu* (December 18),
various Yùshǐ were dispatched to arrest corrupt and tyrannical eunuchs such as Yuán Qí.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Yǐwèi* (January 7, 1432),
Yuán Qí and eleven others were executed in the marketplace,
and their crimes were posted to be shown to the world.
On the day *Dīngwèi* (January 19),
Jīn Yòuzī passed away.
On the day *Gēngxū* (January 22),
Yùshǐ were dispatched to inspect the military agricultural colonies and water conservancy in Níngxià and Gānzhōu.
In this year,
Zhànchéng, Liúqiú, Wǎlà, Hāmì, Sūméndálá, and Yìlìbǎlǐ sent tribute.
In the seventh year, in spring, the first month, on the day *Xīnyǒu* (January 24, 1432), the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse,
and the morning court congratulations were waived.
On the day *Guǐyǒu* (February 5),
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the day *Jiǎwǔ* (March 8),
the judicial authorities were instructed to review prisoners due to the harmony of spring.
In the third month, on the day *Gēngshēn* (April 13),
an edict was issued to implement policies of leniency and relief.
On the day *Xīnyǒu* (April 14),
the Ministry of Rites was instructed:
"I have reduced the heavy taxes on official land by three-tenths.
However, I hear that in the past, when edicts to remit taxes were issued,
the Ministry of Revenue often did not implement them,
and even, in severe cases, admonished local officials
not to use imperial edicts as an excuse.
This obstructs and nullifies imperial edicts,
preventing benefits from reaching the lower levels.
From now on, mandates must be carried out,
without any obstruction."
In summer, the fourth month, on the day *Xīnchǒu* (May 4),
arrears of taxes in Shānxī were waived.
On the day *Rényín* (May 5),
merchants were recruited to exchange salt for grain to be transported to the borders.
In the sixth month, on the day *Guǐmǎo* (July 16),
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day *Guǐchǒu* (July 26),
the practice of eunuchs going to minority regions (*fān*) to purchase horses was halted.
In this month,
the "Official's Admonition" (*Guānzhēn*) was completed,
comprising thirty-five chapters,
and shown to all officials.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the day *Yǐwèi* (September 6),
an imperial edict instructed capital officials of the third rank and above to recommend talented scholars with integrity and literary skills,
and the Ministry of Personnel and the Censorate to dismiss incompetent officials in the various regions and departments.
In the ninth month, on the day *Gēngwǔ* (October 21),
various generals inspected the borders.
In this autumn,
tax grain for flood-stricken areas in the two capitals and Jiāxīng, Húzhōu was waived.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the day *Xīnyǒu* (December 12),
Chén Xuān, Earl of Píngjiāng and Director-General of Water Transport, and Shìláng Zhào Xīn and others were summoned to the capital at year-end to discuss the pros and cons of grain taxes.
In this year,
Zhànchéng, Liúqiú, Hāmì, Hāliè, Wǎlà, and Yìlìbǎlǐ sent tribute.
In the eighth year, in spring, the first month, on the day *Dīngmǎo* (February 8, 1433),
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the day *Rénzǐ* (March 25),
prisoners were reviewed,
and over five thousand people were pardoned and exempted.
In the third month, on the day *Bǐngchén* (April 8),
Cáo Nài and others were granted the *Jìnshì Jídì* and *Chūshēn* degrees with varying ranks.
On the day *Gēngchén* (April 22),
internal and external officials were instructed to treat soldiers with kindness and relief,
and those who violated this would be investigated and punished by censors.
In this spring,
due to the long drought in the two capitals, Hénán, Shāndōng, and Shānxī,
envoys were dispatched to provide relief.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day *Wùxū* (May 20),
an imperial edict waived overdue taxes and miscellaneous levies in disaster-stricken capital regions and provinces,
exempted this year's summer taxes,
and granted a one-year tax exemption.
Unjust cases were redressed,
punishments for those below capital offense were reduced,
and the crimes of runaway soldiers and artisans were pardoned.
Local officials were each to recommend one person of virtue and uprightness.
Circuit Censors and Surveillance Commissioners were to impeach corrupt and cruel officials, as well as envoys who caused trouble.
In the fifth month, on the day *Dīngsì* (June 8),
the Grand Commander and Military Commissioner Xiāo Shòu pacified the Wūluómán (烏羅蠻) people of Guìzhōu.
On the day *Dīngmǎo* (June 28),
Shān Yún pacified the Yíshānmán (宜山蠻) people.
In the sixth month, on the day *Yǐyǒu* (July 26),
prayers for rain were unanswered,
so a "Poem Lamenting the Drought" (*Mǐnhàn Shī*) was composed and shown to all officials.
On the day *Xīnchǒu* (August 1),
an imperial edict was issued to internal and external regions to quickly resolve criminal cases.
In this summer,
relief was again provided to the famine-stricken people in the two capitals, Hénán, Shāndōng, Shānxī, and Húguǎng,
and tax grain was waived.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Rénshēn (壬申),
taxes on grain for flood relief in Jiāngxī (江西) were remitted.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐsì (癸巳),
superfluous officials in the capital (Jīngshī 京師) were dismissed.
In the intercalary month, on the day Xīnhài (辛亥),
the Western Regions (Xīyù 西域) presented a qílín (麒麟) as tribute.
On the day Wùwǔ (戊午),
a auspicious star (jǐngxīng 景星) was sighted.
The ceremonial officials requested permission to submit congratulatory memorials,
but all were disallowed.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐyǒu (乙酉),
officials were dispatched to record serious offenders throughout the empire.
On the day Jǐhài (己亥),

an imperial edict instructed the Grand Coordinators (Xúnfǔ 巡撫), Investigating Censors (Xún'àn Yùshǐ 巡按御史), and Three Judicial Commissioners (Sānsī Guān 三司官) of the two capitals (Liǎngjīng 兩京), Húguǎng (湖廣), Jiāngxī (江西), and Hénán (河南) to inspect disaster-stricken areas,
and to remit four-tenths of the autumn grain tax.

the Ministry of Works' (Gōngbù 工部) procurement was abolished.

On the day Yǐwèi (乙未),
Ābózhǐ'ān (阿卜只俺), son of Ālǔtái (阿魯台), surrendered.
On the day Dīngyǒu (丁酉),
he arrived at Xǐmǎlín (洗馬林),
and inspected the fortifications and military readiness.
On the day Jǐhài (己亥),
a grand hunt took place.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ (丙午),
he returned to the palace.
On the day Bǐngchén (丙辰),
Grand Commandant Fāng Zhèng (方政) pacified the rebellious Man (Mán 蠻) in Sōngpān (松潘).

horse markets in Shǎnxī (陝西) were abolished.

there was famine in the Two Metropolitan Areas (Liǎng Jī 兩畿), Zhèjiāng (浙江), Húguǎng (湖廣), and Jiāngxī (江西),
and relief was provided using grain transported from the Southern Capital (Nánjīng 南京) and Línqīng (臨清) granaries.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùxū (戊戌),
executions were suspended.
On the day Gēngzǐ (庚子),
taxes on grain for disaster relief in Sìchuān (四川) were remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ (甲子),
the Emperor was unwell,
and Wèi (衞) Prince Zhānshēn (瞻埏) officiated the sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào 太廟).
In this year,
Siam (Xiānluó 暹羅), Champa (Zhānchéng 占城), Ryukyu (Liúqiú 琉球), Sumatra (Sūméndálà 蘇門答剌), Hāmì (哈密), and Oirat (Wǎlà 瓦剌) paid tribute.
In the tenth year, spring, the first month, on the first day, Guǐyǒu (癸酉),
the Emperor did not hold court,
and ordered the officials to pay respects to the Crown Prince (Huáng Tàizǐ 皇太子) at the Wénhuá Diàn (文華殿).
On the day Jiǎxū (甲戌),
the illness worsened.
Procurement and construction missions of various departments were halted.
On the day Yǐhài (乙亥),
the Emperor passed away in the Qiánqīng Gōng (乾清宮),
aged thirty-eight.
His dying wish was that important state affairs be decided by the Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu 皇太后).
On the day Dīngyǒu (丁酉),
an honorific posthumous title was bestowed,
his temple name was Xuānzōng (宣宗),
and he was buried in Jǐnglín (景陵).
A eulogy states: Rénzōng (仁宗), as Crown Prince,
lost favor with Chéngzǔ (成祖).
That he overcame his peril and regained peace
was largely due to the efforts of the Imperial Grandson (Tàisūn 太孫).
After his enthronement,
officials performed their duties well,
governance was equitable,
laws and order were clear and rectified,
granaries were full and overflowing,
the populace enjoyed their occupations,
and years were free from disaster.
From the founding of the Míng (明) dynasty to this point, sixty years had passed,
the people's spirits gradually relaxed,
and a vibrant appearance of peace and order emerged.
As for the sudden rise of powerful vassal kings,
they were swiftly suppressed;
border dust (conflict) was swept away,
and cunning invaders were terrified.
The Emperor's heroic demeanor and sagacious strategies
were almost enough to follow in the footsteps of his ancestors.

Basic Annals 10: Fore-Annals of Yīngzōng (英宗)
Yīngzōng (英宗) Fǎtiānlìdào Rénmíng Chéngjìng Zhāowén Xiànwǔ Zhìdé Guǎngxiào Ruìhuángdì (法天立道仁明誠敬昭文憲武至德廣孝睿皇帝),
personal name Qízhèn (祁鎮),
was the eldest son of Xuānzōng (宣宗).
His mother was Noble Consort (Guìfēi 貴妃) Sūn (孫)氏.
Four months after his birth,
he was established as the Crown Prince (Huáng Tàizǐ 皇太子),

he ascended the imperial throne.
