In the ninth month, on the *rényín* day,
outstanding taxes in Yúnnán were remitted.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the *rényín* day,
famine relief was provided in Zhèjiāng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
taxes on grain for flood-stricken Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Chángzhōu, Zhènjiāng, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu were remitted.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the monk Yáng Xíngxiáng from Guǎngxī, who falsely claimed to be Emperor Jiànwén,
was shackled and sent to the capital,
and died in the Jǐnyī Wèi prison.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Mù Áng suppressed the rebellious Mán of Shīzōng.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
taxes on grain for disaster-stricken Nánjīng Metropolitan Region, Zhèjiāng, Shāndōng, and Hénán were remitted.
In this year,
Zhànchéng, Liúqiú Zhōngshān, Hāmì, and Wūsīzàng sent tribute.
In the sixth year, in spring, on the *jǐhài* day, the first day of the first month,
there was supposed to be a solar eclipse,
but it was not seen.
The ritual officials requested to present congratulations,
but this was not permitted.
On the *gēngxū* day,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were held at the Southern Suburb.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
because the Zhuānglàng region had repeatedly experienced earthquakes,
His Majesty personally sacrificed at the ancestral temples and the suburban altars,
and dispatched envoys to sacrifice to the Western Sacred Mountain and Boundary.
A large-scale expedition was launched against Lùchuān.
Jiǎng Guì, Marquis Dìngxī, was appointed General Píngmán.
Dūdu Tóngzhī Lǐ Ān and Qiānshì Liú Jù were his deputies.
Wáng Jì, Minister of War, was appointed Grand Supervisor of military affairs.
In the third month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Yú Qiān, Vice Minister of War, was imprisoned.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
due to calamities and anomalies, envoys were dispatched to investigate suspicious cases of imprisonment throughout the empire.
In the fifth month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
Hé Wényuān, Vice Minister of Justice, and Wáng Wénlù, Grand Minister of the Grand Court of Judicial Review, recorded criminal cases in the capital.
Zhōu Chén, Vice Minister and巡撫, and Guō Jǐn, Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Justice, recorded criminal cases in Nánjīng.
Yú Qiān was released and appointed Shaòqīng of the Grand Court of Judicial Review.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
relief was provided for famine in Zhèjiāng and Húguǎng.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
Liú Zhōngfū, Minister of Revenue,
and Wú Xǐ and Chén Cháng, Vice Ministers, were paraded in cangues at Cháng'ānmén.
After more than ten days, they were released and reinstated to their positions.
On the *gēngyín* day,
taxes on grain were remitted for disaster-stricken areas within the capital region.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
the Qiánqīng and Kūnníng Palaces,
and the Fèngtiān, Huágài, and Jǐnshēn Halls were completed.
A grand amnesty was proclaimed.
Běijīng was designated as the permanent capital,
and all civil and military offices no longer referred to it as the "Temporary Imperial Residence."
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Wáng Jì captured the Shàngjiāng stockade in Lùchuān.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
taxes on grain were remitted for disaster-stricken areas in Hénán, Shāndōng, and the prefectures of Fèngyáng, etc.
In the intercalary month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Liú Zhōngfū, Wú Xǐ, and Chén Cháng were again imprisoned.
After more than a year,
Zhōngfū was released and reverted to commoner status,
while Xǐ and Cháng were exiled to the frontier.
In the twelfth month,
Wáng Jì conquered Lùchuān,
and Sī Rènfā fled to Mèngyǎng.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the army returned in triumph.
Lǐ Ān, Vice Grand General of the Left, attacked the remaining bandits in Gāolígòngshān,
but was defeated.
In this year,
Zhànchéng, Wǎlà, and Hāmì offered tribute.
In the seventh year, in spring, in the first month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were held at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
His Majesty went to Tiānshòushān.
In the third month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
His Majesty returned to the palace.
On the *yǐhài* day,
five-tenths of the military farm taxes in Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the *wùyín* day,
Liú Yǎn and others were granted the *jìnshì jízhì* degree and official positions of varying ranks.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
relief was provided for famine in Shǎnxī.
In this month,
taxes on grain were remitted for disaster-stricken areas in Shānxī, Hénán, and Shāndōng.
In the fifth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
in recognition of the merits in pacifying Lùchuān,
Jiǎng Guì was promoted to Marquis,
and Wáng Jì to Earl Jìngyuǎn.
On the *wùyín* day,
Empress Qián was established.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Japanese pirates captured Dàsōngsuǒ.
In the sixth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Jiāo Hóng, Vice Minister of Revenue, was dispatched to prepare defenses against Japanese pirates in Zhèjiāng.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
famine victims in Shǎnxī were relieved,
and children sold by the people were redeemed.
In the eighth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Wáng Jì was again appointed Grand Supervisor of military affairs in Yúnnán.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
auspicious grain was presented from Shǎnxī.
The ritual officials requested to present congratulations,
but this was not permitted.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *rénchén* day,
the Wūliánghā attacked Guǎngníng.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Grand Empress Dowager passed away.
In the twelfth month,
Empress Chéngxiào Zhāo was buried at Xiànlíng.
In this year,
Zhànchéng, Wǎlà, Hāmì, Zhōngshān of Liúqiú, Ānnán, Zhǎowā, Tǔlúfān, and Wūsīzàng offered tribute.
In the eighth year, in spring, in the first month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were held at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
redundant officials in Nánjīng were dismissed.
On the *wùxū* day,
Zhān Ào, Prince of Huái, came to court.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Zhān Gāng, Prince of Jīng, came to court.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
General Píngmán Jiǎng Guì and Wáng Jì were again ordered to lead an army to conquer Sī Jīfā, son of Sī Rènfā, in Lùchuān.
On the *wùyín* day,
lightning struck the *chīwěn* (ornamental ridge-end) of the Fèngtiān Hall.
An imperial edict was issued for self-examination and reform.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
a grand amnesty was proclaimed.
In the sixth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Liú Qiú, Collator, presented ten proposals.
He was imprisoned in the Jǐnyīwèi prison.
Eunuch Wáng Zhèn ordered Commander Mǎ Shùn to kill him.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Xuē Xuān, Shaòqīng of the Grand Court of Judicial Review, was imprisoned.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
Lǐ Shímiǎn, Libationer, was paraded in a cangue at the gate of the Guózǐjiān for three days.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Sī Jīfā requested to surrender.
In winter, in the eleventh month,
Empress Hú, the deposed Empress of Xuānzōng, passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
taxes on grain were remitted for two years for people in Shāndōng who had re-established their livelihoods.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Jiāo Jìng, Imperial Son-in-Law and Commandant, was paraded in a cangue at the right gate of Cháng'ānmén.
In this year,
Zhànchéng, Ānnán, Wǎlà, Hāmì, and Zhǎowā offered tribute.
In the ninth year, in spring, in the first month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
Wáng Wén, Censor-in-Chief of the Right, inspected the borders of Yán'ān and Níngxià.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were held at the Southern Suburb.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Zhū Yǒng, Duke of Chéngguó,
Xú Hēng, Earl of Xīng'ān,
Dūdu Mǎ Liàng and Chén Huái,
together with Eunuchs Sēng Bǎo, Cáo Jíxiáng, Liú Yǒngchéng, and Dàn Zhù, were dispatched in different routes to campaign against the Wūliánghā.
In the second month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Wáng Jì defeated Sī Jīfā and drove him away,
capturing his family members to present (as tribute).
Jì was recalled.
In the third month, on the *xīnhài* day, the first day of the month,
the newly constructed Imperial Academy was completed,
and a ceremony of offering sacrifices and libations to Confucius, the Former Teacher, was held.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Zhū Yǒng and others' army returned.
Yáng Shìqí passed away.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
for their merits in campaigning against the Wūliánghā,
Chén Huái was enfeoffed as Earl Píngxiāng,
and Mǎ Liàng as Earl Zhāoyuǎn.
Zhū Yǒng, Duke of Chéngguó, and others were promoted in rank by varying degrees.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Chén Xún, Grand Academician of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed to serve in the Wényuāngé,
participating in crucial government affairs.
On the *dīnghài* day,
relief was provided for famine in Shāzhōu and the Chìjīn Mongols.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
the Judicial Offices were ordered to record criminal cases in the capital,
and Mǎ Áng, Vice Minister of Justice, recorded criminal cases in Nánjīng.
In the sixth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
relief was provided for famine among the Man people in Húguǎng and Guìzhōu.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
Shí Jǐng, Imperial Son-in-Law and Commandant, was imprisoned.
Yè Zōngliú, a bandit from Chǔzhōu, plundered the Fú'ān silver mine
and killed Zhú Yuān, Councilor of Fújiàn.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
taxes on grain were remitted for disaster-stricken areas in Hénán.
In the intercalary month, on the *wùyín* day,
the silver mines in Fújiàn and Zhèjiāng were reopened.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
unburied corpses were interred.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
lightning struck the *chīwěn* of the Fèngxiān Hall.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
taxes on grain were remitted for disaster-stricken areas in Shǎnxī,
and children sold by the people were redeemed.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
imperial edicts were issued to border generals to prepare against Yěxiān of Wǎlà.
In the ninth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Wáng Jì, Earl Jìngyuǎn, and Chén Yì, Censor-in-Chief of the Right, managed the border defenses in the northwest.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Wūliánghā offered horses as tribute and apologized for their transgressions.
In this year,
the two capital regions (Jīngjī), Shāndōng, Hénán, Zhèjiāng, and Húguǎng experienced severe floods,
and all rivers overflowed.
Xiāmluó, Zhōngshān of Liúqiú, Wǎlà, Ānnán, Wūsīzàng, and Mǎlājiā offered tribute.
In the tenth year, spring, first month, on the *bǐng xū* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Altar.
On the *wù zǐ* day,
an imperial edict called for the recruitment of men of wisdom and courage.
Second month, on the *dīng sì* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the *jǐ wèi* day,
arrears of taxes in Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the *bǐng yín* day,
the Wūliánghā presented horses as tribute
and requested clemency for those who had violated the border,
but this was not granted.
On the *rén shēn* day,
the Emperor went to Tiānshòu Shān.
Third month, on the *bǐng zǐ* day,
he returned to the palace.
On the *gēng chén* day,
Sījīfā offered tribute and apologized.
On the *gēng yín* day,
Shāng Lù and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with different ranks.
Summer, fourth month, on the *jiǎ chén* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *gēng shēn* day,
an imperial edict ordered local officials everywhere to provide for returning refugees and those displaced by famine.
Sixth month, on the *yǐ chǒu* day,
relief was provided to the famine-stricken in Shǎnxī,
and two-thirds of their land tax was remitted.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *yǐ wèi* day,
the price of grain from the warehouses of Hénán and Huáiqìng was reduced
to aid the famine in Shān and Shǎnxī.
Eighth month, on the *guǐ chǒu* day,
autumn grain taxes were remitted in Húguǎng due to drought.
On the *bǐng chén* day,
autumn grain taxes were remitted in the fourteen prefectures and subprefectures of Sū, Sōng, Jiā, and Hú due to floods.
Winter, tenth month, on the *wù chén* day,
the Academician Attendant Miáo Zhōng was made Vice Minister of War,
and the Academician Expositor Gāo Gǔ was made Vice Minister of Works,
both joining the Grand Secretariat to participate in military affairs.
Twelfth month, on the *bǐng chén* day,
Miǎndiàn captured Sīrènfā,
beheaded him, and sent his head to the capital.
On the *rén xū* day,
grain from Hénán was transported to relieve the famine in Shǎnxī.
The Grand General of Guǎngxī, Marquis Ānyuǎn Liǔ Pǔ, suppressed the rebellious barbarians in Qìngyuǎn.
In this year,
Zhōngshān of Liúqiú, Hāmì, Yìlìbǎlǐ, Ānnán, Zhànchéng, Mǎnlàjiā, Xīlán Shān, Sāmǎ'érhǎn, and Wūsīzàng offered tribute.
In the eleventh year, spring, first month, on the *jǐ mǎo* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Altar.
On the *gēng chén* day,
the Emperor granted the eunuch Wáng Zhèn and others' younger brothers and nephews hereditary official posts in the Imperial Bodyguard.
Second month, on the *xīn yǒu* day,
an unusual phenomenon was observed at the Huágài and Fèntiān Halls,
and officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices and make announcements to Heaven and Earth.
On the *guǐ hài* day,
an imperial edict ordered compassion in criminal justice.
Third month, on the *wù chén* day,
Minister of Revenue Wáng Zuǒ, Minister of Justice Jīn Lián, and Censor-in-Chief Chén Yì were imprisoned in the Imperial Bodyguard's jail,
but were soon released.
On the *rén shēn* day,
Censor Liǔ Huá supervised the troops of Fújiàn, Zhèjiāng, and Jiāngxī to suppress mining bandits.
On the *guǐ yǒu* day,
the Emperor went to Tiānshòu Shān.
On the *gēng chén* day,
he returned to the palace.
Summer, sixth month, on the *bǐng chén* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *guǐ yǒu* day,
the market and shop tax in paper currency was increased.
On the *gēng chén* day,
Yáng Pǔ passed away.
Eighth month, on the *wù xū* day,
autumn grain taxes were remitted in disaster-stricken Húguǎng.
On the *gēng shēn* day,
Minister of Personnel Wáng Zhí and others were imprisoned,
but were soon released.
Ninth month, on the *xīn sì* day,
the Yáo of Guǎngxī rebelled,
captured Máozìdé, the Prefect of Huàzhōu,
and killed Battalion Commander Wāng Yì.
Winter, tenth month, on the *jiǎ yín* day,
Attending Censors and Censors were dispatched to distribute rewards to border troops.
Eleventh month, on the *rén shēn* day,
penalties for crimes down to capital punishment were reduced.
In this year,
Zhōngshān of Liúqiú, Xiāmluó, Ānnán, Zhǎowā, Huíhuí Hāmì, Zhànchéng, Yìlìbǎlǐ, Sāmǎ'érhǎn, and Wūsīzàng offered tribute.
In the twelfth year, spring, first month, on the *guǐ yǒu* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Altar.
Third month, on the *guǐ hài* day,
the Emperor went to Tiānshòu Shān.
On the *gēng wǔ* day,
he returned to the palace.
On the *bǐng zǐ* day,
autumn grain taxes were remitted in disaster-stricken Háng, Jiā, and Hú.
Summer, fourth month, on the *dīng sì* day,
autumn grain taxes were remitted in disaster-stricken Sū, Sōng, Cháng, and Zhèn.
Fifth month, on the *jǐ hài* day,
Assistant Minister of the Grand Court of Revision Zhāng Jì provided relief to the famine-stricken in Jìníng and Huái, Yáng.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *jiǎ chén* day,
an imperial edict ordered all border garrisons to train troops in preparation against the Wǎlà.
Eighth month, on the *gēng shēn* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Ninth month, on the *yǐ wèi* day,
Mǎ Yú passed away.
In this year,
Zhōngshān of Liúqiú, Ānnán, Zhànchéng, Wǎlà, Zhǎowā, Hāmì, and Xiāmluó offered tribute.
In the thirteenth year, spring, first month, on the *dīng yǒu* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Altar.
Third month, on the *wù zǐ* day,
an imperial edict ordered the Xuānwèi司 of Mèngyǎng to present Sījīfā.
On the *rén yín* day,
Péng Shí and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with different ranks.
Wáng Jì continued as Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs,
and Assistant Military Commissioner Gōng Jù was appointed General Pacifying Barbarians,
serving as Grand General,
leading an army to suppress Sījīfā.
Summer, fourth month,
autumn grain taxes were remitted in disaster-stricken Zhèjiāng, Jiāngxī, and Húguǎng.
Fifth month, on the *bǐng xū* day,
envoys were dispatched to capture locusts in Shāndōng.
On the *jiǎ chén* day,
Vice Minister of Justice Dīng Xuàn pacified and resettled disaster victims in Hénán and Shāndōng.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *yǐ yǒu* day,
the river burst its banks in Dàmíng,
inundating over three hundred *lǐ*,
and envoys were dispatched to grant exemptions and provide relief.
On the *jǐ yǒu* day,
the river burst its banks in Hénán,
inundating Cáo, Pú, and Dōngchāng,
breaching the Shāwān of Shòuzhāng,
and damaging the transport waterways;
Vice Minister of Works Wáng Yǒnghé was tasked with its repair.
Eighth month, on the *yǐ mǎo* day,
the bandit Dèng Máoqī rebelled in Fújiàn.
On the *jiǎ xū* day,
Censor Dīng Xuān was ordered to capture him.
Winter, eleventh month, on the *bǐng xū* day,
Marquis Níngyáng Chén Mào was appointed Grand General,
with Earl Bǎodìng Liáng Bǎo and Earl Píngjiāng Chén Yù as his deputies,
and Eunuchs Cáo Jíxiáng and Wáng Jǐn overseeing firearms,
and Minister of Justice Jīn Lián participating in military strategy,
to suppress Dèng Máoqī.
On the *jiǎ chén* day,
bandits from Chǔzhōu raided and plundered various counties of Jīnhuá.
On the *gēng xū* day,
Marquis Yǒngkāng Xú Ān was stationed in Shāndōng to defend against Japanese pirates.
Twelfth month, on the *gēng wǔ* day,
Yáo bandits in Guǎngdōng rebelled.
In this year,
Zhōngshān of Liúqiú, Ānnán, and Zhànchéng offered tribute.
Three thousand Wǎlà tribute envoys came,
but the rewards were not given according to precedent,
which then led to conflict.
In the fourteenth year, spring, first month, on the *jiǎ wǔ* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Altar.
On the *yǐ sì* day,
silver taxes were remitted in Zhèjiāng and Fújiàn.
Second month, on the *dīng sì* day,
Censor Dīng Xuān and Commander Liú Fú attacked and beheaded Dèng Máoqī in Yánpíng.
On the *jǐ sì* day,
Wáng Jì defeated Sījīfā at Jīnshā Jiāng,
and again defeated him at Guǐkū Shān,
then returned with his army.
On the *xīn wèi* day,
Assistant Commander Xú Gōng was appointed Grand General,
to suppress the Chǔzhōu bandit Yè Zōngliú,
with Minister of Works Shí Pú participating in military strategy.
Third month, on the *wù zǐ* day,
the Emperor went to Tiānshòu Shān.
On the *guǐ sì* day,
he returned to the palace.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Gēngxū,
rebels from Chǔzhōu attacked Chóng'ān,
killing the Regional Commander Wú Gāng.
On the day Rénxū,
Miao rebels rose in great numbers in Húguǎng and Guìzhōu,
and Wáng Jì was ordered to suppress them.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
thirteen censors were dispatched along with eunuchs to supervise the silver tax in Fújiàn and Zhèjiāng.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Chén Mào defeated the rebels in Shāxiàn.
On the day Rénchén,
there was a drought.
Grand Eunuch Jīn Yīng, together with the judicial officials, reviewed prisoners' cases.
On the day Jǐhài,
Academian-in-waiting Zhāng Yì was assigned to the Wényuān Pavilion,
participating in confidential military affairs.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Wāng Chéng, the Censor for Fújiàn, was executed in the marketplace,
and the former Censor Chái Wénxiǎn was also killed.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Miao rebels from Jìngzhōu attacked Chénxī,
and Regional Commander Gāo Liàng died in battle.
On the day Bǐngchén,
a fire disaster occurred in the Jǐnshēn and other halls in Nánjīng.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
self-reflection and austerity were ordered.
An imperial edict commanded all rotational troops from Hénán and Shānxī, who were on leave, to proceed to Dàtóng and Xuānfǔ.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Sīníng Hóu Sòng Yīng was appointed Grand Coordinator of the military forces in Dàtóng.
On the day Jǐsì,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the empire.
On the day Wùyín,
Píngxiāng Bó Chén Huái,
the Imperial Son-in-Law Commander Jǐng Yuán,
Grand Commanders Wáng Guì and Wú Kèqín,
and Grand Eunuch Lín Shòu,
were assigned to train the capital's troops in Dàtóng and Xuānfǔ,
to prepare for the Oirats.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Esen of the Oirats raided Dàtóng.
Assistant General Wú Hào died in battle,
and an imperial edict for a personal expedition was issued.
The Minister of Personnel, Wáng Zhí, led the officials in remonstrating,
but was not heeded.
On the day Guǐsì,
Prince Chéng was ordered to guard the capital.
On that day,
Sīníng Hóu Sòng Yīng and Wǔjìn Bó Zhū Miǎn engaged the Oirats in battle at Yánghé,
were defeated, and perished.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor departed from the capital.
On the day Yǐwèi,
he reached Lónghǔ Tái,
where the army was alarmed during the night.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
he reached Jūyōng Guān.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
he reached Xuānfǔ.
The officials repeatedly requested him to halt his advance,
but he did not allow it.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
he reached Yánghé.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùshēn,
he reached Dàtóng.
The Garrison Grand Eunuch Guō Jìng remonstrated,
proposing to return the army.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Guǎngníng Bó Liú Ān was appointed General-in-Chief,
garrisoning Dàtóng.
On the day Gēngxū,
the army returned.
On the day Dīngsì,
they reached Xuānfǔ.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Oirat army arrived in great numbers.
Gōngshùn Hóu Wú Kèzhōng and Grand Commander Wú Kèqín died in battle.
Chéngguó Gōng Zhū Yǒng and Yǒngshùn Bó Xuē Shòu went to their rescue,
but encountered an ambush at Yàor Líng,
and the entire army was annihilated.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
they reached Tǔmù,
and were besieged.
On the day Rénxū,
the army collapsed,
with hundreds of thousands dead.
Yīngguó Gōng Zhāng Fǔ,
Tàiníng Hóu Chén Yíng,
Imperial Son-in-Law Commander Jǐng Yuán,
Píngxiāng Bó Chén Huái,
Xiāngchéng Bó Lǐ Zhēn,
Suí'ān Bó Chén Xūn,
Xiūwǔ Bó Shěn Róng,
Grand Commanders Liáng Chéng and Wáng Guì,
Ministers Wáng Zuǒ and Kuàng Yě,
Academicians Cáo Nài and Zhāng Yì,
Vice Ministers Dīng Xuàn and Wáng Yǒnghé,
Vice Censor-in-Chief Dèng Qǐ, etc.,
all died.
The Emperor was taken captive to the north.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
when the capital heard of the defeat,
officials gathered and wept in the court.
Lecturer Xú Chéng proposed moving the capital south,
but Vice Minister of War Yú Qiān objected.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Empress Dowager ordered Prince Chéng to supervise the state.
On the day Wùchén,
the Emperor arrived at Dàtóng.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Empress Dowager ordered the establishment of the imperial son Jiànshēn as Crown Prince.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor arrived at Wēiníng Háizi.
On the day Jiǎxū,
he arrived at Hēihé.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Prince Chéng ascended the throne,
posthumously honoring the Emperor as Tàishàng Huángdì (Retired Emperor).
Collation Notes
Annals, Volume 11, Jǐngdì
Emperor Gōngrén Kāngdì Jǐng,
personal name Qíyù,
was the second son of Xuānzōng.
His mother was Consort Xián Wú.
When Yīngzōng ascended the throne,
he was enfeoffed as Prince Chéng.
In the eighth month of the fourteenth year of Zhèngtǒng,
Yīngzōng was taken captive to the north.
The Empress Dowager ordered the Prince to supervise the state.
On the day Bǐngyín,
grain from Tōngzhōu was moved into the capital.
Troops from the Two Capitals, Shāndōng, and Hénán, originally for coastal defense and grain transport, were summoned to guard the capital.
Níngyáng Hóu Chén Mào was recalled to lead his army back.
On the day Wùchén,
Vice Minister of War Yú Qiān was made Minister of War.
Officials were ordered to speak frankly about current affairs,
and to recommend talented individuals.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Empress Dowager issued an edict to establish the imperial son Jiànshēn as Crown Prince.
Condolences were given to the fallen generals and soldiers.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Wáng Zhèn's household assets were confiscated.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Right Censor-in-Chief Chén Yì pacified the military and civilians within the capital region.
On the day Rénshēn,
Grand Commander Shí Hēng took command of the capital's garrison troops.
On the day Yǐhài,
a directive was sent to border generals,
stating that when the Oirats arrived with the Emperor,
they should not make any rash sally.
Military equipment from Nánjīng was transported to the capital.
Compilers Shāng Lù and Péng Shí entered the cabinet to participate in confidential military affairs.
In this month,
Huáng Xiāoyǎng, a rebel from Guǎngdōng, caused unrest.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the Prince ascended the throne as Emperor,
posthumously honoring the former Emperor as Tàishàng Huángdì,
designating the next year as the first year of Jǐngtài,
declaring a general amnesty throughout the empire,
and remitting three-tenths of the land tax for the second year of Jǐngtài.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Wáng Zhèn's clan was annihilated.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Chǔzhōu rebels were pacified.
On the day Guǐsì,
Adjutant Commander Jì Duó, acting on the Empress Dowager's orders,
conveyed a message to the Retired Emperor.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
sacrifices were offered to the generals and soldiers who died in battle at Xuānfǔ and Tǔmù, and their remains were buried.
On the day Yǐwèi,
General-in-Chief Ānxiāng Bó Zhāng Ān, who was suppressing the Guǎngzhōu rebels,
was defeated and killed.
Adjutant Commander Wáng Qīng was captured,
and died.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Grand Secretary Sūn Xiáng and Bureau Director Luó Tōng were appointed Right Vice Censors-in-Chief,
to guard Zǐjīng and Jūyōng Guān.
On the day Jiǎchén,
fifteen censors were dispatched to recruit soldiers in the capital region, Shāndōng, Shānxī, and Hénán.
Grand Commander-in-Chief Chén Yǒu led his army to suppress the rebellious Miao in Húguǎng and Guìzhōu.
On the day Yǐsì,
an envoy was dispatched to present a letter to the Retired Emperor.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Miao besieged Píngyuè Guard.
Troops from Yúnnán and Sìchuān were mobilized to join Wáng Jì in suppressing them.
Counselor Yáng Xìnmín was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief,
to suppress the Guǎngdōng rebels.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Wùshēn,
Yěxiān escorted the Grand Emperor to Dàtóng.
On the day Rénzǐ,
an imperial edict was issued to the various princes to raise armies for the defense of the state.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Yú Qiān took charge of the various military camps,
and Shí Hēng and the various generals were assigned to defend the nine gates.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Yěxiān captured Zǐjīngguān.
Sūn Xiáng died there,
and the capital was put on high alert.
On the day Dīngsì,
an imperial edict was issued to the Grand Commanders of Xuānfǔ and Liáodōng,
and the Circuit Intendants of Shāndōng, Hénán, Shānxī, and Shǎnxī, as well as the recruiting censors, to lead their troops to reinforce the capital.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Yěxiān pressed upon the capital city.
Grand Commanders Gāo Lǐ and Máo Fúshòu defeated them at Zhāngyìmén.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Right Vice Minister of Communications Wáng Fù and the Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhào Róng were sent as envoys to Yěxiān's camp,
and paid respects to the Grand Emperor at Tǔchéng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
troops were conscripted from Cháoxiǎn,
and local troops from the various guards of Hézhōu were mobilized to reinforce the capital.
Yú Qiān, Shí Hēng, and others repeatedly defeated Yěxiān's forces outside the city.
On the day Rénxū,
the invaders retreated.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
they exited Zǐjīngguān.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
an imperial edict was issued to halt the armies of the various princes.
The Khagan of Wǎlà, Tuōtuōbùhuā, sent an envoy.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Earl of Chāngpíng, Yáng Hóng, was appointed Grand Commander,
with Grand Commanders Sūn Táng and Fàn Guǎng as his deputies,
to suppress the remaining bandits within the capital region.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the passes and strategic points along the border were repaired.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Máo Fúshòu was appointed Vice Grand Commander
to suppress the rebellious Miáo in Chénzhōu.
On the day Rénchén,
the Grand Emperor arrived in Wǎlà.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Assistant Minister Gěng Jiǔchóu pacified the displaced people in Nánnánjī,
and they were granted exemption from corvée labor for three years.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Empress Dowager was honored as the Supreme Saint Empress Dowager.
On the day Xīnhài,
Wáng Jì was appointed General Pacifying the Barbarians
and made Grand Commander
to suppress the rebellious Miáo in Guìzhōu.
The Assistant Grand Commander Dǒng Xīng was made Left Vice Grand Commander
to suppress the bandits in Guǎngdōng,
and the Assistant Minister of Revenue Mèng Jiàn participated in military affairs.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the consort mother Xiánfēi was honored as Empress Dowager.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Consort Wāng Shì was made Empress.
On the day Bǐngchén,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Shí Hēng, Yáng Hóng, and Liǔ Pǔ were assigned to train the capital garrison troops.
On the day Wùchén,
sacrifices were offered to the fallen officers and soldiers outside Xīzhímén.
In this year,
Liúqiú Zhōngshān, Zhànchéng, Wūsīzàng, and Sāmǎ'érhǎn paid tribute.
In the spring of the first year of Jǐngtài, in the first month, on the day Dīngchǒu (the first day of the month),
court greetings were abolished.
On the day Xīnsì,
Chāngpíng was walled.
On the day Rénwǔ,
sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the day Bǐngxū,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were held at the Southern Suburb.
In the intercalary month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Wǎlà invaded Níngxià.
On the day Guǐhài,
an imperial edict was issued that examination candidates for the metropolitan examination should not be restricted by quota.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Grand Commander of Dàtóng, Guō Dēng, defeated Wǎlà at Shāwō,
and then pursued and defeated them again at Kǎoláoshān.
Dēng was enfeoffed as the Earl of Dìngxiāng.
In this month,
tax grain was remitted for the disaster-stricken areas of Dàmíng, Zhēndìng, Kāifēng, and Wèihuī.
In the second month, on the day Wùyín,
the ceremonial plowing of the imperial field took place.
On the day Guǐwèi,
rewards were offered to recruit soldiers and civilians trapped by the enemy.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Shí Hēng was appointed General Pacifying the North,
and led troops to patrol Dàtóng.
The Assistant Commander-in-Chief Yáng Néng was appointed General of Guerrilla Warfare
to patrol Xuānfǔ.
On the day Rénchén,
Eunuch Xǐ Níng was executed.
In the third month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Wǎlà invaded Shuòzhōu.
On the day Xīnhài,
rewards were granted to the descendants of officials who died at Tǔmù.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Wǎlà invaded Níngxià and Qìngyáng.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
they invaded Shuòzhōu.
On the day Guǐhài,
arrears of taxes and summer taxes in the capital region were remitted.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Commanders-in-Chief of Guǎngdōng, Lǐ Shēng and Hé Guì, led troops to apprehend pirates,
and died in battle.
On the day Xīnsì,
Wǎlà invaded Dàtóng,
and the imperial forces repelled them.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Earl of Bǎodìng, Liáng Bǎo, replaced Wáng Jì in suppressing the rebellious Miáo in Guìzhōu.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, Lǐ Mào, investigated prisoners in Nánjīng,
evaluated and dismissed officials from various departments,
and inquired into the welfare of the military and civilians.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Wǎlà invaded Yànmén.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Assistant Grand Commander Liú Ān was appointed Grand Commander
to train troops in Bǎodìng, Zhēndìng, and the three prefectures of Zhuó, Yì, and Tōng.
The Assistant Censor-in-Chief Cáo Tài participated in military affairs.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
famine relief was provided in Shāndōng.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
relief was provided to the counties and prefectures in the capital region that had been invaded.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Wǎlà invaded Dàtóng,
and Guō Dēng repelled them.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐsì,
tax grain was remitted for disaster-stricken Shānxī.
Wǎlà plundered Héqǔ and Dàizhōu,
then advanced south.
An imperial edict ordered Liú Ān to supervise the troops of Zhuó and Yì to resist them.
On the day Wùshēn,
Wǎlà invaded Yànmén.
Troops were sent to reinforce Huánghuāzhèn to guard the imperial tombs.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Dǒng Xīng defeated the bandits in Guǎngdōng,
and Huáng Xiāoyǎng was executed.
On the day Rénxū,
relief was provided to the military and civilians of Dàtóng who had suffered from the invasion.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Assistant Minister Hóu Jìn and Vice Grand Commander Tián Lǐ severely defeated the Miáo in Guìzhōu.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Wǎlà sent an envoy to request peace.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Wǎlà invaded Dàtóng,
and Guō Dēng repelled them.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Yěxiān again escorted the Grand Emperor to Dàtóng.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Left Censor-in-Chief Chén Yì and Wáng Wén were imprisoned for an unsubstantiated investigation into Eunuch Jīn Yīng's family.
They were later released.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Wǎlà invaded Xuānfǔ.
Grand Commander Zhū Qiān and Participating General Jì Guǎng resisted and repelled them.
On the day Wùxū,
tax grain was remitted for disaster-stricken prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the day Jǐhài,
Remonstrance Official Lǐ Shí and Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Luó Qǐ were sent as envoys to Wǎlà.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Gēngxū,
Minister Hóu Jìn and Participating General Fāng Yīng defeated the Miáo in Guìzhōu,
captured their chieftain, and presented him to the capital.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Right Censor-in-Chief Yáng Shàn and Assistant Minister of Works Zhào Róng were sent as envoys to Wǎlà.
The transportation of grain by the people of Shānxī to Dàtóng was suspended.
On the day Guǐhài,
Lǐ Shí and Luó Qǐ returned.
On the day Jǐsì,
Yáng Shàn arrived in Wǎlà,
and Yěxiān agreed to the Grand Emperor's return.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
the Grand Emperor departed from Wǎlà.
On the day Wùyín,
sacrifices were offered to the gods of land and grain.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Reader Shāng Lù was sent to welcome the Grand Emperor at Jūyōngguān.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Grand Emperor returned to the capital.
The Emperor welcomed him at Dōng'ānmén,
and he was lodged in the Nángōng.
The Emperor, leading all officials, paid him respects.
On the day Gēngyín,
a general amnesty was granted to all under heaven.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Right Assistant Minister of Justice Jiāng Yuān also served as a Hanlin Academician,
worked in the Wényuángé,
and participated in state affairs.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
the Circuit Intendant of Hénán and Vice Censor-in-Chief, Wáng Lái, was appointed Supreme Commander of military affairs in Húguǎng and Guìzhōu
to suppress the rebellious Miáo.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day Guǐsì,
outstanding taxes in the capital region were remitted.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnhài,
Hú Yíng (胡濙), Minister of the Ministry of Rites, requested that all officials offer congratulations to the Grand Emperor on his birthday (Wànshòu Jié).
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
he again requested that in the coming year, on New Year's Day (Zhèngdàn), all officials pay court to the Grand Emperor at Yán'ān Mén (延安門).
Both requests were denied.
That year,
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮) presented tribute horses three times.
In the second year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngxū,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Rénzǐ,
an imperial edict ordered that officials from across the empire who were due for dismissal should transport grain outside the passes.
In the second month, on the day Xīnwèi,
a ceremony (shìdiàn) was performed for the Former Teacher Kǒngzǐ (孔子).
On the day Xīnmǎo,
due to unusual celestial phenomena, reforms were undertaken,
and an imperial edict commanded court officials to deliberate and propose policies for leniency and relief.
On the day Guǐsì,
an imperial edict instructed the Grand Coordinators (xúnfǔ guān) in the capital region and Shāndōng (山東) to select honest and capable officials to specialize in promoting agriculture,
distribute uncultivated land to the people,
and provide loans of oxen and seeds.
In the third month, on the day Rén'yín,
Kē Qián (柯潛) and others were granted the Jinshì degree and various ranks.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Liáng Bǎo (梁珤), Wáng Lái (王來), and others suppressed the Miáo (苗) people of Píngyuè (平越),
and presented captives in the capital.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Wǎlà (瓦剌) raided the Mǎyíng (馬營) of Xuānfǔ (宣府);
an imperial order dispatched Assistant General Shí Biāo (石彪) and others to patrol the border.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Shí Hēng (石亨) was ordered to select and train troops from the capital garrisons,
and Minister Shí Pú (石璞) was appointed overall commander of military affairs.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐsì,
Gùyuán (固原) was fortified.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùchén, the first day of the month,
there was supposed to be a solar eclipse, but it was not seen.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
an imperial edict ordered the various guards in Guìzhōu (貴州) to improve garrison farms.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Wùshēn,
the Miáo people of Pǔdìng (普定), Yǒngníng (永寧), and Bìjié (畢節) rebelled again;
Liáng Bǎo and others kept their troops there to suppress them.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénshēn,
there was an earthquake in Nánjīng (南京).
On the day Xīnsì,
the afternoon court audience (wǔcháo) was reinstated.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
officials were prohibited from being reappointed (qǐfù) to former posts after mourning or retirement.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
tax grain in disaster-stricken Shānxī (山西) was remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Wáng Yīníng (王一寧), Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites, and Xiāo Zī (蕭鎡), Libationer (jìjiǔ), were concurrently appointed Academicians of the Hànlín Academy,
stationed in the Wényuān Pavilion,
and participated in military affairs.
That month,
Yěxiān (也先) assassinated his lord, Tuōtuō Bùhuā (脫脫不花).
That year,
Ānnán (安南), Zhōngshān (中山) of Liúqiú (琉球), Wǎlà (瓦剌), and Hāmì (哈密) presented tribute.
In the third year, spring, first month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Liú Guǎnghéng (劉廣衡), Vice Censor-in-Chief (fùdūyùshǐ), reviewed prisoners in Nánjīng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Jīn Lián (金濂), Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, was imprisoned for violating an imperial edict,
but was soon released.
In the third month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Máo Fúshòu (毛福壽) campaigned against the Bāmǎ (巴馬) Miáo people in Húguǎng (湖廣),
and conquered them.
In the summer, fifth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Crown Prince Jiànshēn (見深) was deposed and made Prince of Yí (沂王);
Imperial Prince Jiànjì (見濟) was made Crown Prince.
Empress Wāng (汪) was deposed,
and Crown Prince's mother Háng (杭) was made Empress.
The Grand Emperor's sons, Jiànqīng (見清) was enfeoffed as Prince Róng (榮王),
and Jiànchún (見淳) as Prince Xǔ (許王).
A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Shāwān (沙灣) dike was completed.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
migrants in Hénán (河南) who returned to their occupations
were granted food rations for five years, according to the size of their families.
On the day Yǐsì,
one descendant each of the Yán (顏) and Mèng (孟) families was given official positions.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐhài,
the practice of Grand Coordinators from various provinces coming to the capital for discussions was abolished.
That month,
there was heavy rain,
and the river burst its banks at Shāwān.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Wáng Áo (王翺), Left Censor-in-Chief (zuǒdūyùshǐ), was appointed overall commander of military affairs in the two Guǎng (Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī).
On the day Rén'yín,
Wáng Yīníng died.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
relief was provided for flood-stricken Xú (徐) and Yǎn (兗).
On the day Wùchén,
Hóng Yīng (洪英), Censor-in-Chief (dūyùshǐ),
and Ministers Sūn Yuánzhēn (孫原貞) and Xuē Xīlián (薛希璉), among others, were dispatched throughout the empire
to inspect officials.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
relief was provided for flood-stricken prefectures and counties in the two capital regions,
and tax grain was remitted.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
relief was provided for migrants in the Southern Capital region, Hénán, and Shāndōng.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Jiāng Yuān (江淵) was reinstated.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
due to the earthquake in Nánjīng,
the great floods in Liǎnghuái (兩淮),
and the river bursting its banks,
Wáng Wén (王文), Censor-in-Chief, was ordered to inspect and provide relief.
On the day Yǐwèi,
relief was provided for disaster-stricken prefectures and counties in the two capital regions, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Fújiàn (福建), Guǎngxī (廣西), Jiāngxī (江西), and Liáodōng (遼東).
In the intercalary month, on the day Kuǐwèi,
the silver mines of Chǔzhōu (處州) were opened.
That month,
bandits rose in Fújiàn.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Wùxū,
Wáng Wén, Left Censor-in-Chief, was concurrently appointed Academician of the Hànlín Academy,
stationed in the Wényuān Pavilion,
and participated in military affairs.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Grand Commissioner (dūdū) Sūn Táng (孫鏜) and Assistant Military Commissioner (qiānshì) Shí Biāo (石彪) jointly defended Dàtóng (大同);
Grand Commissioner Concurrently in Charge (dūdū tóngzhī) Wèi Yǐng (衞潁),
and Assistant Military Commissioners Yáng Néng (楊能) and Zhāng Qīn (張欽) jointly defended Xuānfǔ,
to prepare against Yěxiān.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐwèi, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Wùchén,
Grand Commissioner Fāng Yīng (方瑛) pacified the Miáo people of Báishíyá (白石崖).
On the day Jiǎxū,
migrants who had fled from the capital region, Shāndōng, and Shānxī were resettled,
and their taxes and labor services were remitted for five years.
That month,
tax grain in disaster-stricken Shāndōng and Huái-Xú (淮徐) (Huái'ān and Xúzhōu) was remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐsì,
the Tuan Camp (Tuányíng) system was first established,
and Eunuch Ruǎn Ràng (阮讓), Grand Commissioner Yáng Jùn (楊俊), and others were appointed to command separate divisions,
subject to the control of Yú Qiān (于謙), Shí Hēng, Eunuch Liú Yǒngchéng (劉永誠), and Cáo Jíxiáng (曹吉祥).
That month,
autumn grain taxes in disaster-stricken Hénán and Yǒngpíng (永平) were remitted.
That year,
Wǎlà, Zhōngshān of Liúqiú, Zhǎowā (爪哇), Xiāmluó (暹羅), Ānnán, Hāmì, and Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏) came to present tribute.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day Xīnwèi,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Miáo people of Wǔkāi (五開) and Qīnglàng (清浪) rebelled again;
Liáng Bǎo and Wáng Lái campaigned against them.
On the day Gēngxū,
last year's disaster-stricken autumn grain taxes in Jiāngxī were remitted.
In the third month, on the day Wùyín,
the silver mines of Jiànníng (建寧) were opened.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the breach at Shāwān was repaired.
Grain from the Nánjīng granaries was transported to relieve Xúzhōu (徐州).
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngsì,
grain from the Xú (Xúzhōu) and Huái (Huái'ān) granaries was distributed to relieve the starving.
On the day Jǐsì,
Wáng Wén was reinstated.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Xúzhōu suffered another great flood,
and the people grew even more hungry.
Reserved transport grain and salt tax grain were distributed to relieve them.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
grain from the Huái'ān (淮安) granary was distributed to relieve Fèngyáng (鳳陽).
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Shāwān River burst its banks again.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénchén,
Hé Wényuān (何文淵), Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was imprisoned due to the words of Supervising Secretary Lín Cōng (林聰),
and was soon ordered to retire.
On the day Xīnhài,
unburied bodies at Tǔmù (土木), Dàtóng, and Zǐjīngguān (紫荊關) were interred.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Gēngchén,
non-essential public works were suspended.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
relief was provided for the famine in Hénán.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Yěxiān declared himself Khagan.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Gēngyín,
an imperial edict ordered all garrison commanders and Grand Coordinators across the empire to supervise agriculture and sericulture.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Xú Yǒuzhēn (徐有貞), Exhorter (yùdé), was appointed Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief,
to manage the breach in the Shāwān River.
On the day Wùxū,
Yěxiān sent envoys.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Crown Prince Jiànjì (見濟) died.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
tax grain in disaster-stricken Shāndōng was remitted.
On the day Yǐsì,
the border armies were rewarded.
That year,
Zhōngshān of Liúqiú, Ānnán, Zhǎowā, Rìběn (日本), Zhànchéng (占城), Hāmì, and Wǎlà presented tribute.
In the fifth year, in spring, the first month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
the Huánghé cleared,
from Lóngmén to Ruìchéng.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
great sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were performed in the Southern Suburb.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the silver mines of Fúzhōu and Jiànníng were abolished.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Marquis of Píngjiāng Chén Yù and Academician Jiāng Yuān pacified and rehabilitated the disaster-stricken soldiers and civilians of Shāndōng and Hénán.
In the second month, on the *yǐsì* day,
due to untimely rain and sunshine,
an imperial edict called for self-reflection and reform,
and sought forthright counsel.
In the third month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Sūn Xián and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree and official positions of various ranks.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Academician Jiāng Yuān relieved the famine-stricken people of Huáiběi.
Wáng Wén provided relief to Nánjī.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Mǎ Áng, Grand Coordinator of Liǎngguǎng and Vice Censor-in-Chief, defeated the Yáo people of Lóngshuǐ.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Miǎndiàn seized and presented Sījīfā.
In summer, the fourth month, on the first day (*rénwǔ*),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Fāng Yīng defeated the Miáo people of Cǎotáng,
and Fāng Yīng was enfeoffed as the Earl of Nánhé.
In the fifth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Zhāng Lún, Director in the Ministry of Rites, and Zhōng Tóng, Censor, were imprisoned by the Jǐnyīwèi for requesting the restoration of Prince Yí as Crown Prince.
In the sixth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
prisoners were reviewed.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Nánjī.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
provincial governors (*xúnfǔ*) from throughout the empire were again ordered to go to the Capital for discussions.
In the ninth month, on the *rénxū* day,
over two million *shí* of grain tribute from Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Chángzhōu, Yángzhōu, Hángzhōu, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu were remitted.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Liú Guǎnghéng, Vice Censor-in-Chief, was appointed Provincial Governor of Zhèjiāng and Fújiàn,
specifically tasked with suppressing rebels.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
the weaving and purchasing operations in Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Chángzhōu, and Zhènjiāng were abolished.
In the twelfth month,
disaster-stricken tax grain in Nánjī and Zhèjiāng was remitted.
That year,
Ānnán, Liúqiú Zhōngshān, and Zhǎowā presented tribute.
Yěxiān was killed by Zhīyuàn Ālà.
In the sixth year, in spring, the first month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
great sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were performed in the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Eunuch Wáng Chéng, together with judicial officials and the Department of Criminal Justice, reviewed prisoners.
Lǐ Mào, Junior Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, and others reviewed prisoners in Nánjīng and Zhèjiāng.
In summer, the fourth month, on the first day (*bǐngzǐ*),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *xīnsì* day,

an imperial edict instructed the Ministries of Revenue and War, and the provincial governors (*fǔ*), judicial commissioners (*àn*), and Three Judicial Commissioners of the Liǎng Jī, Shāndōng, Hénán, Zhèjiāng, and Húguǎng, to itemize matters for generous relief,
and to abolish all non-urgent affairs.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
prayers for rain were offered in the Southern Suburb.
In the sixth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Zhū Tǐng, a descendant of the Sòng Confucian Zhū Xī, was appointed Hereditary Erudite of the Five Classics in the Hànlín Academy.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the river breached its banks at Kāifēng.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the dike at Shāwān, where the river had breached, was completed.
On the *gēngyín* day,
because portents of disaster were frequently seen in Nánjīng,
an imperial edict instructed all officials to reflect and reform.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
Liáo Zhuāng, Junior Minister of the Nánjīng Court of Judicial Review, was flogged before the palace gate for requesting the restoration of Prince Yí as Crown Prince;
Zhāng Lún and Zhōng Tóng were also flogged in prison,
and Zhōng Tóng died.
In the ninth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
over one million *shí* of rice and wheat were distributed to relieve famine-stricken people in Sūzhōu and Sōngjiāng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
disaster-stricken tax grain in Shǎnxī was remitted.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Fāng Yīng, Earl of Nánhé, was appointed General Who Pacifies the Man and Regional Commander,
to suppress the Miáo people in Húguǎng.
In the twelfth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
disaster-stricken autumn grain in Nánjī was remitted.
That year,
Liúqiú Zhōngshān, Xiānluó, Hāmì, and Mǎnlàjiā presented tribute.
In the seventh year, in spring, the first month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Shí Pú, Minister, pacified the soldiers and civilians of Húguǎng.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
great sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were performed in the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
the Empress died.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
construction of her imperial mausoleum began.
In the third month, on the *wùyín* day,
disaster-stricken tax grain in Yúnnán was remitted.
In summer, the fifth month, on the *wùyín* day,
due to floods, droughts, and other disasters,
an imperial edict instructed all officials, both inside and outside the court, to reflect and reform.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Zhōu Miǎn, a descendant of the Sòng Confucian Zhōu Dūnyí, was appointed Hereditary Erudite of the Five Classics in the Hànlín Academy.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
Empress Sùxiào was buried.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
famine relief was provided in Jiāngxī.
In the twelfth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Fāng Yīng severely defeated the Miáo people in Húguǎng.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
flood relief was provided in the Capital region, Shāndōng, and Hénán.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor was unwell,
and the New Year's Day court audience for the following year was suspended.
That winter,
disaster-stricken tax grain in the Capital region and Shāndōng was remitted,
and overdue taxes were waived.
That year,
Liúqiú Zhōngshān, Sāmǎ'érhǎn, and Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the eighth year, in spring, the first month, on the *wùchén* day,
disaster-stricken tax grain in Jiāngxī was remitted.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Emperor, afflicted by illness, lodged in the Palace of Fasting in the Southern Suburb.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the officials requested the establishment of a Crown Prince,
but this was not granted.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Shí Hēng, Marquis of Wǔqīng, Xú Yǒuzhēn, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and others welcomed the Retired Emperor back to the throne.
In the second month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
the deposed emperor was made Prince of Chéng,
and moved to the Western Palace;
Empress Dowager Wú and all below her retained their former titles.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the prince died in the Western Palace,
aged thirty.
His posthumous title was Lì.
The imperial mausoleum he had constructed was demolished,
and he was buried with the rites of a prince in the Western Hills,
with 200 households of the Wǔchéng Central Guard Army assigned to guard it.
In the eleventh year of Chénghuà, in the twelfth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"My uncle, Prince of Chéng, ascended the throne,
suppressed difficulties and preserved the state,
and secured the imperial ancestral temples and altars of state,
for nearly eight years.
At the time of his critical illness,
treacherous officials, greedy for merit,
groundlessly slandered and framed him,
requesting that his imperial title be stripped.
The late Emperor soon learned of his wrongful treatment,
and frequently regretted it,
subsequently bringing those treacherous officials to justice;
unfortunately, he passed away
before he could rectify the situation.
I, cherishing my kinsman,
shall fulfill my predecessor's will:
his imperial title shall be restored,
and his posthumous title discussed and reported."
Thereupon, an exalted posthumous title was conferred.
An imperial edict instructed the relevant authorities to repair his imperial mausoleum,
and his sacrifices and offerings were to be performed as for other imperial mausoleums.
A eulogy states: Emperor Jǐng, in a time of turmoil,
received the mandate to assume regency,
and soon officially ascended the great throne to secure the people's hearts;
this was a provisional measure that proved to be correct.
He earnestly appointed the capable and virtuous,
and diligently governed;
though powerful invaders penetrated deeply, the imperial ancestral temples and altars of state were pacified,
and his achievement of restoration was truly great.
However, he eagerly sought to replace the heir apparent,
deeply imprisoned [the Retired Emperor] in the Southern Palace,
denied him court audiences,
and was utterly indifferent to their kinship.
Ultimately, when he was in the Palace of Fasting, afflicted by illness,
petty men seized the opportunity to act covertly;
the incident arose suddenly,
and he was unable to conclude his reign with a good reputation.
What a pity!

In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐsì,
famine relief was provided in Húguǎng.
In this year, Hāmì, Shūqiú Zhōngshān, Xīlánshān, and Mǎlájiā paid tribute.
In the spring of the fourth year, in the first month, on the day Dīnghài,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburban altar.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Shí Hēng was imprisoned for his crimes,
and soon died.
In the second month, on the day Rénzǐ,
the Tuáng captured Wúzhōu.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Shí Biāo was executed in the marketplace.
In the third month, on the day Gēngchén,
Wáng Yīkuí and others were granted the Jinshì degree and official appointments of varying ranks.
On the day Wùxū,
autumn grain taxes for disaster-stricken Nánjī were remitted.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
eunuchs were separately dispatched to supervise silver taxes in Zhèjiāng, Yúnnán, Fújiàn, and Sìchuān.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Xiāng Wáng Zhānshàn came to court.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
autumn grain taxes for disaster-stricken Jīnnèi and Zhèjiāng were remitted.
On the day Jǐhài,
the eunuch supervision of silk weaving in Sūzhōu and Hángzhōu was abolished.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐhài,
tax grain for disaster-stricken Húguǎng was remitted.
In the autumn of the seventh month, on the first day Yǐhài,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
from the fifth month until this month, it rained continuously.
The Huái River burst its banks,
submerging civilian and military fields and dwellings.
Envoys were dispatched to provide relief and consolation.
In the eighth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Bólái invaded in three routes.
The Grand Commander of Dàtóng, Lǐ Wén, and the Grand Commander of Xuānfǔ, Yáng Néng, repelled them.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Bólái entered Yànmén,
plundering the various prefectures of Xīn, Dài, and Shuò.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngchén,
Bólái besieged the Right Guard of Dàtóng.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Earl of Fúníng, Zhū Yǒng,
and the Military Commissioners Bái Yù and Bào Zhèng garrisoned the border of Xuānfǔ.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
autumn grain taxes for disaster-stricken Jiāngxī were remitted.
In the winter of the tenth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor reviewed the cavalry archery of the capital garrison commanders in Xīyuàn.
On the day Wùchén,
the Emperor visited Nánhǎizi.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor reviewed the cavalry archery of the military officials accompanying the drill in Xīyuàn.
In the intercalary month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor visited Zhèngcūnbà,
and reviewed armor and military horses.
In this year,
Shūqiú Zhōngshān, Ānnán, Zhānchéng, Zhǎowā, Hāmì, and Wūsīzàng paid tribute.
In the spring of the fifth year, in the first month, on the day Gēngxū,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburban altar.
In the second month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
tax grain for disaster-stricken Shāndōng was remitted.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Assistant Military Commissioner, Yán Biāo, was appointed General for Conquering Barbarians,
serving as Grand Commander,
to suppress the Yáo bandits in Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī.
In the third month, on the day Rénzǐ,
tax grain for disaster-stricken Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Chángzhōu, and Zhènjiāng was remitted.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Grand Commander of Húguǎng and Guìzhōu, Lǐ Zhèn, joined forces with the Guǎngxī army to suppress the Yáo and Tuáng,
and completely routed them.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the day Guǐsì,
the Vice Minister of War, Bái Guī, was dispatched to supervise the various borders of Shǎnxī
to attack Bólái.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
autumn grain taxes for disaster-stricken Hénán were remitted.
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Bólái invaded Héxī,
and the government army suffered a defeat.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Minister of War, Mǎ Áng, was appointed supreme commander of military affairs,
and the Earl of Huáiníng, Sūn Táng, was appointed Grand Commander,
to lead the capital garrison army to repel them.
In the autumn of the seventh month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the supreme commander of the capital garrison and Grand Eunuch Cáo Jíxiáng and the Earl of Zhāowǔ, Cáo Qīn, rebelled.
The Censor-in-Chief of the Left, Kòu Shēn, and the Marquis of Gōngshùn, Wú Jǐn, were killed.
The Earl of Huáiníng, Sūn Táng, led troops to suppress and pacify them.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Cáo Jíxiáng was dismembered in the marketplace,
and his clan was exterminated.
His confederates, Tāng Xù and others, were all executed.
On the day Dīngwèi,
tax grain for disaster-stricken Nánjī was remitted.
On the day Gēngxū,
a general amnesty was proclaimed,
and frank remonstrance was encouraged.
On the day Dīngsì,
the river burst its banks at Kāifēng.
The Vice Minister, Xuē Yuǎn, went to manage the situation.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Military Commissioner Féng Zōng was appointed Grand Commander
to repel the invaders at Héxī.
The Vice Minister of War, Bái Guī, and the Vice Censor-in-Chief, Wáng Hóng, participated in military deliberations.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Bólái submitted a letter requesting peace.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénxū,
there was an earthquake with sound in the capital.
In the winter of the tenth month, on the day Rénshēn,
due to military operations on the western frontier,
it was ordered that commoners and gentry in Hénán, Shānxī, and Shǎnxī who presented horses would be granted official caps and belts.
In the eleventh month, on the first day Dīngyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Rénxū,
the Emperor visited Nánhǎizi.
In this year,
Ānnán, Shūqiú Zhōngshān, Hāmì, and Yìlìbālǐ paid tribute.
In the spring of the sixth year, in the first month, on the day Dīngwèi,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburban altar.
On the day Wùshēn,
Bólái sent envoys to pay tribute.
In the second month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
an edict was issued to Bólái.
In the third month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Féng Zōng and others were recalled.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the day Rénshēn,
autumn grain taxes for disaster-stricken Hénán were remitted.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Yán Biāo pacified all the Yáo in Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī.
On the day Jǐwèi,
autumn grain taxes for disaster-stricken Shǎnxī were remitted.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùchén,
Huái Wáng Qí Quán came to court.
In the autumn of the seventh month,
Huái’ān experienced a sea overflow.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
the Empress Dowager passed away.
In the winter of the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Empress Xiàogōngzhāng was interred.
In this year,
Liúqiú Zhōngshān, Hāmì, Wūsīzàng, and Xiāmluó paid tribute.
In the spring of the seventh year, in the first month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburban altar.
In the second month, on the day Rénxū,
the Grand Mentor Chén Wén was appointed Vice Minister of Rites concurrently Grand Academician of the Hànlín Academy,
and entered the Grand Secretariat to participate in important governmental affairs.
In the third month, on the day Rényín,
there was a drought.
An edict was issued to implement policies of leniency and relief,
and to halt silver mining operations in all locations.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
the Censor for Xuānfǔ and Dàtóng, Lǐ Fān, was arrested
and paraded with a cangue at Cháng’ānmén.
He died soon after.
On the day Bǐngxū,
eunuchs were again dispatched to supervise silk weaving in Sūzhōu and Hángzhōu.
In the fifth month, on the first day Jǐchǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Censor for Liáodōng, Yáng Jìn, was arrested and prosecuted for unauthorized flogging of military officials.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
the Censor for Shānxī, Hán Qí, was arrested
and paraded with a cangue at Cháng’ānmén.
He died a few days later.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the `gēngxū` day,
taxes and grain payments were remitted for disaster-stricken areas in Shǎnxī.
In the intercalary month, on the `jiǎxū` day,
a posthumous title was conferred upon the deposed Empress Hú of Xuānzōng.
On the `wùyín` day,
troops from Húguǎng and Guìzhōu were ordered to unite and suppress the rebellious Miáo of Hóngjiāng.
In the ninth month, on the `jiǎxū` day,
Ōu Xìn, the regional commander of Guǎngdōng, was ordered to join forces with Guǎngxī troops to suppress the Yáo bandits.
In winter, the tenth month, on the `dīngyǒu` day,
relief was provided to the starving in the various prefectures of Xī'ān.
On the `dīngwèi` day,
Wú Zhēn, the Grand Censor Supervising Guǎngxī, was appointed to command all military forces in the two Guǎng provinces
to suppress the Yáo bandits.
In the eleventh month, on the `guǐyǒu` day,
the bandits captured Wúzhōu,
and Sòng Qīn, the retired Provincial Administration Commissioner, died there.
On the `rénwǔ` day,
Lǐ Bīn, the Right Grand Censor, and Lín Cōng, the Vice Grand Censor, were imprisoned in the Jǐnyī Wèi prison.
In the twelfth month, on the `xīnmǎo` day,
Lù Yú, the Minister of Justice,
and Zhōu Xuān and Chéng Xìn, the Vice Ministers, were imprisoned in the Jǐnyī Wèi prison,
and later released.
In this year,
Zhōngshān of Liúqiú, Hāmì, Ānnán, and Wūsīzàng sent tribute.
In the eighth year, spring, the first month, on the `yǐmǎo` day,
the Emperor became ill.
On the `jǐwèi` day,
the Crown Prince began to manage affairs in the Wénhuá Diàn.
On the `jǐsì` day,
the Emperor's illness worsened,
and he issued an edict to abolish the practice of burying palace consorts alive with the deceased.
On the `gēngwǔ` day,
he passed away,
at the age of thirty-eight.
In the second month, on the `yǐwèi` day,
a revered posthumous title was conferred,
the temple name was Yīngzōng,
and he was buried in the Yùlíng Mausoleum.
The eulogy states: Yīngzōng inherited the legacy of Rénzōng and Xuānzōng,
the nation was prosperous,
and the court and populace were tranquil.
Great ministers such as the Three Yángs, Hú Yíng, and Zhāng Fǔ,
who were all meritorious elders from successive reigns,
received the dying Emperor's trust to assist in governance,
and the state's order was not relaxed.
It was only due to Wáng Zhèn's usurpation of power and provocation that
the imperial carriage was forced to relocate.
Yet, after his restoration,
he still remembered him unceasingly;
how deeply he was deluded and infatuated!
He reigned for twenty-four years in total,
without any major harmful policies.
As for conferring a posthumous title on Empress Gōngràng,
releasing the commoners who had been imprisoned,
and abolishing the practice of burying palace consorts alive,
these were acts of great virtue worthy of emulation by later generations.
Collation Notes
Annals, Volume 13: Xiànzōng I
Xiànzōng Jìtiānnìngdàochéngmíngrénjìngchóngwénsùwǔhóngdéshèngxiàochún Huángdì,
whose taboo name was Jiànshēn,
was the eldest son of Yīngzōng.
His mother was Noble Consort Zhōu.
His initial name was Jiànjùn.
When Yīngzōng was detained by the Wǎlà,
the Empress Dowager ordered him to be established as the Crown Prince.
In the third year of Jǐngtài,
he was deposed and made Prince Yí.
In the first year of Tiānshùn,
he was re-established as the Crown Prince,
and his name was changed to Jiànshēn.
In the eighth year of Tiānshùn, in the first month,
Yīngzōng passed away.
On the `yǐhài` day,
he ascended the imperial throne.
The following year was designated as the first year of Chénghuà,
and a general amnesty was granted throughout the empire.
One-third of the land taxes for the following year were remitted.
Internal and external officials guarding Zhèjiāng, Jiāngxī, Fújiàn, Shǎnxī, Línqīng,
and internal officials guarding the various border towns,
who were not present during the Zhèngtǒng era, were all dismissed.
Foreign envoys and secret police officers were all recalled.
In the second month, on the `gēngzǐ` day,
appointments were first made by imperial rescript.
In the third month, on the `jiǎyín` day, the first of the month,
the Empress was honored as Cíyì Huáng Tàihòu,
and Noble Consort Zhōu was honored as Huáng Tàihòu.
On the `wùwǔ` day,
palace women were released.
On the `bǐngyín` day,
the new prison of the Jǐnyī Wèi was demolished.
On the `gēngwǔ` day,
Péng Jiào and others were granted the `jìnshì` degree and official positions with different ranks.
On the `guǐyǒu` day,
the Grand Secretariat and the Nine Ministers were ordered to evaluate the provincial officials across the empire.
On the `wùyín` day,
the Regimental Camps were re-established.
In summer, the fourth month, on the `guǐwèi` day, the first of the month,
there was supposed to be a solar eclipse,
but it was not seen.
In the fifth month, on the `dīngsì` day,
there was a great wind and hailstorm,
and officials were ordered to reflect and reform.
On the `gēngshēn` day,
Emperor Ruì was buried in the Yùlíng Mausoleum.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the `rénshēn` day,
Lady Wú was established as Empress.
In the eighth month, on the `guǐwèi` day,
the imperial lectures (Jīngyán) were held.
On the `jiǎshēn` day,
Confucian scholars were ordered to give daily lectures.
On the `guǐmǎo` day,
Empress Wú was deposed.
Eunuch Niú Yù was imprisoned.
In winter, the tenth month, on the `rénchén` day,
Lady Wáng was established as Empress.
On the `jiǎchén` day,
the martial examination system was established.
In the twelfth month, on the `jiǎchén` day,
minor crimes committed by capital officials were pardoned.
In this year,
bandits rose in great numbers in the two capital regions, Sìchuān, Guǎngdōng, Jīngzhōu, and Xiāngyáng,
making roads impassable.
Ānnán and Wūsīzàng sent tribute.
In the first year of Chénghuà, spring, the first month, on the `yǐmǎo` day,
sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the `jǐwèi` day,
grand sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth in the Southern Suburbs.
On the `jiǎzǐ` day,
Zhào Fǔ, the Co-Administrator of the Chief Military Commission, was made General Conquering Barbarians,
serving as commander-in-chief,
and Hán Yǒng, the Grand Censor, assisted in military affairs,
to suppress the rebellious Yáo of Guǎngxī.
In the second month, on the `wùzǐ` day,
sacrifices were offered to the Gods of Land and Grain.
On the `jiǎwǔ` day,
the ritual plowing of the ceremonial field was performed.
In the third month, on the `gēngxū` day,
the Shāndōuzhǎng Mán of Sìchuān rebelled.
On the `dīngsì` day,
sacrifices were offered to Confucius, the Former Master.
In summer, the fifth month, on the `xīnyǒu` day,
there was a great hailstorm.
On the `rénxū` day,
the Emperor withdrew from the main hall and reduced his meals,
ordering officials to reflect and reform.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the `jǐyǒu` day,
three-tenths of the military garrison farm taxes throughout the empire were remitted.
On the `jiǎzǐ` day,
relief was provided to the starving in the two capital regions, Zhèjiāng, and Hénán.
In the eighth month, on the `dīngchǒu` day,
Shěn Yì, the Vice Minister of Public Works, and Wú Chēn, the Grand Censor, provided relief to the starving people in the two capital regions.
On the `xīnsì` day,
unburied corpses were interred.
On the `gēngyín` day,
Máolǐhái attacked Yánsuí,
and Fáng Néng, the commander-in-chief, defeated him.
In winter, the twelfth month, on the `guǐmǎo` day,
Zhū Yǒng, Earl of Fǔníng, was made General Pacifying Barbarians,
serving as commander-in-chief,
Eunuch Táng Shèn supervised the army,
and Bái Guī, the Minister of Public Works, oversaw military affairs,
to suppress the bandits of Jīngzhōu and Xiāngyáng.
In this month,
Hán Yǒng decisively defeated the Yáo of the Dàténg Xiá,
and the gorge was renamed
`Duànténg`.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Hāmì, Zhǎowā, and Wūsīzàng sent tribute.
In the second year, spring, the first month, on the `wùshēn` day,
the Regimental Camps were abolished.
On the `yǐmǎo` day,
grand sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth in the Southern Suburbs.
On the `xīnyǒu` day,
the spirit tablet of Yīngzōng was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In the second month, on the `guǐwèi` day,
Zōu Gàn, the Vice Minister of Rites, inspected the starving people in the capital region.
In the third month, on the `jiǎchén` day,
Luó Lún and others were granted the `jìnshì` degree and official positions with different ranks.
On the `jǐyǒu` day,
Lǐ Xián's father died,
and he requested to observe the full mourning period,
but this was not granted.
On the `yǐmǎo` day,
Zhū Yǒng decisively defeated Liú Tōng, the bandit of Jīngzhōu and Xiāngyáng, at Nánzhāng.
In the intercalary month, on the `guǐyǒu` day,
relief was provided to the starving in the Southern Capital Region.
On the `yǐwèi` day,
Zhū Yǒng attacked and captured Liú Tōng;
his accomplice Shí Lóng fled,
and subsequently plundered Sìchuān.
In the summer, fifth month, on the day *Guǐyǒu*,
Reviser Luó Lún (羅倫) was demoted to Ti Jǔ (提舉) of Fújiàn (福建) Municipal Shipping Office for criticizing the reappointment of Lǐ Xián (李賢).
On the day *Jǐmǎo*,
an edict was issued prohibiting the encroachment upon or damage to the tombs of ancient emperors, loyal ministers, martyrs, and famous worthies.
In the sixth month, on the day *Jiǎchén*,
Zhào Fǔ's (趙輔) army returned.
On the day *Yǐsì*,
three-tenths of this year's military provisions across the empire were remitted.
On the day *Rénzǐ*,
Yáng Xìn (楊信) was appointed Pínglǔ Jiāngjūn (平虜將軍),
serving as Zǒngbīngguān (總兵官).
Eunuch Péi Dāng (裴當) supervised military affairs,
to defend against invaders in Yánsuī (延綏).
In autumn, seventh month, on the day *Xīnsì*,
the Emperor's younger brother Jiànzhì (見治) was enfeoffed as Xīn Wáng (忻王),
and Jiànpèi (見沛) as Huī Wáng (徽王).
On the day *Wùxū*,
Máolǐhái (毛里孩) attacked Gùyuán (固原).
In the eighth month, on the day *Dīngsì*,
Máolǐhái attacked Níngxià (寧夏),
and Dū Zhǐhuī (都指揮) Jiāo Zhèng (焦政) died in battle.
On the day *Dīngmǎo*,
an imperial decree was issued to offer sacrifices to Yú Qiān (于謙),
and his son Miǎn (冕) was restored to office.
In winter, tenth month, on the day *Dīngwèi*,
Zhū Yǒng (朱永) attacked and captured Shí Lóng (石龍).
The rebels were pacified,
and Zhū Yǒng's (朱永) noble rank was advanced to Hóu (侯).
In the twelfth month, on the day *Jiǎyín*,
Lǐ Xián (李賢) died.
On the day *Bǐngchén*,
Liú Dìngzhī (劉定之), Shà qīng (少卿) of the Tàicháng Sì (太常寺) and concurrently Shìdú Xuéshì (侍讀學士) of the Hànlín Yuàn (翰林院), joined the cabinet to participate in state affairs.
In this month,
the bandits of Duànténg Xiá (斷藤峽) rebelled again.
In this year,
Hāmì (哈密), Liúqiú (琉球), Ānnán (安南), Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏), and Wǎlà (瓦剌) paid tribute.
In the third year, spring, first month, on the day *Jǐmǎo*,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were held at the Southern Suburb.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
Fǔníng Hóu (撫寧侯) Zhū Yǒng (朱永) was appointed Pínghú Jiāngjūn (平胡將軍),
serving as Zǒngbīngguān (總兵官),
to join Yáng Xìn (楊信) in an expedition against Máolǐhái (毛里孩).
In the second month, on the day *Dīngyǒu*, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day *Dīngsì*,
Húguǎng (湖廣) Zǒngbīngguān (總兵官) Lǐ Zhèn (李震) attacked and defeated the Miáo (苗) people of Jìngzhōu (靖州).
In the third month, on the day *Wùchén*,
Shāng Lù (商輅) was summoned to serve as Bīngbù Shìláng (兵部侍郎),
and re-entered the cabinet.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
Máolǐhái (毛里孩) attacked Dàtóng (大同).
On the day *Xīnsì*,
the silver mines in Zhèjiāng (浙江), Fújiàn (福建), Sìchuān (四川), and Yúnnán (雲南) were reopened,
and put under the charge of palace eunuchs.
In summer, fourth month,
Sìchuān (四川) experienced frequent earthquakes,
from the sixth month of the previous year until this month.
On the day *Yǐsì*,
prisoners were reviewed.
On the day *Guǐchǒu*,
the Tuányíng (團營) military organization was re-established.
In the sixth month, on the day *Wùshēn*,
lightning struck the Wǔmén (午門) of Nánjīng (南京).
An imperial edict ordered all ministers to reflect and reform.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
Xiāngchéng Bó (襄城伯) Lǐ Jǐn (李瑾) was appointed Zhēngyí Jiāngjūn (征夷將軍),
serving as Zǒngbīngguān (總兵官).
Bīngbù Shàngshū (兵部尚書) Chéng Xìn (程信) supervised military affairs,
and Eunuch Liú Héng (劉恆) was the supervising censor,
to suppress the Shāndūzhǎng Mán (山都掌蠻) people.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day *Yǐyǒu*,
the collection of supplies in Hénán (河南) was suspended.
In the ninth month, on the day *Xīnwèi*,
relief was provided for the famine in Húguǎng (湖廣) and Jiāngxī (江西).
In winter, twelfth month, on the day *Gēngzǐ*,
Zuǒ Shùzǐ (左庶子) Lí Chún (黎淳) brought up the matter of the dethronement and establishment of the Jǐngtài (景泰) Emperor.
The Emperor said:
"The matter of Jǐngtài (景泰) is in the past,
We do not dwell on it,
and moreover, it is not something that a minister should speak of."
He was severely reprimanded.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
Biānxiū (編修) Zhāng Mào (章懋) and Huáng Zhòngzhāo (黃仲昭),
and Jiǎntǎo (檢討) Zhuāng [●], were flogged
and demoted to various different posts.
In this month,
Chéng Xìn (程信) defeated the Shāndūzhǎng Mán (山都掌蠻) people,
pacifying them.
In this year,
Liúqiú (琉球), Hāmì (哈密), Zhànchéng (占城), Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏) paid tribute.
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮) offered sea eagles and white magpies,
but was ordered not to make such offerings.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day *Jiǎxū*,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were held at the Southern Suburb.
In the third month, on the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
the autumn grain tax for disaster-stricken Húguǎng (湖廣) was remitted.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
an imperial edict prohibited powerful families inside and outside the capital from arbitrarily requesting land.
In summer, fourth month, on the day *Dīngsì*,
prisoners were reviewed.
Chén Wén (陳文) died.
In the fifth month, on the day *Guǐwèi*,
envoys were dispatched to review prisoners throughout the empire.
In the sixth month, on the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
the autumn grain tax for disaster-stricken Jiāngxī (江西) was remitted.
On the day *Xīnhài*,
the Kaichéng (開城) bandit Mǎnjùn (滿俊) rebelled.
Shǎnxī (陝西) Zǒngbīngguān (總兵官) Níngyuǎn Bó (寧遠伯) Rèn Shòu (任壽) and Xúnfǔ Dū Yùshǐ (巡撫都御史) Chén Jià (陳价) went to suppress him.
On the day *Jiǎyín*,
Empress Dowager Cíyì (慈懿皇太后) passed away.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day *Guǐyǒu*,
Dū Dū Tóngzhī (都督同知) Liú Yù (劉玉) was appointed Pínglǔ Fùjiāngjūn (平虜副將軍),
serving as Zǒngbīngguān (總兵官).
Eunuch Liú Xiáng (劉祥) was the supervising censor,
and Fù Dū Yùshǐ (副都御史) Xiàng Zhōng (項忠) was the general supervisor of military affairs,
to suppress Mǎnjùn (滿俊).
In the eighth month, on the day *Guǐsì*,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
Zhū Yǒng (朱永) replaced Liú Yù (劉玉) as Zǒngbīngguān (總兵官).
In this month,
Rèn Shòu (任壽), Chén Jià (陳价), and Níngxià (寧夏) Zǒngbīngguān (總兵官) Guǎngyì Bó (廣義伯) Wú Cóng (吳琮) fought Mǎnjùn (滿俊),
suffering a defeat.
Dū Zhǐhuī (都指揮) Jiǎng Tài (蔣泰) and Shēn Chéng (申澄) were killed.
In the ninth month, on the day *Gēngshēn*,
Empress Xiàozhuāng Ruì (孝莊睿皇后) was buried at Yùlíng (裕陵).
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
relief was provided for the famine in Shǎnxī (陝西).
On the day *Rénshēn*,
due to earthquakes and celestial anomalies, an imperial edict was issued, in which the Emperor blamed himself,
and ordered all ministers to reflect and reform.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
Gěishìzhōng (給事中) Dǒng Mín (董旻), Yùshǐ (御史) Hú Shēn (胡深) and nine others requested the dismissal of Shāng Lù (商輅) and Lǐbù Shàngshū (禮部尚書) Yáo Kuí (姚夔).
They were imprisoned
and flogged.
In winter, tenth month, on the day *Yǐwèi*,
Xiàng Zhōng (項忠) defeated the bandits at Shíchéng (石城).
Fúqiāng Bó (伏羌伯) Máo Zhōng (毛忠) died in battle.
In the eleventh month,
Xiàng Zhōng (項忠) attacked and captured Mǎnjùn (滿俊),
who was sent to the capital
and executed.
On the day *Rénxū*,
Máolǐhái (毛里孩) attacked Liáodōng (遼東).
Zhǐhuī (指揮) Hú Zhēn (胡珍) died in battle.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Jǐyǒu*,
Liáodōng (遼東) Zǒngbīngguān (總兵官) Zhào Shèng (趙勝) reported:
"On the sixth day of the eleventh month,
over a thousand barbarian bandits attacked the camp of Zhǐhuī (指揮) Fù Bīn (傅斌).
Zhǐhuī (指揮) Hú Zhēn (胡珍) led troops to reinforce,
but was shot and killed by the bandits."
Máolǐhái (毛里孩) attacked Yánsuī (延綏).
Dū Zhǐhuī Qiānshì (都指揮僉事) Xǔ Níng (許寧) defeated him.
In this year,
Liúqiú (琉球), Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏), Hāmì (哈密), Rìběn (日本), and Mǎnlàjiā (滿剌加) paid tribute.
In the fifth year, spring, first month, on the day *Yǐchǒu*,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were held at the Southern Suburb.
In the third month, on the day *Xīnchǒu*,
Zhāng Shēng (張昇) and other successful candidates in the imperial examinations were granted the title of Jìnshì (進士) and other ranks.
In summer, fifth month, on the day *Xīnchǒu*,
Lǐbù Shìláng (禮部侍郎) Wàn Ān (萬安) concurrently served as Hànlín Yuàn Xuéshì (翰林院學士),
and joined the cabinet to participate in state affairs.
In the sixth month, on the day *Guǐchǒu*, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
prisoners were reviewed.
In autumn, eighth month, on the day *Xīnyǒu*,
Liú Dìngzhī (劉定之) died.
In winter, eleventh month, on the day *Yǐwèi*,
Máolǐhái (毛里孩) attacked Yánsuī (延綏).
In the winter of this year,
Āluōchū (阿羅出) moved into and resided in the Hétào (河套) region.
Liúqiú (琉qiú), Hāmì (哈密), Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏), Mǎnlàjiā (滿剌加), Ānnán (安南), and Tǔlǔfān (土魯番) paid tribute.
In the sixth year, spring, first month, on the day *Jǐchǒu*,
grand sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were held at the Southern Suburb.
On the day *Jǐhài*,
Dàtóng (大同) Zǒngbīngguān (總兵官) Yáng Xìn (楊信) defeated Máolǐhái (毛里孩) at Húcháigōu (胡柴溝).
In the second month, on the day *Xīnwèi*,
Dàlǐ Sì Shà qīng (大理寺少卿) Sòng Mín (宋旻),
Shìláng (侍郎) Zēng Huī (曾翬), Yuán Jié (原傑), Huáng Chēn (黃琛),
and Fù Dū Yùshǐ (副都御史) Téng Zhāo (滕昭) inspected Jīnán (畿南), Zhèjiāng (浙江), Hénán (河南), Sìchuān (四川), and Fújiàn (福建),
to investigate officials
and inquire about the sufferings of the military and common people.
