For other directly administered provinces that had Xúnfǔ (巡撫) and other officials,
it was ordered that they should do the same.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
prayers for rain were offered at the suburban altar.
On the day *Wùyín*,
relief was provided for the famine in Guǎngxī (廣西).
In the third month, on the day *Jiǎshēn*,
the disaster-stricken tax grain in Húguǎng (湖廣) and Shāndōng (山東) was remitted.
On the day *Rényín*,
an imperial edict ordered military agricultural colonies (Túntián 屯田) in Yánsuī (延綏).
Zhū Yǒng (朱永) was appointed Pínglǔ Jiāngjūn (平虜將軍),
serving as Zǒngbīngguān (總兵官).
Eunuchs Fù Gōng (傅恭) and Gù Héng (顧恆) were supervising censors,
and Wáng Yuè (王越) participated in military consultations,
to defend against Āluōchū (阿羅出) in Yánsuī (延綏).
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
due to prolonged drought, wind, and haze, an imperial edict commanded officials to cultivate self-reflection.
On the day Wùchén,
an imperial edict instructed judicial organs to be prudent in criminal cases.
Grand Eunuch Huái'ēn (懷恩), together with the judicial organs, reviewed prisoners.
From then on, every five years, an internal palace official was sent to review prisoners as a regular practice.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Yìsīmǎyīn (亦思馬因) invaded Xuānfǔ (宣府).
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Wāng Zhí (汪直) was appointed supervisor of military affairs,
and Wáng Yuè (王越) was appointed General Pacifying Barbarians,
serving as Commander-in-Chief
to resist them.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Jiǎxū,
autumn grain taxes were remitted for the disaster-stricken Southern Zhílì (南畿).
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
an order was issued that all local Garrison Commanders-in-Chief (總兵) and Grand Coordinators (巡撫) were to follow the command of Wāng Zhí (汪直) and Wáng Yuè (王越).
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Rénxū,
famine relief was provided in Hénán (河南).
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùzǐ,
one-third of the silver from Tàicāng (太倉) was transferred to the inner treasury.
This year,
Ānnán (安南), Zhànchéng (占城), Mǎlājiā (滿剌加), and Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏) paid tribute.
Lí Hào (黎灝) of Ānnán (安南) invaded the Luáoguō Xuānwèisī (老撾宣慰司),
and an imperial edict was bestowed to admonish him.
In the eighteenth year, spring, first month, on the day Rénwǔ,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Gēngyín,
Liú Jí (劉吉) was reinstated.
In the third month, on the first day Jǐsì,
famine relief was provided in Southern Zhílì (南畿).
On the day Rénshēn,
the Western Depot (西廠) was abolished.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Hǎnshèn (罕慎) recaptured Hāmì (哈密) city.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
summer taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken Shānxī (山西).
In the fifth month,
disaster taxes and grain were remitted for Shāndōng (山東) and Southern Zhílì (南畿).
In the sixth month, on the day Rényín,
Yìsīmǎyīn (亦思馬因) invaded Yánsuī (延綏).
Wāng Zhí (汪直) and Wáng Yuè (王越) dispatched troops to resist and defeat him.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
envoys were sent to provide famine relief in the capital region (畿內) and Shāndōng (山東).
On the day Xīnyǒu,
disaster taxes and grain were remitted for Hénán (河南).
In the intercalary month, on the day Rénshēn,
Assistant Censor Yìng Shíyòng (應時用) requested the dismissal of the internal palace official overseeing imperial porcelain production in Ráozhōu (饒州).
He was imprisoned,
but was redeemed and restored to his post.
In the winter, eleventh month,
autumn grain taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken capital region (畿內), Shǎnxī (陝西), and Liáodōng (遼東).
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
the imperial composition Wénhuá Dàxùn (文華大訓) was completed.
This year,
Liúqiú (琉球), Hāmì (哈密), Xiāmluó (暹羅), Tǔlúfān (土魯番), and Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏) paid tribute.
In the nineteenth year, spring, first month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
In the third month, on the day Bǐngchén,
disaster taxes and grain were remitted for Húguǎng (湖廣).
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
disaster taxes and grain were remitted for Hénán (河南).
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐhài,
Wāng Zhí (汪直) was found guilty
and transferred to the Imperial Horse Bureau (御馬監) in Nánjīng (南京).
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Chén Zhèng (陳政) defeated the Yáo (瑤) people in Guǎngxī (廣西).
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the Little Prince (小王子) from beyond the northern frontier invaded Dàtóng (大同).
On the day Guǐmáo,
Commander-in-Chief Xǔ Níng (許寧) resisted them
but suffered a defeat.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Zhū Yǒng (朱永) was appointed Grand General Pacifying the North (鎮朔大將軍),
serving as Commander-in-Chief,
leading the capital troops to resist them.
In the eighth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the invaders attacked Xuānfǔ (宣府).
Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Qín Hóng (秦紘) and Commander-in-Chief Zhōu Yù (周玉) resisted and repelled them.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Vice Minister of Revenue Lǐ Yǎn (李衍) and Vice Minister of Justice Hé Qiáoxīn (何喬新) inspected the border passes.
On the day Rénshēn,
Wāng Zhí (汪直) was demoted to Imperial Guard Attendant (奉御),
and his associates, Wáng Yuè (王越), Dài Jìn (戴縉), and others, were demoted or dismissed to varying degrees.
This month,
Zhū Yǒng (朱永) defeated the invaders at Dàtóng (大同) and Xuānfǔ (宣府).
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Rénshēn,
Zhū Yǒng (朱永) was recalled.
This year,
Sāmǎ'ěrhǎn (撒馬兒罕) presented lions as tribute.
In the twentieth year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngyín,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day Rénchén,
an imperial edict commanded officials to cultivate self-reflection.
An imperial decree ordered a reduction in tribute items,
strengthening border defenses,
suspending construction projects,
rectifying unjust cases,
easing silver taxes, corvée labor, and horse prices,
and showing compassion for soldiers killed in action at Dàtóng (大同).
On the day Dīngyǒu,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
In the third month, on the day Gēngyín,
Lǐ Mǐn (李旻) and others were granted the titles of presented scholars (進士) of varying ranks.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Grand Eunuch Zhāng Shàn (張善) was appointed supervisor of military affairs.
Marquis of Dìngxī (定西侯) Jiǎng Wǎn (蔣琬) served as Commander-in-Chief,
together with Supreme Commander Minister Yú Zǐjùn (余子俊), to prepare defenses for Dàtóng (大同) and Xuānfǔ (宣府).
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
prisoners were reviewed.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
prisoners were reviewed again,
and capital punishment and lesser sentences were reduced.
In the sixth month,
disaster taxes and grain were remitted for Southern Zhílì (南畿) and Shǎnxī (陝西).
In the autumn, ninth month, on the first day Yǐyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
This month,
the invaders re-entered and occupied Hétáo (河套).
This autumn,
Shǎnxī (陝西) and Shānxī (山西) suffered a severe drought and famine,
leading to cannibalism.
Annual supplies were suspended,
taxes and grain were remitted,
treasury funds were disbursed and grain transported,
and a system of accepting grain payments for official titles was opened to provide relief.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Lín Jùn (林俊), a Director in the Ministry of Justice, and Zhāng Fú (張黻), an experience officer in the Chief Military Commission, were flogged
and both demoted.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
silver mines in the various prefectures of Yuánjiāng (元江), Yúnnán (雲南) were abolished.
In the twelfth month,
summer taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken Shānxī (山西) and Hénán (河南).
This year,
Ānnán (安南), Rìběn (日本), Liúqiú (琉球), Hāmì (哈密), and Tǔlúfān (土魯番) paid tribute.
In the twenty-first year, spring, first month, on the first day Jiǎshēn,
there was a celestial anomaly.
On the day Bǐngxū,
an imperial decree commanded officials to speak freely on current affairs.
On the day Gēngyín,
a general amnesty was proclaimed for the empire.
On the day Yǐwèi,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Yǐsì,
Vice Ministers Lǐ Xián (李賢), Hé Qiáoxīn (何喬新), and Jiǎ Jùn (賈俊) were sent to provide famine relief in Shǎnxī (陝西), Shānxī (山西), and Hénán (河南).
In the second month, on the day Jǐwèi,
over 560 civil and military officials appointed by imperial decree were dismissed.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
disaster taxes and grain were remitted for Shǎnxī (陝西).
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
due to repeated earthquakes on Mount Tài (泰山), envoys were sent to offer sacrifices and report.
On the day Rénxū,
400,000 shi (石) of grain were transported
to relieve famine in Shǎnxī (陝西).
This month,
disaster taxes and grain were remitted for Southern Zhílì (南畿) and Shāndōng (山東).
In the fifth month, on the day Rénxū,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
famine relief was provided for the starving people in the capital.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnsì,
military officials were ordered to contribute grain in exchange for hereditary official positions.
On the day Guǐwèi,
an imperial decree stipulated that during severe heat and cold, court officials should not submit more than five proposals.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the first day Jǐmáo,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Liú Xǔ (劉珝) retired from office.
In the winter, tenth month,
disaster taxes and grain were remitted for Shāndōng (山東), Shānxī (山西), Hénán (河南), Shǎnxī (陝西), and Sìchuān (四川).
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngyín,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Peng Huá (彭華), Grand Academician (詹事), was appointed Junior Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent Grand Academician of the Hànlín Academy (翰林學士),
entering the Grand Secretariat to participate in government affairs.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
famine relief was provided in Southern Zhílì (南畿).
This winter,
the Little Prince (小王子) invaded Lánzhōu (蘭州), Zhuānglàng (莊浪), Zhènfān (鎮番), and Liángzhōu (涼州).
This year,
Hāmì (哈密) and Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏) paid tribute.
In the twenty-second year, spring, first month, on the day Jǐwèi,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
autumn grain taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken Hénán (河南).
In the second month, on the day Gēngchén,
autumn grain taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken Southern Zhílì (畿南) and Húguǎng (湖廣).
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
the estates of imperial relatives and noble families in the capital region (畿內) were investigated.
In the sixth month,
disaster taxes and grain were remitted for Southern Zhílì (南畿) and Shǎnxī (陝西).
On the day Yǐhài,
an imperial edict commanded officials to diligently perform their duties.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
an imperial edict instructed judicial organs to be prudent in criminal cases.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the Lesser Prince invaded Gānzhōu.
Commander Yáo Yīng and others died in battle.
In the ninth month,
taxes on grain for disaster-stricken areas in Hénán and Guǎngdōng were remitted.
On the Dīngmǎo day,
Yǐn Zhí, Left Vice Minister of War, was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently Grand Academician of the Hànlín Academy,
and entered the Grand Secretariat to participate in state affairs.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the Guǐchǒu day,
Zhānchéng was invaded by Ānnán,
and its prince, Gǔlái, came to seek refuge.
In the twelfth month,
taxes on grain for disaster-stricken areas in Jiāngxī and Guǎngxī were remitted.
In this year,
Hāmì and Liúqiú paid tribute.
In the spring of the twenty-third year, the first month,
taxes on grain for disaster-stricken areas in Shǎnxī and Húguǎng were remitted.
On the Gēngxū day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the Yǐyǒu day,
Biān Yōng, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Tián Jǐngxián, Councilor of the Provincial Administration Commission, inspected the borders of Dàtóng.
In the third month, on the Dīngwèi day,
Péng Huá retired.
On the Dīngsì day,
Fèi Hóng and others were granted the titles of Jìnshì and other degrees with distinctions.
On the Guǐhài day,
taxes on grain for disaster-stricken areas in Shāndōng were remitted.
In summer, the fourth month, on the Yǐhài day,
autumn grain taxes for disaster-stricken areas in Zhèjiāng were remitted.
In the fifth month, on the Yǐmǎo day,
due to drought,
envoys were dispatched to pray to the mountains and rivers across the empire.
On the Bǐngchén day,
an imperial edict instructed all officials to introspect and rectify.
In this month,
the Three Guards of Duǒyán avoided Nàhái and moved into Liáodōng,
and were ordered to pasture near the border and
were supplied with rice and cloth.
In the sixth month,
autumn grain taxes for disaster-stricken areas in Shǎnxī and Nánjī were remitted.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the Wùshēn day,
Imperial Prince Yòuyúan was enfeoffed as Xīng Wáng,
Yòulún as Qí Wáng,
Yòubīn as Yì Wáng,
Yòuhuī as Héng Wáng,
and Yòuyùn as Yōng Wáng.
In the eighth month, on the Gēngchén day,
the Emperor fell ill.
On the Jiǎshēn day,
the Crown Prince assumed duties at the Wénhuá Hall.
On the Jǐchǒu day,
the Emperor passed away,
at the age of forty-one.
In the ninth month, on the Yǐmǎo day,
a posthumous title was bestowed,
the temple name was Xiànzōng,
and he was buried in the Màolíng mausoleum.
The encomium states: Xiànzōng was established as Crown Prince early,
and experienced many difficulties in between.
After ascending the throne,
he honored Jǐngdì with a posthumous title,
redressed Yú Qiān's injustice,
repressed Lí Chún and recalled Shāng Lù;
he possessed a magnanimous character befitting a ruler.
The times were peaceful and bright,
the court had many seasoned officials.
The Emperor was earnest in employing capable people,
cautious with heavenly warnings,
remitted taxes and lightened punishments,
and the common people became increasingly prosperous.
The reigns of Rénzōng and Xuānzōng were seen again at this time.
However, by employing Wāng Zhí,
the Western Depot became arrogant and unrestrained,
usurped authority,
and cultivated evil while wielding military power.
An enlightened and decisive emperor like him was misled by them,
only realizing it much later.
Truly, the calamity caused by empresses' relatives and eunuchs is dreadful.
Collation Notes
Annals Volume 15: Xiàozōng
Xiàozōng Jiàn Tiānmíng Dào Chéngchún Zhōngzhèng Shèngwén Shénwǔ Zhìrén Dàdé Jìng Huángdì,
whose personal name was Yòutáng,
was the third son of Xiànzōng.
His mother was Consort Shū Jì Shì.
The Emperor was born in the Western Palace in the seventh month of the sixth year of Chénghuà.
At that time, Noble Consort Wàn was exclusively favored,
and no one in the palace dared to speak of it.
After the Dàogōng Crown Prince passed away,
Xiànzōng first learned of him [Yòutáng]
and had him raised in the palace of Grand Empress Dowager Zhōu.
In the eleventh year,
an imperial edict instructed the Ministry of Rites to name him,
and Grand Academician Shāng Lù and others thereupon requested the establishment of an heir.
In the sixth month of this year,
Consort Shū died suddenly,
and the Emperor, then six years old,
mourned like an adult.
In the eleventh month,
he was established as the Crown Prince.
In the eighth month of the twenty-third year,
Xiànzōng passed away.
In the ninth month, on the Rén yín day,
he ascended the imperial throne.
A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and the next year was designated as Hóngzhì first year.
On the Dīngwèi day,
he dismissed the flattering and favored officials, Vice Minister Lǐ Zīxǐng, Grand Eunuch Liáng Fāng, Empress's maternal relative Wàn Xǐ, and their associates,
and banished them with varying degrees of punishment.
In winter, the tenth month, on the Dīngmǎo day,
superfluous officials appointed by imperial decree were purged,
and more than a thousand people, including Rèn Jié, Right Administrator of Communications, and Vice Minister Kuǎi Gāng, were dismissed
and punished by banishment or dismissal.
The titles of Fǎwáng, Fózǐ, Guóshī, and Zhēnrén were abolished.
On the Yǐhài day,
Empress Dowager Zhōu was honored as Grand Empress Dowager,
and Empress Wáng was honored as Empress Dowager.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
Consort Zhāng was established as the Empress.
On the Dīnghài day,
Wàn Ān was dismissed.
On the Rénchén day,
his mother, Consort Shū, was posthumously honored as Empress Xiàomù.
On the Guǐsì day,
Xú Pǔ, Left Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrently Grand Academician of the Hànlín Academy, entered the Grand Secretariat to participate in state affairs.
In the eleventh month, on the Guǐchǒu day,
Yǐn Zhí was dismissed.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
Liú Jiàn, Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Academician of the Hànlín Academy,
and entered the Grand Secretariat to participate in state affairs.
On the Wùwǔ day,
Liáng Fāng and Lǐ Zīxǐng were imprisoned.
In the twelfth month, on the Rénwǔ day,
Emperor Chún was buried in the Màolíng mausoleum.
In this month,
taxes on grain for disaster-stricken areas in Jiāngxī and Húguǎng were remitted.
In this year,
Ānnán, Xiāmluó, Hāmì, Tǔlúfān, Wūsīzàng, and Liúqiú paid tribute.
Prince Gǔlái of Zhānchéng was enfeoffed as King,
and an edict instructed Límén of Ānnán to return the invaded territory to Zhānchéng.
In the spring of the first year of Hóngzhì, the first month, on the Jǐhài day,
a sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the Bǐngwǔ day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the southern suburbs.
On the Jǐwèi day,
the inspection of military officials guarding the borders began.
In the second month, on the Wùxū day,
sacrifices were offered to the deities of land and grain.
On the Dīngwèi day,
the ceremonial plowing of the imperial field took place.
Hǎnshèn, Left Commissioner-in-chief of the Hāmì Guard, was enfeoffed as Zhōngshùn Wáng.
On the Bǐngchén day,
court officials were forbidden from soliciting public affairs.
In the third month, on the Yǐchǒu day,
the names of civil and military ministers and officials of the fourth rank and above, both inside and outside the court, were listed
and displayed on the wall of the Wénhuá Hall.
On the Guǐyǒu day,
a ceremony was held in honor of Confucius, the Former Master.
On the Yǐhài day,
the Lesser Prince plundered Lánzhōu,
and Commander Liáo Bīn defeated him.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
the Emperor attended the imperial lectures.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
Confucian scholars were ordered to give daily lectures.
In summer, the fourth month, on the Jiǎyín day,
prisoners were reviewed due to the summer heat.
Thereafter, this became an annual practice.
In the sixth month, on the first day, Guǐsì,
there was a solar eclipse.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the Wùchén day,
silver levies in Zhèjiāng were reduced,
and officials managing silver mines were dismissed.
In the eighth month, on the Yǐsì day,
the Lesser Prince invaded Shāndān and Yǒngchāng.
On the Xīnhài day,
he invaded Dúshí and Mǎyíng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the Yǐmǎo day,
relief was provided for famine in Húguǎng and Sìchuān.
In the eleventh month, on the Jiǎshēn day,
the evil monk Jìxiǎo was executed.
On the Yǐyǒu day,
autumn grain taxes for disaster-stricken areas in Hénán were remitted.
In this year,
Tǔlúfān killed Zhōngshùn Wáng Hǎnshèn
and reoccupied Hāmì.
Liúqiú, Zhānchéng, Sāmǎ'érhǎn, Wūsīzàng, and Liúqiú paid tribute.
In the spring of the second year, the first month, on the Dīngmǎo day,
land previously granted to deceased eunuchs was reclaimed
and distributed to the common people.
On the Xīnwèi day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the Guǐsì day,
relief was provided for famine in Sìchuān.
In the third month, on the Jǐwèi day,
two-thirds of the autumn grain taxes for disaster-stricken areas in Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the Wùyín day,
the silver mine at Huìchuān Guard was closed.
In the summer, fifth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
the Yellow River burst its banks at Kāifēng,
flowing into the Qìn Hé.
Fifty thousand people were conscripted to manage it.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Guǐhài,
due to prolonged rain in the capital (Jīngshī) and a great storm with thunder in Nánjīng, the emperor ordered a self-examination and reform,
and sought honest criticism.
On the day Wùyín,
relief was provided for flood victims within the capital region (Jīnnèi);
tax grain was remitted,
and wheat seeds were given to the poor.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
migrants from Sìchuān who returned to their former occupations were granted a three-year exemption from corvée labor.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the spirit tablet of Xiànzōng was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Shùntiān suffered from famine;
grain was distributed for sale at a stabilized price.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎshēn, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Yú Qiān was posthumously granted a title,
and a temple was established for him, named
“Jīnggōng”.
In this year,
Tǔlǔfān offered tribute.
Sāmǎ'érhǎn offered lions and parrots,
but these were declined.
In the third year, spring, first month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the day Rénchén,
autumn grain tax was remitted for those affected by disaster in Hénán.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Ministry of Revenue (Hùbù) requested the remission of tax grain for the Southern Capital region (Nánjī) and Húguǎng.
The emperor said:
“In times of famine, it is right to reduce the burden on the superior and benefit the inferior.
If one must insist on collecting the full amount,
what will become of the suffering people?”
All proposals were accepted.
In the third month, on the day Bǐngchén,
orders were given to accumulate grain in the ever-normal granaries throughout the empire,
with differing amounts based on the size of the communities;
those who failed to meet the quota were to be punished.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Qián Fú and others were granted the Jinshì degree and official ranks with distinctions.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Vice Minister Zhāng Hǎi and Commissioner Yuán Shǒuzhí of the Office of Transmission (Tōngzhèngsǐ) inspected the border.
In the autumn, ninth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Inner Court (Nèifǔ) was prohibited from imposing additional levies for imperial supplies.
In the intercalary month, on the day Guǐsì,
imperial clan members and meritorious relatives were prohibited from requesting land or accepting land donated by others.
In the winter, eleventh month, on the day Jiǎchén,
corvée labor was suspended, and
the imperial eunuchs' production of porcelain was halted.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnhài,
due to the sighting of a comet,
an imperial edict instructed all officials to conduct self-examination and reform,
and to present the advantages and disadvantages for the military and the populace.
On the day Jǐwèi,
there was an earthquake in the capital (Jīngshī).
On the day Rénxū,
imperial provisions were reduced,
and the lantern festival for the upcoming New Year (Shàngyuán) was canceled.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Ānnán, Hāmì, Sāmǎ'érhǎn, Tiānfāng, and Tǔlǔfān offered tribute.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the New Year's (Shàngyuán) holiday was canceled due to self-examination and reform.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the southern suburbs,
and the celebration banquet was canceled.
In the second month, on the day Jǐsì,
the emperor issued an edict to the judicial offices, stating:
“Previously, due to celestial anomalies,
I ordered all provincial offices to review serious criminal cases,
resulting in the release of hundreds of individuals.
I believe that rather than being lenient in the end,
it is better to be prudent from the beginning.
Hereafter, the Three Judicial Offices (sānfǎsī) of both capitals and all judicial officials throughout the empire
must act with compassion and leniency,
administer justice fairly,
and carefully examine the circumstances and crimes to determine what is appropriate,
so as not to deviate from the ancient sages' teaching of sympathetic consideration.”
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnhài,
there was an earthquake in the capital (Jīngshī).
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, and Zhèjiāng suffered from floods;
textile production for the current year was suspended.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
there was an earthquake in Nánjīng.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Imperial Prince Yòuzhī was enfeoffed as Shòu Wáng,
Yòupí as Rú Wáng,
Yòushùn as Jīng Wáng,
Yòushū as Róng Wáng,
and Yòukǎi as Shēn Wáng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
due to the birth of the Imperial First Son,
an imperial edict was issued to the empire.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the river overflowed;
relief was provided for those affected by disaster in Hénán.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Minister Qíu Jùn of the Ministry of Rites (Lǐbù) was concurrently appointed Grand Secretary (Dàxuéshì) of Wényuāngé to participate in state affairs (jīwù).
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngchén,
relief was provided for disaster victims in the Southern Capital region (Nánjī).
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Tǔlǔfān returned Hāmì territory and a golden seal, submitting to the court.
In this year,
Xiāmluó offered tribute.
In the fifth year, spring, first month, on the day Rénwǔ,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Shǎnbā was ordered to inherit the title of Zhōngshùn Wáng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the production of felt rugs in Shǎnxī was reduced by half.
In the third month, on the day Wùyín,
Imperial Prince Hòuzhào was established as the Crown Prince (Huáng Tàizǐ),
and a general amnesty was granted.
Descendants of meritorious officials whose titles had been abolished, but whose spirit tablets were enshrined alongside Tàizǔ in the ancestral temple, were reinstated.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Associate Regional Commander Mǎ Jùn, Counselor Mǎ Xuán, Commander Wáng Shān, and others of Guǎngxī, while suppressing the rebel children (pàntóng) of Gǔtián,
fell into an ambush and died.
In the summer, sixth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
tax grain for disaster victims in the Southern Capital region (Nánjī) from the previous year was remitted.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
relief was provided for famine victims in Nánjīng, Zhèjiāng, and Shāndōng.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Líu Jí retired from office.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
extra textile production in Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, and Zhèjiāng was suspended,
and the supervising officials were recalled.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Rénxū,
Grand Commander Gù Pǔ, Marquis of Zhènyuǎn, of Húguǎng, Censor-in-chief Dèng Tíngzàn, Governor of Guìzhōu, and Eunuch Jiāng Dé, gathered their forces to suppress the Hēi Miáo of Guìzhōu.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
the silver mines of Wēnzhōu and Chùzhōu were closed.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Jīng Wáng Jiànxiāo was found guilty
and demoted to commoner status.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Wūsīzàng, and Tǔlǔfān offered tribute.
Huǒlàzhá offered local products,
which were not accepted,
but they were given provisions and sent back.
In the sixth year, spring, first month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎyín,
descendants of Cháng Yùchūn, Lí Wénzhōng, Dèng Yù, and Tāng Hé were registered
to inherit the title of Commander (Zhīhuīshǐ).
On the day Dīngsì,
Administrator Líu Dàxià was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief (Yòufù Dūyùshǐ)
to manage the breach of the river at Zhāngqiū.
In the third month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Máo Chéng and others were granted the Jinshì degree and official ranks with distinctions.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Sùdàn Āhēimǎ of Tǔlǔfān attacked and captured Shǎnbā,
occupying Hāmì.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Vice Minister Zhāng Hǎi and Commissioner-in-chief Gōu Qiān of the Chief Military Commission (Dūdū Tóngzhī) were dispatched to strategize regarding Hāmì.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
due to prolonged drought,
an edict ordered self-examination and reform,
and sought honest criticism.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
the Little Prince (Xiǎo Wángzǐ) invaded Níngxià,
killing Commander Zhào Xǐ.
In the intercalary month, on the day Yǐwèi,
autumn grain tax for disaster victims in Nánjīng was remitted.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
locusts were caught.
On the day Rénshēn,
Censor-in-chief Mǐn Guī defeated the rebel children (pàntóng) of Gǔtián.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
summer tax for disaster victims in Shùntiān was remitted.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
summer tax for disaster victims in Shǎnxī was remitted.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
due to disasters and damage, the lantern festival for the upcoming New Year (Shàngyuán) was canceled.
On the day Gēngchén,
the production of felt rugs in Gānsù was suspended.
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngshēn,
relief was provided for displaced people (liúmín) in the capital (Jīngshī).
In the twelfth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
an imperial edict instructed all regional commanders and censors to conduct self-examination and reform.
In this year,
Ānnán, Wūsīzàng, Tǔlǔfān, and Xiāmluó offered tribute.
In the seventh year, spring, first month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
due to the storm and thunder at Xiàolíng in the previous winter,
envoys were sent to offer sacrifices and make announcements,
self-examination and reform were ordered,
and honest criticism was sought.
Internal and external officials were ordered to be cautious in judicial matters,
and to release those lightly imprisoned.
In the third month, on the day Guǐsì,
the Hēi Miáo rebellion in Guìzhōu was suppressed.
On the day Wùshēn,
locusts were caught in both capital regions.
In the fifth month of summer, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Eunuch Lǐ Xìng and Earl of Píngjiāng Chén Ruì, together with Liú Dàxià, managed the breach of the Yellow River at Zhāngqiū.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *yǐsì* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Vice Minister of Works Xú Guàn and Grand Coordinator (Xúnfǔ) and Vice Censor-in-Chief (Fù Dū Yùshǐ) Hé Jiàn managed water conservancy in the Southern Metropolitan Region (Nánjī).
In the ninth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
due to flood disasters, the supply of materials handled by Sūzhōu and Sōngjiāng prefectures was suspended.
Customs duties (guānchāo) and household salt (hùyán) were reserved for relief.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the *rénzǐ* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
the Zhāngqiū river works were completed.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
relief was provided to soldiers and civilians in Gānzhōu and Liángzhōu affected by warfare,
and cattle and seeds were distributed.
In this year,
taxes on grain were remitted for Beijing, Hénán, Húguǎng, Shǎnxī, and Shānxī due to disasters.
The Ryukyu Kingdom paid tribute.
As the Turfan (Tǔlǔfān) occupied Hāmì,
their tribute envoys were refused.
In the first month of spring of the eighth year, on the *yǐwèi* day,
the great sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the Southern Altar.
As the Empress Dowager was unwell,
the celebration banquet was cancelled.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Liú Níng, the Grand Commander (Zǒngbīngguān) of Gānsù, defeated the Little Prince (Xiǎo Wángzǐ) at Liángzhōu.
On the first day of the second month, *yǐmǎo*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Qiū Jùn passed away.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Vice Minister of Rites Lǐ Dōngyáng and Junior Expositor (Shǎo Zhànshì) Xiè Qiān entered the Grand Secretariat (Rù Gé) to participate in state affairs.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the river mouth works at Huánglínggāng were completed.
In the third month, on the *rénchén* day,
taxes on grain were remitted for Húguǎng due to disasters.
On the *jǐhài* day,
there was an earthquake in Níngxià.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *jiǎyín* day,
water conservancy works in Sūzhōu and Sōngjiāng prefectures were completed.
On the *rénxū* day,
an edict was issued to the Ministry of Personnel (Lìbù) and the Censorate (Dūcháyuàn), stating that
the promotion and demotion of talent
must be based on actual achievements during investigation,
and one must not listen to biased reports and wrong people.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
autumn taxes were remitted for the Southern Metropolitan Region (Nánjī) due to disasters.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *dīnghài* day,
Yáng Shí, a Song dynasty Confucian scholar, was enfeoffed as Earl of Jiānglè,
and was allowed to be worshipped alongside Confucius in the temple courtyard.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Ōu Pán, the Vice Grand Commander (Fù Zǒngbīngguān) of Guǎngxī, defeated the rebel Yao (Yáo) at Pínglè.
In the eighth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
as various calamities and anomalies had appeared frequently,
an imperial edict was issued to all officials to cultivate and reflect.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
autumn taxes were remitted for Zhílì due to disasters.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Xǔ Jìn, Grand Coordinator (Xúnfǔ) of Gānsù and Surveillance Censor (Qiān Dū Yùshǐ), and Liú Níng, Grand Commander (Zǒngbīngguān), entered Hāmì.
The Turfan (Tǔlǔfān) fled,
and so the army returned.
In this year,
Java (Zhǎowā), Champa (Zhānchéng), and Ū-Tsang (Wūsīzàng) paid tribute.
The Karak Khoja (Kèlì) tribes [attempted to] cross the border at Sùzhōu to seek tribute,
but were refused.
In the first month of spring of the ninth year, on the *rénchén* day,
the great sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the Southern Altar.
In the second month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
taxes on grain were remitted for Hénán due to disasters.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Right Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission (Yòu Tōngzhèng) Zhāng Pú and Junior Minister of the Court of Judicial Review (Dàlǐ Shǎoqīng) Mǎ Zhōngxī inspected the borders.
In the third month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
Zhū Xīzhōu and others were granted the *Jìnshì Jíyǐ* degree and various ranks of *chūshēn*.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *wùzǐ* day,
following a memorial from Prince Mín, Yīngpǐ,
Liú Xùn, the Prefect of Wǔgāng, was arrested.
Investigating Censors (Gěishìzhōng) and Censors (Yùshǐ) Páng Pàn, Liú Shēn, and others remonstrated,
and were imprisoned in the Imperial Bodyguard (Jǐnyīwèi) prison,
but were soon released.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
taxes on grain were remitted for Jiāngxī due to disasters.
In the eighth month of autumn, on the *rénchén* day,
autumn taxes were remitted for Húguǎng due to disasters.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
powerful families were prohibited from encroaching upon the people's interests.
In this year,
Japan (Rìběn), Ryukyu (Liúqiú), and Ū-Tsang (Wūsīzàng) paid tribute.
In the first month of spring of the tenth year, on the *gēngxū* day,
the great sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the Southern Altar.
In the third month, on the *xīnhài* day,
due to drought and haze, self-reflection was ordered,
and direct criticism was sought.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Grand Secretaries (Dà Xuéshì) Liú Jiàn, Lǐ Dōngyáng, and Xiè Qiān were summoned to the Wénhuá Hall to discuss state affairs,
which later became a regular practice.
In the fifth month of summer, on the *wùchén* day,
the Little Prince (Xiǎo Wángzǐ) raided Cháohé Chuān.
On the *jǐsì* day,
he raided Dàtóng.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Vice Ministers (Shìláng) Liú Dàxià and Lǐ Jiè managed military provisions for Xuānfǔ and Dàtóng.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Grand Commissioner (Dūdū) Yáng Yù commanded the capital's garrison troops,
to defend Yǒngpíng.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Turfan (Tǔlǔfān) returned Shǎnbā,
and requested to resume tribute.
In this year,
taxes on grain were remitted for the Southern Metropolitan Region (Nánjī), Shānxī, and Shǎnxī due to disasters,
and relief was provided for flood disasters in Shāndōng and Sìchuān.
Annam (Ānnán), Siam (Xiānluó), and Ū-Tsang (Wūsīzàng) paid tribute.
In the first month of spring of the eleventh year, on the *dīngwèi* day,
the great sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the Southern Altar.
In the second month, on the *jǐsì* day,
the Little Prince (Xiǎo Wángzǐ) sent envoys to seek tribute.
In the fifth month of summer, on the *wùshēn* day,
Yáng Zhù, a Participatory Officer (Cāncāng) of Gānsù, defeated the Little Prince (Xiǎo Wángzǐ) at Hēishān.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
Wáng Yuè, Grand Coordinator (Zǒngzhì) of the Three Borders and Censor-in-Chief (Dū Yùshǐ), raided the Little Prince (Xiǎo Wángzǐ) behind the Hèlán Mountains,
and defeated him.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Xú Pǔ retired.
In the eighth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
relief was provided to the people of Xiángfú affected by river disasters.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *bǐngyín* day,
it was ordered that work assignments should not utilize the garrison troops.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Qīngníng Palace suffered a fire.
On the *dīnghài* day,
an imperial edict was issued to all officials to cultivate and reflect,
direct criticism was sought,
and the lantern display for the Lantern Festival (Shàngyuán) of the coming year was abolished.
In the eleventh month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
the weaving of wool in Shǎnxī was exempted.
On the first day of the intercalary month, *rénxū*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the weaving of colored cloth in Fújiàn was abolished.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
excessive extravagance beyond regulations was prohibited both within and outside the capital.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
due to the fire at Qīngníng Palace, an imperial edict proclaimed a general amnesty.
In this year,
taxes on grain were remitted for Shānxī, Shǎnxī, the Two Metropolitan Regions (Liǎng Jī), Guǎngxī, and Guǎngdōng due to disasters.
The Turfan (Tǔlǔfān) and Ū-Tsang (Wūsīzàng) paid tribute.
In the first month of spring of the twelfth year, on the *xīnwèi* day,
the great sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the Southern Altar,
and the celebration banquet was cancelled.
In the second month, on the *rénchén* day,
summer taxes were remitted for Shāndōng due to disasters.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the prohibition against heterodox teachings deceiving the populace was strictly enforced.
In the third month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
Lún Wén and others were granted the *Jìnshì Jíyǐ* degree and various ranks of *chūshēn*.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *guǐsì* day,
an imperial edict was issued for Xuānfǔ, Dàtóng, and Yánsuí to prepare their borders.
In this month,
taxes on grain were remitted for Húguǎng and Jiāngxī due to disasters.
In the fifth month, on the *wùyín* day,
autumn taxes were remitted for the Southern Metropolitan Region (Nánjī) due to disasters.
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
the Temple of the Foremost Sage at Quèlǐ suffered a fire,
and envoys were sent to offer condolences and sacrifices.
In the eighth month of autumn,
summer taxes were remitted for Hénán and the Southern Metropolitan Region (Nánjī) due to disasters.
In the ninth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
the female bandit Mǐ Lù from Pǔ'ān caused a rebellion.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the reconstruction of Qīngníng Palace was completed.
In this year,
Champa (Zhānchéng), Ū-Tsang (Wūsīzàng), Turfan (Tǔlǔfān), Java (Zhǎowā), and Samarkand (Sāmǎ'ěrhǎn) paid tribute.
In the first month of spring of the thirteenth year, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
the great sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the Southern Altar.
In the second month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
taxes on grain were remitted for Shānxī due to disasters.
On the *gēngyín* day,
regulations for interrogating and sentencing were established.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the law regarding the mutual implication of officials for their subordinates' actions (jǐngjǔ liánzuò zhīfǎ) was strictly enforced.
In summer, the fourth month,
Huǒshāi (火篩) plundered Dàtóng (大同).
The guerrilla general Wáng Gǎo (王杲) was defeated at Wēiyuǎn Wèi (威遠衞).
On the *yǐsì* day,
Chén Ruì (陳銳), Earl of Píngjiāng (平江伯), was appointed General Jìnglǔ (靖虜將軍),
serving as Commander-in-Chief.
The grand eunuch Jīn Fǔ (金輔) supervised the army,
and Xǔ Jìn (許進), Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, was appointed Military Governor
to resist them.
In the fifth month, on the *jiǎyín* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Grand Secretaries Liú Jiàn (劉健), Lǐ Dōngyáng (李東陽), and Xiè Qiān (謝遷) were summoned to Píngtái (平臺)
to discuss the generals of the capital garrisons.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Huǒshāi (火篩) launched a major incursion into Dàtóng Zuǒwèi (大同左衞).
The guerrilla general Zhāng Jùn (張俊) repelled them.
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
autumn grain taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken Jiāngxī (江西),
and the procurement of materials in Shān (山) and Shǎn (陝) was suspended.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Chén Ruì (陳銳) and Jīn Fǔ (金輔) were recalled.
Zhū Huī (朱暉), Duke of Bǎoguó (保國公), and the grand eunuch Fú'ān (扶安) went to replace them,
and more troops were sent to resist the invaders.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *jǐsì* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
relief was provided for flood-stricken Jiāngxī (江西).
In winter, the tenth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
there were earthquakes in both capitals.
In this month,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ (小王子) and his various tribes plundered Dàtóng (大同).
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Huǒshāi (火篩) plundered Dàtóng (大同),
raiding over a hundred *lǐ* (里) to the south.
In this year,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ's (小王子) tribe moved into and settled in the Hétào (河套) region,
and attacked Shénmùbǎo (神木堡) in Yánsuí (延綏).
Liúqiú (琉球), Tǔlúfān (土魯番), and Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏) paid tribute.
In the fourteenth year, spring, the first month, on the *gēngxū* day, the first day of the month,
there was a major earthquake in Shǎnxī (陝西).
On the *jǐwèi* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the *jǐhài* day,
the eunuch supervising weaving in Shǎnxī (陝西) was dismissed.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Lǐ Suì (李鐩), Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works, was appointed Military Governor for border provisions in Yánsuí (延綏).
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Zhū Huī (朱暉), Duke of Bǎoguó (保國公), Shǐ Lín (史琳), Censor-in-Chief and Military Governor, and the supervising grand eunuch Miáo Kuí (苗逵) advanced into Yánsuí (延綏) by different routes.
On the *wùxū* day,
materials from Shǎnxī (陝西) and Shānxī (山西) were exempted.
In this month,
Huǒshāi (火篩) and his various tribes plundered Gùyuán (固原).
In the fifth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
relief was provided for the military and civilians affected by war in Dàtóng (大同),
and their tax grain was remitted.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
disaster-stricken tax grain in Shǎnxī (陝西) was remitted.
On the *wùchén* day,
the temple of the Former Sage at Quèlǐ (闕里) was repaired.
Each Administration Commission was ordered to submit geographical maps.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
bandits from Tàiníng Wèi (泰寧衞) attacked Liáodōng (遼東),
plundering Chángshèng (長勝) and other forts and garrisons.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Wáng Shì (王軾), Minister of Revenue in Nánjīng (南京), concurrently served as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Military Governor,
to suppress the female bandit Mǐ Lù (米魯) in Guìzhōu (貴州).
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Zhū Huī (朱暉) and Shǐ Lín (史琳) launched a surprise attack on Xiǎo Wángzǐ (小王子) in Hétào (河套).
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Censors and Investigating Censors were dispatched to investigate and rectify the *túntián* (屯田) military-agricultural colonies.
In the intercalary month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Dū Zhǐhuī (都指揮) Wáng Tài (王泰) resisted Xiǎo Wángzǐ (小王子) at Yánchí (鹽池),
and died in battle.
On the *wùxū* day,
relief was provided for flood-stricken areas in the two capital regions (Jīngjī, 京畿), Jiāngxī (江西), Shāndōng (山東), and Hénán (河南).
In the eighth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
disaster-stricken tax grain in Hénán (河南) was remitted.
In this month,
Huǒshāi (火篩) and his various tribes attacked Gùyuán (固原),
and greatly plundered Wéizhōu (韋州), Huánxiàn (環縣), Méngchéng (萌城), and Língzhōu (靈州).
On the *jǐsì* day,
the supplies of the Guānglù Sì (光祿寺) were reduced,
as in the first year of the reign.
Huǒshāi (火篩) and his various tribes attacked the eastern route of Níngxià (寧夏).
In the ninth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *dīnghài* day,
envoys were dispatched to recruit soldiers in Yánsuí (延綏), Níngxià (寧夏), Gān (甘), and Liáng (涼).
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Shǐ Lín (史琳) was recalled,
and Qín Hóng (秦紘) was appointed Minister of Revenue and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief
to replace him.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the *guǐsì* day,

Vice Minister Hé Jiàn (何鑑) and Dàlǐ Sìchéng (大理寺丞) Wú Yīguàn (吳一貫) were separately dispatched to provide relief to famine victims in the two capital regions (Jīngjī, 京畿), Shāndōng (山東), and Hénán (河南).
In the twelfth month, on the *wùchén* day,
there was a severe famine in Liáodōng (遼東),
and relief was provided.
In this month,
the invaders emerged from Hétào (河套).
In this year,
disaster-stricken tax grain in Húguǎng (湖廣), Jiāngxī (江西), Shānxī (山西), Shāndōng (山東), Shǎnxī (陝西), Hénán (河南), and the capital regions (Jī nèi, 畿內) was remitted.
Ānnán (安南) and Liúqiú (琉球) paid tribute.
In the fifteenth year, spring, the first month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Zhū Huī (朱暉) returned with his army.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
disaster-stricken tax grain in Hénán (河南) was remitted.
In the third month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
the eunuch supervising porcelain production in Ráozhōu (饒州) was dismissed.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Kāng Hǎi (康海) and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with different ranks.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *rényín* day,
relief was provided for the poor people in the capital.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
disaster-stricken autumn grain in Húguǎng (湖廣) was remitted.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the descendants of Liú Jī (劉基) were recorded to inherit the title of Commander (Zhǐhuīshǐ, 指揮使).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Wáng Shì (王軾) defeated and beheaded Mǐ Lù (米魯),
and the Guìzhōu (貴州) bandits were pacified.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
orders were given to establish *Yǎngjì Yuàn* (養濟院) (relief institutions) and *Lòuzé Yuán* (漏澤園) (cemeteries for the poor) in all border garrisons.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
due to continuous heavy rain and strong winds in Nánjīng (南京) and Fèngyáng (鳳陽),
the Jiāng (江) (Yangtze River) overflowed, causing disaster.
Envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifices and prayers,
and officials in both capitals were instructed to reflect and mend their ways.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the birds and beasts kept in the imperial household were released and reduced.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the lantern festival for the next New Year was abolished.
In the eleventh month, on the *rénshēn* day,
Lí (黎) bandits in Qióngzhōu (瓊州) revolted.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
pearl fishing in Guǎngdōng (廣東) was suspended.
In the twelfth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
the *Dàmíng Huìdiǎn* (大明會典) was completed.
On the *xīnhài* day,
due to illness, the court was not held.
In this month,
disaster-stricken autumn grain in the Southern Capital region (Nánjī, 南畿) was remitted.
In this year,
Liúqiú (琉球) and Ānnán (安南) paid tribute.
In the sixteenth year, spring, the first month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
an official was sent to offer sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple on behalf of the emperor.
In the second month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the court was held.
On the *wùshēn* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the third month, on the *guǐsì* day,
disaster-stricken tax grain in Shānxī (山西) was remitted.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
an edict ordered strict border defense in Xuān (宣) and Dà (大).
In the fifth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
due to disasters in Yúnnán (雲南), officials were instructed to reflect and mend their ways.
Fán Yíng (樊瑩), Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice, inspected Yún (雲) and Guì (貴),
investigating officials
and inquiring about the suffering of the people.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the government troops of Guǎngdōng (廣東) suppressed the Lí (黎) bandits
and defeated them.
In the ninth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
relief was provided for disaster-stricken military and civilians in the two capital regions (Jīngjī, 京畿), Zhèjiāng (浙江), Shāndōng (山東), Hénán (河南), and Húguǎng (湖廣).
In winter, the eleventh month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
the construction of artifacts and the New Year's fireworks for the next year were abolished.
In this month,
disaster-stricken autumn grain in the Southern Capital region (Nánjī, 南畿) was remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
materials from Huái (淮), Yáng (揚), and Zhèjiāng (浙江) were exempted.
In this year,
Ānnán (安南), Xiāmluó (暹羅), Hāmì (哈密), Tǔlúfān (土魯番), and Sāmǎ'érhǎn (撒馬兒罕) paid tribute.
In the seventeenth year, spring, the first month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Gāo Quán (高銓), Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works in Nánjīng (南京), provided relief for the famine in Yīngtiān (應天).
On the *jiǎxū* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the prohibition against false accusations was strictly enforced.
In the second month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
the supply of materials was reduced.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the prohibition against prophecies and seditious writings was strictly enforced.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
disaster-stricken tax grain in Zhèjiāng (浙江) was remitted.
In the third month, on the *rénxū* day,
the Grand Empress Dowager passed away.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the system of one emperor and one empress per chamber in the Imperial Ancestral Temple was established.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Empress Xiàosù was interred.
In the intercalary month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the temple of the Former Teacher at Quēlǐ was completed.
Grand Secretary Lǐ Dōngyáng was dispatched to offer sacrifices and make a report.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
tax grain for disaster-stricken areas in Shāndōng was remitted.
On the day Yǐhài,
due to widespread disasters, an imperial edict was issued to all officials to cultivate self-reflection and amend their ways.
On the day Gēngchén,
all departments were ordered to deliberate in detail on harmful and corrupt policies affecting the people.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénchén,
the eunuchs overseeing textile production in Nánjīng, Sūzhōu, and Hángzhōu were dismissed.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐhài,
it was first decreed that officials of the fifth rank and below in both capitals should undergo an evaluation every six years.
On the day Xīnsì,
Liú Jiàn and Lǐ Dōngyáng were summoned to the Nuǎngé
to discuss border affairs.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Huǒshāi invaded Dàtóng,
and Commander Zhèng Yǔ died fighting bravely.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Guǐsì,
Vice Minister of Works Lǐ Suì, Dali Minor Minister Wú Yīguàn, and Councilor of the Office of Transmission Cóng Lán were dispatched along separate routes to manage the border defenses.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Yán Zhòngyǔ and Councilor of the Office of Transmission Xióng Wěi were assigned to manage border provisions.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùchén,
it was ordered that supervising censors, investigating censors, and officials of the three judicial offices throughout the realm report on the benefits and harms to the military and common people.
For suggestions from scholars and commoners that were deemed adoptable,
the relevant offices were to report them.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the summer tax for disaster-stricken areas in Nánjī was remitted.
On the day Dīnghài,
Mǎ Wénshēng and Dài Shān were summoned to the Nuǎngé,
and instructed regarding the evaluation next year,
that they must investigate actual achievements
to seek what is most appropriate.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngyín,
the judicial authorities were admonished not to act arbitrarily or with bias,
thereby causing prisoners to be unduly detained.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Taichang Minor Minister Sūn Jiāo was dispatched to manage border affairs in Xuānfǔ and Dàtóng.
On the day Dīngsì,
in the Nuǎngé,
Liú Jiàn, Lǐ Dōngyáng, and Xiè Qiān were instructed:
"Regarding the foremost achievements on various borders,
the investigations by the inspecting censors
often drag on for years,
which is not conducive to showing encouragement.
From now on, when reports are submitted,
deadlines shall be set according to distance.
Violators will be interrogated and punished."
Lecturers were instructed to speak frankly and without concealment during their lectures.
In the winter, eleventh month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the silver mines in Yúnnán were abolished.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
the prohibition against hoarding grain for speculation was reiterated.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the autumn tax for disaster-stricken areas in Húguǎng was remitted.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Sāmǎ'érhǎn, Hāmì, and Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the eighteenth year, spring, first month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ's various tribes besieged Língzhōu,
entered Huāmǎchí,
and subsequently plundered Wéizhōu and Huánxiàn.
Vice Minister of Revenue Gù Zuǒ managed military provisions in Shǎnxī.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the southern altar.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ captured Qīngshuǐyíng in Níngxià.
In the second month, on the day Wùchén,
at Fèngtiānmén,
the Emperor instructed the three ministries of Revenue, War, and Works, saying:
"At present, the population is gradually increasing,
yet the household registers and military ranks are daily diminishing.
This is all due to the inadequacy of officials in providing care and comfort,
and their persistence in perfunctory practices.
Let them deliberate on all corrupt policies and report them."
In the third month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Gù Dǐngchén and others were granted the degrees of Jìnshì and Jìdì, with varying ranks.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Wùyín,
Vice Minister of Justice Hé Jiàn pacified and settled the displaced people in Jīngzhōu and Xiāngyáng.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Emperor fell ill.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngyín,
his illness worsened considerably,
and Grand Secretaries Liú Jiàn, Lǐ Dōngyáng, and Xiè Qiān were summoned to receive his last will.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
he passed away in the Qiánqīnggōng,
aged thirty-six.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
an honored posthumous title was conferred,
and his temple name was Xiàozōng.
He was interred in the Tàilíng.
The eulogy states: Of the sixteen reigns of the Míng dynasty,
apart from Tàizǔ and Chéngzǔ,
those who can be praised are only Rénzōng, Xuānzōng, and Xiàozōng.
During the reigns of Rénzōng and Xuānzōng,
the national power was initially expanding,
the governing principles were established,
and simplicity and honesty had not yet deteriorated.
By the time of Chénghuà and later,
it was known as a time of peace and tranquility,
but ease and comfort easily led to negligence and idleness,
and prosperity gradually gave rise to arrogance and extravagance.
Xiàozōng alone was able to maintain modesty and temperance,
govern diligently, and love the people,
carefully striving to preserve stability and sustain prosperity,
thus ensuring a clear and peaceful court order,
and a prosperous and abundant populace.
The Yìjīng says:
"When the wellspring is level and not sloped,
when the wellspring flows forth and does not return,
then despite hardship and uprightness, there will be misfortune."
Perhaps Xiàozōng was the one who understood this principle.

Basic Annals Volume Sixteen: Wǔzōng
Wǔzōng Chéngtiān Dá dào Yīngsù Ruìzhé Zhāodé Xiǎngōng Hóngwén Sīxiào Yì Huángdì,
his personal name was Hòuzhào,
and he was the eldest son of Xiàozōng.
His mother was Empress Xiàokāngjìng.
In the fifth year of Hóngzhì,

He was intelligent by nature
and fond of riding and archery.

Xiàozōng passed away.

to resist them.

the Empress Dowager was honored as Grand Empress Dowager,

In this year,
Zhànchéng, Ānnán presented tribute.
In the first year of Zhèngdé, spring, first month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
sacrifices were offered at the Tàimiào.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was performed at the southern altar.
In the second month, on the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor attended the imperial lectures (Jīngyán).
On the day Yǐchǒu,
he plowed the sacrificial field.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
a ceremony was held for the Former Teacher Kǒngzǐ.
In the summer, fifth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
the annual tribute in silk from Sūzhōu and Hángzhōu textile production was reduced.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
extravagance and waste among officials and commoners were prohibited.

strong winds and rain damaged the glazed tiles of the suburban altar.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
all officials were instructed to cultivate self-reflection and amend their ways.
