In winter, in the tenth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
Hùbù Shàngshū Hán Wén, leading court officials, requested the execution of eight rebellious eunuchs, including Mǎ Yǒngchéng,
with Dàxuéshì Liú Jiàn, Lǐ Dōngyáng, and Xiè Qiān supporting the motion.
On the *wǔwǔ* day,
Hán Wén and others reiterated their request,
but it was not granted.
Liú Jǐn was placed in charge of the Sīlǐ Jiān.
Qiū Jù and Gǔ Dàyòng were appointed as commanders of the East and West Agencies.
Zhāng Yǒng oversaw the Twelve Regiments and the Shénjī Yíng.
Wèi Bīn oversaw the Three Thousand Regiments.
Each occupied a strategic position.
Liú Jiàn, Lǐ Dōngyáng, and Xiè Qiān requested retirement.
Jiàn and Qiān retired on that day.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Lǐ Dōngyáng again requested retirement,
but it was not permitted.
On the *rénxū* day,
Lìbù Shàngshū Jiāo Fāng concurrently became Wényuāngé Dàxuéshì,
and Lìbù Shìláng Wáng Ào concurrently became Hànlín Xuéshì,
entering the cabinet to participate in state affairs.
On the *wùchén* day,
the daily lectures were suspended.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Hán Wén was dismissed.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
the Jǐnyīwèi officers were ordered to inspect the supervising secretaries.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the land tax of the Kǒng clan in Qūfù was exempted.
In this year,
Hāmì and Wūsīzàng sent tribute.
In the second year, spring, in the first month, on the *yǐhài* day, the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the southern suburbs.
In the intercalary month, on the *gēngxū* day,
supervising secretaries Ài Hóng, Lǚ Chōng, Liú Mào, and Nanjing supervising secretary Dài Xiǎn, censors Báo Yànhuī, and nineteen others were flogged below the palace gates.
In the second month, on the *wùxū* day,
censor Wáng Liángchén was flogged at the Wǔmén Gate,
and censor Wáng Shízhōng was put in a cangue at the Dūcháyuan.
In the third month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Dàxuéshì Liú Jiàn and Xiè Qiān,
and Shàngshū Hán Wén, Yáng Shǒusuí, Zhāng Fūhuá, Lín Hàn, and forty-nine others were accused of forming factions,
and all officials were warned.
In this month,
eunuchs serving as garrison commanders were ordered to involve themselves in criminal and political affairs.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
forty thousand monks and Daoists were ordained.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Níng Wáng Chénháo's guards were restored.
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Emperor Xiàozōng's spirit tablet was enshrined in the Tàimiào.
On the *wùyín* day,
the repair of border walls was halted,
and the funds were transferred to the capital.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
the Bàofáng was constructed.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
the巡撫都御史 (patrolling grand censors) of various borders and the grain-transporting *lángzhōng* were arrested and imprisoned.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Nanjing Hùbù Shàngshū Yáng Tínghé became Wényuāngé Dàxuéshì,
participating in state affairs.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénchén* day,
silver mines were opened in Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, and Sìchuān.
In this year,
Liúqiú sent tribute.
In the third year, spring, in the first month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the southern suburbs.
On the *xīnhài* day,
a grand evaluation of outer officials was conducted,
and an imperial decree dismissed Hànlín Xuéshì Wú Yǎn and censor Yáng Nánjīn.
In the second month, on the *jǐsì* day,
it was ordered that Beijing officials who exceeded their leave or were ill for a full year should all retire.
In the third month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Lǚ Nán and other *jìnshì* were granted degrees and official ranks with differences.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
soldiers and commoners who paid silver
could be appointed to offices from *dūzhīhuī qiānshì* downwards.
In the sixth month, on the *rénchén* day,
an anonymous document was found on the imperial path.
All officials were made to kneel outside the Fèntiānmén Gate and questioned.
More than three hundred people were imprisoned in the Jǐnyīwèi jail,
and later released.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
it was ordered that musicians from all over the realm be selected and sent to the capital.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
the Nèi Chǎng was established,
with Liú Jǐn in charge.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Hán Wén was sent to the Jǐnyīwèi prison,
and fined a thousand *shí* of rice to be transported to Dàtóng.
In this month,
bandits rose in Shāndōng.
In the ninth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the names of retired *shàngshū* Yōng Tài, Mǎ Wénshēng, Xǔ Jìn, and Liú Dàxià were expunged from the registers.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Liú Dàxià was arrested and imprisoned,
then exiled to Sùzhōu.
On the *guǐhài* day,
relief was provided for the famine in Nánjīng.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Nanjing Gōngbù Shìláng Bì Hēng provided famine relief in Húguǎng and Hénán.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
famine relief was provided in the prefectures of Fèngyáng.
In this year,
Ānnán, Hāmì, Sāmǎ'érhǎn, and Wūsīzàng sent tribute.
In the fourth year, spring, in the first month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Liú Jiàn and Xiè Qiān's names were expunged from the registers.
In the third month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
famine relief was provided in Zhèjiāng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Lìbù Shìláng Zhāng Cǎi requested irregular evaluations of Beijing officials,
and this was adopted.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Wáng Ào retired.
In the sixth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
Lìbù Shàngshū Liú Yǔ concurrently became Wényuāngé Dàxuéshì,
participating in state affairs.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
envoys were dispatched to verify military colonies in various border regions.
In this month,
there was a military mutiny in Yìzhōu.
In the intercalary ninth month,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ attacked Yánsuí,
besieging Zǒngbīngguān Wú Jiāng in the city of Lǒngzhōu.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
he attacked Huāmǎchí,
and Zǒngzhì Shàngshū Cái Kuān died in battle.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
the imperial edicts of appointment for Liú Jiàn, Xiè Qiān, and 675 other individuals were revoked.
In this year,
bandits rose simultaneously in Liǎngguǎng, Jiāngxī, Húguǎng, Shǎnxī, and Sìchuān.
Liúqiú, Ānnán, Hāmì, Tǔlúfān, and Sāmǎ'érhǎn sent tribute.
In the fifth year, spring, in the first month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the southern suburbs.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the property of the deceased *shàngshū* Qín Hóng was confiscated.
In the second month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Bīngbù Shàngshū Cáo Yuán became Lìbù Shàngshū and concurrently Wényuāngé Dàxuéshì,
participating in state affairs.
In the third month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
prayers for rain were offered,
prisoners were released,
and outstanding taxes from the third year of Zhèngdé were waived.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
rebels in Jiāngxī became rampant.
Yòudū Yùshǐ Wáng Zhé was sent to inspect Nánchāng and Gànzhōu.
Xíngbù Shàngshū Hóng Zhōng was appointed commander-in-chief of military affairs in Chuān, Shǎn, Hénán, and Yúnshàng, and concurrently provided relief in Húguǎng.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *gēngyín* day,
Ānhuà Wáng Zhìpàn rebelled,
killing Xúnfǔ Dū Yùshǐ Ān Wéixué and Zǒngbīngguān Jiāng Hàn.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Yòudū Yùshǐ Yáng Yīqīng was appointed commander-in-chief of military affairs in Níngxià, Yánsuí, Gānzhōu, and Liángzhōu,
and Jīngyáng Bó Shén Yīng was made commander-in-chief
to suppress Zhìpàn.
On the *xīnhài* day,
an imperial edict pardoned the realm.
Eunuch Zhāng Yǒng was appointed governor-general of military affairs in Níngxià.
On this day,
Youjī Jiāngjūn Qiú Yuè ambushed and captured Zhìpàn,
and Níngxià was pacified.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Jiāo Fāng retired.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
the emperor proclaimed himself Dàqìng Fǎwáng,
and the relevant department cast a seal and presented it.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Liú Yǔ was dismissed.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *rénshēn* day,
Hóng Zhōng suppressed the Miǎnyáng rebels,
pacifying them.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Liú Jǐn was imprisoned for treason.
An imperial edict ordered that all political decrees changed since the second year of Zhèngdé revert to the old system.
On the *wùxū* day,
Liú Jǐn's faction was punished,
and Lìbù Shàngshū Zhāng Cǎi was imprisoned.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Cáo Yuán was dismissed.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Níng Wáng's guards were abolished.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Liú Jǐn was executed.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
exiled and banished officials were released.
In the ninth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
the merits of pacifying Zhìpàn were discussed,
and Qiú Yuè was enfeoffed as Xiánníng Bó.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Lìbù Shàngshū Liú Zhōng and Liáng Chǔ both concurrently became Wényuāngé Dàxuéshì,
participating in state affairs.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
for their merits in pacifying Zhìpàn and Liú Jǐn,
eunuch Zhāng Yǒng's elder brother Fù and younger brother Róng were both enfeoffed as *bó*.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the adopted son Zhū Dé, who was a *zhīhuī tóngzhī*, and eunuch Gǔ Dàyòng's elder brother Dàkuān, Mǎ Yǒngchéng's elder brother Shān, and Wèi Bīn's younger brother Yīng were all enfeoffed as *bó*.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day *Jǐhài*,
Zhāng Cǎi’s corpse was exposed in the market.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Jǐchǒu*,
the rebels captured Jiāngjīn,
and the Assistant Administrator Wú Jǐng died there.
In this year,
Japan, Zhànchéng, Hāmì, Sāmǎ’érhǎn, Tǔlúfān, and Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the sixth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day *Guǐyǒu*,
the rebels captured Yíngshān,
killing Assistant Administrator Wáng Yuán.
In the second month, on the day *Bǐngshēn*,
Zhì Pán was executed.
On the day *Jǐyǒu*,
Chén Jīn, the Left Censor-in-Chief, was appointed to command the military affairs of Jiāngxī to suppress the rebels.
In the third month, on the day *Wùchén*,
Yáng Shèn and others were granted the degrees of *Jìnshì Jídì* and *Chūshēn* with differing ranks.
On the day *Gēngwǔ*,
the Earl of Huì’ān, Zhāng Wěi, was appointed General-in-Chief,
and Mǎ Zhōngxī, the Right Censor-in-Chief, was made Military Governor,
to suppress the rebels in Zhílì, Hénán, and Shāndōng.
On the day *Bǐngzǐ*,
districts and counties affected by rebels were exempted from land tax for one year.
In this month,
the Little Prince entered Hétào
and raided various border forts.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day *Guǐwèi*,
Liú Zhōng requested leave to visit his ancestors’ tombs.
In this month,
robbers rose in Huái’ān.
In the sixth month,
robbers rose in Shānxī.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day *Rénshēn*,
the rebels attacked Wén’ān,
and the capital was put on alert.
On the day *Guǐyǒu*,
troops from Xuānfǔ and Yánsuí were dispatched to reinforce.
In the eighth month, on the day *Jǐmǎo*,
Lù Wán, the Vice Minister of War, led border troops to suppress the rebels.
Lín Jùn, the Grand Coordinator of Sìchuān and Censor-in-Chief, captured and beheaded the rebel leaders Lán Tíngruì and Yān Běnsù.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
the rebel Liú Liù attacked Gù’ān.
On the day *Bǐngxū*,
Zhāng Wěi and Mǎ Zhōngxī were recalled.
In the ninth month, on the day *Bǐngyín*,
troops from Xuānfǔ and Liáodōng were again dispatched to reinforce Lù Wán’s army.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day *Guǐwèi*,
the rebels captured Chángshān,
and the Registrar Lǐ Xiān died in battle.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
the rebels burned grain ships in Jìníng Zhōu.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
Bái Cóng, the Vice General-in-Chief of Gānzhōu, defeated the Little Prince at Cháigōu.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Gēngxū*,
the eunuchs Gǔ Dàyòng and Zhāng Zhōng,
and the Earl of Fúqiāng, Máo Ruì, led the capital army to join Lù Wán in suppressing the rebels.
On the day *Bǐngchén*,
Cóng Lán and Wáng Qióng, Vice Ministers of Revenue, provided relief to the Two Capital Regions, Hénán, and Shāndōng.
On the day *Wùwǔ*,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
an imperial edict for self-reflection was issued.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
exposed bones were buried.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Guǐsì*,
Fèi Hóng, the Minister of Rites, concurrently served as Grand Secretary of the Wényuāngé,
participating in state affairs.
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
from Qīnghékǒu to Liǔpù,
the Yellow River ran clear for three days.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
the rebels plundered Cāngxī,
and Fēng Jié, the Vice Commissioner of Military Preparedness, was defeated and died.
In this year,
from the Capital Region to Jiāng, Huái, Chǔ, and Shǔ, bandits killed officials,
with Shāndōng being particularly severe,
where over ninety cities were breached,
and roads were cut off.
Liúqiú and Hāmì presented tribute.
In the seventh year, in spring, in the first month, on the day *Jiǎyín*,
the rebels attacked Bàzhōu,
and the capital was put on alert.
On the day *Dīngsì*,
Dàchéng was captured,
and Zhāng Rǔzhōu, the County Magistrate, and Lǐ Quán, the Chief Clerk, died in battle.
On the day *Jǐwèi*,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the day *Dīngchǒu*,
Péng Zé, the Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Qiú Yuè, the Earl of Xiánníng, were appointed Military Governors,
and the eunuch Lù Yín was appointed Superintendent of the Army,
to suppress the Hénán rebels.
On the day *Jǐmǎo*,
the rebels attacked Láizhōu,
and Cài Xiǎn, the Assistant Commander, and others fought valiantly and died.
In the third month, on the day *Xīnwèi*,
Shí Yuán, the Vice General-in-Chief, suffered a defeat in Hénán,
and Fēng Zhēn, the Assistant Grand Commissioner, fought valiantly and died.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
Lù Wán defeated the rebels at Láizhōu,
and the Shāndōng rebellion was quelled.
On the day *Jiǎyín*,
Chén Jīn suppressed the rebels in Fúzhōu.
On the day *Bǐngyín*,
the rebels killed Mǎ Bǐngrán, the Vice Censor-in-Chief, in the river near Wǔchāng.
In the intercalary month, on the day *Rénchén*,
Qiú Yuè defeated the rebels at Guāngshān,
and the Hénán rebellion was quelled.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day *Guǐsì*,
the Jiāngxī rebels killed Zhōu Xiàn, the Vice Commissioner, at Huálín.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
relief was provided for famine in Sìchuān.
In the eighth month, on the day *Guǐhài*,
Lù Wán pursued and annihilated the rebels led by Liú Qī and others at Lángshān.
In the ninth month, on the day *Yǐyǒu*,
Chén Jīn suppressed the rebels in Huálín.
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
Hóng Zhōng was recalled.
Péng Zé, the Censor-in-Chief, was appointed to command the military affairs of Sìchuān.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
one hundred and twenty-seven adopted sons were granted the imperial surname.
In winter, in the tenth month,
Hénán, Jiāngxī, and Zhèjiāng were exempted from land tax due to disasters and rebel attacks.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Rénshēn*,
Shí Yuán was appointed General for Quelling Rebels,
to join Péng Zé in suppressing the Sìchuān rebels.
On the day *Dīnghài*,
troops from Dàtóng, Xuānfǔ, and Liáodōng were retained in the capital garrisons;
Lǐ Dōngyáng admonished against this,
but was not heeded.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Dīngmǎo*,
Lǐ Dōngyáng retired.
In this month,
the Two Capital Regions, Shāndōng, Shānxī, and Shǎnxī were exempted from land tax due to disasters and rebel attacks.
In this year,
Ānnán, Japan, and Hāmì presented tribute.
In the eighth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day *Guǐyǒu*,
Yú Jiàn, the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, replaced Chén Jīn in suppressing the Jiāngxī rebels.
On the day *Rénwǔ*,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day *Yǐyǒu*,
Jiāng Bīn and Xǔ Tài, border generals, were appointed to command the capital garrisons separately,
and were granted the imperial surname.
Soon, two official halls for military affairs were established,
and Bīn and Tài were ordered to command them separately.
On the day *Guǐsì*,
Cóng Lán, the Vice Minister of Revenue, and Chén Yù, the Assistant Censor-in-Chief, inspected the border.
In the second month, on the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
for their achievements in quelling rebels,
Gǔ Dàyòng’s younger brother Dàliàng and Lù Yín’s nephew Yǒng, both eunuchs, were enfeoffed as Earls.
In the third month, on the day *Wùzǐ*,
the Zhènguófǔ was established to house the official troops of Xuānfǔ.
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
due to drought, an imperial edict instructed all officials to reflect and mend their ways.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day *Yǐchǒu*,
Péng Zé defeated the rebels at Jiànzhōu.
In the fifth month, on the day *Xīnsì*,
Qiú Yuè was appointed General-in-Chief,
and led the capital garrisons to defend against the enemy at Dàtóng.
In the sixth month, on the day *Wùxū*,
the river burst its banks at Huánglínggāng.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
Yú Jiàn defeated the rebels at Guìxī.
In autumn, in the eighth month,
the Southern Capital Region was exempted from land tax due to flood.
Tǔlúfān attacked and occupied Hāmì.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day *Dīngwèi*,
Yú Jiàn repeatedly defeated the rebels in Dōngxiāng,
and the Jiāngxī rebellion was quelled.
In the twelfth month,
Dèng Zhāng, the Vice Minister of Justice of Nánjīng, provided relief for famine in Jiāngxī.
In this year,
Hāmì presented tribute.
In the ninth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day *Dīngchǒu*,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the day *Gēngchén*,
the Qiánqīnggōng suffered a fire.
In the second month, on the day *Gēngzǐ*,
the Emperor first began his private excursions.
On the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
Jìn Guì, the Minister of Rites, concurrently served as Grand Secretary of the Wényuāngé,
participating in state affairs.
On the day *Guǐchǒu*,
Péng Zé and Shí Yuán suppressed the Sìchuān rebels.
In the third month, on the day *Xīnsì*,
Táng Gāo and others were granted the degrees of *Jìnshì Jídì* and *Chūshēn* with differing ranks.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day *Dīngyǒu*,
the guards of Prince Níng were restored,
and granted garrison land.
In the fifth month, on the day *Yǐchǒu*,
Fèi Hóng retired.
On the day *Jǐchǒu*,
Péng Zé was appointed Grand Coordinator of military affairs in Gānsù,
and managed Hāmì.
In the sixth month, on the day *Yǐmǎo*,
the silver mines of Yúnnán were opened.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ attacked Xuānfǔ and Dàtóng.
Grand Eunuch Zhāng Yǒng was appointed Superintendent of Military Affairs,
and Dūdū Bái Yù was appointed Commander-in-Chief.
They led the capital's garrison to repel him.
In the eighth month, on Xīnmǎo, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On Xīnchǒu,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ attacked Báiyángkǒu.
On Yǐsì,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On Jǐwèi,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ entered Níngwǔguān,
plundering Xīnzhōu, Dìngxiāng, and Nínghuà.
In the ninth month, on Rénxū,
he attacked Xuānfǔ and Wèizhōu.
On Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor was injured while playing with a tiger
and did not hold court.
Compiler Wáng Sī was demoted to Stationmaster of Ráopíng for remonstrating.
In winter, the tenth month, on Jǐyǒu,
envoys were dispatched to collect timber in Chuān and Hú.
In the eleventh month, on Xīnyǒu,
Guīshàn Wáng Dānghù was deposed as a commoner
and committed suicide.
In the twelfth month, on Jiǎyín,
Qianqing Palace was built,
and a tax of one million was added to the empire.
In this year,
Ānnán, Hāmì, and Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the tenth year, spring, the first month, on Guǐhài,
at dusk,
a sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
On Wùchén,
at dusk,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth in the Southern Suburb.
In the third month, on Rénshēn,
Yáng Tínghé resigned due to mourning.
In summer, the intercalary fourth month, on Xīnyǒu,
Minister of Personnel Yáng Yīqīng concurrently held the title of Grand Secretary of the Wǔyīng Diàn,
participating in state affairs.
On Wùyín,
Péng Zé was recalled.
In autumn, the eighth month, on Bǐngyín,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ attacked Gùyuán.
In winter, the twelfth month, on Guǐchǒu, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On Jǐmǎo,
autumn grain taxes were remitted due to drought in Nánjī.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Ānnán, Hāmì, and Sāmǎ'érhǎn presented tribute.
In the eleventh year, spring, the first month, on Yǐwèi,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the Southern Suburb.
In summer, the fourth month,
famine relief was provided in Hénán.
In the fifth month, on Gēngyín,
Tǔlǔfān returned with Hāmì.
On Jiǎchén,
more than 3,400 eunuchs were recorded to serve as maritime households.
In this month,
famine relief was provided in Shǎnxī.
In autumn, the seventh month, on Yǐwèi,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ attacked Jìzhōu and Báiyángkǒu.
Grand Eunuch Zhāng Zhōng was appointed Superintendent of Military Affairs,
and Left Dūdū Liú Huī was appointed Commander-in-Chief.
They led the armies of the Eastern and Western Official Halls to repel him.
On Bǐngwǔ,
Vice Ministers of Works Zhào Huáng and Yú Lín were ordered to inspect military preparations within the capital region.
In the eighth month, on Dīngsì,
Left Grand Censor Péng Zé and Chéngguó Gōng Zhū Fǔ led the capital's garrison to defend the border.
On Gēngshēn,
each person affected by the invasion in Wǎnpíng County was given two shí of rice.
On Jiǎzǐ,
Yáng Yīqīng retired.
On Dīngchǒu,
Minister of Rites Jiǎng Miǎn concurrently held the title of Grand Secretary of the Wényuān Gé,
participating in state affairs.
In the ninth month,
Tǔlǔfān reoccupied Hāmì,
invaded Sùzhōu,
and killed Guerrilla Commander Ruì Níng.
In winter, the tenth month, on Jǐyǒu, the first day of the month,
a sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào,
with envoys dispatched to perform the rites on behalf of the Emperor.
In the eleventh month, on Jiǎshēn,
tax grain was remitted due to disasters in Húguǎng.
In this year,
Liúqiú and Tiānfāng presented tribute.
In the twelfth year, spring, the first month, on Jǐchǒu,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the Southern Suburb.
The Emperor then hunted in Nánhǎizǐ,
returning in the middle of the night
to the Fèngtiān Diàn to receive congratulations.
In the third month, on Guǐsì,
Shū Fēn and others were awarded jinshi titles and ranks.
On Wùxū,
salt taxes from Liǎnghuái, Zhèjiāng, Sìchuān, and Hédōng were allocated for textile production in Shǎnxī.
In summer, the fourth month, on Rénzǐ,
Jìn Guì retired.
On Bǐngchén,
Vice Commander-in-Chief Zhèng Lián defeated Tǔlǔfān at Guāzhōu.
In the fifth month, on Bǐngzǐ,
Minister of Rites Máo Jì concurrently held the title of Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé,
participating in state affairs.
In the sixth month, on Yǐsì, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In autumn, the eighth month, on Jiǎchén,
the Emperor traveled in disguise to Chāngpíng.
On Yǐsì,
Liáng Chǔ, Jiǎng Miǎn, and Máo Jì caught up with him at Shāhé
and requested his return,
but he did not listen.
On Jǐyǒu,
he arrived at Jūyōngguān.
Censor of the Pass Zhāng Qīn closed the pass and defied the order,
so he returned.
On Bǐngchén,
he returned from Chāngpíng.
On Wùwǔ,
he held court at night.
On Guǐhài,
Vice Grand Censor Wú Tíngjǔ provided famine relief in Húguǎng.
On Bǐngyín,
at night, he left Déshèngmén in disguise
and went to Jūyōngguān.
On Xīnwèi,
he left the pass
and visited Xuānfǔ,
ordering Gǔ Dàyòng to guard the pass
and not allow any capital officials to leave.
In the ninth month, on Xīnmǎo,
the river burst its banks at Chéngwǔ.
On Rénchén,
he went to Yánghé,
proclaiming himself Superintendent of Military Affairs and Grand General of Valiance and Might, Commander-in-Chief.
On Gēngzǐ,
one million taels of treasury silver were transported to Xuānfǔ.
In winter, the tenth month, on Guǐmǎo,
he stationed his carriage at Shùnshèngchuān.
On Jiǎchén,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ attacked Yánghé
and plundered Yìngzhōu.
On Dīngwèi,
the Emperor personally supervised the armies to repel him,
fighting for five days.
On Xīnhài,
the invaders withdrew,
and he stationed his carriage at Dàtóng.
In the eleventh month, on Dīnghài,
Yáng Tínghé was recalled to the cabinet.
On Wùzǐ,
he returned to Xuānfǔ.
In the twelfth month, on Guǐhài,
officials went to the imperial temporary residence to request his return to the palace,
but they were not allowed to pass through the gate and returned.
In the intercalary month, on Dīnghài,
the arrival of spring was celebrated at Xuānfǔ.
In this year,
Liúqiú and Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the thirteenth year, spring, the first month, on Xīnchǒu, the first day of the month,
the Emperor was in Xuānfǔ.
On Bǐngwǔ,
he returned from Xuānfǔ,
ordering officials to prepare colorful tents, sheep, and wine for a suburban welcome,
and received congratulations in the tent palace.
On Dīngwèi,
the fasting for the Southern Suburb sacrifice was abolished.
On Gēngxū,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth in the Southern Suburb,
and he then hunted in Nánhǎizǐ.
On Xīnhài,
he returned to the palace.
On Xīnyǒu,
he returned to Xuānfǔ.
In this month,
famine relief was provided due to floods in Liǎng Jī and Shāndōng.
Migrants in the capital were given rice,
three dǒu per person.
The dead were buried.
In the second month, on Jǐmǎo,
the Grand Empress Dowager passed away.
On Rénwǔ,
he returned from Xuānfǔ.
In the third month, on Wùchén,
he went to Chāngpíng.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day of Jǐsì, the first day of the month,
the emperor visited the Six Mausoleums,
and then proceeded to Mìyún.
In the fifth month, on the day of Jǐhài, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
The imperial carriage stopped at Xǐfēngkǒu.
On the day of Wùshēn,
the emperor returned from Xǐfēngkǒu.
In the sixth month, on the day of Gēngchén,
the Empress Dowager’s coffin departed from the capital,
and the emperor, in military attire, followed.
On the day of Jiǎshēn,
Empress Xiàozhēnchún was buried.
On the day of Yǐyǒu,
the emperor returned from Chāngpíng.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day of Jǐhài,
the merits from the Yingzhōu campaign were recorded,
and over fifty thousand people received promotions or rewards through imperial favor.
On the day of Bǐngwǔ,
the emperor again went to Xuānfǔ.
In the eighth month, on the day of Yǐyǒu,
the emperor went to Dàtóng.
In the ninth month, on the day of Gēngzǐ,
the imperial retinue reached Piāntóuguān.
On the day of Guǐchǒu,
an imperial decree stated:
“Zhū Shòu, Grand Coordinator of Military Affairs, Valiant Grand General, and Commander-in-Chief, personally led the six armies,
and cleared the border regions.
He is specially enfeoffed as Zhènguó Gōng,
and shall receive an annual stipend of five thousand shí of grain.
The Ministry of Personnel shall implement this decree.”
On the day of Jiǎyín,
Zhū Bīn was enfeoffed as Pínglǔ Bó,
and Zhū Tài as Ānbiān Bó.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day of Wùchén,
the emperor crossed the river.
On the day of Jǐmǎo,
the imperial retinue reached Yúlín.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Gēngzǐ,
the troops from the western official office and the four guard camps were transferred to Xuān and Dà.
On the day of Rénzǐ,
the imperial retinue reached Suídé,
and the emperor visited the residence of Commander-in-Chief Dài Qīn.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Wùyín,
the emperor crossed the river
and visited Shízhōu.
On the day of Wùzǐ,
the imperial retinue reached Tàiyuán.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Tiānfāng, and Wǎlà paid tribute.
In the fourteenth year, spring, first month, on the day of Bǐngshēn, the first day of the month,
the emperor was in Tàiyuán.
On the day of Jiǎchén,
the site for the suburban sacrifice was re-divined.
On the day of Rénzǐ,
the emperor returned to Xuānfǔ.
In the second month, on the day of Rénshēn,
the emperor arrived from Xuānfǔ.
On the day of Dīngchǒu,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the southern suburb,
and then the emperor hunted at Nánhǎizi.
On this day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day of Jǐchǒu,
the emperor promoted himself to Tàishī,
and instructed the Ministry of Rites, saying:
“Zhū Shòu, Grand Coordinator of Military Affairs, Valiant Grand General, Commander-in-Chief, Tàishī, and Zhènguó Gōng, is to patrol the Two Jī and Shāndōng,
to offer sacrifices to the gods and pray for blessings.
Prepare the ceremonies and report them.”
In the third month, on the day of Guǐchǒu,
for remonstrating against the imperial tour,
six persons, including Huáng Gǒng, the Lángzhōng of the Ministry of War, were imprisoned in the Jǐnyī Wèi prison,
and one hundred and seven persons, including Xiūzhuàn Shū Fēn, were made to kneel at Wǔmén for five days.
Zhāng Yīng, the Dūzhīhuī Qiānshì of the Jīnwú Wèi, attempted suicide by stabbing himself in remonstrance;
the guards disarmed him,
saving his life.
He was interrogated and tried,
and then beaten to death with a staff.
On the day of Yǐmǎo,
thirty-three persons, including Sìzhèng Zhōu, Xíngrénsī Fù Yú Tíngzàn, and Zhǔshì Lín Dàlù, were imprisoned in the Jǐnyī Wèi prison.
On the day of Wùwǔ,
Shū Fēn and one hundred and seven others were beaten with staves below the imperial palace.
On this day,
a dust storm darkened the sky during the day.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day of Jiǎzǐ,
the disaster tax grain in the Southern Jī was remitted.
On the day of Wùyín,
Huáng Gǒng and thirty-nine others were beaten with staves below the imperial palace;
eleven of them died in succession.
In the fifth month, on the day of Jǐhài,
an imperial edict stated that for migrants in Shāndōng, Shānxī, Shǎnxī, Hénán, and Húguǎng who returned to their occupations,
the government would provide food, housing, oxen, and seeds,
and exempt them from taxes for five years.
In the sixth month, on the day of Bǐngzǐ,
Níng Wáng Chénháo rebelled,
and Sūn Suì, the Xúnfǔ of Jiāngxī and Yòufù Dūyùshǐ, and Xǔ Kuí, the Nánchāng Bīngbèi Fùshǐ, died.
On the day of Wùyín,
Nánkāng fell.
On the day of Jǐmǎo,
Jiǔjiāng fell.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day of Jiǎchén,
the emperor personally led an expedition to suppress Chénháo.
Ānbiān Bó Zhū Tài was appointed Wēiwǔ Fùjiāngjūn,
leading the troops as vanguard.
On the day of Bǐngwǔ,
Chénháo attacked Ānqìng,
but Dūzhīhuī Yáng Ruì and Zhīfǔ Zhāng Wénjǐn repelled him.
On the day of Xīnhài,
Tídū Nán Gàn Tīng Zhāng Jūnwù Fù Dūyùshǐ Wáng Shǒurén led troops to retake Nánchāng.
On the day of Dīngsì,
Wáng Shǒurén defeated Chénháo at Qiáoshě
and captured him.
In the eighth month, on the day of Guǐwèi,
the imperial carriage departed from the capital.
On the day of Dīnghài,
the imperial retinue reached Zhuōzhōu,
Wáng Shǒurén’s victory report arrived,
but it was secretly withheld.
In the winter, eleventh month, on the day of Yǐsì,
the emperor fished at Qīngjiāngpǔ.
On the day of Rénzǐ,
it was the winter solstice,
and the emperor received congratulations at the residence of Grand Eunuch Zhāng Yáng.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Xīnyǒu,
the imperial retinue reached Yángzhōu.
On the day of Yǐyǒu,
the emperor crossed the river.
On the day of Bǐngxū,
the emperor arrived in Nánjīng.
In this year,
Huái and Yáng suffered from famine,
and people resorted to cannibalism.
Sàmǎ'érhǎn paid tribute.
In the fifteenth year, spring, first month, on the day of Gēngyín, the first day of the month,
the emperor was in Nánjīng.
On the day of Guǐsì,
the site for the suburban sacrifice was re-divined.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day of Jǐwèi,
famine relief was provided to the prefectures of Huái and Yáng.
In the sixth month, on the day of Dīngsì,
the imperial retinue reached Niúshǒushān,
and all the armies were alarmed during the night.
In the autumn, seventh month,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ invaded Dàtóng and Xuānfǔ.
In the eighth month, on the day of Guǐwèi,
the tax grain in Jiāngxī was remitted.
In the intercalary month, on the day of Guǐsì,
the captives from Jiāngxī were received.
On the day of Dīngyǒu,
the emperor departed from Nánjīng.
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
the imperial retinue reached Zhènjiāng,
the emperor visited the residence of Grand Secretary Yáng Yīqīng,
and attended the funeral of the late Grand Secretary Jìn Guì.
In the ninth month, on the day of Jǐsì,
the emperor fished at Jīshuǐchí,
the boat capsized,
but he was rescued,
and subsequently fell ill.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day of Gēngxū,
the imperial retinue reached Tōngzhōu.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Gēngshēn,
those who conspired with Chénháo were punished,
and Lù Wán, Shàngshū of the Ministry of Personnel, was arrested and brought to the imperial temporary residence.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Jǐchǒu,
Chénháo was executed.
On the day of Jiǎwǔ,
the emperor returned to the capital,
and reported the victory at the suburban altars, ancestral temples, and altars of soil and grain.
On the day of Dīngyǒu,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was offered at the southern suburb,
but the emperor fell ill during the initial offering
and could not complete the ceremony.
In this year,
Liúqiú, Zhànchéng, Fólángjī, and Tǔlǔfān paid tribute.
In the spring of the sixteenth year, in the first month, on the day `Guǐhài` (癸亥),
a new site for the suburban sacrifice was chosen.
In the second month, on the day `Jǐhài` (己亥),
Hé Mèngchūn (何孟春), the Vice Censor-in-Chief supervising Yúnnán (雲南), suppressed the Miao (苗) in Mílè (彌勒) Prefecture.
In the third month, on the first day `Guǐchǒu` (癸丑),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day `Gēngshēn` (庚申),
the Western Official Bureau was reorganized into the Wēiwǔ (威武) Encampment.
On the day `Yǐchǒu` (乙丑),
the Emperor's illness became critical.
He issued an edict to the Directorate of Ceremonial, saying:
"My illness cannot be cured.
Convey my intentions to the Empress Dowager.
The affairs of the state are grave;
consult with the Grand Secretaries to manage them.
All previous mistakes were due to me,
not something you officials could have anticipated."
On the day `Bǐngyín` (丙寅),
he passed away in the Leopard Chamber,
at the age of thirty-one.
His dying edict summoned the eldest son of `Xīngxiàn` (興獻) Prince to succeed to the throne.
The Wēiwǔ Encampment was abolished,
and the frontier troops were sent back to their respective borders.
Imperial shops inside and outside the capital were abolished,
and the Tibetan monks from the Leopard Chamber and musicians from the Imperial Music Bureau were released.
On the day `Wùchén` (戊辰),
the dying edict was promulgated throughout the empire.
Imprisoned individuals were released,
women offered from all directions were returned,
non-urgent public works were suspended,
and the gold and treasures from the `Xuānfǔ` (宣府) temporary palace were returned to the imperial treasury.
On the day `Gēngwǔ` (庚午),
Jiāng Bīn (江彬) and others were arrested and imprisoned.
Shìzōng (世宗) ascended the throne.
In the fifth month, on the day `Jǐwèi` (己未),
the Emperor was granted a posthumous honorific title,
and his temple name was Wǔzōng (武宗).
He was buried in Kānglíng (康陵).
The encomium states: From the Zhèngtǒng (正統) reign,
the power of the Míng (明) dynasty gradually weakened.
Yìhuáng (毅皇) personally eliminated the treacherous Jǐn (瑾) [i.e., Liú Jǐn (劉瑾)],
and personally repelled border invaders,
striving to assert his might through military achievements.
However, he indulged in pleasure and amusement,
and befriended petty individuals,
even to the point of personally conferring official titles,
completely disregarding the distinction between high and low.
Fortunately, he personally held the power of appointing officials,
and the ministers holding key positions mended and rectified things,
thus, though the court administration was disordered,
it did not reach a state of danger and ruin.
If he had continued the legacy of Xiàozōng (孝宗),
exercised restraint and prudence,
and possessed the conduct of a moderate ruler,
then the country would have been peaceful and his reputation complete.
How could he have incurred the criticism of later generations?
Collations:
Annals Volume XVII, Shìzōng I.
Shìzōng (世宗) Qīntiānlǚdào Yīngyì Shèngshén Xuānwén Guǎngwǔ Hóngrén Dàxiào Sùhuángdì (欽天履道英毅聖神宣文廣武洪仁大孝肅皇帝),
whose personal name was Hòucōng (厚熜),
was the grandson of Xiànzōng (憲宗).
His father was `Xīngxiàn` Prince Yòuwán (祐杬),
who was enfeoffed in Ānlù (安陸).
He died in the fourteenth year of Zhèngdé (正德).
The Emperor was thirteen years old,
and as the Heir Apparent, he managed state affairs.
In the sixteenth year, in the third month, on the day `Xīnyǒu` (辛酉),
before the mourning period was over,
he was specially ordered to inherit the title.
On the day `Bǐngyín` (丙寅),
Wǔzōng died,
leaving no heir.
Císhòu (慈壽) Empress Dowager, together with Grand Secretary Yáng Tínghé (楊廷hé), decided on the successor.
They sent eunuchs Gǔ Dàyòng (谷大用), Wéi Bīn (韋彬), Zhāng Jǐn (張錦),
Grand Secretary Liáng Chǔ (梁儲),
Duke Dìngguó (定國公) Xú Guāngzuò (徐光祚),
Imperial Son-in-Law Commander Cuī Yuán (崔元),
and Minister of Rites Máo Chéng (毛澄),
bearing the dying edict, to welcome the Prince from his `Xīng` (興) residence.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the day `Guǐwèi` (癸未),
he departed from Ānlù.
On the day `Guǐmǎo` (癸卯),
he arrived at the capital,
stopping outside the suburbs.
The ritual officials prepared the ceremonies,
requesting that he ascend the throne according to the rites for an Imperial Crown Prince.
The Prince looked at Chief Clerk Yuán Zōnggāo (袁宗皐) and said:
"The dying edict names me to succeed to the imperial throne;
I am not an imperial son."
Grand Secretary Yáng Tínghé and others requested that the ceremonies prepared by the ritual officials be followed,
entering through the Dōng'ān (東安) Gate to reside in Wénhuá (文華) Hall,
and choosing a day to ascend the throne.
He did not consent.
At this time, the Empress Dowager urged the assembled officials to submit a memorial requesting his enthronement.
He then received the memorial outside the suburbs.
On that day,
at midday,
he entered through the Dàmíng (大明) Gate,
sent officials to report to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Altars of Land and Grain,
paid respects before the funerary tablet of the deceased Emperor,
paid homage to the Empress Dowager,
and then proceeded to the Fèngtiān (奉天) Hall,
where he ascended the imperial throne.
The following year was designated the first year of Jiājìng (嘉靖),
and a general amnesty was granted throughout the empire.
Officials who had been punished or dismissed for speaking out during the Zhèngdé reign were rehabilitated and compensated.
Half of the land tax for the following year was remitted throughout the empire,
and all overdue taxes from before the fifteenth year of Zhèngdé were completely waived.
On the day `Bǐngwǔ` (丙午),
envoys were dispatched to respectfully welcome his mother, Imperial Consort Jiǎng (蔣氏).
Fèi Hóng (費宏) was recalled to rejoin the Grand Secretariat.
On the day `Wùshēn` (戊申),
ritual officials were ordered to collectively deliberate on the posthumous title for `Xīngxiàn` Prince.
In the fifth month, on the day `Yǐmǎo` (乙卯),
the silver mines of Dàlǐ (大理) were closed.
On the day `Bǐngchén` (丙辰),
Liáng Chǔ retired from office.
On the day `Rénxū` (壬戌),
Assistant Minister of Personnel Yuán Zōnggāo was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of Wényuān (文淵) Hall,
participating in crucial government affairs.
On the day `Rénshēn` (壬申),
Qián Níng (錢寧) was executed.
In the sixth month, on the day `Wùzǐ` (戊子),
Jiāng Bīn was executed.
On the day `Yǐwèi` (乙未),
the birds and beasts in the imperial gardens were released,
and the empire was ordered not to offer any more as tribute.
On the day `Dīngyǒu` (丁酉),
over thirty thousand superfluous military officers of the Imperial Bodyguard were dismissed.
On the day `Wùxū` (戊戌),
disaster relief was provided in Jiāngxī (江西).
On the day `Rényín` (壬寅),
the practice of 'hereditary promotion' of officials was abolished.
On the day `Guǐmǎo` (癸卯),
famine relief was provided in Liáodōng (遼東).
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the day `Rénzǐ` (壬子),
the `jìnshì` (進士) Zhāng Cōng (張璁) submitted a memorial, stating
that the succession was of the imperial line, not of a son,
and requested that his birth parents be honored,
and a temple for `Xīngxiàn` Prince be erected in the capital.
Initially,
the ritual officials had proposed that Xiàozōng be considered his father,
and `Xīngxiàn` Prince be referred to as Imperial Uncle,
referencing Chéng Yí's (程頤) discussion on the rites for Pú (濮) Prince, and submitted this.
It was not approved.
At this point,
Zhāng Cōng's memorial was sent down,
and court officials were ordered to deliberate.
Yáng Tínghé and others strongly argued against it in memorials,
but none were heeded.
On the day `Guǐchǒu` (癸丑),
it was ordered that from now on, one must not be exempted from mourning for one's parents due to official duties,
and this was established as a regulation.
On the day `Dīngsì` (丁巳),
the Little Prince (小王子) attacked Zhuānglàng (莊浪),
and Commander Liú Jué (劉爵) repelled him.
On the day `Bǐngzǐ` (丙子),
newly appointed or enlisted members of the Imperial Bodyguard, directorates, bureaus, temples, factories, treasuries, banner officers, soldiers, and artisans,
totaling over one hundred forty-eight thousand people, were dismissed.
On the day `Dīngchǒu` (丁丑),
bandits arose in Níngjīn (寧津),
and the Prefect of Dépíng (德平), Gōng Liàng (龔諒), died.
In the ninth month, on the day `Yǐmǎo` (乙卯),
Yuán Zōnggāo passed away.
On the day `Gēngwǔ` (庚wu),
Emperor Yì (毅皇帝) was buried in Kānglíng.
In the winter, in the tenth month, on the first day `Jǐmǎo` (己卯),
his father, `Xīngxiàn` Prince, was posthumously honored as Emperor `Xīngxiàn` (興獻帝);
his paternal grandmother, Consort Shào (邵氏) of Xiànzōng, was honored as Empress Dowager;
and his mother, Imperial Consort, was honored as Empress `Xīngxiàn` (興獻后).
On the day `Rénwǔ` (壬午),
Empress `Xīngxiàn` arrived from Ānlù.
In the eleventh month, on the day `Gēngxū` (庚戌),
disaster relief was provided in Jiāngxī.
On the day `Dīngsì` (丁巳),
for his meritorious service in suppressing Chén Háo (宸濠), Wáng Shǒurén (王守仁) was enfeoffed as Count Xīnjiàn (新建伯).
On the day
`Jiǎxū` (甲戌),
the Qiánqīng (乾清) Palace was completed.
The tribute of incense from Guǎngxī (廣西) was abolished.
An edict was issued to the garrison and defense officials in all regions,
stating that all extraordinary levies should be abolished.
In the spring of the first year of Jiājìng, on the guǐchǒu day of the first month,
a great sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
On the jǐwèi day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
The rear hall of the Qīngníng Palace suffered a fire.
It was ordered that Xiàozōng be referred to as Huángkǎo,
Císhòu Huángtàihòu as Shèngmǔ,
and Xīngxiàn Dìhòu as Benshēng Fùmǔ.
On the jǐsì day,
there was a military rebellion in Gānzhōu,
and Xǔ Míng, the巡撫 Dūyùshǐ, was killed.
In the second month, on the jǐmǎo day,
the ritual plowing of the Jítián was performed.
In the third month, on the xīnhài day,
the Fútí Guard presented a live leopard,
but it was rejected.
On the jiǎyín day,
a sacrifice was offered to the Former Teacher Kǒngzǐ.
On the dīngsì day,
the honorific title of Císhòu Huángtàihòu was elevated to Zhāoshèng Císhòu Huángtàihòu,
and Wǔzōng's Empress was titled Zhuāngsù Huánghòu.
On the wǔwǔ day,
the honorific title of Huángtàihòu was elevated to Shòu'ān Huángtàihòu,
and Xīngxiàn Hòu was titled Xīngguó Tàihòu.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the rénchén day,
it was ordered that the巡按 Yùshǐ in each border region inspect military horses and weaponry once every three years.
In the autumn of the seventh month, on the jǐyǒu day,
due to drought in Nánjī, Zhèjiāng, Jiāngxī, Húguǎng, and Sìchuān,
an imperial edict instructed the Fǔ'àn officials to study and implement famine relief policies.
In the ninth month, on the xīnwèi day,
Empress Chén was established.
In the winter of the tenth month, on the xīnmǎo day,
relief was provided for disasters in Nánjī, Húguǎng, Jiāngxī, and Guǎngxī,
with tax exemptions varying by degree.
On the rénchén day,
due to disasters and damage, an imperial edict instructed officials to reflect and reform.
In the eleventh month, on the gēngshēn day,
Shòu'ān Huángtàihòu passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the wùyín day,
relief was provided for those in Shǎnxī affected by bandits and those in Shāndōng subjected to attacks by mining rebels.
This year,
Líuqiú paid tribute.
In the spring of the second year, on the yǐmǎo day of the first month,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the dīngmǎo day,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ attacked Shāhé Bǎo,
and Zǒngbīngguān Háng Xióng fought and repelled him.
In the second month, on the guǐwèi day,
relief was provided for famine in Liáodōng.
On the rénchén day,
Zǒngdū Jūnwù Yòudū Yùshǐ Yú Jiàn and Zǒngbīngguān Lǔ Gāng pacified the bandits in Hénán and Shāndōng.
In the third month, on the yǐsì day,
Āndá raided Dàtóng.
On the jiǎyín day,
Wǔzōng's spirit tablet was enshrined in the Tàimiào.
On the wùwǔ day,
Yáo Lái and others were granted the Jinshì Jídì and Chūshēn degrees, with varying distinctions.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the rénshēn day,
due to calamities and unusual phenomena, an imperial edict instructed officials to reflect and reform.
On the kuǐwèi day,
Shù, a descendant of Sòng Zhū Xī, was appointed as Wǔjīng Bóshì.
On the kuǐsì day,
it was ordered that officials of third rank or higher in the two capitals and Fǔ'àn officials recommend suitable candidates for local administrators.
In the fifth month, on the gēngwǔ day,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ attacked Mìyún Shítánglǐng,
killing Zhǐhuīshǐ Yīn Lóng.
In the sixth month, on the guǐchǒu day,
due to calamities and damage, half of the land tax for the first year of Jiājìng was remitted throughout the empire.
In the autumn of the eighth month, on the xīnyǒu day,
Xiǎo Wángzǐ attacked Dīngzì Bǎo,
and Dū Zhǐhuī Wáng Gāng died in battle.
In the winter of the eleventh month, on the dīngmǎo day,
tax exemptions were granted for disaster-stricken areas in Nánjī.
On the jǐchǒu day,
relief was provided for famine in Hénán.
This year,
Sāmǎ'érhǎn, Tǔlǔfān, and Tiānfāng paid tribute.
In the spring of the third year, on the bǐngyín day, the first day of the month,
earthquakes occurred simultaneously in the two capitals, Hénán, Shāndōng, and Shǎnxī.
On the dīngchǒu day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the bǐngxū day,
Guì È, a Zhǔshì of the Nánjīng Xíngbù, requested that Xiàozōng be referred to as Huángbókǎo,
and the matter was submitted to court officials for deliberation.
In this month,
Yǐnyán launched an invasion.
In the second month, on the bǐngwǔ day,
Yáng Tínghé retired.
On the gēngxū day,
there was an earthquake in Nánjīng.
In the third month, on the rénshēn day,
relief was provided for famine in Huái and Yáng.
On the xīnsì day,
relief was provided for famine in Hénán.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the jǐyǒu day,
the honorific title of Zhāoshèng Huángtàihòu was elevated to Zhāoshèng Kānghuì Císhòu Huángtàihòu.
On the gēngxū day,
the honorific title of Xīngguó Tàihòu was elevated to Benshēng Shèngmǔ Zhāngshèng Huángtàihòu.
On the guǐchǒu day,
Xīngxiàn Dì was posthumously honored as Benshēng Huángkǎo Gōngmù Xiàndì,
and a general amnesty was declared.
On the xīnyǒu day,
Biānxiū Zōu Shǒuyì requested to abolish the title of Xīngxiàn Dì as Kǎo and the establishment of his temple,
and he was imprisoned in the Jǐnyīwèi jail.
In the fifth month, on the yǐchǒu day,
Jiǎng Miǎn retired.
Xiūzhuàn Lǚ Nán spoke about the "Great Rites" not being properly settled,
and he was imprisoned in the Jǐnyīwèi jail.
On the dīngchǒu day,
envoys were dispatched to welcome the spirit tablet of Xiàndì from Ānlù.
On the jǐmǎo day,
Shí Bǎo, the Lìbù Shàngshū, was concurrently appointed Wényuāngé Dàxuéshì,
participating in state affairs.
In the sixth month,
Yùshǐ Duàn Xù and Chén Xiāng requested the punishment of Xí Shū and Guì È,
Lìbù Yuánwàiláng Xuē Huì submitted an explanation for being adopted,
Hónglú Shàolíng Hú Shì spoke about the errors in the ritual discussions of Zhāng Cōng and others,
and all were imprisoned.
In the autumn of the seventh month, on the yǐhài day,
the honorific title of Zhāngshèng Huángtàihòu was revised,
removing the term Benshēng.
On the wùyín day,
court officials knelt at the palace gate to strongly remonstrate,
and 134 people, including Yuánwàiláng Mǎ Lǐ, were imprisoned in the Jǐnyīwèi jail.
On the guǐwèi day,
Mǎ Lǐ and others were flogged in court,
and sixteen people died.
On the jiǎshēn day,
the spirit tablet of Xiàndì was respectfully enshrined in the Guāndé Hall.
On the jǐchǒu day,
Máo Jì retired.
On the xīnmǎo day,
Xiūzhuàn Yáng Shèn,
Jiǎntǎo Wáng Yuánzhèng,
Jǐshìzhōng Liú Jì, Ān Pán, Zhāng Hànqīng, Zhāng Yuán,
and Yùshǐ Wáng Shíkē were flogged in court.
Zhāng Yuán died,
and Yáng Shèn and others were exiled with varying sentences.
In this month,
tax exemptions were granted for disaster-stricken areas in Nánjī and Hénán.
In the eighth month, on the guǐsì day,
there was a military mutiny in Dàtóng,
and Zhāng Wénjǐn, the 巡撫 Dūyùshǐ, was killed.
On the yǐmǎo day,
Jiǎ Yǒng, the Lìbù Shìláng, was appointed Lǐbù Shàngshū and concurrently Wényuāngé Dàxuéshì,
participating in state affairs.
In the ninth month, on the bǐngyín day,
it was decided that Xiàozōng be referred to as Huángbókǎo,
Zhāoshèng Huángtàihòu as Huángbómǔ,
Xiàndì as Huángkǎo,
and Zhāngshèng Huángtàihòu as Shèngmǔ.
On the bǐngzǐ day,
an imperial edict was issued to the empire.
On the bǐngxū day,
Tǔlǔfān invaded,
besieging Sùzhōu.
Jīn Xiànmín, the Bīngbù Shàngshū, was appointed Zǒngzhì Jūnwù,
Háng Xióng, the Shǔ Dūdū Qiānshì, was appointed Zǒngbīngguān,
and eunuch Zhāng Zhōng was appointed Tídū Jūnwù,
to resist the invasion.
In the winter of the eleventh month, on the jǐmǎo day,
Hú Zàn, the Hùbù Shìláng, was appointed Tídū Xuān-Dà Jūnwù,
and Dūdū Lǔ Gāng was appointed Zǒngbīngguān,
to suppress the rebellious soldiers of Dàtóng.
In the twelfth month, on the rénzǐ day,
the bandits in Gān and Liáng retreated,
and Jīn Xiànmín was recalled.
On the wùwǔ day,
the retired Dàxuéshì Yáng Yīqīng was reinstated as Bīngbù Shàngshū,
to oversee military affairs of the three border regions in Shǎnxī.
This year,
Líuqiú paid tribute,
and Lǔmí Guó presented lions and rhinoceroses as tribute.
In the spring of the fourth year, on the bǐngyín day,
Bǔ'érhái from Xīhǎi attacked Gānsù,
and Zǒngbīngguān Jiāng Shì defeated him.
On the xīnwèi day,
a grand sacrifice was offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the yǐmǎo day,
the protracted detention of prisoners was prohibited.
In the third month, on the rénwǔ day,
Rénshòu Palace suffered a fire.
In the summer of the fifth month, on the jiǎxū day,
Lóng Gào, the Zhīfǔ of Lúzhōu, was granted an official rank,
and an imperial edict commanded the empire to emulate Lóng Gào's methods for preparing for famine and providing relief.
On the gēngchén day,
the Shìmiào was constructed to worship Xiàndì.
In the eighth month, on the wùzǐ day,
Rénshòu Palace was rebuilt.
In the winter of the tenth month, on the dīnghài day,
the Yùdé Hall,
and the two palaces Jǐngfú and Ānxǐ were constructed.
In the twelfth month, on the xīncǒu day,
the comprehensive discussion on the Great Rites was concluded,
and it was promulgated throughout the empire.
On the first day of the intercalary month, on the yǐmǎo day,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the yǐhài day,
relief was provided for disasters in Liáodōng.
That year,
Tiānfāng (Mecca or Arabia) paid tribute.
In the spring, the first month, on the day Yǐwèi, of the fifth year,
grand sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎyín,
the Daoist Shào Yuánjié was granted the title of Zhēnrén.
On the day Gēngchén,
taxes on grain for disaster-stricken Shanxī were remitted.
On the day Rénwǔ,
relief was provided for the famine in the capital (Jīngshī).
In the third month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Gōng Yòngqīng and others were granted the titles of Jìnshì and other ranks, with distinctions.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the law regarding long-term tenure for officials of the judicial administration (Yǒusī) was established.
In the summer, the fifth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Yáng Yīqīng was reinstated to the Grand Secretariat.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the day Gēngyín,
taxes on grain for disaster-stricken Sìchuān were remitted.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
relief was provided for the famine in Húguǎng.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Empress Dowager Zhāngshèng conducted ceremonies at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Shìmiào).
In the winter, the tenth month, on the first day Xīnhài,
he personally performed sacrifices following the rites of the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
On the day Rénzǐ,
relief was provided for disasters in Nánjī (Southern Capital region) and Zhèjiāng,
and taxes on grain and materials were remitted.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the "Jìngyī Zhēn" (Admonition on Reverence and Unity) written by the emperor was promulgated in the schools (Xuégōng).
That year,
Xiāmluó (Siam) paid tribute.
In the spring, the first month, on the day Guǐwèi, of the sixth year,
ministers were ordered to report on the advantages and disadvantages among the people.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
grand sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the day Xīnhài,
the Little Prince invaded Xuānfǔ,
and Assistant General Wáng Jīng died in battle.
On the day Guǐhài,
Fèi Hóng and Shí Bǎo retired.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Xiè Qiān was recalled to rejoin the Grand Secretariat.
In the third month, on the day Gēngchén,
the raiders again invaded Xuānfǔ,
and Assistant General Guān Shān died in battle.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Zhái Luán, Vice Minister of Rites, was made Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrently an Academician of the Hanlin Academy,
entering the Grand Secretariat to participate in government affairs.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the day Jǐsì,
taxes on grain for disaster-stricken Guǎngxī were remitted.
In the fifth month, on the first day Dīngchǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Dīnghài,
Wáng Shǒurén, former Minister of War of Nanjing, was concurrently made Left Censor-in-Chief,
to command military affairs in Liǎngguǎng, Jiāngxī, and Húguǎng,
to suppress the rebellious barbarians in Tiánzhōu.
In the autumn, the eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
due to the discussion of the case of Lǐ Fúdá,
Yán Yíshòu, Minister of Justice, Niè Xián, Left Censor-in-Chief, Tāng Mù, Grand Judge of the Dali Temple, and others were imprisoned by the Jǐnyīwèi,
while Guì È and Zhāng Cōng, Vice Ministers,
and Fāng Xiànfū, Junior Reader of the Hanlin Academy, were appointed to oversee the three judicial offices (sānfǎsī),
to jointly interrogate them.
Commander-in-Chief Wáng Xiàn defeated the Little Prince at Shíjiùdūn.
On the day Guǐhài,
Jiǎ Yǒng retired.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Húguǎng.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
autumn grain taxes for disaster-stricken Jiāngxī, Hénán, and Shanxī were remitted.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the "Qīnmíng Dàyù Lù" (Record of the Emperor's Great Judgment) was promulgated throughout the empire.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the day Wùshēn,
Zhāng Cōng, Vice Minister of War, was made Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Academician of the Wènyuān Pavilion,
participating in government affairs.
That year,
Lǔmí (Rum) paid tribute.
In the spring, the first month, on the day Guǐwèi, of the seventh year,
an assessment was conducted of all provincial governors (Xúnfǔguān).
On the day Bǐngxū,
grand sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the third month, on the day Wùyín,
Xiè Qiān retired.
On the day Guǐsì,
Wǔ Wéndìng, Right Censor-in-Chief, was made Minister of War and Commissioner of Military Affairs,
and Liáng Cái, Vice Minister, was appointed to oversee grain storage,
to suppress the rebellious barbarians in Yúnnán.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
sweet dew fell,
and it was reported to the suburban altars and ancestral temples.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the "Mínglún Dàdiǎn" (Great Canon of Human Relations) was completed
and promulgated throughout the empire.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the crimes of the ministers who debated the Rites were determined,
and Yáng Tínghé and others were posthumously stripped of their official registers.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the barbarians in Yúnnán were pacified.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Empress Dowager Xiàohuì was posthumously honored as Grand Empress Dowager,
and Emperor Gōngmùxiàn was posthumously honored as Emperor Gōngruì Yuānré Kūanmù Chúnshèngxiàn.
On the day Xīnsì,
Empress Dowager Zhāngshèng was honored as Empress Dowager Zhāngshèng Círén.
On the day Wùzǐ,
an imperial edict was issued to the empire.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
taxes on grain for disaster-stricken Hénán were remitted.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Wáng Shǒurén suppressed the barbarians in Guǎngxī,
pacifying them all.
On the day Rénwǔ,
relief was provided for disasters in Jiāxīng and Húzhōu.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
the Empress passed away.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Consort Shùn, née Zhāng, was established as Empress.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Little Prince invaded Dàtóng,
and Commander Zhào Yuán died in battle.
That year,
Liúqiú (Ryukyu) paid tribute.
In the spring, the first month, on the day Jǐhài, of the eighth year,
relief was provided for the disaster in Shanxī.
On the day Gēngxū,
grand sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
In the second month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Guì È, Minister of Personnel, was concurrently made Grand Academician of the Wǔyīng Hall,
participating in government affairs.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
relief was provided for the famine in Xiāngyáng.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
there was a drought,
and the emperor personally prayed at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
he prayed to the gods of soil and grain (Shèjì).
In the third month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Empress Dàolíng was buried.
On the day Wùxū,
relief was provided for the famine in Hénán.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Luó Hóngxiān and others were granted the titles of Jìnshì and other ranks, with distinctions.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
due to improper deliberations in a case,
Langzhong Wèi Yīngzhāo and others were imprisoned,
and Xióng Jiá, Right Censor-in-Chief, was stripped of his official register.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Zhāng Cōng and Guì È were dismissed.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the emperor began personally offering sacrifices to mountains and rivers,
which was established as a regulation.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐsì,
Zhāng Cōng was recalled to rejoin the Grand Secretariat.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Yáng Yīqīng was dismissed.
That month,
taxes on grain for disaster-stricken Liǎngjī (two metropolitan regions) and Hénán were remitted,
and relief was provided for famine in Jiāngxī and Húguǎng.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the first day Guǐhài,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Jǐsì,
hereditary enfeoffment of imperial relatives by marriage (Wàiqī) was abolished,
and established as a regulation.
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Guì È was recalled to rejoin the Grand Secretariat.
On the day Jiǎchén,
relief was provided for the disaster in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Wùshēn,
prayers were offered for snow.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
it snowed.
On the day Dīngsì,
the emperor personally went to the suburban altar to offer thanks.
All officials presented congratulations.
That year,
Tiānfāng, Sāmǎ'érhǎn (Samarkand), and Tǔlǔfān (Turpan) paid tribute.
In the spring, the first month, on the day Dīngyǒu, of the ninth year,
grand sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Altar to the First Silkworm (Xiāncántán) was constructed at the Northern Suburb.
On the day Dīngsì,
relief was provided for the famine in Shanxī.
In the second month, on the day Wùchén,
the emperor personally plowed the ceremonial field (Jítián).
On the day Yǐhài,
relief was provided for the famine in the capital (Jīngshī).
On the day Dīngchǒu,
officials and commoners were prohibited from exceeding regulations in their clothing, dwellings, and implements.
In the third month, on the day Dīngsì,
the Empress personally performed the silkworm rite at the Northern Suburb.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
relief was provided for the famine in Yánsuī.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐhài,
the Four Suburban Altars were rebuilt.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐhài,
schools were established for the families of Kǒng, Yán, and Mèng in Qūfù.
In the eighth month, *rénwǔ* day, of autumn,
tax grain was remitted for areas in Jiāngxī affected by disaster.
In the ninth month, *rénchén* day,
the eunuch garrison commanders in Yúnnán were dismissed.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
autumn grain taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken areas in Nánjī.
In the eleventh month, *xīnchǒu* day, of winter,
the sacrificial rites for the Temple of Kǒngzǐ were corrected and standardized,
and the posthumous title for Kǒngzǐ was designated as Zhìshèng Xiānshī Kǒngzǐ.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
sacrifices were offered to Hào Tiān Shàngdì in the southern suburbs.
After the ceremony was completed,
a general amnesty was granted.
In this year,
Liúqiú offered tribute.
In the first month, *xīnmǎo* day, of spring in the tenth year,
prayers for a good harvest were offered at the Dàsì Diàn,
with Tàizǔ and Tàizōng enshrined as co-worshippers.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
temple sacrifices were re-established,
and Dézǔ was enshrined in the Tiāomiào.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Guì È resigned from office.
In the second month, *jiǎxū* day,
autumn grain taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken areas in Lú, Fèng, Huái, and Yáng.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Zhāng Cōng was granted the name Fújìng.
In the third month, *wùshēn* day,
the eunuch division commanders in Sìchuān were dismissed.
In the fourth month, *dīngsì* day, of summer,
the Empress personally conducted sericulture in the Xīyuàn.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the *dì* sacrifice was performed at the Tàimiào.
In the fifth month, *rénzǐ* day,
sacrifices were offered to Huángdì Qí at the Fāngzé.
In the intercalary sixth month, *jǐchǒu* day,
the eunuch garrison commanders in Zhèjiāng, Húguǎng, Fújiàn, Liǎngguǎng, as well as Dúshí, Wànquán, and Yǒngníng, were dismissed.
In the seventh month, *guǐchǒu* day, of autumn,
Vice Minister Yè Xiāng provided relief to the famine in Shǎnxī.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Zhāng Fújìng was dismissed.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Zhèng Wáng Hòuhán presented a white sparrow,
which was offered to the ancestral temple.
In the eighth month, *xīnchǒu* day,
Ānlù Zhōu was renamed Chéngtiān Fǔ.
In the ninth month, *yǐchǒu* day,
the palaces in the Xīyuàn were completed,
and a ceremony was held to offer sacrifices to Chéngzǔ's spirit tablet,
followed by a banquet for the officials.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Lǐ Shí, Minister of the Board of Rites, concurrently served as Grand Secretary of the Wényuān Gé,
and participated in state affairs.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor visited the Xīyuàn,
held court at the Wúyì Diàn,
commanded Lǐ Shí and Zhái Luán to lecture,
and hosted a banquet for the Confucian ministers at the Bīnfēng Tíng.
In the eleventh month, *jiǎyín* day, of winter,
sacrifices to Heaven were offered in the southern suburbs.
On the *wùchén* day,
autumn grain taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken areas in Shǎnxī.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Zhāng Fújìng was summoned to re-enter the Grand Secretariat.

In the first month of the first year of Lóngqìng,
an honorary posthumous title was bestowed.
His temple name was Shìzōng,
and he was buried in Yǒnglíng.
A eulogy states: At the beginning of Shìzōng’s reign,
he vigorously abolished all harmful policies,
and the empire universally praised his rule.
However, successive debates on the Grand Rites
stirred public opinion,
and favored officials, using this as a pretext,
soon instigated a great inquisition.
The profound natural affection and the great righteousness between ruler and parents—
to posthumously honor and establish a temple
was indeed appropriate by ritual standards.
However, to enthrone him in the Grand Ancestral Temple,
and place him above Wǔzōng,
was that not excessive?
At that time,
there were many chaotic events:
the borders were weary,
and bandits caused strife internally.
Yet, he favored Taoism,
his sacrifices were not regular,
construction projects were extensive,
and the imperial treasury reported depletion.
The prosperity and peace of over a hundred years
gradually declined as a result.
Although he eliminated powerful corrupt officials
and held authority firmly,
he was ultimately a ruler of mediocre talent.

Annals, Chapter 19: Mùzōng
Emperor Mùzōng Qìtiān Lóngdào Yuānyì Kuānrrén Xiǎnwén Guāngwǔ Chúndé Hóngxiào Zhuāng,
personal name Zǎihòu,
was the third son of Shìzōng.
His mother was Consort Dù Kāng.
In the second month of the eighteenth year of Jiājìng, he was enfeoffed as Prince Yù,
receiving his patent on the same day as Crown Prince Zhuāngjìng and Prince Jǐnggōng.
Later, when Zhuāngjìng died,
Shìzōng, seeing the prince as eldest and worthy,
and the succession already settled,
and with external and internal concerns and repeated remonstrances,
ordered Prince Jǐng to his demesne.
On *gēngzǐ* day,
in the twelfth month of the forty-fifth year,
Shìzōng passed away.
On *rénzǐ* day,
he ascended the imperial throne.
The next year was designated the first year of Lóngqìng,
and a general amnesty was declared throughout the empire.
Former policies of the previous court that were inconvenient
were all changed according to the imperial will.
Officials who had been punished for their remonstrances were recalled,
and those who had died were granted posthumous honors and pensions.
All Taoist practitioners were handed over to the judicial authorities for punishment.
All Taoist rituals and construction projects, as well as irregular procurements, were abolished.
Half of the land tax for the next year was remitted,
as were outstanding taxes from before the forty-third year of Jiājìng.
Hǎi Ruì, a section chief in the Ministry of Revenue, was released from prison.
This year,
Tǔlǔfān offered tribute.

The encomium states: Mùzōng reigned for six years,
maintaining a respectful and inactive posture,
personally practicing frugality and moderation;
the imperial kitchen saved millions each year.
He permitted Āndá to be enfeoffed and pay tribute,
reduced taxes and eased the burden on the people,
and the borders were peaceful.

he can be called a good ruler.

and factionalism gradually emerged,
yet the emperor was unable to assert firm imperial authority,
or correct long-standing practices.
Perhaps he had an excess of leniency and forgiveness,
but lacked sternness and clear-sightedness.

Shénzōng Fàntiānhédào Zhésùdūnjiǎn Guāngzhāngwǔwǔ Ānrénzhǐxiào Xiǎnhuángdì,
personal name Yìjūn,

His mother was Noble Consort Lǐ.
In the second year of Lóngqìng,
he was made Crown Prince,
being then six years old.
He was exceptionally intelligent.
Mùzōng once galloped a horse in the palace,

"Your Majesty, as the ruler of all under Heaven,
riding alone and galloping,
are you not concerned about the danger of the bit and rein?"
Mùzōng was pleased,
dismounted, and praised him.
Empress Chén was ill in a separate palace.
Every morning, the Crown Prince accompanied the Noble Consort to inquire about her health.
When the Empress heard their footsteps, she would always be delighted,
and force herself to rise.
She would take classic texts and question him,
and he would answer without fail,
which also pleased the Noble Consort.
From then on, the two palaces became even more harmonious.

In the fifth year, spring, the first month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
an edict ordered Fèngyáng and Huái'ān to vigorously promote agricultural settlement.
In the second month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
relief was provided for famine in Guǎngxī.
In the third month, on the day Yǐsì,
Shěn Màoxué and others were granted the degrees of Jìnshì jízhì and Chūshēn with various ranks.
In summer, the fifth month, on the day Guǐsì,
the Luópáng Yáo in Guǎngdōng were pacified.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Guǐhài,
the Yellow River again burst its banks at Cuīzhèn.
In the intercalary month, on the first day Yǐyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse,
but it was not seen due to overcast clouds.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Zhāng Jūzhèng was reinstated.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Yǐsì,
for criticizing Zhāng Jūzhèng for "seizing affection" (not observing mourning),
Editor Wú Zhōngxíng, Compiler Zhào Yòngxián, Assistant Minister Ài Mù, and Secretary Shěn Sīxiào were flogged,
and dismissed or exiled to the frontier with varying sentences.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Jìnshì Zōu Yuánbiāo was flogged
and exiled to the frontier.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
officials were reviewed due to an unusual celestial phenomenon.
In this year,
Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the sixth year, spring, the first month,
the dikes of the breached river were built.
In the second month, on the day Wùxū,
outstanding taxes belonging to Yǎn, Qīng, Dēng, and Lái were remitted.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Empress Wáng was enthroned.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Mǎ Zìqiáng, Minister of Rites, concurrently became Grand Secretary of the Wényuāngé,
and Shēn Shíxíng, Vice Minister of Personnel, concurrently became Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé,
participating in policy decisions.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Zhāng Jūzhèng returned after burying his father.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
outstanding taxes in Húguǎng and Sìchuān were remitted.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
an edict ordered the Board of Revenue to increase the annual "gold flower silver" by two hundred thousand taels.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Zhāng Jūzhèng returned to Jīngshī.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Lǚ Diàoyáng retired.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
an edict ordered that in the prefectures north of the Jiāng River,
any commoner aged fifteen or above without land
would be given one ox and fifty *mǔ* of land by the government to cultivate,
with taxes to commence after three years.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
an edict ordered the prefectures of Sūzhōu to reclaim barren land,
with taxes to commence after six years.
On the day Xīnwèi,
executions were halted.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Mǎ Zìqiáng died.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven in the Southern Suburb.
In this year,
Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the seventh year, spring, the first month, on the day Wùchén,
an edict ordered the destruction of all academies nationwide.
In the second month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
envoys were dispatched to inspect border defenses in various regions.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
outstanding taxes in Huái and Yáng were remitted.
In summer, the fifth month, on the day Guǐhài,
sacrifices were offered to Earth in the Northern Suburb.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the land taxes of imperial relatives and nobility in the two capital regions, Shāndōng, and Shǎnxī were audited.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Rényǐn,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Sū and Sōng,
and grain taxes were remitted.
On the day Wùwǔ,
there was an earthquake in Jīngshī.
In this year,
Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the eighth year, in spring, the second month, on the *xīnwèi* (辛未) day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *wùzǐ* (戊子) day,
the ceremonial plowing of the Imperial fields took place.
On the *wùxū* (戊戌) day,
the Yellow River construction was completed.
In the third month, on the *xīnhài* (辛亥) day,
the two Empresses Dowager were escorted to Tiānshòu Shān (天壽山) to visit the Imperial mausoleums.
The land taxes in the areas passed through were exempted.
On the *jiǎyín* (甲寅) day,
they returned to the palace.
On the *dīngmǎo* (丁卯) day,
Zhāng Màoxiū (張懋修) and others were granted the *jìnshì jíyǐ* (進士及第) and *chūshēn yǒuchā* (出身有差) degrees.
In summer, the intercalary fourth month, on the *gēngshēn* (庚申) day,
the Guangxī (廣西) Bāzhài (八寨) bandits were suppressed.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *xīnchǒu* (辛丑) day,
redundant officials, both internal and external, were dismissed.
On the *yǐsì* (乙巳) day,
famine relief was provided in Sūzhōu (蘇), Sōngjiāng (松), Chángzhōu (常), and Zhènjiāng (鎮).
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngzǐ* (丙子) day,
an edict ordered the survey of private lands.
This year,
Ryūkyū (琉球) sent tribute.
In the ninth year, in spring, the first month, on the *gēngwǔ* (庚午) day,
an imperial decree ordered border officials to prepare for alerts.
On the *xīnwèi* (辛未) day,
redundant officials in various bureaus were cut.
On the *guǐyǒu* (癸酉) day,
the Tǔmán (土蠻) attacked Jǐnzhōu (錦州),
and patrol commander Zhōu Zhīwàng (周之望) was defeated and perished.
On the *jǐmǎo* (己卯) day,
four Hanlin (翰林) officials were ordered to be on duty daily.
On the *xīnsì* (辛巳) day,
redundant officials in Nánjīng (南京) were cut.
On the *jiǎshēn* (甲申) day,
Liaodong (遼東) Grand Commander Lǐ Chéngliáng (李成梁) attacked and defeated the Tǔmán (土蠻) at Àolángtù (襖郎兔).
In the third month, on the *bǐngyín* (丙寅) day,
a grand military review was held.
This month,
the Tǔmán (土蠻) attacked Liaoyáng (遼陽),
and Deputy Grand Commander Cái Fǔ (曹簠) resisted them
but was defeated.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *dīngyǒu* (丁酉) day,
famine relief was provided to disaster-stricken prefectures and counties in Shānxī (山西).
On the *yǐmǎo* (乙卯) day,
disaster relief was provided in Sūzhōu (蘇), Sōngjiāng (松), Huáiyáng (淮), Fèngyáng (鳳), Xúzhōu (徐), and Sùzhōu (宿).
The Ministry of Revenue submitted the *Wànlì Huìjì Lù* (萬曆會計錄).
In autumn, the eighth month, on the *dīngwèi* (丁未) day,
Yángzhōu (揚州) suffered a great flood.
In the ninth month, on the *dīnghài* (丁亥) day,
executions were suspended.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *jǐhài* (己亥) day,
the Tǔmán (土蠻) attacked Guǎngníng (廣寧) and Yìzhōu (義州),
but Lǐ Chéngliáng (李成梁) repelled them.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngxū* (丙戌) day,
disaster relief was provided in Zhēndìng (真定), Shùndé (順德), and Guǎngpíng (廣平),
and taxes and grain levies were exempted.
This year,
redundant officials in various provinces were cut,
corvée and taxes were scrutinized,
and excessive and wasteful expenditures by various bureaus were eliminated.
Ryūkyū (琉球), Annan (安南), Tǔlǔfān (土魯番), Tiānfāng (天方), Sāmǎ'érhǎn (撒馬兒罕), Lǔmí (魯迷), Hāmì (哈密), and Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏) sent tribute.
In the tenth year, in spring, the second month, on the *guǐsì* (癸巳) day,
Shùnyì Wáng (順義王) Āndá (俺答) passed away.
On the *dīngyǒu* (丁酉) day,
accumulated outstanding taxes throughout the empire were exempted.
In the third month, on the *gēngshēn* (庚申) day,
a military mutiny occurred in Hángzhōu (杭州),
and Governor Wú Shànyán (吳善言) was seized.
On the *dīngmǎo* (丁卯) day,
Vice Minister of War Zhāng Jiāyìn (張佳胤) was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng (浙江) to suppress and pacify it.
On the *bǐngzǐ* (丙子) day,
Sùbǎhài (速把亥), chieftain of Tàiníng Wèi (泰寧衛), attacked Yìzhōu (義州),
and Lǐ Chéngliáng (李 Chéngliáng) attacked and beheaded him.
On the *jǐmǎo* (己卯) day,
Japanese pirates raided Wēnzhōu (溫州).
In summer, the fourth month, on the *wùzǐ* (戊子) day, the first day of the month,
an imperial edict was sent to the Ministry of Rites,
ordering the people to engage in agriculture and sericulture in a timely manner
and not to indulge in idleness.
On the *jiǎwǔ* (甲午) day,
Mǎ Jǐng (馬景), a native soldier from Níngxià (寧夏), killed Assistant Regional Commander Xǔ Rǔjì (許汝繼),
and Governor and Censor-in-Chief Jìn Yìnghuái (晉應槐) pursued and executed him.
On the *gēngzǐ* (庚子) day,
due to a prolonged drought, an edict called for self-reflection and cultivation.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngshēn* (庚申) day,

the descendants of the Former Teacher Kǒngzǐ (孔子), and Song (宋) Confucian scholars Zhū Xī (朱熹), Lǐ Dòng (李侗), Luó Cóngyàn (羅從彥), Cài Shěn (蔡沈), Hú Ānguó (胡安國), Yóu Zuò (游酢), Zhēn Déxiù (真德秀), Liú Zǐhuī (劉子翬),
and deceased Grand Secretary Yáng Róng (楊榮) were granted varying exemptions from labor and taxation.
On the *gēngchén* (庚辰) day,
famine relief was provided within the capital region.
In the sixth month, on the *dīnghài* (丁亥) day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *rénchén* (壬寅) day,
famine relief was provided in Tàiyuán (太原), Píngyáng (平陽), and Lù'ān (潞安).
On the *yǐsì* (乙巳) day,
former Minister of Rites Pān Shèng (潘晟) was concurrently appointed Grand Secretary of the Wǔyīng Diàn (武英殿),
and Vice Minister of Personnel Yú Yǒudīng (余有丁) was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wényuān Gé (文淵閣),
participating in state affairs.
Pān Shèng (潘晟) was dismissed shortly thereafter.
On the *bǐngwǔ* (丙午) day,
Zhāng Jūzhèng (張居正) passed away.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *gēngwǔ* (庚午) day,
famine relief was provided in Píngliáng (平), Qìngyáng (慶), Yán'ān (延), Líntáo (臨), and Gǒngchāng (鞏).
In the ninth month, on the *bǐngchén* (丙辰) day,
due to the birth of the Imperial Eldest Son,
an edict pardoned the empire.
On the *jiǎzǐ* (甲子) day,
honorary titles were conferred upon the two Empresses Dowager.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *bǐngshēn* (丙申) day,
Sūzhōu (蘇) and Sōngjiāng (松) suffered a great flood,
and varying remissions and relief were granted.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénchén* (壬辰) day,
Grand Eunuch Féng Bǎo (馮保) was demoted to Imperial Attendant,
and his property was confiscated.
On the *rényín* (壬寅) day,
officials who had previously offered remonstrances had their posts restored.
This year,
disaster-stricken taxes and grain levies in the capital region and Shānxī (山西) were exempted.
Hāmì (哈密) and Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏) sent tribute.
In the eleventh year, in spring, the first month, on the *rénxū* (壬戌) day,
an imperial decree ordered strict border defenses.
In the intercalary second month, on the *jiǎzǐ* (甲子) day,
Āndá's (俺答) son Qǐqìnghā (乞慶哈) succeeded him as Shùnyì Wáng (順義王).
Myanmar (緬甸) raided Yǒngchāng (永昌).
On the *yǐchǒu* (乙丑) day,
the Emperor went to Tiānshòu Shān (天壽山) to visit the Nine Mausoleums,
and land taxes in the areas passed through were exempted.
On the *gēngwǔ* (庚午) day,
the Emperor went to Xīshān (西山) to visit the mausoleums of Empress Gōngràng Zhāng (恭讓章皇后) and Jǐng Huángdì (景皇帝).
On the *xīnwèi* (辛未) day,
he returned to the palace.
On the *yǐyǒu* (乙酉) day,
drought relief was provided to the five prefectures of Líntáo (臨), Gǒngchāng (鞏), Píngliáng (平), Yán'ān (延), and Qìngyáng (慶),
and land taxes were exempted.
In the third month, on the *jiǎshēn* (甲申) day,
Zhāng Jūzhèng's (張居正) official ranks were posthumously revoked.
On the *gēngzǐ* (庚zǐ) day,
Zhū Guózǔ (朱國祚) and others were granted the *jìnshì jíyǐ* (進士及第) and *chūshēn yǒuchā* (出身有差) degrees.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *dīngsì* (丁巳) day,
Zhāng Sìwéi (張四維) left office due to mourning.
On the *jǐwèi* (己未) day,
Vice Minister of Personnel Xǔ Guó (許國) was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé (東閣),
participating in state affairs.
On the *jiǎxū* (甲戌) day,
Chéngtiān (承天) experienced heavy rain,
and the river overflowed.
This month,
a military mutiny occurred in Luódìng (羅定), Guǎngdōng (廣東).
In the fifth month,
our Dà Qīng (大清) Tàizǔ Gāo Huángdì (太祖高皇帝) raised an army to conquer Níkān Wàilán (尼堪外蘭),
capturing Túlún Chéng (圖倫城).
In the sixth month, on the *yǐchǒu* (乙丑) day,
disaster relief was provided in Chéngtiān (承天), Hànyáng (漢陽), Yúnyáng (鄖陽), and Xiāngyáng (襄陽).
In autumn, the eighth month, on the *bǐngchén* (丙辰) day,
disaster-stricken taxes and grain levies in Shānxī (山西) were exempted.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎshēn* (甲申) day,
