the Emperor went to Tiānshòu Shān (天壽山) to visit the Imperial mausoleums.
On the *jǐchǒu* (己丑) day,
he returned to the palace.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *guǐhài* (癸亥) day,
executions were suspended.
On the *xīnwèi* (辛未) day,
Hénán (河南) suffered a flood,
and varying remissions and relief were granted.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐmǎo* (己卯) day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngwǔ* (庚午) day,
Cíníng Gōng (慈寧宮) suffered a disaster,
and an edict called for its repair and self-reflection.
This year,
Ryūkyū (琉球) sent tribute.
In the twelfth year, in spring, the second month, on the *dīngmǎo* (丁卯) day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the *jǐsì* (己巳) day,
the descendants of the exiled relatives of Jiànwén (建文) era officials were released from their banishment.
In the third month, on the *jǐhài* (己hài) day,
the production of porcelain in Jiāngxī (江西) was reduced.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *yǐmǎo* (乙卯) day,
Zhāng Jūzhèng's (張居正) family property was confiscated.
On the *dīngsì* (丁巳) day,
Patrol General Liú Tíng (劉綎) suppressed and pacified the Lǒngchuān (隴川) bandits.
In the fifth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* (甲午) day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the sixth month, on the *xīnhài* (辛亥) day,
due to military campaigns in Yúnnán (雲南),
taxes, grain levies, and outstanding arrears were exempted.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the *bǐngchén* (丙辰) day,
Zhāng Jūzhèng's (張居正) crimes were proclaimed to the empire,
and his family members were banished to the border.
In the ninth month, on the *bǐngxū* (丙戌) day,
the two Empresses Dowager were escorted to Tiānshòu Shān (天壽山) to visit the Imperial mausoleums.
On the *jǐchǒu* (己丑) day,
the Emperor's own tomb was constructed.
On the *xīnmǎo* (辛卯) day,
he returned to the palace.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *dìngsì* day,
executions were suspended.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
tax grain was remitted for disaster-stricken areas in Húguǎng and Shāndōng.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Yú Yǒudīng passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
former Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites, Wáng Xījué, was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Rites and concurrent Grand Secretary of the Wényuāngé,
and Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, Wáng Jiāpíng, was made concurrent Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé,
participating in state affairs.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the opening of silver mines was halted.
This year,
Ānnán and Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the thirteenth year, in spring, in the first month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
the troops of Jiànwǔ Suǒ in Sìchuān mutinied,
injuring Grand Commander Shěn Sīxué.
In the second month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Nánjīng experienced an earthquake.
The capital had not received rain since the eighth month of the previous year,
continuing until this month.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
a grand rain ritual was performed.
In the third month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
a grand rain ritual was performed.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Lǐ Chéngliáng led an expedition beyond the Great Wall to attack Bǎgē'ér Chǎohuā,
and heavily defeated them.
On the *rénchén* day,
the material silver for Hángzhōu weaving and the Imperial Robe Bureau was reduced.
Xú Zhēnmíng, Vice Supervisor of the Imperial Seal Office, oversaw the repair of irrigated fields in the capital region.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
a grand rain ritual was performed.
On the *wùshēn* day,
due to drought, an edict was issued to officials inside and outside the court to address injustices,
and release minor offenders in Fèngyáng and those long imprisoned for crimes.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the emperor walked to the Southern Suburb to pray,
and personally instructed the Grand Secretaries, saying:
"Although the drought
is due to Our lack of virtue,
it is also because officials throughout the empire are greedy,
exploiting the common people,
thereby offending the harmony of Heaven.
Henceforth, officials should be carefully selected."
One year's land rent was remitted for disaster-stricken areas throughout the empire.
In the fifth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
it rained.
In the sixth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Cínínggōng was completed.
On the *rènyín* day,
the mutinous soldiers of Jiànwǔ Suǒ were executed.
This month,
the aboriginal people of Sōng and Mào in Sìchuān rebelled.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the intercalary ninth month, on the *wùxū* day,
disaster relief was provided for Huái and Fèng.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the emperor went to Tiānshòushān to inspect the imperial tomb.
On the *wùshēn* day,
he returned to the palace.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
executions were suspended.
In winter, in the twelfth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
redundant eunuchs in the Xīxīn Sì were dismissed.
This month,
Shùnyì Wáng Qǐqìnghā passed away.
This year,
Tǔlǔfān and Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the fourteenth year, in spring, in the second month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
strict measures against gifts to outer officials were enforced.
In the third month, on the *wùxū* day,
due to drought and haze,
court officials were instructed to present proposals on current government affairs.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
officials in the Six Boards were forbidden from speaking on state affairs,
and the repair of irrigated fields in the capital region was suspended.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Táng Wénxiàn and others were granted advanced scholar degrees and official ranks with distinctions.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
due to a long drought,
an imperial edict for self-reflection and reform was issued.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
the Sōngmào aboriginal people were pacified.
This summer,
relief was provided for famine in Zhílì, Hénán, Shǎnxī, and in Xún, Liǔ, Pínglè in Guǎngxī,
and in twelve counties including Qióngshān in Guǎngdōng.
Bandits rose in Shānxī.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
disaster relief was provided for Jiāngxī.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial edict was issued to the Ministries of Revenue and War to appease disaster victims
and strictly enforce the *bǎojiǎ* system.
This month,
the bandit Wáng Ān in Qí Xiàn gathered a mob and plundered,
but was soon suppressed.
In the ninth month, on the *rénchén* day,
Wáng Jiāpíng left due to mourning.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
executions were suspended.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
funds were disbursed and envoys sent to provide disaster relief for Hénán, Shāndōng, Zhílì, Shǎnxī, Liáodōng, Huái, and Fèng.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
Lú Hóngchūn, a section chief in the Ministry of Rites, was flogged at the palace gate
and stripped of his office
for a memorial requesting careful attention to illness.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
sacrifices to Heaven were offered in the Southern Suburb.
This year,
Tǔlǔfān presented tribute.
In the fifteenth year, in spring, in the first month, on the *rénchén* day,
funds were disbursed for disaster relief for various imperial clans in Shānxī, Shǎnxī, Hénán, and Shāndōng.
In the third month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Qǐqìnghā's son, Chěli Kè, succeeded as Shùnyì Wáng.
In summer, in the fourth month,
the capital suffered from drought
and a major plague.
In the sixth month, on the *wùchén* day,
court officials were forbidden from extravagance and ostentation.
This month,
the capital received heavy rain.
Relief was provided for the poor.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
Húběi experienced locusts,
Jiāngnán suffered from severe floods,
Shānxī, Shǎnxī, Hénán, and Shāndōng suffered from drought,
and the Yellow River breached at Kāifēng.
Remissions and relief were provided with distinctions.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
due to frequent calamities,
an imperial edict ordered provincial governors and surveillance officials to punish corrupt officials,
address unjust cases,
remit taxes, and provide relief.
In the ninth month, on the *dīnghài* day, the first day of the month,
there was supposed to be a solar eclipse,
but it was not seen due to overcast skies.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
executions were suspended.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
Grand Secretary Shēn Shíxíng requested the release of memorials that had been withheld by the emperor.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
the troops in Yún Yáng rioted,
and the巡撫 *xúnfǔ* and Censor-in-Chief Lǐ Cái was dismissed.
This year,
Hāmì, Liúqiú, and Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the sixteenth year, in spring, in the third month, on the *rénchén* day,
an edict ordered the revision of the Veritable Records of Emperor Jǐng,
removing the title "Chéng Lì Wáng,"
but it was not carried out.
Shānxī, Shǎnxī, Hénán, and the Southern Capital region, and Zhèjiāng all suffered from severe famine and plague.
In summer, in the fourth month,
relief was provided for famine in Jiāngběi, Dàmíng, and Kāifēng prefectures.
In the fifth month,
the aboriginal people of Jiànchāng in Sìchuān rebelled and
were pacified.
On the *yǐsì* day,
due to the fire in the military granary and disasters in various provinces,
an imperial edict ordered officials inside and outside the court to reflect and reform.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
due to disasters, the weaving production in Sū and Háng was suspended and reduced.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
summer taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken Shāndōng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
a method for evaluating the performance of frontier officials was established.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
an edict ordered twenty thousand taels of silver from the imperial treasury to be used for inspection rewards at the imperial tombs.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
executions were suspended.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the emperor went to Tiānshòushān to inspect the imperial tomb.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
he stayed at Shíjǐngshān to observe the Húnhé River.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
he returned to the palace.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the troops in Gānsù mutinied,
and the *xúnfǔ* and Censor-in-Chief Cáo Zǐdēng was dismissed.
This month,
Tābùnáng, the chieftain of Qīnghǎi, attacked Xīníng,
killing Vice General Lǐ Kuí.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
memorials that were verbose were prohibited.
This year,
Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the spring of the seventeenth year, the first month, on the *jǐyǒu* day of the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *dīngsì* day,
bandits like Liú Rǔguó from Tàihú, Sù, and Sōng revolted.
Ānqìng Commander Chén Yuè was dispatched
to suppress them, but was defeated and died.
In the second month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
Wúsōng Commander Chén Màogōng suppressed and pacified them.
In the third month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
the custom of personally expressing gratitude for promotions and appointments was abolished.
From then on, the emperor's attendance at court became simpler.
On the *guǐhài* day,
soldiers in Yǒngchāng, Yúnnán mutinied.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Jiāo Hóng and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree and official positions with differing ranks.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Wáng Jiāpíng re-entered the Grand Secretariat.
The demonic monk Lǐ Yuánlǎng from Shǐxīng rebelled,
attacking Nánxióng.
Officials were dispatched to suppress and execute him.
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Zhéjiāng experienced a great storm,
and the sea overflowed.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Yǒngchāng mutiny was quelled.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Southern Jī region and Zhèjiāng suffered a great drought,
and Tàihú dried up.
Forty thousand *tàngjīn* (taels of silver) were issued for relief.
In the autumn, the eighth month, on the *rén yín* day,
the prohibition on anonymous denunciations was strictly enforced.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
executions were suspended.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the project to repair the breach in the Yellow River was completed.
In the twelfth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
an edict was issued to all officials, warning them not to engage in angry disputes or seek victory in their work.
That year,
Ānnán and Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the spring of the eighteenth year, the first month, on the *jiǎchén* day of the new moon,
Grand Secretary Shēn Shíxíng and others were summoned for an audience at Yùdé Palace.
The emperor presented his eldest son to them.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
famine relief was provided in Húguǎng.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the summer tax in the disaster-stricken Jī region was remitted.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Huǒluòchì, a tribal chief from Qīnghǎi, invaded the old Táozhōu.
Vice Regional Commander Lǐ Liánfāng was defeated and died.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the regulations for imperial relatives were revised,
allowing those without titles to manage their own affairs for the first time.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *gēngzǐ* day of the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Grand Secretaries were summoned to discuss border affairs,
and court officials were ordered to recommend military talents.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Zhèng Luò, Minister of War, was appointed Grand Coordinator for the four garrisons of Shǎnxī and the border affairs of Shānxī, Xuān, and Dà.
That month,
Huǒluòchì again invaded Hézhōu and Líntáo.
Commander-in-Chief Liú Chéngsì was defeated.
In the eighth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
the market rewards for Chèlìkè were suspended.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the *wùyín* day,
relief was provided to the soldiers and civilians in war-torn Líntáo.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
nine court officials were dispatched to inspect the borders.
That year,
Ānnán presented tribute.
In the spring of the nineteenth year, the first month,
Myanmar invaded Yǒngchāng and Téngyuè.
In the second month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Commander-in-Chief Yóu Jìxiān defeated the remaining forces of Huǒluòchì in Mǎngláchuān.
In the intercalary third month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
due to the appearance of a comet,
an imperial edict for self-reflection was issued.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
officials of the Censorate and Imperial Censors were reprimanded for "rumormongering and slandering the emperor,"
and each had a year's salary deducted.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
a sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
Thereafter, proxies were sent for all temple sacrifices.
In the fifth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
the native tribes of Sìchuān's four garrisons revolted.
Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Lǐ Shàngsī suppressed and pacified them.
In the sixth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Wáng Xíjué returned home for a visit.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
an edict was issued to court officials, stating
that the nation's affairs were in turmoil,
causing senior officials to repeatedly seek retirement.
Henceforth, those who engaged in rampant slander would be severely punished.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
land taxes for disaster-stricken Hénán were remitted.
In the ninth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
Xǔ Guó retired.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Shēn Shíxíng retired.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Zhào Zhìgāo, Vice Minister of Personnel, was appointed Minister of Rites;
Zhāng Wèi, former Vice Minister of Rites, was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
Both concurrently served as Grand Secretaries of the Dōnggé,
participating in crucial state affairs.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
officers of the capital garrisons rioted at Cháng'ān Gate.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an imperial edict settled the estates of imperial relatives.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
enemies from the Hétào tribes invaded Yúlín and Yánsuí.
Commander-in-Chief Dù Tóng defeated them.
That year,
locusts plagued the Jī region;
the Southern Jī region and Zhèjiāng suffered severe floods,
with varying degrees of tax exemption and relief.
Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the spring of the twentieth year, the first month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Mèng Yǎnghào, an official of the Censorate, was flogged below the palace for his words regarding the establishment of the heir apparent,
and stripped of his official status.
In the third month, on the *wùchén* day,
Bō Bài, a retired Vice Regional Commander from Níngxià, killed Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Dǎng Xīn and Vice Envoy Shí Jìfāng,
and occupied the city in rebellion.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Wáng Jiāpíng retired.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Wèi Xuézéng, Minister of War and Governor-General of Military Affairs, was dispatched to suppress the Níngxià rebels.
On the *wùyín* day,
Wēng Zhèngchūn and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree and official positions with differing ranks.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Commander-in-Chief Lǐ Rúsōng was appointed Supreme Commander of the Shǎnxī forces to suppress the rebels.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Yè Mèngxíong, Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief of Gānsù, led his troops to join Wèi Xuézéng in suppressing the rebels.
Chèlìkè captured rebels,
knocked at the gate to present captives,
and subsequently resumed the two years of market rewards.
In the fifth month,
Japanese invaders attacked Cháoxiǎn,
capturing the royal capital.
King Lǐ ● of Cháoxiǎn fled to Yìzhōu to seek help.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
the various armies advanced to Níngxià.
The rebels enticed the Hétào tribes to invade,
but the government forces repelled them.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
arrears of taxes in Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Vice Regional Commander Zǔ Chéngxùn led troops to reinforce Cháoxiǎn.
They fought the Japanese at Píngyǎng,
but were defeated.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Wèi Xuézéng, Governor-General of the Three Borders, was dismissed.
Yè Mèngxíong replaced him.
Soon after, Xuézéng was arrested and imprisoned.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐsì* day,
Sòng Yìngchāng, Vice Minister of War, was appointed Grand Coordinator for military affairs to defend against the Japanese.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered all Governors and Grand Coordinators nationwide to recommend military talents.
In the ninth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
the Níngxià rebellion was quelled.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the *rényín* day,
Lǐ Rúsōng was appointed Supreme Commander of military affairs for Jì, Liáo, Báodìng, and Shāndōng.
He was concurrently appointed Commander-in-Chief for coastal defense and repelling the Japanese,
to aid Cháoxiǎn.
That month,
disaster-stricken prefectures in the Jī region, Zhèjiāng, and Hénán received varying degrees of tax exemption and relief.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùchén* day,
the emperor presided at the Wǔmén,
receiving the Níngxià captives.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
due to the pacification of the Níngxià rebels,
an announcement was made to the whole empire.
That year,
Xiānmó and Tǔlǔfān presented tribute.
In the spring of the twenty-first year, the first month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Lǐ Rúsōng attacked the Japanese at Píngyǎng,
and captured it.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Wáng Xíjué returned to court.
On the *xīnsì* day,
an imperial edict decreed the simultaneous enfeoffment of the three imperial princes as kings.
Court officials strongly opposed,
and it was subsequently revoked.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Lǐ Rúsōng advanced to attack the royal capital,
but encountered the Japanese at Bìtíguǎn,
and was defeated.
In the second month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
an imperial edict commended the soldiers and officers of the eastern expedition.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Japanese abandoned the royal capital and fled.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
an imperial edict decreed that throughout the empire, during the summer months, prisoners should be reviewed,
and those with minor offenses should be released or have their sentences commuted,
following the example of the two capitals.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Japanese envoy Kǒnishi Hachibei (小西飛) requested peace.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
soldiers from the various border garrisons aiding Cháoxiǎn were recalled.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
a comet appeared;
an edict ordered self-reflection.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
due to disasters and unusual phenomena, an edict warned internal and external officials to implement practical policies.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
executions were suspended.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Gù Yǎngqiān, the Grand Coordinator of Jì and Liáo, was concurrently put in charge of Cháoxiǎn affairs.
Sòng Yìngchāng and Lǐ Rúsōng were recalled.
This year,
relief was provided for famine in Jiāngběi, Húguǎng, Hénán, Zhèjiāng, and Shāndōng.
Mine bandits greatly arose in Hénán.
Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the twenty-second year, spring, the first month, on the day Jǐhài,
an imperial edict stated that various provinces suffered from disasters,
with Shāndōng, Hénán, Xú, and Huái being particularly severe,
bandits were rising everywhere,
officials were negligent,
and imperial edicts were not being implemented.
Henceforth, pacifying the people and suppressing bandits would be the criteria for the promotion or demotion of Governors, Censors, and local officials.
In the second month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
the First Imperial Prince Chángluò began his studies.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
envoys were dispatched to provide relief in Hénán,
and land taxes were remitted.
In the third month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
an edict ordered the compilation of the National History.
In summer, the fourth month, on the first day Jǐyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the fifth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Chén Yúbì, Minister of Rites, and Shěn Yīguàn, Minister of Rites of Nánjīng, were both concurrently appointed Grand Secretaries of the Dōnggé Pavilion,
participating in state affairs.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Wáng Xījué retired.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
there was thunder and rain;
the Xīhuámén gate suffered a disaster,
and an edict ordered self-reflection.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Bóshītù, chieftain of the Hétáo tribes, invaded Yánsuí.
This month,
Mázǔ, the Grand General of Yánsuí, defeated the Hétáo tribal enemy at Xiàmǎguān.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Xíng Jiè, Vice Minister of War of Nánjīng, was appointed Grand Coordinator of military affairs in Chuān and Guì,
to suppress Yáng Yìnglóng, the Pacification Commissioner of Bōzhōu.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
an edict ordered Japanese envoys to come to court.
This month,
Chǎohuā invaded Liáodōng,
and Dǒng Yīyuán, the Grand General, defeated him.
This year,
Liúqiú and Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the twenty-third year, spring, the first month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Dūdū Qiānshì Lǐ Zōngchéng and Zhǐhuī Yáng Fānghéng were dispatched to enfeoff Tàigé Xiùjí as King of Rìběn.
In the third month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Zhū Zhīfān and others were granted the Jinshi degree and official positions with various distinctions.
In summer, the fifth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
an earthquake occurred in the capital;
an edict ordered self-reflection.
In autumn, the ninth month, on the day Wùyín,
Yǒngshàobǔ, chieftain of Qīnghǎi, invaded Gānsù,
and Cāncè Dáyún defeated him.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
an edict ordered the restoration of the Jiànwén reign title.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Húguǎng suffered disasters,
with tax exemptions and relief given differentially.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Grand Secretary Zhào Zhìgāo and others requested the release of memorials held by the emperor,
but there was no response.
This year,
Jiāngběi suffered great floods,
the Huái River overflowed,
inundating the ancestral mausoleum in Sīzhōu.
In the twenty-fourth year, spring, the second month, on the day Wùshēn,
Mázǔ attacked the Hétáo tribes
and defeated them.
In the third month, on the day Yǐhài,
the Qiánqīng and Kūnníng palaces suffered disasters,
and an edict ordered self-reflection.
On the day Rénchén,
an edict was issued criticizing himself.
This month,
Huǒluòchì invaded Táohé,
and Liú Tíng, the Grand General, attacked and repelled him.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Lǐ Zōngchéng fled from the Japanese camp back to Wángjīng.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùchén,
the Hétáo tribal enemy invaded Gānsù,
and Yáng Jùn, the Grand General, attacked and defeated them.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the enfeoffment of Japan was reconsidered,
and Dūdū Qiānshì Yáng Fānghéng and Yóují Shěn Wéijìng were ordered to go.
In the sixth month,
relief was provided for famine in Fújiàn.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Sūn Pīyáng, Minister of Personnel, requested the release of memorials for the promotion and appointment of officials,
but there was no response.
On the day Wùyín,
Empress Rénshèng Huáng Tàihòu passed away.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
eunuchs were first dispatched to open mines within the imperial domain.
Soon after,
mining was ordered in Hénán, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Zhèjiāng, and Shǎnxī,
with eunuchs in charge.
Officials repeatedly remonstrated, but were not heeded.
In the intercalary eighth month, on the first day Yǐchǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Grand Secretary Zhào Zhìgāo requested the emperor to hold court,
release memorials,
and stop mining,
but there was no response.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Yáng Fānghéng arrived in Rìběn,
but Tàigé Xiùjí refused the enfeoffment
and reinvaded Cháoxiǎn.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Empress Xiào'ān Zhuāng was buried.
This month,
the Hétáo tribes invaded Níngxià.
Lǐ Rúbǎi, the Grand General, attacked and defeated them.
This autumn,
the river breached at Huánggūkou.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
executions were suspended.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
eunuchs were first ordered to collect taxes in Tōngzhōu.
Thereafter,
tax commissioners were set up in all provinces.
Officials repeatedly remonstrated, but were not heeded.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐhài,
Chén Yúbì passed away.
Collation Notes
Annals Volume 21: Shénzōng II
In the twenty-fifth year, spring, the first month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Cháoxiǎn envoys came to request aid.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngyín,
the expedition against Japan was reconsidered.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Mázǔ, former Dūdū Tóngzhī, was appointed Grand General for Defending against the Japanese,
commanding the northern and southern armies.
In the third month, on the day Yǐsì,
Yáng Hào, Right Policy Advisor of Shāndōng, was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief,
managing military affairs in Cháoxiǎn.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Xíng Jiè, Vice Minister of War, was promoted to Minister,
Grand Coordinator of military affairs in Jì, Liáo, and Bǎodìng,
and managed the defense against the Japanese.
In summer, the sixth month, on the day Wùyín,
the Huángjí, Zhōngjí, and Jiànjí palaces suffered disasters.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the compilation of the National History was suspended.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Guǐsì,
officials were admonished and instructed.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
an imperial edict granted a general amnesty to the empire.
This month,
Yáng Yìnglóng rebelled,
pillaging Héjiāng and Qíjiāng.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the Japanese broke through Cháoxiǎn's Hánshān,
then approached Nányuán.
Yáng Yuán, the Assistant Grand General, abandoned the city and fled,
and the Japanese pressed on to Wángjīng.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
an earthquake occurred in the capital.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénchén,
Shí Xīng, former Minister of War, was arrested and imprisoned,
sentenced to death.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Lí Wéitán of Ānnán usurped the throne
and sent an envoy to request punishment;
an edict appointed him Grand Pacification Commissioner of Ānnán.
This year,
Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the twenty-sixth year, spring, the first month,
the government troops attacked the Japanese at Wèishān,
but failed.
Yáng Hào and Mázǔ fled to Wángjīng.
In the third month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Zhào Bǐngzhōng and others were granted the Jinshi degree and official positions with various distinctions.
On the day Rénzǐ,
officials went to Wénhuá Mén to submit a memorial requesting the First Imperial Prince's capping ceremony and marriage,
but it was not approved.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Lǐ Rúsōng, Commander-in-Chief of Liaodong, ventured beyond the frontier,
encountered an ambush, and died in battle.
On the *rénshēn* day,
there was a drought in the capital,
and an imperial edict commanded self-reflection.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
Yáng Hào was dismissed.
On the *wǔwǔ* day,
the eunuch Lǐ Jìng gathered pearls in Guangdong.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Zhāng Wèi was dismissed.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Wàn Shìdé, Censor-in-Chief supervising Tianjin, was appointed to manage affairs in Cháoxiǎn.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
the eunuch Lǔ Bǎo sold surplus salt from the two Huái regions.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the ninth month, on the *rénchén* day,
land taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken fields in Zhèjiāng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
commanders-in-chief Liú Tíng and Má Guì attacked the Japanese along separate routes
and defeated them.
Dǒng Yīyuán attacked the Japanese's new stockade
and was defeated.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùxū* day,
the Japanese abandoned Wèishān and fled;
the imperial army advanced and attacked them along separate routes.
In the twelfth month,
Commander-in-Chief Chén Lín defeated the Japanese at Yǐshān,
and Cháoxiǎn was pacified.
In this year,
Wūsīzàng presented tribute.
In the twenty-seventh year, spring, the second month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
eunuchs were dispatched to take charge of the Maritime Trade Superintendencies in Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, and Guǎngdōng.
In this month,
Jiāng Dōngzhī,巡撫 of Guìzhōu, dispatched troops to suppress Yáng Yìnglóng
but was defeated.
In the third month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Lǐ Huàlóng, former Vice Minister of War, was appointed Supreme Commander of military affairs in Chuān, Hú, and Guìzhōu
to suppress Yáng Yìnglóng.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
the Emperor held court at Wǔmén
and received Japanese captives.
In this month,
there was a popular uprising in Línqīng;
they burned the yamen of the tax commissioner Mǎ Táng
and killed thirty-four of his attendants.
In the intercalary month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
due to the pacification of the Japanese,
an imperial edict was issued to the whole empire,
remitting the additional land taxes levied for the eastern expedition.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
due to a prolonged drought,
an imperial edict commanded self-reflection.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
for the weddings of the imperial princes,
an edict ordered the appropriation of 24 million *liǎng* of silver from Tàicāng.
The Ministry of Revenue reported a shortage,
and an order was given to strictly audit the accumulated reserves throughout the empire.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Yáng Yìnglóng captured Qíjiāng;
Assistant Regional Commander Fáng Jiāchǒng and Guerrilla Commander Zhāng Liángxián died in battle.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
a mountain collapsed in Dí dào County, Shǎnxī.
In the ninth month,
the Tǔmán invaded Jǐnzhōu.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
relief was provided to the starving people in the capital.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
due to military operations in Bōzhōu,
additional land taxes were imposed on Sìchuān and Húguǎng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Ān Jiāngchén, Pacification Commissioner of Guìzhōu, was found guilty,
and an edict ordered him to redeem himself by suppressing bandits.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
land taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken fields in Hénán.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
relief was provided to the starving in Jīfǔ and Fèngyáng and other places.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
there was a popular uprising in Wǔchāng and Hànyáng;
they injured the tax commissioner Chén Fèng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
relief was provided to the starving displaced people in the capital.
In this year,
Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the twenty-eighth year, spring, the second month, on the *wùyín* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Lǐ Huàlóng led his army in eight divisions to suppress Bōzhōu.
In summer, the sixth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
Hǎilóngdūn was captured,
Yáng Yìnglóng hanged himself,
and Bōzhōu was pacified.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *xīnhài* day,
there was a drought,
and an imperial edict commanded self-reflection.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Cíqìnggōng was completed.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
garrison troops in Cháoxiǎn were withdrawn.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
executions were halted.
This autumn,
Chǎohuā invaded Liaodong;
Deputy Commander-in-Chief Xiè Shēng and others were defeated and killed.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
the Pílín Miáo in Guìzhōu rebelled;
Commander-in-Chief Chén Lín suppressed them.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Yáng Róng, tax eunuch of Yúnnán, began mining for treasures in Āwǎ and Mèngmì.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
the Emperor held court at Wǔmén
and received captives from Bōzhōu.
In this year,
the two metropolitan regions and various provinces suffered from disasters and calamities;
the people were starving, and bandits arose.
Officials inside and outside the court repeatedly submitted memorials requesting the dismissal of all mining and tax superintendents,
but none were heeded.
Lì Mǎdòu from the Great West presented local products.
In the twenty-ninth year, spring, the first month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
due to the pacification of Bōzhōu,
an imperial edict was issued to the whole empire,
remitting the additional land taxes and outstanding levies in Sìchuān, Guìzhōu, Húguǎng, and Yúnnán,
and pardoning officials and commoners who had committed unintentional errors.
In this month,
the Pílín Miáo rebels were pacified.
In the second month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
relief was provided to the starving in Dàtóng and Xuānfǔ.
In the third month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Zhāng Yǐchéng and others were awarded the *jìnshì* degree with different ranks.
In this month,
there was a popular uprising in Wǔchāng;
they killed six attendants of the tax eunuch Chén Fèng
and burned the yamen of the Provincial Governor.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Chén Fèng was summoned back,
and Dù Mào, the eunuch in charge of the defense of Chéngtiān, replaced him.
In the fifth month,
there was a popular uprising in Sūzhōu;
they killed several attendants of Sūn Lóng, the eunuch in charge of silk weaving.
In the sixth month,
there had been no rain in the capital since the sixth month of the previous year,
and it only started to rain on the *yǐhài* day of this month.
Shāndōng, Shānxī, and Hénán all suffered from severe drought.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the judicial authorities requested a summer review of cases,
but no reply was given.
This summer,
relief was provided to the starving within the metropolitan region.
In autumn, the ninth month, on the *rén'yín* day,
the Yellow River burst its banks at Kāifēng and Guīdé.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Zhào Zhìgāo died.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided to the starving in Guìzhōu.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Shěn Lǐ, former Minister of Rites, and Zhū Gēng were both appointed Grand Secretaries of the Dōnggé,
participating in state affairs.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Chángluò, the eldest imperial son, was established as Crown Prince;
the other sons were enfeoffed: Chángxún as Prince of Fú,
Chánghào as Prince of Ruì,
Chángrùn as Prince of Huì,
and Chángyíng as Prince of Guì.
An imperial edict proclaimed a general amnesty.
On the *rénchén* day,
the honorable title of Empress Dowager Císhèng was further elevated.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
an imperial edict ordered the resumption of horse markets at Kuíyán.
In this year,
Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the thirtieth year, spring, the first month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
due to disasters and unusual phenomena in all directions,
an imperial edict commanded self-reflection.
In the second month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor was unwell;
he summoned Grand Secretary Shěn Yīguàn to Qǐxiánggōng
and ordered the abolition of mining taxes,
the suspension of weaving superintendencies,
the release of those detained,
and the reinstatement of officials who had offered remonstrance.
The next day,
his illness recovered,
and the previous edict was annulled.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Qiánqīnggōng and Kūnnínggōng were rebuilt.
In the intercalary month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
tribute and markets were restored for various tribes in the Hétào region.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Yellow River dried up in Hézhōu.
In the third month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
there was a popular uprising in Téngyuè; they killed the official delegated by the tax eunuch.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Xīnc丑,
relief was provided to the starving in Shùntiān and Yǒngpíng.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐhài,
the judicial offices requested a summer review of cases,
but this was not granted.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
as there was a shortage of frontier provisions,
an order was issued to strictly press for overdue payments.
This month,
Burmese bandits captured the Mánmò Pacification Commission (Xuānfǔsī).
Pacification Commissioner Sī Zhèng fled to Téngyuè,
but the bandits pursued him.
The local officials killed Zhèng to appease the bandits,
and only then did they disperse.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Wùxū,
relief was provided to disaster victims north of the Jiāng River.
On the day Bǐngchén,
executions were halted.
This year,
Liúqiú and Hāmì offered tribute.
In the thirty-first year, spring, the third month, on the day Wùwǔ,
the Ministry of Personnel reported vacancies for prefects (jùnshǒu) throughout the empire,
but this was not granted.
This month,
remaining bandits from Bōzhōu, such as Wú Hóng, caused unrest,
and the local officials suppressed them.
In summer, the fourth month, on the first day Dīnghài,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
the Grand Secretaries requested a summer review of cases,
but this was not granted.
On the day Wùyín,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
Fèngyáng experienced heavy hail,
damaging the ridge of the Imperial Mausoleum's hall.
This summer,
the river burst its banks at Sūjiāzhuāng,
inundating Fēng, Pèi, Yútái, and Shānxìan to the north.
In autumn, the ninth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
bandits rose up north of the Jiāng River.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
executions were halted.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
bandits led by Yáng Sījìng caused unrest in Suīzhōu,
and the local officials suppressed and captured them.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
a seditious book was discovered,
claiming that the emperor wished to replace the crown prince.
An imperial edict ordered a thorough search of the five wards.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
the crown prince was summoned for an audience at the Qǐxiánggōng Palace,
and a personal imperial message was bestowed upon him to console and instruct him.
In the thirty-second year, spring, the second month, on the day Rén'yín,
the Grand Secretaries requested the appointment of surveillance commissioners (sīdào) and prefects (jùnshǒu), and the dispatch of inspecting censors (xúnfāng yùshǐ),
but this was not granted.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Qiánqīnggōng Palace was completed.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Yáng Shǒuqín and others were granted the jinshì degree, with various ranks of official appointment.
In summer, the fourth month, on the first day Xīnsì,
there was a solar eclipse.
This month,
the dredging of the Jiāhé River was completed.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
lightning struck and burned the Mínglóu tower of the Chánglíng Mausoleum.
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
due to the mausoleum disaster,
an order was issued to fill vacant official posts and to show leniency in judicial cases.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Chāngpíng experienced severe floods,
damaging the stone bridges of the four mausoleums: Cháng, Tài, Kāng, and Zhāo.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Gēngxū,
the capital experienced heavy rain,
damaging the city walls.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
relief was provided to residents affected by the floods.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnc丑,
all the officials knelt outside Wénhuámén Gate,
submitting memorials requesting the implementation of practical policies,
but an imperial edict severely rebuked them.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Shuǐhé River engineering project was completed.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùshēn,
relief was provided to the starving in the six prefectures south of the capital (jīnán).
In the intercalary month, on the day Xīnc丑,
members of the imperial clan in Wǔchāng, such as Yùn Zhěn, caused unrest,
killing the Circuit Censor-in-Chief (xúnfǔ dūyùshǐ) Zhào Kěhuái.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
the pacification of Bōzhōu was finally completed.
This year,
Liúqiú and Wūsīzàng offered tribute.
In the thirty-third year, spring, the first month,
the outer city walls of the capital were rebuilt.
On the day Gēngchén,
Yíndìng and Dǎichéng attacked Zhènfān,
and Grand Commander (zǒngbīngguān) Dá Yún defeated them.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Xīnhài,
Yùn Zhěn and others were executed.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Fèngyáng experienced strong winds and heavy rain,
damaging the spirit seats in the mausoleum halls.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
lightning struck the high pole of the observation lamp at the Yuánqiū altar.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐsì,
due to the lightning warning,
an edict ordered self-reflection and reform.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Jǐsì,
executions were halted.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Zhāohuádiàn Palace suffered a disaster.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
land taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken fields in Huáiyáng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rén'yín,
an imperial edict ordered the cessation of mining throughout the empire.
The administration of taxes was returned to the local officials (yǒusī),
with half of the annual revenue submitted to the Imperial Household Department (nèifǔ),
and the other half to the Ministries of Revenue (Hùbù) and Works (Gōngbù).
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
land taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken fields in Hénán.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
due to the birth of the Imperial Eldest Grandson,
an imperial edict proclaimed a general amnesty.
A precedent was established for members of the imperial clan to enter officialdom through imperial examinations.
The pearl-fishing in Guǎngdōng and precious-stone mining in Yúnnán were abolished.
In the thirty-fourth year, spring, the second month, on the day Gēngxū,
an honorific title was added for the Empress Dowager.
On the day Xīnhài,
Grand Secretaries Shěn Lǐ and Zhū Gēng requested the appointment of high officials to the Six Ministries,
but this was not granted.
In the third month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
people from Yúnnán killed the tax superintendent Yáng Róng,
and burned his body.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Zhēndìng, Shùndé, Guǎngpíng, and Dàmíng suffered disasters,
and tax exemptions and relief were granted with variations.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guǐhài,
the dredging of the Zhūwàngkǒu River was completed.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
tribes from the Hétào region attacked Yánsūi,
and the government forces repelled them.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Myanmar captured Mùbāng.
This month,
the imperial domain experienced a great locust plague.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Shěn Yīguàn and Shěn Lǐ retired.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
an imperial edict ordered Shǎnxī to strictly reinforce its frontier defenses.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
executions were halted.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐsì,
Yúnyán launched an incursion,
and Grand Commander Jiāng Xiǎnmó repelled them.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
the demonic rebel Liú Tiānxù in Nánjīng plotted rebellion,
but the matter was discovered and he was executed.
This year,
Ānnán and Liúqiú offered tribute.
All the Khalkha tribes of Měnggǔ submitted to Our Great Qīng.
In the thirty-fifth year, spring, the first month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Censor (gěishìzhōng) Wēng Xiànxiáng stated
that inspecting censors (fǔàn guān) whose terms ended should await an imperial order for their departure,
and should not be permitted to leave on their own,
but this was not granted.
In the second month, on the day Wùxū,
Ānnán rebel Wǔ Déchéng attacked Yúnnán,
and Grand Commander Mù Ruì repelled him.
In the third month, on the day Xīnsì,
Huáng Shìjùn and others were granted the jinshì degree, with various ranks of official appointment.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Wùxū,
Yíndìng and Dǎichéng attacked Liángzhōu,
and Vice Grand Commander (fùzǒngbīng) Chái Guózhù repelled them.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Prince Shùnyì Chělìkè passed away.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùzǐ,

former Minister of Rites (Lǐbù Shàngshū) Yú Shènxíng, Vice Minister of Rites (Lǐbù Shìláng) Lǐ Tíngjī, Vice Minister of Personnel of Nánjīng (Nánjīng Lìbù Shìláng) Yè Xiànggāo, and Minister of Rites concurrently Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé Pavilion (Lǐbù Shàngshū jiān Dōnggé Dàxuéshì),
participated in strategic affairs.
In the sixth month,
Húguǎng and Huī, Níng, Tàipíng, and Yánzhōu experienced severe floods.
In the intercalary month, on the day Xīnsì,
tribute and trade were resumed with the Hétào tribes.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the capital experienced prolonged rain.
The Ministry of Justice (Xíngbù) requested a memorial for a summer review of cases,
but this was not granted.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
relief was provided to the starving within the imperial domain.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
executions were halted.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *Guǐyǒu*,
Shāndōng suffered from drought and famine.
Taxes were remitted, and relief was distributed with distinctions.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Rénzǐ*,
Yú Shènxíng died.
In the twelfth month,
the barbarian Àkè of Jīnshājiāng rebelled,
captured Wǔdìng,
besieged Yúnnán,
and also captured Sōngmíng and Lùfēng.
Annam rebels attacked Qīnzhōu.
That year,
Liúqiú sent tribute.
In the thirty-sixth year, in the spring, first month,
Hénán and Jiāngběi suffered famine.
In the second month, on the day *Wùchén*,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the summer, sixth month, on the day *Jǐmǎo*,
there was a great flood in Nánjī.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *Dīngyǒu*,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
Mining rebels rose in Chēnzhōu.
In the eighth month, on the day *Guǐhài*,
officials responsible for the failures in Yúnnán were punished.
The巡撫都御史 Chén Yòngbīn and the 總兵官 Mù Ruì were imprisoned,
and sentenced to death.
On the day *Gēngchén*,
relief was distributed to the famine-stricken areas of Nánjī, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
the 四川巡撫都御史 Qiáo Bìxīng reported the capture of Àkè in Dōngchuān,
and the rebellion was quelled.
In the winter, eleventh month, on the day *Rénzǐ*,
Zhū Gēng died.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Wùwǔ*,
relief was again provided to Nánjī,
and land tax was remitted.
That year,
Liúqiú sent tribute.
In the thirty-seventh year, in the spring, third month, on the day *Xīnmǎo*,
Gǒngtù captured Dàshèngbǎo.
The 遊擊 Yú Shǒuzhì fought at Xiǎolínghé,
and was defeated.
On the day *Jǐyǒu*,
the 大學士 Yè Xiànggāo requested the release of memorials in which officials attacked each other,
to allow public discussion of right and wrong,
and thus restore public morale,
but his request was not granted.
In the summer, fourth month,
Japanese pirates raided Wēnzhōu.
In the autumn, ninth month, on the day *Guǐmǎo*,
the 左都御史 Zhān Yí resigned by sealing his office and leaving.
On the day *Dīngwèi*,
executions were suspended.
That autumn,
Fújiàn, Zhèjiāng, and Jiāngxī suffered great floods.
Húguǎng, Sìchuān, Hénán, Shǎnxī, and Shānxī suffered drought.
The capital region, Shāndōng, and Xúzhōu suffered from locusts.
In the winter, twelfth month, on the day *Jǐsì*,
one-third of the land tax silver from the capital region and Shāndōng provinces was retained to relieve famine victims.
Bandits in Xúzhōu killed Zhāng Fān, the知縣 of Rúgāo.
That year,
Japan invaded Liúqiú
and captured its king, Shàng Níng.
Hāmì sent tribute.
In the thirty-eighth year, in the spring, third month, on the day *Guǐsì*,
Hán Jìng and others were awarded the ranks of進士及第 and 出身 with various distinctions.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *Dīngchǒu*,
the Zhèngyángmén tower suffered a disaster (fire).
On the day *Xīnmǎo*,
due to the unusual drought,
an imperial edict instructed all officials to attend to their duties,
and not to attack each other.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
relief was provided to the famine-stricken areas of the capital region, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Hénán, Shǎnxī, Fújiàn, and Sìchuān.
In the fifth month,
bandits led by Chén Zìguǎn and others rebelled in Hénán,
and officials suppressed and captured them.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *Xīnchǒu*,
executions were suspended.
In the eleventh month, on the first day *Rényín*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day *Dīngmǎo*,
due to the army's lack of provisions,
an edict instructed court officials to propose long-term national strategies,
but they were not allowed to request funds from the imperial private treasury.
That year,
Wūsīzàng sent tribute.
In the thirty-ninth year, in the spring, second month, on the day *Gēngzǐ*,
enemies from the Hétào tribes attacked Hóngyá and Qīnghú in Gānzhōu,
but the imperial army repelled them.
In the summer, fourth month,
the capital suffered drought.
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
the Yíshéndiàn suffered a disaster (fire).
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
ever-normal granaries were established in border garrisons.
In the fifth month, on the day *Rényín*,
the censor Xú Zhàokuí memorialized, impeaching those who lectured at Dōnglín, accusing them of secretly manipulating the civil service evaluations (jìdiǎn),
and from this point, officials increasingly attacked each other.
Guǎngxī and Guǎngdōng suffered great floods.
In the sixth month,
there was a great flood from Xúzhōu north to the capital.
That summer,
the "hot review" (of legal cases) was suspended.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *Dīngmǎo*,
the Hùbù Shàngshū Zhào Shìqīng resigned by memorializing and leaving.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
executions were suspended.
Cabinet ministers requested the release of minor offenders,
but their request was not granted.
That year,
Xiāmluó sent tribute.
In the fortieth year, in the spring, second month, on the day *Guǐwèi*,
the Lìbù Shàngshū Sūn Pīyáng resigned by memorializing and leaving.
In the third month, on the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
relief was provided to the vagrants in the capital.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *Bǐngyín*,
the censors of various circuits in Nánjīng stated:
"The Six Boards and Censorate are empty,
and all affairs have fallen into disuse.
The emperor has remained deep in the palace for over twenty years,
never once meeting with ministers.
The empire will soon face the worry of collapse."
Their report was not granted.
In the fifth month, on the first day *Jiǎwǔ*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the autumn, eighth month,
the river burst its banks at Xúzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the day *Gēngxū*,
Lǐ Tíngjī resigned by memorializing and leaving.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *Jiǎshēn*,
executions were suspended.
That year,
Shàng Níng, the king of Zhōngshān, Liúqiú, sent an envoy to report his return to his country.
In the forty-first year, in the spring, first month, on the day *Gēngshēn*,
an edict instructed Cháoxiǎn to train troops to guard against Japanese pirates.
In the third month, on the day *Guǐyǒu*,
Zhōu Yánrú and others were awarded the ranks of進士及第 and 出身 with various distinctions.
In the summer, fifth month, on the day *Jǐsì*,
an edict instructed the Lìbù and Dūcháyuàn:
"In recent years, discussions have been chaotic,
and the court, being tolerant, has not intervened.
Consequently, increasingly wild statements and denunciations have been made,
causing ministers to be suspicious and fearful,
all wishing to resign,
which severely damages the dignity of the state.
From now on, any who still form factions and disrupt government
shall not be pardoned."
In the sixth month, on the day *Yǐwèi*,
Bǔshītù succeeded to the title of Shùnyì Wáng.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
the Bīngbù Shàngshū and acting Dūcháyuàn affairs manager Sūn Wěi resigned by memorializing and leaving.
In the ninth month, on the day *Rénshēn*,
the Lìbù Zuǒ Shìláng Fāng Cóngzhé, and the former Lìbù Zuǒ Shìláng Wú Dàonán, along with the Lǐbù Shàngshū and concurrent Dōnggé Dàxuéshì,
participated in state affairs.
On the day *Gēngchén*,
the Lìbù Shàngshū Zhào Huàn resigned by memorializing and leaving.
That year,
the two capital regions, Shāndōng, Jiāngxī, Hénán, Guǎngxī, Húguǎng, and Liáodōng suffered great floods.
Wūsīzàng sent tribute.
In the forty-second year, in the spring, first month, on the day *Yǐchǒu*,
the 總兵官 Liú Tíng suppressed the rebellious barbarians in Jiànchāng,
and pacified them.
In the second month, on the day *Xīnmǎo*,
the Císhèng Huáng Tàihòu passed away.
On the day *Jǐyǒu*,
relief was provided to the famine-stricken capital region.
In the third month, on the day *Bǐngzǐ*,
the Fú Wáng departed for his fief.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *Bǐngxū*,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire in accordance with the empress dowager's dying wish.
In the sixth month, on the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
Empress Xiàodìng was interred.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
the Lǐbù Yòu Shìláng Sūn Shènxíng resigned by memorializing and leaving.
On the day *Kuímǎo*,
Yè Xiànggāo retired from office.
That year,
Ānnán and Tǔlǔfān sent tribute.
In the forty-third year, in the spring, first month, on the day *Yǐchǒu*,
the river construction project at Xúzhōu was completed.
In the third month, on the first day *Dīngwèi*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the fifth month, *jǐyǒu* day, of summer,
Zhāng Chā (張差), a man from Jìzhōu (薊州), entered Cíqìnggōng (慈慶宮) carrying a club,
injuring the eunuchs guarding the gate.
He was imprisoned.
On *dīngsì* day,
Wáng Zhīcǎi (王之寀), a principal official of the Department of Justice responsible for prisons, exposed the circumstances of Zhāng Chā's (張差) case.
The club attack case thus began.
On *jǐsì* day,
the imperial city gates were strictly guarded.
On *guǐyǒu* day,
court officials were summoned for an audience at Cínínggōng (慈寧宮).
Censor Liú Guāngfù (劉光復) was imprisoned.
On *jiǎxū* day,
Zhāng Chā (張差) was executed.
In the sixth month, *wùyín* day,
due to a prolonged drought,
an imperial decree ordered self-reflection.
In the seventh month, *jǐyǒu* day, of autumn,
relief was provided to the famine-stricken within the capital region.
On *jiǎxū* day,
executions were suspended.
In the intercalary eighth month, *gēngxū* day,
the Three Palaces were rebuilt.
On *dīngsì* day,
Shāndōng (山東) suffered a severe drought;
an imperial edict allowed tax silver to be retained for relief.
On *dīngmǎo* day,
various tribes from Hétáo (河套) encroached upon Yánsuí (延綏);
the imperial army resisted them,
suffering a defeat,
and Vice General Sūn Hóngmó (孫弘謨) was captured.
In the tenth month, *xīnyǒu* day, of winter,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the eleventh month, *wùyín* day,
relief was provided to the famine victims in the capital.
In the forty-fourth year, on the first day of the third month, *xīnwèi*, of spring,
there was a solar eclipse.
On *yǐyǒu* day,
Quán Shìshēng (錢士升) and others were granted *jìnshì* degrees with varying ranks.
This spring,
the capital region, Shāndōng (山東), Hénán (河南), Huái (淮), and Xú (徐) suffered a great famine;
remissions and relief were given with variations.
In the fourth month, *wùmǔ* day, of summer,
bandits arose in Hénán (河南);
the authorities were ordered to pacify and suppress them.
In the sixth month, *rén'yín* day,
various tribes from Hétáo (河套) encroached upon Yánsuí (延綏);
Grand General Dù Wénhuàn (杜文煥) repelled them.
On *dīngmǎo* day,
the Yellow River breached at Zhūjiākǒu (朱家口) in Xiángfú (祥符),
inundating the prefectures and counties of Chén (陳), Shí (嵵), Suī (睢), and Zhè (柘).
In the seventh month, *yǐwèi* day, of autumn,
Jínéng (吉能), a chief of Hétáo (河套), attacked Gāojiābǎo (高家堡);
Assistant General Wáng Guóxīng (王國興) was defeated and killed.
This month,
Shǎnxī (陝西) suffered a drought;
Jiāngxī (江西) and Guǎngdōng (廣東) experienced floods;
Hénán (河南), Huái (淮), Yáng (揚), Cháng (常), and Zhèn (鎮) were plagued by locusts;
and bandits greatly arose in Shāndōng (山東).
In the tenth month, *dīngwèi* day, of winter,
executions were suspended.
In the eleventh month, *jǐsì* day,
Lóngdédiàn (隆德殿) suffered a fire.
In the forty-fifth year, in the second month, *wùmǔ* day, of spring,
due to no snow in the previous winter
and no rain in the spring,
an imperial decree ordered self-reflection.
In the third month, *xīnwèi* day,
officials were lacking in the Zhènfǔsī (鎮撫司),
and many prisoners died from prolonged incarceration.
Grand Secretary Fāng Cóngzhé (方從哲) and others requested action,
but there was no response.
On *yǐhài* day,
relief was provided to the famine-stricken in Jiāngxī (江西).
In the fifth month, *bǐngzǐ* day, of summer,
due to prolonged drought,
a second edict ordered self-reflection.
In the sixth month, *bǐngshēn* day,
Southern Jī (畿南) suffered a great famine;
the authorities requested relief,
but there was no response.
This month,
the Grand Secretaries and judicial officials requested a summer review of cases,
but there was no response.
In the seventh month, on the first day, *guǐhài*, of autumn,
there was a solar eclipse.
On *dīngmǎo* day,
Wú Dàonán (吳道南) left due to mourning.
This year,
the two capital regions, Hénán (河南), Shāndōng (山東), Shānxī (山西), Shǎnxī (陝西), Jiāngxī (江西), Húguǎng (湖廣), Fújiàn (福建), and Guǎngdōng (廣東) suffered disasters.
Xiāmluó (暹羅) and Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏) paid tribute.
In the forty-sixth year, in the second month, *yǐsì* day, of spring,
relief was provided to the famine-stricken in Guǎngdōng (廣東).
In the fourth month, *jiǎchén* day, of summer,
the Dà Qīng (大清) army captured Fúshùnchéng (撫順城);
Commander Wáng Mìngyìn (王命印) died.
On *gēngxū* day,
Grand General Zhāng Chéngyǐn (張承胤) led troops to reinforce Fúshùn (撫順),
but was defeated and killed.
In the intercalary month, *gēngshēn* day,
Yáng Hào (楊鎬) was appointed Left Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-chief,
to manage Liáodōng (遼東).
In the sixth month, *rénwǔ* day,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
This summer,
the authorities requested a summer review of cases,
but there was no response.
In the seventh month, *bǐngwǔ* day, of autumn,
the Dà Qīng (大清) army captured Qīnghébǎo (清河堡);
the defending generals Zōu Chǔxián (鄒儲賢) and Zhāng [●] (張●) died.
In the eighth month, *rénshēn* day,
sea transport was used to supply provisions to Liáodōng (遼東).
On *gēngchén* day,
the Nǎimán (乃蠻) and seven other tribes broke through the frontier.
On *xīnsì* day,
executions were suspended.
In the ninth month, *rénchén* day,
the Liáo (遼) army lacked provisions;
the authorities requested the release of tax silver from various provinces,
but there was no response.
On *xīnhài* day,
land taxes were increased nationwide.
On *yǐmǎo* day,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the eleventh month, *jiǎwǔ* day, of winter,
an imperial decree ordered self-reflection due to disasters and anomalies.
In the twelfth month, *dīngsì* day,
Měngkèshílì (猛克什力), a chief of Hétáo (河套), surrendered.
This year,
Tǔlúfān (土魯番), Tiānfāng (天方), Sāmǎ'érhǎn (撒馬兒罕), Lǔmí (魯迷), Hāmì (哈密), and Wūsīzàng (烏斯藏) paid tribute.
In the forty-seventh year, in the second month, *yǐchǒu* day, of spring,
Manager Yáng Hào (楊鎬) mustered his army in Liáoyáng (遼陽);
Grand Generals Lǐ Rúbǎi (李如柏), Dù Sōng (杜松), Liú Tíng (劉綎), and Mǎ Lín (馬林) advanced out of the pass via separate routes.
In the third month, *jiǎshēn* day,
Dù Sōng (杜松) encountered the Dà Qīng (大清) army at Jílín Yá (吉林崖),
and died in battle.
On *yǐyǒu* day,
Mǎ Lín's (馬林) army was defeated at Fēifēn Shān (飛芬山);
Surveillance Commissioner Pān Zōngyán (潘宗顏) died in battle.
On *gēngyín* day,
Liú Tíng's (劉綎) army advanced deep into Ābùdálǐ Gāng (阿布達里岡),
and died in battle.
On *xīnchǒu* day,
Zhuāng Jìchāng (莊際昌) and others were granted *jìnshì* degrees with varying ranks.
In the fourth month, *guǐyǒu* day, of summer,
the armor factory suffered a fire.
In the sixth month, *dīngmǎo* day,
the Dà Qīng (大清) army captured Kāiyuán (開原);
Mǎ Lín (馬林) was defeated and killed.
On *guǐyǒu* day,
Xióng Tíngbì (熊廷弼), an Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, was appointed Right Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-chief,
to manage Liáodōng (遼東).
On *jiǎxū* day,
court officials knelt before Wénhuámén (文華門),
requesting the issuance of memorials and the increase of troops and provisions,
but there was no response.
In the eighth month, *yǐmǎo* day, of autumn,
Shāndōng (山東) suffered locusts.
On *guǐhài* day,
Yáng Hào (楊鎬) was arrested.
In the ninth month, *gēngchén* day,
executions were suspended.
On *wùzǐ* day,
all officials knelt before the palace gate,
requesting the emperor to hold court and administer government,
but there was no response.
In the tenth month, *dīngsì* day, of winter,
relief was provided to the famine victims in the capital.
In the twelfth month,
land taxes were again increased nationwide.
On *xīnwèi* day,
newly recruited relief troops in Zhènjiāng (鎮江), Kuāndiàn (寬奠), and Àiyáng (靉陽) mutinied.
This year,
Xiāmluó (暹羅) paid tribute.
In the forty-eighth year, in the first month, *gēngzǐ* day, of spring,
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮) requested aid.
In the third month, *gēngyín* day,
land taxes were again increased nationwide.
In the fourth month, *guǐchǒu* day, of summer,
Empress Wáng (王氏) passed away.
On *wùmǔ* day,
the Emperor was unwell;
Fāng Cóngzhé (方從哲) was summoned for an audience at Hóngdédiàn (弘德殿).
In the seventh month, *rénchén* day, of autumn,
the Emperor's condition worsened;
Zhāng Wéixián (張惟賢), Duke of Yīngguó (英國),
Grand Secretary Fāng Cóngzhé (方從哲),
Ministers Zhōu Jiāmó (周嘉謨), Lǐ Rúhuá (李汝華), Huáng Jiāshàn (黃嘉善), Zhāng Wèndá (張問達), Huáng Kèzuǎn (黃克纘),
and Vice Minister Sūn Rúyóu (孫如游) were summoned to Hóngdédiàn (弘德殿),
and encouraged the officials to diligently perform their duties.
On *bǐngshēn* day,
the Emperor passed away,
at the age of fifty-eight.
His last will ordered the abolition of all commercial taxes and newly added weaving production items.
In the ninth month, *jiǎshēn* day,
an honorary posthumous title was bestowed,
with the temple name Shénzōng (神宗),
and he was buried at Dìnglíng (定陵).
Guāngzōng (光宗)
Guāngzōng Chóngtiān Qìdào Yīngruì Gōngchún Xiànwén Jǐngwǔ Yuānrén Yìxiào Zhēnhuángdì,
whose taboo name was Chángluò,
was Shénzōng's eldest son.
His mother was Gōngfēi Wáng Shì.
He was born in the eighth month of the tenth year of Wànlì (1582).
Shénzōng held court to receive congratulations,
announced sacrifices to the altars of Heaven and Earth, and to the ancestral temples and the gods of land and grain,
issued an imperial edict to the entire realm,
and bestowed honorific titles upon the Two Empresses Dowager.
Not long after,
Zhèng Guìfēi gave birth to Chángxún
and was favored.
The position of heir apparent remained unsettled for a long time.
Court officials repeatedly submitted memorials earnestly pleading for a decision,
but none were heeded.
In the tenth month of the twenty-ninth year (1601),
he was finally established as the Crown Prince.
In the thirty-first year (1603),
a "demon book" was discovered,
stating that Shénzōng intended to replace the Crown Prince,
and directly accusing Zhèng Guìfēi.
Shénzōng was enraged.
Many people were arrested and implicated,
until finally, someone named Jiǎoshēngguāng was caught,
and dismembered.
The case was then closed.
In the sixth month of the forty-first year (1613),
the wicked person Wáng Yuègān reported a conspiracy,
accusing Kǒng Xué and others of practicing witchcraft and sorcery,
intending to harm the Eastern Palace,
and implicating Zhèng Guìfēi and Fúwáng.
The details of this affair are recorded in the biography of Yè Xiànggāo.
On the Jǐyǒu day of the fifth month of summer in the forty-third year (1615),
a man from Jìzhōu named Zhāng Chāi, carrying a cudgel, entered the Cíqìnggōng,
and this incident again implicated the imperial concubine and eunuchs.
The Crown Prince requested that the matter be handed over to the authorities.
Once the investigation was complete,
Zhāng Chāi was executed in the marketplace,
and two eunuchs died within the forbidden palace.
From this point on, there was
the "Cudgel Attack"
case.
In the seventh month of the forty-eighth year (1620),
Shénzōng passed away.
On the Dīngyǒu day,
the Crown Prince, following the dying wishes, issued a million taels of treasury silver to reward the border guards,
completely abolished mining taxes throughout the empire,
and reinstated all officials who had been punished for their remonstrances.
On the Jǐhài day,
another million taels of treasury silver were disbursed for border rewards.
On the Bǐngwǔ day, the first day of the eighth month,
he ascended the imperial throne.
A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm,
and the following year was designated as the first year of Tàichāng.
Taxes and levies for disaster-stricken provinces were remitted.
On the Jǐyǒu day,
Shǐ Jìxié, Assistant Minister of Personnel, and Shěn Mǒu, Assistant Minister of Rites of Nánjīng, were appointed Minister of Rites and concurrent Grand Secretaries of the Dōnggé,
participating in state affairs.
There was a great drought in Liáodōng.
On the Gēngshēn day,
the Yellow River in Lánzhōu ran clear
for three days.
On the Jiǎzǐ day,
Hé Zōngyàn, Líu Yīyǔ, and Hán Kuàng, Assistant Ministers of Rites, were appointed Minister of Rites and concurrent Grand Secretaries of the Dōnggé,
participating in state affairs.
On the Yǐchǒu day,
Zhū Guózòu, Minister of Rites of Nánjīng, was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrent Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé,
participating in state affairs.
Yè Xiànggāo was summoned.
Envoys were dispatched to review judicial cases.
On the Bǐngyín day,
the Emperor became unwell.
On the Wùchén day,
he summoned the Duke of Yīngguó, Zhāng Wéixián, and thirteen others, including Grand Secretary Fāng Cóngzhé, to the Qiánqīnggōng,
and ordered the eldest imperial son to appear before them.
On the Jiǎxū day,
as his condition became critical,
he again summoned Fāng Cóngzhé and others to receive his dying instructions.
On that very day,
Lǐ Kězhuó, an official from the Hónglú Temple, presented the Red Pill.
On the Yǐhài day, the first day of the ninth month,
he passed away in the Qiánqīnggōng,
having reigned for one month,
at the age of thirty-nine.
When Xīzōng ascended the throne,
following the advice of court officials,
the period after the eighth month of the forty-eighth year of Wànlì was retrospectively designated as the first year of Tàichāng.
In the tenth month of winter,
an honorific posthumous title was bestowed,
and his temple name was Guāngzōng.
He was buried in Qìnglíng.
The encomium states: Shénzōng ascended the throne at a young age,
and Jiānglíng held the reins of government,
scrutinizing names and realities,
bringing the nation almost to prosperity and strength.
Subsequently, he became complacent and constrained,
remaining idle in the deep palace,
leading to the decay of governance,
and a disconnect between ruler and ministers.
Consequently, those petty individuals who loved power and pursued profit rushed and competed,
becoming enemies with officials of integrity,
and factions emerged in chaotic opposition.
This gradually led to the reigns of Zhé and Mǐn,
where corrupt factions grew rampant.
The upright officials at court lacked profound insight and long-term vision to thwart their machinations,
and overcome by resentment and indignation,
they mutually attacked and denounced each other.
This led to the ruler harboring suspicions,
employing both the worthy and the corrupt indiscriminately,
resulting in complete collapse and disintegration,
beyond any hope of rescue.
Therefore, commentators say that the demise of the Míng dynasty
actually began with Shénzōng.
Is this not a true assessment?
Guāngzōng's hidden virtues had long been manifest,
and the whole country looked to him with expectation.
Yet, after reigning for only one month,
Heaven did not grant him a long life.
His measures could not be fully implemented,
the "Three Cases" incited strife,
and factional disasters intensified.
Alas, how lamentable!
Collation Notes
Annals Twenty-Two: Xīzōng
Xīzōng Dátīan Chǎndào Dūnxiào Dúyǒu Zhāngwén Xiāngwǔ Jìngmù Zhuāngqín Zhéhuángdì,
whose taboo name was Yóuxiào,
was Guāngzōng's eldest son.
His mother was the attendant Wáng Shì.
In the eleventh month of the thirty-third year of Wànlì (1605),
Shénzōng announced the birth of his imperial great-grandson
by imperial edict to the entire realm.
In the forty-eighth year (1620),
Shénzōng's dying edict commanded the timely enthronement of the eldest imperial grandson,
but it had not yet been carried out.
On the Yǐhài day of the ninth month,
Guāngzōng passed away,
leaving an edict for the eldest imperial son to succeed to the throne.
After all officials had finished their mourning,
they requested to see the eldest imperial son at the sleeping chambers,
escorted him to the Wénhuádiàn to perform the ceremony,
and then he returned to reside in the Cíqìnggōng.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
the dying edict was issued.
At that time, attendant Lǐ Shì resided in the Qiánqīnggōng.
Zhōu Jiāmó, Minister of Personnel, and others, as well as Censor Zuǒ Guāngdòu, memorialized requesting the attendant to move palaces.
Censor Wáng Ānshùn memorialized criticizing Lǐ Kězhuó's mistaken presentation of the medicine.
The "Red Pill"
and
"Palace Eviction"
cases thus arose.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
the attendant moved to the Rénshòudiàn.
On the Gēngchén day,
he ascended the imperial throne.
An imperial edict proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm,
and the following year was designated as the first year of Tiānqǐ.
On the Jǐchǒu day,
the period after the eighth month of that year was designated as the first year of Tàichāng.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
Lǐ Rúbǎi, Commander-in-chief of Liáodōng, was arrested.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
the brother of the eunuch Wèi Jìnzhōng was granted an inherited title as a thousand-household commander of the Jǐnyīwèi.
The wet nurse and governess Kè Shì was enfeoffed as Fèngshèngfūrén,
and her son was granted an official position.
On the Bǐngwǔ day of the tenth month of winter,
Emperor Xiǎn and Empress Xiàoduānxǐan were buried in Dìnglíng.
On the Wùshēn day,
Yuán Yìngtài, Touring Censor-in-chief of Liáodōng, was appointed Assistant Minister of War,
to take charge of strategic affairs in Liáodōng,
replacing Xióng Tíngbì.
On the Xīnyǒu day,
the imperial lectures were held.
On the Rénxū day,
Sūn Rúyóu, Minister of Rites, was concurrently appointed Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé,
participating in state affairs.
On the Dīngmǎo day,
the Huìluánggōng caught fire.
On the Bǐngzǐ day of the eleventh month,
his imperial birth mother was posthumously titled Empress Xiàoyuánzhēn,
and his natural mother Empress Xiàohé Huángtàihòu.
On the Xīnyǒu day of the twelfth month,
Fāng Cóngzhé retired.
In the spring of the first year of Tiānqǐ, in the first month, on the day Gēngchén,
sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the day Rénchén,
posthumous titles were conferred upon Wǔ Wéndìng and seventy-two other individuals.
On the day Rén Yín,
Censor Wáng Xīnyī requested the abolition of Kè Shì’s incense offerings and cultivated land,
and the recording of Wèi Jìnzhōng’s mausoleum construction.
No action was taken.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎchén,
officials requested the restoration of the tradition of oral memorials and imperial audiences,
which was granted.
On the day Jǐwèi,
an imperial lecture was held.
In the intercalary month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
an edict was issued to the various officials to reform themselves due to dust storms.
On the day Dīnghài,
Sūn Rúyóu retired.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the penal servitude for the relatives of Qí Tài and Huáng Zǐchéng was revoked.
On the day Wùxū,
Zhāohuà diàn caught fire.
In the third month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
the Dà Qīng army captured Shěnyáng.
The regional commanders Yóu Shìgōng and Hè Shìxián died in battle.
Regional commanders Chén Cè, Tóng Zhòngkuí, Qī Jīn, and Zhāng Míngshì led various generals to reinforce Liáo,
and fought at Húnhé,
where they were all defeated and perished.
On the day Rénxū,
the Dà Qīng army captured Liáoyáng.
Director Yuán Yìngtài and others died there.
Investigating Censor Zhāng Quán was captured
and died unyielding.
On the day Bǐngyín,
an edict was issued to the Ministry of War:
“The state employs both civil and military personnel.
For a long time, during periods of peace,
military officials have been treated as mere slaves,
leading to the dispersal of heroes.
Now, the frontier faces many challenges,
and the lack of brave warriors deeply concerns me.
Let the competent authorities carefully select generals from among the mountains, forests, and wetlands.”
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the capital was placed under emergency alert.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the first day Rénshēn,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the unauthorized copying and distribution of military secrets were prohibited.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Xuē Guóyòng,巡撫(Xúnfǔ) of Liáodōng and concurrently Assistant Censor-in-Chief, was appointed Vice Minister of War
to manage the affairs of Liáodōng.
Councillor Wáng Huàzhēn was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief
to serve as巡撫(Xúnfǔ) of Guǎngníng.
On the day Wùyín,
soldiers were recruited in Tōngzhōu, Tiānjīn, Xuānfǔ, and Dàtóng.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
soldiers were recruited in Shǎnxī, Hénán, Shānxī, and Zhèjiāng.
On the day Wùxū,
Empress Zhāng Shì was formally enthroned.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
the Miáo rebellion in Guìzhōu was suppressed.
On the day Jiǎyín,
rumors were prohibited.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Chén Yúzhí, Commander-in-Chief of Shǎnxī, brought Gùyuán troops to reinforce,
but they were routed at Línmíng.
Soon after,
the Níngxià troops reinforcing Liáo were routed at Sānhé.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Hé Zōngyàn entered the Grand Secretariat.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Zhū Guózuò entered the Grand Secretariat.
Xióng Tíngbì was appointed Minister of War and concurrently Right Vice Censor-in-Chief,
to manage the affairs of Liáodōng.
On the day Xīnsì,
Wáng Xiànggān, Minister of War, was appointed Supreme Commander of military affairs in Jì and Liáo.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Yǐsì,
Shěn Què entered the Grand Secretariat.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Máo Wénlóng, a participating general, was promoted to Vice Regional Commander,
stationed at Zhènjiāngchéng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Hángzhōu suffered a great fire,
and an imperial edict halted textile production.
On the day Guǐsì,
executions were suspended.
In the ninth month, on the day Rén Yín,
Emperor Zhēn was buried at Qìnglíng.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Shē Chóngmíng, Pacification Commissioner of Yǒngníng, rebelled,
killed巡撫(Xúnfǔ) Xú Kěqiú,
occupied Chóngqìng,
and dispatched troops to seize Héjiāng, Nàxī, and Lúzhōu.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Xīngwén was captured,
and Magistrate Zhāng Zhèndé died there.
In the winter, in the tenth month, on the day Wùchén,
Censor Zhōu Zōngjiàn requested Kè Shì be sent out,
but was not heeded.
Officials Ní Sīhuī and Zhū Qīnxiàng successively spoke out,
and were all demoted to external posts.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Shǐ Jìxié entered the Grand Secretariat.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Shē Chóngmíng besieged Chéngdū,
but the Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhū Xièyuán held fast.
Soon after, Xièyuán was promoted to Assistant Censor-in-Chief,
and appointed巡撫(Xúnfǔ) of Sìchuān.
Qín Liángyù, female chieftain and Pacification Commissioner of Shígù, raised troops to suppress the rebels.
On the day Rénchén,
Yè Xiànggāo entered the Grand Secretariat.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Zhāng Wǒxù,巡撫(Xúnfǔ) of Hénán and Censor-in-Chief, was appointed Vice Minister of War,
to supervise military affairs in Chuān and Guì.
The巡撫(Xúnfǔ) of Shǎnxī relocated to Hànzhōng,
and the巡撫(Xúnfǔ) of Yúnyáng relocated to Yílíng.
The government forces of Húguǎng proceeded through Wūxiá to Zhōng and Fú to suppress the rebels.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Zhèjiāng troops reinforcing Liáo mutinied at Yùtián.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
because Xióng Tíngbì and Wáng Huàzhēn frequently disagreed on battle and defense strategies,
an envoy was sent to convey an imperial edict.
In this year,
Ānnán, Tǔlǔfān, and Wūsīzàng paid tribute.
In the spring of the second year, in the first month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Dù Wénhuàn, Regional Commander of Yánsuí, and Yáng Yùmào, Regional Commander of Sìchuān, suppressed the Yǒngníng rebels.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Dà Qīng army captured Xīpíngbǎo.
Deputy General Luó Yīguì died there.
Liú Qú and Qí Bǐngzhōng, Regional Commanders of Zhènwǔyíng, resisted in battle at Píngyángqiáo,
but were defeated and perished.
Wáng Huàzhēn fled to Lǘyáng,
and, along with Xióng Tíngbì and others, entered the pass.
Councillor Gāo Bāngzuǒ remained at Sōngshān,
and died there.
On the day Rénxū,
relief was provided to the displaced Liáo people in Shāndōng.
On the day Guǐhài,
Zhāng Hèmíng, Minister of War, inspected the army in Liáodōng.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the capital was placed under emergency alert.
The Hétào tribes encroached upon Yánsuí.
The Yǒngníng rebel general Luó Gānxiàng negotiated surrender,
and together with government forces, attacked the rebels,
lifting the siege of Chéngdū.
In the second month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Ān Bāngyàn, aboriginal Assistant Magistrate of Shuǐxī, rebelled,
captured Bìjié, Ānshùn, Píngbà, Zhānyì, and Lónglǐ,
and then besieged Guìyáng.
Lǐ Yǔn,巡撫(Xúnfǔ) and Censor-in-Chief, and Shǐ Yǒng'ān, Investigating Censor, held fast.
On the day Wùyín,
the collection of additional land tax for two years and the surcharge in the Northern Metropolitan Area were suspended throughout the empire.
Sūn Chéngzōng, Right Vice Minister of Rites, was appointed Minister of War and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé,
participating in state affairs.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Sūn Chéngzōng concurrently managed the affairs of the Ministry of War.
In the third month, on the first day Dīngyǒu,
Liú Yīzhǔ retired.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Xuē Lián, Marquis of Yángwǔ, was put in charge of recruiting soldiers.
Wáng Zàijìn, Vice Minister of War, was appointed Minister and concurrently Right Vice Censor-in-Chief,
to manage military affairs in Liáo, Jì, Tiānjīn, Dēng, and Lái.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Wén Zhènmèng and others were granted the Jinshì degree with different ranks.
On the day Dīngsì,
an imperial edict instructed the government forces of Húguǎng, Yúnnán, and Guǎngxī to reinforce Guìzhōu.
This spring,
internal military drills were conducted.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the capital suffered a drought.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùxū,
Zhāng Jūzhèng’s original offices were restored.
On the day Jǐhài,
the descendants of Fāng Xiàorú were recognized,
and soon after, memorial rites, burial, and a posthumous title were granted.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Xú Hóngrú, a White Lotus rebel in Shāndōng, revolted,
and captured Yùnchéng.
On the day Guǐhài,
Qín Liángyù and Dù Wénhuàn defeated the rebels at Fútúguān.
