Chūn and Qiūfēn ten degrees four minutes,
Jīngzhé and Hánlù twelve degrees twenty-six minutes,
Yǔshuǐ and Shuāngjiàng fifteen degrees five minutes,
Lìchūn and Lìdōng seventeen degrees forty-seven minutes,
Dàhán and Xiǎoxuě twenty degrees forty-seven minutes,
Xiǎohán and Dàxuě twenty-three degrees thirty minutes,
Winter Solstice twenty-four degrees four minutes.
East-west deviation [Dōngxī Piāndù]
takes the meridian of Jīngshī as the center,
and compares the deviation of other places.
The earliness or lateness of all solar terms
and the preceding or succeeding of lunar eclipses
all depend on this.
This is because each person defines east and west as sunrise and sunset [Mǎo-Yǒu],
and south as noon [Wǔ].
However, in the east, the sun rises earlier,
and in the west, it rises later.
A difference of thirty degrees east-west results in a time difference of one Shí.
(Noon in the east is Sǐ in the west,
and noon in the west is Wèi in the east.)
A difference of ninety degrees results in a time difference of three Shí.
(Noon in the east is Mǎo in the west,
and noon in the west is Yǒu in the east.)
A difference of one hundred eighty degrees reverses the day and night hours completely.
(Noon in the east is Zǐ in the west.)
The Westerner Tāng Ruòwàng said:
“On the night of the fifteenth day of the ninth month in the third year of Tiānqǐ,
the full moon and
lunar eclipse occurred at the beginning of Xūchū.
In Jīngshī, the initial eclipse began at one Ke twelve Fēn of Yǒuchū,
while in Western countries like Yìdàlǐyǎ, the full moon occurred during the day
and was not seen.
Calculated, its initial eclipse occurred at three Ke four Fēn of Sǐzhèng,
a difference of three Shí two Ke eight Fēn.
Calculated by the difference in distance,
it is approximately ninety-nine and a half degrees west of Jīngshī.
Therefore, to determine the east-west deviation,
two places must simultaneously observe a lunar eclipse
and compare their timings.
If it is earlier by two parts of sixty minutes of a Shí, it is one degree west;
if later by two parts of sixty minutes of a Shí, it is one degree east.
(The same applies to the earliness or lateness of solar terms.)
Currently, the differences for various provinces have not
been measured; based on the measurements of distances in the Guǎngyú Túdì, a rough list is provided,
which may not be greatly erroneous.
Nánjīng Yìngtiān Fǔ and Fújiàn Fúzhōu Fǔ are both one degree east;
Shāndōng Jǐnán Fǔ is one degree fifteen minutes east;
Shānxī Tàiyuán Fǔ is six degrees west;
Húguǎng Wǔchāng Fǔ and Hénán Kāifēng Fǔ are three degrees forty-five minutes west;
Shǎnxī Xī'ān Fǔ and Guǎngxī Guìlín Fǔ are eight and a half degrees west;
Zhèjiāng Hángzhōu Fǔ is three degrees east;
Jiāngxī Nánchāng Fǔ is two and a half degrees west;
Guǎngdōng Guǎngzhōu Fǔ is five degrees west;
Sìchuān Chéngdū Fǔ is thirteen degrees west;
Guìzhōu Guìyáng Fǔ is nine and a half degrees west;
Yúnnán Yúnnán Fǔ is seventeen degrees west.”
The above deviation values
are recorded in the Chóngzhēn Lìshū Jiāoshí Lìzhǐ.
At that time, an office was established to revise the calendar,
but there was no time for separate measurements,
so many of the degree values are indeed inaccurate.
They are kept
for future reference and correction.
Middle Stars
The middle stars in ancient and modern times differ
due to axial precession [Suìchā].
However, the theories of axial precession [Suìchā]
differ between Chinese and Western methods.
The Chinese method says that solar terms shift westward,
while the Western method says that stars shift eastward,
but their ultimate result is the same.
Now, the middle stars at dusk and dawn in Jīngshī for the first year of Chóngzhēn, as calculated by Lǐ Tiānjīng, Tāng Ruòwàng, and others, are listed below.
Spring Equinox [Chūnfēn]:
At two Ke five Fēn of Xūchū (dusk),
Běihé Sān is in the middle;
at one Ke ten Fēn of Yínzhèng (dawn),
Wěi is in the middle.
Clear and Bright [Qīngmíng]:
At three Ke thirteen Fēn of Xūchū (dusk),
Qīxīng is four degrees east;
(at dusk or dawn, if there is no star exactly in the middle,
then a prominent star before or after the middle is used.
If within three degrees of the middle,
the time difference is less than one Ke,
which can be disregarded.
Four degrees or more,
being somewhat far from the middle,
its deviation is recorded.)
At two Fēn of Yínzhèng Chū (dawn),
Dìzuò is in the middle.
Grain Rain [Gǔyǔ]:
At one Ke seven Fēn of Xūzhèng (dusk),
Yì is seven degrees east;
at two Ke eight Fēn of Yínchū (dawn),
Jī is four degrees east.
Beginning of Summer [Lìxià]:
At three Ke two Fēn of Xūzhèng (dusk),
Zhěn is five degrees east;
at one Ke thirteen Fēn of Yínchū Chū (dawn),

At one Ke twelve Fēn of Hàichū Chū (dusk),

at three Ke three Fēn of Chǒuzhèng (dawn),

At one Ke twelve Fēn of Hàichū Yī (dusk),

at two Ke three Fēn of Chǒuzhèng (dawn),

Astro-geography:
The *Zhōulǐ* records that the Bǎozhāngshì differentiated the lands of the Nine Provinces by their stellar fields,
and all enfeoffed territories had their corresponding stars,
by which portents of disaster or good fortune were observed.
During the Zhēnguān reign of the Táng dynasty,
Lǐ Chúnfēng compiled the *Fǎxiàng Zhì*,
using the twelve divisions from the *Hàn Shū* to allocate them to Táng prefectures and counties.
Yī Xíng, however, believed that the physical features of the world,
such as mountains and rivers, corresponded to the northern and southern celestial boundaries,
and his explanation was more detailed.
In the seventeenth year of Hóngwǔ (1384),
the *Dà Míng Qīng Lèi Tiānwén Fēnyě Shū* was completed,
and bestowed upon the Princes of Qín and Jìn.
The book's general preface states:
"The *Jìn Tiānwén Zhì*'s stellar fields began with Jiǎo and Kàng,
taking the Azure Dragon of the East as the head.
The Táng began with Nǚ, Xū, and Wēi,
taking the earthly branch Zǐ as the head.
Today, we begin with Dǒu and Niú,
taking Xīngjì as the head.
Ancient texts on astronomy all used Dǒu and Niú to demarcate stars,
hence the name Xīngjì,
and this is the basis for our choice."
Herein are recorded the associated stellar divisions for the thirteen *bùzhèngsī*, prefectures, subprefectures, counties, and garrisons of Zhílì, as well as the Dūyá of Liáodōng.
Dǒu three degrees to Nǚ one degree
is the division of Xīngjì.
Yìngtiān, Tàipíng, Níngguó, Zhènjiāng, Chízhōu, Huīzhōu, Chángzhōu, Sūzhōu, and Sōngjiāng nine prefectures belonging to Zhílì,
and Guǎngdé Zhōu,
belong to the Dǒu division.
Shòu, Chú, and Liù'ān three subprefectures of Fèngyáng Fǔ;
Xūyí and Tiāncháng two counties of Sìzhōu;
Gāoyóu, Tōng, and Tài three subprefectures of Yángzhōu Fǔ;
Wúwéi Zhōu of Lúzhōu Fǔ;
Hézhōu of Ānqìng Fǔ;
all belong to the Dǒu division.
Huái'ān Fǔ
belongs to the Dǒu and Niú divisions.
Hángzhōu, Húzhōu, Jiāxīng, Yánzhōu, Shàoxīng, Jīnhuá, Qúzhōu, Chǔzhōu, and Níngbō nine prefectures belonging to Zhèjiāng Bùzhèngsī all belong to the Niú and Nǚ divisions.
Tái Zhōu and Wēn Zhōu two prefectures
belong to the Dǒu, Niú, Xū, and Nǚ divisions.
All belonging to Jiāngxī Bùzhèngsī belong to the Dǒu division.
All belonging to Fújiàn Bùzhèngsī belong to the Niú and Nǚ divisions.
Guǎngzhōu Fǔ belonging to Guǎngdōng Bùzhèngsī also belongs to the Niú and Nǚ divisions.
Huìzhōu
belongs to the Nǚ division.
Zhàoqìng and Nánxióng two prefectures,
Déqìng Zhōu,
all belong to the Niú and Nǚ divisions.
Cháozhōu Fǔ
belongs to the Niú division.
Léizhōu and Qióngzhōu two prefectures,
Yá, Dān, and Wàn three subprefectures,
Huàzhōu of Gāozhōu Fǔ,
Cāngwú, Téng, Cénxī, and Róng four counties of Wúzhōu Fǔ belonging to Guǎngxī Bùzhèngsī,
all belong to the Niú and Nǚ divisions.
Nǚ two degrees to Wēi twelve degrees
is the division of Xuánxiāo.

all belong to the Wēi division.
Tài'ān Zhōu and Qīngzhōu Fǔ
all belong to the Xū and Wēi divisions.

all belong to the Wēi division.
Yánggǔ, Dōng'ē, and Píngyīn three counties of Dōngpíng Zhōu,
Cāngzhōu belonging to Běipíng Bùzhèngsī,
all belong to the Xū, Nǚ, Xū, and Wēi divisions.
Wēi thirteen degrees to Kuí one degree
is the division of Jūzī.
Wèihuī, Zhāngdé, and Huáiqìng three prefectures belonging to Hénán Bùzhèngsī,
Kāizhōu of Dàmíng Fǔ in Běipíng,
Púzhōu of Dōngchāng in Shāndōng,
Guǎntáo, Guān, and Línqīng three counties,
Wénshàng and Shòuzhāng two counties of Dōngpíng Zhōu,
all belong to the Shì and Bì divisions.
Kuí two degrees to Wèi three degrees
is the division of Jiànglóu.
Téng and Yì two counties of Yǎnzhōu in Jìníng Fǔ of Shāndōng,
Jǔzhōu, Ānqiū, Zhūchéng, and Méngyīn three counties of Qīngzhōu Fǔ,
Yízhōu of Jǐnán Fǔ,

According to star charts, when two stars have the same celestial longitude and latitude, it is called 'yǎn' (obscuration);
when their light touches, it is called 'fàn' (trespass),
or also 'líng' (transgression).
Planets (wěixīng) enter and exit within and without the ecliptic.
All stars near
the ecliptic
are their inevitable paths.
Líng and fàn all arise from this.
If their motion is slow, there are few líng and fàn;
if their motion is fast, there are many.
The number can be predetermined,
not like
the unpredictability of comets (huìbèi) and meteors (fēiliú).
Therefore, the celestial phenomena that clearly warn
should correspond to those [predictable ones] and not to these [unpredictable ones].
In historical records and treatises of successive dynasties, many líng and fàn are associated with corresponding
events,
which are either coincidental correlations or mere chance.
Here, we list the instances where planets obscured or trespassed against stars.
Comparing them with events,
those that are verified
are less than one or
two out of ten.
Future generations can observe this.
As for the moon's path, which is similar to that of the planets,
but its motion is much faster,
its entry and exit from the ecliptic
completes a cycle in twenty-seven days.
If one were to calculate its obscurations and trespasses against stars, there would scarcely be a day without one.
How could all of them indicate good or bad fortune to be divined?
Currently, those recorded in the Veritable Records are less than one percent,
yet they are already too numerous to
be fully written,
therefore, they are not written.

Guest Stars
The "Tiānguān Shū" (Treatise on Celestial Offices) in the Shǐjì contains the name "guest star,"
but does not elaborate on its form.
Other strange stars such as Guóhuáng and Zhāomíng are detailed,
but there is no mention of "auspicious stars" or "ominous stars."
Therefore, "guest star"
refers to an exceedingly unusual star,
probably a general term for various strange stars,
not a specific category.
Lǐ Chúnfēng's celestial treatises of Jìn and Suí
first classified stars like Jǐngxīng and Hányù as auspicious stars,
and comets, bo stars, and Guóhuáng-type stars as ominous stars.
He also categorized Zhōubó, Lǎozǐ, and others as guest stars,
claiming to base this on Liú Ruì's astrological interpretations from Jīngzhōu in the late Hàn dynasty.
However, Hányù,
which is called an auspicious star,
has a radiant glow similar to a comet;
Guóhuáng,
which is called an ominous star,
has a shape and color similar to the Nánjí Lǎorén (Canopus).
Are auspicious and ominous truly fixed?
Moreover, Zhōubó is a single star;
it is both classified as an auspicious star,
of which it is said that "its state will greatly prosper,"
and also as a guest star,
of which it is said that "its state will have military uprisings and losses."
Such explanations,
can they truly serve as a standard?
Mǎ Qiān's not distinguishing between them
was indeed for good reason.
Now, examining the Veritable Records,
the changes and appearances of comets and bo stars were particularly striking,
and all were recorded separately.
The Lǎorén Xīng (Canopus) is commonly seen south of the Yangtze,
but it is impossible to see it in Yānjīng (Beijing),
hence it is not recorded.
All other phenomena are classified as guest stars and arranged in order.
In the 7th month of Hóngwǔ 3rd year,
the Grand Astrologer reported the appearance of Wénxīng.
In the 6th month, on the day wùzǐ, of the 9th year,
there was a star as large as a pellet,
white in color.
It stopped in Tiāncāng,
passed through Wàipíng and Juǎnshé,
entered the Zǐwēi Yuán enclosure,
swept across Wénchāng,
pointed inwards,
and entered Zhāng.
In the 7th month, on the day yǐhài, it vanished.
In the 9th month, on the day jiǎxū, of the 11th year,
a star appeared northeast of Wǔchē,
emitting a ray more than a *zhàng* long.
It swept across Nèi Jiē,
entered the Zǐwēi Gōng palace,
swept across Běijí Wǔxīng,
violated Dōngyuán Shàozǎi,
entered the Tiānshì Yuán enclosure,
and violated Tiānshì.
By the 10th month, on the day jǐwèi,
it was obscured by clouds and no longer seen.
In the 9th month, on the day wùyín, of the 18th year,
a star appeared in the Tàiwēi Yuán enclosure,
violated Yòu Zhífǎ,
and exited from Duānmén.
On the day yǐyǒu,
it entered Yì,
a comet over a *zhàng* long.
By the 10th month, on the day gēngyín,
it violated Jūnmén,
and the comet swept across Tiānmiào.
In the 2nd month, on the day bǐngyín, of the 21st year,
a star emerged from Dōngbì.
The prognostication stated,
"Literary officials will be effective."
The emperor was greatly pleased,
believing it a portent for advancing *jìnshì* (scholars).
In the 10th month, on the day gēngchén, of Yǒnglè 2nd year,
southeast of the carriage-road, a star appeared like a cup,
yellow,
bright and moist, and stationary.
In the 9th month, on the day wùxū, of the 22nd year,
a star appeared in the Dǒu constellation,
as large as a bowl,
yellowish-white in color,
its light illuminating the ground,
with a sound
like scattering sand and stones.
In the 8th month, on the day gēngyín, of Xuāndé 5th year,
a star appeared beside Nánhé,
the size of a pellet,
bluish-black in color.
It vanished after twenty-six days.
In the 10th month, on the day bǐngshēn,
Péng Xīng appeared south of Wàipíng,
traveling southeast,
passing through Tiāncāng and Tiānyǔ,
and vanished after eight days.
In the 12th month, on the day dīnghài,
a star like a pellet
appeared beside Jiǔliú,
yellowish-white, bright and moist,
and disappeared after fifteen days.
In the 3rd month, on the day rénwǔ, of the 6th year,
it appeared again.
In the intercalary 8th month, on the day wùwǔ, of the 8th year,
three Jǐngxīng stars
appeared in the northwest in Tiānmén,
one blue, one red, one yellow,
each as large as a bowl,
bright, clear, and moist.
After a long while, they gathered into a crescent shape.
On the day dīngchǒu,
a yellowish-red color appeared in the southeast,
like a star but not a star,
like a cloud but not a cloud,
this was Gūixié Xīng.
In the 11th month, on the day guǐwèi, of Jǐngtài 3rd year,
a star appeared beside Jīshīqì in Guǐsù,
slowly moving westward.
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the eleventh month of the second year of Tiānshùn
a star appeared near Xīngxiù.
Its color was white,
and it moved westward.
By the *bǐngwǔ* day,
its body was faint,
resembling powder and catkins,
and it was near Xuānyuán.
On the *gēngxū* day,
it developed a ray five *cùn* long,
encroaching upon the northwest star of the Huàn position.
By the *rénxū* day of the twelfth month,
it disappeared in Dōngjǐng.
On the *rénchén* day of the sixth month of the fifth year
beside Zōngzhèng in the Tiānshì Yuán,
a star appeared powdery white.
By the *yǐwèi* day,
it transformed into a white vapor and vanished.
On the *bǐngyín* day of the sixth month of the sixth year
a star appeared beside Cèxīng.
Its color was bluish-white,
and it entered the Zǐwēi Yuán,
encroaching upon Tiānláo.
By the *guǐwèi* day,
it resided below Zhōngtái,
its form gradually diminishing.
On the *dīngsì* day of the twelfth month of the third year of Hóngzhì
a star appeared in the Tiānshì Yuán,
moving southeastward.
On the *wùchén* day,
it was seen below Tiāncāng,
gradually approaching Bì.
On the *bǐngyín* day of the twelfth month of the seventh year
a star appeared beside Tiānjiāng,
slowly moving near Dǒu.
By the *gēngxū* day of the first month of the eighth year
it entered Wēi.
On the *wùchén* day of the seventh month of the twelfth year
a star appeared beside Zōngxīng in the Tiānshì Yuán.
It entered the eastern fence of the Zǐwēi Yuán,
passed through Shàozǎi and Shàngshū,
reached the Prince's Hòugōng,
exited beside Shàofǔ on the western fence,
and vanished on the *jǐchǒu* day of the eighth month.
On the *wùchén* day of the tenth month of the fifteenth year
a star appeared beside Tiānmiào,
moving from Zhāng to Yì,
then retreating back to Zhāng,
and vanishing on the *wùyín* day.
On the first day of the first month, *jiǎyín*, of the sixteenth year of Zhèngdé
a star like fire appeared in the southeast,
turning white,
about six or seven *chǐ* long,
stretching horizontally from east to west.
It then transformed into a hooked and bent shape,
and after a long time, it dispersed.
On the day of Lìchūn in the first month of the eighth year of Jiājìng
a long star stretched across the sky.
In the seventh month, it was seen again.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the second month of the eleventh year
a star appeared in the southeast.
Its color was bluish-white,
and it had a ray.
It vanished after nineteen days.
On the first day of the fifth month, *dīngmǎo*, of the thirteenth year
a star appeared in Téngshé,
traversed the sky and entered Gédào.
It vanished after twenty-four days.
On the *wùwǔ* day of the third month of the fifteenth year
a star appeared beside Tiānpèi,
moved eastward across the sky,
and entered Tiānhàn to the west.
It vanished by the *rénchén* day of the fourth month.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the eleventh month of the twenty-fourth year
a star emerged from Tiānpèi,
entered Jī,
turned and moved northeastward,
and vanished after more than a month.
On the *wùchén* day of the first month of the sixth year of Wànlì
a large star like the sun
emerged from the west,
and all the other stars circled it to the west.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the sixth month of the twelfth year
a star emerged from Fáng.
On the *yǐchǒu* day of the ninth month of the thirty-second year
a star like a pellet appeared in the Wěifēn,
reddish-yellow in color,
seen in the southwest.
It became hidden by the tenth month.
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the twelfth month,
it reappeared in the southeast,
still in the Wěifēn.
In the second month of the following year, it gradually dimmed,
and finally vanished on the *dīngmǎo* day of the eighth month.
In the thirty-seventh year
a large star appeared in the southwest,
its rays shooting in all four directions.
On the *yǐmǎo* day of the ninth month of the forty-sixth year
a strip of white vapor appeared in the southeast,
more than a *chǐ* wide,
and more than two *zhàng* long,
extending eastward to Zhěn
and westward into Yì.
It vanished after nineteen days.
On the *bǐngyín* day of the eleventh month,
a mottled white star was seen in the east at dawn.
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the fourth month of the first year of Tiānqǐ

Comets and Broom Stars
The light of a comet is born from its proximity to the sun.
Therefore, those seen in the evening must point eastward,
and those seen in the morning must point westward.
A broom star (*bèi*) is also a type of comet,
but its rays emanate in all four directions.
Astronomers say its disasters are even more severe than those of a comet.
On the *gēngyín* day of the first month of the first year of Hóngwǔ
a comet was seen in Mǎo and Bì.
On the *xīnmǎo* day of the third month,

Celestial Anomalies
From the *rénxū* day to the *jiǎzǐ* day of the eighth month of the twenty-first year of Hóngwǔ,
celestial drums rumbled,
day and night without ceasing.
On the *wùwǔ* day of the third month of the twenty-eighth year,
at dusk, the sky rumbled
like wind and water clashing,
stopping at the first drum of the night.
On the *wùxū* day of the ninth month,
at the first drum of the night,
the sky rumbled like pouring water,
from the northeast to the south,
stopping at the second drum of the night.
On the *wùchén* day of the eighth month of the first year of Xuāndé,
at dusk, the sky rumbled
like successive squalls of rain,
from the southeast to the southwest,
ceasing only after a long time.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the sky rumbled in the southeast,
sounding like ten thousand drums.
On the *gēngyín* day of the third month of the tenth year of Zhèngtǒng,
the sky rumbled in the northwest,
like a flock of birds in flight.
On the *rénzǐ* day of the second month of the first year of Zhèngdé,
at night, the sky rumbled in the northeast,
like wind and water clashing, five to seven times.
On the *jiǎchén* day of the eighth month of the second year of Lóngqìng,
the sky split open in northwest Jiàngzhōu,
closing between the *chǒu* and *yín* hours.
On the *yǐchǒu* day of the ninth month of the sixteenth year of Wànlì,
the sky rumbled in Shīhuīgōu, Gānsù.
In the clouds, there was chaotic barking like dogs,
with sound.
On the *xīnsì* day of the third month of the first year of Chóngzhēn,
at dawn,
the sky was red as blood,
making the windows and doors all red.
In the ninth month of the tenth year,
the sky was reddish-yellow every morning and evening.

a white rainbow pierced the sun.

and 'ears' on its left and right,
a white rainbow pierced them,
followed by yellow qi and qióng qi.
In the 1st year of the Hóngxī reign, 1st month, yǐwèi day,
the sun produced two 'ears',
a white rainbow pierced them.
4th month, dīngwèi day,
it was similar,
and then a complex halo appeared again.
In the 1st year of the Xuāndé reign, 1st month, gēngxū day,
the sun produced greenish-red qióng qi,
followed by a complex halo,
yellowish-red in color.
2nd month, jǐmǎo day,
the sun had two 'ears',
and also a complex halo appeared,
with 'ears' on the left and right,
a double half-halo above it, and back qi.
At dusk,
the moon produced two 'ears',
a white rainbow pierced them.
2nd year, 12th month, jiǎxū day,
the moon produced a complex halo,
with 'ears' on the left and right,
a white rainbow pierced them.
3rd year, 3rd month, gēngyín day,
the sun produced a complex halo,
yellowish-red in color,
two 'ears', and one back qi and one jǐ qi each,
all greenish-red in color.
dīngyǒu day,
a solar halo,
and also a complex halo and two jǐ qi.
12th month, jǐmǎo day,
the sun produced a complex halo.
5th year, 1st month, guǐhài day,
a solar halo,
followed by a complex halo.
2nd month, jiǎwǔ day,
the sun had a complex halo,
followed by jǐ qi.
4th month, gēngchén day,
the sun produced two 'ears',
a white rainbow pierced them.
6th year, 2nd month, jiǎyín day,
a solar halo,
followed by a complex halo and a double half-halo qióng qi.
8th year, 9th month, wùxū day,
at chénshí,
a solar halo,
two 'ears' and back qi,
at shēnshí (3-5 PM) all the qi reappeared.
10th year, 12th month, xīnhài day,
a solar halo,
a white rainbow pierced the two 'ears',
with qióng qi,
followed by a double half-halo and back qi.
In the 1st year of the Zhèngtǒng reign, 2nd month, jǐyǒu day,
a white rainbow pierced the moon.
9th month, dīngwèi day,
it was similar.
12th month, bǐngxū day,
the moon produced back qi,
with 'ears' on the left and right,
a white rainbow pierced them.
3rd year, 4th month, gēngchén day,
the sun produced two 'ears',
a white rainbow pierced them,
followed by a halo.
12th month, guǐxī day,
the moon produced two 'ears',
a white rainbow pierced them,
followed by back qi.
7th year, 12th month, xīnchǒu day,
a lunar halo,
a white rainbow pierced it.
11th year, 1st month, yǐwèi day,
the sun produced back qi,
a white rainbow filled the sky.
14th year, 8th month, wùshēn day,
a solar halo,
with jǐ qi beside it,
followed by 'ears' on the left and right and dài qi,
a rainbow and halo to the northeast, like a pestle.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the second month of the first year of Jǐngtài,
during the *yǒukè* period,
four black arcs of vapor appeared above the sun,
each approximately three *zhàng* long,
and about one *zhàng* above the ground.
Both ends were sharp and pierced the sun;
their shape was like fish.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the twelfth month,
the sun showed a crossed halo,
with an arc of vapor behind/above both on top and bottom,
and a halberd-shaped arc of vapor on each side.
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the first month of the second year,
the sun developed left and right parhelia,
a white rainbow pierced them,
followed by an arc of vapor behind/above.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the second month,
the sun showed a crossed halo.
On the *bǐngchén* day of the first month of the third year,
the sun developed left and right parhelia, an arc of vapor behind/above, and a white rainbow.
On the *rénxū* day of the eleventh month of the fifth year,
there was a moon halo,
left and right paraselenes and an arc of vapor behind/above,
and also a white rainbow,
which pierced the right paraselene.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the sixth month of the seventh year,
there was a sun halo,
followed by a double partial halo and left and right parhelia.
On the *gēngxū* day of the second month of the first year of Tiānshùn,
during the *chénkè* period,
the sun showed a crossed halo,
left and right parhelia,
then an embracing arc of vapor and left and right halberd-shaped arcs of vapor appeared,
and a white rainbow pierced the sun.
During the *wèikè* period,
all the arcs of vapor reappeared.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the sun showed a crossed halo,
left and right parhelia and halberd-shaped arcs of vapor,
a white rainbow pierced the sun,
and it filled the sky throughout the day.
On the *yǐmǎo* day of the second month of the second year,
the sun showed a crossed halo,
with an arc of vapor behind/above it,
and a white rainbow pierced the sun.
On the *wùxū* day of the first month of the seventh year,
the moon developed a linked halo.
On the *rén yín* day of the fourth month of the second year of Chénghuà,
the sun showed a crossed halo,
with a right parhelion.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the sixth month of the eleventh year,
the sun showed a double halo,
left and right parhelia, and an arc of vapor behind/above.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day of the first month of the twelfth year,
the sun showed a crossed halo.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the second month of the twentieth year,
a white rainbow appeared around the sun,
extending across the sky from northeast.
On the *guǐsì* day of the tenth month of the twenty-first year,
during the *sìkè* period,
there was a sun halo,
and left and right parhelia.
During the *wèikè* period,
they reappeared,
and also an embracing arc of vapor and an arc of vapor behind/above appeared.
On the *guǐsì* day of the twelfth month of the twenty-third year,
there was a sun halo,
left and right parhelia,
and also an arc of vapor behind/above and a partial halo appeared.
On the *jiǎxū* day of the first month of the second year of Hóngzhì,
during the *wǔkè* period,
there was a sun halo,
and a white rainbow filled the sky.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the sun showed a crossed halo,
left and right parhelia,
and a white rainbow filled the sky.
On the *rén yín* day of the second month,
the sun developed left and right parhelia and an arc of vapor behind/above,
and also a crossed halo, a partial halo, and two arcs of vapor: an embracing arc and a barrier-like arc.
On the *wùchén* day of the eleventh month,
the moon halo was linked,
and pierced the left and right paraselenes.
On the *gēngxū* day of the second month of the fourth year,
during the *wǔkè* period,
the sun showed a crossed halo,
left and right parhelia,
a halberd-shaped arc of vapor appeared below,
and a white rainbow filled the sky.
On the *yǐsì* day of the eleventh month of the sixth year,
there was a moon halo,
left and right paraselenes,
and they were pierced by a linked halo.
On the *jǐsì* day of the second month of the eighteenth year,
there was a moon halo,
left and right paraselenes,
and a white rainbow filled the sky.
On the *yǐyǒu* day of the first month of the first year of Zhèngdé,
there was a sun halo,
with an arc of vapor behind/above it,
left and right parhelia,
and a white rainbow filled the sky.
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the twelfth month,
there was a moon halo,
and a white rainbow filled the sky.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
it was the same.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the fourth month of the first year of Jiājìng,
the moon developed a linked halo.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the first month of the second year,
there was a moon halo,
and linked left and right paraselenes.
On the *yǐhài* day of the first month of the seventh year,
the sun showed a double halo,
two parhelia and halberd-shaped arcs of vapor,
and a white rainbow filled the sky.
On the *rénchén* day of the second month of the thirteenth year,
a white rainbow stretched across the sky,
there was a sun halo,
and left and right parhelia and halberd-shaped arcs of vapor.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the twelfth month of the eighteenth year,
at the Start of Spring,
there was a sun halo and a right parhelion,
and a white rainbow stretched across the sky.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day of the eleventh month of the twenty-first year,
the moon halo was linked.
On the *xīnchǒu* day of the eleventh month of the forty-first year,
there was a sun halo,
left and right parhelia,
with an embracing arc above and a halberd-shaped arc below,
and a white rainbow filled the sky.
On the *xīnsì* day of the third month of the fifth year of Lóngqìng,
there was a sun halo,
with parhelia,
and a white rainbow stretched across the sky.
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the first month of the thirty-fifth year of Wànlì,
there was a sun halo,
and black vapor obscured the sky.
On the *guǐchǒu* day of the second month of the forty-eighth year,
the sun showed a linked halo,
with an arc of vapor behind/above below it,
and left and right halberd-shaped arcs of vapor,
and a white rainbow filled the sky.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the second month of the first year of Tiānqǐ,
the sun showed a crossed halo,
with left and right parhelia,
and a white rainbow filled the sky.
On the *xīnsì* day of the tenth month of the third year,
the sun developed a double partial halo,
and left and right parhelia.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the second month of the eighth year of Chóngzhēn,
a white rainbow pierced the sun.
Celestial Anomalies
In the 28th year of Hóngwǔ, on the *xīnsì* day of the intercalary 9th month,
the *Lěibìzhèn* array of stars scattered and then re-clustered.
In the 29th year, on the *wùzǐ* day of the 8th month,
the *Qīntiānjiān* reported that
the second star northeast of the *Jǐngxiù* mansion
had gradually dimmed and shrunk in recent years,
clustering improperly.
In the 31st year, on the *guǐhài* day of the 5th month,
the scattered stars of *Lěibìzhèn* gathered.
In the 1st year of Zhèngtǒng, on the *dīngsì* day of the 9th month,
the Wáng xīng (Sirius) was observed to be shaking.
In the 14th year, on the *xīnhài* day of the 10th month,
the same occurred.
In the 6th year of Chénghuà, on the *dīngsì* day,
Yínghuò (Mars) had no light.
In the 13th year, on the *yǐchǒu* day, the first day of the 9th month,
Suìxīng (Jupiter) shone with dazzling brilliance,
and appeared jade-colored.
In the 8th month of the 1st year of Zhèngdé,
Dàjiǎo (Arcturus) and Xīnzhōng xīng (Antares) were shaking,
and the three stars Xuán, Jī, and Quán in the Běidǒu (Big Dipper) were dim.
In the 44th year of Wànlì,
Quán xīng (Alioth) was dim and small,
and Fǔ xīng (Alcor) was submerged.
In the 9th month of the 46th year,
Tàibái (Venus) shone in all directions like the shadow of the moon.
In the 5th year of Tiānqǐ, on the *rénshēn* day of the 7th month,
Yínghuò (Mars) was reddish in color,
large in body,
and had rays.
In the 12th month of the 9th year of Chóngzhēn,
Yínghuò (Mars) was like a torch,
located southeast of the Tàiwēiyuán enclosure.
In the 10th month of the 12th year, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Tiánxīng (Saturn) was dim and hazy.
In the 6th month of the 13th year,
Tàijiē scattered.
In the 9th month,
the three pillars in Wǔchē disappeared.
In the 10th month,
Cānxìu's foot protruded into Yùjǐng.
Four years later, in the 2nd month,
Yínghuò (Mars) displayed angry horns.
In the 3rd month, on the *rénchén* day,
Gē Chéngkē, the director of the *Qīntiānjiān*, reported that
the Dìxīng (Emperor Star) had shifted downwards.
Subsequently,
the Xūanyuan stars also appeared and disappeared erratically,
and their sizes were out of order.
Wénchāng xīng scattered,
Tiānjīn scattered,
Yáoguāng scattered,
and their points and edges were black-blue.
Regarding records of flying stars and meteors in the
observatory's registers,
there was no night without them.
The small and ordinary ones were irrelevant to good or bad fortune,
so only the unusual ones are recorded here.
In the 3rd year of Hóngwǔ, on the *gēngchén* day of the 10th month,
a red star, like a peach,
rose from Tiānfú to Lěibìzhèn,
reached Yǔlínjūn,
and exploded with a sound.
Five small stars followed it,
passing by Tǔsīkōng,
emitting light that illuminated the sky,
suddenly growing as large as a bowl,
dragging a red tail to Tiāncāng where it disappeared.
A moment later, there was a sound from the southeast.
In the 21st year, on the *yǐsì* day of the 8th month,
a red star, like a cup,
traveled over three *zhàng* from the Běidǒu's Shāo to the southeast,
divided into two,
then over five more *zhàng*,
divided into three,
passed through Mǎoxìu and became two again,
passed through Tiānlǐn and merged into one,
disappearing in Tiānyuàn.
In the 1st year of Yǒnglè, on the *dīngmǎo* day of the intercalary 11th month,
a pale blue star,
as large as a *dǒu* (ladle),
its light illuminating the ground,
emerged from the clouds in the middle of the sky.
It traveled southwest,
making a rumbling sound,
and entered the clouds.
In the 2nd year, on the *bǐngwǔ* day of the 5th month,
a red star, as large as a *dǒu*,
its light illuminating the ground,
emerged from the middle of the sky,
traveled northwest and entered the clouds.
In the 16th year,
a star, as large as a *dǒu*,
blue-red in color,
its light illuminating the ground,
traveled east from Liǔxìu until it neared Zhuó.
In the 22nd year, on the *jǐhài* day of the 5th month,
a star, like a small cup,
blue-white in color,
its light illuminating the ground,
rose from the clouds in the southeast.
It traveled northwest,
entered the clouds,
with a sound like a cannon.
In the 7th month, on the *gēngyín* day,
a star, like a bowl,
red in color with light,
entered Kuíxìu and exploded in Cānxìu,
causing many stars to shake.
In the 1st year of Xuāndé, on the *jǐsì* day of the 12th month,
a star, as large as a bowl,
red in light,
emerged from Juǎnshé,
traveled east, passed Dōngjǐng, and fell to the ground,
making a sound like thunder.
In the 1st year of Zhèngtǒng, on the *yǐyǒu* day of the 8th month,
from dusk till dawn,
there were over a hundred large and small meteors.
In the 4th year, on the *guǐmǎo* day of the 8th month,
several hundred large and small meteors.
In the 14th year, on the *guǐchǒu* day of the 10th month,
a star, as large as a cup,
its red light illuminating the ground,
traveled from Sānshī northwest to Shàobì,
its tail transforming into a pale blue-white gas,
over five *chǐ* long,
winding westward.
In the 12th month, on the *wùshēn* day,
a star, as large as a cup,
blue-white in color,
with a sound,
its light illuminating the ground.
It traveled over a *zhàng* southeast from beside Tàiyǐ,
emitted light as large as a *dǒu*,
and disappeared at the western wall of Tiānshì,
followed by four small stars.
In the 2nd year of Jǐngtài, on the *bǐngshēn* day of the 6th month,
over eighty large and small meteors.
In the 8th month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
two red stars: one like a peach,
one like a *dǒu*,
their light illuminating the ground.
One emerged from the western藩 of Zǐwēi and traveled north,
reaching Yīndé,
followed by three small stars;
the other emerged from Tiānjīn,
traveled southeast to Hénán,
followed by over ten small stars.
Their tails exploded,
with a sound like thunder.
In the 3rd year of Tiānshùn, on the *guǐchǒu* day of the 4th month,
a star, as large as a bowl,
its red light illuminating the ground,
traveled from Zuǒqí southeast to Nǚxiù,
its tail exploding.
In the 8th year, on the *rénzǐ* day of the 2nd month,
a star, like a bowl,
its light illuminating the ground,
traveled from Tiānshì to Tiānjīn,
its tail transforming into a pale blue-white gas,
shaped like a snake,
over a *zhàng* long,
and dissipated after a long while.
In the 12th year of Chénghuà, on the *yǐchǒu* day of the 11th month,
at Bōluóbǎo in Yánsuí, there were two stars,
shaped like axles,
one falling into Fánjiāgōu,
the other falling into this fort,
their red light illuminating the sky.
In the 20th year, on the *bǐngshēn* day of the 5th month,
a large star
fell southeast of Pānyú County,
with a sound like thunder,
scattering into over ten small stars.
Afterward, heaven and earth both became dark,
and only much later did light return.
In the 21st year, on the *jiǎshēn* day, the first day of the 1st month,
at the *shēn* hour (3-5 PM),
a fiery light fell from slightly west of the middle of the sky,
transformed into a white gas,
then twisted and rose again with a sound.
After some time,
in the west, there was a red star, as large as a bowl,
traveling west from the middle of the sky, nearing Zhuó,
its tail transforming into a white gas,
winding like a snake for a long while,
and directly to the west, there was a rumbling sound like thunder.
In the first year of Hóngzhì, eighth month, on the day Wùshēn,
at the sì-hour,
a meteor like a small cup appeared in the south.
It traveled more than a zhàng from the south,
as large as a bowl,
reaching the vicinity of turbid clouds in the southwest.
Its tail transformed into white clouds,
moving in a winding, serpentine manner before dispersing.
In the fourth year, tenth month, on the day Dīngsì,
there was a red star,
its light like lightning.
It traveled from the southwest to the northeast,
its sound like a drum.
It fell in Guāngshān County,
transforming into a stone as large as a dǒu.
In Guāngzhōu’s Shāngchéng, a large star was also seen flying through the air,
similar to what was seen in Guāngshān.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎxū,
a star fell northwest of Zhēndìng,
with a red light illuminating the sky.
The sky in the southwest resounded like a drum,
and also like galloping chariots.
In the seventh year, fifth month,
in Xuānfǔ, Shānxī, and Hénán, stars fell during the daytime.
In the eighth year, fourth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
a star like a wheel
traveled to the northwest,
falling in Yánshān County,
its sound like thunder.
In the ninth year, intercalary third month, on the day Wùwǔ,
southeast of Píngliáng, a meteor like the moon appeared,
its red light illuminating the ground.
It stopped in the northwest,
and shortly after, heavenly drums sounded.
In the tenth year, first month, on the day Rénzǐ,
there was a star as large as a dǒu,
yellow-white in color,
its light over thirty zhàng long.
A small star followed it,
falling in the northwestern corner of Níngxià.
The sky resounded like thunder several times.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐsì,
there was a star like a dǒu,
its light obscuring the moon.
It flowed from the northwest,
falling in Yǒngpíng with a sound.
In the eleventh year, first month, on the day Guǐhài,
a meteor fell in Sùzhōu,
as large as a house,
with a sound like thunder,
and then extinguished after a long time.
In the tenth month, on the day Rénshēn,
at dawn,
a red star like a bowl appeared in the east,
traveling over a zhàng.
Its light illuminated the ground,
traveling southeast,
with dozens of small stars following it.
In the fourteenth year, intercalary seventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
in Shāndōng, a star as large as a cartwheel appeared,
its red light illuminating the sky.
It traveled from the southeast to the northwest,
falling in Shòuguāng.
Heavenly drums sounded.
In the sixteenth year, first month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
in Nánjīng, a star flowed during the daytime.
In the first year of Zhèngdé, twelfth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
a star like a bowl
fell in Níngxià Zhōngwèi.
In the sky, there was a red light as large as two mǔ.
In the second year, eighth month, on the day Jǐhài,
in Níngxià, there was a large star
flowing from due south to the southwest and falling.
Behind it was a streak of red light,
three chǐ wide
and five zhàng long.
In the fifth year, fourth month, on the day Dīnghài,
in Léizhōu, there was a large star like the moon,
flowing from the southeast to the northwest,
dividing into two.
Its tail was like a comet,
disappearing as it fell,
with a sound like thunder.
In the sixth year, eighth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
there was a meteor like a winnowing basket,
its tail four or five zhàng long,
with red light illuminating the sky.
It turned from the northwest to the southeast,
having three heads and one tail,
falling in Sìchuān Chóngqìngwèi.
Its color changed to white,
then emitted green flames,
over two zhàng high,
its sound like a thunderclap.
In the fifteenth year, first month, on the day Dīngwèi,
at the yǒu-hour,
a star fell in the office hall of the Lóngzhōugǔ Patrol Post in Shānxī.
In the fourth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
in Shǎnxī Gǒngchāng Prefecture, there was a star like the sun,
red in color,
flowing from the east to the southwest and falling.
Heavenly drums sounded.
In the twelfth year of Jiājìng, ninth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
a meteor like a small cup,
its light illuminating the ground,
traveled from the northeast of the Middle Terrace towards the vicinity of turbid clouds.
Its tail transformed into white vapor.
From the fourth watch to the fifth watch,
large and small meteors in all directions
traveled horizontally and vertically, intersecting,
innumerable,
only ceasing at dawn.
In the fourteenth year, ninth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
in Kāifēng, heavenly drums sounded during the daytime.
There was a star like a bowl,
flowing southeast,
with many small stars following it like pearls.
In the nineteenth year, fifth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
a star fell in Zǎoqiáng,
forming four stones.
In the 3rd year of Wànlì, 5th month, Guǐhài day,
during the daytime,
the Heavenly Drum sounded in Jǐngzhōu.
Two stars fell,
transforming into black stones.
In the 4th year, 11th month, Jiǎwǔ day,
four stars fell in Fèixiàn,
their firelight illuminating the ground.
At dawn,
red spots dropped northwest of the city,
their color like cinnabar,
two lǐ long
and one or two chǐ wide.
In this month,
in Línzhāng, a star about a chǐ long
flew north during the daytime.
In the 13th year, 7th month, Xīnsì day,
a star like a bowl
fell in Shěnqiū's Liánhuājí.
The Heavenly Drum sounded.
In the 15th year, 6th month, Bǐngyín day,
a star fell during the day in Píngyáng.
On Dīngmǎo day,
at Chénkè (7-9 AM),
a star like a dòu
fell in Píngyīn,
with a thunderous roar.
In the 17th year, 1st month, Gēngshēn day,
a star fell in Xīníngwèi,
as large as the moon.
The Heavenly Drum sounded.
In the 20th year, 2nd month, Bǐngchén day,
three stars fell southeast of Mǐnxiàn.
In the 22nd year, 1st month, Wùxū day,
at Qīngshānkǒu in Bǎodìng, there was a large flying star,
its afterglow like a comet,
over twenty zhàng long.
In the 27th year, 3rd month, Gēngzǐ day,
the Heavenly Drum sounded in Gàizhōuwèi,
and three large stars fell consecutively.
In the 30th year, 9th month, Jǐwèi first day,
a large star appeared in the southeast,
red like blood,
as large as a bowl,
suddenly transforming into five,
the central star becoming brighter.
After a long time, they merged into one,
as large as a basket.
On Xīnsì day,
hundreds of large and small stars moved crisscrossing.
In the 10th month, Rénchén day,
at Wǔgēng (3-5 AM),
a meteor rose from mid-heaven,
its light scattering into seven rays,
with a sound like thunder.
In the 33rd year, 9th month, Wùzǐ day,
a star like a bowl
fell in Nánjīng Lóngjiāng Hòuyíng,
its light like fire,
traveling across the ground like a firefly
before extinguishing after some time.
The next day,

Collated Notes
The first (water) of the forty-fifth line in the Treatise.
The Treatises on the Five Elements in historical works,
beginning with the *Hàn Shū*,
meticulously record the legends and prognostications concerning the Five Elements.
Later historians followed this tradition.
Examining the *Hóngfàn*,
it begins with the Five Elements,
as they are what all things in heaven and earth cannot be without.
When applied to human affairs,
there are the Five Matters;
when examined in relation to the Way of Heaven,
there are the various omens.
The mutual influence between heaven and man,
responding in kind,
certainly cannot be said to be without reason.
However, the legends meticulously analyze and explain,
linking a certain anomaly to the corresponding event,
and further citing various evidence
to support their claims.
Therefore, even between father and son, or master and disciple,
there could be disagreements.
Was there truly an intention to match categories?
If one truly knows that the response between heaven and man is as swift as a shadow,
then every word and action would serve as a warning.
To use this as a warning,
the intention is not bad.
However, the Way of Heaven is distant,
and the Way of Man is near.
Comparing them event by event,
there will certainly be times when it proves true and times when it does not.
When it does not prove true,
people will see it as having no omen and become negligent.
The discussions of previous scholars on this
are exhaustive.
Confucius wrote the *Chūnqiū*,
recording anomalies but not explaining them.
The teachings of scholars like Liú and Dǒng,
which were rather close to divination and omens,
are fundamentally not worth recounting.
Bān Shì, in establishing this treatise,
had no choice but to detail the origins of their scholarship.
Yet, the histories of successive dynasties
often adopted the previously seen explanations of earlier scholars,
listing them comprehensively.
When measured against the principles of righteousness,
their proper placement is unknown.
Therefore, in compiling the period since Hóngwǔ,
loosely following the pattern of the Five Elements in old histories,
we record their auspicious and anomalous phenomena,
but events and old explanations that have been previously mentioned
are all excised and not included.
The *Hóngfàn* says,
"Water is said to moisten downwards."
If water does not moisten downwards,
it loses its nature.

Former historians mostly attributed cold, overcast weather, snow and frost, ice and hail, thunder and lightning, fish anomalies, locust and nymph plagues, hog disasters, dragon and snake anomalies, horse anomalies, human ailments, epidemics, drum omens, falling stones, floods, water changes, black misfortunes, and black auspicious signs all to water.
We now follow this.

Chángzhōu, Sì, and Pī experienced a hailstorm,
five cùn deep,
killing wheat and vegetables.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Yízhōu experienced a hailstorm.
The largest hailstones were like plates,
the smallest like bowls,
and many people and livestock were struck dead.
Sixth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
there was a hailstorm.
Seventh month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Táozhōuwèi experienced a hailstorm with ice,
killing grain.
A sudden flood arrived,
and many people and livestock drowned.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Gānsù Xīníng experienced a great hailstorm,
killing grain and livestock.
In the ninth year, fifth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
there was a hailstorm.
In the tenth year, second month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Jiāngxī Xīnchéng experienced a hailstorm with ice,
and some people froze to death.
Third month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Běitōngzhōu experienced an ice storm,
one chǐ deep.
In the thirteenth year, eighth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
there was a hailstorm.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
there was another hailstorm.
Ninth month, on the day Rénxū,
there was yet another hailstorm.
In the fourteenth year, fourth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Xúzhōu, Qīnghé, Táoyuán, and Sùqiān experienced a hailstorm with ice,
five cùn deep on flat ground,
and the summer wheat was completely ruined.
Fifth month, on the day Yǐhài,
Dēng and Lái prefectures experienced a hailstorm, killing grain.
Seventh month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
there was a hailstorm.
In the first year of Zhèngdé, sixth month, on the day Wùchén,
Xuānfǔ Mǎyíngbǎo experienced a great hailstorm,
two chǐ deep,
and all crops were damaged.
In the third year, fourth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Jīngzhōu experienced a hailstorm,
with hailstones as large as chicken eggs,
damaging dwellings and soybeans and wheat.
In the fourth year, fifth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Fèixiàn experienced a great hailstorm,
one chǐ deep,
damaging wheat and grain.
In the eighth year, tenth month, on the day Wùxū,
Píngyáng, Tàiyuán, Qìn, and Fén, and their subordinate cities,
experienced a great hailstorm.
The water on flat ground was over a zhàng deep,
sweeping away and destroying people, livestock, and dwellings.
In the eleventh year, sixth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Xuānfǔ experienced a great hailstorm,
and all crops died.
Ninth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Guìzhōu experienced a great hailstorm.
In the twelfth year, fifth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Ānsù experienced a great hailstorm.
The water on flat ground was three chǐ deep,
damaging grain,
and some people were struck dead.
In the thirteenth year, fourth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Héngzhōu experienced a fierce wind and rapid thunder,
and a hailstorm.
The hailstones were as large as goose eggs,
with sharp edges like knives,
shattering houses
and cutting down trees as if with scissors.
In the first year of Jiājìng, fourth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Yúnnán Zuǒwèi and its subordinate areas experienced a hailstorm.
The hailstones were as large as chicken eggs,
and countless seedlings and houses were damaged.
Fifth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Péngxī experienced a hailstorm.
The hailstones were as large as goose eggs,
and the damage was similar.
In the second year, fifth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Dàtóng Qiánwèi experienced a hailstorm.
In the fourth year, fourth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Dàtóngwèi experienced a hailstorm.
Fifth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Gù'ān experienced a hailstorm.
In the fifth year, fifth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Mǎnchéng experienced a hailstorm.
Sixth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Dàtóngxiàn experienced a hailstorm with ice,
all as large as chicken eggs.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Wànquándūsī and Xuānfǔ both experienced hailstorms.
The largest hailstones were like bowls,
over a chǐ deep.
Seventh month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Nánfēng experienced a hailstorm.
The hailstones were as large as bowls
and shaped like human faces.
Suíchāng experienced a hailstorm,
two chǐ deep in an instant,
severely damaging hemp and beans.
In the sixth year, sixth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Zhènfānwèi experienced a great hailstorm,
killing and injuring over thirty people.
In the fourteenth year, third month, on the day Xīnsì,
Hànzhōng experienced a hailstorm and frost, killing wheat.
Fourth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Kāifēng and Zhāngdé experienced a hailstorm, killing wheat.
In the eighteenth year, fifth month, on the day Rénchén,
Qìngdū, Ānsù, and Héjiān experienced a hailstorm with ice.
The hailstones were as large as fists,
five cùn deep on flat ground,
and some people were killed or injured.
In the twenty-eighth year, third month, on the day Gēngyín,
Línqīng experienced a great hailstorm with ice,
damaging houses and seedlings.
Sixth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Yánchuān experienced a hailstorm with hailstones like buckets,
damaging dwellings
and injuring people and livestock.
In the thirty-fourth year, fifth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Fèngyáng experienced a great hailstorm with ice,
damaging civilian fields and houses.
In the thirty-sixth year, third month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Yízhōu experienced a hailstorm.
The hailstones were as large as basins,
the smallest like chicken eggs,
over a chǐ deep on flat ground,
extending eighty lǐ,
and countless people and livestock were injured or damaged.
In the forty-third year, intercalary second month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
there was a hailstorm.
Fourth month, on the day Gēngyín,
there was another hailstorm.
In the seventh month, xīn-sì day, of the first year of Lóngqìng's reign (1567),
hail fell at Zǐjīngguān Pass,
destroying crops for seventy *lǐ*.
In the third month, xīn-wèi day, of the third year (1569),
hail fell at Píngxī Wèi.
Water surged three *chǐ* high on level ground,
sweeping away houses.
In the fourth month, jǐ-chǒu day,
hail fell in Yúnjiāng Xiàn.
Water was two *chǐ* deep on level ground.
In the fifth month, guǐ-chǒu day,
hail fell at Yánsuíkǒu Běi Mǎyíng Bǎo,
destroying crops for seventy *lǐ*.
In the fourth month, xīn-yǒu day, of the fourth year (1570),
hail fell in Xuānfǔ and Dàtóng.
It was over three *chǐ* thick,
and as large as eggs,
damaging all the grain sprouts.
In the fourth month, wù-wǔ day, of the fifth year (1571),
heavy hail fell.
In the eighth month, yǐ-chǒu day, of the sixth year (1572),
heavy hail fell in Qí and Dìng prefectures,
damaging grain and beans,
and killing three people.
In the fifth month, xīn-sì day, of the first year of Wànlì's reign (1573),
hail fell.
In the fourth month, bǐng-wǔ day, of the fourth year (1576),
heavy hail fell in Bóxīng,
as large as fists or eggs.
It recurred the next day,
killing over fifty men and women,
innumerable cattle and horses,
and destroying all the grain and wheat.
Yǎnzhōu subsequently suffered crop damage.
In the fifth month, yǐ-sì day,
hail fell in Dìngxiāng,
the largest pieces as big as eggs,
damaging all the grain sprouts.
In the eighth month, gēng-zǐ day, of the ninth year (1581),
hail fell in Liáodōng and other garrisons,
as large as chicken eggs,
damaging all the grain.
In the intercalary second month, dīng-mǎo day, of the eleventh year (1583),
hail as large as chicken eggs fell in Tàizhōu and Bǎoìng,
killing innumerable flying birds.
In the fifth month, gēng-zǐ day,
heavy hail fell.
In the fifth month, yǐ-yǒu day, of the thirteenth year (1585),
heavy hail fell in Wǎnpíng,
injuring thousands of people and livestock.
In the fifth month, guǐ-sì day, of the fifteenth year (1587),
heavy hail fell at Xǐfēngkǒu,
as large as dates and chestnuts,
accumulating to over a *chǐ*,
damaging all the field crops, melons, and fruits.
In the fourth month, rén-zǐ day, of the nineteenth year (1591),
hail fell.
In the second month, gēng-yín day, of the twenty-first year (1593),
heavy hail fell in Guìyáng Fǔ.
In the tenth month, bǐng-xū day,
heavy ice hail fell in Wǔjìn and Jiāngyīn,
damaging the five grains.
In the fifth month, yǐ-yǒu day, of the twenty-third year (1595),
hail fell in Línyì,
all forming shapes of men, women, birds, and beasts.
In the eighth month, rén-xū day, of the twenty-fifth year (1597),
wind and hail occurred.
In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year (1600),
heavy wind and hail occurred in Shāndōng,
killing people and livestock,
and damaging grain sprouts.
Hénán also experienced ice hail,
damaging grain and wheat.
In the fourth month, jǐ-wèi day, of the thirtieth year (1602),
heavy hail fell.
In the fifth month, wù-yín day, of the thirty-first year (1603),
hail fell at Fèngyáng Huánglíng.
In the seventh month, dīng-chǒu day,
heavy hail fell.
In the seventh month, bǐng-xū day, of the thirty-fourth year (1606),
heavy hail fell again.
Water was three *chǐ* deep on level ground.
In the fifth month, wù-zǐ day, of the thirty-sixth year (1608),
hail fell.
In the seventh month, dīng-mǎo day, of the forty-first year (1613),
heavy hail fell in Xuānfǔ,
destroying crops.
In the third month, gēng-chén day, of the forty-sixth year (1618),
heavy hail fell in Chángtài and Tóng'ān,
as large as buckets or fists,
damaging city walls, outer walls, and houses,
and crushing over two hundred and twenty people to death.
In the tenth month, rén-wǔ day,
hail fell in Yúnnán.
In the fourth month, rén-chén day, of the second year of Tiānqǐ's reign (1622),
heavy hail fell.
In the ninth month, xīn-chǒu day, of the third year of Chóngzhēn's reign (1630),
heavy hail fell.
In the fifth month of the fourth year (1631),
hail fell in Xiāngyuán,
the largest pieces as big as oxen, filling a *zhàng* (ten *chǐ*),
the smaller ones as big as fists,
killing many people and livestock.
In the sixth month, bǐng-shēn day,
heavy hail fell.
In the fourth month, rén-xū day, of the seventh year (1634),
hail fell in Chángzhōu and Zhènjiāng,
damaging wheat.
In the seventh month, jǐ-yǒu day, of the eighth year (1635),
heavy ice hail fell for three days in Línxiàn,
accumulating to over two *chǐ*,
as large as goose eggs,
damaging crops.
In the fourth month, yǐ-hài day, of the tenth year (1637),
heavy hail fell.
In the intercalary fourth month, guǐ-chǒu day,
heavy hail fell in Wǔxiāng and Qìnyuán,
the largest pieces as big as elephants,
the next largest as big as oxen.
In the sixth month, jiǎ-yín day, of the eleventh year (1638),
hail fell at Gānshíhé Shānchǎng in Xuānfǔ,
killing forty-eight horses.
In the ninth month,
hail fell in Shùntiān.
In the eighth month of the twelfth year (1639),
hail fell for a thousand *lǐ* in Bái Shuǐ, Tóngguān, Luònán, Lǒngxī, and other counties,
lasting half a day,
damaging fields and crops.
In the sixth month, dīng-chǒu day, of the sixteenth year (1643),
hail fell in Qiánzhōu,
as large as oxen,
the smaller ones as large as buckets,
destroying walls and houses,
and killing people and livestock.
Thunder and Lightning
In the eleventh month, wù-shēn day, of the sixth year of Hóngwǔ's reign (1373),
thunder and lightning occurred together.
In the fifth month, jiǎ-wǔ day, of the thirteenth year (1380),
thunder struck Jǐnshēndiàn.
In the sixth month, bǐng-yín day,
thunder struck Fèngtīanmén.
In the tenth month, jiǎ-xū day,
thunder and lightning occurred.
In the twelfth month, jǐ-sì day,
heavy wind, rain, thunder, and lightning occurred in Guǎngzhōu.
In the second month, jiǎ-wǔ day, of the eighteenth year (1385),
thunder, lightning, rain, and snow occurred.
In the fifth month, xīn-chǒu day, of the twenty-first year (1388),
thunder struck the beast-shaped ridge ornament of Xuánwǔmén.
In the sixth month, guǐ-mǎo day,
a fierce wind occurred,
and thunder struck the beast-shaped ridge ornament of Hóngwǔmén.
In the sixth month, jiǎ-zǐ day, of the ninth year of Xuāndé's reign (1434),
thunder struck the beast-shaped ridge ornament of the western outer gate of the Great Altar of Sacrifices.
In the fifth month, wù-yín day, of the eighth year of Zhèngtǒng's reign (1443),
thunder struck the *chīwěn* of Fèngtīandiàn.
In the seventh month, xīn-wèi day,
thunder struck the beast-shaped ridge ornament of the western corner gate tower of Nánjīng.
On this day,
the Dàtóng patrol army reached Shāgōu,
when wind and thunder suddenly arrived,
injuring over two hundred people with torn skin and broken fingers.
On the *xīn-hài* day, the first day of the first month of the ninth year (1444),
thunder, lightning, and heavy rain occurred.
In the intercalary seventh month, rén-yín day,
thunder struck the *chīwěn* of Fèngxīandiàn.
In the twelfth month, rén-yín day, of the eleventh year (1446),
heavy rain, thunder, and lightning occurred,
and stopped the next day.
In the sixth month, bǐng-chén day, of the fourteenth year (1449),
wind, rain, thunder, and lightning occurred in Nánjīng,
and Jǐnshēndiàn suffered a disaster.
In the sixth month, gēng-yín day, of the third year of Jǐngtài's reign (1452),
thunder struck the central gate of the palace courtyard,
injuring people.
In the sixth month, jǐ-mǎo day, of the second year of Tiānshùn's reign (1458),
thunder struck the *chīwěn* of the Great Altar Hall.
In the sixth month, guǐ-chǒu day, of the fourth year (1460),
thunder destroyed four granaries in Jìzhōu.
In the sixth month, wù-shēn day, of the third year of Chénghuà's reign (1467),
thunder struck the main tower of Wǔmén in Nánjīng.
In the second month, yǐ-mǎo day, of the fifth year (1469),
it struck again the beast-shaped ridge ornament of Jùfúdiàn at the Mountain and River Altar.
In the fourth month, xīn-wèi day, of the eighth year (1472),
the first thunder of the year occurred.
In the eleventh month, guǐ-hài day, of the twelfth year (1476),
heavy thunder and rain occurred in Nánjīng.
In the second month, jiǎ-xū day, of the thirteenth year (1477),
heavy snow fell in Ānqìng,
followed by concurrent thunder and lightning.
In the eleventh month, xīn-wèi day, on the winter solstice,
heavy thunder and rain occurred in Hángzhōu.
On wù-yín day,
heavy thunder, lightning, rain, and snow occurred in Jīngmén Zhōu.
In the seventh month, jǐ-hài day, of the seventeenth year (1481),
thunder struck the ridge beast of Chéngtiānmén at the Suburban Altar.
In the eleventh month, dīng-yǒu day,
heavy thunder, rain, and snow occurred in Jiāngnán.
In the first year of Hóngzhì, on the *bǐngzǐ* day of the fifth month,
at *chén* hour,
a thunderclap in Nánjīng damaged the *shòuwěn* on Hóngwǔmén.
At *sì* hour,
it damaged trees on the imperial pathway of Xiàolíng.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
it again damaged the granary tower of Yīngyángwèi
and the flagpole of Jùbǎomén.
In the second year, on the *gēngzǐ* day of the fourth month,
it again destroyed the Zǔshīdiàn of Shénlèguān.
In the third year, on the *rénzǐ* day of the seventh month,
it again damaged the western city wall of Wǔmén.
In the sixth year, on the *dīngwèi* day of the intercalary fifth month,
Jìzhōu experienced severe wind and thunder,
uprooting trees and flattening crops;
some cattle and horses were struck dead.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénxū* day,
there was thunder and rain in Nánjīng,
uprooting trees at Xiàolíng.
In the seventh year, on the *guǐyǒu* day of the sixth month,
the same occurred.
In the seventh month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
Fúzhōu experienced thunder that destroyed a city tower.
In the eighth year, on the *bǐngzǐ* day of the twelfth month,
Chángshā had severe thunder, lightning, rain, and snow.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Nánchāng and Péngshuǐ both experienced severe thunder and lightning,
rain, snow, and hail,
and large trees were broken.
In the tenth year, in the fourth month,
thunder struck the South Mountain of Xīhénglǐng in Xuānfǔ,
causing a collapse of over thirty *zhàng*.
In the seventh month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
lightning struck the *shòuwěn* of Duānlǐmén at Jíwángfǔ.
In the twelfth year, on the *bǐngwǔ* day of the fourth month,
thunder struck Chǔfǔ Chéngyùndiàn.
In the fourteenth year, on the *gēngchén* day of the intercalary seventh month,
Fúzhōu experienced severe wind and thunder,
striking and damaging the flagpole, city tower, and large trees at the drill ground.
In the first year of Zhèngdé, on the *rénchén* day of the fifth month,
thunder struck the *shòuwěn* of the Yījiǎkù in Qīngzhōu,
and fire broke out in the storehouse.
In the sixth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
lightning struck the main ridge of Xīzhōngmén;
a violent wind broke pines and cypresses at the suburban altar,
and many decorative tiles fell from Dàsìdiàn and Zhāigōng.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Nánjīng had a violent storm,
and thunder struck trees on Báitǔgāng at Xiàolíng.
On the first day of the twelfth month, a *jǐsì* day,
Nántōngzhōu experienced thunder again.
In the fourth year, on the *rényín* day of the twelfth month,
Hángzhōu had heavy rain and thunder and lightning,
which recurred two days later.
In the fifth year, on the *bǐngshēn* day of the sixth month,
thunder struck Cháigōubǎo of Wànquánwèi,
killing four garrison soldiers.
In the seventh year, on the *wùchén* day of the fifth month,
thunder struck the flagpole of Wànchūnzhài in Yúgān,
its condition resembling being split by a knife.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
thunder struck the gate of Chéngdūwèi and the flagpole at the drill ground.
In the tenth year, on the *jiǎshēn* day of the intercalary fourth month,
thunder and fire at Zhuànyángyá, Dōngdūn, and Xīnkāilǐngguān in Jìzhōu
injured over thirty people.
In the twelfth year, on the *guǐhài* day of the eighth month,
when Nánjīng was sacrificing to successive emperors,
a great thunderstorm occurred,
killing an official in the fasting room.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Ruìzhōu had severe thunder and lightning.
In the sixteenth year, in the eighth month,
lightning struck Fèngtiānmén.
In the second year of Jiājìng, on the *dīngchǒu* day of the fifth month,
lightning struck Guānxiàngtái.
In the fourth year, on the *jǐchǒu* day of the seventh month,
lightning struck the *shòuwěn* of Nánjīng Cháng'ān Zuǒmén.
In the fifth year, on the *wùyín* day of the fourth month,
lightning struck the *shòuwěn* on the southern corner of Fùchéngmén city tower and the flagpole of Běijiǔpù.
In the tenth year, on the *dīngsì* day of the sixth month,
lightning struck Déshèngmén,
shattering pillars of civilian houses,
and killing four people.
On the *guǐhài* day,
lightning struck the corner tower of Wǔmén and the city tower pillar of Xīhuámén.
In the fifteenth year, on the *jiǎshēn* day of the sixth month,
lightning struck the *shòuwěn* of Nánjīng Xīshàngmén,
killing over ten men and women.
In the sixteenth year, on the *wùxū* day of the fifth month,
thunder struck the *chīwěn* of Jǐnshēndiàn.
In the twenty-eighth year, on the first day of the sixth month, a *dīngyǒu* day,
thunder struck the left *wěn* of Fèngxiāndiàn and the door lattice of the east room.
In the thirty-third year, on the *yǐhài* day of the fourth month,
thunder began.
In the thirty-eighth year, on the *bǐngyín* day of the sixth month,
lightning struck the south and west walls outside the gate of Fèngxiāndiàn.
In the first year of Lóngqìng, in the eighth month,
there was intense heat and thunder.
The next day,
it was extremely cold,
like deep winter.
That night,
thunder struck until dawn.
In the fourth year, on the *xīnyǒu* day of the sixth month,
lightning struck the *chīwěn* of Guǎnglìmén at Yuánqiū.
In the third year of Wànlì, on the *jǐmǎo* day of the sixth month,
lightning struck the *chīwěn* of Jiànjídian.
On the *rénchén* day,
lightning struck the *chīwěi* of Duānmén.
In the sixth year, on the *rényǐ* day of the seventh month,
lightning struck the left eave of Nánjīng Chéngtiānmén.
In the thirteenth year, on the *wùzǐ* day of the seventh month,
thunder struck Guǎnglìmén of the suburban altar,
damaging the inscribed
character
"lì" and the *shòuwěn* of the north gate of Zhāigōng.
In the sixteenth year, on the *rénwǔ* day of the eighth month,
thunder struck the animal heads of the bell and drum towers of Nánjīng Jiù Xī'ānmén.
In the nineteenth year, on the *jiǎxū* day of the fifth month,
Tàipínglù and Xīfēnglù were both struck by lightning,
guard towers collapsed,
and officers and soldiers were injured.
In the twenty-first year, on the *wùxū* day of the fourth month,
thunder struck large trees at Xiàolíng.
In the twenty-second year, on the *jǐyǒu* day of the sixth month,
there was thunder and rain,
and Xīhuámén caught fire.
In the seventh month, on the *rénchén* day,
lightning struck the left *wěn* of the east gate of Qígǔtán.
In the twenty-fourth year, on the night of the *jǐyǒu* day of the second month,
Língxiàn experienced severe thunderstorms,
with firelight spreading over more than ten *lǐ*.
In the twenty-fifth year, on the first day of the seventh month, a *gēngyín* day,
thunder destroyed the rampart and firearms of Huánghuāzhèn.
In the thirty-second year, on the *guǐyǒu* day of the fifth month,
thunder destroyed the tower of Chánglíng,
and also destroyed the pine shed road guard towers of Jìzhèn.
In the thirty-third year, on the *gēngzǐ* day of the fifth month.
Severe thunder and lightning
struck and destroyed the tall pole of Wàngdēng at Nánjiāo.
In the thirty-seventh year, on the *jiǎyín* day of the eighth month,
lightning split the flagpole on the western city wall.
In the first year of Tàichāng, on the *jǐwèi* day of the tenth month,
thunder destroyed the city tower of Huái'ān.
In the sixth year of Chóngzhēn, on the *dīnghài* day of the twelfth month,
there was a severe snowstorm,
with thunder and lightning.
In the ninth year, on the *jiǎxū* day of the first month,
thunder destroyed trees at Xiàolíng.
In the tenth year, on the *yǐhài* day of the fourth month,
thunder and fire in Jìzhōu burned over twenty *lǐ* of Dōngshān.
In the twelfth year, in the seventh month,
lightning struck and broke the watchtower of Mìyún city,
and all the stored cannons and wood were shattered.
In the tenth month, on the *yǐwèi* day of Lìdōng,
thunder and lightning struck violently.
In the fourteenth year, on the *guǐchǒu* day of the fourth month,
thunder and fire originated in the northwest of Jìzhōu,
burning as far as Zhàjiāgǔ,
extending over twenty *lǐ*.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
thunder struck the city tower of the west gate of Xuānfǔ.
In the fifteenth year, on the *guǐmǎo* day of the fourth month,
thunder struck trees at Nánjīng Xiàolíng,
and fire emerged from the trees.
In the sixteenth year, on the first day of the fifth month, a *guǐsì* day,
thunder struck continuously throughout the night.
The next day,
it was seen that the spirit tablet of Tàimiào had fallen horizontally,
and all the copper vessels were melted by fire,
turning into ashes.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
thunder struck the *chīwěn* of Fèngxiāndiàn,
all the folding screens were cracked,
and the copper rings were completely destroyed.
Fish Prodigies
In the forty-first year of Jiājìng, on the *yǐhài* day of the second month,
it rained fish at Jiǔlóngmiào in Dézhōu,
the largest measuring several *cùn*.
In the tenth year of Chóngzhēn, in the third month,
wooden planks in Qiántángjiāng transformed into fish,
some still having their heads and tails unchanged.
Locusts
In the sixth month of the fifth year of Hóngwǔ [1368 CE],
Jǐnán's subordinate counties, and the two prefectures of Qīng and Lái, suffered from locusts.
In the seventh month,
Xúzhōu and Dàtóng suffered from locusts.

Běipíng, Hénán, Shānxī, and Shāndōng suffered from locusts.

In the summer of the eighth year,

In the summer of the fourth year of Jiànwén,
the capital experienced flying locusts that covered the sky,

In the summer of the first year of Yǒnglè,

damaging crops.
In the fourth month of the tenth year,

In the fourth month of the second year of Zhèngtǒng,

In the summer of the fifth year,
Shùntiān, Héjiān, Zhēndìng, Shùndé, Guǎngpíng, Yìngtiān, Fèngyáng, Huái'ān, Kāifēng, Zhāngdé, and Yǎnzhōu suffered from locusts.
In the summer of the sixth year,

In autumn,

In the seventh month of the thirteenth year,
flying locusts covered the sky.
In the summer of the fourteenth year,

In the sixth month of the fifth year of Jǐngtài,
