Calamities from Pigs
In the seventh year of Jiājìng,
in a civilian household in Hángzhōu, there was a pig
with characters born between its flesh and membrane.
In the spring of the twenty-third year of Wànlì,
in a civilian household in Sānhé, eight piglets were born,
one resembling a human,
with fully formed hands and feet,
and one eye on its forehead.
In the fourth month of the thirty-eighth year,
a pig was born in the Yànhélù barracks,
with one body and two heads,
six hooves and two tails.
In the sixth month,
a pig was born in the Dàtóng Hòuwèi garrison,
with two heads, four eyes, and four ears.
In the sixth month of the forty-seventh year,
a pig was born in Huángxiàn,
with two heads, four ears,
one body, and eight legs.
In the seventh month,
a pig was born in Níngyuǎn,
white-bodied and hairless,
with a long nose like an elephant's trunk and a mouth like an elephant's.
In the seventh month of the third year of Tiānqǐ,
a pig was born in Wánpíngxī of Chénzhōu,
with a pig's body and human feet,
and one eye.
In the third month of the fourth year,
a pig was born in Shénmù,
with an extra nose on its forehead growing inversely,
its eyes deeply hidden in its skin and flesh,
invisible when closed.
In the fourth month,
a pig was born in Yúlín,
with one head and two bodies,
two tails and eight legs.
In the sixth month,
a pig was born in Huòzhōu,
with two bodies and two eyes,
an elephant's trunk-like nose,
four ears and four nipples.
In the third month of the first year of Chóngzhēn,
a pig resembling an elephant was born in Shíquán,
with a very large eye below its nose,
hairless body,
and entirely white skin and flesh.
In the second month of the sixth year,
a pig was born in Jiànchāng,
with two bodies and one head,
eight hooves and two tails.
In the seventh month of the fifteenth year,
a pig was born in Liáochéng,
with one head, two tails, and seven hooves.
Calamities from Dragons and Serpents
In the sixth month of the fifth year of Chénghuà
the river burst its banks at Xìnghuāyíng.
There were eggs floating on the river,
as large as a human head,
sharp at the bottom and round at the top,
their color bluish-white.
They were dragon eggs.
On the *gēngchén* day of the sixth month of the ninth year of Hóngzhì
a sudden downpour and lightning strike occurred at the Nánkǒu Watchtower in Xuānfǔ Commandery.
A dragon emerged from a scabbard.
On the *xīnmǎo* day of the fifth month of the eighteenth year
at noon,
a great whirlwind arose,
clouds shrouded the Three Palaces,
as if someone were riding a dragon into the clouds.
On the *dīngmǎo* night of the sixth month of the seventh year of Zhèngdé
in Zhāoyuǎn, a red dragon hung in the sky,
glowing like fire,
circling upwards.
The 'Heavenly Drum' resounded.
On the *guǐhài* day of the sixth month of the twelfth year
a black dragon was seen in Shānyáng.
One dragon sucked up water,
its sound audible for several *lǐ*,
lifting a boat and its female occupant into the air before they fell.
On the *guǐchǒu* day of the fifth month of the thirteenth year
in Yúyěcūn, Chángshú, there was a sudden thunder and lightning.
One white dragon and two black dragons descended together on the clouds,
spitting fire from their mouths,
their eyes like torches.
They demolished over three hundred civilian houses
and sucked twenty-some boats into the air.
Many boatmen fell to the ground
and died of fright.
That night, red rain poured down
and ceased only after five days.
In the fourth month of the fourteenth year
flood dragons fought in Póyáng Lake.
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the fifth month of the fortieth year of Jiājìng
nine flood dragons arose simultaneously in Shēshān, Qīngpǔ,
causing water to surge and form a river.
On the *wùshēn* day of the seventh month of the fourteenth year of Wànlì
there was a great thunderstorm in Shūchéng,
where one hundred fifty-eight flood dragons arose.
Their tracks were like axe splits,
mountains collapsed, fields sank,
and countless people drowned.
That year,
a commoner from Jiànchāng, while gathering firewood in the mountains,
encountered a giant snake
with one horn
and six chicken-like claws.
It neither bit nor startled him.
Some said this was a *fèiyí*.
In the seventh month of the eighteenth year
Yīshì suffered a great flood,
and two dragons fought in the village.
An egg was found,
but soon lost.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the sixth month of the nineteenth year
Gōng'ān experienced a great flood.
There was a giant snake like an ox,
with a red head and black body,
over two *zhàng* long.
Wherever it went, dikes collapsed.
On the *wùxū* day of the fifth month of the thirty-first year
Lìchéng had heavy rain.
Two dragons fought in the water,
mountains and rocks all flew,
and the water on flat ground was ten *zhàng* high.
In the eighth month of the forty-fifth year
a white and a blue dragon fought in Qīnghé Village, Ānqiu.
Horses and abnormalities.
In the ninth month of the eighteenth year of Yǒnglè
Zhūchéng presented a dragon horse.
A commoner's mare was pastured by the seashore.
One day, the sky became dark with clouds and fog,
and something sinuous coupled with the horse.
It gave birth to a colt
with dragon markings,
its color bluish-gray,
which was called a dragon horse.
In the fifth month of the seventh year of Xuāndé
in Xīnzhōu, the horse of a commoner, Wǔ Huàn, gave birth to a colt
with deer ears and an ox tail,
a jade-like face and jadelike hooves,
and flesh patterns covering its body like scales.
In the seventh month,
in Cāngzhōu, an official mare
gave birth to two colts.
The prefecture considered it an auspicious sign
and presented them to the court.
Xuānzōng said:
"This is an ordinary phenomenon of nature,
what is there to be surprised about?"
In the sixth month of the seventeenth year of Chénghuà
a horse in Xīngjì gave birth to two colts.
In the second month of the first year of Hóngzhì
in Píngfēngshān, Jǐngníng, strange creatures appeared in groups,
as large as sheep,
resembling white horses,
numbering in the tens of thousands.
Head to tail, they connected
and gradually ascended into the sky and departed.
In the fourth month of the forty-second year of Jiājìng
tens of thousands of sea horses appeared in Hǎiyán,
traveling on shore for over twenty *lǐ*.
One of them was the largest,
as tall as a building.
Human illnesses.
Previous histories often record the birth of three sons.
However, in recent years, there have been many,
too numerous to detail,
so only the more unusual ones are recorded here.
In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year of Hóngwǔ
in Lóngmén, Hénán, a woman named Sī Mǔdān died for three years
and was revived by possessing the corpse of Yuán Mǎtóu.
In the eleventh month of the first year of Xuāndé
Pí Shì, the wife of Qí Róng, a school officer of the Jǐnyī Guard in the interim capital, gave birth to four sons at once.
In the fourth month of the fourth year of Tiānshùn
a commoner woman in Yángzhōu gave birth to five sons at once.
In the second month of the thirteenth year of Chénghuà
Zhū Shì, the wife of Chén Sēng'ér, a soldier of the Yīngyáng Guard in Nánjīng, gave birth to three sons and one daughter at once.
In the sixth month of the seventeenth year
Wáng Shì, the wife of Zhāng Zhēn, a commoner in Sùzhōu, gave birth to a son
through a裂 (split) on the lower right side of her navel.
In the twelfth month of the twentieth year
a woman in Xúzhōu developed a tumor under her ribs.
It gradually grew larger over time,
and a child emerged from the tumor.
In the twenty-first year
the wife of Zōu Liàng, a commoner in Jiāshàn, first gave birth to three sons,
then to four sons in her second pregnancy,
and to six sons in her third pregnancy.
In the sixth month of the eleventh year of Hóngzhì
Yí Shì, the wife of Huáng Shèng, a centurion of the Téngxiáng Left Guard, gave birth to three sons and one daughter at once.
In the fifth month of the sixteenth year
Cuī Shì, the wife of Zhāng Běnhuá, a commoner in Yìngshān, grew a beard three *cùn* long.
At this time,
a merchant woman in Zhèngyáng grew a beard with three coils,
about a hundred stalks.
In the sixth month of the second year of Jiājìng
the wife of Hú Shèng, a palace attendant of the Qǔjìng Guard, gave birth to a son
with two heads, four hands, and three feet.
In the fourth year
Kǒng Fāng, a farmer in Héngjìng, gave birth to a lump of flesh under his ribs.
When it was cut open and examined,
a child was clearly visible.
In the fifth year
a commoner woman in Jiāngnán gave birth to a monstrosity
with six eyes, four faces,
horns,
one joint each for hands and feet,
single claws,
and a ghostly voice.
In the eleventh year
a commoner woman in Dāngtú gave birth to three sons and one daughter at once.
In the twelfth year
the wife of Lǐ Huá, a soldier of the Guìzhōu Ān Guard, gave birth to a son
with two heads, four hands, and four feet.
In the seventh month of the twenty-seventh year
the daughter of Mǎ Lù, a palace attendant and assistant commander of the Dàtóng Right Guard, Mǎ Jì,
attained the age of seventeen and transformed into a man.
In the twelfth month of the second year of Lóngqìng
Lǐ Liángyǔ, a man from Jìnglè, transformed into a woman.
In the second month of the fifth year
a commoner woman in Tángshān gave birth to a child from her left flank.
In the tenth year of Wànlì
a person from Xīchuān transformed into a wolf.
In the eighteenth year
a commoner woman in Nánsùzhōu gave birth to seven sons at once,
their skin and hair in various colors: red, white, black, and blue.
In the sixth month of the thirty-seventh year
Niú Shì, the wife of Lǐ Yí, a commoner in Fánzhì, gave birth to two daughters
whose heads and faces were connected.
Their hands and feet were separate.
In the forty-sixth year
a commoner woman in Guǎngníng Guard gave birth to a monkey
with two horns and four teeth.
At this time,
a commoner woman in Dàtóng gave birth to four sons at once.
In the summer of the eighth year of Chóngzhēn
a commoner woman in Zhènjiāng gave birth to a son
with two heads on top
and one head on the buttocks,
and both mother and child died.
In the eleventh month of the fifteenth year
a commoner woman in Cáoxiàn gave birth to a child
with two heads,
eyes on top of its head,
and hands reaching below its knees.
Epidemics
In the first month of the sixth year of Yǒnglè,
in Jiànchāng and Fǔzhōu of Jiāngxī,
and Jiànníng and Shàowǔ of Fújiàn, from the previous year until this month,
78,400 people died of plague.
In the eighth year,
in Dēngzhōu, Nínghǎi, and other prefectures and counties, from the first month to the sixth month,
over 6,000 people died of plague.
Shàowǔ experienced a great plague for several years,
and by the winter of this year,
12,000 households had died out.
In the seventh month of the ninth year,
Hénán and Shǎnxī experienced a plague.
In the sixth month of the eleventh year,
three counties in Húzhōu experienced a plague.
In the seventh month,
five counties in Níngbō experienced a plague.
In the winter of the ninth year of Zhèngtǒng,
Shàoxīng, Níngbō, and Táizhōu experienced a great outbreak of plague,
and by the following year, over 30,000 people had died.
In the winter of the fourth year of Jǐngtài,
Jiànchāng, Wǔchāng, and Hànyáng experienced a plague.
In the fourth month of the sixth year,
Xī'ān and Píngliáng experienced a plague.
In the fifth month of the seventh year,
over 20,000 people died of plague in Guìlín.
In the fourth month of the fifth year of Tiānshùn,
Shǎnxī experienced a plague.
In the eighth month of the eleventh year of Chénghuà,
Fújiàn experienced a great plague,
which spread to Jiāngxī,
and countless people died.
In the sixth month of the first year of Zhèngdé,
Píngxī, Qīngliáng, Zhènyuǎn, and Piānqiáo, the four garrisons in Húguǎng, experienced a great plague,
and many people died.
Various places in Jìngzhōu experienced a great plague from the seventh to the twelfth month,
and Jiànníng and Shàowǔ also experienced a great plague starting from the eighth month.
In the tenth month of the twelfth year,
Quánzhōu experienced a great plague.
In the second month of the first year of Jiājìng,
Shǎnxī experienced a great plague.
In the seventh month of the second year,
Nánjīng experienced a great plague,
and many soldiers and civilians died.
In the ninth month of the fourth year,
4,128 people died of plague in Shāndōng.
In the fourth month of the thirty-third year,
the capital city and its suburbs experienced a great plague.
In the first month of the forty-fourth year,
Jīngshī suffered from famine and plague.
In the fourth month of the tenth year of Wànlì,
Jīngshī experienced a plague.
In the fifth month of the fifteenth year,
there was another plague.
In the fifth month of the sixteenth year,
Shāndōng, Shǎnxī, Shānxī, and Zhèjiāng all suffered from severe drought and plague.
In the sixteenth year of Chóngzhēn,
Jīngshī experienced a great plague,
from the second month to the ninth month.
In the spring of the following year,
the northern capital region (Běijī) and Shāndōng experienced a plague.
Drum Omen (Gǔyāo)
On the day Jǐyǒu in the eighth month of the fifth year of Hóngwǔ,
there was a sound like thunder in the air northwest of Xúgōu.
In the eleventh year,
Rùichāng had a loud sound like a bell,
descending from the sky,
without any visible form.
On the night of Yǐsì in the ninth month of the sixth year of Tiānshùn,
the sky was cloudless,
but there was a sound like thunder in the northwest.
On the last night of the second month of the seventh year,
there was a sound in the air.
Grand Secretary Lǐ Xián memorialized,
saying that an invisible sound is called a drum omen (Gǔyāo),
and such an anomaly occurs when the emperor does not care for the people.
On the day Jiǎzǐ in the first month of the thirteenth year of Chénghuà,
Dàizhōu had thunder without clouds.
On the day Wùxū in the eighth month of the fourteenth year,
during the morning court,
officials on the eastern side heard sounds like armor and weapons,
causing them to scatter and fail to form ranks;
it was a long time before order was restored.
On the day Dīngmǎo in the sixth month of the sixth year of Hóngzhì,
Wúchéng Post Station in Shízhōu experienced two tremors without clouds.
On the day Jiǎshēn in the sixth month of the seventeenth year,
Lúshān in Jiāngxī roared like thunder.
On the day Jiǎzǐ in the second month of the twenty-ninth year of Jiājìng,
Zhāngshānyíng Fort in Lóngqìngzhōu experienced a mountain roar.
On the day Jǐwèi in the twelfth month of the twelfth year of Wànlì,
Xiāoxiàn experienced a mountain roar like crashing waves,
continuing all night.
On the day Wùxū in the eighth month of the twenty-eighth year,
there was a sound like thunder in the northwest.
On the day Dīngsì in the eighth month of the seventh year of Tiānqǐ,
when Zhuāngliè ascended the throne,
during the court session,
there was a sound in the air like a heavenly drum,
issuing from the west of the palace hall.
On the day Yǐwèi in the twelfth month of the twelfth year of Chóngzhēn,
Xiāoxiàn experienced a mountain roar.
In this month,
Xīshān roared loudly like thunder,
and like wind and waves.
On the day Rénzǐ in the second month of the thirteenth year,
the city gate of the Zhèjiāng provincial capital roared at night.
In the winter of the sixteenth year,
there was a sound like a turtledove within the chǐwěn (ridge ornament) of the Jiànjí Diàn,
saying
"kǔ kǔ" (bitter, bitter),
its sound gradually growing louder,
then it made dog barking sounds,
uninterrupted for three days and nights.
On the day Xīnchǒu in the third month of the following year,
there was a sound of crying at night at Xiàolíng,
which was also a drum omen (Gǔyāo).
Meteorites (Yǔnshí)
On the day Rénshēn in the sixth month of the sixth year of Chénghuà,
Yángxìn experienced thunder like a whistle,
and a meteorite fell,
shattering into three pieces,
black on the outside and green on the inside.
On the day Xīnhài in the sixth month of the fourteenth year,
Línjìn experienced a heavenly roar,
and a meteorite fell thirty *lǐ* southeast of the county,
penetrating the earth three *chǐ*,
as large as a *shēng* (a measuring vessel),
and black in color.
On the day Rén Yín in the fifth month of the twenty-third year,
Shùlù experienced a sound like thunder in the air,
and a green vapor fell to the ground.
Upon digging, two black stones were found,
one like a bowl,
and one like a chicken egg.
In the third month of the third year of Hóngzhì,
Qìngyáng had countless stones falling like rain,
of varying sizes,
the largest like goose eggs,
the smallest like gorgon fruit (qiànshí).
On the day Dīngsì in the tenth month of the fourth year,
Guāngshān had a red light like lightning,
moving from southwest to northeast,
with a sound like a drum,
and after a long time, it entered the earth,
transforming into a stone,
as large as a *dǒu* (a measuring vessel).
On the day Bǐngshēn in the second month of the tenth year,
a black vapor entered the earth in Xiūwǔ,
transforming into a stone,
shaped like a sheep's head.
On the day Wùyín in the fifth month of the twelfth year,
Shuòzhōu had a sound
like a sudden thunderclap,
white vapor ascended,
and three large stones fell.
On the day Rénxū in the eighth month of the first year of Zhèngdé,
at night, a fireball fell on Jímò,
transforming into a green stone,
round and over a *chǐ* high.
On the day Jǐmǎo in the fifth month of the ninth year,
Bīnzhōu had a sound and meteorites fell.
On the day Jǐwèi in the first month of the thirteenth year,
one meteorite fell in Línshuǐ.
On the day Dīngwèi in the fifth month of the twelfth year of Jiājìng,
Qíxiàn had a sound like a drum,
and a fiery stream fell to the earth becoming a stone.
On the day Guǐmǎo in the third month of the forty-second year,
Huáiqìng experienced a meteorite fall.
On the day Jǐwèi in the third month of the second year of Lóngqìng,
two black stones fell in Xīnchéng, Bǎodìng.
On the day Guǐhài in the fifth month of the third year of Wànlì,
two meteors fell in daylight north of Jǐngzhōu city,
transforming into black stones.
On the day Wùwǔ in the ninth month of the seventeenth year,
black smoke surged up in Wànzǎi,
and a meteorite fell beside the Yǎnwǔ Tīng (Drill Hall).
On the day Xīnyǒu in the fourth month of the nineteenth year,
two meteorites fell in Zūnhuà.
On the day Dīngchǒu in the first month of the forty-fourth year,
in Yìzhōu and Zǐjīngguān, a luminous stone cracked and collapsed.
On the day Dīngwèi in the ninth month of the ninth year of Chóngzhēn,
Tàikāng experienced a meteorite fall.
Floods (Shuǐlǎo)
In the sixth month, on the day *wùchén*, of the first year of Hóngwǔ,
in Yǒngxīn Zhōu, Jiāngxī, there was a great storm,
a *jiāo* emerged,
river water entered the city,
rising eight *chǐ* high,
many people drowned.
The matter was reported,
and an envoy was sent to provide relief.
In the sixth month of the third year,
the Jiāng River overflowed in Lìshuǐ Xiàn,
inundating the homes of the Lì people.
In the seventh month of the fourth year,
the Jiāng River overflowed in Nánníng Fǔ,
damaging the city walls.
In Lóngyóu Xiàn, Qúzhōu Fǔ, there was heavy rain,
water swept away people's homes,
men and women drowned.
In the eighth month of the fifth year,
in Shèng Xiàn, Yìwū, and Yúháng, mountain valley waters surged,
many people drowned.
In the second month of the sixth year,
Chóngmíng Xiàn was submerged by the tide.
In the seventh month,
the Yáng and Yǎ rivers in Lóngyóu Xiàn, Jiādìng Fǔ, swelled,
the next day the Jiāng River in Nánxī Xiàn swelled,
both sweeping away government offices and private residences.
In the eighth month of the seventh year,
the Jiāo Hé River in Gāomì Xiàn overflowed,
damaging crops.
In the seventh month of the eighth year,
Huái'ān, Běipíng, Hénán, and Shāndōng experienced great floods.
In the twelfth month,
Sūzhōu, Húzhōu, Jiāxīng, Sōngjiāng, Chángzhōu, Tàipíng, Níngguó in Zhílì,
and Hángzhōu in Zhèjiāng were all flooded.
In the ninth year,
Jiāngnán and Húběi experienced great floods.
In the seventh month,
Húguǎng and Shāndōng experienced great floods.
In the sixth month of the tenth year,
the Luán and Qī rivers in Yǒngpíng submerged people's homes.
In the seventh month,
eight prefectures in Běipíng experienced great floods,
damaging city walls.
In the seventh month of the eleventh year,
the sea overflowed in the four prefectures of Sū, Sōng, Yáng, and Tái,
many people drowned.
In the tenth month, on the day *bǐngchén*,
the Hé River burst its banks in Lányáng.
In the fifth month of the twelfth year,
mountain waters submerged the county seat of Qīngtián.
In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year,
the tide in Chóngmíng breached the sandbanks.
Many people and livestock drowned.
In the eighth month, on the day *gēngchén*, of the fourteenth year,
the Hé River burst its banks in Yuánwǔ.
In the second month, on the day *rénzǐ*, of the fifteenth year,
the Hé River burst its banks in Hénán.
In the third month, on the day *gēngwǔ*,
the Hé River burst its banks in Cháoyì.
In the seventh month,
the Hé River overflowed in Yíngzé and Yángwǔ.
In this year,
Běipíng experienced great floods.
In the eighth month, on the day *bǐngyín*, of the seventeenth year,
the Hé River burst its banks in Kāifēng,
flowing laterally for dozens of *lǐ*.
In this year,
Hénán and Běipíng were both flooded.
In the eighth month of the eighteenth year,
Hénán was flooded again.
In this year,
Jiāngpǔ and Dàmíng were flooded.
In the first month, on the day *gēngyín*, of the twenty-third year,
the Hé River burst its banks in Guīdé.
In the seventh month, on the day *guǐsì*,
the Hé River burst its banks in Kāifēng,
sweeping away and submerging people's homes.
Also, in Hǎimén Xiàn, wind and tide damaged official and private residences,
many were swept away and drowned.
In this year,
Xiāngyáng, Miǎnyáng, and Ānyáng were flooded.
In the tenth month of the twenty-fourth year,
the two prefectures of Běipíng and Héjiān were flooded.
In the first month of the twenty-fifth year,
the Hé River burst its banks in Yángwǔ,
eleven prefectures and counties in Kāifēng were all flooded.
In the eleventh month of the twenty-sixth year,
the three prefectures of Qīng, Yǎn, and Jìníng were flooded.
In the third month of the twenty-seventh year,
the Wèn Hé River in Níngyáng burst its banks.
In the eighth month of the twenty-eighth year,
Dézhōu experienced great floods,
damaging city walls.
In the eighth month, on the day *dīnghài*, of the thirtieth year,
the Hé River burst its banks in Kāifēng,
water surrounded it on three sides,
encroaching upon warehouses.
In the fifth month of the first year of Yǒnglè (1403),
the Luòhé River in Zhāngqiū breached its banks, damaging crops.
Nānhǎi and Pānyú experienced tidal overflows.
In the eighth month,
the Hónghé River in Ānqiū County breached.
In the sixth month of the second year (1404),
the four prefectures of Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu were all flooded.
In the seventh month,
Húguǎng and Jiāngxī were flooded.
In the ninth month,
the (Yellow) River breached in Kāifēng,
damaging the city.
In the third month of the third year (1405),
the Wēnxiàn River breached its dikes for over forty zhàng (approximately 128 meters).
The Jǐshuǐ and Làoshuǐ Rivers overflowed.
In the eighth month,
many counties under Hángzhōu were flooded,
drowning over four hundred men and women.
In the fifth month of the seventh year (1409),
the river in Ānlù Prefecture overflowed,
breaching the Xuànmǎtān embankment for over sixteen hundred zhàng (approximately 5120 meters).
In the sixth month,
Shòuzhōu was flooded, breaching the city wall.
That year,
over three thousand nine hundred zhàng (approximately 12480 meters) of the riverbank in Tàixīng collapsed into the river.
The Húnhé River breached in Gù'ān.
In the fifth month of the eighth year (1410),
the Wéishuǐ River and the Fúkānghé River in Píngdù Prefecture breached,
submerging one hundred thirteen locations.
In the seventh month,
Píngyáng County experienced tidal overflows,
washing away dwellings.
On the gengshēn day of the eighth month,
the (Yellow) River overflowed in Kāifēng.
On the wùxū day of the twelfth month,
the (Yellow) River breached in Biànliáng,
damaging the city.
In the first month of the ninth year (1411),
Gāoyóu's Bìshè and other nine lakes, along with all the rivers in Tiāncháng, surged.
In the sixth month,
the tides of the five rivers in the prefectures and counties under Yángzhōu swelled for four days,
carrying away many people and livestock.
In the seventh month,
Hǎiníng experienced tidal overflows,
drowning many.
In the eighth month,
the Zhāngshuǐ and Wèishuǐ Rivers breached their dikes, submerging fields.
In the ninth month,
Léizhōu was hit by a hurricane and torrential rain,
submerging Suíxī and Hǎikāng,
damaging over eight hundred qǐng (approximately 5300 hectares) of fields,
and drowning over sixteen hundred people.
That year,
Húguǎng and Hénán were flooded.
In the seventh month of the tenth year (1412),
the Lúgōushuǐ River swelled,
damaging bridges and dikes,
and drowning people and livestock.
Bǎodìng County had fifty-four breaches in its riverbanks.
In the eleventh month,
Wúqiáo, Dōngguāng, Xīngjì, Jiāohé, and Tiānjīn experienced dike breaches, damaging crops.
In the twelfth month,
Ānzhōu experienced water breaches at eighty-nine river mouths, including Zhítíng.
In the tenth month of the twelfth year (1414),
the Sùhé River in Línjìn flowed upstream,
breaching the Yáoxiānqú weir,
flowing into the saltpeter ponds,
submerging civilian fields,
and almost reaching the salt pans.
Chóngmíng experienced a sudden tidal surge,
washing away over five thousand eight hundred households.
In the sixth month of the thirteenth year (1415),
Běijī, Hénán, and Shāndōng were flooded,
damaging dwellings,
submerging fields,
with Línqīng being particularly severe.
The Fǔshuǐ and Zhāngshuǐ Rivers washed away civilian houses in Cízhōu.
In the summer of the fourteenth year (1416),
rivers in Nánchāng and other prefectures swelled,
damaging civilian dwellings.
In the seventh month,
fourteen rivers in Kāifēng Prefecture and its counties breached their dikes.
The Luánshuǐ and Qīshuǐ Rivers in Yǒngpíng overflowed,
damaging civilian fields.
The seven prefectures of Fúnìng, Yánpíng, Shàowǔ, Guǎngxìn, Ráozhōu, Qúzhōu, and Jīnhuá
all experienced sudden surges in their streams,
damaging city walls and houses,
and drowning many people and livestock.
The Liáohé River and Dàizǐhé River in Liáodōng overflowed,
submerging city walls and military屯堡 (túnbǎo, garrisons).
In the summer and autumn of the eighteenth year (1420),
Rénhe and Hǎiníng experienced tidal surges,
with dikes collapsing into the sea for over fifteen hundred zhàng (approximately 4800 meters).
In the fifth month of the twentieth year (1422),
all prefectures in Guǎngdōng experienced tidal overflows,
washing away dwellings,
damaging granaries,
and drowning over three hundred sixty people.
In the summer and autumn,
the Miǎnyáng River in Húguǎng swelled,
and the rivers north and south of Hénán and in Fèngyáng overflowed.
In the fifth month of the twenty-first year (1423),
the Éméixī River swelled,
drowning one hundred thirty people.
In the eighth month,
Qióngzhōufǔ experienced tidal overflows,
drowning many.
In the seventh month of the twenty-second year (1424),
Huángyán experienced tidal overflows,
drowning eight hundred people.
On the gengchén day of the ninth month,
the (Yellow) River overflowed in Kāifēng.
In the sixth month of the first year of Hóngxī (1425),
due to torrential rain,
the Báihé River overflowed,
breaching the dikes at Héxīwù, Báifú, Sòngjiā, and other mouths.
The Zhāngshuǐ and Fǔshuǐ Rivers in Línzhāng breached their dikes in twenty-four places.
The Hūtuóhé River in Zhēndìng greatly overflowed,
submerging fields in three prefectures and five counties.
In the seventh month,
the Báigōuhé River in Róngchéng swelled,
damaging crops.
The Húnhé River breached at Lángwōkǒu east of Lúgōuqiáo,
and Shùntiān, Héjiān, Bǎodìng, and Luánzhōu were all flooded.
In the seventh month of the sixth year of Xuāndé (1431),
the (Yangzi) River greatly swelled,
and half of the civilian dwellings along the river in Xiāngyáng, Gǔchéng, Jūnzhōu, and Yúnxiàn were washed away.
The Huángshuǐ and Rǔshuǐ Rivers overflowed,
submerging ten prefectures and counties of Kāifēng, and Nányáng Rǔzhōu and Hénán Sōngxiàn.
In the fifth month of the third year (1428),
Shàoyáng, Wǔgāng, and Xiāngxiāng experienced a storm for seven days and nights,
and mountain waters surged,
rising six chǐ (approximately 1.9 meters) on level ground.
Yǒngníng Wèi experienced a great flood,
damaging four hundred zhàng (approximately 1280 meters) of the city wall.
In the sixth month,
the Húnhé River overflowed,
breaching the Lúgōuhé River dike for over one hundred zhàng (approximately 320 meters).
In the seventh month,
all seven prefectures of Běijī were flooded.
In the seventh month of the fifth year (1430),
mountain waters in Nányáng surged,
breaching dikes,
and washing away people, livestock, and dwellings.
In the sixth month of the sixth year (1431),
the Húnhé River overflowed,
breaching at Xújiā and other mouths,
and twenty-nine prefectures and counties in Shùntiān, Bǎodìng, Zhēndìng, and Héjiān were all flooded.
The (Yellow) River breached in Kāifēng,
submerging eight counties.
In the sixth month of the seventh year (1432),
the Tàiyuán River and Fénshǔi River both overflowed,
damaging crops.
In the sixth month of the eighth year (1433),
rivers in the eight prefectures along the river in Jiāngxī swelled,
washing away civilian fields,
and drowning countless men and women.
In the first month of the ninth year (1434),
the Qìnshuǐ River in Qìnxiāng swelled,
breaching Mǎqǔwān,
passing through Huòjiā and Xīnxiāng,
turning level ground into a river.
In the fifth month,
Nínghǎi County experienced a tidal breach,
relocating over one hundred seventy qǐng (approximately 113 hectares) of land.
In the sixth month,
the Húnhé River breached its east bank,
from Lánghékǒu to Xiǎotúnchǎng,
and Shùntiān, Shùndé, and Héjiān were all flooded.
In the seventh month,
Liáodōng experienced a great flood.
In the first year of Zhèngtǒng, during the intercalary sixth month,
Shùntiān, Zhēndìng, Bǎodìng, Jǐnán, Kāifēng, and Zhāngdé six prefectures all suffered severe floods.
In the second year,
Fèngyáng, Huái'ān, and Yángzhōu prefectures,
Xú, Hé, and Chú prefectures,
as well as Kāifēng in Hénán,
in the fourth and fifth months, the Yellow River and Huái River rose and overflowed,
sweeping away residents' crops.
In the ninth month,
the Yellow River breached its banks in Yángwǔ, Yuánwǔ, and Xíngzé.
Six counties along the river in Húguǎng were severely flooded, and the river breached its banks.
In the third year,
the Yellow River breached in Yángwǔ,
the Qìn River breached in Wǔzhì,
the Zhāng River breached in Guǎngpíng and Shùndé,
and the Bái River overflowed in Tōngzhōu.
In the fourth year, fifth month,
the capital experienced a great flood,
destroying 3,390 government offices and private residences.
Shùntiān, Zhēndìng,
and Bǎodìng three prefectures, departments, and counties, as well as Kāifēng, Wèihuī, and Zhāngdé three prefectures, all suffered severe floods.
In the seventh month,
the Hūtúo, Qìn, and Zhāng three rivers all breached,
damaging the dikes in Ráoyáng, Xiànxiàn, Wèihuī, and Zhāngdé.
In the eighth month,
the Báigōu and Húnhé two rivers overflowed,
breaching the dike in Ānzhōu, Bǎodìng.
Sūzhōu, Chángzhōu, and Zhènjiāng three prefectures and Jiāngníng five counties all suffered floods,
drowning many men and women.
In the ninth month,
the Hūtúo River again breached in Shēnzhōu,
inundating over a hundred *lǐ*.
From the fifth to seventh month of the fifth year,
the Jiāng River overflowed in Jiāngxī,
and the Yellow River overflowed in Hénán.
In the eighth month,
the tide breached the seawall in Xiāoshān.
In the sixth year, fifth month,
Sìzhōu was flooded by over a *zhàng* of water,
sweeping away houses.
In the seventh month,
the Bái River breached its dikes in Wǔqīng and Huòxiàn at 22 locations.
In the eighth month,
Níngxià experienced prolonged rain,
causing floods,
and destroying many military settlements, fortresses, and beacon towers.
In the eighth year, sixth month,
the Húnhé River breached in Gù'ān.
In the eighth month,
Táizhōu, Sōngmén, and Hǎimén experienced tidal surges and overflows,
damaging city walls, official pavilions, private homes, and military equipment.
In the ninth year, seventh month,
the tide in the sandbars of the Yángzi River rose and overflowed,
reaching a height of one *zhàng* and five or six *chǐ*,
drowning over a thousand men and women.
In the intercalary seventh month,
seven prefectures in Běijī and Yìngtiān, Jǐnán, Yuèzhōu, Jiāxīng, Húzhōu, and Táizhōu all suffered severe floods.
Mountain waters in Hénán flowed into the Wèi River,
submerging private homes in Wèihuī, Kāifēng, Huáiqìng, and Zhāngdé,
and damaging the *wèi*-*suǒ* city walls.
In the tenth year, third month,
the Fén River dike in Hóngdòng breached,
and Pǔrùn Station was relocated to distance it from the disaster.
In the summer,
Fújiàn experienced severe floods,
damaging the *wèi*-city of Yánpíng Prefecture,
and submerging fields and private homes in three counties,
with countless people and livestock swept away.
Many prefectures and counties in Hénán suffered severe floods.
In the seventh month,
Yán'ān *Wèi* experienced a great flood,
damaging the moats and dikes.
In the ninth month,
many *wèi*-*suǒ* in Guǎngdōng suffered severe floods.
In the tenth month,
the Yellow River breached the Gold Dragon Mouth in Shāndōng and the Yánggǔ dike.
In the eleventh year, sixth month,
the Húnhé River overflowed in Gù'ān.
Both capital regions, Zhèjiāng, and Hénán all experienced continuous heavy rain and floods for months.
That year,
Tàiyuán, Yǎnzhōu, and Wǔchāng also all suffered severe floods.
In the twelfth year, spring,
Gànzhōu and Línjiāng suffered severe floods.
In the fifth month,
the Jiāng River in Ji'ān rose and inundated fields.
In the thirteenth year, sixth month,
the Yellow River breached in Dàmíng,
inundating over three hundred *lǐ*,
destroying twenty thousand houses,
and killing over a thousand people.
Hénán, Jǐnán, Qīngzhōu, Yǎnzhōu, and Dōngchāng also all experienced Yellow River breaches.
In the seventh month,
Níngxià experienced severe floods.
The Yellow River breached the Hàn and Táng two dams.
The Yellow River breached at Bāshùkǒu in Hénán.
It spread to Cáo and Pú two prefectures,
reaching Dōngchāng,
and destroying the Shāwān and other dikes.
In the fourteenth year, fourth month,
Ji'ān and Nánchāng, along the Lín River, all suffered floods,
damaging altars, temples, and government offices.
In the first year of Jǐngtài, seventh month,
Yìngtiān experienced severe floods,
submerging private houses.
In the third year, sixth month,
the Yellow River breached at Shāwān, Báimǎtóu, for over seventy *zhàng*.
In the eighth month,
between Xúzhōu and Jìníng,
the flat ground was covered by water one *zhàng* high,
and all private residences collapsed.
Nánjī, Hénán, Shāndōng, Shǎnxī, Ji'ān, and Yuánzhōu all suffered severe floods.
In the fourth year, spring and summer,
the Yellow River repeatedly breached at Shāwān.
In the fifth year, sixth month,
the tide in Yángzhōu breached the dikes of Gāoyóu and Bǎoyìng.
In the seventh month,
Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Huái'ān, Yángzhōu, Lúzhōu, and Fèngyáng six prefectures suffered severe floods.
In the eighth month,
Dōngchāng, Yǎnzhōu, and Jǐnán three prefectures suffered severe floods,
and the Yellow River rose and inundated fields.
In the sixth year, sixth month,
Kāifēng and Bǎodìng both suffered severe floods.
In the intercalary sixth month,
Shùntiān experienced severe floods,
the Luán River overflowed,
damaging city walls and private homes,
with the flood disaster being particularly severe in Héjiān and Yǒngpíng.
In Wǔchāng prefectures, the Jiāng River overflowed, damaging crops.
In the seventh year, sixth month,
the Yellow River breached in Kāifēng,
inundating fields and houses in Hénán and Zhāngdé.
That year,
both capital regions and Shāndōng all suffered floods.
In the first year of Tiānshùn, summer,
Huái'ān, Xúzhōu, Huáiqìng, and Wèihuī all suffered severe floods,
and the Yellow River breached.
In the third year, sixth month,
in Gǔchéng and Jǐnglín,
the Xiāng River surged and overflowed, damaging crops.
In the fourth year, summer,
the Jiāng River rose in Húběi,
submerging wheat and crops.
Běijī and Kāifēng, Rǔníng suffered severe floods.
In the seventh month,
the Huái River breached,
submerging military and civilian fields and houses.
In the fifth year, seventh month,
the Yellow River breached the earthen city wall of Kāifēng,
and a brick wall was built to defend against it.
Three days later,
the brick wall also collapsed,
and the water was over a *zhàng* deep.
The concubines of Prince Zhōu and officials and common people took rafts to escape,
and countless people died in the city.
In Xiāngchéng, the water breached the city gate,
drowning many people.
Chóngmíng, Jiādìng, Kūnshān, and Shànghǎi experienced tidal surges and breaches,
drowning over 12,500 people.
Zhèjiāng also experienced severe floods.
In the sixth year, seventh month,
Huái'ān suffered severe floods,
and the tide overflowed,
drowning over 1,300 salt workers.
In the seventh year, seventh month,
mountain waters in Mìyún suddenly rose,
and military equipment, documents, and houses were all submerged.
In the sixth month of Chenghuà three,
at Jiāngxià, the Jiāng River burst its dikes at the mouth,
extending to Hànyáng,
for over eight hundred and fifty zhàng.
In the fifth year,
Húguǎng experienced a great flood.
The Fén River in Shānxī damaged crops.
In the sixth month of Chenghuà six,
Běijī experienced a great flood.
In the intercalary ninth month of Chenghuà seven,
Shāndōng and the four prefectures of Hángzhōu, Jiāxīng, Húzhōu, and Shàoxīng in Zhèjiāng were all inundated by a sea overflow,
submerging countless fields, houses, people, and livestock.
In the sixth month of Chenghuà nine,
the five prefectures of Jīnán and Huáiqìng all experienced great floods.
In the eighth month,
Shāndōng experienced a great flood.
In the fifth month of Chenghuà eleven,
Húguǎng experienced flooding.
In the eighth month of Chenghuà twelve,
Zhèjiāng experienced gales, tides, and great floods.
Huái’ān, Fèngyáng, Yángzhōu, and Xúzhōu also all experienced great floods.
On the jiǎxū day of the second month of Chenghuà thirteen,
Ānqìng experienced heavy snowfall.
The next day, there was heavy rain,
and the Jiāng River rose sharply.
In the intercalary second month,
Hénán experienced a great flood.
In the ninth month,
the Huái River overflowed,
destroying official residences and private houses in Huái’ān Prefecture and counties,
and drowning many people and livestock.
In the fourth month of Chenghuà fourteen,
the Jiāng River at Xiāngyáng overflowed,
destroying the city walls.
In the fifth month,
Shǎnzhōu experienced a great flood,
and many people drowned.
In the seventh month,
Běijī and Shāndōng experienced flooding.
In the ninth month,
the Yellow River burst its embankment at Kāifēng for fifty zhàng.
In the seventh month of Chenghuà eighteen,
Chāngpíng experienced a great flood,
breaching forty-nine water gates at Jūyōngguān,

Water Anomalies
In the fifth year of Hóngwǔ,
the Yellow River in Hénán dried up,
and travelers could wade across.
In the second year of Tiānshùn, twelfth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the bitter wells of Wǔqiáng turned sweet.
In the fourteenth year of Hóngzhì, eighth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
the Róng County river water was reddish and turbid like the Yellow River.
In the tenth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
the bottom of Máhú Gorge water was white and clear enough to reflect,
the next day it was turbid like rice gruel,
and what solidified on the sand and stones of both banks was like fine dust,
only clearing after seventeen days.
On the day Dīngsì,
the two rivers southeast of the prefecture were white as snow and thick as gruel for three days.
In the fifteenth year, ninth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
the wells in Púzhōu overflowed,
with sand and earth emerging with the water.
In the tenth year of Zhèngdé, seventh month,
the Wén'ān water suddenly froze solid;
that day was extremely cold,
forming ice pillars,
both five Zhàng high and in circumference,
hollow in the middle with holes on the sides.
After a few days, bandits arrived,
and the people who took refuge in the holes
were mostly saved.
In the sixth year of Lóngqìng, fifth month,
the Lóngmù Well in Nánjī turned into wine.
In the twenty-second year of Wànlì, fourth month,
the water outside the Zhèngyáng Gate in Nánjīng was red for three days.
In the twenty-fifth year, eighth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the ponds in Púzhōu,
without wind, surged with waves,
overflowing three or four Chǐ.
The Hàomán River in Línzī suddenly swelled,
and the north and south sides confronted each other and clashed.
Also, the great bay tide in Xiàzhuāng suddenly rose,
gathering and dispersing inconsistently;
when it gathered, it was over a Zhàng,
when it opened, the bottom was visible.
The Xiǎoqīng River in Lè'ān flowed upstream.
At the Zhuānbǎn Two Sluices in Línqīng,
there were great waves without wind.
In the thirtieth year, intercalary second month, on the day Wùwǔ,
the Yellow River at Liánhuāzhài in Hézhōu dried up.
In the forty-sixth year, fourth month,
the water outside Xuānwǔ Gate and Zhèngyáng Gate was red for three Lǐ,
like blood,
and only stopped after a month.
In the forty-seventh year, fourth month,
from Xuānwǔ Gate's Xiǎngzhá to the East Imperial River,
the water turned red again.
In the tenth year of Chóngzhēn,
the wells in Níngyuǎnwèi roared and boiled,
stopping after three days.
The Ruǐ River in Hénán changed color,
becoming dark black and foul-tasting,
and many who drank it fell ill.
In the thirteenth year,
the Wèi River in Huáyīn was red.
In the fourteenth year,
the Lù River in Shānxī flowed northward for seven days and nights,
with a momentum like a surging tide.
In the fifteenth year,
the wells in Dázhōu roared,
and the Hàomán River turned to blood.
In the sixteenth year,

In the 13th year (1640), in the first month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,

Collation Notes
Chapter 55, line 2 (fire, wood)
The Hóngfàn states:
"Fire says, 'Flames rise upwards'."
If fire does not rise upwards,
then it loses its nature.

Former historians largely attributed anomalies like excessive heat, unusual vegetation, calamities of feathered creatures, misfortunes of sheep, fire disasters, unusual fires, and red anomalies or auspicious signs to fire;
we now follow this.

Calamities from Birds and Insects

spreading and burning several hundred homes.

They were very fat when prepared as food,
but touching their bones would cause instant death.

In the second year of Lóngqìng, first month,
the area outside Zhèjiāng Province's capital suffered a disaster,
destroying thousands of houses and boats.
Third month, on the day Yǐhài,
Qiánqīng Gōng and Kūnníng Gōng,
were both completely burned at the same time.
In the fifth year, second month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Nánjīng Guǎng Cāng and Huì Cāng caught fire.
In the first year of Wànlì, on the *jǐhài* day of the eleventh month,
a fire broke out in the rear quarters of Cíníng Gōng.
In the third year, on the *jiǎxū* day of the fourth month,
a fire broke out in the rear workshop of the Gōngbù (Ministry of Works).
In the fifth year, on the *bǐngshēn* day of the tenth month,
there was a fire in the forbidden palace.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the eleventh month,
there was a disaster at the Zōngrén Fǔ (Court of the Imperial Clan).
In the eleventh year, on the night of the *gēngwǔ* day of the twelfth month,
Cíníng Gōng suffered a disaster.
In the twelfth year, on the *jǐyǒu* day of the second month,
Wúyì Diàn suffered a disaster.
On the *guǐmǎo* day, the first day of the twelfth month,
another disaster occurred.
In the fifteenth year, on the *jiǎzǐ* day of the fifth month,
a fire broke out at the Sīshè Jiān (Directorate of Palace Furniture).
In the eighteenth year, on the *xīnyǒu* day of the third month,
a fire broke out at Zhàishān'ér Bǎo in Liáodōng,
destroying the fortress and its weaponry,
and injuring over ninety people.
In the nineteenth year, on the *jiǎchén* day of the twelfth month,
Wànfǎ Bǎodiàn suffered a disaster.
In the twenty-first year, on the full moon of the sixth month,
there was the sound of cannon fire from the rear building of the Tàicāng Gōngshǔ (Granary Public Office),
and all gunpowder and weapons were burnt to ashes.
In the twenty-second year, on the *rén yín* day of the fifth month,
a heavenly fire burnt over a thousand households in Tiělǐng Wèi.
In the twenty-fourth year, on the *jiǎyín* day of the second month,
a fire broke out at the gate of Lù Fǔ.
On the *yǐhài* day of the third month,
a fire started in Kūnníng Gōng,
spreading to Qiánqīng Gōng,
both of which were burnt to ashes.
In the twenty-fifth year, on the *rénwǔ* day of the second month,
a fire in Hángzhōu
burnt over 1,300 official and civilian residences.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Mǎhú Píngshān suffered a disaster,
spreading and burning over 800 households,
and killing twenty-four people.
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the third month,
a major fire in Sìzhōu
burnt over 4,000 civilian residences.
A fire in Xūyí
burnt over 160 civilian residences.
20,000 *shí* of grain were allocated for relief.
On the *wùyín* day of the sixth month,
the Three Halls suffered a disaster;
the fire started at Guījímén,
spreading to Huángjí and other halls,
the two pavilions of Wénzhāo and Wǔchéng,
and the surrounding corridor rooms,
all of which were burnt to ashes at once.
On the *jiǎyín* day of the twelfth month,
a fire broke out at the Lí Bù Wénxuǎn Sī (Ministry of Personnel, Bureau of Selection of Officials) office.
In the twenty-seventh year, on the *rénshēn* day of the eleventh month,
a fire broke out in the Nèifǔ (Inner Court),
spreading and burning the Shàngbǎo Sī (Directorate of Imperial Seals), Yìnshòu Jiān (Directorate of Seals and Ribbons), and the Gōngbù corridor,
stopping at the gable wall of the Yínzuò Jú (Silver Workshop).
In the third month of the twenty-eighth year,
a fire in Nányáng
spread and burnt Táng Fǔ.
In the twenty-ninth year, on the *jǐsì* day of the first month,
a fire broke out in Tiělǐng Wèi,
burning all vehicles and gunpowder.
On the *jǐmǎo* day of the eighth month,
the east side hall of Dàguāngmíng suffered a disaster.
In the thirtieth year, on the *yǐyǒu* day of the second month,
the residence bestowed upon Wèiguó Gōng caught fire.
On the *bǐngshēn* day of the tenth month,
Xiàolíng suffered a disaster.
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the twelfth month,
Pǔtuó Shān Temple in Nánhǎi suffered a disaster.
In the thirty-first year, on the *wùyín* day of the ninth month,
the grain barges in Tōngzhōu caught fire.
In the thirty-third year, on the *yǐchǒu* day of the second month,
Yùmǎ Jiān (Directorate of Imperial Horses) caught fire.
On the *xīnsì* day of the fifth month,
Xǐbái Chǎng caught fire.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the ninth month,
Zhāohé Diàn caught fire.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the imperial army was distributing gunpowder at Kuījiǎ Miào.
The gunpowder, old and solidified like stone,
was being split with axes,
when a fire suddenly erupted,
its sound like thunder.
Swords, spears, and fire arrows shot out over a hundred paces,
and countless soldiers and civilians died.
On the *dīngmǎo* day of the eleventh month,
the Xíngbù Tílão Tīng (Ministry of Justice, Prison Affairs Bureau) caught fire.
In the thirty-fifth year, on the *yǐmǎo* day of the second month,
the Shénqì Kù (Arsenal) in Yìzhōu caught fire.
On the *dīngyǒu* day of the fourth month,
the West Granary in Tōngzhōu caught fire.
On the *jǐmǎo* day of the tenth month,
the Nánjīng Xíngrén Sī (Nanjing Office of Protocol) office was destroyed.
In the thirty-seventh year, on the *gēngzǐ* day of the first month,
Qìng Fǔ caught fire,
burning the sleeping quarters and the treasury.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the third month,
Wǔchāng caught fire;
two days later, another fire occurred,
burning a total of over 260 households.
In the sixth month,
Qìng Fǔ suffered a disaster.
On the *wùwǔ* day of the tenth month,
Cháorì Tán caught fire.
In the thirty-eighth year, on the night of the *dīngchǒu* day of the fourth month,
Zhèngyángmén Arrow Tower caught fire.
In the thirty-ninth year, on the *wùzǐ* day of the fourth month,
Yíshén Diàn suffered a disaster.
In the forty-first year, on the *rénxū* day of the fifth month,
Shǔ Fǔ suffered a disaster,
its gate and hall burnt to ashes.
In the forty-third year, on the *rénwǔ* day of the fourth month,
a fire broke out in Liǔgōu, Huánghuā Zhèn,
spreading for tens of *lǐ*.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the hall and courtyard of Shǔ Fǔ suffered a disaster.
From the second to the fifth month, Chángníng Bǎo in Liáodōng
experienced five fires in total,
destroying innumerable houses, people, and livestock.
In the intercalary eighth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
the grain barges in Tōngzhōu caught fire.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the ninth month,
the Huǒkǒu Shuìxiè (Huǒkǒu Tax Office) was destroyed.
In the forty-fourth year, on the *jǐsì* day of the eleventh month,
Lóngdé Diàn suffered a disaster.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Yánxǐ Gōng in the southern city suffered a disaster.
In the forty-fifth year, on the *rénwǔ* day of the first month,
Dōngcháofáng caught fire,
spreading and destroying Gōngshēngmén.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the eleventh month,
Xuānxǐ Gōng suffered a disaster.
In the forty-sixth year, on the night of the *dīngchǒu* day of the intercalary fourth month,
eight fortress watchtowers in Yīnjiāzhuāng Bǎo, Kāiyuán, were burnt to ashes simultaneously.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the dining hall of Yuàngé Chǎng caught fire.
On the *rénzǐ* day of the ninth month,
Màolíng caught fire.
In the forty-seventh year, on the *guǐyǒu* day of the fourth month,
Kuījiǎ Chǎng (Armory Factory) caught fire.
In the first year of Tàichāng, on the *dīngmǎo* day of the tenth month,
Huìluán Gōng suffered a disaster.
In the first year of Tiānqǐ, on the *wùxū* day of the intercalary second month,
Zhāohé Diàn suffered a disaster.
On the *jiǎchén* day of the third month,
Hángzhōu caught fire,
spreading and burning over 6,000 households.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the eighth month,
it suffered another disaster,
with over 10,000 households inside and outside the city being destroyed.
In the fifth month of the year, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
the main hall of Qídú Miào suffered a disaster,
all gunpowder was burnt,
and many craftsmen and laborers died.
In the third year, on the *xīnmǎo* day of the seventh month,
the palace to the left of the imperial palace in Nánjīng suffered a disaster.
In the sixth year, on the *wùshēn* day of the fifth month,
Wánggōng Chǎng suffered a disaster,
with incessant thunderous sounds from the ground.
The gunpowder ignited spontaneously,
smoke and dust obscured the sky,
and daylight turned dark
for four or five *lǐ*.
On the *guǐhài* day of the fifth month,
Cháotiān Gōng suffered a disaster.
On the *gēngyín* day of the seventh month,
Dēngzhōu City Tower caught fire.
In the seventh year, on the *gēngzǐ* day of the tenth month,
the forward garrison in Níngyuǎn caught fire,
injuring over 200 men and women.
In the first year of Chóngzhēn, fourth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Zǒujūn Dūdūfǔ suffered a fire.
Fifth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the Yīngfángsī caught fire.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Dīngzìkù caught fire.
Seventh month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Gōng'ān Xiàn suffered a fire,
destroying the Wénmiào [Confucian Temple],
and spreading to over five thousand households.
In the second year, eleventh month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Huǒyàojú suffered a fire.
In the third year, third month, on the *wùxū* day,
it suffered another fire.
Eighth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Tóudàoguān suffered a fire,
and its firearms were completely destroyed by explosions.
In the sixth year, first month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
the Jǐnán Shùnmiào suffered a fire.
In the seventh year, ninth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
the Kuījiǎchǎng suffered a fire.
In the eleventh year, fourth month, on the *wùxū* day,
the Xīnhuǒyàojú suffered a fire,
injuring many people.
Sixth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
the Ānmínchǎng suffered a fire,
shaking and destroying city walls and government offices,
and countless residents were killed or injured.
Eighth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Shíyàojú suffered another fire.
Fire Anomalies
On the first day of the first month, *jiǎshēn*, in the twenty-first year of Chénghuà,
there was a fire-light from mid-sky slightly to the west,
which fell downwards,
transformed into white vapor,
and then twisted upwards again,
with a sound like thunder.
In the third year of Hóngzhì, third month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
in Yílǒng, there were red and white flames in the sky,
over three *zhàng* long,
flowing from the northeast of the county seat,
and falling more than sixty *lǐ* to the due east,
with a sound that shook like thunder.
In the eighth year, third month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
the beacon pole of the right guard of Guǎngníng caught fire,
five *cùn* high,
but the pole remained as before.
In the tenth year, fourth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
in Fùpíng, there was a fire-light,
eight or nine *chǐ* long,
as large as a windlass axle,
with a sound,
falling from the southeast to the southwest.
In the first year of Zhèngdé, third month, on the night of the *wùshēn* day,
in Tàiyuán, there was a fire as large as a *dǒu*,
which fell in front of the palace of the King of Nínghuà.
The beacon towers of Guǎngníng had fires at their flagpoles,
six in total.
Seventh month, on the night of the *rénxū* day,
a fire-light fell into a commoner's house in Jìmò,
transforming into a green stone,
round and over a *chǐ* high.
In the seventh year, third month, on the night of the *dīngmǎo* day,
there was a great wind, thunder, and lightning.
In Xiānjūzhài, Yúgān, there was a light like an arrow,
falling onto a flagpole,
then suddenly like a torch dragon,
its light illuminated the four wilds.
Soldiers shook the flag,
and it flew to the top of the pole.
After a while, the fire scattered,
and the tips of all the spears had light like stars.
In the twelfth year, fifth month, on the night of the *jǐhài* day,
a fire meteor fell into the prison of the Dūcháyuàn,
spinning for a long time before extinguishing.
In the fifteenth year, sixth month, on the night of the *guǐwèi* day,
in Táizhōu, three fire meteors fell,
as large as plates,
charring any grass or wood they touched.
In the fifth year of Jiājìng, seventh month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
there were three fireballs,
five or six *chǐ* large,
falling from the north to the east,
their light illuminating the sky.
In the twentieth year, seventh month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
a fireball as large as a *dǒu*
fell to the east of the middle gate of the Zǒujūn Dūdūfǔ,
extinguishing after a long time.
In the second year of Lóngqìng, third month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
the flagpole at the corner of Bǎoníngbǎo in Yánsuí emitted fire,
blazing with sound.
In the fourteenth year of Wànlì,
in Bǎodìng Fǔ, fire emerged from inside the walls of commoners' houses,
extinguishing after three days and nights.
In the fifteenth year, second month,
in the various forts along the border of Suíjìng,
the ridge-beasts and flagpoles all emitted fire.
When soldiers struck them with staves,
the staves also ignited,
and it extinguished in the third watch.
In the twentieth year, third month,
in Shǎnxī, there was fire in the sky,
as large as a basin,
later developing three tails,
falling to the northwest.
In the twenty-first year, second month, on the night of the *gēngchén* day,
the various *shòuwěn* [mythical beast decorations] on the tower of Dàmáoshān all had fire,
like chicken eggs,
red in color.
Immediately it rained and snowed,
and the fire made a hissing sound.
In the twenty-third year, ninth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
in Yǒngníng, there was a fire-light,
shaped like a house,
falling to the northwest.
Yǒngchāng, Zhènfān, and Níngyuǎn saw the same.
In the twenty-fourth year, second month, on the night of the *wùshēn* day,
in Hù Xiàn, there was thunder and rain,
and fire covered the ground,
for over ten *lǐ*.
In the twenty-fifth year, second month, on the *guǐhài* day,
in Píngliáng, the mouths of the tile-beasts emitted fire,
which could not be extinguished by water.
Eighth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
in Sù and Liáng Zhōu, a fire-light was in the sky,
shaped like a cartwheel,
its tail divided into three strands,
about three *zhàng* long.
On the first day of the fifth month, *rényín*, in the sixth year of Tiānqǐ,
a red ball rolled out of the Huǒshénmiào [Temple of the Fire God] at Hòuzàimén.
At the corner of the gate tower of Qiánmén, there were thousands of fireflies,
combining like a cartwheel.
In the first year of Chóngzhēn,
in Xī'ān, there were dozens of fires like millstones or *dǒu*s,
blue in color,
their flames about a *chǐ* high,
sometimes entering private residences,
staying for several days before leaving.
They were propitiated with sheep and pigs,
and caused no harm,
from the fifth month to the seventh month.
In the thirteenth year, sixth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
in Zhèn'ān, a fire-light like a *hú* [ten *dǒu*]
fell from the west to the ground,
charring earth and wood.
Red Omens and Auspices
In the thirteenth year of Chénghuà, second month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
in Shānyīn, Zhèjiāng, a spring gushed like blood.
In the first year of Zhèngdé, first month, on the night of the *yǐyǒu* day,
in Chóngmíng, there was a red light in the sky,
trailing a tail like a rainbow,
rising from the northeast and disappearing to the southwest,
with a sound like thunder.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
a red light erupted in Fèngyáng,
the same color as the sun,
with a sound like thunder.
In the second year, eighth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
a red light appeared in Níngxià,
five *zhàng* long.
In the eighth year, seventh month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
in Lóngquán, there were two red pellets,
falling from the sky into the county seat,
shaped like goose eggs,
leaping into private residences,
and fighting for a long time.
In the thirty-third year of Jiājìng, fourth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
in Cíxī, blood gushed over a *chǐ* high in a commoner's house.
In the thirty-seventh year, fifth month, on the *wùchén* day,
in Dōngyáng, in the house of a commoner named Zhāng Sīqí, the ground cracked in five or six places,
and blood gushed out like threads,
about a *chǐ* high.
The blood coagulated,
and dogs came to eat it.
Digging the ground, nothing was found.
In the thirty-ninth year, second month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
in Zhúxī, blood emerged from a commoner's house.
In the sixth year of Lóngqìng, intercalary second month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
in Liáodōng, a red wind raised dust, covering the sky.
In the sixth year of Wànlì, seventh month, Dīngchǒu day (July 1578),
at the home of Jīn Chāng in Sōngmén Wèi, blood gushed out three *chǐ* high,
with a sound.
In the thirteenth year of Wànlì, fourth month, Yǐchǒu day (April 1585),
Wáng Lù of Hóngmín sought lodging at Yáo Lěi's home.
He saw blood coming out of the ground,
and, startled, ran to the market.
The market also flowed with blood.
The villagers struck implements and shouted,
and then it stopped.
In the nineteenth year of Wànlì, sixth month, Gēngxū day (June 1591),
at Máojiā Pǔ in Cíxī, blood gushed out from eight spots,
each as large as a basin,
and about a *chǐ* high.
Blood splashed a boat,
and the boat immediately bled.
It splashed people's feet,
and their feet also bled,
stopping after several *kè*.
In the twenty-sixth year of Wànlì, ninth month, Jiǎchén day (September 1598),
at the home of Jiǎ Jiǔjīng in Xiāoshān, blood came out,
about a *chǐ* high.
In the first year of Tiānqǐ, sixth month, Gēngyín day (June 1621),
at Zhàoqìng, the commoner Wáng Tǐjī's courtyard sprayed blood,
like a gushing spring.
In the seventh year of Chóngzhēn, second month, Wùwǔ day (February 1634),
Hǎifēng had a rain of blood.
In the eighth year of Chóngzhēn, eighth month, Wùyín day (August 1635),
in Xuānchéng, blood came out of a pond.
The *Hóngfàn* says,
“Wood is said to be bending and straightening.”
If wood does not bend and straighten,
then it loses its nature.
Previous historians attributed rain, madmen, sumptuary violations, chicken plagues, rat infestations, wood ice, wood abnormalities, and both green omens and green portents all to wood.
We now follow this.
Rain
In the thirteenth year of Hóngwǔ, seventh month (July 1380),
Hǎikāng had heavy rain,
damaging the county administration.
In the twenty-third year of Hóngwǔ, eleventh month (November 1390),
in twenty-nine prefectures and counties of Shāndōng, there was prolonged rain,
damaging wheat and grain.
In the first year of Jiànwén, third month, Yǐmǎo night (March 1399),
the Prince of Yān camped at Sūjiāqiáo.
There was heavy rain,
and the flat ground had three *chǐ* of water,
reaching the prince's couch.
In the first year of Yǒnglè, third month (March 1403),
the capital had continuous rain,
damaging the southwest corner of the city wall for over fifty *zhàng*.
In the seventh month (July 1403),
Jiànníng Wèi had continuous rain, damaging the city.
In the second year of Yǒnglè, seventh month (July 1404),
Xīn'ān Wèi had continuous rain, damaging the city.
In the eighth month (August 1404),
continuous rain damaged the city of Běijīng for over five thousand *zhàng*.
In the sixth year of Yǒnglè, seventh month (July 1408),
Sīmíng had continuous rain, damaging the city.
In the seventh year of Yǒnglè, ninth month (September 1409),
five *wèi* garrisons in Zhèjiāng
had hurricanes and sudden downpours,
damaging city walls and sweeping away houses.
In the eighth year of Yǒnglè, seventh month (July 1410),
Jīnxiāng Wèi had hurricanes and sudden downpours,
damaging city walls and public offices.
In the twelfth year of Yǒnglè, ninth month (September 1414),
Mìyún Hòu Wèi had continuous rain, damaging the city.
In the twentieth year of Yǒnglè, first month (January 1422),
Xìnfēng had rain and water damaging the city.
Qúchéng Wèi was similar.
In the twenty-first year of Yǒnglè, second month (February 1423),
Lù'ān Wèi had continuous rain, damaging the city.
That year,
Jiànchāng Shǒuyù Suǒ,
Huái'ān, Huáilái, and other *wèi* garrisons,
all had continuous rain, damaging their cities.
In the twenty-second year of Yǒnglè, second month (February 1424),
Shòuzhōu Wèi had rain and water damaging the city.
In the third month (March 1424),
Gànzhōu and Zhènwǔ two *wèi* garrisons had rain and water damaging the city.
In the fourth month (April 1424),
continuous rain damaged Mìyún and Jìzhōu cities.
That year,
the Southern and Northern metropolitan areas and the prefectures and counties of Shāndōng
had continuous rain that severely damaged wheat and grain.
In the summer of the first year of Hóngxī (1425),
Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu had accumulated rain that damaged crops.
In the intercalary seventh month (August 1425),
the capital had heavy rain,
damaging the city walls of Zhèngyáng, Qíhuà, Shùnchéng, and other gates.
In the ninth month (September 1425),
prolonged rain damaged the city of Mìyún Zhōng Wèi.
In the first year of Xuāndé, fifth month (May 1426),
Yǒngxǐ and Yuèqīng had hurricanes and torrential rain,
damaging public and private offices, as well as altars and temples.
In the first year of Zhèngtǒng, seventh month (July 1436),
Shùntiān, Shāndōng, Hénán, and Guǎngdōng had continuous rain that damaged crops.
In the fourth year of Zhèngtǒng, summer (1439),
Jūyōng Guān and Dìngzhōu Wèi had continuous rain that damaged the city.
In the fifth year of Zhèngtǒng, second month (February 1440),
Nánjīng had strong winds and heavy rain,
damaging the ridge of Běishàng Mén,
and overturning official and civilian boats.
In the seventh year of Zhèngtǒng (1442),
Jǐnán, Qīngzhōu, Láizhōu, Huái'ān, Fèngyáng, and Xúzhōu
had continuous rain from May to June that damaged crops.
In the ninth year of Zhèngtǒng, intercalary seventh month (August 1444),
Yěhú Lǐng and other places had continuous rain that damaged city walls, moats, and watchtowers.
In the eleventh year of Zhèngtǒng, spring (1446),
seven prefectures and sixteen counties in Jiāngxī had continuous rain,
and fields and grain were submerged.
In the twelfth year of Zhèngtǒng, sixth month (June 1447),
Ruìjīn had continuous rain,
the market water was over a *zhàng* high,
sweeping away granaries,
and drowning over two hundred people.
In the thirteenth year of Zhèngtǒng, fourth month (April 1448),
rainwater damaged the border granary at Gǔběikǒu in Shùntiān.
From May to June (1448),
Fèngyáng and Huīzhōu had prolonged rain that damaged crops.
In the ninth month (September 1448),
Níngdū had heavy rain that damaged city walls and dwellings,
and many people drowned.
In the third year of Jǐngtài (1452),
Yǒngpíng and Yǎnzhōu had prolonged rain that damaged grain.
Dàsōng and twenty other *wèi* garrisons had prolonged rain that damaged their cities.

Madmen
On the first day of the Guǐsì month of the fifth month of the third year of Jǐngtài
on the occasion of establishing the crown prince the following day,
an incense pavilion was set up at Fèntiānmén.
A man from outside suddenly entered,
grabbed a red staff, struck the incense pavilion, and said:
"First strike the wood of the east, Jiǎ and Yǐ!"
In the eighteenth year of Jiājìng
the emperor was about to travel south.
A soldier, Sūn Táng, walked from the central bridge of the imperial road to below Fèntiānmén,
ascended the golden platform,
and sat there for a long time,
unnoticed by the gate guards.
He then climbed higher and shouted loudly,
and upon discovery, he was arrested.
He turned out to be mentally ill.
Dress of Ominous Signs
In the first year of Zhèngdé
women widely used pearl-studded head coverings,
calling them yīnglù.
In the first month of the thirteenth year
when the imperial retinue returned to the capital,
the emperor ordered court officials to wear yèsà, large hats, and luándài.
Jiěshìzhōng Zhū Míngyáng said,
yèsà and large hats
were used for travel,
not for appearing before the sovereign.
All these were close to being dress of ominous signs (fúyāo).
In the twelfth month of the fifteenth year
when the emperor returned to the capital after subduing Chén Háo,
he paraded those who had sided with the rebel and hung the heads of the rebels on poles,
all marked with white banners;
for several lǐ, everything was white.
At that time, the emperor was already unwell,
and those who saw it recognized its inauspiciousness.
During the Chóngzhēn era,
court officials liked to use sago palm fiber or bamboo shoot sheaths for belts,
for their convenience.
Commentators said that gold and silver were heavy and precious,
while sago palm fiber and bamboo sheaths were cheap and light,
implying that the cheap was about to replace the precious.
At that time, common people in the north made cè (a type of headgear)
with their brims low and tilted,
covering their eyebrows and eyes,
and called it
"not recognizing relatives."
Later, due to banditry and chaos, the people scattered,
and when they met relatives on the road,
some cried silently, not daring to speak,
or just waved their arms and left.

the rats finally disappeared.
Also, in the Guānshān mountains of Qínzhōu, thousands of rats transformed into quails.

Collation Notes
Gazetteer, 6th of 5 lines, 3rd character (gold, earth)
The Hóngfàn states:
"Metal yields to transformation."
If metal does not yield to transformation,
it loses its nature.
Previous histories often attributed drought, poetic omens, disasters of hairy creatures, dog calamities, metal and stone portents, and white portents and white auspicious signs all to metal;
we follow this now.

drought,

there was a drought.
