Poetic Omens
In the first year of Wú (1367) of Tàizǔ,
Zhāng Shìchéng's younger brother, the false Prime Minister Shìxìn, and Huáng Jìngfū, Yè Déxīn, Cài Yànwén were in power.
At that time, there was a seventeen-character ballad that said:
"The Prime Minister conducts affairs,
relying solely on Huáng, Cài, and Yè.
Once the west wind rises,
it will be a dry tortoise."
Soon after,
Sūzhōu was pacified,
Shìxìn and the three others were all executed,
this was its fulfillment.
In the early years of Jiànwén,
a Daoist priest sang on the road:
"Do not pursue the swallow,
the pursued swallow flies high,
flies high to the emperor's domain."
Then he suddenly disappeared.
This was a prophecy of the Jìngnán Campaign.
In the second year of Zhèngtǒng (1437),
the capital suffered drought,
and small children in the streets and alleys made earth dragons to pray for rain,
bowing and singing:
"Rain god, rain god,
city god and earth god.
If rain comes again,
return our land."
Those who interpreted it said that
"Yǔdì"
(rain god)
meant *yǔ dì* (give to the younger brother),
as *dì* (emperor) and *dì* (younger brother) sound the same.
"Chénghuáng" (city god)
referred to
Prince Chéng.
"Zàilái" (come again)
and
"huán tǔdì" (return the land)
referred to
the restoration of the throne.
In the final years of the Wànlì 萬曆 reign,
a Daoist priest sang in the market, saying:
"Guǐ 委 當 head sit,
Qié 茄 flower everywhere grow."
Northerners read 客 (kè) as 楷 (kǎi),
and 茄 (qié) was a homophone for 魏 (wèi).
This was interpreted as an omen for Wèi Zhōngxián 魏忠賢 and Kè Shì 客氏.
Also, outside the east gate of Chéngdū 成都, at the Zhènjiāng Qiáo 鎮江橋 Huílán Tǎ 迴瀾塔,
which was repaired by Bùzhèng Yú Yīlóng 布政余一龍 during the Wànlì 萬曆 era.
Zhāng Xiànzhōng 張獻忠 conquered Shǔ 蜀 and destroyed it.
While digging for bricks,
an ancient stele was unearthed.
On it was seal script that read:
"Yú Yīlóng 余一龍 repaired the pagoda,
Zhāng Xiànzhōng 張獻忠 dismantled the pagoda.
When the years Jiǎ 乙, Yǐ 乙, Bǐng 丙 arrive,
this land will flow red with blood.
The demonic fate ends in Chuānběi 川北,
Poisonous air spreads to Chuāndōng 川東.
The beak-flute needs no bamboo,
One arrow pierces the chest.
Hàn Yuánxīng 漢元興 first year,
Chancellor Zhūgě Kǒngmíng 諸葛孔明 recorded."
When the imperial army campaigned westward,
Xiànzhōng 獻忠 was shot and killed.
At that time, Sù Wáng 肅王 was the general.
There was also a popular rhyme that said:
"Yè Tái 鄴臺 again Yè Tái 鄴臺,
Cáo Cāo 曹操 comes out again."
The bandit Luó Rǔcái 羅汝才 styled himself Cáo Cāo 曹操,
and this was its omen.
Disasters of Insects
In the eighth month of the ninth year of Hóngzhì 弘治 (1496),
a black bear climbed from Liánchí 蓮池 in the capital city up to Xīzhímén 西直門 along the city wall.
The government troops pursued it but
could not capture it.
It bit one person to death
and injured another.
In the sixth month of the eleventh year (1498),
a bear entered the city from Xīzhímén 西直門.
Lángzhōng Hé Mèngchūn 郎中何孟春 said:
"We should prepare for bandits,
and also be cautious about fire.
During the Shàoxīng 紹興 era of the Sòng 宋 dynasty, a bear reached Yǒngjiā 永嘉 city.
The prefect Gāo Shìzé 高世則, observing that the character for bear (熊) contains the radical for fire (灬),
warned the prefecture to be careful about fire.
Indeed, the dwellings were subsequently burned down.
This is its omen."
That year,
there were many fires in the city.
In the seventh month of the fifth year of Jiājìng 嘉靖 (1526),
there was a tiger in Nánchéng Xiàn 南城縣
that had human hands and feet.
In the sixth month of the forty-fifth year (1566),
Lǐ Qián 李乾, a clerk in the Tàiyīyuàn 太醫院, presented a rabbit
whose body had five colors,
considering it an auspicious rabbit.
Calamities of Dogs
In the twentieth year of Jiājìng 嘉靖 (1541),
a dog was born in a civilian's home
with eight legs, four ears, and four eyes.
In the seventh month of the forty-seventh year of Wànlì 萬曆 (1619),
a civilian's home in Huáining 懷寧 gave birth to a dog,
five inches long,
four inches high,
with one head, two bodies, and eight legs,
resembling a human.
Metal Anomalies
On the Jiǎxū 甲戌 day of the first day of the first month of the eleventh year of Hóngwǔ 洪武 (1378),
during the morning court,
as the golden bell in the palace began to be struck,
it suddenly broke into two.
On the evening of the Dīngmǎo 丁卯 day of the sixth month (1378),
there was wind and rain in Níngxià Wèi 寧夏衞,
and helmets, flags, and spears all emitted fire.
On the Jiǎzǐ 甲子 day of the twelfth month of the twelfth year (1379),
the bronze pot in the Qiáolóu 譙樓 of Xúzhōu Wèi 徐州衞 rang by itself.
On the Yǐchǒu 乙丑 day,
it rang again.
That year,
stone bamboo shoots grew in Hú Wéiyōng's 胡惟庸 well.
When removed,
bamboo shoots grew out again from the side three times.
The following year,
Wéiyōng 惟庸 was executed.
On the Yǐmǎo 乙卯 day of the fourth month of the second year of Jiànwén 建文 (1400),
Yān Wáng 燕王 camped at Sūjiā Qiáo 蘇家橋.
The fire from the weapons was like a ball,
striking each other up and down,
with the clanging of metal,
and bowstrings ringing by themselves.
On the Rénzǐ 壬子 day of the sixth month of the thirteenth year of Chénghuà 成化 (1477),
coins rained down in Jīngshī 京師.
On the Jiǎyín 甲寅 day of the third month of the fourth year of Zhèngdé 正德 (1509),
the bell in the city tower of Gàizhōu Wèi 蓋州衞 rang by itself three times.
In the seventh year (1512),
the bells and drums in Qín Shǐhuáng Miào 秦始皇廟 in Wéndēng 文登 rang by themselves.
Chéngshān Wèi 成山衞 was the same.
On the Jiǎwǔ 甲午 day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Jiājìng 嘉靖 (1527),
coins rained down in Jīngshī 京師.
On the seventh day of the seventh month of the sixth year of Lóngqìng 隆慶 (1572),
something boomed,
flew to the coast of Huátíng 華亭 in Zhílì 直隸, and fell to the ground.
It was a bell.
The casting date and year were still visible,
and those who recognized it said it came from Mǐn 閩.
On the Jiǎshēn 甲申 day of the tenth month of the twenty-first year of Wànlì 萬曆 (1593),
the command flags, sword and spear tips of the Shāndōng Dūfǔ 山東督撫 all emitted fire,
and made a sound.
On the Gēngyín 庚寅 day of the fifth month of the twenty-sixth year (1598),
the large bell in the Gǔlàng Chénglóu 古浪城樓 rang by itself three times.
On the Dīngwèi 丁未 day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tiānqǐ 天啟 (1626),
stone lions in the capital were thrown out of the city.
Silver, money, and document registers drifted to Chāngpíng Yuèwǔchǎng 昌平閱武場.
On the Guǐsì 癸巳 day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Chóngzhēn 崇禎 (1633),
an iron axe flew down into Huòshān Xiàn 霍山縣.
On the Xīnsì 辛巳 day of the twelfth month of the eighth year (1635),
at the fourth watch of the night,
the great cannon on the Nánchéng Lóu 南城樓 of Shāndōng Zhèn 山東鎮 rang like a bell.
It continued until dawn,
when a loud roar ended it.
On the Bǐngshēn 丙申 day of the third month of the thirteenth year (1640),
the ancient bell in the Chénghuáng Miào 城隍廟 of Qízhōu 蘄州 rang by itself.
White Anomalies and Auspicious Omens
On the Gēngxū 庚戌 day of the sixth month of the first year of Hóngxī 洪熙 (1425),
there was a white vapor in the middle of the sky,
spanning the sky from east to west.
On the night of the Guǐwèi 癸未 day of the sixth month of the first year of Xuāndé 宣德 (1426),
there was a pale white vapor,
spanning the sky from east to west.
On the Gēngchén 庚辰 day of the eighth month (1426),
there was a white vapor in the southeast,
resembling a flock of sheep startled and fleeing.
After it disappeared,
there was black vapor like a dead snake,
which soon divided into two.
On the night of the Xīnhài 辛亥 day of the twelfth month of the fifth year of Hóngzhì 弘治 (1492),
there was a white vapor in the east,
extending across the sky from north to south,
five zhàng 丈 above the ground.
On the night of the Wùshēn 戊申 day of the third month of the first year of Zhèngdé 正德 (1506),
a red light was seen in the sky over Tàiyuán 太原,
like a bent bow,
six or seven chǐ 尺 long.
It then turned yellow,
then white,
gradually growing to over twenty zhàng 丈,
its light spanning the sky.
On the full moon of the twelfth month of the seventh year of Jiājìng 嘉靖 (1528),
white vapor spanned Tiānjīn 天津.
The Hóngfàn 洪範 says,
"Soil is for sowing and reaping."
If sowing and reaping are not successful,
then the soil loses its nature.

Previous histories often attribute wind, dust storms, darkness, flower anomalies, insect calamities, cattle disasters, earthquakes, mountain collapses, rain of hair, growth of hair from the ground, famine, and yellow anomalies/auspicious omens all to Earth.
We now follow this.
Wind
In the sixth month of the sixth year of Xuāndé 宣德 (1431),
a great hurricane struck Wēnzhōu 溫州,
damaging government offices, ancestral temples, granaries, and city walls.
In the seventh month of the fourth year of Zhèngtǒng 正統 (1439),
great winds affected the four prefectures of Sūzhoū 蘇州, Sōngjiāng 松江, Chángzhōu 常州, and Zhènjiāng 鎮江,
uprooting trees and destroying crops.
In the second year of Tiānshùn, second month,
a violent storm uprooted the pine trees at Xiàolíng.
The beast ridges and beams and pillars of Yìwénlíng's palace hall were mostly destroyed.
In the third year, fourth month,
Shùntiān, Héjiān, Zhēndìng, Bǎodìng, Guǎngpíng, and Jǐnán experienced continuous fierce winds for days,
and the wheat seedlings were completely ruined.
In the fourteenth year of Chénghuà, eighth month, on the dìngwèi day,
there was a great wind in Nánjīng,
uprooting trees at the Tàimiào.
In the fifteenth year, eighth month, on the xīnmǎo day,
a great wind uprooted trees at Xiàolíng.
In the twenty-first year, fifth month,
a great wind in Nánjīng uprooted trees at the Tàimiào,
and destroyed the beast-shaped ornaments on the roof ridges (wěnshòu) of the Dàsìdiàn and various gates of the Imperial City.
In the third year of Hóngzhì, sixth month, on the rénwǔ day, first day of the month,
there was a great wind in the Jìnglǔwèi of Shǎnxī,
the sky and earth turned dark,
then changed into a red glow like fire,
and after a long time, it subsided.
In the seventh year, third month, on the jǐhài day,
fierce winds struck the various guards of Guǎngníng,
and the city walls of Shěnyáng and Jǐnzhōu collapsed for over a hundred zhàng.
In the first year of Zhèngdé, sixth month, on the xīnyǒu day,
a violent storm broke the pines and cypresses at the Jiāotán,
and damaged the beast tiles of the Dàsìdiàn and Zhāigōng.
In the second year, intercalary first month, on the guǐhài day,
great winds in Lúlóng and Qiān'ān uprooted trees and destroyed houses.
On the yǐchǒu day,
a great wind damaged the right beast-shaped ornament (wěn) of the Fèngtiānmén.
In the third year, second month, on the jǐchǒu day,
there was a violent storm in Dàtóng,
house tiles flew around,
and it stopped after three days.
In the ninth year, second month, on the dìngsì day,
Chánglè experienced heavy rain and hail,
fierce winds and thunder,
and all house tiles flew off.
Fifth month, on the wùchén day,
a violent storm in Qūfù destroyed the beast-shaped ornament (wěnshòu) of the Xuānshèngmiào.
In the twelfth year, fourth month, on the bǐngchén day,
Láibīn experienced great winds, rain, and hail,
destroying official and private dwellings,
and all house tiles flew off.
Eleventh month, on the guǐsì day,
Nánjīng experienced great winds and snow,
toppling trees in front of the Xiàolíng hall and pine and cypress trees inside and outside the surrounding wall.
Twelfth month, on the jǐyǒu day,
a great wind struck Dàlǐwèi,
damaging the city gate tower.
In the thirteenth year, third month, on the jiǎyín day,
Qìngfú experienced great winds and hail,
damaging the Xuégōng.
In the sixteenth year, twelfth month, on the xīnmǎo day,
Gānsù Xíngdūsī experienced fierce winds,
damaging countless official and private dwellings and trees.
In the first year of Jiājìng, seventh month, on the jǐsì day,
Nánjīng experienced violent storms and rain,
the beast-shaped ornaments (wěnshòu) and ridge railings of the suburban altars and shrines (jiāoshè), imperial tombs (língqǐn), palaces and gates (gōngquè), and city walls were all damaged,
and over ten thousand trees were uprooted.
In the fifth year,
Shǎnxī repeatedly experienced great winds,
which swept away temples and hundreds of civilian houses,
leaving no trace.
In the eighteenth year of Wànlì, third month, on the jiǎchén day,
Dàmíng experienced fierce winds,
the sky alternately turned black and red.
In the twenty-sixth year, tenth month, on the guǐhài day,
inside the northwest tower of the Jiāfēnglùtái,
a whirlwind arose fiercely,
black qi rushed skyward,
and there was firelight inside the tower.
In the thirty-fourth year, seventh month, on the bǐngxū day,
a great wind uprooted trees at the Cháorìtán.
In the forty-first year, eighth month, on the yǐwèi day,
Qīngzhōu experienced great winds that uprooted trees,
and toppled city houses.
In the first year of Tiānqǐ, third month, on the xīnhài day,
a great wind raised dust that filled the four directions.
In the fourth year, fifth month, on the guǐhài day,
a sudden whirlwind arose on the eastern danchi of the Qiánqīnggōng,
a large piece of iron from the Nèiguānjiān, as big as a rooftop,
spun in the air,
and fell on the western danchi,
clanging loudly like thunder.
Eighth month, on the wùxū day,
cold winds in Jìzhōu killed people.
In the fourteenth year of Chóngzhēn, fifth month,
Nányáng experienced great winds that uprooted houses.
Seventh month, on the yǐhài day,
Fúzhōu experienced great winds,
damaging official residences and civilian houses.
In the fifteenth year, fifth month,
Bǎodìng and Guǎngpíng and other counties experienced strange winds,
damaging wheat and grain.
In the sixteenth year, first month, on the dìngyǒu day,
a great wind
broke the front door bolt of the Wǔfènglóu into three pieces,
and the rafters of the Jiànjídian were all broken.
The wind and dust storm made everything dark.
In the first year of Jiànwén, seventh month, guǐyǒu day,
the Prince of Yān raised an army.
Clouds and winds rose from all directions,
and people could not be distinguished even at close quarters.
A little later, a patch of blue sky about a chi wide appeared in the east,
and fire lit up the ground,
illuminating everything above and below.
In the eighth year of Tiānshùn, second month, rénzǐ day,
a windstorm and haze made it dark during the day.
In the sixth year of Chénghuà, second month, dīngchǒu day,
Kāifēng was dark during the day as if it were night,
and a yellow haze covered the sky.
In the third month, xīnsì day,
rain and haze made it dark during the day.
In the ninth year, third month, guǐwèi day,
in Jǐnán and its prefectures,
a fierce wind made it dark during the day,
and people could not be distinguished even at close quarters.
In the twenty-first year, third month, wùzǐ day,
Dàmíng experienced a windstorm and haze.
From chén hour to shēn hour,
red and yellow filled the sky,
then suddenly it was black like night.
After that, sand rained down,
and it only stopped after several days.
In the capital, from the first month to the third month,
there was a windstorm and haze but no rain.
In the second year of Hóngzhì, second month, xīnhài day,
Kāifēng was dark during the day as if it were night.
In the third month,
yellow dust chilled everything,
and a windstorm and haze covered the sky for several days.
In the fourth year, eighth month, yǐmǎo day,
Nánjīng was dark and dim.
In the seventh year, third month, jǐhài day,
Guǎngníng and its various garrisons were dark during the day.
In the fifth year of Zhèngdé, third month, jiǎzǐ day,
there was a great windstorm and haze,
and the sky was dark and dim for several days.
In the sixteenth year, eleventh month, xīnyǒu day,
Gānsù Xíngdū Sī experienced a black wind and daytime darkness,
which only dissipated the next day.
In the first year of Jiājìng, ninth month, jǐsì day,
there was a great windstorm and haze,
and it was dark during the day.
In the eighth year, first month, wùxū day (the first day of the month),
there was a windstorm and haze,
as dark as dusk.
In the twenty-sixth year, seventh month, yǐchǒu day,
Gānzhōu Wǔwèi experienced a windstorm and daytime darkness,
the color first red, then yellow.
In the twenty-eighth year, third month, bǐngshēn day,
wind and haze filled all four directions,
and the sun was ghastly white,
for five days in total.
In the thirtieth year, first month, xīnmǎo day,
a great wind raised dust that obscured the sky,
making it dark during the day.
In the fortieth year, second month, jǐyǒu day,
it was also like this.
In the fourth month, guǐsì day,
there was a great wind and rain,
and yellow earth made it dark during the day.
In the forty-third year, third month, on the full moon,
an unusual wind arose,
with a reddish-yellow haze,
which did not stop until the twenty-first day.
In the second year of Lóngqìng, first month, New Year's Day,
a great wind raised sand and moved stones,
making it dark and dim during the day.
This was uniform from Běijī to Jiāng and Zhè.
In the seventeenth year of Wànlì, first month, yǐchǒu day,
Gàizhōu Wèi experienced a windstorm and daytime darkness,
damaging government offices and residences.
In the twenty-fifth year, second month, wùyín day,
the capital experienced a windstorm and haze.
In the twenty-ninth year, fourth month,
there were continuous days of windstorm and haze.
In the thirty-eighth year, fourth month, wùxū day,
Chóngyáng experienced a windstorm and daytime darkness,
which became more intense at night,
damaging countless official and civilian houses and trees.
Before the eighth month of the forty-eighth year,
the prefectures of Yúnnán occasionally experienced daytime darkness.
In the first year of Tiānqǐ, fourth month, yǐhài day, at noon,
Níngxià Hóngguǎng Bǎo experienced a great windstorm and haze,
with falling ash flakes like melon seeds,
uninterrupted and numerous,
stopping after more than an hour.
As the sun was about to set,
it turned reddish-yellow,
like cooking smoke on the outside,
enveloping about a mu of land,
and where the sunlight shone, it looked like flames,
disappearing at midnight.
In the fourth year, second month, xīncǎo day,
a windstorm and daytime darkness occurred,
with dust and sand obscuring the sky,
and it continued for several days without stopping.
In the first year of Chóngzhēn, first month, guǐhài day,
Yǒngnián Xiàn experienced daytime darkness,
and people could not be distinguished even at close quarters.
In the seventh year, third month, wùzǐ day,
Huángzhōu was dark during the day as if it were night.
In the thirteenth year, intercalary first month, bǐngshēn day,
the sun in Nánjīng was dim and hazy,
a great windstorm and haze occurred,
with fine ash falling from the sky,
and nothing could be seen five paces away.
Four years later, in the third month, bǐngshēn day,
there was a windstorm and daytime darkness.
Flower Anomalies
In the sixteenth year of Hóngzhì, ninth month,
peaches and plums bloomed in Ānlù.
In the first year of Zhèngdé, ninth month,
plum blossoms bloomed profusely in Wǎnpíng Zǎolín Zhuāng.
That winter,
all flowers bloomed in Yǒngjiā.
In the sixth year, eighth month,
peaches and plums bloomed in Bàzhōu.
Insect Anomalies
In the fifth year of Jǐngtài, third month,
in the five prefectures south of the capital, insects ate mulberry leaves,
and spring silkworms did not thrive.
In the sixth year of Hóngzhì, eighth month, jǐsì day,
in Línjìn, insects rained down like snow.
In the seventh year, third month,
in Guǎngníng and its various garrisons, black insects fell to the ground,
as large as flies,
and after a while, they burrowed into the earth.
Cattle Calamities
In the twelfth year of Zhèngdé,
a cow in Xúzhōu gave birth to a calf
with one head and two tongues,
two tails and eight legs.
In the fifth year of Jiājìng, seventh month,
a cow in Nányáng gave birth to a calf
with one head and two bodies.
In the sixth year, eleventh month,
a cow in Zhāngpǔ gave birth to a calf
with three eyes and three horns.
In the eleventh year, second month,
a yellow cow in Tóngrén gave birth to a calf,
its body covered in patterns,
and it died immediately.
In the twelfth year,
a calf in Shāndōng Píngshān Wèi had patterns,
its front two legs and tail
were all covered in scales and armor,
with fine hair in between.
In the thirteenth year of Wànlì, ninth month,
a cow in Guāngshān gave birth to a creature,
with firelight filling the ground,
and its scales and armor bristled,
it died overnight.
In the thirty-seventh year, fifth month,
cows in Lìchéng and Gāoyuàn counties each gave birth to calves,
with two heads, three eyes,
two noses, and two mouths.
In the thirty-eighth year, third month,
a cow in Huòjiā gave birth to a calf
with one body and two heads,
four eyes and four ears,
two mouths and two legs,
and one tail.
In the thirty-ninth year, second month,
a cow in Jíxiàn gave birth to a calf
with one shoulder and two heads,
two mouths and four eyes,
two ears and seven hooves.
In the fourth month, a cow in the Jiàngyí Bù gave birth to a calf
with a human head and sheep ears.
In the forty-fifth year, eighth month,
a cow in Kāizhōu gave birth to a calf
with two mouths and three eyes.
In the first year of Tiānqǐ, tenth month,
a cow in Huìníng gave birth to a strange beast,
its entire body covered in scales and armor,
with firelight.
In the third year, tenth month,
a cow in Yuánlíng gave birth to a calf
with one body, two heads, and three tails.
In the seventh year, third month,
a cow in Jǔzhōu gave birth to a calf like a qílín.
In the thirteenth year of Chóngzhēn,
a cow in Xiāngyáng gave birth to a calf
with two heads and two eyes.

it shook twice more.
In the tenth month, on the days Wùyín and Xīnmǎo,
it shook again.

In the nineteenth year, in the sixth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,

In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐmǎo,

In the twenty-third year, in the first month, on the day Gēngchén,

In the second year, in the eleventh month, on the day Guǐchǒu,

In the sixth year, in the fifth month, on the day Rénxū, and in the eleventh year, in the eighth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ, the capital shook again.
In the thirteenth year, in the ninth month, on the day Rénxū, and in the fourteenth year, in the ninth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
the capital experienced earthquakes.
In the eighteenth year, in the sixth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Běijīng experienced an earthquake.
In the twenty-second year, in the sixth month, on the day Rénshēn,
Nánjīng experienced an earthquake.
In the first year of Hóngxī, in the second month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Lù'ānwèi experienced an earthquake,

In this year,
Nánjīng experienced earthquakes,
a total of forty-two times.
In the first year of Xuāndé, in the seventh month, on the day Guǐsì,
the capital experienced an earthquake,
with sound,
from the southeast to the northwest.
In this year,
Nánjīng experienced nine earthquakes.
In the second year, in spring,
it shook ten more times.
In the third year,
it shook repeatedly again.
In the fourth year,
both capitals experienced earthquakes.
In the fifth year, in the first month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Nánjīng experienced an earthquake.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
it shook again.
In the third year of Zhèngtǒng, in the third month, on the day Jǐhài,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
it shook again.
On the day Jiǎchén,
it shook twice more.
In the fourth year, in the sixth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
it shook again.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐhài,
it shook again.
In the fifth year, on the first day of the tenth month, Gēngwǔ,
Lánzhōu and Zhuānglàng experienced earthquakes for ten days.
In the tenth and eleventh months, it shook repeatedly,
damaging castles and houses,

In the tenth year, in the second month, on the day Dīngsì,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the second year of Jǐngtài, in the seventh month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the third year, in the seventh month,
seventeen sites in Zhūkēng Village of Yǒngxīn collapsed.
In this year,
Nánjīng experienced an earthquake.
In the fifth year, in the tenth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the capital experienced an earthquake,
with sound,
starting from the northwest to the southeast.
In the sixth year, in the second month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Ānfú experienced a great thunderstorm.
Two sections of the Yángtáng pond at Báiquánbēi collapsed,
one was three *zhàng* deep
and over ten *zhàng* wide,
the other was six *chǐ* deep
and more than one *zhàng* wide.
In the first year of Tiānshùn, in the tenth month, on the day Yǐsì,
Nánjīng experienced an earthquake.
In the first year of Chénghuà, fourth month, jiǎshēn day
(April 19, 1465), Jūnzhōu experienced an earthquake that lasted twenty-three days before ceasing.
In the third year (1467),
Sìchuān had an earthquake,
with a total of three hundred and seventy-five tremors.
In the fifth month, rénshēn day (May 22, 1467),
Xuānfǔ and Dàtóng experienced an earthquake
with sound.
Wēiyuǎn and Shuòzhōu also shook,
damaging beacon towers and walls,
and injuring people.
In the fourth year, eighth month, guǐsì day (September 26, 1468),
the capital (Jīngshī) had an earthquake
with sound.
In the twelfth month, wùxū day (January 20, 1469),
Húguǎng experienced an earthquake.
In the fifth year, twelfth month, bǐngchén day (January 7, 1470),
Rǔníng, Wǔchāng, Hànyáng, and Yuèzhōu experienced earthquakes on the same day.
In the sixth year, first month, dīnghài day (February 7, 1470),
Hénán experienced an earthquake.
In this same year,
Húguǎng also shook.
In the tenth year, fourth month, rénwǔ day (May 15, 1474),
Hèqìng experienced an earthquake.
In the ninth month, jǐsì day (October 3, 1474),
from yín (3-5 AM) to shēn (3-5 PM),
there were fifteen more tremors,
damaging government offices and civilian homes,
and injuring people and livestock.
In the tenth month, dīngyǒu day (November 27, 1474),
Língzhōu’s Dàshājǐng驛 (post station) experienced an earthquake,
with a sound like thunder.
Thereafter, there were repeated tremors day and night,
until the eleventh month, jiǎyín day (December 14, 1474),
when there were eleven tremors in one day,
and many city walls and houses collapsed.
In the twelfth year, first month, xīnhài day (February 4, 1476),
Nánjīng experienced an earthquake.
In the tenth month, xīnsì day (October 25, 1476),
the capital (Jīngshī) experienced an earthquake.
In the thirteenth year, first month, jǐsì day (February 19, 1477),
Fèngyáng and Línhuái experienced an earthquake
with sound.
In the intercalary second month, guǐmǎo day (April 3, 1477),
Líntáo and Gǒngchāng experienced an earthquake.
In the tenth month, there was a xīnyǒu day (November 24, 1477) that collapsed.
In the fourth month, wùxū day (May 20, 1477),
Gānsù experienced ground fissures,
and also shook
with sound.
Yúlín and Liángzhōu also shook.
Níngxià experienced a great earthquake,
with a sound like thunder.
Eighty-three sections of city walls collapsed.
Gānzhōu, Gǒngchāng, Yúlín, Liángzhōu, as well as Yízhōu, Tánchéng, Téng, Fèi, Yì, and other counties
all experienced tremors on the same day.
In the ninth month, jiǎxū day (October 25, 1477),
the capital (Jīngshī) experienced three earthquakes.
In the fourteenth year, sixth month (July 1478),
Guǎngxī’s Tàipíng Fǔ experienced an earthquake.
By the eighth month, yǐsì day (September 2, 1478),
there had been a total of seven tremors.
In the seventh month (August 1478),
Sìchuān’s Yánjǐng Wèi experienced continuous earthquakes,
causing government buildings to collapse,
and many people and livestock to die.
In the sixteenth year, eighth month, dīngsì day (September 1, 1480),
Sìchuān’s Yuècuì Wèi experienced seven tremors in one day,
and continued to shake for several days thereafter.
In the seventeenth year, second month, jiǎyín day (March 11, 1481),
Nánjīng, Fèngyáng, Lúzhōu, Huái’ān, Yángzhōu, Hézhōu, Yǎnzhōu, and Hénán’s prefectures and counties
all experienced earthquakes on the same day.
In the fifth month, wùxū day (June 24, 1481),
Zhílì’s Jìzhōu, Zūnhuà Xiàn experienced an earthquake.
In the sixth month, jiǎchén day (July 10, 1481),
it shook again,
three times in one day.
Yǒngpíng Fǔ and Liáodōng’s Níngyuǎn Wèi also experienced three tremors.
In the twentieth year, first month, gēngyín day (February 18, 1484),
the capital (Jīngshī), as well as Yǒngpíng, Xuānfǔ, and Liáodōng all shook.
Xuānfǔ experienced ground fissures,
with sand gushing out of the water.
Tiānshòushān, Mìyún, Gǔběikǒu, and Jūyōngguān suffered much destruction to their city walls and beacon forts,
and some people were crushed to death.
In the fifth month, jiǎyín day (June 20, 1484),
Dàizhōu experienced seven tremors.
In the ninth month, xīnsì day (October 16, 1484),
Fèixiàn experienced ground subsidence,
two feet deep
and about three zhàng in length and width.
In the twenty-first year, second month, rénshēn day (March 7, 1485),
Tài’ān experienced an earthquake.
In the third month, rénwǔ day (April 15, 1485),
it shook again,
with a sound like thunder,
and Tài Shān swayed.
Four days later, there was another slight tremor.
On guǐsì, yǐwèi, and gēngzǐ days, it shook continuously.
In the intercalary fourth month, guǐwèi day (June 4, 1485),
Gǒngchāng Fǔ, Gùyuán Wèi, and Lán, Hé, Táo, Mín (four prefectures)
all experienced earthquakes
with sound.
On guǐsì day (June 4, 1485),
Sūzhōu’s Zūnhuà Xiàn experienced an earthquake
with sound.
After several days, it shook continuously again,
and city walls and civilian houses collapsed.
In the fifth month, rénxū day (June 23, 1485),
the capital (Jīngshī) shook twice.
In the ninth month, bǐngchén day (October 1, 1485),
Liánzhōu and Wúzhōu experienced earthquakes
with sound,
shaking continuously for sixteen days.
In the eleventh month, bǐngyín day (December 10, 1485),
the capital (Jīngshī) experienced an earthquake.
In the twenty-second year, sixth month, rénchén day (July 11, 1486),
Hànzhōng Fǔ and Níngqiāng Wèi experienced ground fissures,
some over ten zhàng,
some six or seven zhàng.
Bǎojī Xiàn had a fissure three lǐ long
and over a zhàng wide.
In the ninth month, xīnhài day (October 18, 1486),
Chéngdū experienced seven or eight tremors daily,
all with sound.
The next day,
it shook again.
In the first year of Hóngzhì, eighth month, on the day Rén-yín,
Hàn and Mào Prefectures experienced an earthquake,
collapsing thirty-seven fortified houses in villages like Huángtóu,
with fatalities among the population.
On the day Wù-shēn,
the ground in Gégǔbǎo, Xuānfǔ, sank three chǐ deep,
measuring one hundred and fifty bù long and one zhàng wide.
In the Shāhé River, a ridge emerged,
one chǐ high,
and seventy bù long.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīn-mǎo,
Sìchuān experienced an earthquake,
lasting three consecutive days.
In the second year, fifth month, on the day Gēng-shēn,
Chéngdū experienced an earthquake,
lasting three consecutive days,
with sound.
In the third year, twelfth month, on the day Jǐ-wèi,
the capital city experienced another earthquake.
In the fourth year, sixth month, on the day Xīn-hài,
it shook thrice again.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐ-mǎo,
Nánjīng experienced an earthquake,
all houses shaking.

In the sixth year, third month,
Níngxià experienced an earthquake,

a total of twenty tremors.
In the fourth month, on the day Jiǎ-chén,
Kāifēng, Wèihuī, Dōngchāng, and Yǎnzhōu experienced an earthquake on the same day,
with sound.
In the seventh year, second month, on the day Dīng-chǒu,
Qǔjìng experienced an earthquake,
damaging houses

the two capitals both experienced six tremors.
In the eighth year, third month, on the day Jǐ-hài,
Níngxià experienced twelve earthquakes,
the sound like thunder,
toppling border walls, watchtowers, and houses,

From the ninth month, on the day Jiǎ-wǔ, until Xīn-chǒu,
Ānnán Wèi experienced twelve tremors.
From the tenth month, on the day Rén-xū, until Jiǎ-zǐ,
Hǎizhōu experienced nine tremors.

Nánjīng experienced another earthquake.
In the ninth year,
the two capitals each experienced two earthquakes.
In the tenth year, first month, on the day Wù-wǔ,
the capital city and Shānxī experienced an earthquake.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐ-hài,
Hǎifēng experienced an earthquake,
the sound like thunder,
stopping after several days.

Zhēndìng, Níngxià, Yúlín, Zhènfān, Língzhōu, and Tàiyuán all shook.
Túnliú was particularly severe,

Guìlín experienced ground sounds like thunder,

In the thirteenth year, seventh month, on the day Jǐ-sì,
the capital city experienced an earthquake.

In the fourteenth year, first month, on the first day Gēng-xū,

On the day Xīn-chǒu,
Pú and Xiè Prefectures,
Jiàng, Xià, Pínglù, Rónghé, Wénxǐ, Ruìchéng, and Yīshì Counties all experienced earthquakes,
with sound.
However, Ānyì and Wànquán were particularly severe,
with some civilians crushed to death.
In the first year of Zhèngdé, from the Guǐyǒu day to the Yǐhài day of the second month [February 1506],
Hépíng experienced more than ten earthquakes,
with sounds like thunder.
On the Guǐchǒu day of the fourth month [April 1506],
Yúnnán Fǔ experienced two consecutive days of tremors.
The Mùmì Pass experienced five earthquakes, each with sounds like thunder,
destroying city walls and houses,
and injuring people.
On the Dīngsì day of the eighth month [August 1506],
Àoshān Wèi in Láizhōu Fǔ experienced an earthquake,
with a sound like thunder.
The city walls were damaged.
Afterward, there were repeated tremors.
From the ninth month to the twelfth month [September to December 1506], Láizhōu
experienced forty-five earthquakes,
all with sounds like thunder.
In the second year
Zhènnán Fǔ’s Ānzhōu and Xīnxīng Zhōu experienced consecutive tremors for three days,
shaking people's residences,
and some people died.
In the fourth year
the ground in Guǎngníng’s Dàxīng Bǎo collapsed,
four chi long,
three chi wide,
and over four zhàng deep.
On the night of the Jǐhài day of the fifth month [May 1509],
Wǔchāng saw six flashes of green light like lightning,
with sounds like thunder,
followed by an earthquake.
In the sixth year
Chǔxióng experienced five earthquakes over three days.
Then, until the fifth month of the following year [May 1512], it experienced consecutive tremors for thirteen more days.
On the Jiǎchén day of the tenth month [October 1511],
Dàlǐ Fǔ’s Dèngchuān Zhōu, Jiànchuān Zhōu, and Ěrhǎi Wèi experienced earthquakes.
Hèqìng and Jiànchuān were particularly severe,
destroying city walls and government offices,
and some people were crushed to death.
On the Wùwǔ day of the eleventh month [November 1511],
Jīngshī experienced an earthquake.
Bǎodìng and Héjiān Fǔs and their eight counties and three guards,
and Shāndōng’s Wǔdìng Zhōu,
all trembled on the same day.
Bàzhōu experienced nineteen tremors over three consecutive days.
In the seventh year
from that day until the Jiǎzǐ day [May 1512], Chǔxióng Fǔ
experienced consecutive earthquakes,
with sounds like thunder.
On the Jǐsì day of the eighth month [August 1512],
Téngchōng Wèi experienced earthquakes for two days,
destroying city towers and official and civilian residences.
Red water surged out,
completely submerging fields and crops,
and many people died or were injured.
In the eighth year
Chéngdū and Chóngqìng Fǔs,
and Tóngchuān and Qióng Zhōus,
all experienced earthquakes.
In the ninth year
Fèngyáng Fǔ experienced an earthquake with sound.
On the Yǐsì day of the eighth month [August 1514],
Jīngshī experienced a major earthquake.
On the Rénchén day of the tenth month [October 1514],
Zhōufǔ,
Tàiyuán Fǔ’s Dài, Píng, Yúcì, and ten other zhōu and counties,
and Dàtóng Fǔ’s Yìngzhōu, Shānyīn, and Mǎyì two counties,
all experienced earthquakes,
with sounds.
In the tenth year
Yúnnán’s Zhàozhōu and Yǒngníng Wèi experienced an earthquake,
which did not stop for over a month.
Some days had twenty to thirty tremors.
Black gas emerged like mist,
the ground cracked and water surged out,
destroying countless city walls, government offices, and civilian residences.
Several thousand people died,
and twice that number were injured.
On the Dīngchǒu day of the eighth month [August 1515],
Dàlǐ Fǔ experienced an earthquake,
and until the Yǐwèi day of the ninth month [September 1515],
it experienced another major earthquake for four days.
In the eleventh year
Nánjīng experienced an earthquake,
and Wǔchāng Fǔ also trembled.
On the Jǐwèi day of the twelfth month [December 1516],
Chǔxióng and Dàlǐ Fǔs,
and Ménghuà and Jǐngdōng Wèis all trembled.
In the twelfth year
Fúzhōu Fǔ and its Yúgàn and Fēngchéng two counties,
and Quánzhōu Fǔ,
all experienced earthquakes.
Zhèjiāng’s Jīnxiāng Wèi experienced fifteen tremors
from that day until the Jǐchǒu day of the seventh month [July 1517].
On the Wùchén day of the sixth month [June 1517],
Yúnnán’s Xīnxīng Zhōu and Tōnghǎi, Héxī, and Gěi counties experienced earthquakes,
destroying city towers and houses,
and some civilians were crushed to death.
On the Jǐmǎo day of the ninth month [September 1517],
Jǐ, Qīng, Dēng, and Lái Fǔs experienced earthquakes.
In this year
Quánzhōu experienced several tremors from the second to the sixth month,
and Jīnhuá from the second to the seventh month.
All experienced multiple tremors.
In the thirteenth year
Dàlǐ Fǔ and Zhào and Dèngchuān Zhōus,
and Làngqióng County experienced earthquakes.
On this day,
Ménghuà Fǔ also trembled.
On the Jiǎwǔ day of the tenth month and the Guǐmǎo day of the eleventh month [October and November 1518],
it trembled again.
In the fourteenth year
Jīngshī experienced an earthquake.
On the Bǐngwǔ day of the ninth month [September 1519],
Chāngpíng Zhōu, Xuānfǔ, Kāipíng, and other wèi also trembled.
On the Bǐngchén day [September 1519],
Fú, Xīng, and Quán Fǔs experienced earthquakes.
In the fifteenth year
Ānníng, Yáoníng, Bīnzhōu, Ménghuà, and Hèqìng all experienced earthquakes.
Ménghuà trembled for two days,
toppling city walls and dwellings,
and some civilians were crushed to death.
On the Xīnyǒu day of the eighth month [August 1520],
Jǐngdōng Wèi experienced an earthquake,
with sounds like thunder.
City walls and government offices were shaken and toppled,
and the ground cracked in many places.
On the Yǐchǒu day [August 1520],
Jǐnán, Dōngchāng, and Kāifēng experienced earthquakes.
In the first month of the second year of Jiājìng,
Nánjīng, Fèngyáng, Shāndōng, Hénán, and Shǎnxī experienced earthquakes.
On the day Rénshēn in the seventh month,
various garrisons in Dìnghǎi, Zhèjiāng, experienced earthquakes;

On the first day, bǐngyín, of the first month of the third year,
Liǎngjī, Hénán, Shāndōng, and Shǎnxī simultaneously experienced earthquakes.
On the day Xīnhài in the second month,
the three prefectures of Sūzhōu, Chángzhōu, and Zhènjiāng experienced earthquakes.
In this year,
Nánjīng experienced earthquakes twice.
On the day Guǐmǎo in the eighth month of the fourth year,
Xúzhōu, one garrison and three prefectures/counties in Fèngyáng, and the two prefectures of Huáiqìng and Kāifēng all experienced earthquakes;
the sound was like thunder.
On the day Rénshēn in the ninth month,
Fèngyáng, Xúzhōu, and two counties in Kāifēng experienced renewed earthquakes.
On the day Guǐhài in the fourth month of the fifth year,
Yǒngchāng, Téngchōng, and Téngyuè experienced earthquakes on the same day.
Ānnán Garrison in Guìzhōu experienced an earthquake;
the sound was like thunder,
and city walls were damaged.
On the day Rénshēn,
it shook again.
On the day Wùchén in the tenth month of the sixth year,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
On the day Dīngyǒu in the eighth month of the twelfth year,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
On the day Gēngyín in the tenth month of the fifteenth year,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
All garrisons and outposts in the Dūzhǐsī of Shùntiān, Yǒngpíng, Bǎodìng, and Wànquán
all shook,
the sound was like thunder.
On the day Guǐyǒu in the ninth month of the sixteenth year,
Yúnnán experienced an earthquake.
On the day Gēngyín in the seventh month of the eighteenth year,
Chǔxióng, Lín'ān, and Guǎngxī experienced earthquakes.
On the day Gēngwǔ in the fourth month of the nineteenth year,
Táozhōu and Gānsù both shook.
On the day Jiǎxū in the ninth month of the twenty-first year,
Píngyáng, Gùyuán, Níngxià, and Táozhōu experienced earthquakes on the same day,
with sound.
On the day Dīngsì in the eleventh month,
Gǒngchāng, Gùyuán, Xī'ān, and Fèngxiáng experienced earthquakes.
On the day Yǐsì in the third month of the twenty-second year,
Tàiyuán experienced an earthquake,
with sound,
lasting ten days in total.
In the third month of the following year,
it recurred.
On the day Gēngchén in the fourth month,
the four prefectures of Fújiàn, Xìnghuà, Quánzhōu, and Zhāngzhōu experienced earthquakes.
On the first day of the third month of the twenty-third year,
Tàiyuán experienced an earthquake with sound for ten days.
On the day Wùyín in the seventh month of the twenty-seventh year,
the capital experienced an earthquake;
Shùntiān and Bǎodìng prefectures both shook.
On the day Guǐchǒu in the eighth month,
the capital shook again;
Dēngzhōu Prefecture and Guǎngníng Garrison also shook.
On the day Yǐwèi in the ninth month of the thirtieth year,
the capital experienced an earthquake,
with sound.
On the day Guǐhài in the second month of the thirty-first year,
Fèngyáng Prefecture experienced an earthquake,
with sound.
On the day Bǐngxū in the third month,
Shānxī experienced an earthquake,
with sound.
On the day Rènyín in the twelfth month of the thirty-fourth year,
Shānxī, Shǎnxī, and Hénán simultaneously experienced earthquakes,
the sound was like thunder.
Wèinán, Huázhōu, Cháoyì, Sānyuán, Púzhōu, and other places were particularly severe.
In some places, the ground split open and springs gushed forth,
with fish and other creatures inside;
in others, cities, walls, and houses
sank into the ground;
or flat ground suddenly became hills;
or there were several tremors in one day;
or tremors continued for many days without stopping.
The Yellow River and the Wèi River overflowed greatly;
Huàyuè and Zhōngnán Shān roared;
the Yellow River became clear for several days.
Eighty-three thousand and more officials, soldiers, and civilians were crushed to death.
On the day Gēngshēn in the first month of the thirty-seventh year,
Shǎnxī experienced an earthquake.
On the day Dīngchǒu in the third month,
Chāngpíng Zhōu experienced an earthquake.
On the day Dīngmǎo in the fifth month,
Púzhōu experienced continuous earthquakes for three days,
the sound was like thunder.
On the day Jiǎshēn in the sixth month,
it shook again.
On the day Bǐngwǔ in the tenth month,
Huázhōu experienced an earthquake,
the sound was like thunder.
On the day Rénzǐ it shook again,
and on the day Wùwǔ it shook greatly again,
collapsing and burying many houses.
On the day Xīnsì in the seventh month of the thirty-eighth year,
Nánjīng experienced an earthquake,
with sound.
In the fourth month of the thirty-ninth year,
Jiāxīng and Húzhōu experienced earthquakes,
houses swayed like sails.
River water surged violently,
all the fish leapt out.
On the day Wùxū in the second month of the fortieth year,
Shāndān Garrison in Gānsù experienced an earthquake,
with sound,
damaging castles and houses.
On the day Rénshēn in the sixth month,
Tàiyuán, Dàtóng, and Yúlín experienced earthquakes;
Níngxià and Gùyuán were particularly severe.
City walls, beacon towers, and government offices were all destroyed;
black and yellow sandy water gushed from the ground;
countless soldiers and civilians were crushed to death;
cities like Guǎngwǔ and Hóngsì were ruined.
On the day Bǐngshēn in the first month of the forty-first year,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In this year,
Níngxià experienced an earthquake,
collapsing border walls.
On the day Guǐsì in the first month of the forty-fifth year,
the three prefectures of Fújiàn, Xìnghuà, and Quánzhōu experienced earthquakes on the same day.
On the day Jiǎyín in the third month of the second year of Lóngqìng,
Qìngyáng, Xī'ān, Hànzhōng, and Níngxià in Shǎnxī;
Púzhōu and Ānyì in Shānxī;
Yúnyáng in Húguǎng; and fifteen prefectures/counties in Hénán
experienced earthquakes on the same day.
On the day Wùyín,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
On this day,
Dēngzhōu in Shāndōng and Shùnyì and other counties in Sìchuān experienced earthquakes on the same day.
In Lètíng, the ground split open more than three zhàng in two places,
and black sandy water gushed out.
Níngyuǎn city collapsed.
On the day Guǐwèi in the fourth month,
Huáiqìng, Nányáng, Rǔníng, and Níngxià experienced earthquakes on the same day.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Fèngxiáng, Píngliáng, Xī'ān, and Qìngyáng experienced earthquakes,
damaging cities and injuring people.
On the day Xīnyǒu in the seventh month,
the ground in Língchuān split for over thirty paces.
On the day Gēngchén in the eleventh month of the third year,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
On the day Wùxū in the fourth month of the fourth year,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
On the day Bǐngwǔ in the second month of the fifth year,
the residence of the Prince of Jìngjiāng in Guǎngxī, the dwellings of the imperial clan, and the offices of the Provincial Administration Commission
all collapsed into the ground.
On the first day, Xīnmǎo, of the sixth month,
the capital experienced earthquakes three times.
In the eighth month, on the day *wùshēn*, of the first year of the Wànlì reign,
Jīngzhōu experienced an earthquake.
It did not cease until the day *bǐngyín*.
In the second month, on the day *guǐhài*, of the second year,
Chángtīng experienced an earthquake,
which split the ground into pits
and swallowed up civilian residences.
In the second month, on the day *jiǎxū*, of the third year,
Húguǎng and Jiāngxī experienced earthquakes.
In the fifth month, on the first day *wùxū*,
Xiāngyáng, Yúnzāyáng, and Nányáng Fǔ and its subordinate areas experienced earthquakes for three days.
On the day *jǐhài*,
Xìnyáng also experienced a quake.
In the sixth month, on the day *wùzǐ*,
Fúzhōu, Tīngzhōu, Zhāngzhōu and other prefectures, as well as Hàiyáng Xiàn in Guǎngdōng, all experienced earthquakes.
In the ninth month, on the day *wùwǔ*,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the tenth month, on the day *dīngmǎo*,
it quaked again.
On the day *jǐmǎo*,
Mínzhōuwèi experienced an earthquake.
From the day *jǐchǒu* to *rénwǔ*,
there were over a hundred consecutive tremors.
In the second month, on the day *gēngchén*, of the fourth year,
Jìzhèn and Liáozhèn experienced earthquakes.
On the day *xīnsì*,
it quaked again.
In the second month, on the day *xīnsì*, of the fifth year,
Téngyuè experienced over twenty tremors,
and it quaked again the next day.
Mountains collapsed and waters surged,
destroying over a thousand temples, ancestral halls, and granaries.
Seven-tenths of civilian residences collapsed,
and countless soldiers and civilians were crushed to death.
In the second month, on the day *xīnmǎo*, of the sixth year,
in a field in Lín’guì Cūn, a plume of green smoke rose straight up,
followed by a crack in the earth more than a *zhàng* wide.
A rumbling drum-like sound was heard,
and civilian residences, large trees, and rocks all sank.
In the seventh month, on the day *wùwǔ*, of the seventh year,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the fifth month, on the day *rénwǔ*, of the eighth year,
Zūnhuà experienced several tremors,
which ceased after seven days.
In the seventh month, on the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Jǐngpíng Lù experienced a major earthquake,
destroying several hundred *zhàng* of city walls.
In the fourth month, on the day *jǐyǒu*, of the ninth year,
Wèizhōu experienced an earthquake,
with a sound like thunder.
Houses were cracked by the tremors.
Dàtóng Zhèn, its various forts, prefectures, and counties
all experienced earthquakes at the same time,
with sound.
In the second month, on the day *wùzǐ*, of the eleventh year,
Chéngtiān Fǔ experienced an earthquake.
In the second month, on the day *dīngmǎo*, of the twelfth year,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the fifth month, on the day *jiǎwǔ*,
it quaked again.
In the second month, on the day *dīngwèi*, of the thirteenth year,
Huái’ān, Yángzhōu, Lúzhōu, as well as Shàngyuán, Jiāngníng, Jiāngpǔ, and Lùhé all experienced earthquakes.
The river waves boiled.
In the third month, on the day *wùyín*,
Shānyīn Xiàn in Shānxī experienced an earthquake,
which ceased after fifteen days.
In the eighth month, on the day *jǐyǒu*,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the fourth month, on the day *guǐyǒu*, of the fourteenth year,
it quaked again.
In the third month, on the day *rénchén*, of the fifteenth year,
Kāifēng Fǔ and its subordinate areas experienced three earthquakes.
Zhāngdé, Wèihuī, and Huáiqìng quaked on the same day.
In the fifth month,
Shānxī experienced an earthquake.
In the sixth month, on the day *gēngshēn*, of the sixteenth year,
the capital experienced two more tremors.
In the seventh month, on the day *jǐwèi*, of the seventeenth year,
Hángzhōu, Wēnzhōu, and Shàoxīng experienced earthquakes.
In the sixth month, on the day *bǐngzǐ*, of the eighteenth year,
Líntáo in Gānsù experienced an earthquake,
destroying city walls and civilian dwellings,
and crushing countless people and livestock to death.
In the eighth month,
Fújiàn experienced repeated tremors.
In the intercalary third month, on the day *jǐsì*, of the nineteenth year,
Chāngpíng Zhōu experienced an earthquake.
In the tenth month, on the day *wùxū*,
Shāndānwèi experienced an earthquake,
destroying city walls.
In the fifth month, on the day *dīngyǒu*, of the twenty-third year,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the twelfth month, on the day *guǐhài*,
Shǎnxī experienced an earthquake,
with a sound like thunder.
In the eleventh month of the twenty-fourth year,
Fújiàn experienced an earthquake.
In the first month, on the first day *rénchén*, of the twenty-fifth year,
Sìchuān experienced earthquakes for three days.
In the eighth month, on the day *jǐmǎo*,
Liáoyáng, Guǎngníng, and other garrisons experienced earthquakes,
and water surged for three days.
On the day *jiǎshēn*,
the capital experienced an earthquake,
and Xuānfǔ, Jìzhèn, and other places all quaked.
In the twelfth month, on the day *yǐyǒu*,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the first month, on the first day *dīnghài*, of the twenty-sixth year,
Níngxià experienced an earthquake.
The next day,
the ground in Chánglè sank five *zhàng*.
In the eighth month, on the day *dīngchǒu*,
the capital experienced an earthquake,
with sound.
In the seventh month, on the day *xīnwèi*, of the twenty-seventh year,
Chéngtiān, Miànyáng, and Yuèzhōu experienced earthquakes.
In the second month, on the day *wùyín*, of the twenty-eighth year,
the capital experienced an earthquake,

In the fourth month, on the day *bǐngwǔ*, of the thirty-first year,
Zhōngxiáng Xiàn in Chéngtiān Fǔ experienced an earthquake,
and houses were destroyed and cracked.
In the fifth month, on the day *wùyín*,
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the intercalary ninth month, on the day *gēngchén*, of the thirty-second year,
Gǒngchāng and Lǐquán experienced over ten tremors in one day,
and city walls and civilian residences were both destroyed.
The boundary between Báiyáng and Wúquán cracked for three *zhàng*,

In the fifth month, on the day *xīnchǒu*, of the thirty-third year,
Lùchuān experienced an earthquake,
with sound,

In the sixth month, on the day *gēngwǔ*,

In the sixth month, on the day *bǐngchén*, of the thirty-fourth year,
Shǎnxī experienced an earthquake.
In the seventh month, on the day *yǐmǎo*, of the thirty-fifth year,

In the second month, on the day *wùchén*, of the thirty-sixth year,

In the seventh month, on the day *dīngyǒu*,

In the second month, on the day *yǐhài*, of the fortieth year,

Yánsuí’s `Gūshān` city sank thirty-five `zhàng` [approx. 112 meters],

`Jǐnán` and eight dependent counties of `Dōngchāng`

destroying countless civilian residences.

experienced an earthquake as if turning over,
destroying city walls totaling over seven thousand nine hundred `zhàng` [approx. 25.28 km],
over eleven thousand eight hundred houses,
and crushing to death over twelve thousand men and women.
In the eleventh month, on the day `Guǐmǎo`,
Shǎnxī experienced an earthquake.
On the first day of the fourth month, `Gēngshēn`, of the third year
the capital experienced an earthquake.
In the tenth month, on the day `Yǐhài`,
it shook again.

the capital experienced another earthquake.

The three guards of `Tiānjīn`, `Xuānfǔ`, and `Dàtóng` all experienced dozens of tremors,
with tragic casualties.
`Língqiū` in Shānxī shook dozens of times day and night,
only stopping after more than a month.
City walls and residences were all destroyed,
and countless people were crushed to death.

`Nánjīng` also experienced an earthquake.

various guards, camps, garrisons, and forts of `Níngxià`,
from the first month, `Jǐsì`, to the second month, `Jǐhài`,

some as loud as thunder,
others as small as drums or wind.
City walls, houses, border walls, and beacon towers all collapsed.

Mountains collapsed.
In the sixth year of the Hóngwǔ reign, on the *rénxū* day of the first month, during the night,
a mountain in Fúqiāng, Gāoshān, collapsed.
In the eighth year of the Zhèngtǒng reign, in the eleventh month,
a mountain in Shàoxīng, Zhèjiāng, shifted to flat fields.
That same year,
mountains collapsed in two places in Shǎnxī.
In the thirteenth year,
Shǎnxī experienced continuous autumn and summer rains,
and mountains in Tōngwèi, Píngliáng, and Huátíng three counties tilted,
killing over eighty military and civilian personnel.
In the fourth year of the Tiānshùn reign, in the tenth month,
Xīngzǐshān cracked.
In the eighth year of the Chénghuà reign, in the seventh month,
the North Mountain in Lǒngzhōu roared for three days,
cracking to form a gully
half a *lǐ* long,
then closing again.
In the sixteenth year, on the *rénzǐ* day of the fourth month,
the Báishí Xuěshān on the north bank of the Jīnshā Jiāng in Jùjīnzhōu cracked for about a *lǐ*,
and the mountains on both banks converged,
the vegetation on the mountains remaining as before.
The river flow below was blocked,
and all grain and millet were submerged.
After a long time, the blockage below gradually opened,
and the water began to flow out.
In the sixth month,
a small mound emerged from the flat ground in Chánglè;
people and animals who stepped on it would sink.
The following year,
another high mountain emerged.
In the seventeenth year, on the *xīnchǒu* day of the twelfth month,
a mountain south of the city of Shòuyáng Xiàn collapsed,
with a sound like a bull's roar.
In the third year of the Hóngzhì reign, on the *yǐsì* day of the sixth month,
a mountain collapsed and the ground sank in Hézhōu.
In the ninth year, on the *gēngyín* day of the sixth month,
Shānyīn and Xiāoshān two counties experienced heavy rain and mountain collapses on the same day.
In the fourteenth year, in the intercalary seventh month,
the Wūsà Jūnmínfǔ experienced heavy rain and mountain collapses.
In the fifteenth year, on the *wùshēn* day of the eighth month,
a stone mountain collapsed at Héhékǒu in Xuānfǔ.
In the eighteenth year, on the *bǐngzǐ* day of the sixth month,
Shāzǐgōu in Hézhōu experienced a great thunderstorm at night,
and the stone banks and mountains collapsed,
shifting seven or eight *lǐ*,
the collapsed area cracking into a gully,
trapping fields, houses, civilians, and livestock.
In the first year of the Zhèngdé reign, on the *guǐhài* day of the twelfth month,
rocks collapsed on Sānbiǎoshān in Jìmò.
In the fourth year, on the *jiǎyín* day of the third month,
mountains collapsed in two places in Dàjiāyù, Dōngshān, Liáodōng,
about ten *zhàng* apart.
In the fifth year, on the *guǐsì* day of the sixth month,
a mountain collapsed in Qínzhōu,
damaging many houses and crops.
The mountain at Lóngwánggōukǒu also collapsed.
In the sixth year, on the *bǐngyín* day of the seventh month,
Zhāngzǐxī in Kuízhōu experienced a sudden downpour,
and a mountain collapsed.
In the thirteenth year, on the *guǐhài* day of the fifth month,
a mountain collapsed at Hēiyánjǐng in Yúnnán,
blocking the well.
In the fifteenth year, on the *dīngchǒu* day of the eighth month,
Zhàozhōu in Yúnnán experienced heavy rain,
and a mountain collapsed.
In the fourth year of the Jiājìng reign, on the *yǐyǒu* day of the seventh month,
Jiājiāshān in Qīngyuán collapsed.
In the fifth year, on the *rénshēn* day of the fourth month,
Dǎisūtún in Guìzhōu collapsed.
In the nineteenth year, on the *jǐsì* day of the twelfth month,
Sònghuángguān on Éméishān roared,
cracked open,
and gushed spring water for eight days.
In the twenty-first year, on the *yǐyǒu* day of the sixth month,
Shāzǐlǐng in Guīzhōu experienced a great thunderstorm,
and cliffs and rocks collapsed,
blocking the river flow for about two *lǐ*.
In the twenty-sixth year, on the *guǐyǒu* day of the seventh month,
Jiètóulǐng in Mábeishān, Chéngchéng,
roared day and night for several days.
The mountain suddenly broke in the middle,
and moved,
three *lǐ* east-west,
and five *lǐ* north-south.
In the second year of the Lóngqìng reign, on the *gēngxū* day of the fifth month,
a mountain collapsed in Yǒngníngzhōu.
That same year,
the ground cracked in three places in Lètíng,
all gushing black sandy water.
In the fourth year, in the eighth month,
a mountain in Húzhōu collapsed,
forming a lake.
In the twenty-fifth year of the Wànlì reign, in the sixth month,
Tàishān collapsed.
In the twenty-seventh year, on the *jiǎwǔ* day of the eighth month,
a mountain east of Dídào city collapsed,
forming a gully below.
Five mountains, large and small, emerged from the cultivated land south of the mountain,
over twenty *zhàng* high.
In the thirty-third year, on the *bǐngwǔ* day of the eighth month,
Huáshān southwest of Zhènjiāng cracked two or three *chǐ*.
In the thirty-seventh year, on the *xīnyǒu* day of the sixth month,
Nánshān in Gānsù collapsed.
In the third year of the Tiānqǐ reign, on the *yǐmǎo* day of the intercalary tenth month,
Chángshān in Rénshòu roared like thunder,
cracking seven *lǐ*,
three *chǐ* wide,
and immeasurably deep.
In the ninth year of the Chóngzhēn reign, in the twelfth month,
a loess mountain collapsed at Jīnjīlǐng in Zhènjiāng.
Eight years later,
there were two mountains in Qínzhōu,
very far apart,
with millions of households living between them.
One day there was an earthquake,
the two mountains converged,
and the residents were all trapped within.
Rain of hair, growth of hair on the ground
In the nineteenth year of the Hóngwǔ reign, on the *bǐngzǐ* day of the ninth month,
the sky rained flocculent material.
In the first year of the Xuāndé reign, on the *jiǎwǔ* day of the seventh month,
hair grew from the ground,
over a *chǐ* long.
In the eighth year of the Zhèngtǒng reign,
white hair grew from the ground in Zhèjiāng.
In the thirteenth year of the Chénghuà reign, in the fourth month,
the ground cracked in Gānsù,
and white hair grew.
In the fifteenth year, in the fifth month,
white hair grew from the ground in Chángzhōu.
In the seventeenth year, in the fourth month,
white hair grew from the ground in Nánjīng.
In the first year of the Hóngzhì reign, on the *bǐngyín* day of the fifth month,
Chángníng Xiàn in Lúzhōu had rain of hair.
In the twelfth year of the Zhèngdé reign, in the fourth month,
black and white hair grew from the ground in Jīnhuá,
over a *chǐ* long.

Collation Notes
Treatise Seven, Calendar One
The methods of later generations surpassed those of antiquity,
and the reason for their repeated improvements and increasing precision
was most evident in the calendar.
The Táng dynasty treatise stated that heaven is a moving object,
and over time, it will deviate,
making it necessary to repeatedly change the method to calculate it.
This statement seems plausible,
but it is not so.
The Yì (Book of Changes) says:
"The way of Heaven and Earth
is to observe constants."
For the movement of Heaven is exceedingly strong,
absolutely constant,
fundamentally without difference between ancient and modern times.
As for the anomalies of tropical year precession, waxing and waning, and variations in speed,
which were absent in ancient times but present now,
it is because their magnitudes are very small,
only becoming noticeable after accumulating over long periods.
The ancients did not perceive them,
but later generations recognized them,
and it is not that Heaven's movements have changed.
If Heaven truly moved for a long time and deviated,
then it would inevitably be chaotic, inconsistent, and without fixed principles;
how could it be revised and made more precise?
Observing what is recorded in the biographical treatises,
events like the year losing its proper sequence or the sun's degrees going astray
are not seen in recent times,
which also proves the point.
Indeed, Heaven's movements are manifold,
and human intelligence and power are limited.
Holding measuring instruments of chǐ and xún,
and looking up to measure the vast sky,
how can one fully comprehend everything without omission?
Only by combining the thoughts of ancient and modern people,
following and improving upon existing works,
can one hope to achieve conformity.
Therefore, it is impossible to create a method that is fixed and unchangeable.
From Huángdì to Qín,
the calendar was revised six times.
The Hàn dynasty revised it four times.
From Wèi to Suí,
it was revised fifteen times.
From Táng to the Five Dynasties,
fifteen revisions.
The Sòng dynasty seventeen revisions.
From Jīn to Yuán,
five revisions.
Only the Dàtǒng Calendar of the Míng dynasty,
which was essentially the Shòushí Calendar of the Yuán dynasty,
was used for over two hundred and seventy years
without any change to its system.
After Chénghuà,
eclipses often did not match predictions,
and proposals to revise the calendar were numerous.
Besides those who made baseless claims, such as Yú Zhèngjǐ and Lěng Shǒuzhōng,
figures like Huá Xiāng, Zhōu Lián, Lǐ Zhīzǎo, and Xíng Yúnlù had insightful observations.
The prince Zhèng Shìzǐ Zài'yù compiled Lǜlì Róngtōng (Comprehensive Treatise on Music and Calendar)
and presented the Shèngshòu Wànniánlì (Ten-Thousand Year Calendar for the Imperial Lifespan).
His theory was based on Hétáng, the imperial censor of Nándū,
who deeply grasped the essence of the Shòushí Calendar
and was able to compensate for its shortcomings.
However, the court officials were rigid in adhering to old traditions,
and those in power were hesitant to make changes,
so it was rejected and not implemented.
In the Chóngzhēn era,
a proposal to adopt new Western methods was discussed.
The grand secretaries Xú Guāngqǐ and the Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lǐ Tiānjīng were successively ordered to oversee the matter.
Over one hundred and thirty volumes of calendrical texts were completed,
many of which revealed what the ancients had not.
At that time, Wèi Wénkuí, a commoner, submitted a memorial to refute it,
and an imperial decree established two bureaus for verification and testing.
After years of calibration and measurement,
the new method was uniquely precise,
but it was also not promulgated.
From this perspective,
no calendar has ever been in use for a long time without deviation.
How could it not be revised from time to time
to conform to Heaven's movements?
Now, collecting various theories and discussions
that are beneficial to calendrical methods,
they are recorded at the beginning of this chapter.
As for the Dàtǒng Calendar, the origins of its legislative principles are described
to supplement the deficiencies of the Yuán dynasty's treatise.
The Huíhuí Calendar was always subordinate to the Qīntiān Jiān
and used in conjunction with the Dàtǒng Calendar,
so it is also appended here.
Evolution of the Calendar
In the eleventh month, Yǐwèi day, of the first year of Wú (1367), at the winter solstice,
Liú Jī, the Superintendent of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau, and his subordinate Gāo Yì, presented the Wùshēn Dàtǒng Calendar.
Tàizǔ (Emperor Hongwu) instructed, saying:
"In ancient times, calendars were promulgated in the last month of winter,
which was too late.
Now, at the winter solstice,
it is also not ideal.
It should be set to the first day of the tenth month
as a decree."
In the first year of Hóngwǔ (1368), the bureau was renamed Sītiān Jiān (Directorate of Astronomy),
and a Huíhuí Sītiān Jiān (Muslim Directorate of Astronomy) was also established.

An imperial edict summoned Zhāng Yòu, the Superintendent of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau of the Yuán dynasty, and Hēi de'ér, the Muslim Grand Eunuch for Astronomy, along with twelve others, a total of fourteen people.
Soon after, Zhèng Ālǐ and ten other officials from the Muslim Astronomical Bureau were summoned to the capital
to discuss calendrical methods.
In the third year (1370), the Directorate was renamed Qīntiān Jiān (Imperial Observatory),
and four sections were established: Astronomy (Tiānwén),
Clepsydra (Lòukè),
Dàtǒng Calendar (Dàtǒng Lì),
and Huíhuí Calendar (Huíhuí Lì).
The Director and Assistant Director oversaw them.

Annually, the Dàtǒng Mínlì (Popular Dàtǒng Calendar), Yùlǎn Yuèlìlì (Imperial Lunar Calendar), Qīzhèng Chándùlì (Calendar of the Seven Luminaries' Positions), Liùrén Dùnjiǎlì (Six-Rén Dùnjiǎ Calendar), Sījì Tiānxiàng Zhànyànlì (Seasonal Astronomical Phenomena Verification Calendar), and Yùlǎn Tiānxiànglù (Imperial Record of Astronomical Phenomena) were produced,
each submitted in due course.
The exact seconds and moments of solar and lunar eclipses, and the directions of rising and setting,
were reported in advance.
In the third month of the tenth year (1377),
the Emperor discussed with his officials the movements of Heaven and the Seven Luminaries.
They all responded with Cài's theory of leftward rotation.
The Emperor said:
"Since I raised an army,
I have observed the celestial phenomena.
Heaven rotates leftward,
and the Seven Luminaries rotate rightward.
The calendrical scholars' theory
is indeed correct and unchangeable.
Why do you all still adhere to Cài's theory?
Is this what is called 'investigating things to extend knowledge'?"
In the ninth month of the fifteenth year (1382),
an imperial edict commanded Lǐ Chōng and Wú Bózōng of the Hànlín Academy to translate the Huíhuí calendrical texts.
In the seventeenth year, in the intercalary tenth month,
the Erudite of Clepsydra, Yuán Tǒng, said:
"The calendar is named Dàtǒng,
but its accumulated calculations still follow the numbers of Shòushí,
which is not how one should show respect for the beginning and correctness.
Moreover, Shòushí takes the Xīnsì year of Zhìyuán as its epoch,
and by the Jiǎzǐ year of Hóngwǔ, it has accumulated 104 years.
As the years pass and the numbers accumulate,
it gradually deviates from the celestial degrees.
It is appropriate to revise it.
The movements of the Seven Luminaries are irregular,
their principles are profound.
I have heard there is a Guō Bóyù,
who is skilled in the principles of the Nine Calculations.
It is fitting to summon him to make the calculations
to establish the system for this dynasty."
The report was approved.
Yuán Tǒng was promoted to Superintendent (jiānlìng).
Yuán Tǒng then took the Shòushí Lì,
removed its theory of annual increase and decrease (suìshí xiāozhǎng zhī shuō),
analyzed its regulations,
and obtained four volumes.
He took the seventeenth Hóngwǔ year, the Jiǎzǐ year, as the epoch (lìyuán),
and named it Dàtǒng Lìfǎ Tōngguǐ.
In the twenty-second year, the titles of Superintendent (jiānlìng) and Assistant (chéng) were changed to Director (jiānzhèng) and Deputy (fù).
In the twenty-sixth year,
the Deputy Director (jiānfù) Lǐ Défāng said:
"The Director (jiānzhèng) Yuán Tǒng changed the epoch to the Hóngwǔ Jiǎzǐ year,
and did not use the method of increase and decrease.
By examining the Winter Solstice of the Tiānzhèng (Heavenly Right) in the fifteenth Wùyín year of Duke Xiàn of Lǔ,
compared to the Xīnsì epoch,
there is a strong deviation of four and a half days.
Now we should revert to using the Xīnsì epoch and the method of increase and decrease."
After the memorial was submitted,
Yuán Tǒng presented a rebuttal.
Tàizǔ said:
"Both theories are difficult to rely upon.
Only the one that accurately verifies the conjunction and movements of the Seven Luminaries is correct."
From then on, the epoch of the Dàtǒng Calendar was the Hóngwǔ Jiǎzǐ,
but the calculations still followed the Shòushí method.
In the thirty-first year, the Muslim Qīntiānjiān was abolished,
but its Muslim calendar section remained as before.
When Yǒnglè moved the capital to Shùntiān,
the day and night hours of Yìngtiān were still used.
It was not until the fourteenth year of Zhèngtǒng that the numbers for Shùntiān were adopted.
That winter,
Jǐngdì ascended the throne.
The astronomical student Mǎ Shì memorialized that
the day and night hours should not be changed.
The matter was sent to the court officials for deliberation.
The Director (jiānzhèng) Xǔ Dūn and others said:
"The former Director Péng Déqīng measured that the North Pole in Běijīng is 40 degrees above the horizon,
which is more than seven degrees higher than Nánjīng.
The Winter Solstice day is 38 kè,
and the Summer Solstice day is 62 kè.
This was approved and incorporated into the Dàtǒng Calendar,
to be a permanent rule.
Mǎ Shì's words are baseless and absurd,
and should not be heeded."
The Emperor said:
"The degrees of the sun's rising and setting
should be based on the center of the four directions.
The capital is now in the land of Yáo's Yōudū;
how can it be taken as the standard?
Hereafter, when creating calendars,
the old system of Hóngwǔ and Yǒnglè shall still be used."
On the Xīnmǎo day of the first month of Jǐngtài's first year,
there was a lunar eclipse at the third kè of Mǎozhèng.
The observatory officials mistakenly calculated it for the first kè of Chénchū,
thus failing to provide rescue.
The case was sent to the Ministry of Justice,
and they were sentenced to penal servitude.
An imperial edict pardoned them.
In the tenth year of Chénghuà,
due to the numerous incompetent observatory officials,
Tóng Xuān, who was the Education Commissioner of Yúnnán, was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (tàichángsì shǎoqīng),
in charge of the observatory affairs.
On the Wùxū day of the full moon in the eleventh month of the fifteenth year,
there was a lunar eclipse.
The observatory's calculation was again incorrect,
but the Emperor, considering celestial phenomena to be subtle,
did not blame them.
In the seventeenth year,
Yú Zhèngjǐ, an instructor from Zhēndìng, submitted a proposal for calendar reform.
An imperial edict instructed the Ministry of Rites and Tóng Xuān to examine it.
The Minister (shàngshū) Zhōu Hóngmó and others said:
"Yú Zhèngjǐ merely based his calculations of qi and suò on the Huángjí Jīngshì Shū and the astronomical and calendar records of past dynasties,
and also arbitrarily created an '87-year approximate method' (bāshíqī nián yuēfǎ),
in which large and small months alternate.
His actions are rash and arrogant;
he should be punished for his crime."
So Yú Zhèngjǐ was sent to the imperial prison.
In the nineteenth year,
the astronomical student Zhāng Shēng memorialized on calendar reform.
The Qīntiānjiān stated that the ancestral system could not be changed,
and Zhāng Shēng's proposal was thus shelved.
In the middle of Hóngzhì's reign,
lunar eclipses repeatedly did not match predictions,
and solar eclipses were also incorrect.
In the twelfth and thirteenth years of Zhèngdé,
consecutive predictions of the start and end of solar eclipses
were all incorrect.
Thereupon, the Erudite of Clepsydra, Zhū Yù, memorialized:
"Two hundred and thirty-seven years have passed since the Xīnsì year of Zhìyuán.
After such a long time, errors are inevitable.
If we do not make appropriate adjustments,
it will likely become more and more erroneous over time.
I beg for a high minister to be selected to oversee this matter,
and order the officials and students of this observatory to calculate half by the old method
and half by the new method,
and verify them against each other.
The Muslim section should verify using the Xīyù Jiǔzhí Lìfǎ.
Furthermore, officials should be dispatched to various provinces
to wait for the earth-gaugewith gǔiguī (gnomon) to measure the early or late arrival of the solar terms.
Through repeated comparisons and verifications,
eclipses can be corrected,
and the Seven Luminaries can be aligned."
The Ministry replied:
"Zhū Yù and the observatory officials may not all be proficient in calendar studies.
Now, for the lunar eclipse on the fifteenth of the tenth month,
the calculations made by the Palace Official Zhōu Lián and others
differ from the ancient method and Zhū Yù's memorial.
We request to verify this at the appointed time."
Later, Zhōu Lián and others said:
"The difference in the sun's path and annual regression is 1 fen 50 miao.
Now, in the Yǐhài year of Zhèngdé,
235 years have passed since the Xīnsì year of Zhìyuán.
The precession of the equinoxes on the equator
should regress by 3 degrees, 52 fen, and 50 miao.
Without correction, how can calculations be accurate?
After careful consideration and verification,
I have found that the Tiānzhèng Winter Solstice before the Bǐngzǐ year of Zhèngdé
should fall on the 27th day, 475 fen,
which is the first kè of Chǒuchū on the Xīnmǎo day.
The sun's path on the equator is 6 degrees, 47 fen, 50 miao in the constellation Jīsù,
and on the ecliptic it is 5 degrees, 96 fen, 43 miao in the constellation Jīsù, to be taken as the epoch.
The transfer of qi and intercalary changes follow the four responses,
and the entire celestial sphere's ecliptic and equator,
as well as all various tables (lìchéng),
shall all be subject to precession,
and be corrected as appropriate.
We request an imperial edict for the Ministers of Rites and the Director (jiānzhèng) to oversee this matter."
The Ministry memorialized:
"The ancient method should not be lightly changed.
We request to retain the old method.
Separately select scholars proficient in calendar studies
to verify with Zhōu Lián and others using the new method,
and then make another request."
This was followed.
In the fifteenth year,
Zhèng Shànfū, an Assistant Director (yuánwàiláng) of the Ministry of Rites, said:
"Of solar and lunar eclipses,
solar eclipses are the most difficult to predict.
Lunar eclipse magnitudes
only depend on the distance from the node,
with no other seasonal additions or subtractions.
Moreover, the moon is small and the shadow cone is large,
so what is seen in all eight directions is the same.
However, if the sun is obscured by the moon,
then the sun is large and the moon is small,
the sun is above and the moon is below,
the sun is distant and the moon is near.
The sun's movement varies with the four seasons,
and the moon's movement has nine orbital paths.
Therefore, the observation differs between north and south,
and the times also vary.
It is essential to set up gnomons based on the location
and seek agreement according to the time.
For example, the solar eclipse on the Xīnmǎo day of the eighth month of Zhèngdé's ninth year,
calendar officials reported an eclipse of 8 fen 67 miao,
yet in the regions of Mǐn and Guǎng,
it reached a total eclipse.
How could the times, fen, and miao
be the same?
Now, it is appropriate to reset the epoch based on eclipses,
and for the times, fen, and miao,
the fractional parts must be analyzed in detail.
Otherwise,
as years and months accumulate,
the movements of the luminaries (zhān lí tiǎo nüè)
will again be out of alignment."
No reply was given.

In the sixteenth year, because Lè Hé, a Supervising Secretary (jǐshìzhōng) of the Ministry of Revenue in Nánjīng, and Huá Xiāng, a Department Director (zhǔshì) of the Ministry of Works, were both proficient in calendar studies,
they were both promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (guānglù shǎoqīng),
and put in charge of observatory affairs.
In the second year of Jiājìng
Xiāng Yán
stated: "From ancient times to the present, there have been three schools excellent at managing calendars.
The Tài Chū (calendar) of the Hàn dynasty used pitch-pipes,
the Dà Yǎn (calendar) of the Táng dynasty used yarrow stalks,
and the Shòu Shí (calendar) of the Yuán dynasty used sundial shadows, all of which are close to the truth.
To correct the calendar without ascending a platform to measure shadows
is all empty talk and guesswork.
I request permission to temporarily cease attending court audiences,
to supervise the eunuchs Zhōu Lián and others,
and before the winter solstice, to proceed to the Guānxiàngtái (Observatory)
to make day and night calculations and measurements.
A daily log and monthly record shall be kept,
until the winter solstice of next year,

to verify the degrees of the twenty-four solar terms, solstices, equinoxes, new and full moons, the sun's path, the moon's position, the yellow and red equatorial paths, stars at dusk and dawn, and the seven planets and four nodes.
Comparing these with the measurements taken in the Xīnsì year of the Yuán dynasty,
we will record how they differ or agree,
and report the discrepancies.
Furthermore, an imperial edict should be issued to the Ministry of Rites to invite scholars proficient in mathematical astronomy to the capital,
to meticulously determine the precession of the equinoxes,
thereby establishing a system for our dynasty."
The matter was passed to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation,
but Gòu said the calendar should not be changed,
differing considerably from Xiāng Yán.
The Ministry of Rites stated:
"Xiāng Yán's desire to personally conduct observations
is not without reason.
We request that both officials express their views fully,
exploring the extremes of their agreements and differences,
to align with the ways of Heaven."
This was approved.
In the seventh year
the Qīn Tiān Jiān (Imperial Observatory) reported:
"For the new moon of the intercalary tenth month,
the Huíhuí Lì (Islamic Calendar) predicts a solar eclipse of two fen and forty-seven miao (minutes),
while the Dàtǒng Lì (Great Unification Calendar) predicts no eclipse."
Later, there was no eclipse.
On the Guǐsì new moon of the third month of the nineteenth year
the observatory officials said there would be an eclipse,
but later there was none.
The Emperor was pleased,
believing it to be Heaven's favor,
but it was actually due to errors in calculation.
In the third year of Lóngqìng
Zhōu Xiàng, the Assistant Administrator of Shùntiān Prefecture and concurrently in charge of the observatory, published the Dàtǒng Lì Fǎ (Great Unification Calendar Method),
which originally compared the similarities and differences of ancient and modern calendars.
On the Guǐyǒu new moon of the eleventh month of the twelfth year of Wànlì
the Dàtǒng Lì predicted a solar eclipse of ninety-two miao (seconds),
while the Huíhuí Lì predicted no eclipse.
Later, the Huíhuí Lì proved correct.
Hóu Xiānchūn, a Supervising Censor of the Ministry of Rites, then stated:
"Recently, lunar eclipses occurred in the constellation Yǒu but were predicted for Xū;
an eclipse was about to conclude but was predicted to be nine fen (tenths) short of completion,
the discrepancies are severe.
The Huíhuí Lì's calculations for solar and lunar eclipses
and the transit of the five planets
are the most precise.
Why not incorporate them into the Dàtǒng Lì
for verification?"
An imperial edict approved this.
On the night of the Jiǎxū day in the fifth month of the twentieth year
and the observatory officials' calculation was off by one day.
In the twenty-third year
Zhèng Shìzǐ Zài Yù presented two books: Shèng Shòu Wàn Nián Lì (Calendar of Myriad Years for His Majesty's Longevity) and Lǜ Lì Róng Tōng (Harmonious Integration of Pitch-Pipes and Calendar).
His memorial briefly stated:
"When Gāo Huángdì (Emperor Tàizǔ) brought about the revolution,
the Yuán calendar was not yet old,
and the solar terms and new moons had not yet deviated,
so no changes were made,
only discussion and refinement.
After many years,
the solar terms and new moons gradually deviated.
The Hòu Hàn Zhì (History of the Later Hàn Dynasty) states that 'every three hundred years, the Dòu Lì (Dipper Calendar) changes its constitution.'
