Also, to its southeast is the Bǎiquán River,
whose downstream becomes the Fēng River,
also named Wō River,
and also named Yuānyāng River.
To its west is the Xīwángshè Patrol and Inspection Office.
Shāhé (south of the prefecture).
In the 4th year of Hóngzhì, due to sand blockage, the county seat was moved to Xīshān Xiǎotún.
In the 18th year and 6th month, it was restored to its old seat.
To its southwest is Mount Qìngkǒu,
which produces iron.
To its south is the Shā River,
also named Yú River.
Nánhé (east of the prefecture,
slightly south).
To its south is the Zhāng River,
which merges with the Fēng River west of the county.
Also, to its northwest is the Zhī River,
which is a subterranean flow emerging from the side.
Rèn (northeast of the prefecture).
To its northeast is the Zhī River.
To its east is the Fēng River.
Nèiqiū (north of the prefecture).
To its southeast is the Zhī River.
Tángshān (northeast of the prefecture).
To its northwest is Mount Yáo.
To its west is the Zhī River.
Píngqīng (east of the prefecture,
slightly south).
To its southwest is the Zhāng River,
to its west is the Shā River,
and also the Míng River.
To its east is the Fǔyáng River.
In the 30th year of Wànlì,
the Zhāng River, accompanied by the Fǔyáng River, flowed north,
meeting the Shā, Míng, and other rivers,
and the old course of the Zhāng River became even more disordered.
Jùlù (northeast of the prefecture).
The Zhāng River was formerly east of the county,
with two rivers, large and small,
also called the new and old rivers.
Later, they shifted north,
no longer reaching the county's boundary,
and the two rivers became flat land.
To its north is the Jùlù Marsh,
which is the Dàlù Marsh of Lóngpíng County.
There were formerly salt springs by the marsh.
Guǎngzōng (east of the prefecture,
slightly north).
In the 10th year and 6th month of Hóngwǔ, it was merged into Píngxiāng and Jùlù counties.
In the 13th year and 11th month, it was re-established.
The Zhāng River was formerly to its west.
Also, to its east is the Kūjiàng River.
) Guǎngpíng Prefecture (formerly Yuán Guǎngpíng Circuit,
directly administered by the Zhōngshū Province).
In the 1st year of Hóngwǔ, it became a prefecture.
In the 10th month, it belonged to the Hénán Sub-province.
In the 2nd year and 3rd month, it came under this jurisdiction.
It governs nine counties.
It is 1,000 *lǐ* northeast of the Capital.
In the 4th year of Hóngzhì, there were 27,764 households
and 212,846 people.
In the 6th year of Wànlì,
there were 31,420 households
and 264,898 people.
Yǒngnián (the prefectural seat).
To its north is the Shā River.
Also, there is the Míng River,
flowing in from Wǔ'ān County in Hénán.
To its southwest is also the Fǔ River,
flowing in from Línzhāng County in Hénán,
also called the Fǔyáng River.
To its west is the Línmíngzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office.
To its southwest is also Huánglóngzhèn.
Qǔzhōu (northeast of the prefecture).
To its southwest is the Zhāng River.
To its east is the Fǔyáng River.
Féixiāng (southeast of the prefecture).
The Zhāng River is to its northwest.
Jīzé (northeast of the prefecture).
The Zhāng River is to its east.
Also, to its west is the Míng River,
and also the Shā River comes from the south to merge with it.
Guǎngpíng (southeast of the prefecture).
To its north is the Zhāng River.
Chéng'ān (south of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Cízhōu.
It was abolished in the early Hóngwǔ reign.
In the sixth month of the fourth year, it was re-established,
and came to belong to the prefecture.
To the southwest is the Huánshǔi River,
which flows in from Línzhāng Xiàn, Hénán,
and its lower course merges with the Wèihé River.
Further south is the Zhāngshuǐ River,
which also flows in from Línzhāng Xiàn, Hénán.)
Wēi (northeast of the prefecture.
Yuán Wēizhōu.
During the Zhìzhèng period,
Míngshuǐ Xiàn, the seat of the zhōu, was abolished and merged into the zhōu.
In the fourth month of the second year of Hóngwǔ, it was demoted to a xiàn.
The Zhāngshuǐ River was formerly to the south,
and the Míngshuǐ River flows in from the west.)
Hándān (southwest of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Cízhōu.
In the first year of Hóngwǔ, it came to belong to the prefecture.
To the northwest is the Mínghé River.
To the east is the Xiànyánghé River.)
Qīnghé (northeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Dàmíng Lù.
In the ninth month of the sixth year of Hóngwǔ, it came to belong to the prefecture.
To the east is the Wèihé River.)
Dàmíng Fǔ (Yuán Dàmíng Lù,
directly administered by the Zhōngshū Shěng.)
In the first year of Hóngwǔ, it became a fǔ.
In the tenth month, it belonged to the Hénán Fēnshěng.
In the third month of the second year, it came to belong to the current administration.
It administered one zhōu
and ten xiàn.
It is one thousand one hundred sixty lǐ northeast of the capital.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì, the registered households numbered sixty-six thousand two hundred seven,
and the population was five hundred seventy-four thousand nine hundred seventy-two.
In the sixth year of Wànlì,
there were seventy-one thousand one hundred eighty households,
and a population of six hundred ninety-two thousand fifty-eight.
Yuánchéng (dependent seat.
The old city was to the east.
In the thirty-first year of Hóngwǔ, it was damaged by the Wèihé River,
and moved here.
To the east is Shālù Shān.
To the west is the Zhānghé River.
To the north is the Wèihé River,
which is also the Yǒngjì Qú,
flowing in from Jíxiàn, Hénán,
and its lower course merges with the Zhānghé River.
To the northeast is the Xiǎotán Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Dàmíng (south of the prefecture,
slightly east.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was the seat of Dàmíng Fǔ together with Yuánchéng Xiàn.
In the fifth month of the tenth year of Hóngwǔ, it was abolished and merged into Wèi Xiàn.
In the second month of the fifteenth year, it was re-established.
In the ninth year of Yǒnglè, it was moved to its current seat.
To the north is Qiè Shān,
and to the southeast is the Wèihé River.)
Wèi (west of the prefecture,
slightly north.
The old seat was west of the xiàn.
In the third year of Hóngwǔ, it was moved here.
To the south is the Wèihé River,
and also the old and new Zhānghé Rivers,
whose lower courses all merge with the Wèihé River.)
Nánlè (east of the prefecture.
To the south is the Fánshuǐ River,
which flows north into the Wèihé River.)
Qīngfēng (southeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Kāizhōu.
In the third month of the seventh year of Hóngwǔ, it was changed to belong to the prefecture.
To the southwest is the Chánshuǐ River,
which flows underground to the southwest of the old Fánshuǐ City,
and is called the Fánshuǐ River.)
Nèihuáng (southwest of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Huázhōu.
In the third month of the seventh year of Hóngwǔ, it was changed to belong to the prefecture.
To the north is the Wèihé River.
To the east is the Fánshuǐ River.
To the west is the Huánshuǐ River.
To the northwest is Huílóng Zhèn,
which has the Huílóng Miào Xúnjiǎnsī.
In the thirty-sixth year of Jiājìng,
the Zhānghé River burst its banks here,
flowing into the Wèi River.)
Jùn (southwest of the prefecture.
The seat of Yuán Jùnzhōu was west of Fúqiū Shān.
In the fourth month of the second year of Hóngwǔ, it was demoted to a xiàn,
and its seat was moved to Píngpō, northeast of the mountain.
In the twenty-ninth year of Jiājìng, the city was again moved to the mountain peak,
which is its current seat.
To the east is Dàpēi Shān,
also known as Líyáng Shān,
and also Qīngchán Shān.
To the west is the Wèihé River.
To the north is the Qíshuǐ River,
flowing in from Qíxiàn, Hénán,
passing south of the xiàn,
and flowing east into the Wèi River,
called the Líshuǐ River,
and also Jùnshuǐ River.
Further west is Chángfēng Bó.
To the southwest is Xīnzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Huá (southwest of the prefecture.
Yuán Huázhōu.
In the fourth month of the second year of Hóngwǔ, Bǎimǎ Xiàn, the seat of the zhōu, was abolished and merged into it.
In the third month of the seventh year, it was demoted to a xiàn.
To the northwest is the Wèihé River.
To the southeast is Lǎo'àn Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Kāizhōu In the fourth month of the second year of Hóngwǔ, Púyáng Xiàn, the seat of the zhōu, was abolished and merged into it.
(The old course of the Dàhé River was south of the city.
In the thirteenth year of Zhèngtǒng,
the river burst its banks and flowed into it.
In the fifth year of Jǐngtài, it was blocked.)
It is one hundred sixty lǐ
north of the prefecture,
and administers two xiàn.
Chángyuán (south of the zhōu.
The old seat was northeast of the xiàn.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ, due to riverine disasters, it was moved to the ancient Púchéng.
To the south is the old course of the Huánghé River.
To the southeast is Zhūjiākǒu.
In the thirteenth year of Zhèngtǒng,
the river burst its banks here.
Further south is Dàshèkǒu.
In the fifteenth year of Wànlì,
the river again burst its banks here.
Further southeast is Dàgāng Xúnjiǎnsī,
originally seated in Yǒngfēng Lǐ,
later moved to Zhúlín,
and then moved to Dàgāng.)
Dōngmíng (north of the zhōu.
In the fifth month of the tenth year of Hóngwǔ, it was abolished and merged into the zhōu and Chángyuán Xiàn.
In the ninth month of the third year of Hóngzhì, it was re-established,
and belonged to the prefecture.
During the Wànlì reign,
it again belonged to the zhōu.
Its old seat was south of the present xiàn.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was moved west of the present xiàn.
In the third year of Hóngzhì, it was first moved to its present seat.
To the south is the Huánghé River,
and it has the Dùshèngjí Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Yǒngpíng Fǔ (Yuán Yǒngpíng Lù,
directly administered by the Zhōngshū Shěng.)
In the second year of Hóngwǔ, it was renamed Píngluán Fǔ.
In the third month of the fourth year, it became Yǒngpíng Fǔ.
It administered one zhōu
and five xiàn.
It is five hundred fifty lǐ west of the capital.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì, the registered households numbered twenty-three thousand five hundred thirty-nine,
and the population was two hundred twenty-eight thousand nine hundred forty-four.
In the sixth year of Wànlì,
there were twenty-five thousand ninety-four households,
and a population of two hundred fifty-five thousand six hundred forty-six.
Lúlóng (dependent seat.
To the southeast is Yáng Shān.
To the west is the Luánhé River,
flowing from Kāipíng through the xiàn territory,
and the Qīhé River flows in from the north.
To the east is the Féirúhé River,
passing west of the city into the Qīhé River.
To the north is Táolínkǒu Guān.)
Qiān'ān (northwest of the prefecture.
To the north is Dū Shān.
To the east is the Luánhé River.
Further north are the Liújiākǒu, Língkǒu, Qīngshānkǒu, and other passes.)
Fǔníng (east of the prefecture,
slightly south.
The old seat was west of the Yánghé River,
moved in the twelfth month of the sixth year of Hóngwǔ.
In the thirteenth year, it was again moved to the east of Tù'ěr Shān.
To the southeast, it borders the sea.
Further east is the Yúhé River,
and also the Yánghé River,
also named Yánghé,
both flowing in from beyond the Great Wall,
and both flowing southeast into the sea.
To the east is Shānhǎiguān.
In the ninth month of the fourteenth year of Hóngwǔ, Shānhǎi Wèi was established here.
To the north is Fǔníng Wèi,
established in the second month of the first year of Yǒnglè.
There are also Dǒngjiākǒu, Yìyuànkǒu, and other passes.
To the east is Yīpiànshíkǒu,
also named Jiǔménshuǐkǒu.)
Chānglí (To the southeast of the prefecture.
To the northwest is Jiéshí Shān.
To the southeast is the Míng Hǎi,
also called Qīlǐ Hǎi.
There is the Hēiyáng Hé,
which is the sea route from Tiānjīn to the county.
There is also Pú Pō,
which formerly produced salt,
and where the Huìmín Yánchǎng was established.
To the north are the passes of Jièlǐng Kǒu, Jiànhàn Lǐng, and others.
) Luánzhōu. In the ninth month of the second year of Hóngwǔ, Yìfēng Xiàn, the seat of the prefecture, was merged into it.
(It borders the sea to the south.
To the east is the Luán Hé.
To the south is the Kāipíng Zhōngtún Wèi,
which was moved here in the second month of the first year of Yǒnglè from Shā
yù.
) It is forty lǐ northeast of the prefecture.
It administers one county.
Lètíng (Southeast of the zhou.
It borders the sea to the south.
To the west is the Luán Hé,
which, after passing through Yuèpó Gǎng north of the county, divides into two:
the eastern one is called Húlú Hé,
and the western one is called Dìngliú Hé,
each flowing into the sea.
In the middle of Jǐngtài,
the Húlú Hé became blocked,
and only the Dìngliú Hé flowed into the sea on its own;
its waters were clear and blue,
and it was also called Lǜyáng Gōu.
To its southwest is the Xīnqiáo Hǎikǒu Xúnjiǎnsī.
In the forty-third year of Wànlì, it was moved to Zhēnzǐ Zhèn, west of Luánzhōu.
) Yánqìng Zhōu (Formerly Lóngqìng Zhōu in the Yuán dynasty,
it belonged to Dàdū Lù.
) In the early Hóngwǔ period,
it belonged to Yǒngpíng Fǔ.
In the third month of the third year, it belonged to Běipíng Fǔ,
but was soon abolished.
In the third month of the twelfth year of Yǒnglè, Lóngqìng Zhōu was established,
belonging to Běijīng Xíngbù.
In the eleventh month of the eighteenth year, it was directly administered by Jīngshī.
In the first year of Lóngqìng, it was renamed Yánqìng Zhōu.
(To the west is Bǎnquán Shān.
To the south is Bādálǐng.
To the northeast is Guī Chuān,
commonly known as Qīngshuǐ Hé,
whose lower reaches flow into the Sānggān Hé.
To the southwest is Gū Hé.
To the southeast is Chàdào Kǒu,
which connects with Jūyōng Guān.
At the pass is the Jūyōngguān Shǒuyù Qiānhù Suǒ,
established in the third year of Hóngwǔ.
In the fourth year of Jiànwén, the King of Yān changed it to Lóngqìng Wèi,
and in the first year of Lóngqìng, it was called Yánqìng Wèi.
To the southeast is also Liǔgōu Yíng,
where in the early Lóngqìng period,
a city was built,
serving as a defensive position.
) It administers one county.
It is one hundred and eighty lǐ southeast of Jīngshī.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì, there were one thousand seven hundred eighty-seven households
and two thousand five hundred forty-four people.
In the sixth year of Wànlì,
there were two thousand seven hundred fifty-five households
and nineteen thousand two hundred sixty-seven people.
Yǒngníng (Originally Yǒngníng Wèi,
established in the ninth month of the twelfth year of Hóngwǔ.
In the third month of the twelfth year of Yǒnglè, a county was established in the wèi city.
Guī Chuān is to the west.
To the east is Sìhǎiyě Bǎo,
established in the eighth year of Tiānshùn.
To the west
north is Jìnghú Bǎo,
to the southeast is Hēihànlǐng Bǎo,
to the north is Zhōusìgōu Bǎo,
all established in the Jiājìng period.
There is also Liúbīnbǎo,
established in the thirty-second year of Wànlì.
) Bǎo'ān Zhōu (In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Shùnníng Fǔ of Shàngdū Lù.
) In the early Hóngwǔ period,
it was abolished.
In the intercalary ninth month of the second year of Yǒnglè, Bǎo'ān Wèi was established.
In the first month of the thirteenth year, the zhōu was re-established in the wèi city,
belonging to Běijīng Xíngbù.
In the eleventh month of the eighteenth year, it was directly administered by Jīngshī.
(The old zhōu city was at the foot of the southwestern mountain,
and in the second year of Jǐngtài, it was moved to Léijiā Zhàn,
To the southwest is Zhuōlù Shān,
from which Zhuō Shuǐ flows.
To the northwest is Mójī Shān,
also called Jīmíng Shān,
and there is also Yàorlíng.
The Sānggān Hé is to the southwest,
flowing in from Wèizhōu in Shānxī,
and Guī Chuān comes in from the east,
called Héhé Kǒu.
To the west is Níng Chuān,
which also flows into the Sānggān.
To the east are Dōngbālǐ Bǎo, Liángtiántún Bǎo, and Mágǔkǒu Bǎo,
all established in the twenty-fifth year of Hóngwǔ.
To the south is Měiyù Shǒuyù Qiānhù Suǒ,
originally at Měiyù Lǐng west of the zhōu,
established in the twelfth year of Yǒnglè.
In the second month of the sixteenth year, it was moved to Dǒngjiā Zhuāng.
In the second year of Jǐngtài, it was moved here again,
bordering Wèizhōu in Shānxī.
) It is three hundred lǐ southeast of Jīngshī.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì, there were four hundred forty-five households
and one thousand five hundred sixty people.
In the sixth year of Wànlì,
there were seven hundred seventy-two households
and six thousand four hundred forty-five people.
The Wànquán (萬全) Regional Military Commission (Duōzhǐshǐ Sī 都指揮使司) (formerly Shùnníng Fǔ 順寧府 during the Yuán (元) dynasty,
which belonged to the Shàngdū Lù 上都路).
In the third month of the fourth year of Hóngwǔ (洪武) (1371),
the prefecture was abolished.
In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xuāndé (宣德) (1430), the Commission was established here.
It governed fifteen Guards (Wèi 衞),
(Wèizhōu (蔚州), Yánqìng Zuǒ (延慶左), Yǒngníng (永寧), and Bǎo'ān (保安) four Guards were all established in their respective prefectures and counties),
〔一五〕 three Defensive Chiliarchy Commands (Shǒuyù Qiānhù Suǒ 守禦千戶所),
(Guǎngchāng (廣昌) and Měiyù (美峪) two Commands were also established in their respective places),
five Forts (Bǎo 堡).
It was three hundred and fifty *lǐ* (里) southeast of the capital.
Xuānfǔ Zuǒ Wèi (宣府左衞) (formerly Xuāndé Xiàn (宣德縣) during the Yuán (元) dynasty,
which was the seat of Shùnníng Fǔ (順寧府)).
In the fourth year of Hóngwǔ (洪武) (1371),
the county was abolished.
In the second month of the twenty-sixth year (1393), the Guard was established,
subordinate to the Shānxī Xíng Dū Sī (山西行都司).
In the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year (1395), it was renamed Xuānfǔ Hù Wèi (宣府護衞),
subordinate to Gǔ Wáng Fǔ (谷王府).
In the eleventh month of the thirty-fifth year (1402), the Xuānfǔ Hù Wèi was abolished,
then re-established,
and its seat moved to Báodìng (保定).
In the second month of the first year of Yǒnglè (永樂) (1403), it was directly subordinate to the Hòujūn Dūdū Fǔ (後軍都督府).
In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xuāndé (宣德) (1430), it returned to its former seat,
and its affiliation was changed.
(The Gǔ Wáng Fǔ (谷王府) was established in the fourth month of the twenty-fourth year of Hóngwǔ (洪武) (1391),
and in the first year of Yǒnglè (永樂) (1403) it moved to Chángshā (長沙) in Húguǎng (湖廣).
To the west is the Luán Hé (灤河),
which originates from Tànshān (炭山)
and flows downstream into the Kàipíng (開平) border.
To the south is the Sānggān Hé (桑乾河),
into which the Yáng Hé (洋河) flows from the east.
There is also the Shùnshèng Chuān (順聖川),
extending over two hundred *lǐ*,
whose downstream also merges with the Sānggān Hé.
To the north are two cities, east and west;
the eastern city was Shùnshèng Xiàn (順聖縣),
which belonged to Shùnníng Fǔ (順寧府) during the Yuán (元) dynasty,
and the western city was Hóngzhōu (弘州),
which belonged to Dàtóng Lù (大同路) during the Yuán (元) dynasty;
both were abolished during the Hóngwǔ (洪wu) period.
In the fourth year of Tiānshùn (天順) (1460), the two cities were repaired and built.
Also to the northeast are the Dàbáiyáng (大白陽), Xiǎobáiyáng (小白陽), and Lóngmén Guān (龍門關) forts, among others.
To the southeast is the Jīmíngyì (雞鳴驛) fort.
To the north is the Gěyù (葛峪) fort.
To the northwest are the Chángyùkǒu (長峪口), Qīngbiānkǒu (青邊口), Yángfáng (羊房) forts, among others.)
Xuānfǔ Yòu Wèi (宣府右衞). Established in the second month of the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ (洪武) (1393),
in the same city as the Left Guard,
subordinate to the Shānxī Xíng Dū Sī (山西行都司).
In the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year (1395), it was renamed Xuānfǔ Hù Wèi (宣府護衞),
subordinate to Gǔ Wáng Fǔ (谷王府).
In the eleventh month of the thirty-fifth year (1402), the Xuānfǔ Hù Wèi was abolished,
then re-established,
and its seat moved to Dìngzhōu (定州).
In the second month of the first year of Yǒnglè (永樂) (1403), it was directly subordinate to the Hòujūn Dūdū Fǔ (後軍都督府).
In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xuāndé (宣德) (1430), it returned to its former seat,
and its affiliation was changed.
Xuānfǔ Qián Wèi (宣府前衞). Established in the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ (洪武) (1393),
with its seat in Xuānfǔ Chéng (宣府城),
subordinate to the Shānxī Xíng Dū Sī (山西行都司).
In the second month of the first year of Yǒnglè (永樂) (1403), it was directly
subordinate to the Hòujūn Dūdū Fǔ (後軍都督府).
In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xuāndé (宣德) (1430), its affiliation was changed.
Wànquán Zuǒ Wèi (萬全左衞) (formerly Xuānpíng Xiàn (宣平縣) during the Yuán (元) dynasty,
which belonged to Shùnníng Fǔ (順寧府)).
In the fourth year of Hóngwǔ (洪武) (1371),
the county was abolished.
In the second month of the twenty-sixth year (1393), the Guard was established,

and then east to merge with Luán Hé.
) It is _ lǐ from Běipíng Dū Sī.
Yíxīng Shǒuyù Qiānhù Suǒ (Originally Yíxīng Xiàn,
subordinate to Xīngzhōu.
In the 1st year of Zhìhé, 8th month, it was promoted to Yíxīng Zhōu.
) In the 2nd year of Hongwǔ, a wèi was also established,
subordinate to Yǒngpíng Fǔ.
In the 3rd year, 3rd month, it was subordinate to Běipíng Fǔ.
In the 6th month, the wèi was changed to a shǒuyù qiānhù suǒ.
In the 5th year, 7th month,
the zhōu was abolished,
and the suǒ remained.
In the 1st year of Yonglè,
the suǒ was abolished.
It is _ lǐ from Běipíng Dū Sī.
Nánjīng. The region of Yǔgòng's Yáng, Xú, and Yù three zhōus.
In the Yuán dynasty, the land north of the Jiāng was subordinated to the Hénán Jiāngběi děngchù Xíng Zhōngshūshěng.
Furthermore, the Huáidōng Dào Xuānwèishǐ Sī (governing Yángzhōu Lù) was established and belonged to it.
The land south of the Jiāng belonged to the Jiāngzhè děngchù Xíng Zhōngshūshěng.
In the bǐngshēn year of Míng Tàizǔ's reign, in the seventh month, the Jiāngnán Xíng Zhōngshūshěng was established.
(Governing Yìngtiān Fǔ.)
In the eighth month of Hóngwǔ's first year, Nánjīng was established.
The Xíng Zhōngshūshěng was abolished.
Yìngtiān Fǔ and other fǔs were directly subordinate to the Zhōngshūshěng.
The wèi and suǒ were directly subordinate to the Dà Dūdū Fǔ.
In the first month of the eleventh year, Nánjīng was renamed Jīngshī.
On the jǐhài day of the first month of the thirteenth year, the Zhōngshūshěng was abolished.
Its subordinate entities were directly administered by the Liù Bù.
On the guǐmǎo day, the Dà Dūdū Fǔ was renamed Wǔjūn Dūdū Fǔ.
Its subordinate entities were directly administered by the Zhōngjūn Dūdū Fǔ.
In the first month of Yǒnglè's first year, it was again called Nánjīng.
It administered fourteen fǔs,
four directly subordinate zhōus,
seventeen subordinate zhōus,
and ninety-seven xiàns.
(Comprising over thirteen thousand seven hundred forty lǐ.)
North to Fēng and Pèi,
(bordering Shāndōng and Hénán.)
West to Yīngshān,
(bordering Hénán and Húguǎng.)
South to Wùyuán,
(bordering Zhèjiāng and Jiāngxī.)
East to the sea.
Three thousand four hundred forty-five lǐ from Běijīng.
Yìngtiān Fǔ (formerly Jíqìng Lù in the Yuán dynasty,
belonging to the Jiāngzhè Xíngshěng.)
In the bǐngshēn year of Tàizǔ's reign, in the third month, it was called Yìngtiān Fǔ.
In the eighth month of Hóngwǔ's first year, the capital was established,
and it was called Nánjīng.
In the eleventh year, it was called Jīngshī.
In Yǒnglè's first year, it was again called Nánjīng.
(In the ninth month of Hóngwǔ's second year, construction of the new city began;
it was completed in the eighth month of the sixth year.
Inside was the Gōngchéng,
also called Zǐjìnchéng,
with six gates: the main south gate was called Wǔmén,
the left was called Zuǒyè,
the right was called Yòuyè,
the east was called Dōng'ān,
the west was called Xī'ān,
the north was called Běi'ān.
Outside the Gōngchéng were six gates: the main south gate was called Hóngwǔ,
the east was called Cháng'ānzuǒ,
the west was called Cháng'ānyòu,
to the north of the east was called Dōnghuá,
to the north of the west was called Xīhuá,
the north was called Xuánwǔ.
Outside the Huángchéng was the Jīngchéng,
ninety-six lǐ in circumference,
with thirteen gates: the south was called Zhèngyáng,
to the west of the south was called Tōngjì,
further west was called Jùbǎo,
southwest was called Sānshān,
called Shíchéng,
the north was called Tàipíng,
to the west of the north was called Shéncè,
called Jīnchuān,
called Zhōngfù,
the east was called Cháoyáng,
the west was called Qīngliáng,
to the north of the west was called Dìnghuái,
called Yífèng.
Later, the two gates Zhōngfù and Yífèng were blocked,
leaving eleven gates.
Its outer wall,
built in the fourth month of Hóngwǔ's twenty-third year,
was one hundred eighty lǐ in circumference,
with sixteen gates: the east were Yáofāng, Xiānhè, Qílín, Cāngbō, Gāojiáo, Shuāngqiáo;
the south were Shàngfāng, Jiágāng, Fèngái, Dàxùnxiàng, Dà'āndé, Xiǎo'āndé;
the west was Jiāngdōng;
the north were Fóníng, Shàngyuán, Guānyīn.)
It administered eight xiàns.
In Hóngwǔ's twenty-sixth year, there were 163,915 households
and 1,193,620 people.
In Hóngzhì's fourth year,
there were 144,368 households
and 711,003 people.
In Wànlì's sixth year,
there were 143,597 households
and 790,513 people.
Shàngyuán (an yǐ xiàn.
In the bǐngshēn year of Tàizǔ's reign, the xiàn government was moved to Chúnhuà Zhèn,
and the following year it returned to its old seat.
To the northeast is Zhōngshān.
To the south of the mountain is Xiàolíng Wèi,
established in Hóngwǔ's thirty-first year.
To the north is Fùzhōushān.
To the northwest are Jīmíngshān and Mùfǔshān.
Also, to the northeast is Shèshān.
To the southeast is Fāngshān.
To the north it borders the Dà Jiāng.
To the southeast is Qínhuái Shuǐ,
which flows north into the city,
then flows west out
and enters the Dà Jiāng.
Also, to the north is Xuánwǔ Hú.
To the east is Qīngxī.
There is also Chúnhuà Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Jiāngníng (an yǐ xiàn.
To the south are Jùbǎoshān and Niúshǒushān.
To the southwest are Sānshān, Lièshān, and Címǔshān.
To the west it borders the Dà Jiāng.
To the northeast is Jìng'ān Hé.
To the southwest are Dàshèng Guān and Jiāngníng Zhèn.
To the southeast is Líng Guān.
To the west are four Jiāngdōng Xúnjiǎnsīs.
To the north is Lóngjiāng Guān,
where a hùfēnsī was established.)
Jùróng (east of the fǔ.
To the south is Máoshān.
To the north is Huàshān,
where the Qínhuái Shuǐ originates.
To the north it borders the Dà Jiāng.
To the northwest is Lóngtán Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Lìyáng (southeast of the fǔ.
In the Yuán dynasty it was Lìyáng Zhōu.
In Hóngwǔ's second year, it was demoted to a xiàn.
To the southeast are Tiěshān and Tóngshān.
To the southwest is Tiěyěshān.
To the north is Chángdàng Hú,
also named Táohú,
bordering Yíxīng and Jīntán two xiàns.
To the northwest is Lìshuǐ,
also named Lài Shuǐ,
which receives water from Dānyáng Hú,
flows east as Yíxīng Xiàn Jīngxī,
enters Tàihú,
formerly named Yǒngyáng Jiāng,
also called Zhōng Jiāng.
To the northwest is Shàngxīng Bù Xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.)
Lìshuǐ (east of the fǔ.
In the Yuán dynasty it was Lìshuǐ Zhōu.
In Hóngwǔ's second year, it was demoted to a xiàn.
To the southeast is Dōnglúshān,
where another source of Qínhuái Shuǐ originates.
To the south is Shíjiù Hú,
which connects west to Dānyáng Hú,
and empties into the Dà Jiāng.)
Gāochún (south of the fǔ.
In Hóngzhì's fourth year, it was established from Gāochún Zhèn of Lìshuǐ Xiàn.
To the southwest are Gùchéng, Dānyáng, and Shíjiù lakes.
To the southeast is Guǎngtōng Zhèn,
commonly known as Dōngbà,
with Guǎngtōng Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Jiāngpǔ (west of the fǔ.
Originally Pǔzǐkǒu Xúnjiǎnsī of Liùhé Xiàn.
In the sixth month of Hóngwǔ's ninth year, it was changed to a xiàn.
Land from Hé and Chú two zhōus and Jiāngníng Xiàn was separated and added to it.
In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year, it was moved to the newly opened road junction north of the Jiāng,
and a Xúnjiǎnsī was still established in its old seat.
To the southeast it borders the Dà Jiāng,
where Jiānghuái Wèi is located,
established in the first month of Hóngwǔ's twenty-eighth year.
There is also Xījiāngkǒu Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Liùhé County (Northwest of the prefecture.
Originally belonged to Zhēnzhōu.
In the 3rd year of Hóngwǔ (1370), it was directly administered by Yángzhōufǔ.
In the 22nd year, 2nd month (1389), it came under this prefecture.
To the east is Guābùshān,
bordering the Great River (Dàjiāng).
The Chúhé River flows from the west,
entering it.
There is a Guābù Xúnjiǎnsī (Patrol and Inspection Bureau).)
Fèngyángfǔ (Originally Hāozhōu in the Yuán dynasty,
belonged to Ānfēnglù.)
In the 1st year of Wú (1367), Tàizǔ elevated it to Línháofǔ.
In the 2nd year, 9th month of Hóngwǔ (1369), the Middle Capital (Zhōngdū) was established,
and a Liúshǒusī (Retention Command) was set up here.
In the 6th year, 9th month (1373), it was called Zhōnglìfǔ.
In the 7th year, 8th month (1374), it was called Fèngyángfǔ.
(In the 2nd year, 9th month of Hóngwǔ (1369), the Zhōngdū city wall was built west of the old city.
It was completed in the 3rd year, 12th month (1370).
Its circumference was 50 *lǐ* and 443 *bù*.
Nine gates were erected: the main south gate was called Hóngwǔ,
the left gate to the south was called Nánzuǒjiǎdì,
the right gate was called QiánYòujiǎdì,
the east gate to the north was called Běizuǒjiǎdì,
the west gate was called Hòuyòujiǎdì,
the main east gate was called Dúshān,
the left gate to the east was called Chángchūn,
the right gate was called Cháoyáng,
and the main west gate was called Túshān.
The center was the Imperial City (Huángchéng),
with a circumference of 9 *lǐ* and 30 *bù*.
The main south gate was called Wǔmén,
the north gate was called Xuánchéng,
the east gate was called Dōnghuá,
and the west gate was called Xīhuá.)
It administered 5 departments (zhōu) and
13 counties (xiàn).
It was 330 *lǐ* from Nánjīng.
In the 26th year of Hóngwǔ (1393), the households numbered 79,107,
and the population was 427,303.
In the 4th year of Hóngzhì (1491),
the households numbered 95,010,
and the population was 931,108.
In the 6th year of Wànlì (1578),
the households numbered 111,070,
and the population was 1,202,349.
Fèngyáng County (Dependent.
In the 7th year, 8th month of Hóngwǔ (1374), it was established by separating land from Línhuáixiàn,
serving as the prefectural seat.
In the 11th year (1378), land from Hóngxiàn was again added to it.
It borders the Huái River to the north.
To the south is Mòshān,
from which the Háo River flows westward.
To the southwest is Huánglíngchéng,
where a Guard (wèi) was established in the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ (1369).
To the northwest is Chánghuáiguān,
where the Chánghuáiwèi was established in the 6th year of Hóngwǔ (1373).
To the northeast is Hóngtánghútúntiánshǒuyùqiānhùsuǒ (Thousand-Household Guard for Farming and Defense at Hongtang Lake),
established in the 11th year of Hóngwǔ (1378).)
Línhuái County (Northeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was called Zhōnglí,
serving as the seat of Hāozhōu.
In the 2nd year, 9th month of Hóngwǔ (1369), it was renamed Zhōnglì.
In the 3rd year, 11th month (1370), it was renamed Línhuái.
In the 7th year (1374), it became subordinate to the prefecture.
It borders the Huái River to the north.
There are two Háo Rivers:
the eastern source is from Háotángshān,
and the western source is from Mòshān.
They converge southwest of the city,
flowing eastward into the Huái River.)
Huáiyuǎn County (Northwest of the prefecture.
Jīngshān is southwest of the county.
Túshān is southeast of the county.
The Huái River flows through the gorge between the two mountains,
with the Běiféishuǐ (North Fei River) entering it.
Further north, the Wōshǔi also enters the Huái River,
known as Wōkǒu.
To the southwest is the Luòshuǐ River,
which forms the boundary with Shòuzhōu,
passing through Xīnchéngcūn south of the county and entering the Huái River.
There is a Luòhézhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Dìngyuǎn County (South of the prefecture.
To the south is the Chíhé River.
To the west is the Luòhé River.
Also, there are the Yīngwǔwèi to the north
and the Fēixióngwèi to the northeast,
both established in the 11th year of Hóngwǔ (1378).)
Wǔhé County (Northeast of the prefecture.
Originally belonged to Sìzhōu in the Yuán dynasty.
In the 4th year, 2nd month of Hóngwǔ (1371), it came under this prefecture.
The old seat was south of the county.
In the 1st year of Yǒnglè (1403), it was destroyed by water
and moved to the northwest boundary.
In the 25th year of Jiājìng (1546), it was moved north of the Huìhé River,
which is its current seat.
It borders the Huái River to the east.
To the southeast is the Chónghé River,
to the northwest are the Huìhé River and Tuóhé River,
and to the northeast is the Tónghé River,
all flowing together into the Huái River,
known as Wǔhékǒu.
To the west was an Shàngdiàn Xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.)
Hóng County (Northeast of the prefecture.
Originally belonged to Sìzhōu in the Yuán dynasty.
In the 7th year, 7th month of Hóngwǔ (1374), it came under this prefecture.
To the south is the Biànhé River.
To the southeast is the Tónghé River.
To the west is the Tuóhé River.)
Shòuzhōu (Originally Ānfēnglù in the Yuán dynasty,
belonged to Hénánjiāngběixíngshěng.)
In the Bǐngwǔ year (1366), Tàizǔ called it Shòuchūnfǔ.
In the 1st year of Wú (1367), it was called Shòuzhōu,
belonging to Línháofǔ.
In the 2nd year,
9th month of Hóngwǔ (1369), it was directly administered by the Zhōngshūshěng.
In the 4th year, 2nd month (1371), it returned to the prefecture,
after which Shòuchūnxiàn, the seat of the department, was merged into it.
(It borders the Huái River to the north.
The Huái River passes through a mountain gorge,
known as Xiáshí
Mountain,
where the Xīféishuǐ (West Fei River) flows in.
To the northeast is Bāgōngshān,
below which the Dōngféishuǐ (East Fei River) flows,
entering the Huái River to the west,
known as Féikǒu.
To the northwest is the Yǐngshuǐ River,
which also enters the Huái River.
To the south is the Sháopíshuǐ River,
and to the west is the Bēishuǐ River,
both entering the Huái River.
To the north was Xiàcàixiàn,
and to the south was Ānfēngxiàn,
both abolished during Hóngwǔ.
There is a Xiàcàizhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.
To the east are Běilúzhèn and to the west Zhèngyángzhèn, two
Xúnjiǎnsī.)
It is 180 *lǐ* east of the prefecture,
administering 2 counties.
Huòqiū County (Southwest of the department.
To the southwest is Dàbiéshān.
It borders the Huái River to the north,
with the Shǐhé River and Fēnghé River both flowing into it.
To the south are Kāishùnzhèn and Dīngtǎdiàn,
and to the west is Gāotángdiàn, three Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Méngchéng County (North of the department.
To the north is the Wōshuǐ River,
and also the Běiféishuǐ River.)
Sìzhōu (Originally belonged to Huái'ānlù in the Yuán dynasty.)
In the 1st year of Wú (1367), Tàizǔ made it belong to Línháofǔ.
In the 2nd year, 9th month of Hóngwǔ (1369), it was directly administered by the Zhōngshūshěng.
In the 4th year, 2nd month (1371), it returned to the prefecture,
after
Línhuáixiàn, the seat of the department, was merged into it.
(It borders the Huái River to the south,
with the Biànshuǐ River flowing from north of the city southward into it.)
It is 210 *lǐ* west of the prefecture,
administering 2 counties.
Xūyí County (South of the department.
To the southeast is Dūliángshān.
To the northeast is Guīshān.
To the west is Fúshān.
It borders the Huái River to the north,
with the Chíhé River flowing from the west into it.
To the northeast is Hóngzéhú,
where the Huái River collects.
To the west is an Jiùxiàn Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Tiāncháng County (Southeast of the department.
Yěshān is south of the county.
To the northwest is Shíliánghé,
whose lower reaches form the Wǔhú (Five Lakes),
connecting to Gāoyóuzhōu.
To the northeast is a Chéngménxiāng Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Sùzhōu (Originally belonged to Guīdéfü in the Yuán dynasty.)
In the 4th year, 2nd month of Hóngwǔ (1371), it came under this prefecture.
(Lóngshān is to the southwest,
from which the Běiféishuǐ River flows.
To the north is the Suīhé River,
flowing from Yǒngchéngxiàn in Hénán,
its lower reaches reaching
Sùqiānxiàn where it joins the Huái River,
also known as Xiǎohé.
To the south is the Biànhé River,
also flowing from Yǒngchéngxiàn.
There is also the Huìhé River, which joins the Huànshuǐ River.
To the southeast is the Tuóshuǐ River.)
It is 233 *lǐ* southeast of the prefecture.
It administers 1 county.
Língbì (zhōu dōng.
To the southwest is Qíméi Shān.
To the north is Qìngshí Shān.
The Huáng Hé is to the northeast.
To the south is the Biàn Hé.
To the north is the Suī Hé.
Further to the south is Gùzhèn Xúnjiǎn Sī.
) Yǐngzhōu (In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Rǔníng Fǔ.
) In the second month of the fourth year of Hóngwǔ, it became subordinate.
(The Huái Hé is to the south,
flowing in from Gùshǐ Xiàn, Hénán,
and its lower reaches merge with the Dà Hé before flowing into the sea.
Further south is the Rǔ Shuǐ,
flowing in from Xī Xiàn,
Hénán,
passing through Zhūgāo Zhèn and entering the Huái Hé.
Further north is the Yǐng Hé,
flowing in from Shěnqiū Xiàn, Hénán.
In the twenty-fourth year of Hóngwǔ,
the Huáng Hé breached its banks in Hénán,
merged with the Yǐng Hé at Chénzhōu,
passed through Tàihé
Xiàn,
then passed north of the prefectural city,
then passed through Yǐngshàng Xiàn,
and entered the Huái Hé at Shòuzhōu.
In the ninth year of Yǒnglè,
the river returned to its old course.
During the Xuāndé, Zhèngtǒng, Chénghuà, and Zhèngdé periods,
the Huáng Hé and Yǐng Hé were sometimes open and sometimes
blocked.
Locally, the Yǐng Hé was also called the Xiǎohuáng Hé.
To the northwest, there is also Shěnqiū Zhèn Xúnjiǎn Sī.
) It is 440 *lǐ* east of the prefecture.
It administers two counties.
Yǐngshàng (southeast of the zhōu.
To the east is the Yǐng Hé.
To the south is the Huái Hé.
To the northeast is the Xīféi Shuǐ.
Tàihé (northwest of the zhōu.
To the south is the Yǐng Shuǐ,
also known as the Shā Hé.
To the north is the Xīféi Shuǐ.
There are also Hóngshān and Běiyuán Hé two Xúnjiǎn Sī.
) Bózhōu (In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Guīdé Fǔ.
) In the early Hóngwǔ period,
Qiáoxiàn, the seat of the zhōu, was merged into it.
Soon after, it was demoted to a county,
subordinate to Guīdé Zhōu.
In the sixth year, it became subordinate to Yǐngzhōu.
In the tenth month of the ninth year of Hóngzhì,
it was again promoted to a zhōu.
(To the west is the Wō Hé,
flowing in from Lùyì Xiàn, Hénán,
and to the north is the Mǎshàng Hé,
which flows into it.
To the south is the Xīféi Shuǐ,
which is also the Xiàféi Shuǐ.
Further to the southeast is Chéngfù
Xiàn,
which was abolished during the Hóngwǔ period.
There is also Yìmén Xúnjiǎn Sī.
) It is 450 *lǐ* southeast of the prefecture.
Huái'ān Fǔ (In the Yuán dynasty, it was Huái'ān Lù,
subordinate to Huáidōng Dào Xuānwèi Sī.
) In the *bǐngwǔ* year of Tàizǔ's reign, in the fourth month, it became a prefecture.
It administers two zhōu
and nine counties.
It is 500 *lǐ* southwest of Nánjīng.
In the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ, it had 80,689 households
and 632,541 people.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì,
it had 27,978 households
and 237,527 people.
In the sixth year of Wànlì,
it had 109,205 households
and 906,033 people.
Shānyáng (the prefectural seat.
To the north, it borders the Huái Hé.
Gāojiā Yàn is to its southwest.
To the south is the Yùnhé,
which was dredged during the Yǒnglè period.
To the southwest is the Yǒngjì Hé,
opened in the ninth year of Wànlì,
65 *lǐ* long,
also called the Xīnyùnhé.
To the southeast is Shèyáng Hú.
To the northeast are Mǎluó Xiāng, Miàowān Zhèn, and Yángzhài Xiāng, three Xúnjiǎn Sī.
Qīnghé (west of the prefecture.
The county seat borders the Huáng Hé.
At the end of Chóngzhēn,
the seat was moved to Gānlú Chéng, southeast of the county.
To the south is the Huái Hé,
which merges with the Huáng Hé to the northeast,
called Qīngkǒu,
formerly called Sìkǒu.
From Xúzhōu to this point,
it is all the old course of the Sì Shuǐ,
which was usurped by the Huáng Hé.
To the south is Hóngzé Hú,
with Hóngzé Xúnjiǎn Sī.
Further east is Mǎtóu Zhèn Xúnjiǎn Sī.
Yánchéng (southeast of the prefecture.
To the east, it borders the sea,
with salt fields.
To the north is Shèyáng Hú.
To the west is Qīnggōu, and to the northwest are Yùkǒu Zhèn, two Xúnjiǎn Sī.
Āndōng (northeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Āndōng Zhōu.
In the first month of the second year of Hóngwǔ, it was demoted to a county.
To the northeast, Qú Shān is to the south.
To the northeast is Yùzhōu Shān,
in the sea.
In the early Hóngwǔ period,
Dōnghǎi Xúnjiǎn Sī was established here.
Later it was moved to Xīnbà, south of the zhōu.
To the southwest is the Lián Hé,

where a city wall was built in the thirty-seventh year of Jiājìng.)
Jìngjiāng (prefecture northeast.
In the intercalary ninth month of the seventh year of Chénghuà, it was established from Mǎtuó Shā of Jiāngyīn Xiàn.
The Great River [originally] divided into two branches,
encircling the county to the north and south.
After Tiānqǐ,
tidal sands accumulated,
and the Great River north of the county gradually became dry land.
To its southwest is the Xīngǎng Patrol and Inspection Bureau.) Zhènjiāng Fǔ (Originally Zhènjiāng Lù
subordinate to the Jiāngzhè Xíngshěng.)
In the third month of the *bǐngshēn* year of Tàizǔ's reign, it was named Jiānghuái Fǔ;
in the twelfth month, it was named Zhènjiāng Fǔ.
It administered three counties.
It is two hundred *lǐ* west of Nánjīng City.
In the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ, there were eighty-seven thousand three hundred sixty-four households,
and five hundred twenty-two thousand three hundred eighty-three mouths.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì,
there were sixty-eight thousand three hundred forty-four households,
and one hundred seventy-one thousand five hundred eight mouths.
In the sixth year of Wànlì,
there were sixty-nine thousand thirty-nine households,
and one hundred sixty-five thousand five hundred eighty-nine mouths.
Dāntú (adjacent.
To its north is Běigù Shān,
bordering the Great River.
In the river, to its northwest is Jīn Shān,
and to its northeast is Jiāo Shān.
Also, at the river mouth west of the city, there is Suàn Shān.
Also, Jīngxiàn Shān is to its east,
and Chuí Shān is to its north,
bordering the river as a strategic defense.
Also, to its south is the Grand Canal.
To its west is Gāozī Zhèn, to its northeast is Ānxiàng, to its east is Dāntú Zhèn, to its north is Jiāngjiāzuī, four Patrol and Inspection Bureaus.)
Dānyáng (prefecture southeast.
To its north it borders the Great River,
and there is also Liànhú.
To its south is the Grand Canal.
Also, to its east is the Lǚchéng Zhèn Patrol and Inspection Bureau,
soon moved to the east of the town.
There is also the Bāogǎng Patrol and Inspection Bureau,
soon moved to Gùxiàng.)
Jīntán (prefecture southeast.
To its west is Máoshān.
To its southeast is Chángdàng Hú,
also named Táohú,
which has the Húxī Patrol and Inspection Bureau.
To its north is Báihèxī.) Lúzhōu Fǔ (Originally Lúzhōu Lù,
subordinate to the Hénán Jiāngběi Xíngshěng.)
In the seventh month of the *jiǎchén* year of Tàizǔ's reign, it became a prefecture,
and the Jiānghuái Zhōngshū Xíngshěng was established here,
but was soon abolished.
It administered two departments,
and six counties.
It is five hundred ten *lǐ* from Nánjīng.
In the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ, there were forty-eight thousand seven hundred twenty households,
and three hundred sixty-seven thousand two hundred mouths.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì,
there were thirty-six thousand five hundred forty-eight households,
and four hundred eighty-six thousand five hundred forty-nine mouths.
In the sixth year of Wànlì,
there were forty-seven thousand three hundred seventy-three households,
and six hundred twenty-two thousand six hundred ninety-eight mouths.
Héféi (adjacent.
To its west is Jīmíng Shān,
from which Féishuǐ originates,
flowing southeast into Cháohú.
To its southwest is Zǐpéng Shān.
To its east are Fúchá Shān and Héng Shān.
Also, to its southeast is Sìdǐng Shān,
overlooking Cháohú,
which is over four hundred *lǐ* in circumference,
and contains Lǎoshān and Gūshān.
Also, to its northeast is Chúshuǐ,
originating from Lóngtán,
its lower reaches flowing into the River at Lùhé Xiàn.
Also, to its east is Diànfù Hé,
and to its south is Sānchà Hé,
all flowing into Cháohú.
To its northeast was Liáng Xiàn,
abolished in early Hóngwǔ.
To its southwest was the Lúzhèn Guān Patrol and Inspection Bureau,
later moved to Shíliáng Zhèn to the east of the county.)
Shūchéng (prefecture southwest.
To its southwest is Lóngmián Shān,
bordering Tóngchéng Xiàn.
To its west is Sānjiǎo Shān.
Also, Cháohú is to its east.
Also, to its south is Běixiá Guān,
also bordering Tóngchéng.)
Lújiāng (prefecture south.
Originally subordinate to Wúwéi Zhōu.
In early Hóngwǔ,
it was reclassified as subordinate to the prefecture.
To its northeast is Yěfù Shān.
To its east is Cháohú.
To its southeast is Huángpí Hú.
To its west is Lěngshuǐ Guān,
which has a Patrol and Inspection Bureau.) Wúwéi Zhōu. In the Hóngwǔ era,
the administrative seat, Wúwéi Xiàn, was merged into the *zhōu*.
(The Great River is to its southeast.
To its east is Rúxū Shuǐ,
also named Tiānhé,
diverging from Cháohú,
and flowing northeast into the River.
Also,
to its east is Àolóng Hé Zhèn,
to its southeast are Níchà Hé Zhèn and Tǔqiáo Hé Zhèn,
and to its north is Huángluò Hé Zhèn, four Patrol and Inspection Bureaus.)
It is two hundred eighty *lǐ* northwest of the prefecture.
It administers one county.
Cháo (department north.
To its southeast is Qībǎo Shān,
facing Rúxū Shān in Hánshān Xiàn,
with Xīguān on top of it.
Cháohú is to its west,
and the Zhàogāo Hé flows into it from the northwest.
To its south is Shíliáng Hé,
which is the upper stream of Rúxū,
and Qīngxī flows into it from the southeast.
To its southwest is the Jiāohú Patrol and Inspection Bureau.) Lù'ān Zhōu. In the second month of the fourth year of Hóngwǔ,
it became subordinate to Zhōngdū Línzhāo Fǔ,
with the administrative seat Lù'ān Xiàn merged into the *zhōu*.
In the fifteenth year, it was reclassified as subordinate.
(To its west is Pèishuǐ,
also called
Bìshuǐ,
its lower reaches flowing into the Huái River at Shòuzhōu.
To its southwest was the Mábù Patrol and Inspection Bureau,
later abolished.
Also, to its northwest was the Héshàng Tān Patrol and Inspection Bureau,
which in the Hóngzhì era became subordinate to Huòshān Xiàn,
later moved to Xīndiàn,
and still
subordinate [here].)
It is one hundred eighty *lǐ* east of the prefecture.
It administers two counties.
Yīngshān (department southwest.
The county seat was originally Hùhé Xiāng;
in the twelfth year of Chóngzhēn, it was moved to Zhāngshān in the northwest,
and in the sixteenth year, it was again moved to Tiānlóu Xiāng in the northern border region.
Duōyún Shān is in the northwest,
bordering Luótián Xiàn in Húguǎng.
To its west is Yīngshān Hé,
which is the upper source of Xīshuǐ in Húguǎng.)
Huòshān 霍山 (Southwest of the prefecture.
Originally the Xúnjiǎnsī 巡檢司 (Patrol and Inspection Bureau) of the old Bùzhèn 埠鎮 in Liù'ān Zhōu 六安州.
In the second year of Hóngzhì 弘治
To its south is Huòshān 霍山,
also called Tiānzhùshān 天柱山,
also called Héngshān 衡山,
and also known as the Southern Sacred Mountain (Nányuè 南岳).
To its southeast is Tiělúzāi Shān 鐵鑪山 (Iron Furnace Mountain),
rich in iron smelting.
To its southwest is Sìshíbābān Shān 四十八盤山 (Forty-Eight Turns Mountain).
The Pìhé 淠河 river is to its east,
originating from Huòshān 霍山.
Its lower reaches flow into the Huái 淮 river at Shòuzhōu 壽州.
To its northwest are Qiānluófàn 千羅畈 and to its southwest are Shàngtǔshì 上土市, two Xúnjiǎnsī 巡檢司.)
Ānqìng Fǔ 安慶府 (Originally Ānqìng Lù 安慶路 in the Yuán 元 dynasty,
subordinate to Hénán Jiāngběi Xíngshěng 河南江北行省.)
In the eighth month of the Xīncǎo 辛丑 year
In the fourth month of the Rén'yín 壬寅 year
It administered six counties.
It is 650 li north of Nánjīng 南京.
In the 26th year of Hóngwǔ 洪武
and the population was 422,804.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì 弘治
households numbered 46,050,
and the population was 616,089.
In the sixth year of Wànlì 萬曆
households numbered 46,609,
and the population was 543,476.
Huáiníng 懷寧 (The seat of the prefecture.
To its south it borders the Great River (Dàjiāng 大江).
To its west, the Wǎnshuǐ 皖水 flows into it,
called Wǎnkǒu 皖口.
To its northwest is the Guānyīngǎng Xúnjiǎnsī 觀音港巡檢司.
To its east is the Chángfēngshāzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī 長風沙鎮巡檢司.)
Tóngchéng 桐城 (Northeast of the prefecture.
To its east is Fúshān 浮山,
also named Fúdù Shān 浮度山.
To its northwest is Lóngmián Shān 龍眠山.
To its north is Běixiá Shān 北峽山,
bordering Shūchéng 舒城,
where the Běixiáguān Xúnjiǎnsī 北峽關巡檢司 is located.
Further north is Xīxiá Shān 西峽山,
also called Nánxiáshí 南峽石;
compared to Xiáshí 峽石 in Shòuzhōu 壽州, this one is south.
To its southeast it borders the Jiāng 江,
where the Cōngyánghé 樅陽河 river flows,
entering from the northwest.
To its east is Liùbǎizhàng 六百丈.
To its southeast are Mǎtàshí 馬踏石 and Yuánzǐgǎng 源子港, three Xúnjiǎnsī 巡檢司.)
Qiánshān 潛山 (Northwest of the prefecture.
Abolished at the end of the Yuán 元 dynasty.
Reestablished in the early Hóngwǔ 洪武 era.
To its northwest is Qiánshān 灊山,
also called Tiānzhùshān 天柱山,
also called Wǎngōngshān 皖公山,
which is Huòshān 霍山.
The Wǎnshuǐ 皖水 originates from it.
A separate stream is called Qiánshuǐ 灊水.
Their combined flow enters the Dàjiāng 大江.
There is also Tiāntángshān 天堂山,
the source of the Hòubùhé 後部河.
There is a Tiāntángzhài Xúnjiǎnsī 天堂寨巡檢司.)
Tàihú 太湖 (Northwest of the prefecture.
To its northwest is Sīkōng Shān 司空山.
West of the city is the Mǎlùhé 馬路河,
which is the lower reaches of the Hòubùhé 後部河.
To the east, it joins the Qiánshuǐ 灊水.
To its northwest are Nányáng 南陽 and Báishā 白沙.
To its northeast is Xiǎochí 小池.
To its north is Hòubù 後部, four Xúnjiǎnsī 巡檢司.)
Sùsōng 宿松 (Southwest of the prefecture.
To its east is Mǎtóushān 馬頭山.
The Xiǎogū Shān 小姑山 is in the Dàjiāng 大江 south of the county,
bordering Péngzé Xiàn 彭澤縣 in Jiāngxī 江西.
There is a Xiǎogū Shān Xúnjiǎnsī 小姑山巡檢司.
To its southwest are Guīlíntān 歸林灘 and to its south is Jīngjiāngkǒu 涇江口, two Xúnjiǎnsī 巡檢司.)
Wàngjiāng 望江 (Southwest of the prefecture.
To its south it borders the Jiāng 江.
To its east is Léichí 雷池,
which flows south into the Jiāng 江,
called Léijiāngkǒu 雷江口,
also called Léigǎng 雷港.
There is a Xúnjiǎnsī 巡檢司 there.
To its west is Bóhú 泊湖.
To its north is Cíhú 慈湖.
To its northeast is Zhānghú 漳湖.
Their lower reaches all flow into the Jiāng 江.
To its southwest is Yángwānzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī 楊灣鎮巡檢司.)
Tàipíng Fǔ 太平府 (Originally Tàipíng Lù 太平路 in the Yuán 元 dynasty,
subordinate to Jiāngzhè Xíngshěng Jiāngdōng Dào 江浙行省江東道.)
In the sixth month of the Yǐwèi 乙未 year
It administered three counties.
It is 135 li east of Nánjīng 南京.
In the 26th year of Hóngwǔ 洪wu
and the population was 259,937.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì 弘治
households numbered 29,466,
and the population was 173,699.
In the sixth year of Wànlì 萬曆
households numbered 33,262,
and the population was 176,085.
Dāngtú 當塗 (The seat of the prefecture.
North of the city is Cǎishí Shān 采石山,
also named Niúzhǔ Shān 牛渚山,
overlooking the Dàjiāng 大江.
To its southwest is Bówàng Shān 博望山,
facing Liángshān 梁山 in Hézhōu 和州 across the river,
also called Dōngliáng Shān 東梁山.
Dānyánghú 丹陽湖 is to its southeast,
spanning over 300 li.
It branches into Wúhú 蕪湖,
and flows west into the Jiāng 江.
To its south is Gūshú Xī 姑熟溪.
There is also Huángchí Hé 黃池河.
To its southwest is Dàxìn Hé 大信河.
To its north is Cíhú 慈湖.
All these flow into the Dàjiāng 大江.
There are Cǎishí 采石 and Dàxìn 大信, two Xúnjiǎnsī 巡檢司.)
Wúhú 蕪湖 (Southwest of the prefecture.
To its southwest is Zhànniǎo Shān 戰鳥山,
in the Dàjiāng 大江.
To its northwest are Qījí 七磯.
To its south is Lǔmíng Jiāng 魯明江,
also named Lǔgǎng 魯港.
There is also Shígè Hé 石硊河.
Both flow into the Dàjiāng 大江.
To its west is Hékǒuzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī 河口鎮巡檢司,
later moved to Lǔgǎngzhèn 魯港鎮.)
Fánchāng 繁昌 (Southwest of the prefecture.
To its northwest is Kēshān 磕山,
in the Jiāng 江.
Sānshānjī 三山磯 is to its northeast,
bordering the Jiāng 江.
To its west is Dígǎng 荻港,
flowing into the Dàjiāng 大江.
There are Sānshān 三山 and Dígǎng 荻港, two Xúnjiǎnsī 巡檢司.)
Chízhōu Fǔ 池州府 (Originally Chízhōu Lù 池州路 in the Yuán 元 dynasty,
subordinate to Jiāngzhè Xíngshěng Jiāngdōng Dào 江浙行省江東道.)
In the eighth month of the Xīncǎo 辛丑 year
then soon after called it Chízhōu Fǔ 池州府.
It administered six counties.
It is 550 li northeast of Nánjīng 南京.
In the 26th year of Hóngwǔ 洪武
and the population was 198,574.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì 弘治
households numbered 14,091,
and the population was 69,478.
In the sixth year of Wànlì 萬曆
households numbered 18,377,
and the population was 84,851.
Guìchí 貴池 (The seat of the prefecture.
To its south is Qíshān 齊山.
To its north it borders the Jiāng 江.
To its east is Méigēngǎng 梅根港.
To its west is Chíkǒuhé 池口河,
which is Guìchí 貴池 itself.
Further west is Lǐyánghé 李陽河.
All flow into the Dàjiāng 大江.
There are Chíkǒuzhèn 池口鎮 and Lǐyánghé 李陽河, two Xúnjiǎnsī 巡檢司.)
Qīngyáng 青陽 (East of the prefecture.
To its southwest is Jiǔhuá Shān 九華山.
To its north is Qīngshān 青山.
To its west is Wǔxīshuǐ 五溪水,
originating from Jiǔhuá Shān 九華山.
To its south is Línchénghé 臨城河.
All converge and flow into the Dàtōnghé 大通河, which then enters the Jiāng 江.)
Tónglíng 銅陵 (Northeast of the prefecture.
To its south is Tóngguān Shān 銅官山.
To its east is Chéngshān 城山.
To its west it borders the Dàjiāng 大江.
To its south is Dàtōnghé 大通河.
To its north is Dígǎnghé 荻港河.
Both flow into the Dàjiāng 大江.
There is a Dàtōng Xúnjiǎnsī 大通巡檢司.)
Shídài 石埭 (Southeast of the prefecture.
To its north is Língyáng Shān 陵陽山.
To its west is Lìshān 櫟山,
from which Guānxi 官溪 originates.
This is the source of the Chíkǒuhé 池口河.
Shūxī 舒溪 is to its south.
Its lower reaches join Lǔgǎng 魯港 in Wúhú Xiàn 蕪湖縣 and flow into the Jiāng 江.)
Jiàndé 建德 (Southwest of the prefecture.
To its south is Lóngkǒuhé 龍口河,
which flows southeast into Dúshānhú 獨山湖 in Ráozhōu Fǔ 饒州府.
There is also Yáochéngxī 堯城溪,
whose lower reaches become Jiāngkǒuhé 江口河 in Dōngliú Xiàn 東流縣,
and flows into the Jiāng 江.
To its southwest is Yǒngfēngzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī 永豐鎮巡檢司.)
Dōngliú Fǔ (west.
To the southwest is Mǎdāng Shān,
which rests against the great river [Dà Jiāng],
and borders Péngzé Xiàn in Jiāngxī.
To the south is Xiāngkǒu Hé,
which flows into the river.
There was a Xiāngkǒu Zhèn patrol and inspection office [Xúnjiǎnsī],
which was later moved to Jíyáng Zhèn.)
Níngguó Fǔ (formerly Níngguó Lù in the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to the Jiāngzhè Xíngshěng.
) In the Dīngyǒu year, 4th month, of Tàizǔ's reign, it was named Níngguó Fǔ.
In the Xīnchǒu year, 4th month, it was named Xuānchéng Fǔ.
In the Bǐngwǔ year, 1st month, it was named Xuānzhōu Fǔ.
In the 4th month of Wú Yuánnián, it was restored to Níngguó Fǔ.
It administered six counties.
Its northern distance to Nánjīng is 310 lǐ.
In the 26th year of Hóngwǔ, the census recorded 99,732 households [biānhù] and
532,259 individuals [kǒu].
In the 4th year of Hóngzhì,
there were 60,364 households and
371,543 individuals.
In the 6th year of Wànlì,
there were 52,148 households and
387,019 individuals.
Xuānchéng (the seat of the prefecture.
To the north is Jìngtíng Shān.
To the west is Qīngyì Jiāng,
which flows northwest to Wúhú Xiàn and enters the river.
Also, to the east is Wǎnxī,
which merges with Jùxī to the northeast,
and flows north into the great river [Dà Jiāng].
Also, Nánhú is also to the northeast,
and flows into Jùxī.
To the north is Huángchí Zhèn, and to the northeast is Shuǐyáng Zhèn, two patrol and inspection offices.
Nánlíng (west of the prefecture.
To the west is Gōng Shān.
To the south is Lǚ Shān,
from which Huáishuǐ originates.
To the east is Qīngyì Jiāng.
Also, to the southwest is Zhāngshuǐ,
which merges with Huáishuǐ,
and enters Qīngyì Jiāng.
Also, to the south is Lǐng patrol and inspection office.
Jīng (west of the prefecture.
To the south is Chéngliú Shān.
To the west is Shǎngxī,
also called Jīngxī,
its upper stream being Shūxī.
Also, to the southeast, Téngxī comes to merge with it,
and its lower stream flows into Qīngyì Jiāng.
To the southeast is Rúmá Líng patrol and inspection office.
Níngguó (southeast of the prefecture.
To the west is Zǐ Shān.
To the northwest is Wénjí Shān.
To the southeast is Qiānqiū Líng,
which has a pass.
To the east is Dōngxī,
which originates from Tiānmù Shān in Yúqián Xiàn, Zhèjiāng.
To the west is Xīxī,
which originates from Lóngcóng Shān in Jìxī Xiàn,
which is the upper source of Jùxī.
To the southeast is Yuè Shān patrol and inspection office,
formerly located at the foot of Yuè Shān.
During the Hóngwǔ era, it was moved to Niǔkǒu,
and later moved to Shíkǒu Zhèn.
Also, to the southwest is Húlè patrol and inspection office.
Jīngdé (south of the prefecture.
To the north is Shíbì Shān.
To the west is Zhèng Shān.
To the southwest is Ruò Líng,
which borders Tàipíng and Shè two counties.
To the east is Huīshuǐ,
which flows in from Jìxī Xiàn,
which is the upper stream of Téngxī.
To the northeast is Wū Líng patrol and inspection office,
now abolished.
Also, to the north is Sānxī patrol and inspection office.
Tàipíng (southwest of the prefecture.
To the south is Huáng Shān,
which divides the border with Shè Xiàn.
To the west is Lóngmén Shān,
which has a patrol and inspection office.
To the south is Máchuān,
which merges with Shūxī and flows into Jīng Xiàn,
becoming Shǎngxī.
To the southwest is Hóngtán patrol and inspection office,
later moved to Guōyánqián.
Huīzhōu Fǔ (formerly Huīzhōu Lù in the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to the Jiāngzhè Xíngshěng.)
In the Dīngyǒu year, 7th month, of Tàizǔ's reign, it was named Xìng'ān Fǔ.
In Wú Yuánnián, it was named Huīzhōu Fǔ.
It administered six counties.
Its northern distance to Nánjīng is 680 lǐ.
In the 26th year of Hóngwǔ, the census recorded 125,548 households and
592,360 individuals.
In the 4th year of Hóngzhì,
there were 7,251 households and
65,861 individuals.
In the 6th year of Wànlì,
there were 118,943 households and
566,948 individuals.
Shè (the seat of the prefecture.
To the northwest is Huáng Shān,
also called Yī Shān,
from which Xīn'ān Jiāng originates,
flowing southeast to become Shèpǔ.
Also, to the east is Xīn'ān Jiāng,
which reaches Jiàndé Xiàn in Zhèjiāng,
and merges with Dōngyáng Jiāng to form the upper source of Zhèjiāng.
Also, Yáng zhī Shuǐ is to the west,
also called Huīxī,
which merges into Shèpǔ.
To the southeast are Jiēkǒu Zhèn and Wánggàn Zhài, two patrol and inspection offices.
To the northwest is Huáng Shān patrol and inspection office.
Xiūníng (west of the prefecture.
To the northeast is Sōngluó Shān.
To the west is Báiyuè Shān.
To the southeast is Shuài Shān,
from which Shuàishuǐ originates,
a separate source of Xīn'ān Jiāng.
To the southwest is Zhèxī,
which flows east and merges with Shuàishuǐ.
Also, to the west is Jíyáng Shuǐ,
also called Báihè Xī,

Gazetteer Volume 17, Geography 2, Shāndōng, Shānxī.
Shāndōng was the land of Qīng and Yǎn two zhōu in Yǔgòng.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was directly administered by the Central Secretariat (Zhōngshū Shěng),
and also had the Shāndōng Dōngxī Dào Xuānwèi Sī (with its seat in Yìdū Lù) established under it.
In the fourth month of the first year of Hóngwǔ, the Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng of Shāndōng and other areas was established.
(Its seat was in Jìnán Fǔ.)
In the twelfth month of the third year, the Qīngzhōu Dūwèi was established.
(Its seat was in Qīngzhōu Fǔ.)
In the tenth month of the eighth year, the Dūwèi was renamed Shāndōng Dū Zhīhuīshǐ Sī.
In the sixth month of the ninth year, the Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng was renamed Chéngxuan Bùzhèngshǐ Sī.
It administered six fǔ,
fifteen subordinate zhōu,
and eighty-nine xiàn.
(It had over six thousand four hundred lǐ.)
To the south it reached Tánchéng,
(bordering Nánzhílì.)
To the north it reached Wúdì,
(bordering Běizhílì.)
To the west it reached Dìngtáo,
(bordering Běizhílì and Hénán.)
To the east it reached the sea.
It was one thousand eight hundred fifty lǐ from Nánjīng,
and nine hundred lǐ from the capital.
In the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ, there were seven hundred fifty-three thousand eight hundred ninety-four households,
and five million two hundred fifty-five thousand eight hundred seventy-six people.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì,
there were seven hundred seventy thousand five hundred fifty-five households,
and six million seven hundred fifty-nine thousand six hundred seventy-five people.
In the sixth year of Wànlì,
there were one million three hundred seventy-two thousand two hundred six households,
and five million six hundred sixty-four thousand ninety-nine people.
