To the west is the Zīshuǐ River,
whose lower course reaches Shòuguāng and enters the sea.
To the southwest is Yánshénzhèn Town,
from which the Xiàofùhé River originates,
entering the borders of Zīchuān County.
There is the Yánshénzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office;
in the thirty-seventh year of Jiājìng (1558), a wall was built.
To the southwest of the town is Qīngshíguān Pass.
Línzī (To the northwest of the prefecture.
To the south is Niúshān Mountain.
There is also Dǐngzúshān Mountain,
from which the Nǚshuǐ River originates,
whose lower course joins the Běiyángshuǐ River.
There is also Náoshān Mountain.
There is also Nánjiāoshān Mountain,
below which is Tiānqíyuān Abyss.
East of the city is the Zīshuǐ River.
To the west is the Mǐnshuǐ River.
There is also the Xìshuǐ River.
Their lower courses all flow into the Shíshuǐ River.
This Shíshuǐ River flows from southwest to northeast,
also called Érshuǐ River.
The Huáshuǐ River also flows into it.
Their lower courses all reach Luò'ān County and enter the sea.
To the south is the Zīhédìan Patrol and Inspection Office,
which was later abolished.
Bóxīng (To the northwest of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Bóxīngzhōu Prefecture.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ (1369), it was demoted to a county.
To the south are the Xiǎoqīnghé River and
the Shíshuǐ River.
Gāoyuàn (To the northwest of the prefecture.
To the southeast is Shāngshān Mountain.
To the southwest is the Xiǎoqīnghé River.
To the northwest is the Tiánzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office,
which was later abolished.
Luò'ān (To the north of the prefecture.
To the northeast, it borders the sea
and has salt fields.
To the north is the Xiǎoqīnghé River.
To the east is the Shíshuǐ River.
To the southeast are the Zīshuǐ River,
the Běiyángshuǐ River,
and the Jùyángshuǐ River.
All converge at Gāojiāgǎng Port to the northeast of the county and enter the sea.
This port is the ancient Mǎchēdú Channel.
There is the Gāojiāgǎng Patrol and Inspection Office.
To the northwest is the Luò'ānzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office.
To the northeast is Tángtóuzhài Fortress,
where a *Bǎihùsuǒ* (Company Commander's Post) is stationed.
Shòuguāng (To the northeast of the prefecture.
To the north, it borders the sea
and has salt fields.
To the west are the Zīshuǐ River
and the Běiyángshuǐ River.
To the east is the Jùyángshuǐ River.
To the northwest is Qīngshuǐpō Lake,
which is the ancient Jùdìnghú Lake.
Its northern part connects to Gāojiāgǎng Port in Luò'ān County.
To the northeast is the Guǎnglíngzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office.
Chānglè (To the east of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Wéizhōu Prefecture,
then was abolished soon after,
and later re-established,
still belonging to Wéizhōu Prefecture.
In the early Hóngwǔ period,
its affiliation was changed.
To the northwest is its old city.
During the Hóngwǔ period,
it was moved to its current seat.
To the southeast is Fāngshān Mountain,
from which the Eastern Dānshuǐ River originates,
flowing north past the old city of Chānglè.
The Western Dānshuǐ River flows and joins it.
Its lower course reaches Shòuguāng County and enters the sea.
To the south is the Báilángshuǐ River,
which enters the sea at Wéixiàn County.
Línqú (To the east of the prefecture.
To the south are Qúshān Mountain
and Dàxiànshān Mountain,
on which is the Mùlíngguān Patrol and Inspection Office.
To the east is Yíshān Mountain,
also named Dōngtàishān Mountain,
from which the Shùshuǐ River and the Míshuǐ River both originate.
The Míshuǐ River
is also named Jùyángshuǐ River.
To the west, it joins the Shígōushuǐ River,
and reaches Shòuguāng to enter the sea.
To the northeast is Dānshān Mountain,
also named Wánshān Mountain,
from which the Western Dānhé River and the Báilángshuǐ River originate.
Ānqiū (To the southeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Mìzhōu Prefecture.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ (1369), in the seventh month,
the prefecture was abolished
and it became subordinate to the prefecture.
To the southwest are Móushān Mountain
and Wùshān Mountain.
To the northeast is Zuòshān Mountain.
To the east is the Wéishuǐ River,
whose lower course flows through Wéixiàn County and enters the sea.
To the north is the Wènshuǐ River,
whose source also comes from Yíshān Mountain.
Its lower course joins the Wéishuǐ River.
Zhūchéng (To the southeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was the seat of Mìzhōu Prefecture,
subordinate to Yìdūlù Circuit.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ (1369), in the seventh month,
the prefecture was abolished
and it became subordinate to the prefecture.
To the southeast is Lángyéshān Mountain.
To the southwest are Chángshān Mountain
and Mǎ'ěrshān Mountain.
To the north is the Wéishuǐ River.
To the northeast is the Lúshuǐ River,
which flows and joins it.
To the south is the Xìnyángzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office.
To the south is the Nánlóngwānhǎikǒu Patrol and Inspection Office.
Méngyīn County (Southwest of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Jǔzhōu.
In the 7th month of Hóngwǔ 2 (1369), it was transferred to the prefecture.
To its south is Méngyīn Mountain.
To its east is Chángshān Mountain,
where Méngshuǐ River originates.
It flows north into Yíshuǐ River.
To its southeast was the Zǐjīngguān Patrolling and Inspection Division,
which was abolished during the Wànlì era.)
Jǔzhōu Prefecture (In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Yìdū Lù.
In the early Hóngwǔ era,
Jǔ Xiàn, the seat of the zhou, was absorbed into it.
To its west is Fúlái Mountain.
To its northwest is Jīwū Mountain,
from which Wéishuǐ River originates.
To its southwest is Shùshuǐ River,
which flows
into Yízhōu Prefecture.
To its south are Shízìlù and to its southwest Gégōudiàn, two Patrolling and Inspection Divisions.
) It is 200 lǐ north of the prefecture seat.
It administers two counties.
Yíshuǐ County (Northwest of the zhou.
To its northwest is Dàbiàn Mountain,
connected to Diāo'yá Mountain,
from which Yíshuǐ River originates.
It flows south through Yízhōu Prefecture and into the Sì River.
To its northeast is Shùshuǐ River.)
Rìzhào County (Northeast of the zhou.
To its east, it borders the sea
and has salt pans.
To its southeast is the Jiācāngzhèn Patrolling and Inspection Division.)
Láizhōu Prefecture (In the Yuán dynasty, it was Láizhōu,
belonging to Bānyáng Lù.
In Hóngwǔ 1 (1368), it was elevated to a prefecture.
In Hóngwǔ 6 (1373), it was demoted to a zhou.
In the 5th month of Hóngwǔ 9 (1376), it was again elevated to a prefecture.
It administers two zhou
and five counties.
It is 640 lǐ west of the Bùzhèngsī.
Yè County (The prefecture seat.
To its north, it borders the sea
and has salt pans.
There is also Sānshāndǎo Island,
located on the south shore of the sea.
To its northeast is Wànlǐshā.
To its southwest is Yèshuǐ River,
which flows north into the sea.
To its southeast is Xiǎogūhé River.
To its northeast is the Wángxúzhài Guard Myriad-Household Office,
established during the Jiājìng era.
To its west is Hǎicāng and to its north Cháihúzài, two Patrolling and Inspection Divisions.)
Píngdù Zhōu (In the Yuán dynasty, it was Jiāoshuǐ County.
In the 1st month of Hóngwǔ 22 (1389), it was reorganized.
To its north is Láishān Mountain.
To its west is Jiāoshuǐ River,
the lower reaches of which flow north into the sea at Chāngyì.
To its east is Dàgūhé River,
originating from
Túnquǎn Mountain in Huáng County.
It flows through the zhou
and merges with Xiǎogūhé River.
Together they are generally called Gūhé River,
which enters the sea at Jìmò County.
Xiǎogū,
is also known as Yóushuǐ River.
To its southwest is the Tíngkǒuzhèn Patrolling and Inspection Division.)
It is
100 lǐ north of the prefecture seat.
It administers two counties.
Wéi County (West of the zhou.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Wéizhōu,
belonging to Yìdū Lù.
In Hóngwǔ 1 (1368), Běihǎi County, the seat of the zhou, was absorbed into it.
In Hóngwǔ 9 (1376), it belonged to Láizhōu Prefecture.
In the 5th month of Hóngwǔ 10 (1377), it was demoted to a county.
In the 1st month of Hóngwǔ 22 (1389), it was transferred
to the zhou.
To its south is Wéishuǐ River,
which flows northeast into the sea.
To its northeast is the Gùdīdiàn Patrolling and Inspection Division.)
Chāngyì County (Northwest of the zhou.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Wéizhōu.
In the 5th month of Hóngwǔ 10 (1377), it was absorbed into Wéixiàn County.
In the 1st month of Hóngwǔ 22 (1389), it was re-established
and came to belong to this zhou.
To its east is Wéishuǐ River.
To its northeast is Jiāohé River.
To its north is the Yú'érzhèn Patrolling and Inspection Division.)
Jiāozhōu Prefecture (In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Yìdū Lù.
In the early Hóngwǔ era,
Jiāoxī County, the seat of the zhou, was absorbed into it.
In Hóngwǔ 9 (1376), it came to belong to this prefecture.
To its southwest is Tiějué Mountain,
where Jiāoshuǐ River originates,
also called Jiāoshān Mountain.
To its northeast
is Gūhé River,
which flows south into the sea.
To its southeast, at the river mouth, are Língshān Wèi
and Āndōng Wèi,
both established in the 5th month of Hóngwǔ 31 (1398).
There is also Xiàhézhài Myriad-Household Office,
to the southwest of Língshān Wèi.
Shíjiùdǎo Zhài Myriad-Household Office
is to the south of Āndōng Wèi.
Both were established after the Hóngzhì era.
To its southwest is the Gǔzhèn Patrolling and Inspection Division.
To its north is the Fēngměngzhèn Patrolling and Inspection Division.)
It is 220 lǐ north of the prefecture seat.
It administers two counties.
Gāomì County (Northwest of the zhou.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Jiāozhōu.
In Hóngwǔ 1 (1368), it belonged to Qīngzhōu Prefecture.
In the 5th month of Hóngwǔ 9 (1376), it belonged to Láizhōu Prefecture,
but soon returned to belonging to this zhou.
To its east is Jiāoshuǐ River.
To its west is Wéishuǐ River.
To its southwest is Mìshuǐ River,
also called Bǎichǐgōu,
which flows north to meet Wéishuǐ River.)
Jìmò County (East of the zhou.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Jiāozhōu.
In the early Hóngwǔ era,
it belonged to Qīngzhōu Prefecture.
In the 5th month of Hóngwǔ 9 (1376), it belonged to Láizhōu Prefecture.
In the 5th month of Hóngwǔ 10 (1377), it returned to belonging to this zhou.
To its southeast is Láoshān Mountain,
located by the seashore.
There is also Tiánhéngdǎo Island,
in the sea to the northeast.
To its east is Áoshān Wèi,
established in the 5th month of Hóngwǔ 21 (1388).
To its northeast is Xióngyá Guard Myriad-Household Office,
and to its south is Fúshān Guard Myriad-Household Office,
both established during the Hóngwǔ era.
To its northeast is Kǎolǎodǎo Patrolling and Inspection Division.
The old Jìmò Barracks were previously south of the county,
but in Xuāndé 8 (1433), they were moved and established north of the county,
with a city wall.)
Dēngzhōu Prefecture (In the Yuán dynasty, it was Dēngzhōu,
belonging to Bānyáng Lù.
In Hóngwǔ 1 (1368), it belonged to Láizhōu Prefecture.
In Hóngwǔ 6 (1373), it was directly administered by Shāndōng Xíngshěng.
In the 5th month of Hóngwǔ 9 (1376), it was elevated to a prefecture.
It administers one zhou
and seven counties.
It is 1050 lǐ west of the Bùzhèngsī.
Pénglái County (The prefecture seat.
It was abolished in the early Hóngwǔ era.
In the 5th month of Hóngwǔ 9 (1376), it was re-established.
To its north is Dānyá Mountain,
overlooking the great sea.
To its south is Mìshén Mountain,
where Mìshuǐ River originates.
To its southwest is Hēishí Mountain,
where Hēishuǐ River originates.
They flow through the south of the city, merge,
and flow north into the sea.
To its west is Lóngshān Mountain,
which produces iron.
To its east is the Gāoshān Patrolling and Inspection Division,
originally established on Shāmén Island in the sea,
later moved to the foot of Zhūgāoshān Mountain.
To its southeast is the Yángjiādiàn Patrolling and Inspection Division.)
Huáng County (Southwest of the prefecture.
To its southeast is Láishān Mountain.
To its southwest is Túnquǎn Mountain,
from which Dàgūshuǐ River originates.
To its east is Huángshuǐ River,
and to its southeast is Jiàngshuǐ River,
which merge and flow into the sea.
To its west is the Mǎtíngzhèn Patrolling and Inspection Division.)
Fúshān County (Southeast of the prefecture.
To its northeast is Zhīfú Mountain,
which borders the sea on three sides.
To its southwest is Yìjǐnghé River,
which flows north into the sea.
The Qíshān Guard Myriad-Household Office is to its northeast,
established in Hóngwǔ 31 (1398).
To its north is the Sūnkuǎngzhèn Patrolling and Inspection Division.)
Qīxiá County (Southeast of the prefecture.
To its east is Jùyú Mountain,
which formerly produced gold,
and is also called Jīnshān Mountain.
There is also Bǎijiàn Mountain,
and to its northwest Běiqū Mountain;
both mountains formerly produced iron.
To its south is Cuìpíng Mountain,
from which Dàhé River originates,
which is the upper source of Yìjǐnghé River.)
Zhāoyuǎn County (Southwest of the
Prefecture. Originally belonged to Láizhōu
in the Yuán dynasty. It came under this jurisdiction in the fifth month of the ninth year of Hóngwǔ.
To its northeast is the Yuántuán River,
which flows north into the sea.
To its west is the Dōngliáng Hǎikǒu Patrol and Inspection Office.
Láiyáng County (South of the
Prefecture. Originally belonged to Láizhōu
in the Yuán dynasty. It came under this jurisdiction in the fifth month of the ninth year of Hóngwǔ.
To its southeast is the Chāngshǔi River,
whose source is Chāngshān Mountain in Wéndēng County,
also known as Chāngyángshuǐ,
which flows south into the sea.
To its east is Xīyǎngzé Lake.
Further to its southeast is Dàsōng Wèi,
established in the fifth month of the thirty-first year of Hóngwǔ.
To the west of the Wèi is Dàshān Qiānhùsuǒ,
established during the Chénghuà period.
Further to its south is the Xíngcūnzài Patrol and Inspection Office.
) Nínghǎi Prefecture (Originally directly administered by the Shāndōng Dōngxī Dào Xuānwèisī
in the Yuán dynasty.) In the early Hóngwǔ period,
its administrative seat, Mùpíng County, was abolished and incorporated,
and it came under the jurisdiction of Láizhōu Fǔ.
In the ninth year, its affiliation was changed.
(To its east is the Jīnshuǐ
River,
also known as Qìnshuǐ.
To its southwest is the Wǔzhàng River,
both flowing north into the sea.
Further to its southwest is the Rǔshānzhài Patrol and Inspection Office.
) It is 220 *lǐ* west of the Prefecture.
It governs one county.
Wéndēng County (Southeast of the
Prefecture. Originally belonged to Nínghǎi Zhōu
in the Yuán dynasty. In the early Hóngwǔ period,
its affiliation was changed to Láizhōu Fǔ.
In the fifth month of the ninth year, it belonged to Dēngzhōu Fǔ,
and later reverted to the jurisdiction of the Prefecture.
To its southeast is Chìshān Mountain.
To its south is Chéngshān Mountain,
and also Tiěcháshān Mountain.
Further to its west is Tiěguānshān Mountain.
To its southeast it borders the sea.
To its south is Jìnghǎi Wèi,
to its east is Chéngshān Wèi,
to its north is Wēihǎi Wèi,
all established in the fifth month of the thirty-first year of Hóngwǔ.
Further to its southeast is Níngjīn Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ,
also established in the thirty-first year of Hóngwǔ.
Further to its east is Hǎiyáng Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ,
south of Jìnghǎi Wèi.
Jīnshān Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ
is west of Wēihǎi Wèi.
Bǎichǐyá Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ
is north of Wēihǎi Wèi.
Xúnshān Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ
is southeast of Chéngshān Wèi.
All were established during the Chénghuà period.
Further to its north are Xīnwāngzhài, to its northeast Wēnquánzhèn, and to its east Chìshānzhèn, three Patrol and Inspection Offices.
) Liáodōng Dūzhīhuīshǐsī (The Yuán dynasty established the Xíngzhōngshūshěng of Liáoyáng and other places,
with its seat in Liáoyáng Lù.
) In the seventh month of the fourth year of Hóngwǔ, Dìngliáo Dūwèi was established.
In the sixth month of the sixth year, Liáoyáng Fǔ and County were established.
In the tenth month of the eighth year, Dūwèi was changed to Liáodōng Dūzhīhuīshǐsī.
Its seat was Dìngliáo Zhōngwèi,
governing twenty-five *wèi*
and two *zhōu*.
In the tenth year,
both the Prefecture and County were abolished.
It extends east to the Yālù Jiāng,
west to Shānhǎiguān,
south to Lǚshùn Hǎikǒu,
and north to Kāiyuán.
By sea to Shāndōng Bùzhèngsī,
it is 2,150 *lǐ*.
It is 1,400 *lǐ* from Nánjīng,
and 1,700 *lǐ* from the capital.
Dìngliáo Zhōngwèi (The Yuán dynasty Liáoyáng Lù,
with its seat in Liáoyáng County.)
Abolished in the fourth year of Hóngwǔ.
Re-established in the sixth year.
Abolished again in the tenth year.
A *wèi* was established in the seventeenth year.
(To its southwest is Shǒushān Mountain.
To its south is Qiānshān Mountain.
Further to its southeast is Ānpíngshān Mountain,
which has an iron mine.
Further to its west is the Liáo Hé,
flowing in from outside the frontier,
and entering the sea at Hǎizhōu Wèi.
Further to its northwest is the Húnhé River,
also known as Xiǎoliáoshuǐ.
To its northeast is the Tàizǐhé River,
also known as Dàliángshuǐ,
and also Dōngliángshuǐ.
Its lower reaches all flow into the Liáo Shuǐ.
Further to its east is the Yālù Jiāng,
which flows southeast into the sea.
Further to its east is Fènghuángchéng City,
southeast of Fènghuángshān Mountain,
built in the seventeenth year of Chénghuà,
serving as the route for Cháoxiǎn's tribute missions.
Further to its south is Zhènjiāngbǎo Chéng City.
Furthermore, Liánshānguān Pass is also to its southeast.
) Dìngliáo Zuǒwèi and Dìngliáo Yòuwèi were both established in the eleventh month of the sixth year of Hóngwǔ.
Dìngliáo Qiánwèi was established in the second month of the eighth year of Hóngwǔ.
Dìngliáo Hòuwèi was originally Liáodōng Wèi,
established in the second month of the fourth year of Hóngwǔ.
It was renamed in the second month of the eighth year.
In the tenth month of the ninth year, its seat was moved to the north of Liáoyángchéng City,
and soon after reverted.
Dōngníng Wèi was originally the five *qiānhùsuǒ* of Dōngníng, Nánjīng, Hǎiyáng, Cǎohé, and Nǚzhí,
established in the thirteenth year of Hóngwǔ.
It was reorganized and established in the seventh month of the nineteenth year.
Zìzài Zhōu was established in the seventh year of Yǒnglè at Sānwàn Wèichéng City,
and later relocated.
The five Wèi and one Zhōu listed above,
are all administered within the city of the Dūsī.
Hǎizhōu Wèi: Originally Hǎizhōu,
in the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was established in the old Chéngzhōu city.
In the ninth year, a Wèi was established.
In the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year,
the Zhōu was abolished.
(To its southwest, it borders the sea,
with salt fields.
To its west is the Liáohé,
where the Húnhé and Tàizǐhé converge into the sea,
known as Sānchàhé.
Further west are the Nán and Běi Tōngjiāng,
which also join the Liáohé.
To its east is Dàpiànlǐng Guān,
with salt fields.
) It is one hundred and twenty lǐ northeast of the Dūsī.
Gàizhōu Wèi: (Originally Gàizhōu in the Yuán dynasty,
belonging to Liáoyáng Lù.)
It was abolished in the fourth year of Hóngwǔ.
In the sixth month of the fifth year, it was re-established.
In the tenth month of the ninth year, a Wèi was established.
In the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year,
the Zhōu was again abolished.
(To its northeast is Shíchéngshān.
Further north is Píngshān,
below which are salt fields.
Further east is Zhùbìshān,
to its west it borders the sea,
with Liányúndǎo,
on which there is a pass.
Further east is Níhé,
to its south is Qīnghé,
to its southeast is Bìlǐhé,
all their lower reaches flow into the sea.
Further south is Yǒngníng Jiānchéng,
established in the seventh year of Yǒnglè.
Further northwest is Liángfángkǒu Guān,
sea transport ships enter the Liáohé from here,
with salt fields nearby.
Further east is Shíménguān.
To its west are salt fields.
To its north are iron fields.)
It is two hundred and forty lǐ north of the Dūsī.
Fùzhōu Wèi: Originally Fùzhōu,
established in the old Fùzhōu city in the sixth month of the fifth year of Hóngwǔ.
In the ninth month of the fourteenth year, a Wèi was established.
In the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year,
the Zhōu was abolished.
(To its west it borders the sea.
To its southwest is Chángshēngdǎo.
Further south is Shāhé,
which joins Máhé,
flowing west into the sea.
To its east is Délìyíngchéng,
built by local people in the late Yuán dynasty,
in the second month of the fourth year of Hóngwǔ, Liáodōng Wèi was established here,
but soon moved.
Further south is Lègǔguān.
To its west are salt fields.
To its north are iron fields.)
It is four hundred and twenty lǐ north of the Dūsī.
Jīnzhōu Wèi: Originally Jīnzhōu,
established in old Jīnzhōu in the sixth month of the fifth year of Hóngwǔ.
In the fourth month of the eighth year, a Wèi was established.
In the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year,
the Zhōu was abolished.
(To its east is Dàhēishān,
from which Xiǎoshāhé flows out.
There is also Xiǎohēishān,
from which Luòmǎhé and Chéngshāhé both flow out.
The Wèi borders the sea on its east, west, and south sides.
To its south is Nánguāndǎo.
To its east is Liánhuādǎo.
To its southeast is Jīnxiàndǎo.
Further east is Pídǎo,
and also Chángxíngdǎo.
To its south are Shuāngdǎo and Sānshāndǎo.
To its southwest is Tiěshāndǎo.
To its northeast is Xiāojiādǎo,
with a pass.
Furthermore, Lǚshùnkǒu Guān is to the south,
sea transport ships land here,
there are two cities, south and north,
the northern city has the Zhōngzuǒ Qiānhùsuǒ,
established in the twentieth year of Hóngwǔ.
Further southeast is Wànghǎiguō Shíchéng,
established in the seventh year of Yǒnglè.
Furthermore, to the east of the Wèi are iron fields.
To its northeast are salt fields.)
It is six hundred lǐ north of the Dūsī.
Guǎngníng Wèi: (Originally Guǎngníng Fǔ Lù in the Yuán dynasty.)
It was abolished in the early Hóngwǔ reign.
In the fifth month of the twenty-third year, a Wèi was established.
(In the third month of the twenty-fifth year of Hóngwǔ, the Liáo Wáng Fǔ was built.
During the Jiànwén reign,
it was restyled as Húguǎng Jīngzhōu Fǔ.
To its west is Yīwúlǘshān.
To its south it borders the sea.
To its east is Lùhé,
to its northeast is Zhūzǐhé,
all their lower reaches flow into the Liáohé.
Furthermore, Bǎnqiáohé is to the west,
flowing south into the sea.
To its north is Báitǔchǎng Guān,
and also Fēnshuǐlǐng Guān.
To its northwest is Wèijiālǐng Guān.
Further north is Yìzhōu,
which belonged to Liáoyáng Lù in the Yuán dynasty.
In the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ, Guǎngníng Hòutún Wèi was established here.
In the eighth year of Yǒnglè,
the Zhōu was abolished,
and the Wèi was moved to Yìzhōu Wèichéng.
Further southwest is Lǘyáng Guān,
to its northeast is Wàngpíng Xiàn,
both belonged to Guǎngníng Lù in the Yuán dynasty.
Further northwest is Chuānzhōu,
which belonged to Dàníng Lù in the Yuán dynasty.
Further northeast is Shùnzhōu,
to its northwest is Chéngzhōu,
both belonged to Dōngníng Lù in the Yuán dynasty.
Further southwest is Zhōngxiùchéng,
where a Qiānhùsuǒ was established in the Yuán dynasty.
All were abolished during the Hóngwǔ reign.)
It is four hundred and twenty lǐ east of the Dūsī.
Guǎngníng Zhōng Wèi and Guǎngníng Zuǒ Wèi were both established in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ.
They were abolished in the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year.
In the eleventh month of the thirty-fifth year, they were re-established.
Guǎngníng Yòu Wèi: Originally administered Dàlínghé Bǎo,
established in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ.
It was abolished in the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year.
In the eleventh month of the thirty-fifth year, it was re-established.
The three *wèi* listed above
are all located in the *Guǎngníng Wèi* city.
The *Guǎngníng Qián Wèi* and *Guǎngníng Hòu Wèi* were both established in the first month of the 26th year of the Hóngwǔ reign.
Both were later abolished.
*Yìzhōu Wèi* (Yìzhōu in the Yuán dynasty
belonged to the Dàníng Circuit).
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
the prefecture was abolished.
The *wèi* was established in the eighth month of the 20th year.
(To the northwest is the Dàlínghé,
which flows into the sea downstream.
To the northeast is the Qīnghé,
which joins the Dàlínghé downstream.)
It is 540 *lǐ* southeast of the *Dūsī*.
*Guǎngníng Hòu Tún Wèi* was established in the first month of the 26th year of the Hóngwǔ reign in old Yìzhōu.
In the 8th year of the Yǒnglè reign, its seat was moved to *Yìzhōu Wèi* city.
*Guǎngníng Zhōng Tún Wèi* (Jǐnzhōu in the Yuán dynasty
belonged to the Dàníng Circuit).
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
the prefecture was abolished.
The *wèi* was established in the ninth month of the 24th year.
(To the east is Mùyè Shān.
To the west are Dōng Hóngluó Shān and Xī Hóngluó Shān.
To the southwest is Xìng Shān.
To the southeast is Rǔfēng Shān.
Further east are the Dàlínghé and Xiǎolínghé.
Further west is Nǚ'érhé,
which joins the Xiǎolínghé.
Further south is Sōngshān Bǎo,
located west of Sōngshān.
In the first month of the 5th year of the Xuāndé reign, the Zhōngzuǒ Qiānhù Suǒ was established here,
administering from Xìngshān Yì to Xiǎolínghé Yì.
To the east is Dàlínghé Bǎo.
In the first month of the 26th year of the Hóngwǔ reign, *Guǎngníng Yòu Wèi* was established here,
and abolished in the fourth month of the 28th year.
In the first month of the 5th year of the Xuāndé reign, the Zhōngyòu Qiānhù Suǒ was established here,
administering from Línghé Yì to Shísānshān Yì.
Further, south of the city are two salt fields
and one iron field.
Further west is an iron field.)
It is 600 *lǐ* southeast of the *Dūsī*.
*Guǎngníng Zuǒ Tún Wèi* was established in the ninth month of the 24th year of the Hóngwǔ reign west of the Liáohé,
and later moved to *Guǎngníng Zhōng Tún Wèi* city.
*Guǎngníng Yòu Tún Wèi* (the territory of Guǎngníng Fǔ in the Yuán dynasty).
In the first month of the 26th year of the Hóngwǔ reign, it was established at Shísānshān Bǎo.
In the 27th year, it moved to Línhǎi Xiāng of the old Lüyáng County.
(To the north are Shísān Shān.
West of the mountains is Shísānshān Bǎo.
To the west is the Dàlínghé.
Further southwest is Wàngméi Lǐng.
Further south is a salt field.
To the east is an iron field.)
It is 540 *lǐ* southeast of the *Dūsī*.
*Guǎngníng Qián Tún Wèi* (Ruìzhōu in the Yuán dynasty
belonged to the Dàníng Circuit).
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it belonged to Yǒngpíng Fǔ.
In the seventh month of the 7th year,
the prefecture was abolished.
The *wèi* was established in the first month of the 26th year.
(To the northwest are Wànsōng Shān.
To the north is Shíbāpán Shān.
To the west is Mázi Yù,
with an iron field.
To the southeast is Shānkǒu Yù,
with a salt field.
To the northeast is Liùzhōu Hé,
which flows into the sea at Shéshān Wù downstream.
To the west is Shānhǎi Guān,
bordering Fúníng County of Běizhí.
There is also Jíshuǐhé Bǎo.
In the first month of the 5th year of the Xuāndé reign, the Zhōngqián Qiānhù Suǒ was established here,
administering from Shānhǎi Dōngguān to Gāolǐng Yì.
Further east is Xìnglín Bǎo.
In the first month of the 5th year of the Xuāndé reign, the Zhōnghòu Qiānhù Suǒ was established here,
administering from Shāhé Yì to Dōngguān Yì.)
It is 960 *lǐ* east of the *Dūsī*.
*Níngyuǎn Wèi* was established in the first month of the 5th year of the Xuāndé reign by partitioning the territories of *Guǎngníng Qián Tún Wèi* and *Guǎngníng Zhōng Tún Wèi*,
with its seat at Tāngchí.
(To the northwest is Dàtuán Shān.
To the northeast is Chánglíng Shān.
To the south it borders the sea.
To the east is Táohuā Dǎo.
To the southeast is Juéhuá Dǎo city.
To the west is Níngyuǎn Hé,
which is also Nǚ'érhé,
also named Sānnǚ Hé.
Further east is Tǎ Shān,
with the Zhōngzuǒ Qiānhù Suǒ,
administering from Liánshān Yì to Xìngshān Yì.
To the west is the Xiǎoshāhé Zhōngyòu Qiānhù Suǒ,
administering from Dōngguān Yì to Cáozhuāng Yì.
Both were established in the first month of the 5th year of the Xuāndé reign.
Further south are two salt and iron fields.)
It is 770 *lǐ* east of the *Dūsī*.
*Shěnyáng Zhōng Wèi* (Shěnyáng Lù in the Yuán dynasty).
Abolished in the early Hóngwǔ reign.
The *wèi* was established in the intercalary fifth month of the 31st year.
(In the 24th year of the Hóngwǔ reign, the Shěn Wáng Fǔ was built.
In the 6th year of the Yǒnglè reign, it moved to Lùzhōu, Shānxī.
To the east is Dōngmóu Shān.
To the south is the Húnhé,
and further east, the Shěnhé flows into it.
Further west is the Liáohé.
Further northeast is the Fúshùn Qiānhù Suǒ,
established in the 21st year of the Hóngwǔ reign.
East of the *suǒ* is Fúshùn Guān.
Further north is the Púhé Qiānhù Suǒ,
also established in the 21st year of the Hóngwǔ reign.)
It is 120 *lǐ* south of the *Dūsī*.
*Shěnyáng Zuǒ Wèi* and *Shěnyáng Yòu Wèi* were both established in the Hóngwǔ reign.
Abolished in the early Jiànwén reign.
Re-established in the seventh month of the 35th year of the Hóngwǔ reign,
then again abolished.
*Shěnyáng Zhōng Tún Wèi* was established in the intercalary fifth month of the 31st year of the Hóngwǔ reign.
Abolished during the Jiànwén reign.
Re-established in the eleventh month of the 35th year of the Hóngwǔ reign,
it belonged to the Běipíng Dūsī,
later to the Hòujūn Dūdū Fǔ,
and was provisionally administered from Héjiān County, Běizhí.
*Tiělǐng Wèi* was established in the third month of the 21st year of the Hóngwǔ reign at the ancient Tiělǐng city.
In the fourth month of the 26th year, it moved to the territory of ancient Yīnzhōu,
which is its present seat.
(To the west is the Liáohé,
to the south is the Fànhé,
and further south is the Xiǎoqīnghé,
all flowing into the Liáohé.
Further south is Yìlù city.
In the 29th year of the Hóngwǔ reign, the Yìlù Qiānhù Suǒ was established here.
Fànhé city is south of the *wèi*,
also called Fànhé city.
In the 4th year of the Zhèngtǒng reign, the Fànhé Qiānhù Suǒ was established here.
To the southeast is Fèngjí County,
which is the ancient Tiělǐng city,
bordering Gāolí.
The county was established in the early Hóngwǔ reign,
then soon abolished.
There was also Xiánpíng Fǔ,
which in the Yuán dynasty was directly administered by the Liáodōng Xíngshěng.
In the first month of the 2nd year of the Zhìzhèng reign, it was demoted to a county.
Abolished in the early Hóngwǔ reign.)
It is 240 *lǐ* south of the *Dūsī*.
*Sānwàn Wèi* (Kāiyuán Lù in the Yuán dynasty).
Abolished in the early Hóngwǔ reign.
In the twelfth month of the 20th year, *Sānwàn Wèi* was established west of the old city,
concurrently establishing the Wùzhě Yěrén Qǐlímí Nǚzhēn Jūnmín Fǔ.
In the 21st year,
the *fǔ* was abolished,
and the *wèi* moved to Kāiyuán city.
(In the 24th year of the Hóngwǔ reign, the Hán Wáng Fǔ was built.
In the 22nd year of the Yǒnglè reign, it moved to Píngliáng, Shǎnxī.
To the northwest is Jīn Shān.
To the east is Fēnshuǐ Dōnglǐng.
To the north is Fēnshuǐ Xīlǐng.
To the west is the Dàqīnghé,
and to the east is the Xiǎoqīnghé,
which flow together
and downstream flow into the Liáohé.
Further north is the Shànghé,
and to the northeast is the Àihé,
which flow together,
called Liáohǎi,
which is the upper source of the Liáohé.
Further north is the Jīnshuǐhé,
which flows north into the Sōnghuā Jiāng outside the frontier.
Zhènběi Guān is to the northeast.
Guǎngshùn Guān is to the east.
Further west is Xīn'ān Guān.
To the southwest is Qīnghé Guān.
To the south is Shāntóu Guān.
Further north is Běichéng,
which is Niújiāzhuāng.
In the third month of the 23rd year of the Hóngwǔ reign, *Liáohǎi Wèi* was established here.
In the 26th year,
the *wèi* moved.
Further south is Zhōnggù City,
established in the 5th year of the Yǒnglè reign.)
It is 330 *lǐ* south of the *Dūsī*.
*Liáohǎi Wèi* was established in the third month of the 23rd year of the Hóngwǔ reign at Niújiāzhuāng.
In the 26th year, it moved to *Sānwàn Wèi* city.
*Ānlè Zhōu* was established in the 7th year of the Yǒnglè reign,
in *Sānwàn Wèi* city.
Shānxī. It was the domain of Jìzhōu in the Yǔ Gòng.
In the Yuán dynasty, the Hédōng Shānxī Dào Xuānwèi Shǐ Sī was established,
(with its seat in Dàtóng Lù.)
It was directly administered by the Zhōngshū Shěng.
In the fourth month of the second year of Hóngwǔ (1369), the Shānxī Děngchǔ Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng was established.
(Its seat was in Tàiyuán Lù.)
In the twelfth month of the third year (1370), the Tàiyuán Dūwèi was established.
(It shared the same seat as the Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng.)
In the tenth month of the eighth year (1375), the Dūwèi was renamed Shānxī Dū Zhǐhuīshǐ Sī.
In the sixth month of the ninth year (1376), the Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng was renamed Chéngxuān Bùzhèng Shǐ Sī.
It administered five fǔ,
three directly administered zhōu,
sixteen subordinate zhōu,
and seventy-nine xiàn.
(It comprised over four thousand four hundred lǐ.)
To the east, it reached Zhēndìng,
(bordering Běizhí.)
To the north, it reached Dàtóng,
(beyond which lay the frontier lands.)
To the southwest, it all reached the Hé (Yellow River),
(bordering Shǎnxī and Hénán.)
It was 2,400 lǐ from Nánjīng
and 1,200 lǐ from the Jīngshī (capital).
In the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ (1393), the registered households numbered 595,444,
with a population of 4,072,127.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì (1491),
there were 575,249 households,
with a population of 4,360,476.
In the sixth year of Wànlì (1578),
there were 590,097 households,
with a population of 5,319,359.
Tàiyuán Fǔ (formerly Jìníng Lù in the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to the Hédōng Shānxī Dào Xuānwèi Sī.)
In the twelfth month of the first year of Hóngwǔ (1368), it was renamed Tàiyuán Fǔ,
administering five zhōu
and twenty xiàn.
Yángqǔ (dependency.
In the fourth month of the third year of Hóngwǔ (1370), the Jìn Wáng Fǔ was built outside the city, to the northeast.
To the west is the Fén Shuǐ,
flowing from Jìnglè Xiàn through here,
its lower reaches joining the Dà Hé at Yínghé Xiàn.
To the northwest is the Tiānmén Guān Xúnjiǎnsī.
To the northeast is the Shílǐng Guān Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Tàiyuán (southwest of the fǔ.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was called Píngjìn,
its seat was to the northeast of the present location.
In the fourth year of Hóngwǔ (1371), it was moved to the west of the Fén Shuǐ,
to the southern gate of the former Jìnyáng city.
In the eighth year (1375), it was renamed Tàiyuán.
To the west is Xuánwèng Shān,
also known as Lóng Shān,
and also as Jiézhù Shān,
from which the Jìn Shuǐ originates,
flowing downstream into the Fén.
To the northwest is Méng Shān.
To the east is Fén Shuǐ.
To the southeast is Dòngwō Shuǐ,
its source is in Lèpíng,
flowing downstream into the Fén.)
Yúcì (southeast of the fǔ.
To the southeast is Tú Shuǐ,
entering Dòngwō Shuǐ.)
Tàigǔ (southeast of the fǔ.
To the southeast is Mǎlǐng,
On it is Mǎlǐng Guān,
with a Xúnjiǎnsī.
To the west is Tàigǔ,
also known as Xiányáng Gǔ.
To the northeast is Xiànggǔ Shuǐ,
flowing into the Fén.)
Qí (south of the fǔ,
slightly west.
To the southeast is Hújiǎ Shān,
from which Lóngzhōu Shuǐ originates,
flowing downstream to Píngyáo and entering the Fén.
To the south is Lóngzhōuyù Xúnjiǎnsī.
Further east is Tuánbǎi Zhèn.)
Xúgōu (south of the fǔ.
To the north is Dòngwō Shuǐ,
which joins the Fén here.)
Qīngyuán (southwest of the fǔ.
To the north is Qīngyuán Shuǐ,
flowing east,
and south into the Fén.)
Jiāochéng (southwest of the fǔ.
To the northeast is Yángcháng Shān.
To the southeast is Fén Shuǐ.
Further west is Wénshuǐ.)
Wénshuǐ (southwest of the fǔ.
To the southwest is Yǐnquán Shān.
flowing south into the Fén.
Further northeast is Yóu Shuǐ,
which some believe to be Wūzé.)
Shòuyáng (east of the fǔ.
To the west is Shāxióng Lǐng.
To the south is Dòngwō Shuǐ,
into which Hēishuǐ flows and merges.)
Méng (northeast of the fǔ.
It was Méng Zhōu in the Yuán dynasty.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ (1369), it was demoted to a xiàn.
To the northeast is Báimǎ Shān.
To the north is Hūtuó Hé,
flowing east into Píngshān Xiàn of Běizhí.
To the northeast is Fúmǎ Guān,
also known as Báimǎ Guān.
Further east is Yúzǎo Guān.)
Jìnglè (northwest of the fǔ.
It was Guǎndōng Zhōu in the Yuán dynasty.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ (1369), it was renamed Jìnglè Xiàn.
To the northeast is Guǎncén Shān,
from which Fén Shuǐ originates.
Further northeast is Yānjīng Shān,
with a Tiānchí (Heavenly Lake) on it.
Further north is Nínghuà Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ,
established in the second year of Hóngwǔ (1369).
Further southeast is Liǎnglǐng Guān,
where a Gùzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī was established,
later moved to Shùnshuǐ Cūn slightly to the east.
Further south is Lóufán Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.
Further northeast is Shāpólǐng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Tiānmén Guān in Yángqǔ Xiàn.)
Héqǔ (northwest of the fǔ.
It was abolished in the Yuán dynasty.
In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year of Hóngwǔ (1380), it was re-established.
To the west is Huǒ Shān,
facing the Dà Hé.
Along the river are Niángniáng Tān and Tàizǐ Tān,
both dangerous crossings of the river in the bend.
To the north is Guānhé,
named because it passes through Piāntóu Guān,
flowing northwest into the Dà Hé.
In the twelfth month of the eleventh year of Chénghuà (1475), Piāntóu Guān Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ was established,
making it one of the Sān Guān (Three Passes) along with Níngwǔ and Yànmén.)
Píngdìng Zhōu (To the east is Mián Shān,
from which Zéfā Shuǐ originates,
which is the upper source of Yě Hé. It joins Zhān Shuǐ,
flowing east to Píngshān Xiàn and entering Hūtuó.
To the southwest is Dòngwō Shuǐ,
which joins Fúhuà Shuǐ,
flowing west into the Fén.
To the southeast is Xīngù Guān Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ.
Further east is Gù Guān,
which is Jǐngxíng Guān.
In the third year of Hóngwǔ (1370), Gù Guān Xúnjiǎnsī was established here.
There are also Wěizé and Pánshí two passes to the east
and north of the xiàn,
both bordering Jǐngxíng Xiàn.)
It is 180 lǐ northwest of the fǔ.
It administers one xiàn.
Lèpíng (southeast of the zhōu.
To the east is Gāoluò Shān,
also known as Líng Shān.
To the southwest is Shào Shān,
also known as Zhānlǐng,
the source of Zhān Shuǐ and Qīngzhāng two waters.
Zhān flows east into Zéfā Shuǐ,
Zhāng flows north,
then turns southwest,
entering Liángyú Shuǐ in Héshùn Xiàn.
Further west is Dǒuchuán Lǐng,
where Dòngwō Shuǐ originates.
Also, Jìngyáng Zhèn is to the southeast of the xiàn.)
Xīn Zhōu (In the early Hóngwǔ period,
Xiùróng Xiàn, the seat of the zhōu, was merged into it.
(To the north is Hūtuó Hé,
and also Xīn Shuǐ,
also known as Sìlú Chuān,
flowing into it from the north.
To the southwest is Niúwěizhuāng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved ten lǐ north of the zhōu.
Further west is Zhàixī Xúnjiǎnsī,
to the northwest is Shāgōu Xúnjiǎnsī,
both were later abolished.
Also, Xīnkǒu Zhài is also north of the zhōu.
Further southeast is Chìtáng Guān.)
It is 160 lǐ south of the fǔ.
It administers one xiàn.
Dìngxiāng (east of the prefecture,
slightly north.
To the north is the Hūtuó Hé.
Further south is Cóngxiàng Shān,
where Sānhuì Shuǐ flows and converges.
To the northeast is Húgǔzhài Xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.)
Dàizhōu was demoted to a county in the second year of Hóngwǔ.
In the second month of the eighth year, it was re-promoted to a prefecture.
(Gōujù Shān is to the west,
also named Xīxíng,
also called Yànmén Shān.
To its north is Yànmén Guān,
where the
Yànmén Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ was established
in the tenth month of the twelfth year of Hóngwǔ.
Further, to the north of the pass, Guǎngwǔyíng Chéng was established.
Further east is Xiàwū Shān,
also named Xiàhú.
Further south is the Hūtuó Hé,
which originates from Fán
zhì and enters the prefectural boundary,
flowing southwest through Guō, Xīn, and Dìngxiāng,
then east through Wǔtái and Yú,
entering Zhēndìng's boundary.
Further north are Tàihélǐng and Shuǐqínkǒu two Xúnjiǎnsī,
both later abolished.)
Southwest
it is three hundred and fifty *lǐ* from the prefecture.
It administers three counties:
Wǔtái (southeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Táizhōu.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ, it was changed to Wǔtái Xiàn.
In the second month of the eighth year, it came under its jurisdiction.
To the northeast is Wǔtái Shān,
where the Qīngshuǐ Hé flows,
flowing northeast,
converging with the Sīyáng Hé,
and entering the Hūtuó Hé to the south.
Further southeast is Gāohóngkǒu Xúnjiǎnsī.
Further northeast are Dàgǔkǒu and Fànxiānshān two Xúnjiǎnsī,
both later abolished.)
Fánzhì (east of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Jiānzhōu.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ, it was changed to Fánzhì Xiàn.
In the second month of the eighth year, it came under its jurisdiction.
The old administrative seat was to the south of the county;
in the second month of the third year of Chénghuà, it was moved to Dōngyì Cūn.
In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Wànlì, it was relocated to Shílóng Gāng north of the river.
To the northeast is Qínxì Shān,
the source of the Hūtuó Hé,
which meanders one thousand three hundred and seventy *lǐ*,
reaching Jìnghǎi Xiàn in northern Zhílì and entering the sea.
Further north are Rúyuèkǒu, to the northeast is Běilóukǒu, and to the east is Píngxínglíng, three Xúnjiǎnsī,
all later abolished.
Further east is Lánglíng Guānchéng,
constructed in the seventeenth year of Hóngwǔ.)
Guō (southwest of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Guōzhōu.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ, it was demoted to a county.
In the second month of the eighth year, it came under its jurisdiction.
To the southwest is Guō Shān.
To the southeast is Shígǔ Shān,

Shānxī Xíngdū Zhǐhuī Sī (Shanxi Branch Regional Military Commission)
was originally the Dàtóng Dūwèi (Datong Commandery Guard), established in the first month of Hóngwǔ (洪武) 4th year (1371).
(Its seat was in Báiyángchéng (Baiyang City).)
In the tenth month of Hóngwǔ 8th year (1375), its name was changed.
In the eighth month of Hóngwǔ 25th year (1392), its seat was moved to Dàtóng Fǔ (Datong Prefecture).
In the second month of Hóngwǔ 26th year (1393), it administered twenty-six guards,
(Xuānfǔ Zuǒwèi (Xuanfu Left Guard) and Yòuwèi (Right Guard),
Wànquán Zuǒwèi (Wanquan Left Guard) and Yòuwèi (Right Guard),
and Huái'ān Wǔwèi (Huai'an Five Guards)
were later transferred to the Wànquán Dūsī (Wanquan Regional Military Commission).)
Later, it administered fourteen guards.
(Shuòzhōu Wèi (Shuozhou Guard) had its seat in the state city;
Āndōng Zhōngtúnwèi (Andong Central Garrison Guard) was temporarily seated in Yìngzhōu chéng (Yingzhou city).)
Dàtóng Qiánwèi (Datong Front Guard) was established in the second month of Hóngwǔ 7th year (1374),
sharing the same city as the Xíngdū Sī.
Dàtóng Hòuwèi (Datong Rear Guard) was established in the eighth month of Hóngwǔ 25th year (1392),
sharing the same city as the Xíngdū Sī,
but was soon abolished.
In the second month of Hóngwǔ 26th year (1393), it was re-established,
with its seat east of the Xíngdū Sī,
and later again moved to the Xíngdū Sī city.
(East of it was Jùluòchéng (Juluo City),
built in Tiānshùn (天順) 3rd year (1459).
In the ninth month of Jiājìng (嘉靖) 2nd year (1523), the Jùluò Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ (Juluo Defense Myriarchy) was established there,
and became subordinate to it.)
Dàtóng Zhōngwèi (Datong Central Guard) was established in the eighth month of Hóngwǔ 25th year (1392),
sharing the same city as the Xíngdū Sī,
but was later abolished.
Dàtóng Zuǒwèi (Datong Left Guard) was established in the eighth month of Hóngwǔ 25th year (1392),
sharing the same city as the Xíngdū Sī.
It was abolished in Hóngwǔ 35th year (1402).
In the ninth month of Yǒnglè (永樂) 1st year (1403), it was re-established.
In Yǒnglè 7th year (1409), its seat was moved to Zhènshuò Wèichéng (Zhenshuo Guard City).
Dàtóng Yòuwèi (Datong Right Guard) was established in the eighth month of Hóngwǔ 25th year (1392),
sharing the same city as the Xíngdū Sī.
It was abolished in Hóngwǔ 35th year (1402).
In the ninth month of Yǒnglè 1st year (1403), it was re-established.
In Yǒnglè 7th year (1409), its seat was moved to Dìngbiān Wèichéng (Dingbian Guard City).
Zhènshuò Wèi (Zhenshuo Guard) was established in the second month of Hóngwǔ 26th year (1393),
subordinate to the Xíngdū Sī.
In the second month of Yǒnglè 1st year (1403), its seat was moved to Běizhí Jìzhōu (Jizhou, Northern Zhili),
directly administered by the Hòujūn Dūdūfǔ (Rear Military Command).
Consequently, the guard city became vacant.
In Yǒnglè 7th year (1409), Dàtóng Zuǒwèi was moved to govern it.
In Zhèngtǒng (正統) 14th year (1449), Yúnchuān Wèi (Yunchuan Guard) was again moved to govern it concurrently.
(To the east is Diāolǐng Shān (Diaoling Mountain).

Collated Notes
Gazetteer Volume 18, Geography 3: Hénán, Shǎnxī
Hénán: The region of Yǔgòng's Yù, Jì, Yáng, and Yǎn four prefectures.
The Yuán dynasty placed the lands north of the Yellow River directly under the Zhōngshū Shěng,
and the lands south of the Yellow River under the Hénán Jiāngběi Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng.
(Its seat was Biànliáng Lù.)
In the fifth month of the first year of Hóngwǔ, a Zhōngshū Fēnshěng was established.
(Its seat was Kāifēng Fǔ.)
In the fourth month of the second year, the Fēnshěng was changed to Hénán Děngchù Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng.
In the twelfth month of the third year, the Hénán Dū Wèi was established.
In the tenth month of the eighth year, the Dū Wèi was changed to a Dū Zhǐhuīshǐ Sī.
In the sixth month of the ninth year, the Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng was changed to a Chéngxuān Bùzhèngshǐ Sī.
It administered eight prefectures (*fǔ*),
one directly administered department (*zhílì zhōu*),
eleven subordinate departments (*shǔ zhōu*),
and ninety-six counties (*xiàn*).
(It comprised 3,880-odd *lǐ*.)
North to Wǔ'ān,
(bordering Běizhí and Shānxī.)
South to Xìnyáng,
(bordering Jiāngnán and Húguǎng.)
East to Yǒngchéng,
(bordering Shāndōng and Jiāngnán.)
West to Shǎnzōu,
(bordering Shānxī and Shǎnxī.)
It is 1,175 *lǐ* from Nánjīng,
and 1,580 *lǐ* from the capital.
In the 26th year of Hóngwǔ, the census recorded 315,617 households,
and 1,912,542 people.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì,
there were 575,249 households,
and 4,360,476 people.
In the sixth year of Wànlì,
there were 630,067 households,
and 5,193,602 people.
Kāifēng Fǔ (formerly Biànliáng Lù in the Yuán dynasty,
belonging to Hénán Jiāngběi Xíngshěng.)
In the fifth month of the first year of Hóngwǔ, it was named Kāifēng Fǔ.
In the eighth month, Běijīng was established.
In the eleventh year,
the capital status was abolished.
It administered four departments (*zhōu*)
and thirty counties (*xiàn*).
Xiángfú (dependent.
In the first month of the eleventh year of Hóngwǔ, the Zhōu royal residence was established.
The Yellow River used to be north of the city.
In the thirteenth year of Zhèngtǒng,
the river breached in Xíngyáng,
flowing eastwards past the southwest of the city,
and thus the city was then north of the river.
To the east was Kāifēng Xiàn,
which in the Yuán dynasty was administered together within the city walls,
but was abolished in the Hóngwǔ era.
To the south is Zhūxiān Zhèn.
To the northeast is Chénqiáo Zhèn.)

South is Guóluèzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.
There is also the old Hángǔguān.
Further southwest is Hóngguān.
Wēnxīang (southwest of the *zhōu*.
Southeast is Kuāfùshān,
also known as Qínshān,
in which there is Dàgǔguān.
Its northern border is the river,
which flows in from Ruìchéng County in Shānxī,
and then southeast to Yǒngchéng County,
entering the border of Dàngshān County in Nánzhí.
West is Húshuǐ,
and Pánjiànshuǐ also flows north into it.
Further west is Tóngguān,
which borders Huáyīn County in Shǎnxī.
) Guīdé Fǔ (in the Yuán dynasty, it was directly subordinate to the Hénán Jiāngběi Xíngshěng.)
In the 5th month of the 1st year of Hóngwǔ, it was demoted to a *zhōu*
and belonged to Kāifēng Fǔ.
In the 6th month of the 24th year of Jiājìng, it was promoted to a prefecture.
It administers one *zhōu*
and eight counties.
It is three hundred and fifty *lǐ* west of the Bùzhèngsī.
Shāngqiū (dependent.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was called Suīyáng.
It was abolished in the early Hóngwǔ era.
In the 6th month of the 24th year of Jiājìng, it was re-established
and renamed.
Its old seat was in the south,
but in the 15th year of Hóngzhì, it was destroyed by the river.
In the 9th month of the 16th year, it was moved to its current seat.
Its northern border is the river.
After the Zhèngtǒng era,
the river burst its banks and flowed south.
The city was once north of the river,
but after the Zhèngdé era,
it remained south of the river.
North is Dīngjiādàokǒu Xúnjiǎnsī.
Southeast is Wǔjīnnguān Xúnjiǎnsī.
Nínglíng (west of the prefecture.
South is Suīshuǐ.
North is Táoyuánjí Xúnjiǎnsī.
Lùyì (south of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Bózhōu.
It was reassigned in the Hóngwǔ era.
South is Yǐngshuǐ,
and Cáihé flows in from the west,
known as Cáihékǒu,
which is the Shāhé of Shěnqiū County.
North is Wōshuǐ,
which flows east into the territory of Bózhōu in Nánzhí.
Xiàyì (east of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was called Xiàyì.
In the early Hóngwǔ era,
it was renamed.
Its northern border is the Great River.
Southeast is Suīshuǐ.
Yǒngchéng (southeast of the prefecture.
In the 5th month of the 1st year of Hóngwǔ, it belonged to Kāifēng Fǔ.
In the 11th month, it was reassigned here.
North are Dàngshān
and Mángshān,
both bordering Dàngshān County in Nánzhí.
Suīshuǐ and Kuàishuǐ are both south of the county.
South is Pàoshuǐ,
which silted up during the Hóngzhì era.
Yúchéng (northeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Jìníng Lù.
In the 1st month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, it was reassigned here.
South is the old city.
In the 9th year of Jiājìng, it was moved to its current seat.
North is the Yellow River.
) Suīzhōu (in the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Biànliáng Lù.)
In the early Hóngwǔ era,
it belonged to Kāifēng Fǔ,
and Xiāngyì County, the seat of the *zhōu*, was abolished and merged into it.
In the 5th month of the 10th year, it was demoted to a county.
In the 11th
month of the 13th year, it was re-promoted to a *zhōu*.
In the 6th month of the 24th year of Jiājìng, it was reassigned here.
(Its northern border is the river.
Suīshuǐ is also northeast of the *zhōu*.
) It is one hundred and seventy *lǐ* east of the prefecture.
It administers
two counties.
Kǎochéng (north of the *zhōu*.
It was abolished at the end of the Yuán dynasty.
In the 8th month of the 4th year of Hóngwǔ, it was re-established
and belonged to Kāifēng Fǔ.
In the 5th month of the 10th year, it was again abolished.
In the 11th month of the 13th year, it was re-established and belonged to the *zhōu*.
Its old seat was southeast of the county.
In the 13th year of Zhèngtǒng, it was moved.
Its northern border is the Great River.
Zhèchéng (southeast of the *zhōu*.
It was abolished at the end of the Yuán dynasty.
In the 8th month of the 4th year of Hóngwǔ, it was re-established
and belonged to Kāifēng Fǔ.
In the 5th month of the 10th year, it was abolished and merged into Nínglíng County.
In the 11th month of the 13th year, it was re-established
and belonged to the *zhōu*.
North is Suīshuǐ.
South is Wōshuǐ.
) Rǔníng Fǔ (in the Yuán dynasty, it was directly subordinate to the Hénán Jiāngběi Xíngshěng.)
In the early Hóngwǔ era,
it remained as such.
It administers two *zhōu*
and twelve counties.
It is four hundred and sixty *lǐ* from the Bùzhèngsī.
Rǔyáng (dependent.
In the 3rd month of the 1st year of Tiānshùn, Xiùwáng Fǔ was established.
In the 8th year of Chénghuà, it was abolished.
In the 10th year, Chóngwáng Fǔ was established.
In the early Hóngwǔ era,
the county was abolished.
In the 7th month of the 4th year, it was re-established.
North is Rǔshuǐ,
its source is Tiānxīshān,
it flows east into the territory,
and passes Xīncài southeast into the Huái.
South is Yìshuǐ,
and also Wènshuǐ,
and also Qínshuǐ,
and northwest is Qìnshuǐ,
popularly known as Níhé,
the lower reaches of all of which flow into the Rǔ.
South of the city is Cháitán.
East is Yángbù Xúnjiǎnsī.
Zhēnyáng (east of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Xīzhōu.
In the 4th year of Hóngwǔ, it was abolished and merged into Rǔyáng County.
In the 4th year of Jǐngtài, Zhēnyángzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī was established here.
In the 12th month of the 18th year of Hóngzhì, the county was re-established,
and the Xúnjiǎnsī was moved to Tóngzhōngdiàn south of the county,
retaining its old name,
but was soon abolished.
South is Huáishuǐ.
Rǔshuǐ is east of the county,
and Diānshuǐ flows into it from the north.
Shàngcài (north of the prefecture.
It was abolished in the early Hóngwǔ era.
In the 5th month of the 4th year, it was re-established.
West is Rǔshuǐ,
and Shāshuǐ flows from the southwest to join it.
Xīncài (east of the prefecture,
a little to the south.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Xīzhōu,
and was later abolished.
In the 5th month of the 4th year of Hóngwǔ, it was re-established
and reassigned.
South is Rǔshuǐ,
and Yìshuǐ flows from north of the city to join it.
Northeast is Wǎdiàn Xúnjiǎnsī.
Xīpíng (northwest of the prefecture.
North is Rǔshuǐ,
its source is the two mountains of Yúnzhuāng and Zhūshí southwest of the county.
Since the old Rǔ was dammed at the end of the Yuán dynasty,
this water became the source of the Rǔ.
In the 9th year of Jiājìng, it was again blocked,
and was changed to the upper reaches of Hónghé.
Quèshān (southwest of the prefecture.
In the fifth month of the 10th year of Hóngwǔ, it was abolished and merged into Rǔyáng County.
In the 11th month of the 13th year, it was re-established.
In the ninth month of the 11th year of Chénghuà, it was transferred to Xìnyáng Zhōu.
In the eighth month of the second year of Hóngzhì, it was again made subordinate to the prefecture.
To the northwest is Lǎngshān,
also called Lèshān.
To the north is the Huángyǒu River,
whose lower course is the Liàn River,
flowing into the Rǔ River.
Further west is the Zhúgōu Patrol and Inspection Station.
To the south is the Mínggǎng Patrol and Inspection Station.
Suípíng (west of the prefecture,
a little to the north.
To the southwest is Cháyá Shān,
and to its southeast, connecting it, is Mǎ'ānshān.
Further west is Hóngshān,
from which the source of Lóngpí emerges.
Since the waters from the various mountains of Yúnzhuāng in Xīpíng County were blocked,
this was consequently taken as the source of the Rǔ River.
To the south is the Quí River,
and also the Shā River.
Further north is the Shíyáng River,
whose lower courses all flow into the Rǔ River.
Xìnyáng Zhōu (In the Yuán dynasty, it was Xìnyáng County,
subordinate to Xìnyáng Zhōu,
which was later abolished.
)In the tenth month of the first year of Hóngwǔ, Xìnyáng Zhōu was established here,
subordinate to the Hénán Sub-province.
In the second month of the fourth year, it was subordinate to the Zhōngdū Línháo Prefecture.
In the eighth month of the seventh year, its subordination was changed.
In the fifth month of the 10th year, it was demoted to a county.
In the ninth month of the 11th year of Chénghuà, it was again promoted to a zhōu.
(To the southwest is Xiánshǒu Shān.
To the south is Shìyǎ Shān,
and also Xiànshān.
To the southeast is Shíchéng Shān,
also called Míngshān.
To the north is the Huái River,
and further south is the Shī River flowing into it.
)It is 270 lí northeast of the prefecture.
It administers one county.
Luóshān (east of the zhōu.
It was the seat of Xìnyáng Zhōu in the Yuán dynasty;
later both the zhōu and county were abolished.
In the tenth month of the first year of Hóngwǔ, the zhōu was established at the old Xìnyáng County,
and Luóshān County was re-established and made subordinate to it.
In the fifth month of the 10th year, it was directly subordinate to Rǔníng Fǔ.
In the ninth month of the 11th year of Chénghuà, it was returned to the zhōu.
To the north is the Huái River,
and further south the Xiǎohuáng River flows into it.
To the southeast is the Dàshèngguān Patrol and Inspection Station,
bordering Húguǎng's Huángpí.
To the southwest is Jiǔlǐguān,
also known as Huángxiànguān,
one of the three passes of Yìyáng,
with a Patrol and Inspection Station,
bordering Húguǎng's Yìngshān County.
Guāng Zhōu: In the early Hóngwǔ era,
Dìngchéng County, the seat of the zhōu, was abolished and merged into it.
In the second month of the fourth year, it was transferred to the Zhōngdū Línháo Prefecture.
In the 13th year, it returned to its former subordination.
(To the north is the Huái River.
Further south is the Huáng River,
flowing north into the Huái River.
To the southwest is Yīnshānguān.
)It is 300 lí northwest of the prefecture.
It administers four counties.
Guāngshān (southwest of the zhōu.
To the south is Shípán Shān.
To the north it borders the Huái River.
To the south is the Huáng River,
also called Guāndùhé.
Further south is Mùlíngguān.
To the southwest are also five passes: Báishā, [一０]Tǔmén, Dòumùlǐng, Huángtǔlǐng, and Xiūshànchōng,
bordering Húguǎng's Máchéng County.
To the southeast is the Niúshānzhèn Patrol and Inspection Station,
later moved to Chángtán.
There was also the Shāwōzhèn Patrol and Inspection Station,
later abolished.
Gùshǐ (northeast of the zhōu.
To the south is Báilùyá.
To the north it borders the Huái River.
To the east is the Shǐ River,
to the west is the Pì River,
both entering the border of Nánzhí Huòqiū County,
and their lower courses flow into the Huái River.
Further northeast is Zhūgāo Zhèn,
bordering Nánzhí Yǐng Zhōu,
with a Patrol and Inspection Station.
Xī (northwest of the zhōu.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Xī Zhōu.
In the second month of the fourth year of Hóngwǔ, it was subordinate to the Zhōngdū Línháo Prefecture.
Soon it was demoted to a county,
subordinate to Yǐng Zhōu.
In the seventh year, it returned to its former subordination.
To the south it borders the Huái River.
To the northeast is the Rǔ River.
To the north is the Yángzhuāngdiàn Patrol and Inspection Station,
later moved to Gùchéngcāng northeast of the county.
Shāngchéng (southeast of the zhōu.
In the fourth month of the 11th year of Chénghuà, it was established from parts of Gùshǐ County.
To the south is Jīngāngtái Shān.
Further southeast is Zhúgēn Shān.
To the east is Dàsū Shān,
from which the Guàn River flows,
entering Nánzhí Huòqiū County.
Further east is the Niúshān River,
which is the upper source of the Shǐ River.
To the southwest is the Wǔshuǐguān River.
Further south are the Wǔ Rivers,
whose lower courses all flow into the Shǐ River.
Further south is the Jīngāngtái Patrol and Inspection Station,
originally located below Jīngāngtái Shān.
In the 27th year of Jiājìng, it was moved to Shuǐdōng'àn southeast of the county.
Further south is Chánglǐngguān,
and to the southeast is Sōngzǐguān,
both bordering Húguǎng's Luótián County.
) Nányáng Fǔ (In the Yuán dynasty, it was directly subordinate to Hénán Jiāngběi Xíngshěng.
)In the early Hóngwǔ era,
it remained so.
It administers two zhōu
and 11 counties.
It is 680 lí from the Bùzhèngsī.
Nányáng (the administrative seat.
In the 24th year of Hóngwǔ, the Táng Wáng Fǔ was built.
To the south of the city is Jīngshān.
To the north are Bǎichóngshān and Zhìhéngshān.
There is also Fēnshuǐlǐng,
whose waters flow north into the Rǔ River,

To the southwest is Wòlónggāng.
To the east is the Yù River,

To the southwest is the Tuān River,
and to the northwest is the Ěr River,
both flowing into the Yù River.
Zhènpíng (west of the prefecture.
In the fifth month of the 10th year of Hóngwǔ, it was abolished and merged into Nányáng County.
In the 11th month of the 13th year, it was re-established.
To the northwest is Wǔduǒshān,
which produces copper.
To the east is the Láohé,
flowing into the Yùhé.
Táng (southeast of the prefecture.

To the northeast is Dàhúshān, [一０]also called Húshān,

and also the Mì River,
whose lower courses all flow into the Yù River.
Further northeast is Shíjiákǒuguān.
Bìyáng (east of the prefecture.

In the second month of the second year of Hóngwǔ, it was abolished and merged into the zhōu.
In the 11th month of the 13th year,
the zhōu was abolished,
and the county was re-established.
To the east is Tóngshān,
from which the Mì River flows.
Further north is the Wǔ River,

with a Patrol and Inspection Station.
Tóngbó (southeast of the prefecture.

Further east is Dàfù Shān.
To the northwest is Tāizān Shān,
from which the Huái River originates.
Further west is the Lǐ River,
also called the Lǐ River,
whose lower course flows into the Mì River.
Nánzhào (north of the prefecture seat.
In the 12th month of the 12th year of Chénghuà (1476), it was established from the Nánzhào Fort in Nányáng County.
To its north is Dānxiá Mountain,
also known as Liú Mountain.
To its north is Lǔyáng Pass,
which is also the Sānyā Lùkǒu,
bordering Lǔshān County.

Dèngzhōu (in the Yuán dynasty, it administered Ráng County.
) In the 2nd month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ (1369),
the county was abolished.
In the 11th month of the 13th year (1380), the county was re-established.
In the 5th month of the 14th year (1381), it was again merged into the prefecture.
(To its south is Xīwēi Mountain.
To its northwest is Báiyá Mountain.
To its north is the Tuān River,
and further east is the Niè River,
also known as the Zhào River,
which flows in from the north.

It administers three counties.
Nèixiāng (north of the prefecture,
a little to the west.
To its east is Xióng'ěr Mountain,
from which the Tuān River originates.
To its southwest is the Xī River,
and also the Dān River.
Further north is Jútán.
To its northeast was the Jīndǒu Shān Xúnjiǎnsī,
which was later abolished.
To its northwest is the Xīxiákǒu Guān Xúnjiǎnsī.
To its southwest is Dǎngzǐkǒu Guān.
Further west is Wǔguān,
where the road leads out to Shāngzhōu in Shǎnxī.
Xīnyě (southeast of the prefecture.
To its west are the Qīng River
and the Tuān River;
further north is the Bǐ River;
to its east is the Jí River,
all of which flow into the Yù River.
Xīchuān (west of the prefecture.
It was established in the 6th year of Chénghuà (1470) from a part of Nèixiāng County.
To its southeast is Tàibái Mountain.
There is also Dānyá Mountain.
To its east is the Jūn River,
and further southwest are the Xī River
and the Dān River, all flowing into it,
and then south into the Hàn River.
To its northwest are Huāyuántóu Xúnjiǎnsī
and Jīngzǐkǒu Guān.
Further west is Xiákǒuzhèn,
connecting to Yùzhōu in Húguǎng to the south.)
In the early Hóngwǔ era, Fāngchéng County, where the prefecture seat was located, was merged into it.
(To its northeast is Fāngchéng Mountain,
from which the Zhǔ River originates,
flowing downstream into the Bǐ River.
) It is 120 *lǐ* southwest of the prefecture seat.
It administers two counties.
Wǔyáng (northeast of the prefecture.
The Rǔ River is north of the county,
formerly flowing into the border of Xīpíng County.
At the end of the Yuán dynasty, a weir was built at the Wō River to block its flow,
making it flow east to the Yǐng River,
and the water in Xīpíng then branched off to become the Rǔyuán.
To its south are the Wǔ River,
also called the Wǔ River,
and the Qìn River,
the lower reaches of both flowing into the Rǔ River in Rǔníng Fǔ.
To its southwest is the Shā River,
which is the Yē River.
Further north is the Lǐ River,
the lower reaches returning to the old Rǔ River.
Yè (north of the prefecture,
a little to the east.
To its north is Huángchéng Mountain,
also called Chángchéng Mountain,
and there is the Rǔ River.
Further north is the Zhàn River,
which flows into the Rǔ River.
To its northeast is the Shā River,
also called the Yē River,
and also called the Zhī River.
Further north, the Kūn River flows into it,
and its lower reaches flow into the Rǔ River.
Further north is Kūnyáng Pass.

directly under the Zhōngshūshěng.)
In the 10th month of the 1st year of Hóngwǔ (1368), it became a prefecture,
subordinate to the Hénán Fēnshěng.
It administers six counties.
It is 300 *lǐ* southeast of the Bùzhèngsī.
Hénèi (adjacent.
In the 22nd year of Yǒnglè (1424), the Wèi King's Palace was built.
In the 3rd year of Zhèngtǒng (1438), it was abolished.
In the 8th year (1443), the Zhèng King's Palace moved here from Fèngxiáng Fǔ in Shǎnxī.
To its north is the Tàiháng Mountain,
and also Wǎnzǐchéng Mountain,
which has a pass.
There is also the Qìn River,
originating in Qìnyuán County, Shānxī,
flowing into the prefecture's territory,
and its lower reaches enter the Dàhé at Wǔzhì.
There is also the Dān River,
flowing in from Zézhōu,
and emptying into the Qìn River.
Further west is Báixiāngchéng,
built in the 4th year of Chóngzhēn (1631).
Jìyuán (west of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Mèngzhōu.
In the 5th month of the 10th year of Hóngwǔ (1377), it was transferred to the prefecture.
To its south, it borders the Dàhé.
To its west is Wángwū Mountain,
connecting to the border of Yuánqǔ County, Shānxī,
from which the Jì River originates.
To its northwest is Cóng Mountain,
from which the Xiù River originates.
Further northeast is the Qìn River,
flowing between the two mountains,
also called the Fāngkǒu River.
Further northwest is Zhǐ Pass.
[一二]To its west is Shàoyuánzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.
Xiūwǔ (east of the prefecture,
a little to the north.
To its west is the Qìn River.
Wǔzhì (east of the prefecture.

To its east is the Qìn River,
entering it at Nánjiǎkǒu.
Further northeast is Liánhuāchí;
in the 15th year of Wànlì (1587),
the Qìn River breached here.
Further northwest is Níngguōchéng,
built during the Jǐngtài era.
Mèng (south of the prefecture,
a little to the west.
In the Yuán dynasty, Mèngzhōu.
In the early Hóngwǔ era,
Héyáng County, where the prefecture seat was located, was merged into it.
In the 5th month of the 10th year (1377), it was downgraded to a county.
To its southwest, it borders the Dàhé.
Wēn (southeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Mèngzhōu.
In the 5th month of the 10th year of Hóngwǔ (1377), it was transferred to the prefecture.
To its south, it borders the Dàhé;
the Xiù River flows into it from the northwest.
Further southwest is the Jì River,
which formerly flowed from Jìyuán County through Yǎnhézhèn,
and emptied south into the River;

directly under the Zhōngshūshěng.)

In the 10th month, it was subordinate to the Hénán Fēnshěng.

Jí (adjacent.
In the 8th month of the 4th year of Hóngzhì (1491), the Rǔ King's Palace was built.
In the 20th year of Jiājìng (1541), it was abolished.
In the 2nd month of the 5th year of Lóngqìng (1571), the Lù King's Palace was built.

Zuòchéng (east of the prefecture,
a little to the south.

In the 11th month of the 13th year (1380), it was re-established.
Xīnxiāng (southwest of the prefecture.

To its northwest is the Qīng River.

To its west is the ancient Qìn River;
after the 13th year of Yǒnglè (1415),
it would sometimes breach and sometimes dry up.
Huòjiā (west of the prefecture,
a little to the south.
In the fifth month of Hongwǔ 10 (1377), it was abolished and merged into Xīnxiāng County.
In the eleventh month of Hongwǔ 13 (1380), it was re-established.
The Yellow River used to be south of the county.
In the middle of Tianshùn 6 (1462),
the river shifted from Wǔzhì to Yuánwǔ,
and the flow within the county's boundaries ceased.
To the north is the Qīngshǔi River,
and the Xiǎodānhé River joins it.
Qí (north of the prefecture.
It was Qí Prefecture in the Yuan dynasty,
later abolished.
In the ninth month of Hongwǔ 1 (1368), it was re-established.
In the twelfth month, it was demoted to a county.
To the northwest is the Qíshǔi River,
and the Qīngshǔi River flows into it from the northeast,
then flows down into the Wèihé River.
Huī (northwest of the prefecture.
It was Huī Prefecture in the Yuan dynasty,
later abolished.
In the ninth month of Hongwǔ 1 (1368), it was re-established.
In the twelfth month, it was demoted to a county.
To the west are the Tàiháng Mountains.
To the northwest is Báilù Mountain.
There is also Sūmén Mountain,
also named Bǎimén Mountain.
On the mountain is Bǎimén Spring,
its waters flowing through a hundred channels.
Its lower course forms the Wèishǔi River,
hence it is also named Wèiyuán.
To the southwest is also the Qīngshǔi River.
To the northwest are the Hóuzhàochuān and Xīyāzǐkǒu sub-prefectural police stations.
)Zhāngdé Prefecture (It was Zhāngdé Circuit in the Yuan dynasty,
directly administered by the Central Secretariat.
)In the intercalary seventh month of Hongwǔ 1 (1368), it became a prefecture.
In the tenth month, it belonged to the Henan Branch Province.
It administered one zhou [prefecture]
and six counties.
It is 360 li south of the Provincial Administration Commission.
Ānyáng (Its seat.
In the fourth month of Yonglè 2 (1404), the Prince of Zhào's palace was built.
At the end of the Yuan dynasty,
the county was abolished.
In the ninth month of Hongwǔ 1 (1368), it was re-established.
To the northeast is Hánlíng Mountain.
To the northwest is Tóng Mountain,
which formerly produced copper.
To the north is the Ānyánghé River,
originally named Huánshuǐ,
and entering the Wèihé River at Nèihuáng County in Beizhí.
Also to the north is the Zhuózhāngshuǐ River.
)Línzhāng (northeast of the prefecture.
Abolished at the end of the Yuan dynasty.
In the ninth month of Hongwǔ 1 (1368), it was re-established.
To the west are the Qīng and Zhuó Zhāngshuǐ Rivers,
which merge here,
named Jiāozhāngkǒu,
and enter the Beizhí area.
There is also the Fùshuǐ River,
its lower course flowing into the Zhānghé River.
To the southwest is also the Huánshuǐ River.
)Tāngyīn (south of the prefecture.
Abolished at the end of the Yuan dynasty.
In the ninth month of Hongwǔ 1 (1368), it was re-established.
To the west is the Dàngshuǐ River,
passing north of the county seat,
and its lower course flows into the Wèishǔi River.
)Lín (west of the prefecture,
a little to the south.
It was Lín Prefecture in the Yuan dynasty,
later abolished.
In the ninth month of Hongwǔ 1 (1368), it was re-established.
In the fourth month of Hongwǔ 2 (1369), it was demoted to a county.
To the northwest is Lónglǜ Mountain,
also called Línlǜ,
from which the Huánshuǐ River originates.
To the southwest is Tiānpíng Mountain.
To the west are the Tàiháng Mountains.
Also to the north is the Zhuózhāngshuǐ River,
flowing in from Píngshùn County in Shanxi.
)Cí Prefecture (In the Yuan dynasty, its seat was Fúyáng County,
belonging to Guǎngpíng Circuit.
Later both the prefecture and county were abolished.
)In the eleventh month of Hongwǔ 1 (1368), the prefecture was re-established,
belonging to Guǎngpíng Prefecture.
In the fourth month of Hongwǔ 2 (1369), it came under this administration.
(To the west
and north is Shénjūn Mountain,
from which the Fùshuǐ River originates.
To the south is also the Qīngzhāngshuǐ River.
To the north is the Chēqíguān sub-prefectural police station.
)It is 70 li south of the prefecture.
It administered two counties.
Wǔ'ān (northwest of the prefecture.
Abolished at the end of the Yuan dynasty.
In the eleventh month of Hongwǔ 1 (1368), it was re-established.
To the southeast is Fù Mountain,
from which the Fùshuǐ River originates.
To the southwest is Cí Mountain,
which produces lodestone.
To the northeast is the Mínghé River,
flowing into the Hándān County area of Beizhí.
To the west is also the Gùzhèn sub-prefectural police station.
)Shè (west of the prefecture,
a little to the north.
In the Yuan dynasty, it belonged to Zhēndìng Circuit,
later abolished.
In the eleventh month of Hongwǔ 1 (1368), it was re-established,
belonging to Zhēndìng Prefecture.
In the fourth month of Hongwǔ 2 (1369), it came under this administration.
To the south is the Shèshuǐ River,
which is the Qīngzhāngshuǐ River,
flowing in from Líchéng County in Shanxi.
To the northeast is also the Piāndiàn sub-prefectural police station,
later moved to Wú'éryùkǒu southwest of the county.
)Rǔ Prefecture (In the Yuan dynasty, it belonged to Nányáng Prefecture.
)At the beginning of Hongwǔ,
Liáng County, the seat of the prefecture, was abolished and merged into it.
In the ninth month of Chénghuà 12 (1476), it was directly administered by the Provincial Administration Commission.
(To the southeast is Huò Mountain.
There is also Yúchǐ Mountain,
from which the Shèshuǐ River originates,
entering Yè County.
To the southwest is also Mínggāo Mountain.
There is also Kōngtóng Mountain.
To the south is the Rǔshuǐ River.
To the west is Guǎngchéng Marsh.
It is 490 li northeast of the Provincial Administration Commission.
Lǔshān (southwest of the prefecture.
To the east is Lǔ Mountain.
To the west is Yáoshān Mountain,
where the Pòshǔi River originates,
and to the southwest the Bōshuǐ River flows into it.
To the northwest is also the Xiēmǎlíngguān sub-prefectural police station.
)Jiá (east of the prefecture,
a little to the south.
To the southeast is the Rǔshuǐ River,
and to the west the Hùjiànshuǐ River flows into it.
)Bǎofēng (southeast of the prefecture.
In the fourth month of Chénghuà 11 (1475), it was established by separating land from Rǔ Prefecture.
To the south are the Rǔshuǐ River
and also the Pòshuǐ River.
)Yīyáng (west of the prefecture,
a little to the south.
In the twelfth month of Chénghuà 12 (1476), it was established from the former Yīquè County of Rǔ Prefecture,
and land from Sōng and Lǔshān counties was added.
To the west is Yīyáng Mountain.
There is also Yáoshān Mountain,
which is also Tiānxī Mountain.
On it is the Fēnshuǐlíng watershed,
from which the Pòshǔi River originates,
commonly known as Shāshuǐ.
To the south is also the Rǔshuǐ River.
To the west is the Yīshuǐ River.
To the southwest is the Shàngdiànzhèn sub-prefectural police station,
moved to Chángjièlǐng in the twelfth month of Chénghuà 12 (1476).
There was also the Pǔjiùguān sub-prefectural police station,
now defunct.
Shǎnxī province was the territory of Yǔgòng's Yōng and Liáng provinces.
In the Yuán dynasty, the Shǎnxī-etc. Branch Secretariat
(whose seat was Fèngyuán Circuit)
and the Gānsù-etc. Branch Secretariat
(whose seat was Gānzhōu Circuit) were established.
In the 4th month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ (1369), the Shǎnxī-etc. Branch Secretariat was established.
(Its seat was Xī'ān Prefecture.)
In the 12th month of the 3rd year (1370), the Xī'ān Metropolitan Guard was established.
(It shared the same seat as the Branch Secretariat.)
In the 10th month of the 8th year (1375), the Metropolitan Guard was renamed the Shǎnxī Provincial Military Commission.
In the 6th month of the 9th year (1376), the Branch Secretariat was renamed the Provincial Administration Commission.
It administered 8 prefectures,
21 dependent departments,
and 95 counties.
(There were 3,597 *li*.)
To the east, it reached Huàyīn,
(bordering HéNán and Shānxī.)
To the south, it reached Zǐyáng,
(bordering Húguǎng and Sìchuān.)
To the north, it reached Hétào,
and to the west, Sùzhōu.
(Beyond these were frontier lands.)
It was 2,430 *li* from Nánjīng
and 2,650 *li* from the capital.
In the 26th year of Hóngwǔ (1393), the registered households numbered 294,526,
〔一五〕with a population of 2,316,569.
In the 4th year of Hóngzhì (1491),
households numbered 306,644,
with a population of 3,912,370.
In the 6th year of Wànlì (1578),
households numbered 394,423,
with a population of 4,502,067.
Xī'ān Prefecture (originally Fèngyuán Circuit in the Yuán dynasty,
belonging to the Shǎnxī Branch Secretariat)
was renamed Xī'ān Prefecture in the 3rd month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ (1369).
It administered 6 departments
and 31 counties.
Cháng'ān (the provincial capital,
whose seat was in the western part.
In the 4th month of the 3rd year of Hóngwǔ (1370), the Qín Prince's Mansion was built.
To the north is Lóngshǒushān.
To the south is Zhōngnánshān.
To the southwest is Tàiyīshān,
and also the Zǐwǔgǔ valley,
which contains a pass.
To the north is the Wèishuǐ river,
whose source is in Niǎoshǔshān.
It flows through the county,
and enters the Huánghé at Huàyīn.
To the west is the Fēngshuǐ river.
To the northwest is the Hàoshuǐ river,
which converges with the Biāoshuǐ river.
〔一六〕To the south is the Juéshuǐ river,
also called the Xuèshuǐ river,
which converges with the Làoshuǐ river.
All flow north into the Wèi river.)
Xiánníng (the provincial capital,
whose seat was in the eastern part.
The Wèishuǐ river is to the south.
To the east is the Chǎnshuǐ river,
which converges with the Bàshuǐ river and flows into the Wèi river.)
Xiányáng (northwest of the prefecture.
Its old seat was north of the Wèi river;
in the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ (1369) it was moved south of the Wèi river.
To the northeast is the Jīngshuǐ river,
which flows east into the Wèi river.
To the southeast is the Fēngshuǐ river,
which flows north into the Wèi river.)
Jīngyáng (north of the prefecture.
To the northwest is Gānquánshān.
To the south is the Jīngshuǐ river,
whose source is in Qiāntóushān.
It flows through the county,
and enters the Wèi river at Gāolíng county.
To the north is the Yěgǔshuǐ river,
which converges with the Qīnggǔshuǐ river,
and flows down into the Wèi river.)
Xīngpíng (west of the prefecture,
slightly to the north.
To the south is the Wèishuǐ river.)
Líntóng (east of the prefecture,
slightly to the north.
To the southeast is Líshān,
which has hot springs.
To the north is the Wèishuǐ river.
To the west is the Tóngshuǐ river,
and to the east is the Xìshuǐ river.
Both flow north into the Wèi river.
To the east is the Língshuǐ river,
also called Língshuǐ,
which also enters the Wèi river at Língkǒuzhèn.
To the south is Yányì,
which historically produced salt.)
Wèinán (east of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty it belonged to Huàzhōu.
In the 11th month of the 38th year of Jiājìng (1559), it was transferred to the prefecture.
To the north is the Wèishuǐ river.)
Lántián (southeast of the prefecture.
To the south is Qīpánshān.
Nearby is the "●" slope,
known as the "Seven Pans and Twelve ●s,"
a perilous path to Lán Guān.
There is also Yáoshān.
To the southeast is Lántiánshān,
which has a pass.
To the west is the Bàshuǐ river,
to the northwest is the Chángshuǐ river,
also called Jīngxī,
and to the south is the Wǎnggǔshuǐ river,
also called Wǎngchuān.
All flow into the Bàshuǐ river.)
Hù (southwest of the prefecture.
To the south is Niúshǒushān,
where the Làoshuǐ river originates.
To the north is the Wèishuǐ river.
To the southwest is Gānquán,
and to the west is Měibēi.
Both converge with the Làoshuǐ river
and flow into the Wèi river.
The Fēngshuǐ river is to the south,
converging with the waters of Gāoguāngǔ and Tàipínggǔ,

Zhōuzhì (southwest of the prefecture.
To the southwest is Luògǔ valley.
The valley is 420 *li* long,
and there is a pass at its mouth.
Within the valley are the patrol and inspection stations of Shíbāpán and Cháijiāguān.
To the north is the Wèishuǐ river.
To the south is the Lóngshuǐ river,
and to the southwest, the Hēishuǐ river flows into it.
To the east is the Luògǔshuǐ river,
and to the southeast is the Mángshuǐ river.
Both flow north into the Wèi river.)
Gāolíng (northeast of the prefecture.
To the southwest is the Wèishuǐ river,
and the Jīngshuǐ river flows from the northwest to converge with it.)
Fùpíng (northeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty it belonged to Yàozhōu.
In the 36th year of Wànlì (1608), it was transferred to the prefecture.
To the southwest is Jīngshān.
To the northwest is the Qījuānshuǐ river,
which historically flowed south of Báishuǐ county into the Luò river.
Since the Zèngqú canal was dammed and abandoned,

To the northeast was the Měiyuán Patrol and Inspection Station,
which was later abolished.)
Sānyuán (north of the prefecture,
slightly to the east.
In the Yuán dynasty it belonged to Yàozhōu.
In the 11th month of the 3rd year of Hóngzhì (1490), it was transferred to the prefecture.
To the northwest is Yáoménshān.
To the northeast is the Qījuānshuǐ river.
To the west is the Qīngshuǐ river,
whose lower course flows into the Wèi river.)
Lǐquán (northwest of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty it belonged to Gānzhōu.
In the 11th month of the 38th year of Jiājìng (1559), it was transferred to the prefecture.
To the northwest is Jiǔzōngshān,
and also Wǔjiàngshān.
To the east is the Jīngshuǐ river,

Huàzhōu (To the south is Shàohuáshān.
To the north is the Wèishuǐ river,

To the west is the Chìshuǐ river,

There is also the Shíqiáoshuǐ river.
All flow north into the Wèi river.)
It is 200 *li* west of the prefecture.
It administers
2 counties.
Huàyīn (To the east of the zhōu.
To the south is Huàshān,
also called Tàihuà,

To the east is Niúxīngǔ.

To the south

There is also Zhǒnglíngshān,
