To the east are
Wǔguān and to the west are Qínlíng Èr Xúnjiǎnsī.

Shāngnán (To the east of the zhōu,

Shānyáng (To the south of the zhōu,

Zhèn'ān (To the southwest of the zhōu.

To the southwest is Jǔshuǐ,
also named Luòshuǐ.

Cháoyì (To the east of the zhōu.

To the south is Wèishuǐ.

Héyáng (To the northeast of the zhōu.
To the east is the Huánghé.
Hánchéng (To the northeast of the zhōu.
To the west is Liángshān,

To the northeast is Lóngménshān,
standing opposite across the river.
Chéngchéng (To the north of the zhōu.
To the west is the Luòshuǐ.
Báishuǐ (To the northwest of the zhōu.

it was moved to its present seat.
To the west is the Luòshuǐ,

To the northwest is Mǎliántān Xúnjiǎnsī.

Yǒngshòu (To the north of the zhōu.

Sānshuǐ (To the northeast of the zhōu.

Gazetteer, Volume 19, Geography 4: Sìchuān, Jiāngxī
Sìchuān: The region of the two states of Liáng and Jīng in the Yǔgòng.
The Yuán dynasty established the Sìchuān Děngchù Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng.
Its seat was Chéngdū Lù.
)It also established the Luóluó Méngqìng Děngchù Xuānwèi Sī,
(Its seat was Jiànchāng Lù.
)which was subordinate to the Yúnnán Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng.
In the 6th month of the 4th year of Hóngwǔ, Míng Shēng was pacified.
In the 7th month, the Sìchuān Děngchù Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng was established.
In the 9th month, the Chéngdū Dū Wèi was established.
(It shared its seat with the Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng.
)In the 10th month of the 8th year, the Dū Wèi was changed to the Sìchuān Dū Zhīhuīshǐ Sī.
It administered one Zhāotǎo Sī,
two Xuānwèi Sī,
five Ānfǔ Sī,
twenty-two Zhǎngguān Sī, and various Wèi Suǒ.
In the 6th month of the 9th year, the Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng was changed to the Chéngbù Bùzhèngshǐ Sī.
It administered thirteen Fǔ,
six Zhílì Zhōu,
one Xuānfǔ Sī,
one Ānfǔ Sī,
fifteen subordinate Zhōu,
one hundred and eleven Xiàn,
and sixteen Zhǎngguān Sī.
(It encompassed over 1,150 lǐ.)
To the north, it reached Guǎngyuán,
(bordering Shǎnxī.)
to the east, it reached Wūshān,
(bordering Húguǎng.)
to the south, it reached Wūsā and Dōngchuān,
(bordering Guìzhōu and Yúnnán.)
to the west, it reached Wēimào,
(bordering Xīfān.)
It was 7,260 lǐ from Nánjīng
and 10,710 lǐ from the capital.

and 1,466,778 people.

1,200 *lǐ* north of the Bùzhèngsī.

To the northeast, it borders the Great River.
Nèijiāng flows in from Shuāngliú Xiàn,
which is Mùmǎ Chuān.
They converge and flow south,
also called Wǔyáng Jiāng.
In the river, there is Gǔlóu Tān.
There is also Chì Shuǐ,
which also flows into the Great River from the northeast.
Dānléng (West of the prefecture.
Established in the 12th month of the 6th year of Hóngwǔ,
belonging to Jiādìng Fǔ.
In the 5th month of the 10th year, it was abolished and merged into Méixiàn.
In the 11th month of the 13th year, it was re-established,
and came to belong to this prefecture.
To the southeast, there is Qīngyī Shuǐ,
originating in Shānlúshān Xiàn,
flowing through here,
its lower course reaching Jiādìng Zhōu and entering the Great River.
Qīngshén (South of the prefecture.
In the 5th month of the 10th year of Hóngwǔ, it was abolished and merged into Jiādìng Zhōu.
In the 11th month of the 13th year, it was restored to its affiliation.
To the west, there is Xióng'ěr Shān,
with Qīngyī Shuǐ flowing beneath it.
Also to the east, there is the Great River.
To the southeast, there is Sōngbǎi Tān.
To the east, there is Lítóu Wān Xúnjiǎnsī.
)Qióngzhōu (In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Jiādìng Fǔlù.
)In the 4th month of the 9th year of Hóngwǔ, it was downgraded to a county,
still belonging to Jiādìng Zhōu.
In the 2nd month of the 19th year of Chénghuà, it was re-established as a prefecture,
directly administered by the Bùzhèngsī.
(To the west, there is Gǔchéng Shān,
which produces iron.
Also to the southeast, there is Tóngguān Shān,
which produces copper.
To the west, there is Xiāngtái Shān,
below which is a fire well,
and also a salt well.
To the south, there is Qióng Shuǐ,
flowing in from Yǎzhōu,
and entering the Great River at Xīnjīn Xiàn.
To the south, there is Jiāmén Guān Xúnjiǎnsī.
To the west, there is Huǒjǐng Bà Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved 25 *lǐ* south of the prefecture.
)It is 300 *lǐ* northeast of the Bùzhèngsī.
It administers two counties.
Dàyì (North of the prefecture,
slightly to the east.
In the 5th month of the 10th year of Hóngwǔ, it was abolished and merged into Qióngxiàn.
In the 11th month of the 13th year, it was re-established,
belonging to Jiādìng Zhōu.
In the 2nd month of the 19th year of Chénghuà, it was restored to its affiliation.
To the northwest, there is Hèmíng Shān,
bordering Chóngqìng Zhōu.
To the east, there is Yá Jiāng,
its lower course flowing into Qióng Shuǐ.
Pújiāng (Southeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was abolished and merged into the prefecture.
In the 12th month of the 6th year of Hóngwǔ, it was re-established,
belonging to Jiādìng Fǔ.
In the 2nd month of the 19th year of Chénghuà, it was restored to its affiliation.
To the south, there is Pú Shuǐ,
originating in Míngshān Xiàn,
flowing through here,
and entering the border of Qióngzhōu to the east.
To the west, there is Shuānglù Xúnjiǎnsī.
)Jiādìng Zhōu (Formerly Jiādìng Fǔlù in the Yuán dynasty.
)In the 4th year of Hóngwǔ, it became a *fǔ*.
In the 4th month of the 9th year, it was downgraded to a prefecture,
with Lóngyóu Xiàn, the seat of the prefectural administration, abolished and merged into it,
directly administered by the Bùzhèngsī.
(To the east, there is Sānguī Shān.
There is also Jiǔdǐng Shān.
The Great River is east of the city,
also called Tōng Jiāng.
Also to the west, there is Yáng Jiāng,
which is the Dàdù Hé,
flowing in from Éméi Xiàn,
passing below Wūyóu Shān east of the city,
and converging with the Great River.
Also to the southwest, there is Qīngyī Shuǐ,
which at Shuānghú west of the city,
converges with Yáng Jiāng.
To the southeast, there is Jīnshí Jǐng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.
)It is 260 *lǐ* north of the Bùzhèngsī.
It administers six counties.
Éméi (West of the prefecture.
To the southwest, there is Éméi Shān,
with Dà'é, Zhōng'é, and Xiǎo'é,
from which Luómù Jiāng emerges.
Yáng Jiāng is south of the county,
flowing in from the Yi border of Lízhōu,
and converging with Luómù Jiāng.
Also to the southwest, there is Zhōngzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Dàwéi Shān.
There is also Tǔdì Guān,
connecting with the barbarian border.
Jiājiāng (Northwest of the prefecture.
To the west, there is Qīngyī Shuǐ,
and also Hóngyǎ Chuān,
which converges with it.
Hóngyǎ (Northwest of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was abolished and merged into Jiājiāng.
In the 5th month of the 18th year of Chénghuà, it was re-established.
To the northwest, there is Qīngyī Shuǐ.
To the west, there is Hóngyǎ Chuān.
There is also Zhúqìng Shān Xúnjiǎnsī.
Jiànwéi (Southeast of the prefecture.
Formerly administered from Yùjīn Zhèn.
Now administered from Chéngfēi Zhèn,
moved here during the Hóngwǔ era.
To the east, there is the Great River.
To the northeast, Sìwàng Xī flows into it.
There is Sìwàng Xīkǒu Xúnjiǎnsī.
Also to the north, there is Shímǎ Guān Xúnjiǎnsī.
Róngzhōu (east of the prefecture.
Originally Róngzhōu.
Established in the twelfth month of Hóngwǔ 6 (1373).
Demoted to a county in the fourth month of Hóngwǔ 9 (1376).
To the east is Róngchuān Shuǐ.
There are Wèngxī Guān and Fēishuǐ Guān,
both established during the Hóngwǔ reign.
There is also Dàpíng Àikǒu,
established in the eighth month of Chénghuà 12 (1476).
Wēiyuǎn (east of the prefecture.
Established in the twelfth month of Hóngwǔ 6 (1373),
subordinate to Jiāndìng Fǔ.
Abolished and merged into Róng Xiàn in the fifth month of Hóngwǔ 10 (1377).
Re-established in the eleventh month of Hóngwǔ 13 (1380).
) Lúzhōu (in the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Chóngqìng Lù.
) In Hóngwǔ 6 (1373), it was directly administered by Sìchuān Xíngshěng.
In Hóngwǔ 9 (1376), it was directly administered by the Bùzhèng Sī.
(The old seat of government was at Xiǎncǎobà, east of the prefecture.
During the Hóngwǔ reign,
it was moved here.
To the west of the city is Bǎoshān.
To the southwest is Fāngshān.
The Dàjiāng is to the east,
also known as Lújiāng,
and also Wènjiāng.
The Zīshuǐ comes from the north of the prefecture and joins it,
also called Zhōngjiāng.
There was also the Lúzhōu Wèi,
established in the tenth month of Hóngwǔ 21 (1388) in the prefectural city,
and moved to Dùchuánpù southwest of the prefecture in the fourth month of Chénghuà 4 (1468).
To the south are Shípéng Zhèn and to the north Lǐshì Zhèn, two Xúnjiǎnsī.
There are also Jiāngmén, Shuǐliúyá, Dòngsǎo, and other passes and forts,
all established in the fourth month of Chénghuà 4 (1468).
To the south there is also Lóngtòuguān,
repaired and built during the Chóngzhēn reign.
) It is 1,550 *lǐ* northwest of the Bùzhèng Sī.
It governs three counties.
Nàxī (southwest of the prefecture.
To the north, it borders the Dàjiāng.
To the west of the city is Nàxī Shuǐ,
flowing from the southwest of the Fānbù region to join it.
There is the Nàxīkǒu Xúnjiǎnsī.
To the south are Dàomǎ Guān and Shíhǔ Guān,
both connecting to Yúnnán and Jiāozhǐ roads.
Jiāng'ān (west of the prefecture,
slightly south.
To the north, it borders the Dàjiāng.
The Miánshuǐ flows into it from the southwest,
which is called Miánshuǐkǒu.
To the south there is also Yùxī,
and also Jìngtān,
both flowing into and joining the Miánshuǐ.
There is Bǎnqiáo Xúnjiǎnsī.
Héjiāng (east of the prefecture,
slightly north.
The old seat of government was south of Shénbì Shān.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign, it was moved to the foot of Ānlè Shān,
which is the present seat of government.
To the south there is also Róng Shān,
popularly known as Róngzǐ Shān.
To the north, it borders the Dàjiāng.
To the west, Zhīxī and Běixī flow into it,
hence it is called Héjiāng.
To the south there is also Ānlè Xī,
flowing northwest into Jiāng'ān Xiàn.
) Yǎzhōu (in the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Tǔbō Xuānwèisī of Shǎnxī Xíngshěng.
) In Hóngwǔ 4 (1371), with the integration of the prefectural seat, Yándào Xiàn,
it was directly administered by the Bùzhèng Sī.
(To the east is Càishān,
also known as Zhōugōng Shān.
Below it is Jīngshuǐ,
also known as Zhōugōng Shuǐ.
To the southeast there is also Róngshuǐ,
also known as Chángfén Hé.
There is also Xiǎoxī,
also known as Bǎizhàng Hé.
Upon reaching the prefectural boundary,
all flow together into Qīngyī Jiāng.
To the north is Jīnjī Guān.
To the northeast is Jīnshā Guān.
) It is 450 *lǐ* northeast of the Bùzhèng Sī.
It governs three counties.
Míngshān (northeast of the prefecture.
In Hóngwǔ 10 (1377), it was abolished and merged into the prefecture.
Re-established in the eleventh month of Hóngwǔ 13 (1380).
To the northeast is Bǎizhàng Shān.
Next to it is Bǎizhàng Xiàn,
which belonged to the prefecture in the Yuán dynasty,
and was abolished during the Hóngwǔ reign.
To the west is Méngshān.
To the south is Qīngyī Jiāng.
Róngjīng (southwest of the prefecture.
Míng Yùzhēn abolished it and merged it into Yándào Xiàn.
Re-established during the Hóngwǔ reign.
To the northeast is Tóngshān.
To the east is Qiónglái Shān,
bordering Lízhōu territory,
with Jiǔzhé Bǎn on it.
To the west is Dàguān Shān,
where Qiónglái Guān is located.
To the north is Chángfén Hé.
To the south is Zhōugōng Shuǐ,
both flowing into the prefectural boundary.
To the northwest is Zǐyǎn Guān,
its territory bordering Xīfān.
There is also Diāomén Zhài,
also called Héchuān Zhèn.
The Yuán dynasty established Diāomén Ānfǔsī here.
In Hóngwǔ 5 (1372), Diāomén Bǎihùsuǒ was established here.
Its territory borders Tiānquán.
Lúshān (northwest of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was called Lúshān,
later abolished.
Re-established in the twelfth month of Hóngwǔ 6 (1373),
and renamed Lúshān.
To the east is Lúshān,
where Qīngyī Shuǐ originates.
To the south is Sānjiāng Dù,
its water flows through Duōgōng Xiá,
then downstream into Píngqiāng Jiāng.
To the northwest is Lín Guān,
formerly called Líng Guān,
renamed in the early Zhèngtǒng reign.
There is Lín Guān Xúnjiǎnsī.
To the south there is also Fēixiān Guān.
) Yǒngníng Xuānfǔsī (Yuán dynasty Yǒngníng Lù.
) In Hóngwǔ 7 (1374), it became Yǒngníng Zhǎngguānsī.
In the first month of Hóngwǔ 8 (1375), it was promoted to Xuānfǔsī.
In Tiānqǐ 3 (1623), it was abolished,
and its territory belonged to the prefecture.
(The old city was to the west.
In Hóngwǔ 15 (1382), it was moved to the present seat.
To the southeast is Shīzǐ Shān.
To the northwest is Qīngshān.
To the south is Yǒngníng Hé,
flowing northeast through Lúzhōu territory,
and entering the Dàjiāng.
To the southeast there is also Chìshuǐ Hé.
To the east is Yúfú Guān,
established in Hóngwǔ 4 (1371).
) It governs two Zhǎngguānsī.
It is 1,800 *lǐ* from the Bùzhèng Sī.
Jiǔxìng Zhǎngguānsī (southwest of the司城.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Jiǔxìng Luóshì Dǎng Mányí Zhǎngguān Qiānhù.
Re-established in the twelfth month of Hóngwǔ 6 (1373).
In Tiānqǐ 6 (1626), it was transferred to Lúzhōu.
To the south is Tōngjiāng Xī,
which meets at Jiāngmén Xiá in Nàxī to the northeast.
To the southwest is Jīn'é Chí.
Tàipíng Zhǎngguān Sī (originally Yuán Dàbà Jūnmín Fǔ,
abolished during the Hóngwǔ reign.
Re-established in the 4th year of Chénghuà, 4th month).
Tiānquán Liùfān Zhāotǎo Sī (originally Yuán Liùfān Zhāotǎo Sī.
) Re-established in the 6th year of Hóngwǔ, 12th month,
directly administered by the Sìchuān Bùzhèng Sī.
In the 21st year, 2nd month, it was transferred to the Dūsī.
(To the east is Duōgōng Shān.
To the south is Hé Shuǐ,
also named Shǐyáng Hé,
also named Duōgōng Hé,
flowing into the Qīngyī Jiāng in Yǎzhōu.
Furthermore, within the Xīfān territory is Kěbáhǎi,
its lower course merges with Yúnnán Yàngbèi Shuǐ,
flowing into Jiāozhǐ.
Also, Jìnmén Guān and Zǐshí Guān are both to the west of this Sī.
Moreover, to the east are Shànsuǒ, Zhāngsuǒ, Níshān, Tiānquán, Sījīng, Lè'ài, Shǐyáng, Lèwū, Zàichéng, and Língguān, a total of ten Bǎihùsuǒ.)
It is 550 lǐ east of the Bùzhèng Sī.
Sōngpān Wèi (originally Sōngzhōu during the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to the Yúnnán Xíngshěng.
) In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it continued as such.
In the 12th year, 4th month, Sōngzhōu Wèi was additionally established.
In the 13th year, 8th month, the Wèi was abolished.
Soon after,
the Wèi was re-established.
In the 20th year, 1st month, the Zhōu was abolished,
and the Wèi was renamed Sōngpān Děngchǔ Jūnmín Zhǐhuīshǐ Sī,
subordinate to the Sìchuān Dūsī.
In the 42nd year of Jiājìng, the Jūnmín Sī was abolished,
and it remained a Wèi.
(To the east is Xuělán Shān,
with a pass on it.
To the south is Hónghuā Shān.
To the northwest is Gānsōng Líng.
Furthermore, to the north are Dà and Xiǎo Fēnshuǐ Líng.
To the west is Mín Jiāng,
flowing from Táozhōu Wèi in Shǎnxī through here,
also called Pānzhōu Hé.
Moreover, to the east is Fú Jiāng,
originating from Xiǎo Fēnshuǐ Líng,
flowing southeast,
entering the jurisdiction of Xiǎohé Suǒ.
To the north is Pānzhōu Wèi,
established during the Hóngwǔ reign
from the former Pānzhōu.
In the 20th year, it was incorporated.
Moreover, to the west is Zhènyí Guān,
established in the 4th year of Yǒnglè, 7th month.
Furthermore, to the northwest is Liúshā Guān.
Also, to the east are Wàngshān, Xuělán, Fēngdòng, Hēisōnglín, Sānshè, and Xiǎoguānzi Guān.
To the south are Xīníng, Guīhuà, Ānhuà, Xīntáng, Běidìng, and Pújiāng, six passes.
There is also Píngyí Guān,
established in the 14th year of Wànlì.
Furthermore, to the south is Zhènpíng Guān.
Moreover, to the northwest is Zhānglà Bǎo,
established in the 11th year of Hóngwǔ.)
It administers one Qiānhùsuǒ,
sixteen Zhǎngguān Sī,
and five Ānfǔ Sī.
It is 760 lǐ southeast of the Bùzhèng Sī.
Xiǎohé Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ (established in the 4th year of Xuāndé, 1st month.
To the north is Shījiā Shān,
also named Wén Shān,
with Wénshān Guān at its foot.
To the south is Xiǎohé,
which is the Fú Shuǐ,
flowing east into the Lóng'ān Fǔ
boundary,
with an Iron Chain Bridge spanning it.

Pānwòzhài Zhǎngguān Sī (established in the 5th year of Zhèngtǒng, 7th month.)
Biésīzhài Zhǎngguān Sī (established in the 10th year of Xuāndé, 5th month.)
Bālang Ānfǔ Sī (established in the 15th year of Yǒnglè, 2nd month.)

Ājiǎozhài Ānfǔ Sī
Máng'erzhě Ānfǔ Sī (These two Sī
were both established in the 5th year of Zhèngtǒng, 7th month.)
Sīnǎng Rì Ānfǔ Sī (established in the 11th year of Zhèngtǒng, 7th month.)
Diéxī Shǒuyù Jūnmín Qiānhùsuǒ. Originally Diéxī Yòu Qiānhùsuǒ,
established in the 11th year of Hóngwǔ from the ancient Yìzhōu,
subordinate to Màozhōu Wèi.
In the 25th year, it was re-established
and directly administered by the Dūsī.
(To the south is Páizhà Shān.
To the west is Wèn Jiāng;
to the south, Hēishuǐ flows into it,
forming Yì Shuǐ.
Furthermore, to the south are Nánqiáo, Zhōngqiáo, and Chèdǐ, three passes;
to the north are Yǒngzhènqiáo Guān and Zhènpíng Guān;
to the west is Diéxīqiáo Guān;
to the east is Xiǎo Guān,
all established in the 11th year of Hóngwǔ.)
It administers two Zhǎngguān Sī.
It is 580 lǐ southeast of the Bùzhèng Sī.
Diéxī Zhǎngguān Sī (north of the Suǒ city.)
Yùjí Zhǎngguān Sī (west of the Suǒ city.
Both were established in the 1st year of Yǒnglè, 1st month.)
Lízhōu Shǒuyù Jūnmín Qiānhùsuǒ. Originally Lízhōu Zhǎngguān Sī,
established in the 9th year of Hóngwǔ, 7th month.
In the 11th year, 6th month, it was elevated to Ānfǔ Sī,
directly administered by the Bùzhèng Sī.
In the 24th year of Wànlì, it was demoted to Qiānhùsuǒ,
directly administered by the Dūsī.
(To the northeast is Shèngzhōng Shān,
below which is Lízhōu,
which during the Yuán dynasty was subordinate to the Tǔbō Xuānwèi Sī of the Shǎnxī Xíngshěng.
In the 5th year of Hóngwǔ, the county seat of Hàn Yuán Xiàn was incorporated into the Zhōu.
It was abolished after Yǒnglè.
To the northwest is Fēiyuè Shān,
both sides of which border the territory of the Shēng Qiāng.
To the southwest is Dàtián Shān,
its eastern foot being Dàtián Bà,
where Lízhōu Tǔqiānhùsuǒ was established in the 24th year of Wànlì.
Also, to the east is Chōngtiān Shān.
To the south is Bìzhàng Shān.
To the northwest again is Sǔn Shān.
To the south is Dàdù Hé,
which is the ancient Ruò Shuǐ.
In the 15th year of Hóngwǔ, 6th month, Dàdùhé Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ was established,
later moved to the northwest corner of the Sī city.
Also, to the southwest is Hàn Shuǐ,
its source being Xiānrén Dòng on Fēiyuè Shān,
also called Liúshā Hé,
its lower course reaches Shìjiàn Shān,
and enters Dàdù Hé.
South of the river is Qīngxī Guān,
bordering the Jiànchāng Xíngdūsī.
To the west is Hēiyá Guān,
established in the 16th year of Hóngwǔ.
There is also Jiāozǐ Guān,
with a road leading to Chánghéxī and other places.)
It is 690 lǐ northeast of the Bùzhèng Sī.
Píngchádòng Zhǎngguān Sī (originally Róngjiāng, Zhīzǐ, Píngchá Děngchǔ Zhǎngguān Sī during the Yuán dynasty.)
Established in the 8th year of Hóngwǔ, 1st month,
subordinate to Yǒuyáng Xuānfǔ Sī.
In the 17th year, it was directly administered by the Bùzhèng Sī.
(To the west is Bǎisuì Shān.
Shàoxī originates from its east,
Mǎnxī originates from its west,
merging to flow into Mǎisài Hé.)
It is 1670 lǐ north of the Bùzhèng Sī.
Róngxī Zhīmázǐpíng Zhǎngguān Sī (originally Róngjiāng, Zhīzǐ, Píngchá Děngchǔ Zhǎngguān Sī during the Yuán dynasty.)
Re-established in the 8th year of Hóngwǔ,
subordinate to Húguǎng Sīnán Xuānwèi Sī.
In the 17th year, 5th month, it was directly administered by the Sìchuān Bùzhèng Sī.
Ānníng Xuānfǔ Sī. Established in the 13th year of Chénghuà, 2nd month,
it administers two Zhǎngguān Sī.
Huáiyuǎn Zhǎngguān Sī
Xuānhuà Zhǎngguān Sī (Both were established in the 13th year of Chénghuà, 2nd month,
concurrent with the Xuānfǔ Sī.)
Yǒuyáng Xuānwèi Sī (originally Yǒuyáng Zhōu during the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to Huáidé Fǔ.
Míng Yùzhēn reformed it into Yánbiān Xīdòng Jūnmín Xuānwèi Sī.)
In the 5th year of Hóngwǔ, 4th month, Yǒuyáng Zhōu was re-established,
and Yǒuyáng Xuānwèi Sī was concurrently established;
the Zhōu was soon abolished.
In the 8th year, 1st month, the Xuānwèi Sī was renamed Xuānfǔ Sī,
subordinate to the Sìchuān Dūsī.
In the 16th year of Yǒnglè, it was transferred to Chóngqìng Wèi.
In the 1st year of Tiānqǐ, it was elevated to Xuānwèi Sī.
(To the southeast is Yǒushuǐ,
which merges with Píngchá Shuǐ,
and at Chénzhōu Fǔ in Húguǎng, it merges with the river,
where there is Níngjùn Jiāng Xúnjiǎnsī.)
It is 490 lǐ northwest of Chóngqìng Fǔ.
It administers three Zhǎngguān Sī.
Shíyēdòng Zhǎngguān Sī (southeast of the Sī.
Originally Shíyē Jūnmín Fǔ during the Yuán dynasty.

the county was changed to Níng County,
and the prefecture was abolished and incorporated into it.
In the sixteenth year of Hóngzhì,
the county was elevated to a prefecture.
(To its west is
Mùfùshān,
where the Xiūshuǐ River originates,
and its lower reaches flow into Póyánghú Lake.
To its east is Hèyuánshuǐ,
originating from Jiǔgōngshān,
and its lower reaches merge with the Xiūshuǐ River.
To its west was Shānshì Patrol and Inspection Office,
later moved to Chóngxiāng
Běicūn.
To its south were Dìngjiāng and Bādiélǐng, two Patrol and Inspection Offices,
which were abolished.
) It is 360 lǐ southeast of the prefecture capital. Ruìzhōufǔ Prefecture (It was Yuán Ruìzhōulù Circuit,
subordinate to the Jiāngxī Xíngshěng.
) In the second year of Hóngwǔ, it became a prefecture.
It administered three counties.
It is 200 lǐ northeast of the Bùzhèngsī. Gāo'ān (dependent county.
To its north is Mǐshān.
To its northwest is Huálínshān.
To its north is Shǔjiāng River,
which flows in from Shànggāo County,
then flows eastward to converge at Xiàngyátán in Nánchāng and enters the Zhāngjiāng River,
also known as Jǐnshuǐ.
This is a different Shǔjiāng,
not the great river originating from Mínshān.
To its south is Qǔshuǐ,
which also flows eastward into the Zhāngjiāng River.
To its south were Yīngānglǐng and Hóngchéng, two Patrol and Inspection Offices,
which were abolished.
) Shànggāo (southwest of the prefecture capital.
To its south is Méngshān,
which formerly produced silver and lead.
To its west is Tiānlǐng.
Further west is Shǔjiāng River,
which flows in from Wànzài County,
and at Língjiāngkǒu northwest of the county, it merges with the Yánxīshuǐ River of Xīnchāng County.
There is also Xiékǒushuǐ,
which originates from Méngshān,
and also flows into it west of the county.
To its west were Lílóuqíao and Mátáng, two Patrol and Inspection Offices.
) Xīnchāng (west of the prefecture capital.
It was Yuán Xīnchāngzhōu.
In the early Hóngwǔ era,
it was demoted to a county.
To its west is Yánxīshuǐ River,
also known as Ruòyexī Stream,
which flows south into Shǔjiāng River at Shànggāo County.
To its north is Téngjiāng River,
and its lower reaches merge with the Yánxīshuǐ River.
To its west were Huánggāngdòng and to its north Dàgūlǐng, two Patrol and Inspection Offices.
) Jiǔjiāngfǔ Prefecture (It was Yuán Jiāngzhōulù Circuit,
subordinate to the Jiāngxī Xíngshěng.
) In the Xīncǒu year of Tàizǔ's reign, it became Jiǔjiāngfǔ Prefecture.
It administered five counties.
It is 300 lǐ south of the Bùzhèngsī. Déhuà (dependent county.
To its south is Lúshān,
also called Kuānglú.
To its southeast is Póyánghú Lake,
and in the lake is Dàgūshān Island.
The county borders the Dàjiāng River to the north,
also called Xúnyángjiāng.
The north bank is Húguǎng Huángméi County,
and the south bank passes through Húkǒu and Péngzé counties
before entering the territory of Nánzhí Dōngliú County.
In the river is Sāngluòzhōu Island,
bordering Nánzhí Sùsōng County.
To its west is Púnpǔ River,
which flows in from Ruìchāng County,
passes west of the city,
and flows into the Dàjiāng River,
which is known as Púnkǒu.
To its southeast is Nǚ'érpǔ,
originating from Lúshān,
and flowing northeast into Póyánghú Lake.
To its west was Chéngzǐzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office.
To its east were Nánhúzǐ and to its west Lóngkāihé, two Patrol and Inspection Offices,
which were later abolished.
) Dé'ān (southwest of the prefecture capital.
To its south is Bóyángshān,
which ancient texts identify as Fūqiǎnyuán,
from which the Bóyángchuān River originates
and flows southeast into Póyánghú Lake.
To its northeast is Gǔliánshuǐ,
originating from Lúshān,
and its lower reaches also flow into Póyánghú Lake.
) Ruìchāng (west of the prefecture capital.
To its west is Qīngpúnshān,
from which the Púnshuǐ River originates.
To its north is the Dàjiāng River,
and the north bank borders Húguǎng Guǎngjì County.
) Húkǒu (east of the prefecture capital.
It borders the Dàjiāng River to the north.
To its south is Shàngshízhōngshān.
To its north is Xiàshízhōngshān.
To its south is Qīngshān,
located in Póyánghú Lake.
To its southwest is Póyánghú Lake itself,
where the waters of Zhāng and Gòng and other rivers converge
and flow into the Dàjiāng River from here.
To its south was Húkǒuzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office,
later moved to Shàngshízhōngshān.
To its northwest was Jiāoshízhīzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office,
later moved to Huángmáotán.
) Péngzé (east of the prefecture capital,
a little to the north.
It borders the Dàjiāng River.
To its north is Xiǎogūshān Island in the river.
On the river bank is Pénglàngjī Shoal,
opposite Xiǎogūshān.
To its northeast is Mǎdāngshān,
lying across the Dàjiāng River.
There is Mǎdāngzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office.
To its southwest were Fēngshān and Jīzhèn, two Patrol and Inspection Offices.
) Nánkāngfǔ Prefecture (It was Yuán Nánkānglù Circuit,
subordinate to the Jiāngxī Xíngshěng.
) In the Xīncǒu year of Tàizǔ's reign, in the eighth month, it became Xīníngfǔ Prefecture.
In the fourth month of the Rènyín year, it was renamed Nánkāngfǔ Prefecture.
It administered four counties.
It is 300 lǐ south of the Bùzhèngsī.
Xīngzǐ (adjacent
to the northwest lies Lúshān.
To the north is Xiéshān,
located in Póyánghú.
East of the lake is Gōngtínghú,
and to the northwest is Luòxīnghú.
Further west is Gǔliánshuǐ,
which flows down into Póyánghú.
To the east is the Chánglǐng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Zhǔxī Zhèn south of the county,
and then moved again to Qīngshān Zhèn northeast of the county,
retaining its original name.
Dūchāng (east of the prefecture.
To the southwest is Shíbìshān,
bordering Zhāngjiāng.
To the southeast is Póyánghú,
to the north is Hòugǎng Hé,
where all waters converge and enter.
To the northwest is the Zuǒlí Xúnjiǎnsī,
by the lake.
To the southeast is the Cháipéng Xúnjiǎnsī,
located in the lake.
Jiànchāng (southwest of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Jiànchāng Zhōu.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was demoted to a county.
To the southwest is Chángshān,
to the south is Xiūshuǐ,
flowing in from Níngzhōu,
also known as Xīhé.
To the east is the Lútán Xúnjiǎnsī.
Ānyì (southwest of the prefecture.
Established in the second month of the 13th year of Zhèngdé by ceding Ānyì and four other townships from Jiànchāng Xiàn.
To the east is Dōngyáng Xīnjìng Shuǐ,
to the east is Lóngjiāng Shuǐ,
both flowing into Xiūshuǐ.
) Ráozhōufǔ (in the Yuán dynasty, Ráozhōulù,
belonging to Jiāngzhè Xíngshěng.
) In the Xīnchǒu year, eighth month of Tàizǔ's reign, it became Póyángfǔ,
subordinate to Jiāngnán Xíngshěng.
Soon it was renamed Ráozhōufǔ,
and became subordinate.
It administered seven counties.
It is 240 li southwest of Bùzhèngsī.
Póyáng (adjacent.
In the first year of Zhèngtǒng,
the Huái Wángfǔ moved here from Sháozhōufǔ in Guǎngdōng.
To the northwest is Póyángshān,
located in Póyánghú.
The lake is 300 li long,
40 li wide,
extending across the borders of Nánkāng, Ráozhōu, Nánchāng, and Jiǔjiāng prefectures.
To the south is Pójiāng,
whose source is in Wùyuán Xiàn and Qímén Xiàn of Nánzhí,
converging downstream east of the city.
Further south, Guǎngxìn Shàngráo Jiāng joins it,
encircling the city and exiting to the northwest,
then dividing into two,
both entering Póyánghú,
also known as Shuānggǎng Shuǐ.
Further east is Dōnghú,
also named Dūjūnhú,
flowing into Pójiāng.
To the northwest is the Tángyīn Xúnjiǎnsī,
moved to Shuānggǎngkǒu.
To the north is the Shímén Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.
Further northeast is Dàyángbù.
To the west is Bāzìnǎo.
Yúgān (south of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Ráogān Zhōu.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was demoted to a county.
To the northwest is Kānglángshān,
bordering the southern shore of Póyánghú,
hence its water is named Kānglánghú.
Further west is Zútínghú.
Further south is Yúshuǐ,
also called Sānyúshuǐ.
Further south is Lóngkū Hé,
which joins Yúshuǐ,
flowing down into Pójiāng.
There is the Kāngshān Xúnjiǎnsī,
formerly on Kānglángshān,
later moved to Huángbù.
To the west is Ruìhóng Zhèn,
on the shore of Póyánghú.
Lèpíng (east of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Lèpíng Zhōu.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was demoted to a county.
To the northeast is Fèngyóushān.
To the south is Lè'ān Jiāng,
which is the upper reach of Pójiāng.
To the north is the Bājiàn Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.
To the south is the Xiānhè Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Héxī Zhèn in Wànnián Xiàn.
Fúliáng (east of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Fúliáng Zhōu.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was demoted to a county.
To the south is Chāngjiāng,
where all waters from Qímén Xiàn in Nánzhí flow and converge,
it is another source of Pójiāng.
To the northwest is the Táoshù Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Lèshàng Shì northeast of the county.
To the southwest is Jǐngdézhèn,
where the Yùqì Chǎng was established in the early Xuāndé reign.
Déxīng (east of the prefecture.
To the east is Yínshān,
which formerly produced silver.
To the north is Tóngshān,
at the foot of which is Dǎnquán,
capable of turning iron into copper when immersed.
To the southwest is Jiànjié Shuǐ,
flowing in from Yìyáng Xiàn.
To the north is Dàxī,
flowing in from Wùyuán Xiàn in Nánzhí.
Downstream, both converge into Lè'ān Jiāng.
To the east is the Báishā Xúnjiǎnsī.
To the southwest is the Yǒngtài Xúnjiǎnsī,
now defunct.
Ānrén (south of the prefecture,
slightly to the east.
To the south is Jǐnjiāng,
also named Ānrén Gǎng,
flowing in from Guìxī Xiàn,
entering Yúgān's territory to the northwest,
becoming Lóngkū Hé.
Further east is Báitǎ Hé,
flowing into Jǐnjiāng.
To the south are Báitǎ and to the east are Tiánnán, two Xúnjiǎnsī,
later defunct.
Wànnián (southeast of the prefecture.
Established in the seventh year of Zhèngdé from Wànchūn Xiāng of Yúgān Xiàn,
and supplemented with land from Póyáng, Lèpíng, and Guìxī counties.
To the north is Wànniánshān.
To the east is Táoyuán Dòng,
from which Táoyuán Shuǐ flows,
passing southwest of the county,
downstream becoming Yúshuǐ.
To the northeast are Héxī Zhèn and to the north are Shítóujiē, two Xúnjiǎnsī,
both later defunct.
) Guǎngxìnfǔ (in the Yuán dynasty, Xìnzhōulù,
belonging to Jiāngzhè Xíngshěng.
) In the Gēngzǐ year, fifth month of Tàizǔ's reign, it became Guǎngxìnfǔ.
It administered seven counties.
It is 630 li northwest of Bùzhèngsī.
Shàngráo (adjacent.
To the northwest is Língshān,
which formerly produced crystal.
To the south is Dīngxīshān,
which produces iron.
Further south is Tóngshān.
To the north is Shàngráo Jiāng,
flowing in from Yùshān Xiàn,
passing north of the city,
downstream joining Pójiāng at Póyáng Xiàn.
Further west is Zhūxī,
whose source is Língshān,
also called Língxī,
flowing into Shàngráo Jiāng.
To the south are Bāfāngchǎng and to the northeast are Zhèngjiāfāng, two Xúnjiǎnsī.
Yùshān (east of the prefecture.
There is Sānqīngshān.
There is also Huáiyùshān,
from which Yùxī flows,
dividing into two streams,
one entering Zhè to the east,
the other becoming Shàngráo Jiāng to the west.
To the southeast is the Liǔdūzhài Xúnjiǎnsī.
Yìyáng (west of the prefecture.
To the south is Jūnyángshān,
which formerly produced silver.
To the east is Yìyáng Jiāng,
which is the lower reach of Shàngráo Jiāng,
and Yìxī also flows into it.
There is also Géxī,
whose source is Língshān in Shàngráo Xiàn,
downstream flowing into Pójiāng.
There is also Xìnyì Gǎng,
flowing in from Shàowǔ in Fújiàn,
joining Géxī.
Guìxī (west of the prefecture.
To the southwest is Xiàngshān.
There is also Lónghǔshān,
where Shàngqīnggōng is located.
To its south is Xiānyán.
Further south is Xiāngxī,
also named Guìxī,
whose upper course is the Shàngráojiāng.
There is also Xūxī,
which flows in from Guāngzé Xiàn in Fújiàn,
and joins it.
To the south is the Guǎnjièzhài Patrol and Inspection Division.
To the west is the Shénqiánjiē Patrol and Inspection Division,
originally Shénfēngzhài,
located north of the county.
It was later relocated to Tánxī,
and renamed.
Yánshān (south of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was Yánshān Zhōu,
directly administered by the Jiāngzhè Xíngshěng.
Its seat was south of Bāshùlǐng.
At the beginning of the Hóngwǔ reign,
it was downgraded to a county,
and relocated to its present seat.
To the southwest is Tóngbǎoshān,
where springs permeate iron,
which can be made into copper.
There is also Yánshān,
which produces lead, copper, and azurite.
To the north is Éhúshān.
To the south is Fēnshuǐlǐng,
bordering Chóng'ān Xiàn in Fújiàn,
on which is the Fēnshuǐguān Patrol and Inspection Division.
There is also Zǐxīlǐng,
from which the Zǐxīshuǐ emerges.
To the north is Shàngráojiāng,
which at Ruìkǒu,
merges with the Zǐxī, Tóngmù, and Huángbò rivers,
and enters the territory of Yìyáng Xiàn,
known as Yánshānhékǒu.
To the northeast is Shíxī,
which also flows to join the Shàngráojiāng.
To the southwest is the Shífózhài Patrol and Inspection Division,
later relocated to Húfángjiē in Shànzhèng Xiāng.
Further west is the Zhùbó Patrol and Inspection Division,
whose seat was Ruìkǒuzhèn,
now abolished.
Yǒngfēng (south of the prefecture.
To the southeast is Píngyángshān,
which formerly produced silver ore.
To the south is Yǒngfēngxī,
its source originating from the border of Pǔchéng Xiàn in Fújiàn,
its lower course joining the Yùxī at the border of Shàngráo Xiàn.
Further east is Yǒngpíngxī,
which to the west converges with the Shānxī and waters from various valleys,
flowing into Yǒngfēngxī.
To the east is the Zhèyángzhài Patrol and Inspection Division.
There was also the Shānxīzhài Patrol and Inspection Division,
now abolished.
Xīng'ān (west of the prefecture.
In the eighth month of the 39th year of Jiājìng, it was established from Hèngfēngzhài in Yìyáng Xiàn,
with land from Shàngráo and Guìxī counties added to it.
South of the county is Sòngxī,
its sources all originating from Língshān,
its lower course flowing into the Shàngráojiāng.
To the east is the Yāyánzhài Patrol and Inspection Division,
later abolished.
) Jiànchāng Fǔ (In the Yuán dynasty, Jiànchāng Lù,
belonging to the Jiāngxī Xíngshěng.)
In the first month of the Rén'yín year of Tàizǔ's reign, it was established as Zhàoqìng Fǔ,
soon after renamed Jiànchāng Fǔ.
It administered five counties.
To the northwest, it was 400 lǐ from the Bùzhèngsī.
Nánchéng (prefectural seat.
In the 22nd year of Yǒnglè, the Jīng Wáng Fǔ was built.
In the 10th year of Zhèngtǒng, it was relocated to Qízhōu in Húguǎng.
In the 23rd year of Chénghuà, the Yì Wáng Fǔ was built.
To the southwest is Mágūshān.
To the east is Xújīang,
also named Jiànchāngjiāng,
flowing in from Nánfēng Xiàn,
its lower course flowing into Jīnxī Xiàn.
To the east are Lántián, and to the north Fúniú, two Patrol and Inspection Divisions.
Further south are Zēngtán, and to the north Yuèkǒu, two Patrol and Inspection Divisions,
now abolished.
To the southeast is Shānguān,
bordering Guāngzé Xiàn in Fújiàn.
Nánfēng (south of the prefecture,
slightly west.
In the Yuán dynasty, Nánfēng Zhōu,
directly administered by the Jiāngxī Xíngshěng.
At the beginning of the Hóngwǔ reign,
it was downgraded to a county.
To the south is Jūnshān.
Further southeast is Bǎizhànglǐng,
which forms the boundary with Jiànníng Xiàn in Fújiàn.
There is also Xūshuǐ.
To the southeast is the Lóngchí Patrol and Inspection Division,
originally Huángshāyuánpíng,
located southwest of the county.
It was later relocated to Shuānggǎngkǒu south of the county,
then to Bǎizhànglǐng southeast of the county,
then to Kāndū,
and soon after relocated here,
and renamed.
Further south is Tàipíng, and to the north Xiānjūn, two Patrol and Inspection Divisions,
now abolished.
Xīnchéng (southeast of the prefecture.
To the west is Fúshān,
from which the Líshuǐ emerges,
passing west of the county,
its lower course joining the Xūjiāng.
Further east is Fēiyuánlǐng,
from which the Fēiyuánshuǐ emerges,
its lower course entering the Xūjiāng at Nánchéng Xiàn.
There is also Wǔfúgǎng,
its source originating from Shānguān,
its flow joining the Fēiyuánshuǐ.
To the southeast is the Jígāo Patrol and Inspection Division,
relocated to Shuǐkǒucūn,
later relocated to Déshèngguān south of the county,
then relocated to Xúnkǒu east of the county,
retaining its old name.
To the southwest is the Tóng'ān Patrol and Inspection Division,
later relocated to Zhāngcūn west of the county,
and soon after restored.
Guǎngchāng (southwest of the prefecture.
To the northwest is Jīnzhàngshān.
To the southwest is Méilǐng.
Further south is Xuèmùlǐng,
from which the Xūshuǐ emerges,
passing south of the city,
and flowing into Nánfēng Xiàn.
To the southwest are Xiùlǐng, and to the south Quánzhèn, two Patrol and Inspection Divisions.
Lúxī (southeast of the prefecture.
Originally the Lúxī Patrol and Inspection Division of Nánchéng Xiàn,
in the 12th month of the 6th year of Wànlì, it was changed to a county.
To the east is Lúxī,
its source originating from Wǔfèngshān in Chóng'ān Xiàn, Fújiàn,
flowing to the county,
then north into Ānrén Gǎng.
) Fǔzhōu Fǔ (In the Yuán dynasty, Fǔzhōu Lù,
belonging to the Jiāngxī Xíngshěng.)
In the first month of the Rén'yín year of Tàizǔ's reign, it was established as Línchuān Fǔ,
soon after renamed Fǔzhōu Fǔ.
It administered six counties.
To the north, it was 240 lǐ from the Bùzhèngsī.
Línchuān (prefectural seat.
To the south is Línggǔshān.
To the west is Tóngshān,
which formerly produced copper.
East of the city is Ruǐshuǐ,
its upper course connected to the Xūjiāng,
flowing in from Jīnxī Xiàn,
and to the east joining the Zhāngjiāng.
Further west is Línshuǐ,
its source originating from Chóngrén Xiàn,
its flow joining the Ruǐshuǐ.
To the north are Wēnjiāzhèn, to the south Qīngní, and to the west Qīngyuǎn, three Patrol and Inspection Divisions.
There was also the Báigān Patrol and Inspection Division,
later abolished.
Chóngrén (west of the prefecture.
To the south is Bāshān,
also named Línchuānshān,
from which the Línshuǐ emerges,
also called Bāshuǐ.
Further south is Huágàishān,
from which the Xīníngshuǐ emerges,
their lower courses all joining the Ruǐshuǐ.
Further southwest is Bǎotángshān,
from which the Bǎotángshuǐ emerges from its base,
to the north joining various streams within the county,
and flowing into the Línshuǐ.
To the east is the Zhōufāng Patrol and Inspection Division.
Further northwest are Dīngfāng, and to the south Hétíng, two Patrol and Inspection Divisions,
now abolished.
Jīnxī (southeast of the prefecture.
To the east is Jīnkūshān,
which formerly produced gold.
There is also Yúnlínshān,
spanning the territories of Fǔ, Xìn, and Jiànchāng prefectures.
There is also Yáshān,
bordering Guìxī Xiàn.
To the south is Fúshuǐ,
which is the lower course of the Xūshuǐ,
flowing in from Nánchéng Xiàn,
to the north joining the Qīngjiāngshuǐ,
and further north joining the Shíméngǎngshuǐ.
It then flows north as Kǔzhúshuǐ,
and then west as the Ruǐshuǐ of Línchuān Xiàn.
Yíhuáng (Southwest of the prefecture.
To its east is the Yíhuángshuǐ,
which flows down into the Rǔ.
To its south is the Zhǐmǎsì Xúnjiǎnsī.
There is also the Shàngshèng Xúnjiǎnsī,
now defunct.)
Lè'ān (Southwest of the prefecture.
To its northwest is Dàpánshān,
which borders Xīngàn and Yǒngfēng counties.
The Bǎotángshuǐ originates there,
and flows down to join the Línshuǐ.
To its east is Fúróngshān,
from which the Áoxīshuǐ flows,
down to join the Gànshuǐ.
To its north are the Lóngyì and Wàngxiān Xúnjiǎnsī.
To its northwest is also the Nánpíng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later defunct.)
Dōngxiāng (East of the prefecture.
Established in the 8th month of the 7th year of Zhèngdé from Xiàogāng of Línchuān County,
with land from Jīnxī, Jìnxián, Yúgàn, and Ānrén counties added to it.
To its southwest is the Rǔshuǐ.
To its northeast is Hèngshān, and to its northwest are the Gǔxī Xúnjiǎnsī,
later defunct.)
Jí'ān Fǔ (Formerly Jí'ān Lù in the Yuán dynasty,
belonging to the Jiāngxī Xíngshěng.)
Made a prefecture in the Rén'yín year of Tàizǔ's reign.
Administers nine counties.
Five hundred ninety *lǐ* northeast of the Bùzhèngsī.
Lúlíng (Dependent.
To its north is Luóshān,
to its south is Shéngāngshān.
The two mountains face each other,
with the Gànjiāng flowing below them.
It also flows north past the east of the city,
and further north past Hǔkǒushí,
into Xiájiāng County,
becoming the Qīngjiāng.
To its south are the Fùtián, to its west the Jǐnggāng, and to its southwest the Áochéng, three Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Tàihé (South of the prefecture,
a little to the west.
Formerly Tàihé Zhōu in the Yuán dynasty.
In the 1st month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, it was changed to Tàihé Xiàn.
To its east is Wángshān,
also known as Kuāngshān.
The Gànjiāng is south of the city,
flowing in from Wàn'ān County,
passing by Niúhǒushí to the west of the county,
and then entering Lúlíng County to the northeast.
To its south is also the Yúntíngjiāng,
also named Zēngshuǐ,
whose source is in Xīngguó County,
flowing north to Zhūlínkǒu where it empties into the Gànjiāng.
To its west are the Hànhéshì, to its northeast the Huāshítán, and to its southeast the Sāngùshān, three Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Jíshuǐ (Northeast of the prefecture.
Formerly Jíshuǐ Zhōu in the Yuán dynasty.
In the 1st month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, it was demoted to a county.
To its east is Dōngshān.
To its north is Wánglǐng.
To its northeast is also the Jíwénshuǐ,
a tributary of the Gànshuǐ.
To its north is the Báishā Xúnjiǎnsī,
relocated to Sānqūtān northwest of the county,
retaining its old name.)
Yǒngfēng (East of the prefecture.
To its east is Guōshān.
To its south is Shíkōnglǐng,
and also the Ēnjiāng,
which flows down into the Gànjiāng.
To its southeast are the Céngshān, to its south the Shāxī, and also the Biǎohú, three Xúnjiǎnsī.
To its northeast is also the Shìtián Xúnjiǎnsī,
later defunct.)
Ānfú (West of the prefecture,
a little to the north.
Formerly Ānfú Zhōu in the Yuán dynasty.
In the 1st month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, it was demoted to a county.
To its west is Lúxiāoshān,
from which the Lúshuǐ flows,
passing north of the city,
flowing east to join the Wángjiāng,
and then further east to join the Héshuǐ,
entering the Gànjiāng below Shéngāngshān in Lúlíng County.
To its south is the Huángmáo Xúnjiǎnsī,
governing Huángpízhài,
later relocated to Shílóngzhèn west of the county.
To its west is the Luótáng Xúnjiǎnsī,
governing Yángzé,
later relocated to Jiāngbèi,
both retaining their old names.)
Lóngquán (Southwest of the prefecture.
To its southeast is Qiántángshān.
To its west is Shíhánshān.
To its south is the Suíshuǐ,
flowing east into the Gànjiāng.
To its northwest is the Běixiāng Xúnjiǎnsī.
To its southwest is the Héyuán Xúnjiǎnsī,
later relocated to Zuǒ'ānsī west of the county,
retaining its old name.
To its west is the Xiùzhōu Xúnjiǎnsī,
originally Jīntián,
north of the county,
later relocated and
renamed.)
Wàn'ān (South of the prefecture.
To its east is Jiāoyuánshān,
which produces iron.
West of the city is the Gànjiāng.
The river's shoals stretch for three hundred *lǐ*,
with eighteen shoals within the county's borders,
Huángkǒng being the most dangerous.
To its south is also the Zàokǒujiāng,
flowing north from Gànxiàn into the Gànjiāng.
There is the Zàokǒu Xúnjiǎnsī,
southwest of the county.
To its northeast is also the Tāntóu Xúnjiǎnsī.
To its southeast is also the Xīpíngshān Xúnjiǎnsī,
defunct.)
Yǒngxīn (Southwest of the prefecture.
Formerly Yǒngxīn Zhōu in the Yuán dynasty.
In the 1st month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, it was demoted to a county.
To its southeast is Yìshān.
To its west is Qiūshān,
also named Héshān,
from which the Héshuǐ flows,
also named Yǒngxīnjiāng,
flowing down to Tàihé County to enter the Gànjiāng.
To its southeast are the Shàngpíngzhài, to its northwest the Lìchuánzhài, also the Héshānzhài, and also the Xīn'ānzhài, four Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Yǒngníng (Southwest of the prefecture.
To its north is Qīxīlǐng.
To its west is Jiāngshānshuǐ,
whose source is in the border of Húguǎng's Chálíng Zhōu,
flowing south of the county,
and joining the Héjiāng in Yǒngxīn County.
To its west is the Shēngxiāngzhài Xúnjiǎnsī.
To its southwest is the Lóngtóuzhài Xúnjiǎnsī,
soon defunct.)
Línjiāng Fǔ (Formerly Línjiāng Lù in the Yuán dynasty,
belonging to the Jiāngxī Xíngshěng.)
Made a prefecture in the Guǐmǎo year of Tàizǔ's reign.
Administers four counties.
Two hundred seventy *lǐ* northeast of the Bùzhèngsī.
Qīngjiāng (Dependent.
To its east is Gézàoshān,
stretching for over two hundred *lǐ*.
To its south is the Gànjiāng,
also named Qīngjiāng,
with the Qīngjiāngzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī there.
There is also the Yuánjiāng,
flowing in from Xīnyù County,
and joining it south of the county.
To its west is Xiāoshuǐ,
to its south is Gànshuǐ,
both also joining the Gànjiāng at Qīngjiāngzhèn east of the county.
To its southwest is the Tàipíngshì Xúnjiǎnsī,
defunct.)
Xīngàn (South of the prefecture.
Formerly Xīngàn Zhōu in the Yuán dynasty.
In early Hóngwǔ,
it was demoted to a county.
To its northwest is Lílíng,
from which the Gànshuǐ flows.
To its west is also the Qīngjiāng,
and to its south is the Xiàngjiāng,
and the Níjiāng,
all flowing into the Qīngjiāng.
To its east is the Wǎngshān Xúnjiǎnsī,
later relocated to Lánqiáo,
then soon restored.)
Xīnyù (West of the prefecture.
Formerly Xīnyù Zhōu in the Yuán dynasty.
In early Hóngwǔ,
it was demoted to a county.
To its west is Tóngshān,
which formerly produced copper.
To its north is Méngshān.
To its south is the Yúshuǐ,
which is the Yuánjiāng,
into which the Yǐngjiāngshuǐ flows from the north.
To its north is the Shuǐběixū Xúnjiǎnsī.)
Xiájiāng Prefecture (south of
Fǔnán. Originally Xiájiāng Patrol and Inspection Post of Xīngàn County,
it was changed to a county in the 4th month of the 5th year of Jiājìng.
Six townships were detached from Xīngàn County to augment it.
To its south is Yùsī Shān.
There is also the Gànjiāng River,
also named Xiájiāng,
into which Huángjīn Shuǐ flows and joins.
) Yuánzhōu Fǔ (formerly Yuánzhōu Lù in the Yuan dynasty,
subordinate to the Jiāngxī Xíngshěng.)
It became a prefecture in the Gēngzǐ year of Tàizǔ's reign.
It administered four counties.
Its northeast lies 390 lǐ from the Bùzhèngsī.
Yíchūn (the administrative seat.
To its south is Pánlóng Shān.
There is also Yǎng Shān.
Furthermore, Xiùjiāng River is north of the city,
its source is in Píngxiāng County,
it flows through the west of the prefecture,
also called Chóujiāng River,
which is the upper reaches of the Yuánjiāng River.
To the west are Huángpǔ and to the south are Jiànfùlǐng, two Patrol and Inspection Posts.
Fēnyí (east of the prefecture.
To its east is Zhōngshān Xiá.
To its west is Chāngshān Xiá.
The Xiùjiāng River flows between these two gorges,
enters Xīnyù County,
and becomes the Yúshuǐ River.
)〔一一〕
Píngxiāng (west of the prefecture.
Formerly Píngxiāng Zhōu in the Yuan dynasty.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was downgraded to a county.
To its east is Luóxiāo Shān,
from which Luóxiāo Shuǐ originates,
dividing into two branches.
The eastern branch becomes Lúxī Shuǐ,
which further downstream becomes Xiùjiāng River,
entering Yíchūn County.
The western branch enters the border of Lǐlíng County in Húguǎng,
joining Lùshuǐ.
〔一二〕Also, to the west is Píngchuān Shuǐ,
also called Yángqí Shuǐ,
〔一三〕flowing west through the south of the county,
and further downstream joining Lùshuǐ.
To the north are Ānlè Zhèn and to the southeast Dà'ānlǐ, two Patrol and Inspection Posts.
Also, to the west is Cǎoshì Patrol and Inspection Post,
later moved to Chālǐng Guān,
retaining its old name.
Also, to the west is Xiāngdōng Shì.
To the east is Lúxī Zhèn.
Wànzài (north of the prefecture.
To its north is Lóngjiāng River,
which downstream is the Shǔjiāng River of Ruìzhōu Fǔ.
To its northeast, Kānglè Shuǐ flows in.
To its west is Tiěshān Jiè Patrol and Inspection Post.
There is also Gāocūn Zhèn Patrol and Inspection Post,
which was soon abolished.
) Gànzhōu Fǔ (formerly Gànzhōu Lù in the Yuan dynasty,
subordinate to the Jiāngxī Xíngshěng.)
It became a prefecture in the Yǐsì year of Tàizǔ's reign.
It administered twelve counties.
Its northwest lies 1180 lǐ from the Bùzhèngsī.
Gàn (the administrative seat.
To its south is Kōngtóng Shān.
Zhāng Shuǐ and Gòng Shuǐ flank the mountain on its left and right,
flowing through the east and west of the city.
Gòng Shuǐ is also named Dōngjiāng River,
flowing into the prefecture from Chángtīng County, Fújiàn.
Zhāng Shuǐ is also named Xījiāng River,
flowing into the prefecture from Yízhāng County, Húguǎng.
To the north of the city,
they converge to form the Gànjiāng River.
To its north is Guìyuán Patrol and Inspection Post,
later moved to Yōuzhèn.
To its northeast is Módaozhài Patrol and Inspection Post,
later moved to Shíyuànpù.
To its south is Chángluò Patrol and Inspection Post,
later moved to Huángjīn Zhèn, west of the county.
All retained their old names.
Yúdū (east of the prefecture.
To its northeast is Gāoshābǎo Shān.
Also, to the north is Yú Shān,
from which Yúshuǐ originates,
converging with the waters of Níngdū and Huìchāng,
circling the city westward,
and at Gàn County,
joining Gòngshuǐ.
To its northeast is Píngtóuzhài Patrol and Inspection Post.
There were also Yìnshān and Qīngtáng, two Patrol and Inspection Posts,
later abolished.
Xìnfēng (southeast of the prefecture.
To its east is Táojiāng River,
flowing in from Lóngnán County,
passing north of the county,
becoming Xìnfēngjiāng River,
and further downstream flowing into Gòngshuǐ.
To its southeast is Xīntián Patrol and Inspection Post.
To its west are Táozhī Xū,
and also Huángtián and Tántáng,
and to the east there were four newly established Patrol and Inspection Posts,
later abolished.
Xīngguó (northeast of the prefecture.
To its north is Fùsì Shān.
To its northeast is Liànjiāng River,
flowing southwest,
joining Yúshuǐ and entering Gòngjiāng River.
To its east is Yīwěi Xiāng and to its northeast Huílóngzhài, two Patrol and Inspection Posts.
Huìchāng (east of the prefecture,
slightly south.
Formerly Huìchāng Zhōu in the Yuan dynasty.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was downgraded to a county.
To its south is Sìwàng Shān,
below which is Yángjiǎoshuǐ Ài.
To its north is Xiānghóng Shuǐ,
which is Gòngshuǐ,
flowing northwest,
meeting Yúshuǐ.
To its south is Xiāngxiāngzhài and to its north Chéngxiāngzhèn, two Patrol and Inspection Posts.
Also, to the west is Hékǒu Patrol and Inspection Post,
later abolished.
Ānyuǎn (south of the prefecture.
Formerly subordinate to Níngdū Zhōu in the Yuan dynasty.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was changed to be subordinate to the prefecture.
To its west is Ānyuǎn Shuǐ,
also called Liánshuǐ,
flowing into Gòngshuǐ in Huìchāng County.
Also, to its south is Sānbǎikēng Shuǐ,
further downstream flowing into Lóngchuān County, Guǎngdōng.
To its northwest is Bǎnkǒu Patrol and Inspection Post.
Níngdū (northeast of the prefecture.
Formerly Níngdū Zhōu in the Yuan dynasty.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was downgraded to a county.
To its northwest is Jīnjīng Shān.
To its north is Méilǐng.
To its south is Níngdū Shuǐ,
which converges with Sǎnshuǐ, Yúndāng, Qǔyáng, Huángshā, and Chánglè, five waters.
Also, to its northeast is Qiánhuà Shuǐ,
all further downstream entering Yúshuǐ.
There is also Méichuān Shuǐ,
originating from Méilǐng,
further downstream also passing through Yúdū County and entering Gòngshuǐ.
To its southeast is Xiàhézhài Patrol and Inspection Post.
Ruìjīn (east of the prefecture.
Formerly subordinate to Huìchāng Zhōu in the Yuan dynasty.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was changed to be subordinate to the prefecture.
To its northeast is Chénshí Shān,
from which Miánjiāng River originates,
flowing south of the county into Gòngshuǐ,
and then west into Huìchāng County,
becoming Xiānghóng Shuǐ.
To its northwest is Ruìlín and to its northeast Húpí, two Patrol and Inspection Posts.
To its southeast is Gǔchéng Zhèn,
a route leading to Chángtīng County, Fújiàn.
Lóngnán (south of the prefecture.
Formerly subordinate to Níngdū Zhōu in the Yuan dynasty.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was changed to be subordinate to the prefecture.
To its southwest is Dōngtáo Shān,
from which Táoshuǐ originates,
flowing northeast and converging with various waters.
To the north of the county, below Gōng Shān,
it joins Wò Shuǐ and Lián Shuǐ to form Sānjiāngkǒu,
and then flows north to become the Táojiāng River of Xìnfēng County.
There is Dōngtáo Ài.
In the early Chóngzhēn reign,
the Xiàlì Patrol and Inspection Post of Dìngnán County was moved to be stationed there.
Shíchéng (northeast of the prefecture.
In the 11th month of the 1st year of Yuánzhēn in the Yuan dynasty, it became subordinate to Níngdū Zhōu.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was changed to be subordinate to the prefecture.
To its north is Yáshū Shān.
To its east is Bàshuǐ,
which southwest joins Qiánhuà Shuǐ,
entering Gòngjiāng River.
To its north is Zhuōshāzhài Patrol and Inspection Post,
later moved to Chìjiāng Shì, west of the county,
retaining its old name.
Dìngnán (Southeast of the prefecture.
In the third month of the third year of Lóngqìng
and land from Ānyuǎn and Xìnfēng counties was added to it.
To its northwest is Chéng Lǐng,
and further south is Shénxiān Lǐng.
To its east is Zhǐhuī Fēng.
To its northeast is Jiǔzhōu Hé,
whose lower course joins the Táo Jiāng in Xìnfēng Xiàn.
To its northeast is the Xiàlì Xúnjiǎnsī,
which later moved to Gāoshā Liántáng,
and then again to Dōngtáo Ài in Lóngnán Xiàn.
Chángníng (Southeast of the prefecture.
In the third month of the fourth year of Wànlì
and land from Huìchāng Xiàn was added to it.
To its southeast is Dǐng Shān,
and further south is Dàmào Shān,
both bordering the territories of Mǐn and Guǎng.
Further east is Xúnwù Shuǐ,
which flows into Lóngchuān Xiàn in Guǎngdōng.
To its northwest is the Huángxiāng Xúnjiǎnsī.
To its south is the Xīnpíng Xúnjiǎnsī,
originally Dàdūn,
later renamed.
To its north are Shuāngqiáo and to its south is Dānzhúlóu, two Xúnjiǎnsī,
which were later abolished.
)Nán'ān Fǔ (Originally Nán'ān Lù in the Yuán dynasty,
belonging to Jiāngxī Xíngshěng.)
In the Yǐsì year of Tàizǔ's reign, it became a prefecture.
It governed four counties.
It is 1,520 lǐ northeast of the Bùzhèngsī.
Dàyǔ (A dependency.
To its southwest is Dàyǔ Lǐng,
one of the Wǔ Lǐng,
also known as Méi Lǐng,
with a pass on it called Méi Guān.
There is also Zhāng Jiāng,
also called Nán Jiāng,
also called Héng Jiāng,
whose lower course joins Gòng Shuǐ.
To its west is the Yùlín Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī,
its seat in Jīngdū Cūn,
later moved to Fújiāng Ài,
and again to Huángní Gǎng.
To its northeast is the Chìshí Lǐng Xúnjiǎnsī,
its seat in Fēngshān Lǐ,
later moved to Xiǎoxī Chéng,
then again to Fēngshān Xīnchéng,
and later to Fēngshān Shuǐxī Cūn,
all retaining their old names.
To the south of the county is Shuǐnán Chéng,
facing the prefectural city across the river,
built in the 40th year of Jiājìng
To its northwest is Xīntián Chéng.
Further north is Fènghuáng Chéng,
and further west is Yángméi Chéng,
both built in the 44th year of Jiājìng
Further east is Jiǔsuǒ Chéng,
also built in the 44th year of Jiājìng
Nánkāng (Northeast of the prefecture.
To its northwest is Qín Shān,
from which Qín Shuǐ emerges,
flowing eastward to Nánkǒu where it enters Zhāng Jiāng.
To its north is Yánglǐng Shān.
To its south is Fúróng Jiāng,
which is Zhāng Jiāng.
To its northeast is Tánkǒu Zhèn and to its north is Xiāng'ān Zhèn, two Xúnjiǎnsī.
Shàngyóu (Northeast of the prefecture.
Originally Yǒngqīng Xiàn in the Yuán dynasty.
In the early Hóngwǔ reign,
it was renamed.
To its west is Shū Shān,
also called Tàifù Shān.
To its east is Dàyóu Shān,
from which Yóu Shuǐ emerges,
flowing downstream to Nánkāng Xiàn,
where it enters Zhāng Jiāng.
To its west is the Fúlóng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Tàifù Cūn,
retaining its old name.
Chóngyì (North of the prefecture.
In the third month of the 14th year of Zhèngdé
and land from Dàyǔ and Nánkāng counties was added to it.
To its southwest is Nièdū Shān.
To its west is Tǒng Gāng.
There is also Zhāng Jiāng,
flowing in from Yízhāng Xiàn in Húguǎng.
There is also Héng Shuǐ,
passing south of the county.
Further southwest is Zuǒ Xī,
whose lower courses all join Zhāng Jiāng.
To its northwest is the Shàngbǎo Xúnjiǎnsī,
originally Guòbù,
later moved and renamed.
To its southwest is the Qiánchǎng Xúnjiǎnsī,
originally in Qián Shān,
later moved to Nièdū.
To its southeast is the Chánglóng Xúnjiǎnsī,
originally seated in Lóngpíng Lǐ,
later moved to Jiāngtóu in Shàngdé Lǐ, northeast of the county,
all retaining their old names.

Gazetteer 20, Geography 5, Húguǎng, Zhèjiāng
Húguǎng.
The regions of Jīng, Yáng, Liáng, and Yù prefectures in Yǔ Gòng.
In the Yuán dynasty, the Húguǎng Děngchù Xíngzhōngshūshěng was established,
(with its seat in Wǔchāng Lù,)
and the Húnán Dào Xuānwèisī (with its seat in Tiānlín Lù) was also established and belonged to it.
Xiāngyáng and three other circuits were assigned to the Hénán Jiāngběi Děngchù Xíngzhōngshūshěng,
and the Jīnghú Běidào Xuānwèisī (with its seat in Zhōngxīng Lù) was also established and belonged to it.
In the second month of the Jiǎchén year of Tàizǔ's reign, Chén Lǐ was pacified,
and the Húguǎng Děngchù Xíngzhōngshūshěng was established.
In the 12th month of the third year of Hóngwǔ, the Wǔchāng Dūwèi was established.
(Governed concurrently with the Xíngzhōngshūshěng.)
In the 10th month of the eighth year, the Dūwèi was reformed into the Húguǎng Dūzhīhuīshǐsī.
In the sixth month of the ninth year, the Xíngzhōngshūshěng was reformed into the Chéngxuān Bùzhèngshǐsī.
It governed 15 prefectures,
two directly administered departments,
17 subordinate departments,
108 counties,
two Xuānwèisī,
four Xuānfǔsī,
five Ānfǔsī,
21 Zhǎngguānsī,
and five Mányí Zhǎngguānsī.
(Comprising more than 3,480 lǐ.)
North to Jūnzhōu,
(bordering Hénán and Shǎnxī.)
South to Jiǔyí,
(bordering Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī.)
East to Qízhōu,
(bordering Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī.)
West to Shīzhōu,
(bordering Sìchuān and Guìzhōu.)
It is 1,715 lǐ from Nánjīng,
and 5,170 lǐ from the capital.
In the 26th year of Hóngwǔ, the registered households numbered 775,851,
and the population 4,702,660.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì,
households were 504,870,
and population 3,781,714.
In the sixth year of Wànlì,
households were 541,310,
and population 4,398,785.
Wǔchāng Fǔ (Originally Wǔchāng Lù in the Yuán dynasty,
belonging to Húguǎng Xíngshěng.)
In the second month of the Jiǎchén year of Tàizǔ's reign, it became a prefecture.
It governed one department [zhōu] and nine counties.
Jiāngxià (A dependency.
In the fourth month of the third year of Hóngwǔ, the residence of the Prince of Chǔ was built on Huánglóng Shān within the city.
To its east is Huánghú Shān,
below which is Huánghú Jī,
facing the Great River.
Further south is Jīn Shuǐ,
also called Tú Shuǐ,
flowing west to Jīnkǒu where it enters the river.
There is the Jīnkǒu Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī there.
Further north is Hǔhuáng Zhōu and southwest is Niányúkǒu Zhèn, two Xúnjiǎnsī.
Wǔchāng (East of the prefecture.
To its west is Fán Shān,
also called Xī Shān,
producing silver, copper, iron, and amethyst.
To its south is Shénrén Shān,
below which is Báilù Jī.
To its west is Xīsài Shān,
bordering Dàyě Xiàn.
To its north, it borders the river,
with Lú Zhōu in the middle,
also called Luó Zhōu.
Further southwest is Fán Gǎng,
also called Fán Xī,
also called Yuán Xī,
gathering from 99 lakes and marshes south of the county,
entering the Great River to the north,
where it is called Fánkǒu.
Further east is Nán Hú,

Jìngzhōu (In the Yuán dynasty, Jìngzhōu Lù,
directly subordinate to Húguǎng Xíngshěng.)
In the *Yǐsì* year of Tàizǔ's reign, in the seventh month, it became Jìngzhōu Jūnmín Ānfǔsī.
In the first year, it was downgraded to a department.
In the third year, it was elevated to a prefecture.
In the fourth month of the ninth year, it was again downgraded to a department,
with Yǒngpíng Xiàn, the seat of the department, merged into it,
directly subordinate to the Bùzhèngsī.
(To the south is Shìláng Shān,

Its distance from the Bùzhèngsī to the northeast was 1,850 *lǐ*.

During the Yuán dynasty, the Jiāngzhè and other Provincial Secretariat Branches were established,
(governing Hángzhōu Lù,)
and further divided into the Zhèdōng Circuit Pacification Commission,
(governing Qìngyuán Lù,)
which was subordinate to it.
In the 戊xū year of Tàizǔ's reign, 12th month, a branch of the Central Secretariat was established.
(Governing Níngyuè Fǔ.
In the 癸mǎo year, 2nd month, its seat was moved to Yánzhōu Fǔ.)
In the 丙wǔ year, 12th month, the branch secretariat was abolished,
and the Zhèjiāng and other Provincial Secretariat Branches were established.
(Governing Hángzhōu Fǔ.)
In the 3rd year of Hóngwǔ, 12th month, the Hángzhōu Metropolitan Guard was established.
(Administered jointly with the Provincial Secretariat Branch.)
In the 8th year, 10th month, the Metropolitan Guard was reorganized into the Zhèjiāng Regional Military Commission.
In the 9th year, 6th month, the Provincial Secretariat Branch was reorganized into the Administration Commission.
It administered eleven prefectures,

and seventy-five counties.
