flowing from south of the county seat into Liǔxī.
To the west is Shǒugē Lǐng Patrol and Inspection Department,
moved to Zhūliǔ Cūn southwest of the county,
then to Zhàn Cūn west of the county,
then to Yángjiā Táng,
retaining its old name.)
Yánzhōu Fǔ (The Yuán dynasty's Jiàndé Lù,
belonged to the Jiāngzhè Provincial Secretariat Branch.)
In the 戊xū year of Tàizǔ's reign, 3rd month, it was made Jiàn'ān Fǔ,
soon renamed Jiàndé Fǔ.
In the 壬yín year, 2nd month, it was renamed Yánzhōu Fǔ.
It administered six counties.
Its northeast is 270 li from the Provincial Administration Commission.
Jiàndé (Dependent.
To its north is Wūlóng Shān.
To its west is Tóngguān Shān.
Moreover, the Xīn'ān Jiāng river flows in from Chún'ān Xiàn,
passes south of the city,
and the Dōngyáng Jiāng river comes from the southwest to join it.
Also, to its northeast is Xūxī,
which flows into the river,
and is called Xūkǒu,
also known as Jiàndé Jiāng.
To its east is the Guǎnjiè Patrol and Inspection Division.
Tónglú (Northeast of the prefecture.
To its west is Fùchūn Shān,
also named Yánlíng Shān.
Tóng Jiāng is to its south,
which is the Zhèjiāng river,
also known as Mù Jiāng.
It flows in from Jiàndé Xiàn,
passes below the fishing platform of Fùchūn Shān,
where it is called Qīlǐ Lài,
and then to the east, passes below Tóngjūn Shān,
where it is called Tóng Jiāng.
Tóngxī flows in from the county's northeast,
where it is called Tóngjiāngkǒu,
its upper reaches being Tiānmù Xī of Fēnshuǐ Xiàn.
There was a Tóngjiāng Patrol and Inspection Division,
later moved to Tóngjūn Shān,
and then to Zhǎixī Bù.
Chún'ān (West of the prefecture.
To its south is Yúnméng Shān.
To its west is Dūdū Shān,
and also Wēipíng Dòng,
also named Qīngxī Dòng,
and also known as Bāngyuán Dòng.
To its south is Xīn'ān Jiāng,
flowing in from Nánzhí Shè Xiàn,
also named Qīngxī.
To its west were Jiēkǒu, and also Yǒngpíng, and to its south Hángkǒu, three Patrol and Inspection Divisions,
later abolished.
To its east is Jǐnxī Guān,
established during the Jiājìng era.
Suì'ān (West of the prefecture,
slightly south.
To its west is Wǔqiáng Xī,
where Shuāngxī flows in to join it,
called Sāndù Kǒu,
passing south of the city,
flowing northeast into Qīngxī of Chún'ān.
To its south was the Fènglín Patrol and Inspection Division,
later abolished.
Shòuchāng (Southwest of the prefecture.
To its southeast is Yándòng Shān.
To its west is Shòuchāng Xī,
flowing northeast to Jiàndé Xiàn,
entering Xīn'ān Jiāng.
To its south is Chánglè Xī,
flowing southeast to Lánxī Xiàn,
entering Dōngyáng Jiāng.
To its west was Shètián, and to its southwest Shàngméi, two Patrol and Inspection Divisions.
Fēnshuǐ (Northeast of the prefecture.
To its east is Tiānmù Xī,
its upper reaches being Zǐxī of Yúqián Xiàn and Liǔxī of Chānghuà Xiàn.
Its lower reaches are Tóngxī of Tónglú Xiàn.
Also, to its southeast is Qiánxī,
flowing in from Chún'ān Xiàn,
flowing east into Tiānmù Xī.
To its east was Wúcūn Patrol and Inspection Division,
later abolished.
) Jiāxīng Fǔ (Originally Jiāxīng Lù in the Yuan dynasty,
subordinate to the Jiāngzhè Xíngshěng.
) In the *bǐngwǔ* year of Tàizǔ's reign (1366), in the eleventh month, it was made a prefecture,
directly administered by the capital.
In the fourteenth year (1381), in the eleventh month, its administration was changed to Zhèjiāng.
It governed seven counties.
It is 195 *lǐ* southwest of the Bùzhèng Sī.
Jiāxīng (Dependent.
To its south is Nánhú,
also named Yuānyāng Hú,
which flows into the Grand Canal.
There is also Chángshuǐ Táng,
which connects to Hǎiníng in the southwest,
and to the border of Hǎiyán Xiàn in the northeast.
Also, to its east is Shuāngxī,
which flows out to the east as Huátíng Táng,
and the grain transport boats of Nánzhí Sōngjiāng Fǔ
enter the Grand Canal from here.
Xiùshuǐ (Dependent.
Established in the third month of the fifth year of Xuāndé (1430) by carving out land from Jiāxīng Xiàn.
To its west is the Grand Canal,
which passes north through Wénjiā Hú,
reaching the Grand Canal of Nánzhí Wújiāng Xiàn.
To its northeast are the Shānqīng Zhá and Wángjiāngjìng, two Patrol and Inspection Divisions.
Jiāshàn (East of the prefecture.
Originally Wèitáng Zhèn Patrol and Inspection Division of Jiāxīng Xiàn,
it was changed to a county in the third month of the fifth year of Xuāndé (1430).
To its south is Huátíng Tánghé,
to its east Wèitáng Hé,
to its northeast Qīngfēng Jīng,
all flowing into it.
To its northwest is Fēnhú,
which forms the boundary with Nánzhí Wújiāng Xiàn.
Also to its north is Zhāngliàn Tángshuǐ,
which also flows into Huátíng Tánghé,
reaching Mǎohú of Huátíng Xiàn.
To its northeast were Fēngjīng, and to its northwest Táozhuāng, two Patrol and Inspection Divisions,
now abolished.
Chóngdé (Southwest of the prefecture.
Originally Chóngdé Zhōu in the Yuan dynasty.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ (1369) it was downgraded to a county.
To its northwest is the Grand Canal,
flowing in from Déqīng Xiàn.
To its southeast is Yǔxī,
also named Yǔ'ér Zhōngjīng,
and also named Shāzhǔ Táng.
Also, to its northeast is Shímén Tángshuǐ,
connecting to the Grand Canal in the southeast,
and reaching Wūzhèn of Guī'ān in the north.
Tóngxiāng (West of the prefecture,
slightly south.
Established in the third month of the fifth year of Xuāndé (1430) from Fèngmíng Xiāng of Chóngdé Xiàn.
To its north is the Grand Canal,
bordering Chóngdé Xiàn.
There is also Lànxī,
which reaches Yīngdòu Hú of Wújiāng Xiàn in the north,
and Xúnxī of Húzhōu Fǔ in the west.
To its north is Zàolín Zhèn Patrol and Inspection Division.
Pínghú (East of the prefecture.
Established in the third month of the fifth year of Xuāndé (1430) from Dāngtú Zhèn of Hǎiyán Xiàn.
To its southeast is Gùyì Shān.
To its south is Yǎ Shān,
popularly called Wǎ Shān.
Also, Dānghú is east of the county seat,
its lower reaches flowing out into the sea at Hǎiyán Gěnpǔ Kǒu.
To its west is Shìxī Hé,
flowing in from Jiāxīng Xiàn,
and entering Dānghú.
Its branch flowing south
enters the sea via Zhàpǔ southeast of the county;
that flowing north
enters the sea via Lúlì Pǔ northeast of the county.
Next to the *pǔ* is the Lúlì Saltworks.
Also, to its north is Dōngmǎo,
which is the upper reaches of Huátíng Sānmǎo.
To its east was Báishāwān Patrol and Inspection Division,
governing Guǎngchén Shù,
later moved to Dúshān southeast of the county.
Also, to its southeast was Zhàpǔ Zhèn Patrol and Inspection Division,
later moved to Liángzhuāng,
retaining its old name.
Hǎiyán (Southeast of the prefecture.
Originally Hǎiyán Zhōu in the Yuan dynasty.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ (1369) it was downgraded to a county.
To its south is Qínzhù Shān,
and also Chángqiáng Shān.
To its southwest is Fènghuáng Shān.
To its northeast is Tāng Shān,
and also Dú Shān,
where a saltworks was formerly established.
To its east it borders the sea,
with a sea dike for defense,
totaling 4,800 *zhàng* from north to south.
There are also the Dōng, Xī, and Nán three sea outlets,
and the Xī Hǎikǒu, located northeast of the county,
is especially strategic.
To its northeast is Lǚ Gǎng,
with a saltworks at its mouth.
To its southwest is Báoláng Shì,
with a Salt Tax Administration.
To its northeast was the Shǒuyù Zhàpǔ Qiānhù Suǒ,
and to its southeast the Gěnpǔ Shǒuyù Qiānhù Suǒ,
both established in the tenth month of the nineteenth year of Hóngwǔ (1386).
East of the city was Hǎikǒu Patrol and Inspection Division,
later moved to Shāyāo Cūn,
and to its south Gěnpǔ Patrol and Inspection Division,
later moved to Qínzhù Shān,
both retaining their old names.
) Húzhōu Fǔ (Originally Húzhōu Lù in the Yuan dynasty,
subordinate to the Jiāngzhè Xíngshěng.
) In the *bǐngwǔ* year of Tàizǔ's reign (1366), in the eleventh month, it was made a prefecture,
directly administered by the capital.
In the fourteenth year (1381), in the eleventh month, its administration was changed to Zhèjiāng.
It governed one *zhōu*
and six counties.
It is 190 *lǐ* south of the Bùzhèng Sī.
Wūchéng (The seat of the prefecture.
To the north is Biànshān,
also called Biànshān.
To the southwest is Shíchéngshān.
To the south is Xiànshān,
originally named Xiǎnshān.
To the southwest is Tóngshān,
also named Tóngxiànshān.
To the north is Tàihú,
bordering the prefectural boundaries of Sūzhōu and Chángzhōu in Nánzhí.
To the northeast are the two outlets of Dàqiánhú and Xiǎoméihú.
All the waters within the prefectural territory flow into Tàihú here.
To the west is Tiáoxī,
originating from the northern slopes of Tiānmù in Xiàofēng,
flowing past the foot of Píshān,
To the south is Yúbùxī,
which is Tiáoxī within Hángzhōu's territory,
flowing from Déqīng Xiàn past the south of the prefecture,
converging to form Yùhú,
also called Zhàxī.
To the east is the Hòupān Cūn Xúnjiǎn Sī,
later moved to Nánxún Zhèn,
retaining its old name.
To the northeast is the Dàqiánhú Kǒu Xúnjiǎn Sī.
Guī'ān (The seat of the prefecture.
To the south is Jīngàishān,
also named Héshān.
There is also Héngshān.
To the east is Shēngshān,
also called Wūshān,
and also Ōuyúshān.
The Grand Canal is to the east of the city,
originating from the two waters of Tiáoxī and Yúbùxī,
dividing into the Grand Canal,
flowing northeast through Nánxún Zhèn,
entering the boundary of Wújiāng Xiàn,
and joining the Grand Canal of Jiāxīng.
To the south is Díyáng,
also called Dígǎng,
connecting to the Grand Canal to the northeast.
Its branch stream flows southeast out of Wūzhèn,
and joins Lànxī of Tóngxiāng.
which is a branch of Yúbùxī,
flowing through Nánxún.
To the southeast is Liánshì Xúnjiǎn Sī.
To the southwest is Shàngwò Bù Xúnjiǎn Sī,
later abolished.
Chángxīng (Northwest of the prefecture.
Originally Chángxīng Zhōu in the Yuan dynasty.
In the Dīngyǒu year of Tàizǔ's reign, in the third month, its name was changed to Cháng'ān Zhōu.
In the Rènyín year, it was restored to Chángxīng.
In the second year of Hóngwǔ, it was downgraded to a county.
To the northwest is Gùzhǔshān,
which produces tea,
also named Xīgùshān,
and also Wúwàngshān.
To the northeast is Tàihú,
which forms the boundary with Yíxīng Xiàn of Nánzhí by dividing the middle of the flow.
To the west is Ruòxī,
flowing downstream into Tàihú.
To the southwest is Jīngxī,
flowing southeast into Tiáoxī.
To the northeast are Gāotáng and to the southwest are Sì'ān, two Xúnjiǎn Sī.
To the west are Héxī and to the south are Hépíng, two Xúnjiǎn Sī,
which were abolished.
Déqīng (South of the prefecture,
slightly to the east.
To the northeast is Gǎnsānshān.
To the southeast is the Grand Canal,
and Yúbùxī,
also called Zhàxī,
which is another name for Tiáoxī.
To the northeast is Xīnshì Zhèn Xúnjiǎn Sī.
To the east is Xiàtáng Xúnjiǎn Sī,
later moved to Wǔliǔ Gǎngkǒu.
To the east is Héyè Pǔ Xúnjiǎn Sī,
which was abolished.
Wǔkāng (Southwest of the prefecture.
To the east is Fēngshān,
also named Fángfēngshān.
There is also Yúshān.
To the southwest is Fùzhōushān.
To the south is Qiánxī,
into which Hòuxī flows from the northeast,
flowing downstream into Déqīng's Yúbùxī.
) Ānjí Zhōu (Originally Ānjí Xiàn in the Yuan dynasty.
) In the eleventh month of the first year of Zhèngdé, it was elevated to a zhōu.
(To the southwest is an old city.
During Hóngwǔ, it was relocated to its current seat.
To the southeast is Báiyángshān,
which formerly produced tin.
To the west is Tiáoxī.
There is also Lóngxī,
which is a branch of Tiáoxī.
To the southeast is Dúsōng Guān Xúnjiǎn Sī.
There was also Dìpù Xúnjiǎn Sī,
which was abolished.
) It is twenty *lǐ* northeast of the prefectural seat.
It administers
one county.
Xiàofēng (Southwest of the zhōu.
Established in the twenty-third year of Chénghuà by carving out land from Ānjí Xiàn,
and was subordinate to the prefecture.
In the second year of Zhèngdé, it was changed to be subordinate to the zhōu.
To the south is Tiānmùshān.
There is the Tiānmùshān Xúnjiǎn Sī.
To the southwest is Jīnshíshān,
which is the highest point of Tiānmù.
To the south is Tiáoxī,
which originates from Tiānmùshān.
This is another source of Tiáoxī.
To the west is Sōngkēng Xúnjiǎn Sī.
) Shàoxīng Fǔ (Originally Shàoxīng Lù in the Yuan dynasty,
subordinate to the Zhèdōng Dào Xuānwèi Sī.
) In the twelfth month of the Bǐngwǔ year of Tàizǔ's reign, it was made a prefecture.
It administers eight counties.
It is 138 *lǐ* northwest of the Bùzhèng Sī.
Shānyīn (The seat of the prefecture.
To the south is Kuàijīshān,
its branch mountain being Yúnménshān.
There is also Fǎhuáshān.
To the southwest is Lántíngshān.
To the northwest is Túshān.
To the north it borders the sea,
with Sānjiāngkǒu.
The three rivers are:
one is Zhèjiāng;
one is Qiánqīngjiāng,
which is the lower reach of Púyángjiāng,
its upper source flowing in from Pújiāng Xiàn,
to Qiánqīng Zhèn west of the county,
it is called Qiánqīngjiāng;
one is Cáowánjiāng,
which is the lower reach of Yǎnxī,
its upper source flowing in from Shèng Xiàn,
turning east then north,
passing the Cáowá Miào east of the prefecture,
it is Cáowájiāng,
then turning west then north,
meeting Qiánqīngjiāng and Zhèjiāng and flowing into the sea.
To the west is the Grand Canal,
flowing in from Xiāoshān Xiàn,
then southeast through Kuàijī Xiàn,
then east into the boundary of Shàngyú Xiàn.
To the south is Jiànhú,
fourteen or fifteen *lǐ* long,
commonly known as Báitǎyáng,
into which Ruòyéxī converges.
To the north is Báishuǐhú,
which connects to the Grand Canal.
To the north is Sānjiāng Shǒuyù Qiānhù Suǒ,
on the sunny side of Fúshān,
established in the second month of the twentieth year of Hóngwǔ.
There is also Sānjiāng Xúnjiǎn Sī,
in Fúshān Táosōng Zhuāng.
To the northwest is Báiyáng Xúnjiǎn Sī.
Kuàijī (The seat of the prefecture.
To the southeast is Kuàijīshān,
its eastern part connecting to Wǎnwěi, Qínwàng, and Tiānzhù mountains.
To the east are Yínshān and Xīshān,
which formerly produced silver ore and tin.
To the southeast is Ruòyéshān.
To the east is Cáowánjiāng.
To the southeast is Píngshuǐxī,
which joins Yǎnxī to the south.
To the northeast is Lìhǎi Shǒuyù Qiānhù Suǒ,
established in the second month of the twentieth year of Hóngwǔ.
There was also Huángjiāyàn Xúnjiǎn Sī,
later moved west of Lìhǎi Suǒ,
then moved to Zhuànfēng Zhèn within Shàngyú Xiàn's boundary,
retaining its old name.
Xiāoshān (northwest of the prefecture.
To the southwest is Hǔzhuǎ Shān.
To the southeast is Kān Shān.
Both overlook the Zhèjiāng River.
Beside Kān Shān is a small mountain called Biēzǐ Shān.
The Zhèjiāng River flows from the west of the county northeast,
emerging from it,
and connects to the great sea in the east,
also called Hǎimén.
To the southeast is Xiá Shān.
The Qiánqīng Jiāng River passes through it,
then turns north and east again,
entering the border of Shānyīn Xiàn.
To the west of the city is the Grand Canal,
which connects to the Qiánqīng Jiāng River in the east.
There is also Xiāng Hú.
To the southwest is the Yúpǔ Xúnjiǎnsī.
Further west is Xīxīng,
also called Xīlíng.
Those going to Qiántáng cross the river from here.
Zhūjì (southwest of the prefecture.
During the Yuán dynasty, it was Zhūjì Zhōu.
In the first month of the Jǐhài year of Tàizǔ's reign, it was renamed Zhūquán Zhōu.
In the twelfth month of the Bǐngwǔ year, it was demoted to Zhūjì Xiàn.
To the southwest is Xīnchéng,
at the foot of Wǔzhǐ Shān.
It was built by Lǐ Wénzhōng
in the Guǐmǎo year of Tàizǔ's reign.
To the west is Cháng Shān.
There is also Wǔxiè Shān.
To the south is Gōuchéng Shān.
There is also Huàn Jiāng,
which is Púyáng Jiāng,
also called Qīngyì Jiāng.
To the southwest were Chángqīng Guān and to the west Yángtáng Guān, two Xúnjiǎnsī,
now abolished.
Yúyáo (northeast of the prefecture.
During the Yuán dynasty, it was Yúyáo Zhōu.
In the early Hóngwǔ era,
it was demoted to a county.
To the south is Xīnchéng,
facing the county seat across the river.
The Yáo Jiāng River flows through it.
To the south is Sìmíng Shān.
To the north it borders the sea.
The Yáo Jiāng River originates from Tàipíng Shān to the southwest of the county,
also named Shùn Jiāng.
It flows northwest to Shàngyú Xiàn,
then turns northeast and exits,
passing south of the county.
Further east it becomes the Qián Jiāng of Cíxī.
To the northeast is Zhúxī Hú,
whose flow is diverted to form the Dōnghéng Hé.
To the west is Móushān Hú,
whose flow is diverted to form the Xīhéng Hé.
Both flow into the Yáo Jiāng River.
To the northwest is Línshān Wèi,
established in the second month of the twentieth year of Hóngwǔ.
To the northeast is Sānshān Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ,
also named Hǔshān,
also established in the second month of the twentieth year of Hóngwǔ.
To the northeast is Sānshān Xúnjiǎnsī,
located on Jīnjiā Shān,
later moved to Pò Shān.
To the north is Méishān Xúnjiǎnsī,
located at Méishān Zhài,
later moved to Húhǎitóu, northwest of the county.
There is also Miàoshān Xúnjiǎnsī,
located at Miàoshān Zhài,
later moved to Zhōngyuán Yàn in the border of Shàngyú Xiàn,
retaining its old name.
Shàngyú (east of the prefecture.
To the northwest is Xiàgài Shān,
with its northern side against the sea,
and its southern side overlooking Xiàgài Hú.
To the southwest is Dōng Shān.
To the east is Fùzhī Shān,
connecting to the border of Shèng Xiàn.
Further east is Tōngmíng Jiāng,
which is the upper reaches of the Yáo Jiāng River.
There is also the Grand Canal,
in front of the county seat.
To the northwest is Báimǎ Hú,
which connects to Xiàgài Hú in the north.
Connected to it is Shàngfēi Hú,
also called Shàngpí Hú.
Its flow is diverted to form Wǔfū Hú,
〔一七〕which reaches Yúyáo's Xīhéng Hé in the northeast.
To the west is Liánghú Xúnjiǎnsī,
originally located at Liáng Hú,
later moved to Bǎiguān Shì,
retaining its old name.
Shèng (southeast of the prefecture.
To the east is Dānchí Shān.
To the northeast is Shèng Shān.
To the north is Tuó Shān.
There is also Qīngfēng Lǐng.
To the west is Tàibái Shān.
To the south is Yǎn Xī,
whose source is in the various mountains of Tiāntái,
and whose lower reaches form the Cáozē Jiāng River.
To the west were Chánglè Zhèn and to the northwest Guǎnjiě Zhài, two Xúnjiǎnsī,
now abolished.
Xīnchāng (southeast of the prefecture.
To the east is Wòzhōu Shān.
To the southeast is Tiānmǔ Shān.
Further east is Dōng Xī,
whose source is in Tiāntái Shān,
and which flows northwest into the border of Shèng Xiàn.
To the south were Cǎixiá Zhèn, Fēnglè, and Shànzhèng, three Xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.
)Níngbō Fǔ (During the Yuán dynasty, it was Qìngyuán Lù,
subordinate to Zhèdōng Dào Xuānwèisī.
)In the twelfth month of the first year of Tàizǔ's Wú reign, it became Míngzhōu Fǔ.
In the second month of the fourteenth year of Hóngwǔ, it was renamed Níngbō.
It governs five counties.
It is 360 lǐ northwest of the Bùzhèngsī.
Yín (adjacent.
To the east is Mào Shān.
To the southwest is Sìmíng Shān,
circling over 800 lǐ.
To the east is Guàndǐng Shān,
which formerly produced iron.
To the southeast is Āyùwáng Shān.
There are Tàibái and Tiāntóng mountains.
To the northeast it borders the sea.
There is Yín Jiāng,
also named Yǒng Jiāng.
To the southeast is Fènghuà Jiāng.
To the northwest is Cíxī.
All flow and converge there.
To the southwest is Xiǎojiāng Hú.
Further west is Guǎngdé Hú.
To the east is Dōngqián Hú.
All divert their flow into Yín Jiāng.
To the north is Lóngshān Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ,
established in the eleventh month of the nineteenth year of Hóngwǔ.
To the east is Yǒngdōng Xúnjiǎnsī,
located at Yǒngdōng Yú,
later moved to Zhúshān Hǎikǒu, southeast of Dìnghǎi Xiàn,
retaining its old name.
There were also Dàishān and Luófēng, two Xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.
Cíxī (northwest of the prefecture.
During the Yuán dynasty, it was called Cíxī.
In the sixteenth year of Yǒnglè, the character
was changed
to "谿".
To the southwest is Chē Shān.
To the northeast it borders the sea.
To the south is Cíxī,
also called Qián Jiāng,
which is the lower reaches of the Yáo Jiāng River.
Lán Xī, Wén Xī, and other waters all flow and converge there.
To the northwest is Mínghè Yánkèsī.
Guānhǎi Wèi is also to the northwest,
established in the eleventh month of the nineteenth year of Hóngwǔ.
There is also Sōngpǔ Xúnjiǎnsī,
located at Pǔdōng,
later moved to Pǔxī.
There is also Xiàngtóu Xúnjiǎnsī,
located at Xiàngtóu Zhài,
later moved to Yángpǔ,
abolished,

contiguous with Yùhuán Shān.
