in the sea.
Further to the northwest is Jīngxī.
Also, beside the county seat are Dōng and Xī (East and West) Erxī.
To the southwest is Guǎntóujiāng.
To the west is Xiàngpǔhé,
to the northeast is Shímǎgǎng,
all their lower courses reach the sea.
There is Chánglín Salt Pan.
Further to the west is Pánshí Wèi,
established in the twentieth year of Hóngwǔ (1387), second month.
To the east is Pánshí Shǒuyù Hòuxiānhùsuǒ,
established in the fifth year of Chénghuà (1469).
To the northeast is Púqí Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ,
also established in the twentieth year of Hóngwǔ (1387), second month.
To the west is Guǎntóu Xúnjiǎnsī,
moved its seat to Qítóuzhài southwest of the county,
later restored.
To the southeast is Běijiān Xúnjiǎnsī,
its seat at the foot of Yùhuánshān,
soon moved to Cài'ào northeast of the county,
then moved to Báishālǐng east of the county,
then moved to Ètóu,
then moved to the foot of 'Àoshān,
retaining its old name.
Píngyáng (southwest of the prefecture.
Formerly Píngyáng Zhōu in the Yuan dynasty.
In the third year of Hóngwǔ (1370), it was demoted to a county.
To the southwest is Nányàndàngshān,
and Yùcāngshān.
Further, in the southeastern sea are Dàyántóushān,
and Nánjǐshān.
Further to the west is Qiáncāngjiāng,
also called Héngyángjiāng,
flowing southeast through Jiāngkǒuguān into the sea.
To the south is Tiānfùnán Salt Pan.
Further to the south is Jīnxiāng Wèi,
and Púmén Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ,
to the northeast is Zhuàngshì Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ,
all established in the twentieth year of Hóngwǔ (1387), second month.
To the southeast are Páocáo, and also Dǒumén, two Xúnjiǎnsī.
To the south is Jiāngkǒu Xúnjiǎnsī,
its seat at Xiàbù,
later moved to Dùtóu.
Further to the east is Xiānkǒu Xúnjiǎnsī,
moved to Màichéngshān south of the county,
retaining its old name.
Further to the southeast is Guīfēng Xúnjiǎnsī,
now defunct.
Tàishùn (southwest of the prefecture.
In the third year of Jǐngtài (1452), it was established from Luóyángzhèn of Ruì'ān Xiàn,
and territory from Píngyáng Xiàn was added to it.
To the south is Fēnshuǐshān,
with a pass on it,
which is the boundary between Zhè and Mǐn.
Further to the west is Báixī,
its lower course reaches Fújiàn Níngdé Xiàn and enters the sea.
Further to the east is Xiānjūxī,
flowing into Ruì'ān territory and entering the sea.
To the north is Chícūn Xúnjiǎnsī.
To the south is Sānguān Xúnjiǎnsī,
originally Yángwàng,
later renamed.
To the southeast is Yāyáng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.
Also, Luóyáng Dìyīguān is east of the county.
Treatise 21: Geography 6: Fújiàn, Guǎngdōng, Guǎngxī
Fújiàn: The region of Yángzhōu in Yǔgòng.
During the Yuán dynasty, the Fújiàn Dào Xuānwèi Sī was established,
(governed from Fúzhōu Lù.)
It was subordinate to the Jiāngzhè Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng.
In the first month of the sixteenth year of Zhìzhèng, the Xuānwèi Sī was changed to a Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng.
In the twelfth month of the first year of Wú under Tàizǔ, Chén Yǒudìng was pacified.
In the fifth month of the second year of Hóngwǔ, the Fújiàn Děngchǔ Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng was re-established.
In the second month of the seventh year, the Fúzhōu Dūwèi was established.
(It shared governance with the Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng.)
In the tenth month of the eighth year, the Fúzhōu Dūwèi was changed to the Fújiàn Dū Zhǐhuīshǐ Sī.
In the sixth month of the ninth year, the Xíng Zhōngshū Shěng was changed to the Chéngxuān Bùzhèngshǐ Sī.
It administered eight fǔ,
one zhílì zhōu,
and fifty-seven subordinate xiàn.
(It comprised three thousand seven hundred and ninety-seven lǐ.)
To the north, it reached Lǐng,
(bordering Zhèjiāng.)
To the west, it reached Tīngzhōu,
(bordering Jiāngxī.)
To the south, it reached Zhào'ān,
(bordering Guǎngdōng.)
To the east, it reached the sea.
It was two thousand eight hundred and seventy-two lǐ from Nánjīng,
and six thousand one hundred and thirty-three lǐ from the capital.
In the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ, there were eight hundred and fifteen thousand five hundred and twenty-seven registered households,
and three million nine hundred and sixteen thousand eight hundred and six people.
In the fourth year of Hóngzhì,
there were five hundred and six thousand thirty-nine households,
and two million one hundred and six thousand sixty people.
In the sixth year of Wànlì,
there were five hundred and fifteen thousand three hundred and seven households,
and one million seven hundred and thirty-eight thousand seven hundred and ninety-three people.
Fúzhōu Fǔ (formerly Fúzhōu Lù in the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to the Fújiàn Dào.)
In the first year of Wú under Tàizǔ, it became a fǔ.
It administered nine xiàn.
Mǐn (seat of government.
To the south is Diàotái Shān,
also called Nántái Shān.
To the southeast is Gǔshān.
To the south is Fāngshān,
also named Gānguǒ Shān.
Below it is Guānmǔ Yǔ,
where there is a Xúnjiǎn Sī.
To the southeast, it borders the sea.
To the south is the Mǐnjiāng,
also called Jiànjiāng,
which flows into the fǔ territory from Nánpíng Xiàn.
To the southeast, it receives water from various streams,
and to the west of the fǔ it is called Hóngtángjiāng.
It divides into two branches:
the one flowing south is called Táojiāng,
and the one flowing east is called Nántáijiāng.
Below Gǔshān, they merge into one.
Further to the southeast is Mǎtóujiāng,
which flows in from Yǒngfú Xiàn
and is called Xīxiájiāng.
Further east, the Dōngxiájiāng flows in and joins it.
Further southeast, it reaches Wǔhǔmén
and enters the sea.
To the east is the Mǐn'ān Zhèn Xúnjiǎn Sī.
Hóuguān (seat of government.
To the west are Qíshān,
Xuěfēngshān,
and Jiànjiāng.
There is also Xīchán Pǔ.
To the southwest are Yángqí, Wúshān, Fènggāng, Zémiáo, Yánzé, Xiānbǎn, and other six pǔs.
All are branches of the Jiànjiāng,
and they eventually rejoin the main stream to enter the sea.
To the northwest was Huái'ān Xiàn,
which was moved into the city walls in the twelfth year of Hóngwǔ
and administered jointly with Mǐn and Hóuguān.
It was abolished in the ninth month of the eighth year of Wànlì.
To the northwest are Zhúqí and Wǔxiànzhài, two Xúnjiǎn Sīs.
Chánglè (east of the fǔ,
slightly south.
To the east, it borders the sea and has a sea dike.
To the north is Mǎtóujiāng.
Further east is the Shǒuyù Méihuā Qiānhùsuǒ,
established in the second month of the twenty-first year of Hóngwǔ.
To the northeast are Shíliángjiāoshān and Sōngxiàzhèn, two Xúnjiǎn Sīs.
Further east is the Xiǎozhǐshān Xúnjiǎn Sī,
later moved to Dàzhǐ'ào.
Fúqīng (south of the fǔ,
slightly east.
Formerly Fúqīng Zhōu in the Yuán dynasty.
In the second month of the second year of Hóngwǔ, it was demoted to a xiàn.
To the southeast, it borders the sea and has salt fields.
In the sea is Hǎitán Shān,
and also Xiǎoliàn Shān.
To the south is Lóngjiāng,
and also Jìngjiāng.
To the southeast is Hǎikǒu,
where all rivers converge to enter the sea.
Further east is Zhèndōng Wèi.
To the southeast is the Shǒuyù Wàn'ān Qiānhùsuǒ.
Both were established in the second month of the twenty-first year of Hóngwǔ.
There are also Zélǎng Shān, Niútóumén, and Bìtóu Shān, three Xúnjiǎn Sīs.
Further east is the Hǎikǒu Zhèn Xúnjiǎn Sī,
moved to Sōngxiàzhèn in Chánglè Xiàn in the twentieth year of Hóngwǔ.
Liánjiāng (northeast of the fǔ.
To the northeast, it borders the sea.
In the sea is Běijiāo Zhèn Xúnjiǎn Sī.
To the south is Liánjiāng,
which enters the sea to the east.
To the northeast is the Shǒuyù Dìnghǎi Qiānhùsuǒ,
established in the second month of the twenty-first year of Hóngwǔ.
Luóyuán (northeast of the fǔ.
To the east, it borders the sea.
To the west is Luóchuān,
which flows south and divides into three branches entering the sea.
To the south is Yìngdé Zhèn.
Gǔtián (northwest of the fǔ.
Jiànjiāng is south of the xiàn,
flowing in from Nánpíng Xiàn,
passing south of the city.
A large stream joins it there,
which is called Shuǐkǒu.
Further southeast, it passes below Mótīnlǐng,
where the river flow becomes calm after navigating dangerous terrain,
then flows east into Mǐnqīng Xiàn territory.
To the east is Shānyáng Zhèn,
where silver mines are found.
There was a Xúnjiǎn Sī there,
later abolished.
To the southwest is Gǔkǒu Zhèn, and to the northwest is Xīxī Zhèn, two Xúnjiǎn Sīs,
which were also soon abolished.
Mǐnqīng (northwest of the fǔ.
To the southwest is Dàmào Shān.
To the north is Jiànjiāng,
and to the southwest, Méixī flows in and joins it.
To the east is Qīngyáo Zhèn Xúnjiǎn Sī,
abolished.
Yǒngfú (southwest of the fǔ.
To the southwest is Gāogài Shān,
and further south is Chénshān.
To the east is Dōngxī,
which collects water from various mountain streams,
and its lower course converges with Lóngjiāng in Fúqīng to enter the sea.
There was also Jìmén Xúnjiǎn Sī,
later moved to Sōngkǒuchéng,
and then soon restored to its original location.
Xīnghuà Fǔ (formerly Xīnghuà Lù in the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to the Fújiàn Dào Xuānwèi Sī.)
In the first year of Hóngwǔ, it became a fǔ.
It administered two xiàn.
It was two hundred and eighty lǐ north of the Bùzhèngshǐ Sī.
Pútián (seat of government.
To the southeast, it borders the sea.
In the sea are Méizhōu Yǔ
and Nánrì Shān,
both facing the Ryukyu Kingdom to the east.
To the south is Mùlánxī,
to the north is Yánshòuxī,
to the northeast is Dílúxī,
and also Tōngyìnggǎng.
All converge and flow into the sea.
To the northwest was Xīnghuà Xiàn,
abolished in the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Zhèngtǒng.
To the east is Pínghǎi Wèi.
To the southeast is the Shǒuyù Púxǐ Qiānhùsuǒ.
Both were established in the second month of the twenty-first year of Hóngwǔ.
To the east is Qiàntóu, to the northwest is Dàyángzhài, and to the southeast is Jíle, three Xúnjiǎn Sīs.
To the east is Chōngqìn Xúnjiǎn Sī,
originally governed from Xúnyáng,
later moved to Xīngfú.
There was also Qīngshān Xúnjiǎn Sī,
originally governed from Nánshào in Wǔshèng Lǐ,
later moved to Fèngguó Lǐ.
To the southeast is Nánrì Shān Xúnjiǎn Sī,
later moved to Xīn'ān.
To the northeast is Yíngxiānzhài Xúnjiǎn Sī,
later moved to Gǔlóushān.
To the east is Zhìtóu, and to the southeast is Xiǎozhì, two Xúnjiǎn Sīs,
later abolished.
Xiānyóu (West of the prefecture seat.
To the north are the Èrfēi Shān.
To the northeast is Hé Lǐng.
To the south borders Jiǔlǐ Hú,
a lake situated among myriad mountains.
Its lower course flows into the territory of Pútián Xiàn,
joining the Yánshòu Xī.
To the west is Sānhuì Xī,
which is the upper source of the Mùlán Xī.
To the west is the Báilǐng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later relocated to Wénshū Zhài.
To the south are Fēngtíng Shì and Tánbiān Shì, two Xúnjiǎnsī to the west,
later abolished.
) Jiànníng Fǔ (Originally Jiànníng Lù during the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to the Fújiàn Dào Xuānwèisī.
) In the first year of Hóngwǔ, it was made a prefecture.
It administered eight counties.
In the first month of the fourth year, the Jiànníng Dūwèi was established here.
In the tenth month of the eighth year, it was changed to the Fújiàn Xíng Dūzhīhuīshǐsī.
Its southeast is five hundred twenty-five *lǐ* from the Bùzhèngsī.
Jiàn'ān (Dependent.
To the northeast are the Fènghuáng Shān,
producing tea.
To the east is Dōng Xī,
also known as Jiàn Jiāng,
flowing from Qìngyuán Xiàn in Zhèjiāng through here,
then joining Xī Xī to the west.
Also, to the southeast is the Shòulǐng Xúnjiǎnsī.
Ōuníng (Dependent.
To the west is Xī Xī,
its source in Chóng'ān Xiàn,
converging with waters from various streams to the east,
flowing into the county territory,
then joining Dōng Xī to the east,
and entering the territory of Yánpíng Fǔ to the south.
To the northwest is the Yíngtóu Jiē Xúnjiǎnsī.
Jiànyáng (Northwest of the prefecture seat.
To the northwest is Xī Shān.
To the southeast is Jǐnjiāng,
also called Jiāoxī,
having two sources,
which converge east of the county seat, below Dōng Shān,
and flow south to reach Jiànxī.
Chóng'ān (Northwest of the prefecture seat.
To the south are the Wǔyí Shān,
within which is Qīngxī,
its nine bends flowing into Chóngxī.
To the northwest is Fēnshuǐ Lǐng,
with the Fēnshuǐguān Xúnjiǎnsī atop it.
Its westward-flowing waters enter Jiāngxī province,
while its eastward-flowing waters enter the county territory,
being the source of Chóngxī.
Locally it is called Dàxī,
passing west of the city and exiting to the south,
also called Xī Xī.
Its other source is from Cènyáng Shān, northeast of the county,
also called Dōng Xī,
flowing southwest to join Xī Xī,
then joining the Wǔyí waters to the south and entering the territory of Jiànyáng Xiàn,
which is the upper source of Jǐnjiāng.
Also, to the northwest are Wēnlín, Cènyáng, Tóngmù, Jiāolǐng, Gǔkǒu, Láozhú, Guānyīn, and other passes,
which, with Fēnshuǐguān, are the passes into Chóng'ān.
Pǔchéng (Northeast of the prefecture seat.
To the north is Yúliáng Shān,
where the source of Jiànxī emerges.
There is also Gàixiān Shān,
Lí Lǐng,
and Fēng Lǐng,
also named Dàgān Lǐng,
all being major routes between Zhèjiāng and Mǐn.
Also, to the northeast is Zhèlǐng,
marking the border with Líshuǐ Xiàn in Zhèjiāng,
from which Zhèshuǐ emerges,
flowing to join Dàxī.
Also, to the south is Nánpǔ Xī,
also called Dàxī,
which is Jiànxī itself,
its lower course joining Jiāoxī in Jiànyáng.
To the east is Gāoquán, to the northeast is Xīyuán, and to the northwest is Péntíng—three Xúnjiǎnsī.
Sōngxī (East of the prefecture seat.
To the east are myriad mountains.
To the northeast is Jiùfēng Shān,
bordering Pǔchéng and Lóngquán in Zhèjiāng.
To the south is Sōngxī,
its source in Qìngyuán Xiàn in Zhèjiāng,
also called Sōngyuán Shuǐ.
Also, to the west is Shānxī,
their lower courses all flowing into Jiànxī.
To the north is the Èrshísì Dōu Xúnjiǎnsī.
To the south is the Dōngguān Xúnjiǎnsī,
later relocated to Wū'ānlǐng,
then relocated to Tiělǐng,
and then relocated to Xiáqiáo.
Zhènghé (East of the prefecture seat.
To the south is Qīxīng Xī,
its source in Tóngpán Shān east of the county,
its lower course joining Sōngxī.
Also, to the east is Dānxī,
flowing through Fú'ān Xiàn into the sea.
Also, to the southeast is the Chìyán Xúnjiǎnsī.
Shòuníng (East of the prefecture seat.
In the eighth month of the sixth year of Jǐngtài, it was established from Yánghǎi Cūn in Zhènghé Xiàn,
with land from Fú'ān Xiàn added to it.
To the east is Chánxī,
which is the upper source of Chángxī in Fúníng Zhōu.
To the east is the Yúxī Xúnjiǎnsī,
later relocated to Guāntái Shān north of the county,
and then relocated to Xiétān Zhèn.
) Yánpíng Fǔ (Originally Yánpíng Lù during the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to the Fújiàn Dào Xuānwèisī.
) In the first year of Hóngwǔ, it was made a prefecture.
It administered seven counties.
Its southeast is four hundred five *lǐ* from the Bùzhèngsī.
Nánpíng (Dependent.
To the south are the Jiǔfēng Shān.
To the northeast are the Yǎnxiān Shān.
Southeast of the city is Jiànxī,
which is Jiànjiāng,
also called Dōng Xī,
flowing in from Jiànníng Fǔ,
passing south through Āndàn Tān,
then west through Jiànjīn,
and joining Xī Xī.
Xī Xī originates from the territories of Tīng and Shào prefectures,
reaching west of the county,
joining Shāxī in Shā Xiàn,
forming Shāxīkǒu;
then east to Jiànjīn,
joining Dōng Xī;
then south to Yóuxīkǒu,
joining Dàxī,
also named Nánxī;
then east to Fúzhōu Fǔ,
and entering the sea;
locally it is also called Sānxī.
To the southeast is Cāngxiá, to the northwest is Dàlì—two Xúnjiǎnsī.
Jiānglè (West of the prefecture seat.
To the south are Tiānjiē Shān.
To the northwest are Bǎizhàng Shān.
To the south is Jiāngxī,
also called Dàxī,
which is the upper source of Xī Xī.
Also, to the northwest is Méixī,
flowing in from the Shàowǔ territory,
joining Dàxī.
Also, to the north is the Wàn'ānzhài Xúnjiǎnsī.
Shā (Southwest of the prefecture seat.
To the northwest is Yòushān.
South of the county seat is Shāxī,
also named Tàishǐ Xī,
flowing in from Yǒng'ān Xiàn,
passing east of the county,
with Pīlì and other rapids,
its lower course joining Xī Xī.
To the north is the Běixiāngzhài Xúnjiǎnsī.
Yóuxī (South of the prefecture seat.
To the north is Dānxī Lǐng,
also named Táomù Lǐng,
below which is Dānxī.
To the east is Yóuxī,
its upper sources originating one from Lóngyán Xiàn,
one from Déhuà Xiàn,
converging southwest of the county,
then flowing north to meet Tāngquán and twenty other streams,
exiting north at Yóukǒu,
entering Jiànxī,
also called Hútóuxī.
To the west are Yīngguǒ Zhài and Gāocáibǎn—two Xúnjiǎnsī.
Shùnchāng (West of the prefecture seat,
slightly north.
To the south is Páihuái Lǐng.
To the northwest is Shùnyáng Xī,
its source in Jiànyáng Xiàn,
then flowing east south of the county,
joining Jiāngxī,
then flowing east through Shākǒu,
joining Shāxī in Shàowǔ Xiàn,
then flowing east west of the county,
joining Xī Xī,
Xī Xī being Zǐyún Xī in Shàowǔ Xiàn,
then flowing east into Nánpíng Xiàn territory,
becoming Nánpíng's Xī Xī.
Also, to the northwest is the Rénshòuzhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.
Yǒng'ān (southwest of the prefecture.
Originally the Fúliú Patrol and Inspection Office of Shāxiàn,
the Yǒng'ān Chiliarchy was established here in the 14th year of Zhèngtǒng.
In the 3rd year of Jǐngtài, it was reorganized into a county,
and land from Yóuxī Xiàn was added to it.
To its northeast is Gòngchuānshān.
To its southeast is Shíluóshān.
To its west is Yānxī,
whose four sources converge,
pass northeast of the city,
and downstream become Shāxī of Shāxiàn.
Further west is Ānshā Zhèn, and to the southwest are Húkǒuzhài, two Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Further northwest is Huángyáng Patrol and Inspection Office,
now defunct.
Dàtián (southwest of the prefecture.
In the 2nd month of the 15th year of Jiājìng, Dàtián from Yóuxī Xiàn was established,
and land from Yǒng'ān, Zhāngpíng, and Déhuà counties was added to it.
To its north is Wǔtáishān.
To its south is Dàxiānshān.
To its east is Yínpíngshān,
which produces silver and iron.
Further south is Yóuxī,
which flows in from Lóngyán Xiàn,
and then flows east into Yóuxī Xiàn territory.
Further southeast is Huāqiáo Patrol and Inspection Office.
Further southwest is Táoyuándiàn Patrol and Inspection Office,
originally belonging to Zhāngpíng Xiàn,
and later belonging here.
To its north are Yīngzhài, and to its southwest are Ānrén Ài, two Patrol and Inspection Offices,
later defunct.
)Tīngzhōufǔ (originally Tīngzhōulù in the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to the Fújiàndào Xuānwèisī.) In the 1st year of Hóngwǔ, it became a prefecture.
It administered eight counties.
It is 975 li east of the Provincial Administration Commission.
Chángtīng (the prefectural seat.
To its north is Wòlóngshān.
Further north is Xīnlèshān,
from which Gòngshuǐ originates,
flowing into Jiāngxī territory.
To its west is Xīnlùlǐng.
To its east is Yínjiāng,
also known as Dōngxī,
and also called Zuǒxī,
flowing in from Nínghuà Xiàn.
Downstream, it passes through Dàpǔ Xiàn in Guǎngdōng and enters the sea.
It contains 500 rapids,
and is also called Tīngshuǐ.
Further southeast is Zhèngxī,
to its west is Xīxī,
to its north is Běixī,
to its south is Nánxī,
all converging with Dōngxī.
Further west is Gǔchéngzhài Patrol and Inspection Office.
Nínghuà (northeast of the prefecture.
To its south is Tánfēijì.
There is also Dàxī,
whose source is Wànhúquán north of the county.
A branch flows to form Qīngxī of Qīngliú Xiàn,
while its main course flows into Chángtīng Xiàn,
forming the upper reaches of Yínjiāng.
To its north is Ānyuǎnzhài Patrol and Inspection Office.
Shàngháng (south of the prefecture.
To its west is Jīnshān,
on which there is Dǎnquán,
which can turn iron into copper when immersed.
To its southwest is Yángshān,
which produces ore.
To its south is Dàxī.
Wǔpíng (southwest of the prefecture.
To its north is Huánggōnglǐng.
To its south is Huàlóngxī,
which downstream flows into Chéngxiāng Xiàn in Guǎngdōng.
To its southwest is Wǔpíngchéng.
In the 1st month of the 24th year of Hóngwǔ, the Wǔpíng Chiliarchy was established here.
To its southeast is Xiàngdòng Patrol and Inspection Office,
later moved to Xuánshéng Ài southwest of the county.
To its north is Yǒngpíngzhài Patrol and Inspection Office,
later moved to Bèizhài northwest of the county.
Qīngliú (northeast of the prefecture.
To its south is Fēngshān.
To its southeast is Tiěshíshān,
facing Jiǔlóngxī to its south.
There is Tiěshíjītóu Patrol and Inspection Office.
To its southwest is Qīngxī,
flowing in from Nínghuà Xiàn.
To its northeast, it merges with Bànxī,
then flows southeast through Jiǔlóngtān into Yǒng'ān Xiàn territory.
It is also called Lóngxī,
which is the upper source of Yānxī.
Liánchéng (southeast of the prefecture.
Originally called Liánchéng (蓮城),
after the 17th year of Hóngwǔ,
"蓮" (lián)
was changed
to "連" (lián).
To its east is Liánfēngshān.
To its south is Wénxī,
which downstream reaches Qīngxī of Qīngliú Xiàn.
To its southwest is Běiyuánzhài Patrol and Inspection Office,
later moved to Lángcūn Ài south of the county,
and later again moved to Xīnquán Ài southwest of the county.
Guīhuà (northeast of the prefecture.
In the 1st month of the 7th year of Chénghuà, it was established from Míngxī Zhèn of Qīngliú Xiàn,
and land from Jiānglè, Shāxiàn, and Nínghuà counties was added to it.
To its north is Tiělǐng.
To its south is Guīhuàxī,
which downstream merges with Jiāngxī of Jiānglè Xiàn.
To its east is Xiàyáng Patrol and Inspection Office.
Yǒngdìng (south of the prefecture.
In the 14th year of Chénghuà, it was established from Tiánxīndì in Xīnánlǐ of Shàngháng Xiàn,
and land from Shèngyùn and other four lì was added to it.
To its west is Dàxī,
which is Tīngshuǐ.
It flows through here from Shàngháng Xiàn,
and then flows east into Dàpǔ Xiàn territory in Guǎngdōng.
To its southeast is Sāncénglǐng Patrol and Inspection Office.
To its northeast is Tàipíng Patrol and Inspection Office,
later moved to Gāopō.
To its southwest is Xīnghuà Patrol and Inspection Office,
governing Gǔzhèn in Xīnánlǐ,
soon abolished,
then re-established,
and later moved to Fēngtóu in Shàngháng Xiàn.
)Shàowǔfǔ (originally Shàowǔlù in the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to the Fújiàndào Xuānwèisī.) In the 1st year of Tàizǔ Wú, it became a prefecture.
It administered four counties.
It is 670 li southeast of the Provincial Administration Commission.
Shàowǔ (the prefectural seat.
To its east is Sāntáishān.
To its southeast is Qītáishān,
and also Dàorénfēng.
There is also Qiáoxī,
originating from Qiáolánshān,
passing through the city,
exiting the north gate,
merging with Zǐyúnxī,
and flowing to Shùnchāng Xiàn as Shùnyángxī.
Further southeast is Shuǐkǒu Patrol and Inspection Office.
Further east are Ná kǒu, to its south Tóngxún, and to its northeast Yángfāng, three Patrol and Inspection Offices,
now defunct.
Guāngzé (northwest of the prefecture.
To its north is Yúnjìlǐng.
To its northwest is Shānlǐng,
with Shānguān on it,
bordering Nánchéng Xiàn in Jiāngxī.
Hángchuān originates there,
also named Dàxī,
and downstream flows into Zǐyúnxī.
There is also Dàsìzhài Patrol and Inspection Office,
east of Shānguān.
Further northwest is Huángtǔguān.
Tàiníng (southwest of the prefecture.
To its west is Jīnráoshān.
To its northwest is Dàshānlǐng.
To its west are Twenty-four Streams,
with Tānjiāng flowing in from the south,
and downstream converging with Qiáoxī.
Jiànníng (southwest of the prefecture.
To its north is Bǎizhànglǐng,
from which Lánxī originates.
To its south is Suíjiāng,
whose source is Jīnráoshān,
also named Suījiāng or Níngxī.
At Suíchéngkǒu,
it merges with Lánxī and flows into Tàiníng Xiàn territory.
To its west is Xī'ān Patrol and Inspection Office,
originally governing Lǐxīnbǎo,
later moved to Qiūfāng Ài,
soon abolished,
then re-established,
and later again moved to Huángnípù in Xīn'ānbǎo.
)Quánzhōufǔ (originally Quánzhōulù in the Yuán dynasty,
subordinate to the Fújiàndào Xuānwèisī.) In the 1st year of Hóngwǔ, it became a prefecture.
It administered seven counties.
It is 410 li east of the Provincial Administration Commission.
Jìnjiāng (county seat.
To the northeast is Quánshān,
also named Qīngyuán.
To the southeast is Bǎogài Shān.
To the south is Língyuán Shān.
To the southeast, it borders the sea,
where there are salt pans.
In the sea are the Pēnghú Islets.
To the south is Jìnjiāng,
which flows in from Nán'ān Xiàn,
passes beneath Shítǎ Shān west of the city,
then goes southeast to Dàiyǔ and enters the sea.
To the northeast is Luòyáng Jiāng,
flowing south into the sea.
To the southeast is Yǒngníng Wèi,
and to the south is Shǒuyù Fúquán Qiānhùsuǒ,
both established in the second month of the twenty-first year of Hóngwǔ (1388).
To the southeast are Xiángzhī, and also Wūxún; to the south are Shēnhù, and also Wéitóu—four Patrol and Inspection Offices.
To the southwest is Ānpíng Chéng,
built during the Jiājìng reign.
To the southeast is Shíhú Chéng,
built during the Wànlì reign.
Nán'ān (west of the prefectural seat,
slightly north.
To the southeast, it borders the sea.
To the south is Huánglóng Xī,
which is the upper reaches of Jìnjiāng,
into which Táolín Xī flows from the west.
To the south is Shíjǐng Xúnjiǎnsī.
Also, to the northwest is Àotóu, and to the southwest is Dáhé—two Patrol and Inspection Offices,
which were later abolished.
Tóng'ān (southwest of the prefectural seat.
To the west is Wénpǔ Shān.
To the south, it borders the sea,
where there are salt pans.
To the northwest is Xīxī,
which flows and merges with Dōngxī to the east of the county,
and Zhùxī to the west of the county,
then flows southeast into the sea.
To the southwest is Shǒuyù Jīnmén Qiānhùsuǒ,
and to the west is Shǒuyù Gāopǔ Qiānhùsuǒ,
both established in the second month of the twenty-first year of Hóngwǔ (1388).
Also, to the southwest is Yǒngníng Zhōngzuǒ Qiānhùsuǒ,
located on Jiāhé Yǔ,
which is now Xiàmén,
established in the second month of the twenty-seventh year of Hóngwǔ (1394).
To the west is Zhùxī, to the south is Tǎtóu Shān, to the southeast is Tiánpǔ, and also Chénkēng—four Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Also, to the southwest is Báijiāo Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Huáikǒu Zhài west of the county.
To the southeast is Lièyǔ Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Shíxún Gǎngkǒu.
Also, there is Guān'ào Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Tàshí Zhài.
Also, there is Fēngshàng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Xiàdiàn Gǎngkǒu west of the county.
Huì'ān (northeast of the prefectural seat.
To the southeast, it borders the sea,
where there are salt pans.
To the west is Luòyáng Jiāng.
Also, to the southeast is Shǒuyù Chóngwǔ Qiānhùsuǒ,
established in the second month of the twenty-first year of Hóngwǔ (1388),
and moved to the northeast of the county during the Jiājìng reign.
To the east of the city are Huángqí, to the south is Tàkū, to the southeast is Xiǎozuǒ, and to the northeast is Fēngwěi—four Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Also, to the northeast are Túlíng, and also Shāgé; to the southeast is Xiǎodōu—three Patrol and Inspection Offices,
abolished in the twentieth year of Hóngwǔ (1387).
Ānxī (west of the prefectural seat.
To the northwest is Fó'ěr Shān.
To the south is Lánxī.
Also, to the northwest is Yuánkǒu Dù Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Báihuá Bǎo,
then soon restored.
Yǒngchūn (northwest of the prefectural seat.
To the northwest is Xuěshān,
from which Táolín Xī emerges,
flows east through Nán'ān Xiàn,
merges north with Lánxī,
forming Shuāngxī Kǒu,
then flows east through Nán'ān Xiàn,
and merges south with Huánglóng Xī.
To the west is Chényán Zhài Xúnjiǎnsī,
abolished during the Hóngwǔ reign.
Déhuà (northwest of the prefectural seat.
To the northwest is Dàiyún Shān.
To the west is Tàihú Shān.
To the south is Dīngxī,
and also Chǎnxī,
which merge and flow north,
entering the territory of Xīnghuà Xiānyóu.
Also, to the northwest is Gāozhèn Xúnjiǎnsī,
originally Dōngxī Tuán,
later its seat was moved,
and its name changed.
To the southeast is Hǔbào Guān.
) Zhāngzhōu Fǔ (formerly Zhāngzhōu Lù in the Yuan dynasty,
subordinate to Fújiàn Dào Xuānwèi Sī.
) In the first year of Hóngwǔ (1368), it became a prefecture.
It administered ten counties.
To the northeast, it is seven hundred *li* from the Provincial Administration Commission.
Lóngxī (county seat.
To the east is Qíshān.
To the west is Tiānbǎo Shān.
To the north is Huáfēng Líng,
also named Lóngtóu Líng.
To the southeast, it borders the sea,
where there are Dānxiá and other islets.
Also, to the northeast is Jiǔlóng Jiāng,
also named Běixī,
its upper source is in Chángtīng and Shāxiàn,
it flows into the county boundary,
passes beneath Lóngtóu Líng,
where it is called Xiá zhōng (within the gorge),
reaches the east of the county and exits the gorge,
becoming Liǔyíng Jiāng,
and to the south Nánxī flows into it.
Further southeast, it is Zhènmén Gǎng,
entering the sea.
There is Liǔyíng Jiāng Xúnjiǎnsī.
Also, to the south is Jiǔlóng Líng Xúnjiǎnsī.
Zhāngpǔ (south of the prefectural seat.
To the south is Liángshān,
and further southeast is Liángshān,
facing Liángshān.
To the northeast is Dàwǔ Shān.
The county borders the sea on its southeast and two other sides.
To the south is Zhāngjiāng,
also called Yúnxiāo Xī,
which merges with Lǐ'ào Xī and enters the sea.
There is also Shíchéng Xī.
To the northeast is also Zhènhǎi Wèi,
and to the east is Shǒuyù Liù'áo Qiānhùsuǒ.
To the southeast of the *ao* (bay) are Gǔléi, and also Hòugé; to the east is Jǐngwěi'ào; to the southwest is Pántuó Líng—four Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Also, to the southeast is Qīngshān Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved its seat to Yuèzhì,
and further southwest is Yúnxiāo Zhèn,
all established in the second month of the twenty-first year of Hóngwǔ (1388).
Lóngyán (west of the prefectural seat.
To the east is Lóngyán Shān,
and also Dōngbǎo Shān,
which formerly produced silver and lead.
To the west is Zǐjīn Shān.
To the north is Jiǔhóu Shān.
Also, to the south is Lóngchuān,
its lower reaches flow into Zhāngpíng county boundary,
forming the upper source of Jiǔlóng Jiāng.
To the northeast is Yànshí Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Hǎolín Kǒu.
Chángtài (east of the prefectural seat.
To the south is Chángtài Xī,
its lower reaches flow into Jiǔlóng Jiāng.
To the southeast is Cháotiān Líng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Xīkǒu.
Nánjìng (west of the prefectural seat.
Its former seat was in the southwest,
north of Shuāngxī.
In the forty-fifth year of Jiājìng (1566), it was moved north to the foot of Dàmào Shān.
In the twenty-third year of Wànlì (1595), it was restored to its old seat.
To the north is Ōuliáo Shān.
To the south is Shuāngxī,
which enters Lóngxī Xiàn boundary,
and becomes Nánxī.
To the north are Yǒngfēng, and to the northwest are Héxī—two Patrol and Inspection Offices.
There are also Xiǎoxī and Hánxī—two Patrol and Inspection Offices,
later abolished.
Zhāngpíng (northwest of the prefectural seat.
Established in the sixth year of Chénghuà (1470) from Jiǔlóng Xiāng of Lóngyán Xiàn,
with five *li* of land including Jūfrén separated and added to it.
To the southeast is Xiànghú Shān.
To the south is Bǎijiā Shè Dòng,
situated at the junction of five counties: Lóngyán, Ānxī, Lóngxī, Nánjìng, and Zhāngpíng.
There is also Jiǔlóng Xī,
flowing through here from Lóngyán Xiàn,
its lower reaches flow into Lóngxī Xiàn.
To the south is Guīhuà Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Xīkǒu east of the county.
Also, to the northeast is Xīnán Xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.
Pínghé (southwest of the prefectural seat.
Established in the sixth month of the fourteenth year of Zhèngdé (1519) from Hétóu Dàyángpō of Nánjìng Xiàn,
with land from Zhāngpǔ Xiàn separated and added to it.
To the southeast is Sānpíng Shān.
To the east is Dàfēng Shān,
from which Hétóu Xī originates,
dividing into several streams reaching the sea,
and to the west Lúxī flows and merges into it.
There is Lúxī Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Fāngtóu Bǎn,
and renamed Zhāngdīng Xúnjiǎnsī.
Zhàoshēn (to the south of the prefecture.
Originally the Nánzhào Defense Myriad-Household Command,
established in the 18th year of Hóngzhì.
In the 12th month of the 9th year of Jiājìng, it was converted into a county.
To its south, it borders the sea.
Along the coast is Chuānlíng Shān.
In the sea is Nán'ào Shān.
Further east is Dōngxī,
a branch of Hétóuxī,
which flows southeast into the sea.
To its south is the Xuánzhōng Defense Myriad-Household Command,
and to its east is the Tóngshān Defense Myriad-Household Command,
both established in the 2nd month of the 21st year of Hóngwǔ.
To its east are the Jīnshí and Hóngdàn two Patrol and Inspection Commands.
To its southwest is Fēnshuǐ Guān,
the boundary between Zhāngzhōu and Cháozhōu,
where a Patrol and Inspection Command is based.
Hǎichéng (to the southeast of the prefecture.
In the 12th month of the 45th year of Jiājìng, it was established from Jìnghǎiguǎn of Lóngxī County,
with land from Zhāngpǔ County added to it.
To its northeast, it borders the sea.
To its west is Nánxī,
which flows in from Lóngxī County,
and merges with Liǔyíng Jiāng to flow into the sea.
To its east is Hǎimén Patrol and Inspection Command,
later relocated to Qīngpǔ Shè.
To its northeast is Háomén Patrol and Inspection Command,
originally based at Hǎicāng Yáng,
later relocated to Sōngyǔ in the county's northeast.
To its east is Dǎowěi Patrol and Inspection Command.
To its northwest is Shímǎ Zhèn.
Níngyáng (to the northwest of the prefecture.
Originally the Dōngxīyáng Patrol and Inspection Command of Lóngyán County,
established in the 11th year of Zhèngtǒng.
In the 12th month of the 45th year of Jiājìng, it was converted into a county,
with land from Dàtián and Yǒng'ān two counties added to it.
To its south is Xiāngliáo Shān.
To its southeast is Dōngyáng,
where streams converge.
)Fúníng Zhōu (In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Fúzhōu Lù.
)In the 8th month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, it was demoted to a county,
subordinate to Fúzhōu Fǔ.
In the 3rd month of the 9th year of Chénghuà, it was promoted to a prefecture-level department (zhōu),
directly administered by the Administration Commission (Bùzhèng Sī).
(To its north is Lóngshǒu Shān.
To its east is Sōng Shān.
At the foot of the mountain is Fēnghuǒmén Water Stockade,
relocated here in the 9th year of Zhèngtǒng from Sānshā Bǎo in the sea.
To its northeast is Dàlǎo Shān.
To its southeast, it borders the sea.
In the sea are Gē Shān, Tái Shān, Guān'ào Shān, and Píngfēng Yǔ.
To its east is Báishuǐ Jiāng.
To its west is Chángxī,
which originates in Shòuníng County,
and enters the sea at Gǔzhènmén southwest of the county.
To its east is Fúníng Wèi,
and to its south is the Dàjīn Defense Myriad-Household Command,
both established in the 2nd month of the 21st year of Hóngwǔ.
To its northwest is Zhàyáng Patrol and Inspection Command,
and also Lúmén Patrol and Inspection Command,
later relocated to Tóngshān Bǎo.
To its northeast is Dàyúndāng Patrol and Inspection Command,
later relocated to Qínyǔ Bǎo.
To its east is Qīngwān Patrol and Inspection Command,
later relocated to Yáyì Bǎo.
To its south is Gāoluó Patrol and Inspection Command,
later relocated to Lǘxiá Bǎo.
There is also Yántíng Patrol and Inspection Command,
later relocated to Xiàxǔ Bǎo.
To its northeast are Jiāngyáng,
and Xiǎolán.
To its northwest are Xiǎo'ào and Kùxī.
To its southwest is Lántián.
To its south are the Xījiù six Patrol and Inspection Commands,
later abolished.
)It administered two counties.
To its southwest, it is 545 li from the Administration Commission.
Níngdé (to the southwest of the zhōu.
In the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, it belonged to Fúzhōu Fǔ.
In the 9th year of Chénghuà, it came under this zhōu.
To its north are Huòtóng Shān,
and Guīyǔ.
To its southeast, it borders the sea.
In the sea is Guānhù Shān,
below which is Guānjǐng Yáng.
Further east is Ruìfēng,
also in the sea.
To its west is Qiónglóng Xī.
To its southwest is Chìjiàn Hú.
To its north is Wàimiǎo Xī.
Their lower reaches all reach the sea.
To its north is Dōngyáng Málǐng Patrol and Inspection Command,
later relocated to Háncūn,
then relocated to Yúndànmén northeast of the county,
then relocated to Huángwān east of the county,
later returning to its original seat.
To its south is Nánjìng Guān.
To its east is Chángqí Zhèn.
Fú'ān (to the northwest of the zhōu.
In the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, it belonged to Fúzhōu Fǔ.
In the 9th year of Chénghuà, it came under this zhōu.
To its southwest is Chéng Shān.
The sea is to its south.
To its northwest is Chángxī,
which enters Fúníng Zhōu territory to its southeast.
To its northwest is Báishí Patrol and Inspection Command,
later relocated to Huángqí Zhèn southeast of the county.
Guǎngdōng. In Yǔgòng, it was the domain of Yángzhōu and beyond Yángzhōu's borders.
In the Yuán dynasty, the Guǎngdōng Dào Pacification Commissioner's Office was established,
(its seat at Guǎngzhōu Lù.)
It belonged to the Jiāngxī Branch Secretariat.
The Hǎiběi Hǎinán Dào Pacification Commissioner's Office was also established,
(its seat at Léizhōu Lù.)
It belonged to the Húguǎng Branch Secretariat.
In the 3rd month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, the Hǎiběi Hǎinán Dào was subordinated to the Guǎngxī Branch Secretariat.
In the 4th month, Guǎngdōng Dào was renamed the Guǎngdōng and Other Places Branch Secretariat.
In the 6th month, the territories administered by the Hǎinán Hǎiběi Dào were all subordinated to it.
In the 11th month of the 4th year, the Guǎngdōng Metropolitan Military Command (Dūwèi) was established.
(It was seated with the Branch Secretariat.)
In the 10th month of the 8th year, the Metropolitan Military Command was renamed the Guǎngdōng Regional Military Commission (Dūzhīhuīshǐ Sī).
In the 6th month of the 9th year, the Branch Secretariat was renamed the Administration Commission (Chéngxuān Bùzhèngshǐ Sī).
It administered 10 prefectures (fǔ),
1 directly administered zhōu,
7 subordinate zhōus,
and 75 counties.
(Comprising 4028 li.)
To its north are the Wǔlíng Mountains,
(bordering Jiāngxī.)
To its east is Cháozhōu,
(bordering Fújiàn.)
To its west is Qīnzhōu,
(bordering Guǎngxī.)
To its south is the Qióng Hǎi.
It is 4300 li from Nánjīng,
and 7835 li from the capital.
In the 26th year of Hóngwǔ, there were 675,599 households
and 3,007,932 people.
In the 4th year of Hóngzhì,
there were 467,390 households
and 1,817,384 people.
In the 6th year of Wànlì,
there were 530,712 households
and 5,040,655 people.
Guǎngzhōu Fǔ (In the Yuán dynasty, it was Guǎngzhōu Lù,
subordinate to the Guǎngdōng Dào Pacification Commissioner's Office.)
In the 1st year of Hóngwǔ, it became a prefecture (fǔ).
It administered one zhōu,
and 15 counties.
Nánhǎi (dependent).
To its northwest are Shímén Shān and Shuāngnǚ Shān.
To its south, it borders the sea.
Further south is Sānjiāngkǒu.
The three rivers are:
one is Xī Jiāng,
whose upper reaches merge the Qián, Yù, and Guì three rivers,
flowing in from Wúzhōu Fǔ in Guǎngxī;
one is Běi Jiāng,
which is Zhēnshuǐ;
one is Dōng Jiāng,
which is Lóngchuānshuǐ.
All of them converge with Xī Jiāng,
pass south of Pānyú County,
and enter the South China Sea.
To its northwest is Sānjiāng Patrol and Inspection Command,
originally based at Cèshuǐ Cūn,
later relocated to Cūnbǎo.
There are also Jīnlì, to its southwest Shén'ān, and also Huángdǐng, and also Jiāngpǔ, four Patrol and Inspection Commands.
Further south is Wǔdǒukǒu Patrol and Inspection Command,
later relocated to Módaokǒu,
then relocated to Fóshān Zhèn.
Pānyú (dependent).
Within the city are the Fān and Yú two mountains,
from which the county takes its name.
To its east is Lùbù, to its south Shāwān, to its north Mùdé, to its southeast Jiāotáng, and also Shīlǐng, five Patrol and Inspection Commands.
Shùndé (to the southwest of the prefecture).
In the 3rd year of Jǐngtài,
it was established from Dàliáng Bǎo of Nánhǎi County,
with land from Xīnhuì County added to it.
To its northwest is Xī Jiāng.
To its south are Mǎníng, and to its north Zǐní, two Patrol and Inspection Commands.
To its west is Jiāngcūn Patrol and Inspection Command,
later relocated to Chápǔ northwest of the county.
To its north is Níngdū Patrol and Inspection Command,
later relocated to Dōuzhān Bǎo.
To its southeast is Mǎgāng Patrol and Inspection Command,
later abolished.
Dōngguǎn (To the southeast of the prefecture.
To the south, it borders the sea.
In the sea there are three islets.
There are the bays of Nántóu, Túnmén, Jīqī, Fótángmén, Shízìmén, Lěngshuǐjiǎo, Lǎowànshān, Língdīngyáng, etc.
To the north is the Dōng Jiāng.
To the west is Zhōngtáng, to the southwest is Báishā, and also Quēkǒuzhèn, with three patrols.
To the northeast is the Jīngshān Patrol.
It was originally administered at Cháyuán,
later moved to Jīngkǒucūn,
and its name was changed.
Also, to the southwest is the Hǔtóushān Pass,
established in the 27th year of Hóngwǔ.
Xīn'ān (To the southeast of the prefecture.
It was originally the Xīnnán Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ of Dōngguǎn,
established in the 8th month of the 14th year of Hóngwǔ.
In the 1st year of Wànlì, it was changed to a county.
To the south, it borders the sea.
There is the Dàpéng Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ,
also established in the 8th month of the 14th year of Hóngwǔ.
To the southeast are Guānfù and to the northwest are Fúyǒng, two patrols.
Sānshuǐ (To the north of the prefecture.
Established in the 5th month of the 5th year of Jiājìng from Lóngfènggāng of Nánhǎi county,
and parts of Gāo'ān county were added to it.
The Xī Jiāng is to the south,
and the Běi Jiāng is to the west.
Also, to the southwest are Sānjiāng, to the north is Xūjiāng, and to the east is Xīnánzhèn, three patrols.
Also, to the south is the Héngshí Patrol.
Zēngchéng (To the east of the prefecture.
To the east is the Zēng Jiāng.
To the south is the Dōng Jiāng.
To the southwest are Wūshí and to the northwest are Máotián, two patrols.
Lóngmén (To the east of the prefecture.
Established in the 6th year of Hóngzhì from Qīxīnggāng of Zēngchéng county,
and parts of Bóluó county were added to it.
To the south is Lóngmén Shuǐ,
also called Jiǔlín Shuǐ,
which flows into the Dōng Jiāng.
To the east is the Shànglóngmén Patrol.
Xiāngshān (To the south of the prefecture.
To the south, it borders the sea.
To the east is Língdīngyáng.
To the north is the Huángpǔ Patrol.
To the northwest is the Dàlǎn Patrol,
originally named Xiāngshān,
later its name was changed.
Xīnhuì (To the southwest of the prefecture.
To the south, it borders the sea,
with Yáshān in the middle.
To the northeast is the Xī Jiāng.
To the southwest is the Ēnpíng Jiāng,
also named Xiàngāng Shuǐ.
To the southeast are Cháolián and to the west are Niúdùwān, two patrols.
Also, to the northwest is the Lèjìng Patrol,
later moved to Shíluógāng, north of the county.
Also, to the northeast is the Dàwǎ Patrol,
originally administered at Zhōnglè Dū,
later moved to Luántáicūn.
Also, to the south is the Shācūn Patrol,
originally administered at Dàshéngāng,
later moved to Xiāndòngcūn,
and then moved again to Chángshācūn,
and later returned to its original administration.
Xīnníng (To the southwest of the prefecture.
Established in the 11th year of Hóngzhì from Shàngkēngyù of Déxíng Dū of Xīnhuì county,
and parts of Wénzhāng and other five Dū were added to it.
To the south, it borders the sea.
To the north is the Ēnpíng Jiāng,
also named Chángshā Hé.
Also, to the south is the Guǎnghǎi Wèi,
established in the 9th month of the 27th year of Hóngwǔ.
To the west is the Wànggāo Patrol.
To the southwest is the Chénggāng Patrol,
later abolished.
Cónghuà (To the northeast of the prefecture.
Established in the 2nd year of Hóngzhì from Héngtáncūn of Pānyú county,
and parts of Zēngchéng county were added to it.
In the 9th year, it was moved to Liúxī Mǎchǎngqū.
To the northeast is the Liúxī Patrol,
originally administered at Shítáncūn, north of the county,
later moved to Shéngāngcūn.
Qīngyuǎn (To the north of the prefecture.
To the east is Zhōngsù Xiá.
To the west is Dàluó Shān.
Also, the Zhēn Shuǐ is to the northeast of the county,
and the ● Shuǐ comes from the southeast to join it,
called the ● Jiāngkǒu,
where there is the ● Jiāng Patrol.
Also, to the southwest are Huíqí and to the northwest are Bīnjiāng, two patrols.
To the northeast is the Héngshíjī Patrol,
later abolished.
) Liánzhōu (In the Yuán dynasty, it was Guìyáng Zhōu,
directly under Guǎngdōng Dào.
) In the 3rd month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, it was merged into Liánzhōu.
In the 4th month,
Liánzhōu was abolished,
and its territory belonged to Liánshān.
In the 9th month of the 3rd year,
Liánshān was abolished,
and its territory belonged to Yángshān.
In the 14th year, Liánzhōu was established here,
subordinate to the prefecture.
(To the northeast is Guì Shuǐ.
To the west is Huáng Shuǐ,
also called Kuāng Shuǐ,
flowing in from Níngyuǎn county in Húguǎng,
joining the Zhēn Shuǐ to the southeast.
To the northwest is the Zhūgāng Patrol.
Also, there is the Xī'àn Patrol,
administered in Rénnèi Xiāng,
later moved to the territory of Yángshān county.
) To the southeast, it is 560 lǐ from the prefecture.
It administers two counties.
Yángshān (To the northeast of the zhōu.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Guìyáng Zhōu.
In the 3rd month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ,
Guìyáng Zhōu was abolished,
and it belonged to Liánzhōu.
In the 4th month,
Liánzhōu was abolished,
and it belonged to Sháozhōu Fǔ.
In the 4th month of the 14th year, it was changed to Liánzhōu,
the zhōu was moved to the old administration of Guìyáng Zhōu,
the county was re-established,
and was subordinate to it.
To the south is Yángxī,
which is Kuāng Shuǐ.
To the northwest is the Xīngzǐ Patrol.
To the east is the Xī'àn Patrol,
moved here from Liánzhōu,
administered at Qīnglián Shuǐkǒu.
Also, to the north are Huángxī and Yángshān, two passes.
Liánshān (To the west of the zhōu.
In the Yuán dynasty, Liánzhōu was administered here,
directly under Guǎngdōng Dào.
In the 4th month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ,
the zhōu was abolished,
and it belonged to Sháozhōu Fǔ.
In the 9th month of the 3rd year, it was merged into Yángshān.
In the 11th month of the 13th year, it was re-established.
In the 4th month of the 14th year, it was subordinate to the zhōu.
The old administration was at Zhōngshān, northwest of the county.
In the 1st year of Yǒnglè, it was moved to Chéngshānxià, west of the county.
In the 6th year of Tiānshùn, it was moved again to Xiǎopíng.
To the south is Huánglián Shān.
To the north is Gāoliáng Shuǐ,
also named Dàhuò Shuǐ,
which flows east to the zhōu boundary into Huáng Shuǐ.
To the west is the Yíshàn Patrol,
which is the old county administration at Chéngshānxià.
) Zhàoqìng Fǔ (In the Yuán dynasty, it was Zhàoqìng Lù,
belonging to Guǎngdōng Dào.
) In the 1st year of Hóngwǔ, it became a prefecture.
It administers one zhōu
and eleven counties.
To the south, it is 230 lǐ from the Bùzhèngsī.
Gāoyào (Dependent [county].
To the north is Shíshì Shān.
To the south is Tónggǔ Shān.
To the east are Gāoxiá Shān and Lànkē Shān.
To the south of the city is the Xī Jiāng.
Also, to the south is Xīn Jiāng.
To the southeast is Cāngwú Shuǐ.
All flow into it.
To the southeast is the Gǔyé Patrol,
administered at Féngcūn in Lóngchí Dū,
later moved to Héngchá Xiàdū, east of the county.
To the east is the Lùbù Patrol,
initially in Xiàcūn,
later moved to Shàngcūn Shuǐkǒu.
To the east is the Héngchá Patrol,
initially administered in Shàngbàndū,
later moved to Shuǐkǒu,
and soon abolished.
Gāomíng (To the southeast of the prefecture.
It was originally the Gāomíngzhèn Patrol of Gāoyào county.
In the 12th month of the 11th year of Chénghuà, it was changed to a county,
and parts of Qīngtài and other Dū were added to it.
To the south is Cāngbù Shuǐ,
also named Cāng Jiāng,
which flows down into the Xī Jiāng.
To the northeast is the Tàipíng Patrol,
administered in Tàipíng Dū,
later moved to Hánhǎikǒu, east of the county.
Then moved again to Shāntáisì, southwest of the county,
and then moved again to Qīngxī Shēnshíqí Hǎibīn, east of the county.
Sìhuì (North of the prefecture.
To the south is Běijiāng.
To the east is Nánjīn Patrol and Inspection Office,
governing Huánggāngcūn,
later moved to Nánjīn Shuǐkǒu, southeast of the county seat.
Xīnxīng (South of the prefecture.
In the Yuan dynasty, it was the seat of Xīnzhōu,
directly administered by Guǎngdōng Dào.
In the 4th month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ
the zhōu was abolished,
and it came under this prefecture.
To the east is Xīnjiāng.
To the southwest is Lìjiāng Patrol and Inspection Office.
Further south is Lùyuán Patrol and Inspection Office,
later abolished.
Kāipíng (South of the prefecture.
Originally Kāipíng Tún of Ēnpíng Xiàn.
In the late Ming dynasty, it was changed into a xiàn,
with land from Xīnxīng and Xīnhuì counties added to it.
To the south is Ēnpíngjiāng,
whose source is in Píngchéngshān, northwest of the old Ēnpíng Xiàn,
flowing east to join Wūshí Shuǐ,
then flowing into the border of Xīnhuì Xiàn in Guǎngzhōu.
To the southeast is Shāgāng Patrol and Inspection Office,
originally governing Shāgāngcūn,
later moved to Chángshācūn in Píngkāng Dū.
Further south are Sōngbǎi and to the north Sīhé two Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Yángchūn (South of the prefecture.
In the Yuan dynasty, it belonged to Nán'ēn Zhōu.
In the 1st year of Hóngwǔ, it belonged to Xīnzhōu.
In the 4th month of the 2nd year,
Xīnzhōu was abolished,
and it belonged to the prefecture.
To the west is Mòyángjiāng.
To the north is Gǔliáng Patrol and Inspection Office,
later abolished,
then re-established west of the county seat,
and again moved to Xiǎoshuǐkǒu in Nánxiāng Dū.
Further north is Sīliáng Patrol and Inspection Office,
later abolished.
Yángjiāng (South of the prefecture.
In the Yuan dynasty, Nán'ēn Zhōu was governed here,
directly administered by Guǎngdōng Dào.
In the 1st year of Hóngwǔ,
Nán'ēn Zhōu was abolished,
and it was changed to belong to Xīnzhōu.
In the 4th month of the 2nd year,
Xīnzhōu was abolished,
and it belonged to the prefecture.
To the south, it borders the sea.
In the middle is Hǎilíngshān,
to the northwest of the mountain is Hèzhōushān,
where Hǎilíng Patrol and Inspection Office is located.
To the west is Mòyángjiāng,
whose source is below Yúnfúshān, north of the old Tónglíng Xiàn,
flowing south past Yángchūn Xiàn,
converging with various waters,
passing through the old city of Nán'ēn,
flowing directly into Běijīn Gǎngmén,
and entering the sea.
To the southeast is Hǎilǎng Defensive Myriad-Household Office,
to the southwest is Shuāngyú Defensive Myriad-Household Office,
both established in the 27th year of Hóngwǔ.
Further northeast is Liántángbǎo,
and to the west Tàipíngbǎo,
both built during the Jiājìng era.
Ēnpíng (South of the prefecture.
Originally Ēnpíng Patrol and Inspection Office of Yángjiāng Xiàn,
initially governing the old Ēnpíng Xiàn northeast of the county seat,
later moved to Ēnpíngbǎo.
In the 6th month of the 14th year of Chénghuà, the bǎo was changed to a xiàn,
with land from Xīnxīng and Xīnhuì counties added to it,
and the Patrol and Inspection Office was moved to Chéngcūn southeast of the county seat,
retaining its old name,
later again moved to Báiméngtún.
To the south of the county is Ēnpíngjiāng.
Guǎngníng (Northwest of the prefecture.
Established in the 10th month of the 38th year of Jiājìng from the territory of Sìhuì Xiàn.
Initially governing below Támpǔshān southeast of the county seat,
later moved to below Fúxīngshān in Dàpǔcūn,
which is its current seat.
To the north is Suíjiāng,
and also Lóngkǒu Túntián Myriad-Household Office,
also established in the 38th year of Jiājìng.
To the northwest is Jīnxī Patrol and Inspection Office.
To the south is Fúxī Patrol and Inspection Office,
initially governing Dōngxiāng Shuǐkǒu,
later moved to Fúxīkǒu,
and again moved to Guānbù.
)Déqìng Zhōu (In the Yuan dynasty, Déqìng Lù,
belonging to Guǎngdōng Dào.) In the 1st year of Hóngwǔ, it became a prefecture.
In the 4th month of the 9th year, it was downgraded to a zhōu,
with the prefectural seat Duānxī Xiàn merged into it,
and it came under this prefecture.
(To the west
is Xiǎoxiāngxiá,
Xījiāng flows through it,
and Duānxī flows into it from the northeast.
To the east is Yuèchéngxiāng Patrol and Inspection Office,
governing the old Yuèchéng Xiàn,
later moved to Língxī Shuǐkǒu.
) It is 210
lǐ east of the prefecture.
It administers two counties.
Fēngchuān (West of the zhōu.
In the Yuan dynasty, Fēngzhōu was governed here,
directly administered by Guǎngdōng Dào.
In the 3rd month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ,
the zhōu was abolished,
and it was changed to belong to this prefecture.
To the south is Xījiāng,
to the west Hèjiāng,
to the northwest Dōng'ānjiāng,
all flowing into it.
To the north is Wéndé Patrol and Inspection Office,
initially governing Dàzhōukǒu northwest of the county seat,
later moved to Hèjiāngkǒu west of the county seat,
and again moved to this location.
Kāijiàn (Northwest of the zhōu.
In the Yuan dynasty, it belonged to Fēngzhōu.
In the 3rd month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, it was changed to belong to this prefecture.
To the west is Kāijiāng,
also named Fēngxī,
which is the lower reaches of Hèjiāng.
To the north is Gǔlìng Patrol and Inspection Office,
governing Gǔlìngcūn,
later moved to Rùcūn northeast of the county seat.
)Sháozhōu Fǔ (In the Yuan dynasty, Sháozhōu Lù,
belonging to Guǎngdōng Dào Xuānwèi Sī.) In the 1st year of Hóngwǔ, it became a prefecture.
It administers six counties.
It is 800 lǐ west of the Bùzhèng Sī.
Qǔjiāng (Prefectural seat.
In the 22nd year of Yǒnglè, Huáiwáng Fǔ was established,
in the 1st year of Zhèngtǒng it was moved to Ráozhōu Fǔ in Jiāngxī.
To the south is Liánhuāshān.
To the northeast is Sháoshíshān.
To the west is Guìshān.
Zhēnshuǐ is to the east,
to the southeast is Cáoxīshuǐ,
to the west is Wǔshuǐ,
all flowing into it,
embracing the city in a winding manner,
hence it is called Qǔjiāng;
its lower reaches are known as Shǐxīngjiāng.
To the northeast are Píngpǔ and to the south Ménggù two Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Lèchāng (Northwest of the prefecture.
To the south is Chāngshān.
To the northeast is Língjūnshān.
To the west is Sānlóngshuǐ,
which is Wǔshuǐ.
To the north are Jiǔfēng, to the northwest Huángpǔ, and also Luójiāwān three Patrol and Inspection Offices.
To the east is Gāoshèng Patrol and Inspection Office,
later abolished.
Yīngdé (Southwest of the prefecture.
In the Yuan dynasty, Yīngdé Zhōu,
directly administered by Guǎngdōng Dào.
In the 3rd month of the 2nd year of Hóngwǔ, it was downgraded to a xiàn,
and came under this prefecture.
To the south is Gāoshíshān,
also named Zhēnyángxiá.
Also, Zhēnshuǐ is to the east of the county seat,
also named Qínshuǐ,
Kuàngshuǐ is to the west of the county seat,
also named Guāngshuǐ,
at the southwest of the county seat they converge,
called Guāngkǒu,
where Guāngkǒu Patrol and Inspection Office is located.
Further south is Lóngtóushuǐ,
which joins Zhēnshuǐ.
Further east are Xiànggāng, to the north Qīngxī, to the west Hánguāng three Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Further south is Nányá Patrol and Inspection Office,
abolished.
Rénhuà (Northeast of the prefecture.
Governing Shuǐxīcūn,
later moved to Chéngkǒucūn.
To the northwest is Wúzhúlǐng,
from which Wúxīshuǐ flows,
its lower reaches become Tóngxī,
entering Zhēnshuǐ.
To the northeast is Fúxī Patrol and Inspection Office.
Further north is Ēncūn Patrol and Inspection Office.
Rǔyuán (It is located to the west of the prefecture.
Its original administrative seat was Yútáng.
In the first year of Hóngwǔ, it was moved to Zhōutóujīn.
To the west lies Lài Lǐng,
one of the Five Ridges.
To the northwest is Wǔshuǐ,
which flows in from Yízhāng Xiàn in Húguǎng.
There is the Wǔyáng Xúnjiǎnsī.
Wēngyuán (It is located to the southeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Yīngdé Zhōu.
In the third month of the second year of Hóngwǔ, it was reassigned to this prefecture.
The old city was in the northwest.
The present administrative seat was originally Cháng'ān Xiāng.
In the early Hóngwǔ period,
it was moved here.
To the north is Bǎoshān.
To the east is Língchí Shān,
from which Wēngxī emerges,
which is also known as Lóngtóu Shuǐ.
To the east is the Guìyā Shān Xúnjiǎnsī,
initially administered from Cháyuán Pù,
later moved to Nánpǔ.
) Nánxióng Fǔ (In the Yuán dynasty, it was Nánxióng Lù,
belonging to Guǎngdōng Dào.
) In the first year of Hóngwǔ, it was established as a prefecture.
It administered two counties.
It is one thousand and ninety *lǐ* west of the Bùzhèngsī.
Bǎochāng (This is the prefectural seat.
Dàyú Lǐng is to the north,
also called Méi Lǐng.
On it is Méiguān,
where Zhēnshuǐ originates.
To the northwest is Língjiāng Shuǐ,
which flows into it.
To the south, it flows into the sea at Pānyú,
and is called the Běijiāng.
Also, to the east of the county is Xiǎoyú Lǐng.
To the northwest is Bǎishùn, and to the southeast is Píngtián, two Xúnjiǎnsī.
Also to the northeast is the Hóngméi Xúnjiǎnsī,
formerly administered at the foot of Méiguān,
later moved here.
Shǐxīng (It is located to the west of the prefecture.
To the west is Shǐxīng Jiāng,
which is Zhēnshuǐ.
To the south is the Qīnghuàjìng Xúnjiǎnsī.
Also to the northeast is the Huángtáng Xúnjiǎnsī,
originally administered at Yīngluò Pù,
later moved to Huángtáng Jiāngkǒu,
and then to Huángtián Pù.
) Huìzhōu Fǔ (In the Yuán dynasty, it was Huìzhōu Lù,
belonging to the Guǎngdōng Dào Xuānwèisī.
) In the first year of Hóngwǔ, it was established as a prefecture.
It administered one sub-prefecture and ten counties.
It is three hundred and sixty *lǐ* northwest of the Bùzhèngsī.
Guīshàn (This is the prefectural seat.
To the south, it borders the sea.
Xījiāng is to the southwest.
To the east is Dōngjiāng,
which flows into the prefectural territory from Ānyuǎn Xiàn in Jiāngxī,
also called Lóngchuān Jiāng.
To the southwest, it meets Xījiāng and flows into the sea at Pānyú Xiàn.
To the southeast is the Pínghǎi Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ,
established in the ninth month of the twenty-seventh year of Hóngwǔ.
There are also the Nèi-Wài Guǎnlǐ and the Bìjiǎ two Xúnjiǎnsī.
Bóluó (It is located to the northwest of the prefecture.
To the northwest is Luófú Shān.
To the south is Dōngjiāng.
To the west is Shíwān, and to the northwest is Shànzhènglǐ, two Xúnjiǎnsī.
Chángníng (It is located to the west of the prefecture.
In the first month of the third year of Lóngqìng, it was established from Hóngyànzhōu in Guīshàn Xiàn,
with land from Yīngdé and Wēngyuán two counties of Sháozhōu Fǔ added to it.
In the first year of Wànlì, the administrative seat was moved to the foot of Jūnzǐ Fēng.
To the south is Xīnfēng Jiāng,
which flows downstream into Lóngjiāng.
To the west is the Píng Xúnjiǎnsī.
Also to the north is the Huángdòng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.
Yǒng'ān (It is located to the northeast of the prefecture.
In the first month of the third year of Lóngqìng, it was established from Ānmín Zhèn in Guīshàn Xiàn,
with land from Chánglè Xiàn added to it.
To the west is Dōngjiāng.
To the southwest is the Kuānrénlǐ Xúnjiǎnsī,
administered at Kǔzhúpài,
later moved to Táozǐyuán.
There is also the Xùnzhìlǐ Xúnjiǎnsī,
administered at Fènghuánggāng,
later moved to Wūshítún, east of the county.
Soon, both returned to their former administrative seats.
Hǎifēng (It is located to the east of the prefecture.
To the north is Wǔpō Lǐng.
To the south, it borders the sea,
also known as Chángshā Hǎi.
Also to the southeast is Jiéshí Wèi.
To the east is the Jiǎzǐmén Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ.
Both were established in the tenth month of the twenty-seventh year of Hóngwǔ.
To the south is the Jiéshèng Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ,
established in the second month of the twenty-eighth year of Hóngwǔ,
originally named Jiéjìng,
renamed in the third month.
There is the Jiǎzǐmén Xúnjiǎnsī.
Also to the west is the Ébù Lǐng Xúnjiǎnsī.
Also to the southwest is the Chángshā Gǎng Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Xièdào.
Lóngchuān (It is located to the northeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, Xún Zhōu was administered here,
directly subordinate to Guǎngdōng Dào.
In the fourth month of the second year of Hóngwǔ,
the sub-prefecture was abolished,
and it became subordinate to this prefecture.
To the east is Huòshān.
To the south is Lóngjiāng,
which is the upper course of Dōngjiāng,
flowing in from Ānyuǎn Xiàn in Jiāngxī.
To the east is the Tōngqú Xúnjiǎnsī,
later moved to Lǎolóng Bù,
soon returned to its former administrative seat.
To the northeast is the Shíyīdū Xúnjiǎnsī.
Chánglè (It is located to the northeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Xún Zhōu.
In the fourth month of the fourth year of Hóngwǔ, it became subordinate to this prefecture.
The old administrative seat was north of Zǐjīn Shān.
In the early Hóngwǔ period,
it was moved to the present administrative seat.
To the southeast is Xīngníng Jiāng.
To the south is the Shí'èrdū Xúnjiǎnsī.
Also to the west is the Qīngxī Xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.
Xīngníng (It is located to the northeast of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Xún Zhōu.
In the fourth month of the second year of Hóngwǔ, it became subordinate to this prefecture.
To the south is Xīngníng Jiāng,

To its northeast is Wǔjìng Prefecture,
established in the 3rd year of Chénghuà (1467),
abolished at the end of Wànlì.
Also to its east is Dàhuángjiāngkǒu, to its north is Jìngníngxiāng, to its northeast is Dàxuānxiāng, also Sīlóngxiāng, also Mùpánpǔ, to its southwest is Chánglínxiāng six Xúnjiǎnsī.
Also to its south is Luóxiù Tu Xúnjiǎnsī,
also to its north is Bìtānbǎo, Zhènxiábǎo,

To its east is Niúshǐwānbǎo,
to its west is Yānchōngbǎo, Xiùjiāngbǎo,

Píngnán (to the east of the prefecture.
To its southeast is Gōngjiāng River,
which is the Xúnjiāng River,
to its east the Báimǎjiāng River flows into it.
There was also Fèngyìwèi,
established in the 28th year of Hóngwǔ (1395) in the 8th month in Fèngyì Prefecture,
moved here in the 6th year of Zhèngtǒng (1441) in the 5th month.
To its northeast is Dàtóng, to its northwest is Tàichuān, to its southwest is Wǔlín three Xúnjiǎnsī.
Also to its south is Dòngxīn, to its southeast is Sānduī, to its northeast is Dàxiá, to its northwest is Pínglǐng four Tu Xúnjiǎnsī.
Guì [County] (West of the prefecture.
Formerly Guìzhōu,
directly administered by the Guǎngxī Liǎngjiāng Circuit.
In the tenth month of Hóngwǔ 2, it was demoted to a county
and came under [this prefecture].
Nánshān is to the south.
There are also Dōng, Xī, and Běi Mountains.
To the south is the Yù Jiāng,
also called the Nán Jiāng.
All streams flow into it.
There is the Xiàngwǔ Jūnmín Qiānhùsuǒ,
originally the Xiàngwǔ Shǒuyù Qiānhùsuǒ.
In the tenth month of Hóngwǔ 18, it was established in Xiàngwǔ Zhōu.
In the third month of Hóngwǔ 30, it was promoted to a Jūnmín Suǒ.
In the fifth month of Zhèngtǒng 6, it moved to outside the north gate of the county.
In Wànlì 23, it moved again to Xiècūnjùn, northwest of the county.
To the southeast are Xīn'ānzhài and Běishānzhài, two Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Also to the south is Qiáotóuxū, to the west is Wǎtángdù, also Wǔzhōuzhài, also Dōngxuédù, and also Guōdōnglǐ, five Patrol and Inspection Offices,
now defunct.
Also to the southeast is Sānjiāngchéng,
built during the Wànlì era.
) Liǔzhōu Fǔ (Formerly Liǔzhōu Lù in the Yuán dynasty.
) In Hóngwǔ 1, it was made a prefecture.
It administered two prefectures (*zhōu*)
and ten counties.
It is 400 *lǐ* northeast of the Provincial Administration Commission. Mǎpíng (The seat [of the prefecture].
In the Yuán dynasty, it was a direct dependency of the prefecture.
In Hóngwǔ 1, the prefectural seat was moved here.
To the south is the Liǔ Jiāng,
also called the Xúnshuǐ,
and also the Qián Jiāng.
Its upper course flows from Lípíng Fǔ, Guìzhōu, into the prefectural territory.
Its lower course flows to Guìpíng Xiàn and merges with the Yù Jiāng,
also called the Yòu Jiāng.
To the south are Xīnxīngzhèn and Dūbózhèn, two Patrol and Inspection Offices.
There was also the Guīhuàzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office,
now defunct.
Luòróng (Northeast of the prefecture.
The former seat was Báilóngyán.
During the Tiānshùn era,
it moved to Zhūdòng.
During the Zhèngdé era,
it was occupied by the Yáo and Zhuàng peoples.
In the eleventh month of Jiājìng 3, it was recovered.
In the first month of Wànlì 4, it moved to Língtáng.
The old seat at Zhūdòng became Pínglèzhèn,
and one hundred soldiers were left to guard it.
South of the city is the Luòqīng Jiāng.
It enters the Liǔ Jiāng at Mǎpíng Xiàn.
To the southwest are Jiāngkǒuzhèn and Yùn Jiāng, two Patrol and Inspection Offices.
To the east is the Pínglèzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office,
located at Shíliú Jiāng.
Later it moved to Zhōngdù, northeast of the county.
Also to the southwest was the Zhāngluòzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office,
now defunct.
Liǔchéng (Northwest of the prefecture.
The former seat was south of Lóng Jiāng.
In the Yuán dynasty, it was the prefectural seat.
In Hóngwǔ 1, the seat moved to east of Lóng Jiāng,
and the prefecture seat moved to Mǎpíng Xiàn.
The Lóng Jiāng flows in from Tiānhé Xiàn,
and merges with the Róng Jiāng,
which is the upper course of the Liǔ Jiāng.
To the east is the Dōngquánzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office.
To the north is the Gǔchénzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office,
initially located on the east bank of the Róng Jiāng,
later moved to Mǎtóuyì.
Also to the northeast are Gǔqīngzhèn, to the west is Luòhǎozhèn, and also Liàodòngzhèn, three Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Luóchéng (Northwest of the prefecture.
In the tenth month of Hóngwǔ 2, it was established from Luóchéng Xiāng,
subordinated to Róngzhōu.
In the fifth month of Hóngwǔ 10, it came under [this prefecture].
To the north is the Wǔyáng Jiāng.
Its lower course merges with the Róng Jiāng.
To the north are Wǔyángzhèn, also Mòlízhèn, and also Tōngdàozhèn, three Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Also formerly there were Ānxiāngzhèn, Lèshànzhèn, and Zhōngdòngzhèn, three Patrol and Inspection Offices,
now defunct.
Huáiyuǎn (North of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Róngzhōu.
In Hóngwǔ 10, it was abolished,
and the Sānjiāngzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office was established.
In the eleventh month of Hóngwǔ 13, the county was re-established
and came under [this prefecture],
its seat at the confluence of the Dàróng Jiāng and the Xún Jiāng.
In Wànlì 19, its seat moved to Dānyángzhèn.
To the northwest is Jiǔqū Shān.
South of the mountain is Shímén Shān.
The two mountains stand guard, flanking [the river].
The Fúlù Jiāng flows through them from Yǒngcóng Xiàn, Guìzhōu.
At Róng Xiàn it becomes the Róng Jiāng.
At Liǔchéng Xiàn it becomes the Liǔ Jiāng.
Also to the northeast is the Xún Jiāng,
which flows from Jìngzhōu, Húguǎng, and joins there.
There is the Xúnjiāngzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office.
Also to the northwest is Wànshízhèn,
and also Yíliángzhèn and Dānyángzhèn, three Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Róng (Northwest of the prefecture.
Formerly Róngzhōu in the Yuán dynasty,
directly administered by the Guǎngxī Liǎngjiāng Circuit.
In the tenth month of Hóngwǔ 2, Róngshuǐ Xiàn, the seat of the prefecture (*zhōu*), was merged into it,
and it came under [this prefecture].
In the fifth month of Hóngwǔ 10, it was demoted to a county.
To the southeast is Língyán Shān.
To the north is Yúnjì Shān.
Its western part is called Shàngshímén,
as two mountains stand guard, flanking [the river],
with the Róng Jiāng flowing in the middle.
Also to the east is Bǎojī Shān,
which produces iron.
To the northeast are Sīguǎnzhèn, to the southeast is Qīngliúzhèn, and to the southwest is Étóu'ài, three Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Also to the north is the Cháng'ānzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office,
originally on the east bank of the Róng Jiāng,
later moved to the west bank.
There was also the Dàyuēzhèn Native Patrol and Inspection Office.
There were also Bǎojiāngzhèn, Lǐyuánzhèn, and Xīdòngzhèn, three Patrol and Inspection Offices,
now defunct.
Láibīn (South of the prefecture.
In the Yuán dynasty, it belonged to Xiàngzhōu.
In the fifth month of Hóngwǔ 10, it came under [this prefecture].
To the southwest is Bái'niúdòng.
To the north is Báiyúnòng.
To the south is the Dà Jiāng,
also called the Dūní Jiāng.
To the west is the Jièpáizhèn Patrol and Inspection Office,
later moved to Nángāng, south of the county.
) Xiàngzhōu (Formerly directly administered by the Guǎngxī Liǎngjiāng Circuit in the Yuán dynasty.
) In the tenth month of Hóngwǔ 2, it came under [this prefecture],
with Yángshòu Xiàn, the seat of the prefecture (*zhōu*), merged into it.
(To the west is Xiàng Shān.
To the east is Léi Shān.
To the south is the Xiàng
Jiāng,
which is the Liǔ Jiāng.
To the northeast is the Lóngménzhài Patrol and Inspection Office.
There were also Éjǐngzhèn and Jiānshānzhèn, two Patrol and Inspection Offices,
now defunct.
) It is 113 *lǐ* northwest of the prefecture,
and administers one county:
Wǔxuān (South of the prefecture (*zhōu*).
In the Yuán dynasty, it was called Wǔxiān.
In Xuāndé 6, its name was changed.
The former seat was Yīnjiāng.
In the third month of Xuāndé 6, it moved to Gāolì.
To the southeast is the Dàténgxiá,
later named Yǒngtōngxiá.
To the west is the Liǔ Jiāng.
There is also the Dūní Jiāng,
also called the Héngshuǐ Jiāng,
which flows into it.
Its lower course becomes the Yòu Jiāng of Xúnzhōu Fǔ,
and also enters the Liǔ Jiāng.
To the northwest are Ānyǒngzhèn and to the southwest Xiànguōzhèn, two Patrol and Inspection Offices.
Also to the east were Dōngxiāng, also Zhōuchōng, and also Xiándé, three Patrol and Inspection Offices,
now defunct.
) Bīnzhōu (Formerly directly administered by the Guǎngxī Liǎngjiāng Circuit in the Yuán dynasty.
) In the ninth month of Hóngwǔ 2, Lǐngfāng Xiàn, the seat of the prefecture (*zhōu*), was merged into it.
In the tenth month, it came under [this prefecture].
(To the southeast is Zhènlóng Shān.
To the southwest is
Dēngtái Shān.
To the west is Gǔlòu Shān.
Below it is Gǔlòuguān.
Gǔlòushuǐ emerges from there,
and flows into the Bīnshuǐ.
The Bīnshuǐ is to the south,
which is the Dūní Jiāng.
To the east is the Ānchéngzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office.
Also to the east was the
Liángcūn Patrol and Inspection Office,
later defunct.
) It is 300 *lǐ* north of the prefecture,

Qiānjiāng (North of the prefecture (*zhōu*).
To the west is Gǔdǎng Shān,

To the northeast is the Dà Jiāng,
which is the Dūní Jiāng.
To the east is the Qiānjiāng Túntián Qiānhùsuǒ,
established in the ninth month of Hóngwǔ 25.
To the southeast is the Qīngshuǐzhèn Patrol and Inspection Office.
There were also Luómùzhèn and Lǐguǎngzhèn, two Patrol and Inspection Offices,
now defunct.

To the north is Dūlìbǎo.

Shànglín (West of the zhōu,

To the west is Dàmíng Shān,

The wèi was formerly in Nándān Zhōu,

In the 12th month of Yǒnglè 2nd year, it was moved east of Shànglín Xiàn,
in the 5th month of Zhèngtǒng 6th year, it was moved to Bīnzhōu Chéng,

To the southwest is Zhōu'ān Bǎo,

To the northwest is Sānpàn Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.

Qìngyuǎn Fǔ (Yuán Qìngyuǎn Lù.)
In Hóngwǔ 1st year, it became a fǔ.
In the 1st month of 2nd year, it was changed to Qìngyuǎn Nándān Jūnmín Ānfǔsī.

It administered four zhōu,

To the northeast, it is 570 lǐ from the Bùzhèngsī.
Yíshān (Dependent.
To the north is Lóngjiāng,
which flows east into Róng Xiàn,
and joins Róngjiāng.
To the west is Héchí Shǒuyù Qiānhù Suǒ,
established in the 10th month of Hóngwǔ 28th year in Héchí Xiàn,
and moved to this location in Yǒnglè 6th year.
To the east is Dàcáo Zhèn, to the west is Huáiyuǎn Zhèn, and also Déshèng Zhèn, and also Dōngjiāng Zhèn, these four xúnjiǎnsī.)
Tiānhé (North of the fǔ,
a little to the east.
The old xiàn seat was in Gāozhài.
In Hóngwǔ 2nd year, it was moved to Lánshí.
In Zhèngtǒng 7th year, it was again moved to Gānchǎng.
In Jiājìng 13th year, it was again moved to Fúlù Zhèn.
In Wànlì 19th year, it was finally moved to its present seat.
To the southwest is Lóngjiāng,
flowing in from Dúshān Zhōu in Guìzhōu.
To the north is Dōngchán Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī,
and also Sīnóng Zhèn, Guīrén Zhèn, these two native xúnjiǎnsī.)
Xīnchéng (South of the fǔ,

To the north is Sānzhài Bǎo Tǔxúnjiǎnsī.)
Héchí Zhōu (Yuán Héchí Xiàn.)
In the 5th month of Hóngzhì 17th year, it was promoted to a zhōu.
(The xiàn's old seat was in Huáidé Gùchéng, north of the zhōu.
In Tiānshùn 6th year, it was moved to Píngfēng Shān.
In Chénghuà 13th year, it returned
to Huáidé.
In Jiājìng 4th year, it was again moved to the south of Fèngyí Shān.
To the west is Zhìzhōu Shān.
To the east is Jīnchéng Jiāng,

North of the river is Jīnchéng Zhèn Xúnjiǎnsī.
Further east are
Dūmíng Zhèn, Tǔbǎo Zhèn, these two xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.)
To the east, it is 250 lǐ from the fǔ.
It administers two xiàn.
Sī'ēn (Northeast of the zhōu.
Formerly subordinate to the fǔ,

The old seat was in Huánjiāng Zhōu.
At the end of Yǒnglè,
it was moved to Qīngtán Cūn.
In the 11th month of Xuāndé 3rd year, it was moved to Báishān Zhài.
In Chénghuà 8th year, it was moved to Ōujiā Shān.
To the south is Huánjiāng,
to the north is Dàixī,

There are Ānhuà Zhèn, Guīsī Zhèn, these two xúnjiǎnsī.
Also Pǔyì Zhèn, Jí'ān Zhèn, Běilán Zhèn, these three xúnjiǎnsī,
now abolished.)
Lìbō (Northwest of the zhōu.
In the 9th month of Hóngwǔ 17th year, it was established from Sī'ēn Xiàn territory,
subordinate to the fǔ.
In Zhèngtǒng 12th year, it was transferred to Nándān Zhōu.
In the 9th month of Chénghuà 11th year, it again became subordinate to the fǔ.
In Zhèngdé 1st year, it came to be subordinate to this zhōu.
To the southeast of the zhōu is Láocūn Jiāng,
which originates from Chénméng Làntǔ Zhǎngguānsī in Guìzhōu,

and becomes Jīnchéng Jiāng.
Also to the east are Qiónglái, to the south is Méngshí, and also Fāngcūn, these three native xúnjiǎnsī,
later abolished.)
Nándān Zhōu Established in the 7th month of Hóngwǔ 7th year.
Abolished in 28th year,
then soon re-established.
(To the west is Mèngyīng Shān,
formerly a silver mine.
To the south is Dūní Jiāng,
flowing in from Dìngfān Zhōu in Guìzhōu.)
To the east, it is 240 lǐ from the fǔ.
Dōnglán Zhōu Established in Hóngwǔ 12th year.
(Xīlán Zhōu was incorporated into it,

To the southeast is Àidòng Jiāng,

also named Hóng
shuǐ Hé,

Nàdì Zhōu (Yuán Dì Zhōu.)
Re-established in Hóngwǔ 1st year.

40 lǐ from the fǔ.
Yǒngshùn Zhǎngguānsī (Southwest of the fǔ.)
Yǒngdìng Zhǎngguānsī (South of the fǔ.

Yǒng'ān Zhǎngguānsī (Established in the 9th month of Hóngzhì 9th year from eighteen lǐ of Tiānhé Xiàn territory.)
Nánníng Fǔ (Yuán Nánníng Lù.)
In Hóngwǔ 1st year, it became a fǔ.

Xuānhuà (Dependent.
To the east is Kūnlún Shān,

Also Héng Shān,

Lóng'ān (Northwest of the fǔ.

Jiāng,

50 lǐ southeast of the fǔ.

Volume 22 Geography 7 Yúnnán Guìzhōu.
Yúnnán. Yǔgòng's Liángzhōu region's outer territories.
The Yuán dynasty established the Yúnnán and other areas Grand Secretariat Branch Secretariat (Xíngzhōngshūshěng).
(Governed from Zhōngqìnglù.)
In the 15th year of Hóngwǔ, on the day Guǐchǒu of the second month, Yúnnán was pacified,
and the Yúnnán Grand Commandery Administrative Office (Dūzhǐhuīshǐsī) was established.
On the day Yǐmǎo, the Yúnnán and other areas Provincial Administration Commission (Chéngbùzhèngshǐsī) was established.
(Co-governed with Yúnnánfǔ.)
It administered 58 prefectures (fǔ),
75 departments (zhōu),
55 counties (xiàn),
and 6 indigenous tribes (mánbù).
Later, it administered 19 prefectures,
2 frontier prefectures (yùyífǔ),
40 departments,
3 frontier departments (yùyízhōu),
30 counties,
8 pacification commissions (xuānwèisī),
4 pacification offices (xuānfǔsī),
5 sub-prefectural pacification offices (ānfǔsī),
33 chief offices (zhǎngguānsī),
and 2 frontier chief offices (yùyízhǎngguānsī).

(bordering with Sìchuān.)

(bordering with Guǎngxī.)

(bordering with Xīfān.)

(bordering with Jiāozhǐ.)
