and the people receive blessings and peace.
First offering,
tune of Shòuhé: The rites are solemn, the first offering proceeds,
all officials hurry forward, jade pendants tinkling.
Your servant respectfully presents the jade goblet,
may the Emperor's heart discern and accept, and the year be prosperous and bountiful.
Second offering,
tune of Jǐnghé: The second cup is raised with reverence,
clear sweet wine is poured and presented.
Looking up at the divine presence, joyful and serene,
Your servant is deeply moved by the imperial grace, truly sincere.
Final offering,
tune of Yǒnghé: Three offerings, and a slight sincerity;
the purification ritual concludes, the Emperor's (Dì) gaze is upon it.
The populace is bathed in virtue, the year is bountiful, and good fortune is bestowed;
Your subject bows his head, exerting sincere prayer.
Removing the sacrificial vessels,
tune of Nínghé: The three offerings are complete, the ceremonies are solemn;
the sacrificial vessels are respectfully removed, not daring to delay.
May good fortune remain, vast and great;
let there be rain and sunshine according to the season.
Sending off the spirits,
tune of Qīnghé: The sacrificial rites are reported as complete, the Emperor's (Dì) gaze is manifest;
Your subject's feelings have reached above, touching the August Heaven (Hàocāng).
On a cloud-path, solemnly driven, returning to the Imperial Abode (Dìxiāng);
Your subject bears the grace and favor, how could it be forgotten?
Auspicious winds and propitious mists fill the altar enclosure;
the common people and all lands shall fully obtain prosperity and peace.
Observing the burning,
tune of Tàihé: Distantly beheld, the celestial path is long;
far, vast, and boundless, going to the upper realm.
Bundles of silk offered to the fire ascend to be heard;
sincerity is conveyed, and abundant grace endures.
The music concludes with nine performances, and spirits and humans are harmonized;
Your subjects, along with all lands, are all blessed by imperial favor.
In the 17th year of Jiājìng, the grand banquet musical scores were established.
Welcoming the spirits,
tune of Zhōnghé: Oh, majestic and pure, extensively covering with benevolence;
having created myriad treasures, bestowing favor upon these common people.
Receiving its brilliance, there is no way to repay;
hence, we trace the ancient past and reverently display this bright purification.
Solemn and vast courtyard, distant purple sky (Zǐmín);
sheng and yong begin to play, auspicious winds guide the clouds.
Your subject bows and prostrates, with utmost diligence in his heart;
beholding the precious imperial carriage, a myriad of spirits arrayed like a forest.
May they deign to arrive, extending their favor and mandate;
linger and accept, observing my reverence and earnestness.
Presenting jade and silk,
tune of Sùhé: Holding jade tablets and silks in the jade hall;
the August Emperor (Shènghuáng) will joyfully approach.
Holding my heart, pure and unified;
bearing the Emperor's (Dì) virtue, vast and encompassing.
Presenting the sacrificial meat,
tune of Nínghé: The year's work is abundant, and all things are accomplished;
millet and rice are fragrant, permeating the sacrificial tripods with their aroma.
Respectfully presenting them, ashamed of their humble insignificance;
the grand ritual is not burdensome, only sincerity matters.
First offering,
tune of Shòuhé: Golden winds stir, the jade palace is clear;
the first cup is offered, communing with the holy spirits.
Looking upon the profound creation, cherishing great blessings;
how to respond? My heart throbs.
Second offering,
tune of Yùhé: The Emperor (Dì) favors me and dwells to accept;
a multitude of sounds converge.
Again I offer a cup, unable to exhaust my subject's heart;
only may the Emperor (Dì) be pleased, for the people are His charge.
Final offering,
tune of Xīhé: Bringing peace to myriad states, with frequent abundant years;
this humble body of mine truly bears the August Heaven (Hàotiān).
Wine three times offered, the heart grows more devout;
the Emperor's (Dì) command joins the retinue, do not quickly depart.
Removing the sacrificial vessels,
tune of Yōnghé: The sacrificial rites are complete, spirits and humans are solemn and harmonious;
honoring the Emperor (Dì) and honoring the parents, striving to exhaust my subject's sincerity.
Only vast grace is boundless;
the sacred countenances stand majestically.
Sending off the spirits,
tune of Qīnghé: The nine Shao (Jiǔsháo) are completed, gold and jade clinking;
the hundred officials stand in solemn array, feathers and shields are put away.
August Heaven (Huángtiān) is above, and the brilliant ancestors (Zhāokǎo) are beside;
the solemn father (Yánfù) matches Heaven, reverently performing his duty.
The grand offerings are concluded, the spirits depart without a fixed direction.
Dark clouds rise, phoenixes and swans soar together.
Divine light shines back, luxuriant and fragrant;
cherishing and gazing, may prosperity and auspiciousness be granted.
Sons, grandsons, and common people shall only take the Emperor (Dì) as their guide;
Oh, brilliant virtue, forever cherished and not forgotten.
Observing the burning,
tune of Shíhé: The dragon carriage disappears into the distance, returning to the upper realm;
golden winds respond to the rhythm, and the pyre rises.
Reaching sincere devotion, joining with divine light.
The Imperial Court (Dìtíng) accepts, jade and silk are presented;
looking down upon the lower land, remembering with favor.
May my people be granted lasting prosperity and health.
In the 18th year of Jiājìng, the grand banquet musical scores at Xīngdū.
Welcoming the spirits,
tune of Zhōnghé: Looking up at the Most High above, the August Vault (Huángqióng);
covering the nine vast regions, pervading everywhere, without end east or west.
When the King (Wáng) goes on royal tours and excursions, he must receive Heaven's gaze;
this journey of your foolish subject truly bears its protection.
First offering,
tune of Shòuhé: Oh, brilliant imperial favor, Your subject's gratitude is deep;
patrolling the lands of the former vassal state, truly residing to receive Heaven.
My humble feelings wish to repay, this heart is earnest;
a jade goblet and dark silks are respectfully offered before the altar.
Second offering,
tune of Fūhé: Music plays three times;
the cup is raised and presented again.
The Emperor (Dì) observes the subtle sincerity, saying "Your sincerity is true";
Your humble subject bows his head, how dare he not be solemn in this refinement?
Final offering,
tune of Chénghé: Your subject came to this land,
originally for the thought of parents.
What of thinking of parents?
To prosper their descendants.
If descendants can prosper,
it is not by merely receiving the Emperor's (Dì) presence; what else could be the cause?
Removing the sacrificial vessels,
tune of Yǒnghé: Solemn are the implements, the sacrificial rites proceed;
the ceremonies are prepared, music and dance are displayed.
My movements, whether retreating or advancing, are crude and wild;
bathed in enveloping benevolence, how can it be measured?
Sending off the spirits,
tune of Gǎnhé: The King's (Wáng) hunt has a precedent in purification and observation;
oh, the burnt offering (chái jì) is foremost, revering the August Heaven (Shàngcāng).
Your subject's feelings are not exhausted, anxious day and night;
only extending foolish sincerity, truly relying on grace and favor.
Distantly gazing, six dragons soar and ascend;
the Emperor (Dì) bestows blessings, for ten thousand generations of eternal prosperity.
In the 11th year of Jiājìng, the musical scores for the rain sacrifice (yú jì) were established.
In the 17th year, they were abolished.
Welcoming the spirits,
tune of Zhōnghé: Oh, majestic Supreme Ruler (Shàngdì),
residing in the jade palace.
Listen, ye common people,
[一一] boundless compassion without end.
Banners and pennants arrive,
serpentine cloud dragons.
Rainfall is widespread,
all treasures come to fruition.
Presenting silks,
tune of Sùhé: As the spirits arrive,
present these patterned red silks.
Grand music is played,
fragrant aroma fills the air.
Profound purification is greatly ablaze,
reaching the purple heavens (zǐmíng).
Earnestly praying for rich dew,
to moisten my beautiful crops.
Presenting the sacrificial meat,
tune of Xiánhé: A hundred rivers bring moisture,
famous mountains produce clouds.
Excessive drought rages fiercely,
rich dew is scarce.
Praying for a good year to Heaven,
sacrificial animals placed on the sacrificial vessels.
As the spirits arrive,
respond with sweet rain.
First offering,
tune of Shòuhé: Solemn and grand sacrifice,
an auspicious day and propitious hour.
Pouring from those wine vessels,
pepper fragrance and a rich aroma.
Great merits extensively help,
timely rain and timely sunshine.
Only the spirits listen,
granting abundant harvests.
Second offering,
tune of Jǐnghé: Majestic purification sacrifice,
greatly kind and greatly enlightened.
Looking up to receive acceptance,
bowing down respectfully to comply.
There is sweet wine,
there is clear wine,
cloud music accompanies the offerings,
solemn and harmonious.
The holy spirits are awe-inspiring,
observing and accepting sincerity.
Final offering,
tune of Yǒnghé: Divine acceptance is unfailing,
the swift approach is dignified.
Fine jade is displayed,
sacrificial wine is offered.
The ritual is repeated three times,
sincerity followed in one accord.
All preparations made with earnest intention,
the offerings presented with ever greater reverence.
The spirits' manifest blessings,
protect our farmers.
Removing the sacrificial vessels,
tune of Nínghé: Oh, the fierce drought,
the people are weary and distressed.
With sacrificial animals and wine,
both dancing and reciting poetry.
The ritual of three offerings is complete,
respectfully removing without delay.
May the spirits listen,
and rain upon our public and private lands.
Sending off the spirits,
tune of Qīnghé: Thus we proceed with reverence and purity,
solemnly serving the August Heaven (Hàoqióng).
Looking up to pray for sweet rain,
to benefit our three crops.
Having accepted and arrived,
they return to the vast sky.
May the lower lands be moistened,
and all regions be united in this.
Gazing at the Signal Fire.
Tune of Tàihé: The vermilion dragon whirls the chariot,
rites complete, music accomplished.
The signal fire having been raised,
it brilliantly summons the pure offerings.
May the Emperor bestow well-being,
with rain distributed and clouds moving.
May our millet and rice be abundant,
and broadly receive its brightness.
When the sacrifice is complete,
the children performing the musical dance sing the Tune of Yúnmén: The essence of the auspicious dragon appears from time to time,
it surveys the stellar division Qúnwěi hanging in the night sky.
Thus, the grand music resounds loudly,
and rows of imperial dancers gracefully sway.
We pray to the local altars of soil, without fail,
presenting jade tablets and bi discs with utmost reverence.
Dense clouds are needed over the six deserts,
and sweet timely rain pours from the nine heavens.
Our farmers are greatly comforted,
and are granted bright abundance for the year.
Musical Odes for the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain, in Separate Altars but Shared Enclosure, in the First Year of Hóngwǔ.
Welcoming the Deities.
Tune of Guǎnghé: Spirits of the five soils,
essences of the hundred grains.
The nation relies on the soil for peace,
the people live by food.
The foundation of the realm is now established,
the sacrificial rites are refined and illuminated.
May the deities arrive,
we respectfully and reverently welcome them.
Presenting the Silks.
Tune of Sùhé: When there is a nation and its people,
the Altars of Soil and Grain are paramount.
The initial bright offering is made,
jade and silk are devoutly presented.
Although the offerings are not extraordinary,
reverence truly conveys them.
Taking this as the rite,
we hope to reach the enlightened deities.
Presenting the Sacrificial Meat.
Tune of Nínghé: The revered altar faces north,
the bright sacrifice is now displayed.
There are pure sacrificial animals,
the rite is manifested through the offerings.
The grand ritual vessels are arrayed,
inner sincerity is expressed.
As the glorious destiny is sustained,
divine blessings will abound.
First Offering.
Tune of Shòuhé: Regarding the Grand Altar of Soil, it is said:
High become mountains and forests,
deep become rivers and marshes.
Revered hills stretch broadly,
and there are also plains and lowlands.
It is administered by the deity,
and all spirits perform their duties.
The clear sweet wine is first presented,
earnestly we summon and reach.
Regarding Gōulóng as co-sacrificed, it is said:
He leveled and governed the waters and land,
a divine achievement for ten thousand generations.
The people are at peace, things thrive,
the creative transformations are in harmony.
His boundless benefaction,
calls for abundant gratitude in sacrifice.
Co-sacrificed with dignity,
revered by the nation.
Regarding the Grand Altar of Grain, it is said:
Millet, panicled millet, rice, and sorghum,
wheat and barley bring forth auspiciousness,
serving as the heaven for the people.
Years of bumper harvests,
their merit is immense,
their grace is truly everlasting.
Thus, fragrant offerings are brought forth,
to be enjoyed and presented.
Regarding Hòujì as co-sacrificed, it is said:
The majestic Hòujì,
is able to match Heaven.
He gave birth to excellent seeds,
and cultivated vast fields.
The people live by eating grains,
his merit will last for ten thousand years.
An altar is established in the capital,
to receive these auspicious and pure offerings.
Second Offering.
Tune of Yùhé: Regarding the Grand Altar of Soil, it is said:
Broad and profound without bias,
its essence is vast!
Its virtue equals the yielding Kūn,
from it all things are born!
It bestows upon the people the benefits of the land,
divine transformation takes effect!
Reverently performing the sacrifice with devotion,
it is an auspicious omen for the nation!
Regarding Gōulóng as co-sacrificed, it is said:
He surveyed the four directions,
his great achievements were manifest.
The Nine Provinces were pacified,
the Five Phases are in order.
The altar positions are settled,
sacrificial animals and wine are presented.
This is revered, this is solemn,
a brilliant ritual code.
Regarding the Grand Altar of Grain, it is said:
For the myriad people,
what they rely on is grain.
Rain and sunshine are timely,
families are provided for and people are content.
Granaries fill the capital,
the deity bestows abundant blessings.
We respectfully present these rites,
the bright service is truly solemn.
Regarding Hòujì as co-sacrificed, it is said:
He personally labored in farming,
possessing the Way of the prime minister.
No weeds or tares,
truly firm and good.
Agriculture established the nation,
the royal foundation is eternally preserved.
From now on, may there be abundant years,
and may we always offer duckweed and algae.
Final Offering.
Tune of Yùhé,
lyrics are the same as the Second Offering.
Removing the Vessels.
Tune of Yōnghé: The rites display their diligence,
the music plays its rhythm.
Various offerings are fragrant,
the deities are reached.
Solemnly, the officials,
then remove the sacrificial vessels.
Reverent and harmonious,
all share in the joy.
Sending Off the Deities.
Tune of Ānhé: The altar is clean and pure,
the sovereign is firm and upright.
Where the deities return,
they rest here in peace.
The land is tranquil and secure,
the year's grains are smoothly completed.
The sacrificial matters are clear and bright,
forever achieving peace and prosperity.
Gazing at the Burial.
Tune of Shíhé: As the morning light is about to emerge,
both offerings and enjoyment are completed.
Burying these sacrificial animals and silks,
they reach the obscure depths.
Deities and humans are in harmony and joy,
truly fulfilling our hearts.
Perpetual pure sacrifices,
begin from this day.
Musical Odes for the Combined Sacrifice to the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain in the Eleventh Year of Hóngwǔ.
Welcoming the Deities.
Tune of Guǎnghé: We believe that soil and grain are the artisans of creation,
establishing life for the people, thus worthy of profound gratitude.
The people sing and dance, harmonious in the morning,
preparing the feast and performing duties, awaiting and welcoming.
Imagining the sages arriving, auspicious winds arise,
we reverently bow our heads and announce a bountiful year.
First Offering.
Tune of Shòuhé: Ethereal qi merges, things are nurtured,
the people's lives are established, bearing hidden merits.
We shall present jade and silk, offering our humble sincerity,
the first pouring of sweet wine is presented, the people's blessings are vast.
Second Offering.
Tune of Yùhé: I bid the musicians and dancers to again raise their cups,
may the deities brilliantly respond, and the military and people be healthy.
Thoughts of reverence surely abound, the spiritual aura pervasive,
with deep gratitude, we bow to the auspicious light.
Final Offering.
Tune of Xīhé: Shields and feathers fly and swirl, wine flows in three rows,
fragrant smoke curls, cloud banners and canopies flutter.
I now bow my head, joyful yet awe-struck,
the divine countenances are pleased, and colorful clouds appear.
Removing the Food Offerings.
Tune of Yōnghé: Humbly presenting the modest rites, the deities are pleased to receive,
resounding silks and bamboos, music and dance soar.
May auspiciousness widely descend upon all regions, near and far,
may all the people throughout the land be entirely well and secure.
Sending Off the Deities.
Tune of Ānhé: The ethereal qi gently flows, auspicious light spreads,
dragon chariots and phoenix carriages soar aloft.
From afar, we gaze and bow, wondering where they depart,
the people's blessings remain, and timely rain and sunshine prevail.
Gazing at the Burial.
Tune of Shíhé: Bearing the food offerings, we proceed to the burial place,
bells ring and dances lead, sounds clanging harmoniously.
We reflect that the deities have accepted, and the people's blessings rise,
I now bow my head, thanking the gracious light.
Musical Odes for the Newly Established Imperial Altars of Soil and Grain in the Tenth Year of Jiājìng.
Welcoming the Spirits.
Tune of Shíhé: The east wind melts the earth's veins,
The foremost task is farming and labor.
(For the autumn sacrifice, it says:
"The golden wind fills all treasures,
Rejoicing in the completion of farming and labor."
) Sacrificing to the spirits here in the royal garden,
May they come and accept, comforting my heart.
First Offering.
Tune of Shòuhé: Spirits, approach,
Ritually presented are pure libations,
Humble silks are in the chest,
The first offering is respectfully observed.
May the spirits discern this,
And enjoy these offerings of algae and duckweed.
What do I sacrifice for?
Prayer and recompense are the reasons.
May the spirits bestow blessings,
Then will our people prosper.
Second Offering.
Tune of Yōnghé: Two cups are now raised,
Expressing this earnest devotion.
May the spirits be pleased and accept,
Auspicious mists billow thickly.
Final Offering.
Tune of Nínghé: The ritual concludes with three rounds of wine,
Rejoicing in abundant grains: millet, panicled millet, and sorghum.
Farm work awaits prosperity and health,
I bow my head in anticipation.
Removing Offerings.
Tune of Bǎohé: The ritual is announced complete,
The three offerings are finished.
Removing them without delay,
May blessings be poured upon the fields.
Meeting with auspicious rewards,
Protecting this bountiful harvest.
Sending Off the Spirits.
Tune of Guǎnghé: Plowing and weeding are paramount,
(For the autumn sacrifice, it says:
"Plowing and weeding are announced complete."
) Laboring for beans and bamboo baskets.
The grains rely on this,
In these vast fields.
I will use them for sacrifice,
May the spirits linger a while.
May auspicious blessings remain,
Matching my purity and piety.
Respectfully mounting their chariots, swirling among the clouds,
Bestowing upon us bountiful years.
Observing the Burial.
Same tune.
Music for Sacrifices to the Heavenly Deities and Earthly Deities in the second year of Hóngwǔ.
Welcoming the Heavenly Deities.
Playing the Tune of Zhōnghé: Auspicious day, propitious hour,
The sacrificial rites are duly arranged.
The esteemed deity of Tàisuì,
Thunder, rain, wind, and clouds.
How majestic their numinous power,
Clearly discerning my heart.
Waiting for them and welcoming them,
May they come and accept.
After presenting the silks,
All is the same as the morning sacrifice.
Welcoming the Earthly Deities.
Playing the Tune of Zhōnghé: Auspicious day, propitious hour,
The sacrificial rites are duly arranged.
Only the deities of the earth,
A myriad of spirits in abundance.
The嶽zhèn, the海dú,
Mountains, rivers, and the chénghuáng,
Within Zhōngguó,
And extending to the four directions.
How majestic their numinous power,
Clearly discerning my heart.
Waiting for them and welcoming them,
May they come and accept.
After presenting the silks,
All is the same as the morning sacrifice.
Music for Combined Sacrifices to Heavenly Deities and Earthly Deities in the sixth year of Hóngwǔ.
Welcoming the Spirits.
Tune of Bǎohé: Auspicious day, propitious hour,
The sacrificial rites are duly arranged.
The esteemed deity of Tàisuì,
Thunder, rain, wind, and clouds,
The嶽zhèn, the海dú,
Mountains, rivers, and the chénghuáng.
Within Zhōngguó,
And extending to the four directions.
How majestic their numinous power,
Clearly discerning my heart.
Waiting for them and welcoming them,
May they come and accept.
After presenting the silks,
All is the same as the morning sacrifice.
Music for Separate Sacrifices to Heavenly Deities and Earthly Deities restored in the ninth year of Jiājìng.
Welcoming the Heavenly Deities.
Tune of Bǎohé: Auspicious day, propitious hour,
The sacrificial rites are duly arranged.
Propitious clouds and sweet rain,
Spirits of wind and thunder.
How resplendent their numinous power,
Their merit manifested among the people.
Assisting in the profound transformation,
Proclaiming vast benevolence.
Now making this recompense sacrifice,
Discerning these offerings of algae and duckweed.
After presenting the silks,
All is as before.
Welcoming the Earthly Deities.
Tune of Bǎohé: Auspicious day, propitious hour,
The sacrificial rites are duly arranged.
Numinous mountains, regional guardians,
Spirits of the seas and rivers,
The capital region and the four directions,
Spirits of mountains and marshes.
Nurturing spirits and dividing regions,
Blessing our people.
Presenting this recompense offering,
Discerning our reverence and solemnity.
After presenting the silks,
Also as before.
Music for Sacrifices to the Stars and Constellations of the Zhou Heavens in the fourth year of Hóngwǔ.
Welcoming the Spirits.
Tune of Nínghé: The stars and constellations display their patterns,
Arranged across the dark firmament,
Choosing this auspicious day,
The sacrificial rites are honored.
How majestic their numinous power,
Clearly discerning my heart.
Respectfully waiting and welcoming,
Hoping they will come and accept.
Presenting the Silks.
Tune of Bǎohé,
Words are the same as the morning sacrifice.
First Offering.
Tune of Bǎohé: The spirits have lingered,
Various items are now presented.
At the beginning of the sacrifice,
Sweet wine is now laid out.
Looking up to their numinous radiance,
That they may enjoy and accept.
What is offered with the wine?
Music played with eight tones.
Second Offering.
Tune of Zhōnghé: The spirits have already accepted the first offering,
The second offering is again raised,
Pouring sweet wine,
Respectfully presented to the spirits.
How vast they are above,
Feasting and finding peace.
May this express my humble thoughts,
Communicating with the divine.
Final Offering.
Tune of Sùhé: The spirits have already accepted the second offering,
The final offering is now prepared.
Though the humble rites are meager,
May they convey the intention.
Presenting this wine,
Completing my regular sacrifice.
May the spirits regard and accept,
Forever joyous.
Removing the Vessels.
Tune of Yùhé: The sacrificial rites are about to conclude,
The spirits have already accepted.
Removing these vessels,
To complete the ritual.
May the spirits be joyful and pleased,
Without interruption from beginning to end.
The music plays again,
May it convey humble sentiments.
Sending Off the Spirits.
Tune of Yōnghé,
Words are the same as the morning sacrifice.
Observing the Burning Pit.
Tune of Yōnghé: The spirits have already enjoyed the sacrifice,
Their numinous chariots now return.
The sacrificial smoke has risen,
The divine silks are now burned.
Majestic in the vast heavens,
Swiftly they depart.
My earnest heart,
Gazing but unable to reach.
Music for Sacrifices to Tàisuì and the Monthly Generals in the eighth year of Jiājìng.
Welcoming the Spirits: Auspicious day, propitious hour,
The sacrificial rites are duly arranged,
Assisting the nation and protecting the people,
The esteemed deity of Tàisuì,
The monthly generals of the four seasons,
Gōngcáo and Sīchén.
How majestic their numinous power,
Clearly discerning my heart,
Waiting for them and welcoming them,
May they come and accept.
After presenting the silks,
All is the same as the divine deities.
Music for the Ancestral Temple in the first year of Hóngwǔ.
Welcoming the Spirits,
Tune of Tàihé: The source of blessing opened,
virtue through the generations was honored.
I, with my humble person,
established the foundation and accomplished merit.
In the capital,
the ancestral temple is to the east.
May my descendants,
forever cherish the ancestral ways.
Our essence is the same,
our breath interconnected.
Come and be honored,
the imperial spirits appear and merge.
Presenting the Imperial Decree and Seal,
Tune of Xīhé:
) As water has a source,
as a tree has roots.
Ancestors accumulated good deeds,
blessings descend upon later generations.
The imperial decree and seal are carved with jade,
virtue is manifest and names are honored.
Reverently performing the rites,
looking up to repay great grace.
Presenting the Sacrificial Meats,
Tune of Nínghé:
) Bright are the ancestors,
whose spirits rest in the pure temple.
Offering livestock,
not merely to fulfill filial piety.
May we communicate with the divine,
may we achieve good governance.
This is the way of emperors,
and also the teaching of the ancestors.
First Offering,
Tune of Shòuhé:
First Offering says:
We think of the august high ancestor,
profoundly mysterious.
His distant years passed,
his spirit is in heaven.
Graciously presiding over the great hall,
his remaining blessings are endless.
May he be pleased with the offerings,
and forever ensure its transmission.
For Yìzǔ Miào,
First Offering says:
We think of the august great-grandfather,
pure, diligent, and of ancient virtue.
Hiding his brilliance in the fields,
Heaven bestowed abundant blessings upon him.
He protected my great-grandson,
broadly opening the realm.
Remembering the distant past with utmost reverence,
diligently following former rules.
For Xīzǔ Miào,
First Offering says:
Our august ancestor,
good and sagacious, left behind plans.
His abundant virtue is everlasting,
flowing with the Sì River.
It sprouted in his descendants,
and bright sacrifices are now performed.
His auspicious nourishment is like the sea,
how can his grace be repaid?
For Rénzǔ Miào,
First Offering says:
Our august father,
both pure and benevolent.
He did not display himself,
but enabled his successors.
His son possessing the empire,
honor reverts to the parent.
The auspicious reign is renewed,
thus it has its cause.
Second Offering,
Tune of Yùhé: Facing our closest kin,
as if they were alive.
Their spiritual essence is bright,
influencing and arriving in the courtyard.
As if seeing their form,
as if hearing their voice.

tune of Yǒnghé: The spirit is omnipresent,
resplendent in heaven.
We welcome and send it off,
at the banquet of offerings.
Crowned robes are arrayed,
gold and stone instruments are suspended.
When it departs, there is nowhere it does not go,
its pendants fluttering.
Viewing the Burial,
tune of Tàihé: Prayer silks, sacrificial animals, and sweet wine,
the First Farmer has already partaken,
leaving nothing, not defiling,
buried deep and profound.
Profound is its burial,
illustrious is its presence.
This is the constant of ritual,
not only now, but always.
In the ninth year of Jiājìng, the musical movements for offerings to the First Silkworm were set.
Welcoming the Spirit,
tune of Zhēnhé: Oh, solemn is the spirit,
who first initiated sericulture.
Clothing our myriad people,
protecting our homeland.
This grand ceremony is performed,
on a sunny spring day.
Respectfully we welcome the chariot of rosy clouds,
spiritual energy flowing abundantly.
Presenting the Silks,
tune of Shòuhé: May the spirit descend,
fragrant and sweet.
Now presenting jade disks,
now presenting patterned silks.
Looking up, we pray for clear discernment,
propitious aura pervading.
Behold these silkworm women,
numerous as clouds.
First Offering,
tune the same as Presenting the Silks.
Second Offering,
tune of Shùnhé: Now raising the clear goblet,
the silkworm sacrifice is greatly clear.
To reach and be enjoyed,
drums and zithers, flutes and mouth organs play.
Feminine teaching is widely manifested,
the virtue of the female principle is truly pure.
May the spirit hear it,
and discern this sincere offering.
Final Offering,
tune of Nínghé: May the spirit descend,
the mulberry lands are suitable.
Three reelings, seven finishing processes,
this is the cocoon silk.
The offering ritual has ended,
the spirit will not abandon us.
Bestow upon us pure garments,
with patterns adorning the imperial ceremony.
Removing the Food,
tune of Ānhé: The sacrificial vessels are all removed,
the ritual without fault.
Both rectified and ordered,
our sacrifice is greatly reverent.
We think of the ancients,
Gētán truly virtuous.
May the bright spirits partake,
forever guarding the mulberry paths.
Sending off the Spirit,
tune of Hénghé: The spirit ascends,
the day is clear, rosy clouds steam.
Assisting these women's crafts,
looms and shuttles prosper.
Now returning to the Xuan Palace,
phoenixes soar and ascend.
We gaze but cannot reach,
forever bestowing auspicious signs.
Viewing the Burning,
tune the same as Sending off the Spirit.

In the third year of Hóngwǔ, the musical movements for court audiences were set.
Ascending the Hall,
the tune of Fēilóng Yǐn is played.
Officials perform their bows,
the tune of Fēngyúnhuì is played.
The Chancellor delivers his address,
the tune of Qìng Huángdū is played.
Returning to position,
officials perform their bows,
the tune of Xǐ Shēngpíng is played.
Returning to the Palace,
the tune of Hè Shèngzhāo is played.
All are found in the later 'Nine Movements for Banquets and Feasts'.
Revised in the twenty-sixth year.

Sháolè,

arrayed like stars拱 around the North Star.

In the twenty-sixth year of Hóngwǔ, the musical movements for the Empress's New Year, Winter Solstice, and Qiānqiū Festival audiences were set.

After Xuāndé, the musical movements for the Empress Dowager's audiences were added and set.
The tune of Tiānxiāng Fèngsháo: Dragon-tiered, phoenix-gabled halls, with rosy clouds at dawn,
embroidered curtains open, heavenly fragrance pervades,

all together offer blessings,

The Way of the female principle is tranquil, all creatures are nourished,

In the third year of Hóngwǔ, the musical movements for banquets and feasts were set.
First Movement, the tune of Qǐ Línháo,
named Fēilóng Yǐn: For a thousand years, a sagely ruler is born in Zhonghua,
royal aura forms dragons and tigers.
Raising his sword, he rose from Huaixi,
with brave generals and mighty armies,
in a hundred battles, he conquered strong barbarians.
Galloping through cold and heat on horseback,
generals and soldiers shared sweet and bitter.
Orderly, the dust of war settled,
tyrants suppressed, people pacified,
achievements like Tāng and Wǔ.
Second Movement, the tune of Kāi Tàipíng,
named Fēngyúnhuì: Jade fortresses overlook the river city,
wind and clouds encircle the imperial camp.
Driving tower ships, dragons and tigers move freely,
flying cannons fired by mechanism drive away the Six Jia,
surrendering generals,
defeating Hu barbarian soldiers.
Chatting and laughing, he seized the great whale,
the morale of the three armies increased.
One battle,
the universe became clear and peaceful,
from then on, Hua and Yi united,
establishing the imperial enterprise,
celebrating great peace.
Third Movement, the tune of Ān Jiànyè,
named Qìng Huángdū: Where tigers crouch and dragons coil, a beautiful land,
the true lord founded the base,
a thousand years of wind and clouds gather.
One hundred thousand brave soldiers and iron cavalry,
ministers and commanders all fled in disarray.
Sweeping away vexatious hardships, bestowing virtue and benevolence,
lanes and alleys sing praises,
fields and wilderness exude harmony.
The imperial enterprise widely opened for myriad generations,
the common people all look up to the peaceful and prosperous rule.
Fourth Movement, the tune of Xuē Qúnyóng,
named Xǐ Shēngpíng: Then the yellow axe,
pacified Jīngchǔ, cleared Wú and Yuè.
Cleared Wú and Yuè,
from the late Qín to the Jìn dynasty,
how many heroes!
Yōu, Yān, Qí, Lǔ, their dust settled clean,
Yī, Liáng, Shǔ, Lǒng, people's hearts delighted.
People's hearts delighted,
cart tracks and writing unified,
myriad regions shared the same path.
The fifth performance is the Melody of Pacifying Yōu Dū,
named "Hè Shèng Cháo" (Congratulating the Sagely Dynasty): The Mandate of Heaven shifted, and the barbarian's destiny moved on,
The royal army marched north and pacified Yān Jī.

The time when all lands celebrate and gather.
Eliminating tyranny,
Nurturing the wounded and suffering,
The lands south of the desert eagerly behold the old majesty.

The Three Vassal Lords, in their official attire, bow before the jade steps.
The sixth performance is the Melody of Soothing the Four Barbarians,

In China, there is a true ruler.

Rare treasures and exotic products,

White wolves and black leopards,
Nine-plumed scarlet phoenixes,
Five-colored qílín.
The seventh performance is the Melody of Settling Rewards and Grants,
named "Jiǔ Chóng Huān" (Joy of the Ninth Heaven): Heaven and Earth are clear and expansive,
Merits are discussed and rewards are settled,
Achievements are recognized and noble ranks are granted.
Jade belts and golden talismans,
Sable cicadas (official hats) and hairpins,
Their images depicted in the Qílín Pavilion.
Founding heroes of the Great Míng and Hóng Wǔ reign,
Assisted in establishing the dynasty,
With civil administration and military strategy.
Their descendants,

The eighth performance is the Melody of Great Unification,

Expanding territories,
Settling feudal domains.
The Jiāng and Hàn rivers pay distant homage,
Celebrating the four seas,

Eastern barbarians and western travelers,

The ninth performance is the Melody of Upholding Peace,

All celebrating the era of peace.

Putting aside military affairs to cultivate civil arts,
Rewarding merit and promoting virtue,
All lands are vassals and subjects.
Mountains and rivers are solid and firm,

Sleeping in the open, traveling at night on horseback,

giving birth to the sagely Emperor.

Rivers clear, seas calm,

Preserving this distant fortune,

Numerous dukes and marquises,
beautifully and freshly clothed.

Lamb and pig are offered on ornate platters,

The first performance plays Nánfēng,
followed by the singing of Zàipiān.
Jade cups are joyfully raised again,

Sharing joy at this moment,
"Oh, may the Emperor reign for ten million years!"
