the fragrant wine goblet is in the courtyard.
The pipe sounds shrilly,
the string melodies are clear and cold;
jade strikes, metal resounds,
each displaying its skill.
The hoary elders of the state,
admonish and encourage,
virtue is fragrant,
bequeathed in the sacred scriptures.
The songs of Táng show warning,
to forever preserve a good name;
do not be like Tàikāng,
the wise listen to this.
Eighth, perform the曲 (qǔ) "Fānglǐ": The Xià king grew weary of fragrant wine;
Shāng Tāng distanced himself from sights and sounds.
The sages offered deep warnings,
leaving an excellent name for a thousand springs.
Our emperor ascends to the highest position;
imperial meals ensure honor and glory.
At sunset, he does not have time to eat,
spreading virtue to benefit all beings.
The imperial kitchen prepares a lavish feast;
cauldrons and tripods are busy with cooking.
Not only do they provide richness and sweetness,
they are also sufficient to nourish a long life.
Wise people understand this principle,
always keeping the five qi in balance.
Knowing moderation at all times,
the Heavenly Way is clearly manifest.
Ninth, perform the曲 (qǔ) "Driving Six Dragons": The sun shines brightly at midday, the clepsydra is slow;
the dukes and ministers attend the banquet with stately demeanor.
The music of Sháo is played nine times, nine goblets are offered;
fine incense smoke drifts with the auspicious wind.
All officials dance, the emperor's face is joyful;
may the harvests be abundant and the people healthy, always like this.
The six dragons return the carriage, deep within the Fènglóu;
treasure fans open in unison to support the jade table.
Auspicious stars appear, felicitous clouds are many;
the two luminaries shine brighter, the four seasons are harmonious.
The sage's Dao is as vast as heaven and earth;
what endless joy there is, year after year!
曲 (qǔ) for Presenting Meals, "Water Dragon Chant" (Shuǐlóngyín):
Auspicious clouds and purple mists enshroud the precious hall,
o enlightened sovereign,
in the Dragon Virtue Palace.
Dense mist and haze,
between cypresses and pines, green pines stand tall.
Dragon towers and phoenix pavilions,
carved beams and painted rafters,
this is the Penglái grotto.
曲 (qǔ) "Peaceful Pure Music," "Supreme Purity Song" (Tàiqīng Gē):
All nations come to court, presenting tribute,
bowing in homage to the enlightened sovereign,
unifying Huá and Yí.
Across the world, the eight directions and four seas,
north, south, east, and west.
Relying on his sacred virtue,
surpassing Yáo and Shùn, Yǔ and Tāng,
protecting the home and state in peace,
the whole world is united,
converting weapons into farming tools.
Battle flags are still, wine flags beckon,
bowing to heaven and earth.
"Upper Purity Song" (Shàngqīng Gē): First, may the four seasons have timely winds and rains, bringing joy to the people.
Subduing foreign nations,
bringing treasures;
subduing foreign nations,
bringing treasures;
seeing the monarch,
coming to the imperial hall to offer,
coral, agate, glass,
presented at the vermilion steps.
"Opening the Heavenly Gate" (Kāitiānmén): To ensure longevity,
the sun and moon illuminate heavenly virtue,
may the imperial foundation be forever stable for ten thousand, ten thousand years.
Dukes, ministers, civil and military officials come to the assembly,
opening the tortoise-shell banquet,
holding golden goblets.
Receiving the meal,
playing the曲 (qǔ) "Water Dragon Chant" (Shuǐlóngyín),
same as for presenting meals.
Ascending the throne, returning to the palace, all officials perform rites,
playing the曲 (qǔ) "Long Live Joy" (Wànsuì Lè) and "Worshipping the Son of Heaven" (Cháotiānzǐ),
same as for imperial congratulatory ceremonies.
Grand Celebration Banquet for Great Sacrifices: uses the隊舞 (duìwǔ) "All Nations Come to Court" and "Whip Victorious."
Grand Celebration Banquet for the Emperor's Birthday: uses the隊舞 (duìwǔ) "Nine Yí Presenting Treasures" and "God of Longevity."
Grand Celebration Banquet for the Winter Solstice: uses the隊舞 (duìwǔ) "Praising the Sage and Rejoicing" and "Hundred Flowers Worshipping the Sage."
Grand Celebration Banquet for New Year's Day: uses the隊舞 (duìwǔ) "Hundred Acts Lotus Basin" and "Victorious Drums Gathering Lotus."
Established the banquet music and dances in the eighteenth year of Yǒnglè.
First, perform the曲 (qǔ) "Exalting Longevity": The dragon flew, establishing all directions,
receiving the mandate of Heaven,
invigorating the order.
The constant relations are stable in the four seas,
all under heaven, from every corner, come to pay homage.
Ministers and people dance,
cries of "long live" are raised,
offering goblets to our emperor,
may his sacred longevity be as boundless as heaven.
Dance for Pacifying All Under Heaven,
Part One, "Four Borders Quiet" (Sìbiān Jìng):
His might subdues a thousand nations,
the four夷 (yí) barbarians come as guests, presenting memorials.
Manifesting auspicious signs,
receiving the celestial pattern,
the imperial foundation will forever prosper,
for ten thousand years, the mountains and rivers are grand.
Part Two, "Wind Sweeping the Earth" (Guādì Fēng):
The sacred ruler surpasses Yáo, Shùn, Yǔ, Tāng,
establishing the Five Constants and Three Cardinal Guides.
The eight Mán barbarians offer tribute, coming to court before the current emperor,
bowing their heads in sincere awe.
The prime minister in court,
harmonizes yīn and yáng.
The five grains have a good harvest,
all people are joyful and cheerful.
Congratulating our emperor,
unanimously praising him,
all nations surrender.
Second, perform the曲 (qǔ) "仰天恩 (Yǎng Tiān ēn)": Heaven favors the enlightened sovereign,
the five planets are in order,
the four seas are peaceful,
winds and rains are timely, all grains ripen,
ministers and people dance and rejoice in peace.
The virtuous and worthy are in office,
the state and family are forever auspicious.
Our emperor looks up to boundless grace,
sincerely striving day and night.
Yellow-robed children and white-haired elders, full-bellied, sing the responsive曲 (qǔ),
called "Bean Leaves Yellow" (Dòuyè Huáng): Winds and rains are timely,
the five grains have a good harvest,
granaries are full,
greatly benefiting the people's livelihood.
Relying on the emperor's grace, the four seas are clear,
full-bellied, singing,
white-haired elders and yellow-robed children,
together enjoying universal peace.
Four Barbarian Dance Pieces
Part One:
Xiǎo Jiāngjūn (Little General) Following Heaven's will,
the sagely virtue is sincere,
transforming the foreign states,
all coming to the capital.
The four barbarians submit,
dancing in the imperial court.
They present tributes to the enlightened emperor,
bearing precious treasures.
Part Two:
Diànqián Huān (Joy Before the Hall) The four barbarians across all lands submit to the king's command,
all coming to admire the Great Míng (大明).
Ten thousand states and a thousand nations all return to righteousness,
appearing before the imperial court,
paying homage to the benevolent and sagely one.
Along the celestial steps, ranks of many high officials and nobles
unanimously sing of great peace.
Part Three:
Qìng Fēngnián (Celebrating a Bountiful Year) Harmonious energy increases,
luan (鸞) and phoenixes cry,
purple mists arise,
auspicious clouds and morning glow reflect.
Incense burns in golden censers,
its fragrance permeates,
ranks fill the vermilion steps,
the imperial carriage is full.
Strings, winds, xiao (簫) and sháo (韶) harmonize in five notes,
dragon flutes mingle with phoenix sheng (笙).
Part Four:
Bóhǎi Lìng (Order of Bóhǎi) In golden cups,
wine is filled to the brim.
Before the imperial desk,
a host of heroes are arrayed.
The ruler's virtue is complete,
the imperial plan is celebrated,
long live the emperor, a chorus of voices.
Part Five:
Guòménzǐ (Interlude) The sagely ruler rises,
the sagely ruler rises,
displaying awe-inspiring power,
the barbarians are pacified.
Utmost benevolence, utmost virtue, utmost sagely brilliance,
for ten thousand times ten thousand years,
the imperial enterprise is accomplished.
Third Performance: Melody of Gratitude to Earth's Virtue The imperial heart feels the spirit of the earth,
following Heaven's seasons,
virtue is broad and rich.
Magnanimous and vast, all things prosper;
gathering wonders and nurturing excellence, producing outstanding talents.
The Yellow River is clear, the seas are calm,
qílín (麟) arrive, phoenixes cry,
yin (陰) and yang (陽) are forever in peace,
assisting our civilization.
Carriages and Writings United Dance Piece
Part One:
Xīn Shuǐ Lìng (New Water Melody) Embroidered robes and flowered hats set on the vermilion steps,
all officials with their ceremonial attire gather.
Qílín (麟) arrive and dance,
phoenixes come and parade,
civil and military ranks are neat,
paying respects to the sagely and enlightened emperor.
Part Two:
Shuǐxiānzi (Water Immortal) From all eight directions, splendid barbarians and Chinese,
all people under Heaven admire the sagely virtue.
A world of peace with favorable winds and timely rains,
throughout the universe,
all praise the rituals,
relying on the ruler's grace, the people enjoy peace and prosperity.
For ten thousand times ten thousand years, the imperial foundation is firm,
for ten thousand times ten thousand ages, the rivers and mountains are stable,
for ten thousand times ten thousand years, the boundless blessings are equal to Heaven.
Fourth Performance: Melody of the People's Joy All people in the world,
bear the grace of Heaven and Earth,
and are grateful for the sagely favor.
Heaven and Earth are in their proper places, spring throughout the four seas,
the proper great human relationships of ruler and minister, father and son.
The imperial influence is vast,
people's hearts are pure,
joyfully embracing true nature,
forever supporting the enlightened ruler.
Dance Piece: Rectifying All Nations
Part One:
Qìng Tàipíng (Celebrating Great Peace) Corrupt and chaotic elements disturb the court,
creating disaster,
inciting warfare.
Our emperor was furiously enraged,
personally leading an expedition to Bàshàng (灞上),
pointing the celestial spear,
all enemies surrendered.
Part Two:
Wǔshì Huān (Warrior's Joy) On the battlefield of Báigōu (白溝),
banners and flags gather like clouds, obscuring the sunlight.
Orders are strict, morale is high,
the three armies eagerly rise and advance,
sweeping away remnants like a whirlwind,
songs of triumph spread in all directions.
The benevolent and sagely one does not kill those who surrender,
looking towards Hénán (河南),
the enemies lost their spears.
Part Three:
Gǔnxiùqiú (Rolling Embroidered Ball) The rebellious troops resisted,
relying on their strength,
intent on causing calamity,
building a hundred-foot high city wall in Cāngzhōu (滄洲).
Unleashing scorpion venom,
indulging in tiger-wolf ferocity,
who could withstand them?
Following Heaven's will, with abundant virtue and prosperity,
they turned their spears and laid down their armor, all surrendering,
the generals were appeased and returned to their homelands alive,
from then on, the benevolent reputation became even more manifest.
Part Four:
Zhènzhèn Yíng (Winning Every Battle) It does not count Sūn (孫) and Wú's (吳) excellent military strategies,
divine schemes and wise calculations align with yin (陰) and yang (陽),
the eight formations grandly move in the heavens,
who dares to oppose the tiger's cunning and dragon's strategy?
Ten thousand captives were all released,
grateful for the benevolent grace, they honored Heaven.
Part Five:
Déshèng Huí (Returning Victoriously) On both sides and in four directions,
like birds' wings spreading, like wild geese in formation, following wind and cloud.
Unleashing surprise troops,
enemies are immeasurable,
soldiers are strong, horses are strong.
For a hundred li,
banners laid down, spears at rest,
victorious troops return,
filled with joy.
Part Six:
Xiǎo Liángzhōu (Little Liángzhōu) Enemy soldiers defeated, their spirits lost,
leading fierce warriors,
directly crossing the Cháng Jiāng (長江).
Opening city gates,
markets unchanged,
proclaiming sagely grace,
as vast as the sky.
Imperial edicts are issued,
throughout the world,
all look up to the emperor.
Fifth Performance: Melody of Gratitude for Imperial Grace Today, the four seas are peaceful,
songs of praise arise,
rites and music flourish.
Ruler and ministers joyfully meet, ascending to great peace,
officials in elegant attire feast in the vermilion court.
Civil and military officials,
together bear grace and honor,
with loyal hearts and utmost sincerity,
responding to the enlightened emperor.
Heaven's Mandate to the Virtuous Dance Piece
Part One:
Qìng Xuānhé (Celebrating Universal Harmony) Favorable rain and wind, all things flourish,
unifying Chinese and barbarians.
Abundant grains in the four fields respond to the harmonious energy,
a single stalk bears a hundred ears,
a single stalk bears a hundred ears.
Part Two:
Zhǎi Zhuānr (Narrow Brick) Ships and ladders from ten thousand nations come to the imperial steps,
in a year of great peace,
the great foundation is forever secure.
From east, west, south, and north they come to pay homage,
spreading throughout the world,
broadcasting spring's warmth,
the four barbarians are all guests, and their teachings are beautiful.
Since ancient times, enlightened kings have been cautious in their virtue,
not needing military might to subdue the Róng Dí (戎狄).
Auspicious omens gather,
phoenixes come and parade.
A felicitous era for ten thousand times ten thousand years,
the sagely enlightened ruler,
governing Chinese and barbarians.
Sixth Performance: Melody of Celebrating a Bountiful Year All lands look up to the sagely ruler,
a great unification,
nurturing all people.
In years of abundance, seasons, rain, and dew are even,
grains are plentiful, goods and wealth are abundant.
Singing merrily and striking the earth,
the wind is pure, customs are simple,
the four barbarians all come as guests,
rectifying imperial benevolence.
Seventh Performance: Melody of Gathering Auspicious Omens Heaven favors the Great Míng (大明),
the five planets gather,
portending great peace;
the zōuyú (騶虞) appears, sweet dew falls,
wild silkworms form cocoons, auspicious grains grow,
sweet springs gush from the earth, river waters are clear.
Heaven and Earth for ten thousand times ten thousand years,
the four seas are forever peaceful.
Eighth Performance: Melody of Perpetuating the Imperial Plan Heaven's heart favors the sagely emperor,
rectifying the heavenly mandate,
nurturing all nations.
Benevolent winds are announced, rites and music are displayed,
barbarians bow their heads and pay homage in the bright hall.
The imperial plan is consolidated,
worthy ministers assist.
The light of peace fills the sun and moon,
enduring as Heaven and Earth.
Nine performances of the music of 'Great Peace': Imperial grace covers the eight directions,
the three lights shine,
the four seas are clear.
People are well, things are abundant, and harvests are repeatedly good,
all rejoice, feeding themselves and patting their bellies.
The people sing of the Emperor's power,
like Táng Yáo's (唐堯) utmost benevolence.
Heaven and Earth are forever pure,
together enjoying great peace.
The pieces for guiding the meal, welcoming the meal, presenting the meal, ascending the throne, returning to the palace, and officials performing rites,
are all the same as those from the Hóngwǔ (洪武) era.
For great sacrifices and celebrations of completion,
the "Victory Dance of the Barbarian Tribes with Whip and Tassel" is used;
for the Emperor's birthday (Wànshòu Shèngjié, 萬壽聖節),
the "Nine Barbarian Tribes Presenting Treasures Dance" is used;
for the Winter Solstice (Dōngzhìjié, 冬至節),
the "Dance of Praising the Sage's Joy" is used;
for the New Year's Day (Zhèngdànjié, 正旦節),
the "Hundred Entertainments Lotus Basin Dance" is used.
During the Jiājìng (嘉靖) era, additional music for the celebration banquet was established.
Upon ascending the throne,
the music is "Long Live the Emperor (Wànsuì Lè, 萬歲樂)": Five hundred prosperous periods in a felicitous gathering,
the sagely emperor is inaugurated,
the dragon flies to the heavenly throne.
The day of renewed glory for the nine regions and four seas,
the Great Míng (大明) dynasty,
for ten thousand myriad generations.
When officials perform rites,
the music is "Paying Homage to the Son of Heaven (Cháo Tiānzǐ, 朝天子)": Auspicious mist fills the front,
fragrance encircles the Pénglái (蓬萊) Palace.
The wind returns, and the Sháolǜ (韶律) drums boom,
on the lined steps,
banners gleam,
the sun reaches Zhūchén (朱躔).
Yang energy arises in Chìdiàn (赤甸), harmonious and mellow,
penetrating the upper prime.
Ten thousand myriad years of history,
forever celebrating the heavenly palace banquet.
For presenting the protective robe and flowers,
the music is "Water Dragon Chant (Shuǐlóng Yín, 水龍吟)": Auspicious mists float from the golden censers in the treasured palace,
jade tables are arranged,
delicacies are displayed.
Heavenly flowers gleam with color,
illuminating the emerald cloud robe.
Phoenix-like songs and dances,
Yú (虞) court music plays,
long live the King.
First performance of the music "Presenting Ten Thousand Years (Shàng Wànsuì, 上萬歲)": The sagely ruler drapes his robes,
establishes rites and music,
surpassing Yú (虞) and Táng (唐).
The nine compositions of Xiāosháo (簫韶) bring forth auspicious phoenixes,
the sun and moon illuminate the eight directions from the center of the sky.
People are peaceful, things are abundant,
the times are harmonious, and the year is prosperous.
Presenting the cup of ten thousand years,
the imperial lineage has no bounds.
Performing the "Dance of Pacifying the World" (Píngdìng Tiānxià Wǔqǔ, 平定天下舞曲),
the first is
"Four Borders Tranquil (Sìbiān Jìng, 四邊靜)": Heaven reveals auspiciousness,
the sagely ruler revives the order and discipline.
Praise is abundant,
merit is vast,
the nation's fortune is prosperous and flourishing,
the imperial scheme of ten thousand years is grand.
The second is
"Phoenix and Luan Chant (Fèngluán Yín, 鳳鸞 Yín)": Indeed, the emperor is protected by Heaven, sagely and enlightened,
the glorious mandate is proclaimed,
five clouds shimmer,
three platforms are moist,
seven latitudes shine brightly.
Harmonious energy arises,
auspicious signs appear.
Rectifying the myriad people,
employing all worthies.
Wearing the imperial robes at the imperial lectures,
diligently governing in the Palace of Diligence even at night.
The great sacrifice at the circular mound is precise and reverent,
the clear water is pure,
the dark jade disc is round.
Following Wén (文) of Zhōu (周),
inheriting the offerings of Yīn (殷),
the imperial family is blessed for billions of years.
Second performance of the music "Gazing up at Heaven's Grace (Yǎng Tiān'ēn, 仰天恩)": The imperial firmament reveals sagely divinity,
revering the cosmic movement,
worshipping at the suburban altars.
As the first Yang energy stirs, the aura of early spring appears,
all blessings come together, looking up to ultimate benevolence.
Auspiciousness opens up in the sun and moon,
propitious signs are seen in the stars.
Rites and music harmonize with gods and humans,
the universe is completely renewed.
Welcome Meal music,
"Water Dragon Chant (Shuǐlóng Yín, 水龍吟)": Spring fills the carved plate, offering jade peaches,
the reed pipe stirs,
the sun wheel is high,
the faint light of a clearing sky,
remotely reflecting the imperial robe.
A thousand officials dance,
Jūnsháo (鈞韶) music plays alternately,
the tune is of peace and prosperity.
Present Meal music,
"Water Dragon Chant (Shuǐlóng Yín, 水龍吟)": The purple forbidden palace's splendid feast is warm, responding to winter,
drawn by eight chī (螭),
riding six dragons,
jade goblets and jade wine cups,
offered to the emperor seated on the embroidered throne.
Yáo's (堯) heaven widely operates,
Shùn's (舜) clouds fly,
joyfully listening to songs of praise.
Present Soup music,
the first is
"Great Clarity Song (Tàiqīng Gē, 太清歌)": On the longest day (Winter Solstice),
the yellow path opens,
the auspicious energy of Heaven and Earth is joyful,
Yang grows, Yin recedes.
Jūnsháo (鈞韶) music is played,
the melodies are like a phoenix's zither,
the pitches harmonize with a luan's (鸞) flute.
Looking up at the dragon's countenance,
like the sun and moon,
like Shùn (舜), like Yáo (堯).
Golden censers' warm smoke wafts imperial fragrance,
the jade steps are clear and bright, surrounded by auspicious light,
palace plums and garden willows welcome the beautiful spring,
feasting joyfully on Pénglái (蓬萊) Isle.
The second is
"Upper Clarity Song (Shàngqīng Gē, 上清歌)": Clouds embrace the imperial residence,
five stars reflect the beauty of the three platforms.
Look up at the sun and moon,
the upper sky is clear;
look up at the sun and moon,
the upper sky is clear.
A revival again sees the era of Táng (唐) and Yú (虞),
the primordial energy of great harmony naturally returns with the Yang,
the myriad surnames are joyful.
The third is
"Opening the Gate of Heaven (Kāi Tiānmén, 開天門)": The nine layers of heaven,
the sun turns over the imperial capital at dawn.
Feasting in the heavenly home,
together singing "Fish and Algae".
Dragon scales and pheasant tails are high,
wishing the sagely emperor a long life,
celebrating the clear dynasty.
Performing the "Song of Response with Old Men and Young Boys Patting their Bellies and Singing Praises",
"Imperial Luan Song (Yùluán Gē, 御鑾歌)": Elegant music plays of rising peace,
gazing at the crimson palace,
gathering in the jade capital.
Old men and young boys are full of joy,
singing praises and dancing, the four seas are tranquil.
Golden branches bear splendid beauty,
jade trees contain exquisite essence.
Listening to the sound of beating the earth on the roads of prosperity,
the Emperor's power is inexpressible.
Third performance of the music "Grateful for Heaven's Virtue (Gǎn Hàodé, 感昊德)": Imperial virtue operates with bright light,
the first Yang stirs,
all things are born.
A great report of ascending to the center, the dark jade disc is laid out,
rites are revered, music flows, pleasing the Great Clarity.
Stars hang in the purple pole,
the sun shines on the revolving court,
auspicious energy fills Heaven and Earth,
the world is peaceful and calm.
Performed are dance pieces for soothing and pacifying the Four Barbarians.
The first,
“Hè Shèngcháo”: “The Huá and Yí are unified,
Ten thousand states come together.
Present local products,
Cultivate court tributes,
Longing for the imperial prestige from afar,
From south to north,
From west to east.
Looking up at the celestial palace,
Auspicious qi is dense and profound,
The Four Spirits all arrive,
Qílín, Fènghuáng, Guī, Lóng.”
The second,
“Diànqiánhuān”: “Auspicious clouds and clear mists float around the palace halls,
A pulse of vital harmony circulates.
Rites completed, heaven and earth connect, opening the Zhou banquet,
Phoenix flutes are tuned,
Dragon canopies are spread,
Heaven's heart is moved and people rejoice,
Songs of praise fill the four seas.”
The third,
“Qìng Fēngnián”: “Relying on August Heaven,
Granting abundant years,
Diligent in Yǔ’s farming,
Toiling in Shùn’s fields,
Happily fulfilling the wishes of the three types of farmers.
Auspicious grains are splendid,
Propitious wheat is fresh,
Tributes from the nine zhōu,
Offerings from the eight yán,
Divine granaries and imperial stores are all full,
Sustaining the people to nourish the worthy.”
The fourth,
“Xīnshuǐlìng”: “The sagely virtue of pure sacrifices moves the vast heavens,
Great unification.
The Four Barbarians come with tribute,
Holding jade and silk.
Carriages and writing are uniform,
The era is prosperous,
Together listening to the praises of the common people.”
The fifth,
“Tàipínglìng”: “Grand and brilliant sacrifices,
Heaven watches the August Sovereign,
Illuminating the four quarters,
Benevolence flows all around.
From the four frontiers they come,
Rushing forward and trailing behind,
Presenting myriad treasures,
Filling courts and gardens.
Bowing and kowtowing,
Heaven is high, Earth is thick,
Wishing the sage,
Many sons, blessings, and longevity.”
Fourth, the "Mínlèshēng"曲: "The grand rites of gratitude are newly complete,
Symbolizing the virtue of Heaven,
Operating with imperial sincerity.
The Divine Land and Crimson County are forever pure and peaceful,
Spiritual rain and gentle breezes bring joy and great peace.
Yīn and Yáng flow freely,
All things prosper,
The primal transformation naturally spreads,
Truly nurturing all living beings."
Meal-welcoming曲,
“Shuǐlóngyín”: “Five-colored auspicious clouds support the Jade Emperor,
Opening the celestial gate,
Sitting in bright radiance.
Celestial music plays,
An imperial banquet is spread on a winter day.
Civil officials at ease, military officials joyful,
A scene of great peace,
People surpassing Táng and Yú.”
Meal-serving曲,
“Shuǐlóngyín”: “Jade pitches return to Yáng, a new auspicious era,
Feasting in Hàojīng,
Imperial benevolence pervades.
Brilliance illuminates the Milky Way,
One qi resonates with Sháo and Yīng music,
Zither harmonizes with sound,
Jade qín with clear melody,
Gazing up at the Emperor’s face nearby.”
Soup-serving曲,
“Tàiqīnggē”: “People of myriad lands,
Rejoice in the harmonious era,
Dancing and cheering, benefiting from Heaven's work,
Moving like thunder and wind.
Joyfully encountering today,
Southern Mán, Northern Mò,
Eastern Yí, Western Róng,
Coming to pay tribute.
Dàmínggōng,
With star-like dougǒng.
Nine layers of heaven with six flying dragons,
Among five-colored clouds, a pair of colorful phoenixes,
All under heaven, all lands emulate the greetings of Huáfēng,
Truly aligning with the praise of the Yellow River’s clarity.”
Performed are dance pieces for the unification of carriages and writing,
The first,
“Xīnshuǐlìng”: “Five clouds deeply guard the nine-layered city,
Grateful for the vast grace.
The lone ruler rejoices,
Yáng qi just begins to grow,
Rites are now performed.
Imperial virtue is enlightened,
Setting an example for the state and family.”
The second,
“Shuǐxiānzǐ”: “Myriad lands are settled, joyful and peaceful,
The nine domains share benevolence under the sage's enlightenment.
A thousand years of governance following Heaven's mandate,
Sweet dew falls,
The river offers clarity,
Seeing splendid two-headed wheat with conjoined stalks,
Joyful spiritual snow responds to winter,
Witnessing auspicious clouds rising at dawn,
Divine power and transformation moving in unison.”
Fifth, the "Gǎnhuáng'ēn"曲: "Twin watchtowers shine with five-star light,
Rainbow banners are arrayed,
Purple canopies are spread.
Jade calendar on the revolving terrace ushers in new Yáng,
Heavenly grand music harmonizes the gōng and shāng notes.
Deep grace and abundant dew,
Joy fills the auspicious wine cups,
Sun and Moon illuminate the dragon regalia,
Enduring as Heaven and Earth."
Performed are dance pieces for rectifying myriad states,
The first,
“Qìng Tàipíng”: “Heaven truly cares for our sage and enlightened ruler,
Performing rites at the circular mound,
With utmost virtue and sincerity.
The primal creative power is eternally pure,
Grandly receiving the glorious mandate,
Auspicious signs respond,
The scales of Tai are level.”
The second,
“Qiānqiūsùi”: “The sagely lord rides the dragon, governing myriad states,
Auspicious clouds soar, the enlightened era shines anew.
All officials bow and dance, toasting longevity,
Singing the chapter of Tiānbǎo.”
The third,
“Gǔnxìuqiú”: “Five-colored cloud carriage,
Passes through nine layers,
A propitious sight of a flying dragon.
Shining imperial robes,
With fire, algae, and insects.
Striking the tiger-shaped yǚ,
Beating the zhòng bell,
Alligator drums booming.
Eight delicacies arrayed,
Nine tripods abundant.
Yáo’s brows uplifted with color, Shùn’s eyes with double pupils,
Myriad states all prosperous, the four seas harmonious,
Jointly singing praises of the sage's virtue and divine功.”
The fourth,
“Diànqiánhuān”: “The day of restoration for ten thousand years of rites and music,
The great transformation witnesses renewed brilliance.
The Yellow River clear, the seas calm, auspicious signs arrive,
The Five Phases are orderly,
The Seven Administrations are in alignment,
Surpassing the Three and Five reigns, a true primal gathering,
Singing the ode of Yī, having feasted.”
The fifth,
“Tiānxiàlè”: “Myriad spirits bow towards the pure capital,
Worshipping at the southern suburbs,
Revering Heaven and emulating ancestors.
May the sage,
Inherit Heaven’s mandate and receive blessings,
Achieving harmony and nurturing all things,
The tortoise presents the Fàn,
The horse lays out the Tú.”
The sixth,
“Zuìtàipíng”: “Rites and music, ten thousand years of order,
Songs of praise, the four seas prosperous,
Officials in robes dancing on the nine dragon steps,
Looking up at Lìzhèng from the south.
Purple clouds hold high the Emperors Táng and Yú,
Governing the world with enlightened rule by merely letting their robes hang.
The Hàozhōng bird and the Qífèng present auspicious signs,
Truly, people live in the era of Chéngzhōu.”
Sixth, the "Qìngfēngnián"曲: "The sage diligently follows Heaven,
Pacifying myriad states,
Many years of abundance.
Divine granaries and imperial stores are filled as if from heavenly fields,
Clear millet and fragrant black millet for 孔’s devout sacrifices.
Public sentiment is entirely joyful,
Harmonious qi is widely spread,
The imperial blueprint for eternity is passed down,
Like jade discs joined and pearls linked."
Seventh, the "Jízhēngyìng"曲: "Heaven's protection and the Tai scales are level,
Precious dew descends,
The entire Yellow River runs clear,
Auspicious grains and splendid wheat gather lucky omens,
Distant corners and remote regions are filled with joy.
The lone ruler rejoices,
All affairs are rectified,
Myriad states sing praises of universal peace,
Lìzhèng shines anew."
Eight movements of the tune "Eternal Imperial Map": The capital, Hào, hosts a banquet,
extolling the 'Fish in the Pond' (Yú Zǎo),
singing 'The Deer Cry' (Lù Míng).
The borders are peaceful, all nations tranquil,
with interpreters presenting tribute, the Four Seas are serene.
At Xiánchí, the sun breaks,
at Mèigǔ, clouds arise,
the Imperial Throne looks up to the foremost star,
rejoicing in great abundance and prosperity.
Nine movements of the tune "Rejoicing in Great Peace": The imperial ultimate permanently ascends auspiciousness,
heavenly tallies open,
the great fortune flourishes.
Jade pipes usher in spring, activating the first yang,
golden halls grant banquets, singing 'Nine Chapters' (Jiǔ Zhāng),
beasts dance in Yú's court,
phoenixes soar on Qíshān,
the sun illuminates the dragon robes,
the sovereign is sagely, the ministers good.
Tune for welcoming the meal,
Shuǐlóngyín: Fragrant mist permeates the purple pavilions, layered,
looking up to Heaven's virtue,
gazing upon the Emperor's countenance.
Stars gleam, the sea is moist,
sweet rain intermingles with gentle breezes.
Joy compares to kites and fish,
auspicious signs appear as qílín and phoenixes,
forever presenting the encomium of Juǎnē.
Tune for serving the meal,
first part,
Shuǐlóngyín: Ten thousand households, a thousand gates open Jiànzhāng,
the imperial steps are lofty,
the Emperor's seat is displayed.
The Three Enclosures, the Nine Roads,
the Big Dipper's Jade Armillary Shines.
Primal qi is harmonized,
elegant melodies resound,
the glorious dynasty celebrates the wise and good.
Second part,
Tàiqīng Gē: Ten thousand nations,
all come to court,
bowing and singing praise for the Emperor's benevolence,
looking up to and relying on his creation and nurturing.
He upholds the heavenly order,
yin and yang are in sequence,
people and creatures live happily.
Meeting a sagely ruler,
ten thousand years of spring,
forever receiving auspicious decrees.
Huá, Yí, Mán, Liáo all return to righteousness,
the common people reach old age without knowing war,
patting their bellies, chewing their food, in a realm of great peace,
the Nine Provinces enjoy tranquility.
Playing the "Heaven's Mandate, Virtuous Dance" tune,
first part,
Wànsuìlè: The day the Emperor of Great Peace rises and prospers,
treading the beginning, forever,
yang returns, bringing primal auspiciousness.
Sweet springs and ganoderma fungi, auspicious omens gather,
it is said that five stars converged in the chamber.
Second part,
Hè Shèngzhāo: The one supreme good,
a hundred measures renewed.
Holding the crimson tally,
responding with profound resonance,
enjoying the Great Purity.
Great rites are performed,
sacrificial affairs are brilliantly manifest, moving Heaven's heart,
for countless ages receiving blessings.
The enlightened king is prudent in virtue,
the four barbarians all come as guests.
Playing the "Winning the Whip, Defeating the Barbarians, Processional Dance, Responsive Tune,"
first part,
Zuì Tàipíng: Starry splendor in the purple palace is high,
cloud qi winds around the vermilion tower.
Nine Yi tribes with repeated interpreters arrive by ladder and ship,
the imperial map illuminates the eight directions.
The jade realm is dustless, the bright moon gleams,
the Milky Way turns by itself at dawn over Fúsāng,
all is tranquil and orderly, returning to the kingly way.
A hundred beasts dance,
phoenixes sing to the xiáosháo.
Second part,
Kànhuāhuì: The whole world,
relies entirely on our Emperor, the Most Sage.
See the Jade Gate frequently [opening],
Tiānshān is settled,
the four barbarians submit obediently to the king's command.
Tiānbǎo Gē,
for the common people.
Third part,
Tiānxiàlè: Nine layers of music play, ten thousand flowers bloom,
gazing at the dragon tower,
clouds steam and mist rises.
Looking up to Heaven's craftsmanship,
the Emperor's reign is harmonious and prosperous,
ministers and people rejoice and uphold him.
His benevolence spreads,
throughout the nine regions.
Fourth part,
Qīngjiāngyǐn: When the yellow bell is played, yang and harmony are long,
virtue abounds, Heaven's heart bestows.
Human culture is as bright as the sun and moon,
the nation's power is as majestic as mountains and rivers,
folk songs of the Qú chamber frequently beat the ground.
Playing the "Opening Address" tune,
first part,
Qīngjiāngyǐn: When the heavenly music finishes, the sun is at its zenith,
already intoxicated, joyful sounds stir.
Cloud patterns alongside dragon robes,
a soaring momentum like a majestic phoenix,
ten thousand regions are peaceful and joyful, raising glorious praise.
Second part,
Qiānqiūsuì: Superiors and inferiors rejoice together, the banquet ritual completed,
the first yang surges,
all myriad things are prosperous.
Wind and clouds meet, opening an enlightened era,
the purple ultimate turns the celestial sphere.
The banquet concludes,
tune for officials performing rites,
Cháotiānzǐ: Civil and military officials,
joyfully stir the Chéngmíng Hall,
rites completed, music prepared, praises resound.
Truly close,
looking up at the celestial countenance,
sunlight illuminates the dragon banquet.
Wind turns the pheasant fans, green feathers swirl,
serving the imperial sedan,
between clouds and stars,
five-colored golden insignia sparkle.
Tune for returning to the palace,
Wànsuìlè: Heaven turns to the North Star, clouds become auspicious,
gazing at the layered firmament,
Chónghuá's sun is radiant.
The nine regions and eight cardinal points are joyful and harmonious,
wishing the sage ruler long life,
ten thousand times ten thousand years.
Music for small banquets during the Yǒnglè reign.
First movement of the tune "The Great Beginning,"
Cháotiānzǐ: Chaotic yet undifferentiated,
water and earth form the primal qi,
not distinguishing north and south, east and west,
Heaven and Earth not yet discerned.
All myriad phenomena encompassed,
secrets within,
the mechanism of creation is hard to fathom,
this is the fundamental essence of yin and yang.
Then it becomes the Great Ultimate,
the Two Modes are established thereafter.
Second movement of the tune "Looking Up to the Great Light,"
Guīcháohuān: The Great Ultimate divides,
only then does its form appear,
the pure floats, the turbid sinks, Heaven and Earth are settled.
Sun and moon rise together,
illuminating the azure sky,
all myriad phenomena are clear.
Yang must move,
yin must be still,
yin and yang,
both correspond,
the two qis flow,
all myriad things are born.
Third movement of the tune "The Birth of the People,"
first part,
Gūměijiǔ: Heaven and Earth are clear,
the universe is tranquil,
the six harmonies are pure,
the four cardinal points are correct,
all myriad phenomena originally arise from one qi.
The Three Powers and Five Phases are established,
people and things,
together form groups.
Second part,
Tàipínglìng: As one category, human distinctions are not made,
eating raw, not knowing cooking,
avoiding cold and heat, dwelling in nests and caves,
covering themselves with leaves, seeking each other,
how is this loving one's parents?
Worldly ways of living,
though mixed, each finds peace in its nature.
Fourth movement of the tune "Prosperity of All Things,"
Zuì Tàipíng: The common people live in the world,
all myriad things grow in the mortal realm,
yin and yang operate, revolving in cycles,
over long ages, populations proliferate.
Climate changes are continuously transmitted,
who discerns the intermingling of things?
Hoping for a sage to appear, to rectify the land,
and for the common people to find peace.
Fifth performance of the "Yù Liùlóng" (御六龍)曲,
its first part,
Qīngjiāngyǐn (清江引): People have long looked up to the birth of a sage ruler;
Heaven causes a sage to be born among men.
The sage receives the celestial mandate,
embodies Heaven's principles, and dwells in the central rectitude.
He drives the six dragons,
the sage and enlightened one ascends to the nine heavens.
Its second part,
Bìyùxiāo (碧玉簫): The ruler sits in the divine capital,
and mountains and seas are renewed together.
The people look up to the ruler's grace,
and the sagely governance has human relations.
Human qualities are distinguished.
All things prosper,
the sage receives the celestial mandate,
and a hundred blessings arrive.
Laws are established and made clear,
Heaven's mandate is respected,
the later dynasty flourishes,
all follow the correct path.
Sixth performance of the "Tàijiē Píng" (泰階平)曲,
Shí'èryuè (十二月): The sage speaks of Heaven,
Heaven is the silent sage.
The sage governs justly,
all things prosper,
grace and might flourish,
the altars of soil and grain are secure,
benevolence and virtue are felt,
the land is stable.
Wise and virtuous talents are chosen to establish royal governance,
distinguishing good from evil and distributing rewards and punishments fairly.
The Three Dukes and Nine Ministers,
right and left arms,
all affairs are peaceful and prosperous.
Seventh performance of the "Jūndé Chéng" (君德成)曲,
its first part,
Shí'èryuè (十二月): The imperial foundation flourishes,
the sage emperor cultivates himself,
honors Heaven, and embodies the Way,
his sagely virtue becomes increasingly clear.
He respects Heaven and Earth,
and diligently labors for all people;
he establishes laws and systems,
so that all, high and low, are at peace.
Its second part,
Yáomín Gē (堯民歌): Customs, rites, and music strengthen human relations,
schools are established to advance Confucian classics,
wise ministers and good generals protect the court,
and people throughout the land sing songs of praise and joy.
Wise and virtuous individuals are employed,
wise and virtuous individuals establish great peace,
and all within the four seas return to rectitude.
Eighth performance of the "Shèngdào Xíng" (聖道行)曲,
its first part,
Jīndiàn Wànnián Huān (金殿萬年歡): The three cardinal guides are established,
the nine categories are revived.
The sagely Way is like Heaven,
auspicious grain grows in unison,
cold and heat are moderate.
The sage's boundless power makes the imperial foundation stable,
stronger than bedrock,
auspicious clouds arise,
propitious stars appear perpetually,
the three luminaries shine brightly,
all grains are harvested,
and all people are at peace.
Its second part,
Déshènglìng (得勝令): The sage's virtue moves the August Heaven,
sweet dew descends on mountains and rivers.
All nations come to pay tribute,
rare treasures are fully displayed,
and whips crack below the jade steps.
Look up to the sagely lord,
ascend to the golden hall,
wise and virtuous officials line the vermilion steps,
praising our Emperor,
for a year of abundant harvest.
Ninth performance of the "Lè Qīngníng" (樂清寧)曲,
its first part,
Pǔtiānlè (普天樂): All nations are at peace,
the imperial rule is just.
The Emperor and Empress,
are respected by all under Heaven.
The Emperor governs externally,
forever sagely and enlightened;
the Empress governs internally,
forever peaceful and serene.
Future sages who receive the mandate all follow the correct path,
virtue is passed down,
through sagely sons and divine descendants.
Heaven's majesty is vast,
the land is eternally secure,
and blessings are endless.
Its second part,
Gūměijiǔ (沽美酒): Harmonious qi arises,
filling the jade capital;
auspicious smoke rises,
reflecting the imperial palace.
The enlightened sage establishes the foundation and sets all people in order,
clouds and winds gather at the imperial court,
playing Xiáosháo (簫韶) music,
nine melodies are complete.
Its third part,
Tàipínglìng (太平令): Purple mist conceals golden phoenixes and colorful phoenixes,
auspicious light envelops good generals and wise ministers.
Jade tables are laden with rare delicacies and fine wines,
precious tripods burn fragrant dragon's saliva.
The Supreme One is eternally peaceful,
the heir apparent preserves the achievements,
congratulating the myriad-year-old sole recipient of blessings.
From the second performance to the eighth performance,
all were accompanied by a hundred types of entertainment;
the ninth performance,
was accompanied by the "Yú Yuè Yú Yuān" (魚躍于淵) performance.
At the banquet for officials at Fèngtiānmén (奉天門),
only the "Běntàichū" (本太初), "Yǎngdàmíng" (仰大明), and "Mínchūshēng" (民初生) three pieces were used,
with the same music for serving wine and food.
However, for the officials' prostration ceremony,
the "Cháotiānzǐ" (朝天子)曲 was used.
After the banquet,
the imperial carriage was escorted back to the palace,
using the "Yùluán Gē" (御鑾歌).
These are the musical pieces for the banquet celebrating the completion of Rénshòu Gōng (仁壽宮) during the Jiājìng (嘉靖) reign.
First performance of the "Běntàichū" (本太初)曲,
Cháotiānzǐ (朝天子): The Emperor is sincere and enlightened,
his treasured throne is founded on a prosperous mandate.
A feast is held in the immortal garden with the "Lù Míng" (鹿鳴) song,
the pavilions and halls reflect celestial writings.
"I have distinguished guests,
I play the zither and blow the sheng,"
showing the proper conduct,
manifesting virtuous sounds.
The sun rises, bright and constant,
the imperial rule of ten thousand years is righteous.
Second performance of the "Yǎngdàmíng" (仰大明)曲,
Diànqiánhuān (殿前歡): Heaven protects the sage,
blessing him with longevity and many sons.
Rites and music are cultivated and harmonized for a glorious revival,
bright and re-enlightened,
like mountains,
like hills,
like rivers that keep arriving without ceasing to grow.
Harmonious qi arises,
auspicious signs respond,
all gods receive their mandate,
and all nations come to court.
Third performance of the "Mínchūshēng" (民初生)曲,
its first part,
Gūměijiǔ (沽美酒): The Yellow River runs clear,
precious dew condenses,
auspicious wheat appears,
spiritual magpies call,
all blessings come together to honor the enlightened sage.
Joy at the completion of myriad treasures,
observing the celestial configurations,
the Taiji is peaceful.
Its second part,
Tàipínglìng (太平令): Mindful of agriculture and sericulture,
the basis of clothing and food;
looking up to the ruler's virtue,
which uniquely favors the people's livelihood.
Engaged in farming and digging wells,
are the common people.
Singing "Lù Míng" (鹿鳴),
gods and humans rejoice together.
The enlightened lord feasts distinguished guests,
offering baskets, playing zithers and blowing sheng,
from now on blessings will increase as ordained by Heaven.
Fourth performance of the "Pǐnwù Hēng" (品物亨)曲,
Zuìtàipíng (醉太平): In the jade palace, the sage's countenance is pleased,
the immortal garden is separated from the human world.
Guests play sheng and zithers,
a splendid banquet is opened by Heaven with fine wine,
the "Lù Míng" (鹿鳴) is sung and danced in the golden hall,
relying on our Emperor's blessings, all people are at peace,
singing "Tiānbǎo Huān" (天保歡) while drunk.
Fifth performance of the "Yù Liùlóng" (御六龍)曲,
its first part,
Qīngjiāngyǐn (清江引): The sagely lord, having the Way, enjoys great peace,
feasts extend joy and celebration.
He prioritizes the fundamentals and cares for the people's livelihood,
promoting transformation and solidifying Heaven's mandate.
Rejoicing in its completion,
a grand destiny unfolds for ten thousand years.
Its second part,
Bìyùxiāo (碧玉簫): The Emperor values agriculture and sericulture,
the imperial carriage sets off with brilliant light.
Unicorns roam and phoenixes soar,
a banquet displays the "Tiānbǎo Zhāng" (天保章).
Jade mats are spread,
precious goblets are offered,
and praises flow abundantly after drinking.
Sagely virtue is grand,
imperial grace is vast,
the era surpasses those of Táng (唐) and Yú (虞).
Jìnshàn Qǔ,
Part One,
Shuǐlóng Yín: Jewel zithers and jade sheng pipes loudly play,
The Sagely Son of Heaven
holds the imperial banquet.
Mount Nánshān’s ten thousand years of longevity,
The auspicious sun is directly in the sky.
A year of abundant harvest,
Exquisite dishes from all eight directions,
People enjoy the banquet of peace.
Part Two,
Tàiqīng Gē: Auspicious wheat and fine melons bring good fortune,
Looking up, we are blessed by the Rulers Yáo and Shùn,
Who lovingly nurture the common people,
And through Heaven’s will, send five winds and ten rains.
Autumn harvest and spring prayers are everywhere due to their virtue,
They encourage agriculture and sericulture,
For daily clothing and food.
〔一０〕Honored guests rejoice as the banquet begins,
Crimson clouds hold carved platters of delicacies.
Shānhū (mountain-calls) of ten thousand years, boundless blessings,
Sun rising like rivers flowing.
Part Three,
Shàngqīng Gē: Relying on Our Emperor,
Whose virtue unites Heaven and Earth, creating harmony.
The Four-Three Kings,
The Six-Five Emperors,
The Four-Three Kings,
The Six-Five Emperors,
〔一一〕When the state prospers,
Talented people are the highest auspicious signs.
Nourishing the myriad people,
The nine domains are joyful,
All blessings are appropriate.
Part Four,
Kāitiānmén: The precious palace shines,
Dragons and tigers gather like wind and clouds.
Gazing at the vermilion steps,
Beholding the Ziweī,
Zhōu poems sing of intoxication,
Locusts and qílín feet bring auspiciousness,
Beholding the soaring dragon,
In the heavenly position.
Bīnfēngtíng Banquet, music for the lecturing officials.
First performance, Běntàichū zhī Qǔ:
Cháotiānzǐ: A nine-layered imperial decree is transmitted,
Palace halls open for the autumn banquet.
The season for granting winter clothes, the frosty sky is solemn,
Harvested grains fill the fields everywhere.
Playing zithers and sheng pipes,
Peace and prosperity are seen again,
Artisans sing the "Seventh Month" chapter.
Spring wine is offered at the banquet,
May Our Emperor live for ten thousand years,
And visit Xīyuàn every year.
Second performance, Yǎngdàmíng zhī Qǔ:
Diànqiánhuān: The Phoenix Garden imperial banquet opens,
Yellow flowers reflect on jade steps.
Lùmíng and Tiānbǎo sing of the Three Dynasties,
Ancient tunes newly composed,
Offering the King a goblet of ten thousand years.
The sun and moon are bright,
Heaven and Earth are vast,
See the autumn sacrifices every year.
There are signs of great peace,
The sovereign is enlightened!
Third performance, Mínchūshēng zhī Qǔ,
Part One,
Gūměijiǔ: Spring warmth is joyful,
The enlightened day is long.
Holding elegant baskets,
Gathering tender mulberry leaves.
Picking cocoons and reeling silk in countless boxes.
Dyeing red and yellow, for Kǒngyáng,
Making clothes for the young masters.
Part Two,
Tàipíng Lìng: Diligently cultivate crops,
The year is bountiful,
In the ninth and tenth months, grains enter the threshing floor.
For spring wine, new brews float in the jars,
Villagers and farmers joyfully sing in unison.
Feasting in the public hall,
Slaughtering sheep and raising goblets,
Following with rhinoceros horns,
Wishing the Sagely Longevity,
With the support of all spirits.
Fourth performance, Pǐnwùhēng zhī Qǔ:
Zuìtàipíng: Gathering abundant grains in the fields,
Brewing imperial wine filling the vats,
Public sericulture for weaving black and yellow silks,
Wearing dragon robes and ceremonial attire.
Locusts and crickets harmonize in clear song,
Water and mountain scenery illuminate the immortal retinue,
At Bīnfēngtíng Hall, offering goblets of rosy wine,
Wishing the Sagely Longevity without bounds.
Fifth performance, Yùliùlóng zhī Qǔ,
Part One,
Qīngjiāng Yǐn: Where can such autumn scenery be found?
The Phoenix Garden is to the right of the Dragon Pool.
Farmers’ crops are harvested,
Young masters’ clothes are just being bestowed,
The King of Ten Thousand Years frequently offers wine.
Part Two,
Bìyù Xiāo: Of all our people,
Agriculture and sericulture are the most arduous,
Operating all year long.
Climate changes from winter to spring,
Farmers rejoice,
Women and children are diligent.
Chanting Bīn poems,
Adoring the transforming power,
Threshing grounds are new,
Wind and rain are favorable.
Feasting on the imperial steps,
The dragon countenance is near.
Jìnshàn Qǔ,
Part One,
Shuǐlóng Yín: Caring for the elderly, resting from farming, opening the imperial banquet,
Pouring spring wine,
Bestowing upon the aged,
Slaughtering sheep and cutting chives,
The community drums beat loudly.
Fragrant glutinous rice grains,
Ascending the hall to respectfully offer,
This joy is truly enviable.
Part Two,
Tàiqīng Gē: Ninth month sky,
Opening Xīyuàn,
The imperial residence is Wúyì Diàn,
A lecturing tent is spread.
Scholars gather,
Like rising clouds and shining stars,
Jade weft and pearl constellations.
Beholding imperial compositions,
Illustrating heavenly chapters,
Shining like the Milky Way.
In the era of Yáo and Shùn, the people live in peace,
Imperial granaries and divine storehouses are filled with harvested grains,
Golden brilliance and jade splendor show auspicious signs,
A year of great abundance.
Part Three,
Shàngqīng Gē: In the Phoenix Garden imperial residence,
Public mulberry and imperial plowing are now being performed.
Personally plowing and raising silkworms,
Encouraging men and women,
Personally plowing and raising silkworms,
Encouraging men and women.
〔一二〕Offering lamb,
Ascending the hall to play music and dance,
Mallow, beans, and dates are brought to the precious kitchen,
Mount Wànshòu is acclaimed.
Part Four,
Kāitiānmén: At Bīnfēngtíng,
Together we revere Our Sagely Emperor.
All grains are harvested,
All nations are peaceful.
People are healthy, things are abundant, auspicious signs respond,
Looking up at the movements of Heaven,
Looking down at the spiritual essence of Earth.
Lóngqìng Sān Nián Grand Review of Troops and Return Journey Music.
Wǔchéng zhī Qǔ: Our Emperor completes the military review,
Inspecting the troops,
Strengthening the imperial capital.
Dragon banners illuminate the tiger and leopard camps,
Six armies gather like clouds, armor shining brightly.
Awe-inspiring power spreads far and wide,
Barbarians are shaken with fear,
First praising peace and prosperity,
The four seas are clear.
Jiājìng Era Empress personally raises silkworms, banquet for internal and external court ladies music.
Ascending the throne,
Playing Tiānxiāng Fèngsháo zhī Qǔ: Spring clouds swirl around the fragrant dawn,
Joyfully Heaven and Earth's myriad phenomena flourish,
Orchid streams and fragrant gardens welcome the immortal retinue.
Gathering mulberry branches,
Climbing dense trees,
Personally attending the silkworm palace and cocoon hall.
Jade moon and pearl stars illuminate the vast void,
Opening the banquet and halting the green banners,
A reputation for chastity for ten thousand years.
Jìnshàn Qǔ,
Gūměijiǔ: Silkworm ritual completed,
The phoenix carriage stops,
Offering goblets of rosy wine,
Arranging cloud screens.
Palace consorts and noble ladies look up to Kūnníng.
Auspicious clouds reflect in the purple abyss,
Together offering blessings,
Shining like the auspicious star.
〔一三〕
Returning to the palace,
the Imperial Lúan Gē (歌): Only Heaven raises the enlightened emperor,
the sovereign plows the field,
the empress personally cultivates silkworms,
personally leading the fields and weaving for myriad nations.
Heaven is clear, earth is peaceful, and the people are prosperous and well-off,
the hundred grains are all harvested,
the four barbarians come to pay homage.
His governance rivals that of Yú and Táng,
bringing forth auspicious signs for generations.
During the Yǒnglè (永樂) reign, the musical chapters for the Eastern Palace's banquets and feasts were established.
〔一四〕
The first piece, "Joy of a Thousand Springs" (喜千春之曲),
celebrates the sagely dynasty: Founding the nation and receiving Heaven's mandate,
with an abundance of divine blessings,
unifying the realm,
and expanding its vast territory.
The common people are joyful,
all things radiate glory,
all bathed in the waves of grace.
With celestial melodies,
they collectively praise in songs of peace and prosperity.
All bow in unison,
for a thousand, thousand years to the Eastern Palace,
with the entire nation filled with spring harmony.
The second piece, "Everlasting Southern Mountain" (永南山之曲),
Shuǐ Xiān Zǐ (水仙子): The grand foundation is eternally secure, the ocean waves are clear,
in this prosperous and enlightened age, rites and music flourish,
Huá and Yí are unified, and the rivers and mountains are tranquil.
The people are harmonious,
and rejoice in great peace.
Praising the Eastern Palace for his benevolence, filial piety, wisdom, and brilliance,
upholding the balance of power with rectitude,
conforming to the cosmic order for prosperity and success,
seated in the Central Kingdom for ten thousand generations of prosperity and tranquility.
The third piece, "Osmanthus Branches Fragrance" (桂枝香之曲),
Chán Gōng Qǔ (蟾宮曲): Dawn light merges,
feasting in the Spring Palace,
the sun is bright and the wind is gentle,
auspicious qi abounds.
Constantly presiding over the state's pivotal affairs,
establishing grand principles and laws,
with rites and ceremonies of utmost impartiality.
Serving the sagely sovereign with gentle voice and graceful demeanor,
inquiring about his well-being with diligence, filial piety, and reverence.
Decisive and magnanimous,
strong and enlightened,
his sagely virtues are in harmony with all.
The fourth piece, "Early Spring Dawn" (初春曉之曲),
Xiǎo Liáng Zhōu (小梁州): Residing solemnly in the imperial palace, serving the Zǐ Wēi (紫微) star (emperor),
governing the celestial movements,
all seasons and all things are in harmony.
Relying on the virtue of the enlightened sovereign,
the great enterprise is mightier than a solid rock.
The imperial heir is benevolent, filial, enlightened, loyal, and righteous,
his good reputation spreads far, and he conforms to the civilizing influence and court rituals.
Filial piety can gladden the hearts of loving parents,
respect deepens the sense of hierarchy,
rituals bring harmony between superiors and inferiors, and peace to the people,
inspiring joy and prosperity.
The fifth piece, "Heaven and Earth at Peace" (乾坤泰之曲),
Mǎn Tíng Fāng (滿庭芳): Spring harmony on the imperial banquet mats,
stabilizing the nation and making it prosperous,
revering the sagely and respecting the worthy,
literary excellence and martial prowess bringing convenience to the people.
Rites and music are perfected,
enjoying great enterprises, upholding the Doctrine of the Mean without deviation,
following the constant ways of Heaven, with frugality as primary,
achieving cultural refinement through strict rites and exemplary teachings,
filial piety and reverence for a hundred million years.
The sixth piece, "Ode to Prosperous Fortune" (昌運頌之曲),
Xǐ Qiū Fēng (喜秋風): Civil and military are at peace,
the military and people are joyful.
Feasting in Wén Huá (文華) Palace,
meeting with officials,
the five-colored clouds move in unison with heavenly music.
Congratulating the Spring Palace,
praising the imperial dynasty.
The second to sixth pieces
are all accompanied by various entertainments.
The seventh piece, "The Great Way Opens" (泰道開之曲),
〔一五〕Gū Měi Jiǔ (沽美酒): Spring breeze spreads,
filling the painted pavilion,
facing the beautiful scenery,
Fèng Huáng Zhōu (鳳凰洲).
Holding high golden goblets and jade cups,
with dignified escorts to the left and right,
officials divided by rank,
dukes and marquises arrayed.
Its second part,
Tài Píng Lìng (太平令): Emulating the sagely sovereign's sincerity and diligence,
managing the ancestral rituals solemnly throughout the year,
harmonious melodies and celestial music played in unison,
revering the king's governance and Heaven's blessing.
Bowing, dancing, and kowtowing,
offering praises and presenting wine,
may he live for a thousand, thousand years in peace, prosperity, and longevity.
Music for presenting the imperial meal,
Shuǐ Lóng Yín (水龍吟): Fangxiang, sheng, qin, drums, and music resound,
〔一六〕arranging precious utensils,
unfurling the imperial mats.
Luan carriages and banners,
brocade scenes are continuously connected.
Officials with hairpins and caps hasten forward,
all coming to pay homage,
spring fills the Wén Huá Diàn (文華殿).
Ascending the throne, returning to the palace, all officials perform their rites,
playing the "Thousand Autumns Age" (千秋歲)曲: The years of Yáo and Shùn surpass those of Yǔ and Zhōu,
auspicious clouds arise, encircling the phoenix tower.
Favorable winds and timely rain bring in the five grains,
the myriad people sing praises and anthems.
(Morning court on the first and fifteenth day of the lunar month is the same.)
Collation Notes
Gazetteer, Volume 40: Imperial Guard
In the Zhōu Guān (周官),
the king's imperial guard was divided and managed by subordinates of the Tiān Guān (天官), Chūn Guān (春官), and Xià Guān (夏官) offices,
while the matters of clearance and escort were exclusively under the Qiū Guān (秋官).
During Hàn (漢) court assemblies,
the guard officials arrayed chariots and cavalry,
and displayed flags and banners.
The Táng (唐) dynasty followed the Suí (隋) system,
establishing a Wèi Wèi Qīng (衞尉卿) [Minister of the Imperial Guard]
to manage ceremonial guards and tent-curtain affairs.
The Sòng (宋) Wèi Wèi (衞尉) oversaw the Zuǒ Yòu Jīn Wú Wèi Sī (左、右金吾衞司),
Zuǒ Yòu Jīn Wú Zhàng Sī (左、右金吾仗司),
and Liù Jūn Yí Zhàng Sī (六軍儀仗司),
responsible for clearing roads, patrolling, arranging formations, and guiding ceremonial guards.
The Yuán (元) dynasty established the Gǒng Wèi Sī (拱衞司),
overseeing the Kòng Hè Hù (控鶴戶),
to perform these duties.
Although the systems of successive dynasties had changes and differences,
the general aim was to diligently guard entries and exits,
and strictly define the distinctions between noble and humble.
Carefulness leads to solemnity and dignity,
and solemnity and dignity lead to orderliness.
Therefore, civil aspects are called Yí (儀) [ceremonial],
and military aspects are called Wèi (衞) [guard].
When the Son of Heaven went out,
the carriages and retinue in sequence
were called Lǔ Bù (鹵簿).
However, in the Táng (唐) system,
officials of the fourth rank and above were all granted Lǔ Bù (鹵簿),
so the term could apply to both monarch and ministers.
In the early Míng (明) dynasty, the ritual officials were ordered by imperial decree
to simplify the elaborate Lǔ Bù (鹵簿),
aiming for frugality and discarding extravagance,
to show the intention of valuing simplicity over luxury.
For regular court audiences, the Winter Solstice, New Year's Day, imperial birthdays, court assemblies, as well as enthronements, investitures, and receiving foreign envoys,
the Yí Luán Sī (儀鸞司) arranged the ceremonial guard.
And the Central Palace (Empress), Eastern Palace (Crown Prince), and imperial princes all had their own ceremonial guard systems.
Later, these might have been enhanced over time,
but the creative system of Hóng Wǔ (洪武) was to be the standard.
Here, the general outline recorded in the rites is compiled
for examination.
The ceremonial guards for princely dukes, imperial concubines, and Eastern Palace concubines and below,
as recorded in the Huì Diǎn (會典),
are all included in this chapter.
Imperial ceremonial guard.
On the Xīn Yǒu (辛酉) day of the twelfth month of the first year of Wú (吳) (1367),
the Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, Lǐ Shàncháng (李善長), led the ritual officials to present the enthronement ceremonies.
On that day, early in the morning,
the Gǒng Wèi Sī (拱衞司) arrayed the Lǔ Bù (鹵簿),
stationing armored soldiers to the east and west outside the Wǔ Mén (午門),
and arraying flags and weapons to the east and west outside the Fèng Tiān Mén (奉天門).
Twelve dragon flags,
divided into left and right,
each requiring twelve armored soldiers.
One Běi Dǒu (北斗) flag and one dà (纛) banner were placed in front,
one leopard tail banner was placed behind,
each requiring three armored soldiers.
Two tigers and two leopards,
six trained elephants,
divided into left and right.
Sixty-four cloth flags:
Gate flags, sun flags, moon flags,
Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Wind, Cloud, Thunder, Rain, Jiāng (江), Hé (河), Huái (淮), Jì (濟) flags,
Heavenly Horse, Heavenly Lù (祿), Bái Zé (白澤), Zhū Què (朱雀), Xuán Wǔ (玄武) flags, etc.,
Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water Five Elements flags,
Five Sacred Mountains flags,
Bear flags,
Luan flags and Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions flags,
each in six rows;
each flag required five armored soldiers,
one holding the flag,
four holding bows and crossbows.
Five imperial carriages were arranged outside the Fèng Tiān Mén (奉天門): the Jade Carriage in the center,
the Gold Carriage to its left,
then the Leather Carriage,
the Elephant Carriage to its right,
then the Wooden Carriage,
all arranged in parallel.

To the left and right of the Dān Chí (丹墀) [vermillion steps] were arranged yellow imperial guard banners, yellow parasols, ornate parasols, curved parasols, purple square umbrellas, red square umbrellas, pheasant feather fans, red round fans, feathered canopy banners, leopard tails, dragon-head poles, signal banners, teaching banners, stop banners, vermillion leading banners, halberd plumes, dagger-axe plumes, ceremonial gong plumes, etc.,
each in three rows.

To the left and right of the Dān Bì (丹陛) [vermillion steps] were arranged canopy banners, ringing banners, golden banners, lantern cages, Azure Dragon and White Tiger banners, class swords, 'Wu' staffs, standing melon staffs, reclining melon staffs, ceremonial knives, stirrup staffs, halberds, bone-decorated swords, Vermillion Bird and Black Tortoise banners, etc.,
each in three rows.
To the left and right of the palace gate were arranged one round parasol, a golden folding chair, a golden footrest, a water basin, a water pitcher, a round yellow fan, and a red fan.
All were held by guardsmen.
In the tenth month of the first year of the Hóngwǔ reign, the protocol for the New Year's Day court audience was established.
The Jīnwǔwèi [Guard] set up flags outside Fèngtiānmén.
The Sùwèi [Guard] set up weaponry outside Wǔmén.
The Wèiwèisì [Court of the Imperial Clan] set up yellow imperial guards of honor at the gate of Fèngtiāndiàn, and on the Dānbì and Dānchí.
The Nèishǐjiān [Directorate of Palace Servants] held ceremonial objects on the hall.
Whenever there was the Winter Solstice, the Emperor's Birthday, an enfeoffment, or a visit from a Qīnwáng [prince of the first rank] or a Fānshǐ [foreign envoy],
the ceremony was the same.
However, when an imperial edict or amnesty was proclaimed, or incense was offered,
only the ceremonial guards at the gate of Fèngtiāndiàn and on the Dānbì were set up, and the ceremonial objects were held in the hall.
The arrangement was as follows:
Outside Wǔmén,
swords, shields, shū, and chā were placed to the east and west,
with armored soldiers in red.
In the middle path outside Fèngtiānmén,
the Jīnwǔ and Sùwèi two guards set up twelve dragon flags,
divided left and right,
with twelve armored soldiers in green.
One Běidǒuqí [Big Dipper flag] and one dú [large banner] were at the front,
and one bàowěi [leopard tail flag] was at the rear,
all with three armored soldiers in black.
There were two tigers and two leopards,
and six trained elephants,

Sixty-four flags were arranged on the left and right.
On the left front, the first row consisted of
two ménqí [gate flags],
each with five armored soldiers in red,
one of whom held the flag,
and the other four beneath the flag held bows and arrows.
The second row consisted of
one yuèqí [moon flag],

In the first year of Yǒnglè,
the Lǐ Bù reported that a jiǔ lóng chē should be included in the lú bù,

The Emperor said:
"Propriety values moderation.
Excess is extravagance,
and insufficiency is frugality.
The former court's deliberation was precise.
We should follow the old regulations;
how can we arbitrarily add to them
to encourage extravagance in later generations?
Since the jiǔ lóng chē was absent in the former court,
it should remain as it was."

Chapter 41: Carriages and Apparel (Yúfú Yī): Grand Carriage (Dà Lù), Jade Carriage (Yù Lù), Grand Horse Litter (Dà Mǎniǎn), Small Horse Litter (Xiǎo Mǎniǎn), Walking Litter (Bùniǎn), Grand Cool Walking Litter (Dà Liáng Bùniǎn), Palanquin (Bǎn Jiào), Plough-Root Carriage (Gēnggēn Chē); Carriages and Litters of Empresses and Consorts (Hòufēi Chēyú); Carriages and Litters of the Crown Prince (Huáng Tàizǐ) and Princes (Qīnwáng) and Below; Carriages and Litters of Grandees (Gōngqīng) and Below; Umbrellas and Canopies (Sǎgài); Saddles and Reins (Ānpèi).
When Yǒu Yú Shì (Shùn) governed the world,
carriages and clothes were used for merit.
During the Xià Dynasty, ceremonial robes (fúmiǎn) were made beautiful.
During the Shāng Dynasty, the Grand Carriage symbolized frugality.
In the flourishing Zhōu Dynasty, there were officials in charge of carriages (Jīnchē), ceremonial carriages (Diǎnlù), caps (Biànshī), and apparel (Sīfú).
The Son of Heaven used these to set an example for all states,
and there were five types of carriages,
extending down to ministers and common people.
The Hàn Dynasty inherited the Qín system,
using the Golden-Root Carriage (Jīngēn) as the imperial carriage,
and wearing black ceremonial robes (jūnxuán) for great sacrifices.
In the Eastern Capital (Dōngdū), there were ceremonial items such as the nine-streamer banner (jiǔliú), cloud-patterned banner (yúnhǎn), tasseled crown (liúmiǎn), and embroidered shoes (qújué),
adding splendor to existing practices,
and changing with each passing day.
When the Eastern Jìn (Jiāng Zuǒ) found temporary peace,
the Jade Carriage housed a precious phoenix,
and colored banners held golden dragons.
When wearing ceremonial crowns,
some were adorned with kingfisher feathers, coral, and various pearls.
How could these be what the ancients called the "model carriages" (fǎjià) and "model robes" (fǎfú)?
During the Wǔdé reign of the Táng Dynasty (618-626 CE), regulations for carriages, litters, and apparel were established,
allowing those of higher rank to use items of lower rank,
but those of lower rank could not imitate those of higher rank.
In the early Sòng Dynasty,
the imperial robes (gǔnmiǎn) were not adorned with pearls or jade.
During the Zhènghé reign (1111-1118 CE), an imperial edict ordered the repair of carriages and litters,
and the establishment of various banners.
The Bureau of Rites (Yǐlǐ Jú) clarified and set these,
to be used as established regulations.
Under the Yuán system,
for suburban sacrifices, the Jade Carriage was used,
and imperial robes (gǔnmiǎn) were worn;
for imperial tours,
an elephant litter might be used,
and the four-season zhìsūn robes
were used as appropriate.
As soon as Míng Tàizǔ (Zhū Yuánzhāng) acquired the empire,
he investigated and established national rites,
emphasizing simplicity in carriages and apparel.
He drew upon ancient practices while adapting to current times,
conforming to the spirit of ritual.
By the time of Shìzōng (Jiājìng Emperor),
the Plough-Root Carriage was built for the plowing ceremony,
the leisure cap (yànbian) was worn for relaxed occasions,
the military cap (wǔbiàn) was worn for military drills.
Furthermore, the Loyal and Serene Crown (Zhōngjìng Guān) was created to encourage those in positions of authority,
and the Preserving Harmony Crown (Bǎohé Guān) to foster closeness with the imperial clan.
This also constituted a system established by one ruler.
Alas, the former generations' ceremonial items such as umbrellas and fans, saddles and bridles,
gate halberds and banners,
all distinguished ranks and authority,
and this became even stricter in the Sòng Dynasty.
In the early Míng Dynasty,
virtuous frugality was the foundation.
When the palaces were completed,
no patterned stone was used for paving the ground.
To deter the common people with this example,
even military officials would sometimes decorate their bed curtains with golden dragons,
and use the "nine-five" (jiǔwǔ) numbering system for horse stables,
while wealthy commoners would melt gold for wine vessels,
and adorn them with jade pearls.
Míng Tàizǔ severely punished all such transgressions.
He then ordered scholarly officials to study ancient records and discuss rituals,
to establish regulations for officials and commoners' apparel, residences, and implements.
These were upheld through successive generations,
with new prohibitions added over time.
Here, we further append the distinctions in the imperial seals and treasures of the court, the tallies and credentials within and outside the capital, and the household implements,
at the end.
The Son of Heaven's Chariots.
When the great court assembly was held at the beginning of the Míng dynasty,
the Gǒngwèi Sī (Guard and Protection Office) would set up five chariots at Fèngtiānmén (Gate of Receiving Heaven):
the Jade Chariot was in the center;
to its left was the Gold Chariot,
followed by the Leather Chariot;
to its right was the Elephant Chariot,
followed by the Wood Chariot.
When the imperial carriage left,
the Son of Heaven would ride in the Jade Chariot,
behind which was a sedan chair,
carried by eight bearers.
Later, Tàizǔ consulted the *Zhōulǐ* (Rites of Zhōu) regarding the five chariots,
and inquired of his Confucian ministers,
saying:
"The Jade Chariot is too extravagant.
Why not simply use the Wood Chariot?"
The scholar Zhān Tóng replied:
"Confucius said, 'Ride in the chariot of Yīn,'
which is indeed the Wood Chariot."
Tàizǔ said:
"A chariot decorated with jade
was used only for sacrifices to Heaven in ancient times.
For regular use, the Yīn chariot should be adopted.
However, at the time of sacrifices to Heaven,
if the Jade Chariot is not ready,
the Wood Chariot might not be unacceptable either."
The Cānzhèng (Policy Adviser) Zhāng Chǎng said:
"The Wood Chariot
is a military chariot,
and cannot be used for sacrifices to Heaven."
Tàizǔ said:
"Confucius weighed the rites and music of the four dynasties
and made them a model for all ages.
How could the Wood Chariot not be used for sacrifice?
Sacrifice lies in sincerity and reverence,
not in sticking to ritual forms."
In Hóngwǔ first year (1368),
the relevant department proposed that the imperial carriage and apparel
should be adorned with gold,
but an imperial edict ordered the use of bronze.
The department officials said the expense was small and not worth regretting.
Tàizǔ said:
"I possess the wealth of the four seas;
how could I be stingy with this?
It is simply that if I do not set an example of frugality and restraint, I cannot lead those below me.
Moreover, the habit of extravagance never grows large except from small beginnings."
In the sixth year (1373), he ordered the ritual officials to examine the system of five chariots
and construct two Wood Chariots.
One was lacquered vermilion
and used for sacrifices;
the other was covered with leather
and used for imperial excursions.
In the winter of that year,
the Grand Chariot was completed.
He ordered the construction of one more Grand Chariot,
ten Elephant Chariots,
one Central Palace Chariot,
and ten carriages for the concubines,
all decorated with phoenixes.
These were built because he was about to visit Zhōnglì Fǔ (Zhongli Prefecture),
and thus were not part of the regular system.
In the twenty-sixth year (1393), the system for the imperial procession and Grand Chariot was finally established:
one Jade Chariot,
one Grand Chariot,
one Nine-Dragon Chariot,
and one foot-litter.
Later, the Nine-Dragon Chariot was abolished.
In Yǒnglè third year (1405), the system for the imperial procession and Grand Chariot was revised to include:
one Grand Chariot, one Jade Chariot, one large horse-litter, one small horse-litter, one foot-litter, one large cool foot-litter, and one plank sedan chair,
each with its complete outfit and canopy tent.
The Grand Chariot
was one zhàng, three chi, nine cùn, and five fēn high,
and eight chi, two cùn, and five fēn wide.
The chariot seat was four chi, one cùn and a fraction high,
with a flat platform on top.
The front and rear lattice frames, along with the goose-wing-shaped ornaments and the four hanging ruyi-shaped bead-drop boards.
The shaft was two zhàng, two chi, nine cùn and a fraction long,
lacquered red.
It was adorned with gilded bronze dragon heads, dragon tails, and dragon scale leaf-plates nailed on.
Beneath the flat platform was a square box,
lacquered red on all sides,
with twelve compartments in each frame.
The interior was decorated with green ground and gold outlines,
painted with six beasts:
qílín, suānní, rhinoceros, elephant, heavenly horse, and tiānlù;
and six birds:
luán, phoenix, peacock, zhūquè, zhái, and crane.
To the left and right below the platform were mudguards and two wheels,
connected by one axle.
Each wheel had eighteen spokes,
and its felloes were all lacquered red,
adorned with gilded bronze carved flower leaf-plates.
The hub inside the wheel
was adorned with gilded bronze carved lotus petal wheel-disks,
and yellow velvet straps for pulling the shaft passed through the axle.
The chariot pavilion was six chi, seven cùn, nine fēn high,
with four pillars, each five chi, eight cùn, four fēn long.
The railings and seats were all lacquered red.
The front two pillars were adorned with gold foil,
with precious auspicious flowers at the pillar tops,
cloud-dragon patterns in the middle,
and tortoise patterns at the bottom.
At the front left and right were doors,
five chi, one cùn, nine fēn high,
and two chi, four cùn, nine fēn wide,
adorned all around with twelve carved wood incense-colored boards with gold-outlined auspicious grass patterns.
Beside the doors were two compartments each and a bright *ge*,
all lacquered red,
adorned with gilded bronze carved flower leaf-plates,
and the compartments were woven with yellow cord.
Behind it was a red-lacquered screen,
with five gold-outlined cloud-dragons carved on it,
and one gold-foiled cloud-dragon on a red-lacquered board.
The ground behind the screen was incense-colored,
with four gold-outlined cloud-dragons carved on the upper four compartments,
and cloud boards next to them.
The lower three compartments had three gold-outlined cloud-dragons carved,
and cloud boards next to them as well.
All were adorned with gilded bronze carved flower leaf-plates.
Inside the pavilion was a red-lacquered soft seat framed with yellow cord,
with a lotus-shaped stone pendant below,
and a flower carpet, red brocade cushion, and red-lacquered chair on top.
The backrest had one gold-outlined cloud-dragon carved on it,
below which was one carved cloud board,
and one red-lacquered fúshòu (fortune and longevity) board with a cushion.
In the middle of the chair was a yellow gold-woven chair backrest and seat cushion,
with chair skirts all around,
and yellow silk curtains.
Outside the pavilion were ten red curtains with blue silk borders.
The chariot roof and circular platform were three chi and a fraction high,
with a gilded bronze squatting dragon finial,
with an inverted and upright lotus seat,
from which hung circular yellow cords for climbing to the top.
The platform was lacquered red;
below it, the outer four sides were incense-colored,
with gold-outlined clouds;
the inner four corners were blue,
painted with five-color clouds.
The chariot canopy was decorated with blue,
and inside the pavilion were gold-foiled dougong (bracket sets),
supporting a red-lacquered framed precious canopy,
interlocked with eight finials,
covered with yellow silk,
called the "Yellow House";
in the center and all around were nine embroidered five-color cloud-dragons.
There were three layers of "Heavenly Wheels,"
all lacquered red,
on which were eighty-one carved wood boards with gold-foiled edges and shining leaves,
and inside were three layers of green ground carved wood boards with gold-foiled cloud-dragon patterns,
interspersed with eighty-one painted five-color cloud liner boards.
Around the bottom of the platform,
adorned with brass nails,
were three layers of yellow silk drip curtains,
each with eighty-one pleats,
interspersed with embroidered five-color cloud-dragon patterns.
From the four corners hung blue silk sashes,
each embroidered with a five-color cloud rising dragon.
The four corners of the circular platform were connected to the chariot seat board
by circular yellow cords for climbing to the top,
and also gold-foiled wooden fish.
In front of the chariot pavilion were two turning corner railings, left and right,
and behind it was one straight railing with turning corner railings, left and right,
all lacquered red,
with inlaid carved wood gold-foiled dragons,
interspersed with five-color clouds.
The three railings had a total of twelve pillars,
the pillar tops adorned with carved wood gold-foiled squatting dragons and gold-lined five-color lotus flowers embracing the pillars.
Flower carpets were spread all around inside the railings.
Behind the pavilion stood two Tàicháng Qí (Grand Constant Banners),
made of yellow gauze,
each with twelve streamers,
and each streamer embroidered with one rising dragon, inside and out.
The waist of the left banner was embroidered with the sun, moon, and Big Dipper,
and the pole top had a gilded bronze dragon head.
The waist of the right banner was embroidered with the *fú* character,
and the pole top had a gilded bronze halberd.
Each was adorned with two gilded bronze bells,
with twelve red tassels hanging,
and above the tassels were gilded bronze precious canopies,
and below hung blue cord *ge* and metal fittings.
There was one step ladder,
lacquered red,
adorned with gilded bronze carved flower leaf-plates.
There were two *xíngmǎ jià* (horse stands),
lacquered red,
with yellow velvet flat cords on top,
adorned with gilded bronze leaf-plates.
There was one yellow silk cover (for dust protection),
one oilcloth rain cover, one blue felt cover, and one red-oiled folding ladder, and one red-oiled supporting fork each.
The chariot was pulled by two elephants.
The yùlù
is also drawn by two elephants.
Its design is similar to the dàlù,
but it lacks the ornamentation of a flat platform with twelve grilles underneath.
The two front pillars of the lùtíng
are adorned with coiled, gold-leafed ascending dragons.
Behind the screen, there are no ornaments of the upper four grilles with cloud-dragons or cloud-panels.
Inside the tiānlún, there are carved wooden ornaments of jade-colored cloud-dragon patterns on a green ground.
However, the tàicháng qí and items like the tātī and xíngmǎ
are all the same as the dàlù.
The dàmǎniǎn
was anciently pulled by people.
In the Zhōulǐ, the "Jīnchē" lists five lù for the empress,
one of which
is a "niǎnchē
pulled by ropes."
However, the xiànshī had
